english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantains or shade trees gives young cocoa the living umbrella it needs to protect leaf moisture and survive its early development stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Hefatalɔi tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ Enɛ haa cocoa bibii lɛ naa shade ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu baa lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshweremɔ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and twisting into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔ amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni etsake ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni kɛ ŋmeii niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii kɛ́ adu lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do green caterpillars keep eating the center leaves of my young maize plants before the corn grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which attack the soft funnel of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended controls directly into the leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ he lɛ mra Ni akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni akɛwoɔ baai amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is worn out and needs fertilizer or manure for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When soil loses its nutrients, crop leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, plants grow slowly, and harvest yields drop steadily compared to previous seasons.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baaya nɔ aba shi kɛ akɛto nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ he.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a brief dry spell. If seeds germinate after one rain and no more rain falls for a few weeks, the young roots dry out and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ kome sɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ otsii fioo komɛi. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ pepper dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crowding plants forces them to fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil food, making them grow weak and thin. It also traps moisture between leaves, encouraging fungal diseases.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms onto the ground without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat, poor watering habits, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow strong without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast after I bring them home from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba shia lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly when wounded by farm tools during digging or stored in hot, dark rooms. Storing clean, uninjured yams in a cool, well-ventilated traditional yam barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji okwaayeli nibii ye amɛ awui yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Atoɔ sweet potato ni he tse, ni epilaaa lɛ yɛ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plant roots with dry leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry days, and blocks sunlight so weeds cannot easily sprout and compete with your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli ni otsi hulu lɛ naa koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ onibii akaye akaŋ.

english: What are armyworms and how do I know if they are attacking my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ amɛmiitutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Armyworms are small, destructive caterpillars that eat plant leaves and stems, especially maize. You can tell they are on your farm if you see large holes chewed in the leaves and small brownish or green caterpillars hiding inside the young leaves.
ga: Armyworms ji ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi, titri lɛ, ŋmei. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛyɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ona ŋmeii agboi ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ loo eŋɔli ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants suddenly full of ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are a major sign of chewing pests like armyworms or caterpillars. They feed on the leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to catch sunlight and grow healthy food for you to harvest.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miiye nii. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ shi ni ekwɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa koni okpa.

english: Can armyworms destroy my entire farm if I do not treat them early?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ kɛji mitsaaa amɛ mra?

english: Yes, armyworms travel in large groups and eat very fast. If left unchecked, they can strip all the green leaves off your plants in a few days, which will ruin your harvest completely.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii fãa gbɛ yɛ kui wuji amli ni amɛyeɔ nii oya waa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie tso ko baai eŋɔli fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ baafite onitsumɔ lɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know when my crop is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature; for example, maize husks turn dry and brown, and grain seeds become hard. Once the crop reaches full maturity, it stops growing and is ready to be collected.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmaa lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa Ebaakpa dalɛ ni efee klalo kɛha nibii ni abua naa.

english: Why do some crops take a few months to mature while others are ready much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji fioo dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Every crop type has its own natural growth clock built into its seeds. Leafy vegetables grow quickly in a few weeks, while grain crops like maize or rice take several months to flower, seed, and dry out completely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebɔɔ su ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛwo edumɔwui lɛ amli. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ daa oya yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ewoɔ dumɔwui, ni egbiɔ kwraa.

english: If pests attack my crops early, can the plants still recover and yield well?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra hu? Ani tso lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, if you control the pests quickly while the plant is still growing, the crop can bounce back, produce new healthy leaves, and still give you a good harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ oya be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔɔ baai heei ni mli wa ni oha bo yibiiwoo kpakpa lolo.

english: Do I need to spray my farm with pest chemicals every single week?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa otsi?

english: No, spraying is only necessary when pests are present or threat levels are high. If your crop is healthy and close to harvest, unnecessary spraying wastes money and puts chemicals on food you will soon eat.
ga: Dabi, be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ loo gbeyeishemɔ lɛ fa babaoo pɛ kɛkɛ ehe miihia ni afɔse tsofa lɛ. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ lɛ Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ fiteɔ shika ni ekɛ tsofai woɔ niyenii ni etsɛŋ ni obaaye lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to spray chemical pest medicine on my crops right before I harvest them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani akpa?

english: No, chemicals need time to break down safely. If you spray too close to harvest day, dangerous residues remain on the produce, making it unsafe for humans or animals to consume.
ga: Dabi, tsofai lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfiteɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie shi ni ebɛŋkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ gbi lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Oshara nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ baakã nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa adesai loo kooloi aye.

english: What immediate steps should I take if I notice caterpillars eating my maize?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ ŋmeii miiye mi-abele lɛ?

english: You should apply a recommended pest control product specifically targeted for caterpillars or armyworms. Applying it early in the morning or late evening gives the best results because that is when the pests come out to feed.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɔɔ asraafoi loo asraafoi ahe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nakai beaŋ ji be ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo amɛtaoɔ niyenii.

english: Where can I get safe and effective products to protect my crops from armyworms?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mahe nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: You can obtain approved pest control products from registered agricultural input dealers or directly through government extension officers who will ensure you get the right chemical for your specific crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nibii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ajalɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. loo kɛtsɔ nɔyeli lɛ hiɛyaa nitsulɔi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baaha ona tsofai ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that makes plants green and strong. This often happens when heavy rains wash the soil food away or when the soil is worn out from planting every year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe waɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ afi dumɔ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce soft, empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods stay empty when the soil lacks calcium, which the plant needs specifically to build the nut inside the shell. Adding lime or wood ash to your farm soil before planting helps the pods fill up fully.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ efolo kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa pɔtɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso ashwishwɛ fata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the top stems of my cassava plants before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cassava lɛ yiteŋ dani makpa?

english: Cutting the top leaves forces the cassava plant to stop spending its energy making tall branches and leaves, directing all its energy down into the ground to make the cassava tubers grow bigger and heavier.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ koni ekpa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ niji kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water. When the plant feels stressed by heat, it drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Be mli ni tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiihao kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juice, or by a virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still tiny on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo beni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo yɛ tso ko shishi lɛ?

english: Very small cocoa pods often turn black and dry up because of a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops pods it cannot feed, or because a fungal disease called black pod has attacked them during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ hewɔ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwie shi kɛyashi amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Aloo akɛni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ tutuaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand deep underground; building high mounds keeps the soil soft and well-drained so the tuber can grow long, thick, and smooth without getting blocked by hard earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiii amɛnaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down during strong winds and heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the top of the ground and do not go deep into the earth, making heavy bunches easily pull the whole stem out of soft, wet soil unless you support them with wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Feemɔ ŋmeii ni tsii, ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Ja okɛ tso fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do citrus trees grown from seed take many years to produce fruit compared to grafted ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ citrus tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trees grown directly from seeds spend 7 to 10 years just growing big and mature like a child, whereas grafted seedlings come from branches of adult trees that are already mature and ready to bear fruit in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baahe afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛdara ni amɛdara tamɔ gbekɛ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso ni eda lɛ niji amli lɛ daa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to stop losing water through the leaves, going to sleep above ground while safely keeping its tubers fresh underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛkpa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. ni oyawɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding on the undersides of the leaves. Removing weeds around the field and applying recommended organic or mild insect sprays helps stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo nɔ ni bɛ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is a lack of pollinators. Watering regularly at the roots and protecting plants from extreme heat during flowering helps fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etswaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air circulate, alongside removing diseased pods immediately, protects healthy pods from catching it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛfata he ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baabu ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ahe koni akamɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are producing good tubers underground if I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii kpakpai? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mana hu?

english: As cassava tubers swell below the ground, the main stems at the base become thick and sturdy, and you will often see small cracks or bulges in the soil right around the base of the plant.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ Tso titri ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni etse. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tswaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to manufacture food for big tubers. Staking also lifts leaves off the ground, protecting them from soil-borne diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why do my crops produce less harvest when I plant the exact same crop on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases accumulate in the land. Rotating different crops, such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize, gives the soil time to replenish.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha oná be ni okɛ shikpɔŋ afata he.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not when heavy downpours are expected, as floodwater will wash it off. Applying early in the morning or late afternoon into damp soil ensures the roots absorb it quickly.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni akpaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ lɛ. ejaakɛ nu afua lɛ baaho kɛya Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in the ground fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are old, buried too deep in dry soil, or eaten by ants and soil insects before sprouting. Using quality certified seeds and planting them at shallow depth in moist soil improves germination.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ. Afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli tsɔ Aloo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ana he odaseyeli tsu nii ni adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your plants get all the food and water needed to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, sũ mli nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to grow green and strong. This usually happens when the soil nutrients have been washed away by heavy rain or exhausted from continuous farming without adding manure or fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ haa efiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ masɛi kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. The tall wooden sticks lift the vine leaves up into the air and sunlight, preventing leaf diseases on the ground and helping the tuber under the soil grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Tsoi kakadaji woɔ wain tsei ahe baai kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la mli. Etsiɔ baa helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: How do groundnuts manage to produce nuts under the soil when the flowers grow above ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flower is pollinated in the air, the plant sends out a long stem called a peg that bends downward and pushes itself right into the soil. Once buried inside the earth, the tip of that stem expands to form the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmeii fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afu lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ Tso lɛ naagbee lɛ mli lɛɛɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why can sorghum survive the long dry season in Northern Ghana much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deep roots that dig far into the earth to find water, and its leaves can roll up tight to trap moisture during intense heat. Unlike maize, sorghum can temporarily stop growing during severe drought and start growing again as soon as rain falls.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Sorghum baanyɛ akpa shweremɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebɔi edamɔ ekoŋŋ. ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like they need water. When water stays logged in the soil for too long without draining away, it chokes the roots and creates the right environment for soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and making the bush look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha jwɛi lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking the plant's juice, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Treating the insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kooloi bibii ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme temperature stress, either too much hot afternoon sun or dry winds, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flower. Giving the soil steady moisture and light shade helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa. Kɛji eji shwane mli hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi. Enɛ haaa pollen lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die quickly if there are no plantains or forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ plantains loo koo ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa plants the gentle shade and cool humidity they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get tiny holes in them before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Dani makpa nii po

english: The small holes in cowpea pods are made by pod-boring caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by small moths on the flowers. The caterpillars eat through the outer skin to feed on the sweet young seeds inside before you get the chance to harvest them.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ koni amɛye dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani oná hegbɛ ni okpa.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded land while maize dies if flooded for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shi ŋmãa gboɔ kɛji nu eyi mli obɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that carry air down from the leaves directly into the roots underwater. Maize plants do not have these air tubes, so their roots drown and rot quickly when submerged in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry periods usually mean the cocoa tree is stressed from excessive heat and water shortage. Providing shade trees and spreading dry grass or leaves around the base helps retain soil moisture and protect the roots from heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ha ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding balanced compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, encouraging fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in the same soil where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, while beans and cowpeas naturally feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and putting it back into the earth. Rotating these crops keeps your soil fertile and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them survive hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around your crops acts like a protective blanket over the ground. It stops the sun from drying out the dirt quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Nibii ni adu lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaaa muji akagbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants adapted to suck up water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow lots of big leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and large leaves instead of tubers. Sweet potatoes need balanced nutrients, particularly potassium, to swell their underground roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo bulbs. Niyenii ni ja he miihia ŋmɔtɔ. titri lɛ potassium ni haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ

english: How do shade trees help young cocoa seedlings survive in their first year?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily scorch in harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the air humid and protecting young crops until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard. You can also look for a tiny dark mark at the base of the grain where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Obaanyɛ otao okadii diji bibii hu. Yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do the broad leaves of my plantain trees tear so easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are designed to tear along their veins during strong winds as a safety mechanism. This reduces wind resistance so the main stem does not snap, protecting the heavy fruit cluster underneath.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ koni amɛgbala amɛfãji lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli akɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ gbɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ baa shi. koni akakumɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ aduawai akuu ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because hot direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root systems are strong enough to search for water deep underground.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ ahe waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtao nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I let many small shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ Babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around the mother plant, they compete for the same food and water in the soil, leaving the main plant with less energy to form a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize plants need to build strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as free natural food that helps your maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot removes the specific food maize needs from the soil and allows pests that attack maize to build up in the ground from year to year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ejieɔ abɛi niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi.

english: How do I know which way to point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni afeɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei nine awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the small buds on the stem where old leaves used to be and plant them with the buds pointing upward toward the sky, so the shoots do not spend energy trying to grow out from upside down.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni tsutsu lɛ eji baa momo lɛ nɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards; building high mounds gives the roots plenty of room to grow deep, long, and fat without struggling against hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara amɛmli, amɛlɛ, ni amɛfee loo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa abɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants curl up and fall off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or tiny insects like thrips sucking the juice from the flower stems.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni miinu nu ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants wrinkling and curling inward like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee mli tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaf sap and spread plant diseases that distort normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or old leaves during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai momo yɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant materials keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a vital nutrient the plant needs to stay green and build healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do elders in my village recommend planting beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acts like a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural parasols, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli parasol. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui ni amɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛ hi shi.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun, allowing them to capture maximum light to make food, which leads to bigger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ kane babaoo kɛ́ amɛmiihoo nii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: If you leave too many suckers, they fight with the main plant for water and soil food, which results in small, weak plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ena nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops end up thin and weak if I scatter seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji migbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together compete aggressively with each other for limited root space, soil nutrients, and sunlight, causing all of them to remain undersized.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha shishifãi fioo. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry conditions cause severe water stress inside the tomato plant, forcing it to drop its blossoms to conserve water and survive.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi wo mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shields the topsoil from direct heat, stops water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the root area cool and moist.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Soggy, waterlogged soil cuts off air to the cassava roots, smothering them and creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli, ni emɔɔ amɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmei helai abatutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars burrow deep inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifo mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms seek out the soft center leaves because they are tender, protected from predators, and filled with rich nutrients the young plant is creating.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ baatao baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe ni eyi kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni tsei bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and dry winds. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains or shade trees, to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil cool while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth cycle helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why is my cassava producing a lot of tall branches and leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or when plants are spaced too closely, the cassava focuses its energy on leaf growth instead of storing food in its root tubers. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage bigger tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil moisture during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist using mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛ mulch tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam leaves require maximum sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking exposes leaves to sunlight, keeps them off the damp ground, and reduces exposure to soil-borne diseases and pests.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ. ni eha helai kɛ kooloi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insect pests early stops the leaf damage and keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni ji helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Ayeɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ anɔ mra Ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and decomposes, it releases this natural nutrient into the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛgboi Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant maize and beans together in the same farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and beans makes full use of space and light. The tall maize provides structure, while the lower beans shade the soil to reduce weeds and add vital nitrogen back into the soil, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi kɛ la tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi ni kɛlɛ haa shishitoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii 2 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or dried leaves on the soil around my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weed seeds from growing, and cools the roots of your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa ni ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Should I cut off the dry and spotted lower leaves from my plantain trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pruning old and diseased plantain leaves improves air flow around the plant and prevents diseases like Black Sigatoka from spreading to healthy green leaves that feed the growing plantain bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain baai ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa helai tamɔ sigatoka diŋ lɛ agbɛ ashwã baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fiɔ plantain tsei akui ni miida lɛ asɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Maize plants need rich soil nutrients like nitrogen to stay green and healthy. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks plant food, the crops starve, turn yellow, and become easy targets for diseases.
ga: Abɛi tsei hia shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebatsɔ nɔ ni helai baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya

english: Why do some of my tomato plants get sick with diseases while others nearby stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiye helai yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Just like people, crops with good nutrition and strong roots are better at fighting off sickness. Plants growing in poor soil or crowded spots get stressed and catch diseases much faster than well-nourished ones.
ga: same as humans Nibii ni aduɔ ni niyenii kpakpa kɛ shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ haoɔ ni amɛheɔ helai oya fe tsei ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper crops perform worse every time I plant them in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil continuously drains all the specific nutrients that crop loves and lets disease-causing germs build up in the ground, making future crops weak.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ajɛ mli. ni eha helai ni kɛ hela baa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for food, water, and sunlight. When crowded, individual plants become weak and produce much smaller tubers than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ. Tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo bulb bibii fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops grow slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-vegetables lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves in your farm. They aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your plants hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Shi otsei lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do wild plants in the bush grow green and thick without fertilizer, but my farm crops struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ? Shi ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ?

english: In the wild, rotting leaves constantly fall to feed the soil naturally. On a farm, harvesting crops removes those nutrients, so you must add fertilizer or manure back into the soil to feed the plants.
ga: Yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, baai ni egboi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas that keep the air cool and conserve moisture in the soil for the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei bibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and slowly rots into natural food for the crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer to the soil on the very first day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny seedlings cannot consume a large amount of fertilizer at once, and heavy rain will wash it away before they grow big. Giving fertilizer in small split doses ensures food is available as the plant grows.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛdara. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaaha yɛ fioo mli Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ahi shi be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why should I prune or trim away some of the extra side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches stops the plant from wasting food and energy on unnecessary stems and leaves, directing all its strength into producing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ efiteee niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when there are no big shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Without shade trees to cover them, the intense sun burns the tender leaves and dries out the moisture the plant needs to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my plantain trees grow very tall and thin when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are crowded, they compete for light. Each plant stretches upward as fast as it can to reach the sun, spending its energy on growing tall instead of building a thick, strong stem.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná la. Tso fɛɛ tso tsɔɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ hulu lɛ he. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during high heat to trap moisture inside and protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural way the crop copes with heat stress until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛkpeɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves turn yellow and drop off when heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water collects on the field for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking air in the soil. Without air, the roots cannot feed the plant properly, causing the leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ niyenii ni sa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open under the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ gbá yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when a sudden heavy rain follows a long dry spell. The sudden intake of water causes the inside of the tuber to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is my tomato plant producing plenty of bushy green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus all their strength on producing leaves and stems. To form flowers and fruits, the plant needs balanced nutrients with less nitrogen and more phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni baa lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni afee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni ja. ni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni eyɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium babaoo

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody instead of expanding into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs agboi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand when the soil is too hard or lacks loose organic matter. Hard soil prevents the roots from pushing outward, causing them to stay thin and tough.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any small peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its strength to keep the main stem alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli koni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my garden eggs or eggplants growing in bent, irregular shapes instead of smooth ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo eggplant lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ebɔle ehe ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Irregular shapes often happen when flowers are not fully pollinated by bees or when water supply changes drastically while the fruit is developing, causing one side of the fruit to grow faster than the other.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii kwraa. aloo be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ afã kome daa oya fe ekroko lɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons taste watery and plain instead of sweet when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ ŋɔɔ tamɔ nɔ ni nu kɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli moŋ fe nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Giving watermelons too much water right before harvest dilutes the sugars inside the fruit. Stopping heavy watering a week or two before harvest helps the sugars concentrate for a sweeter taste.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo watermelon mli fe nine dani akpa lɛ, ehaa sugar ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akpa nu ni akɛhaa lɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sugar lɛ feɔ ekome koni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl and turn yellow even when I water and care for them properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni esa akɛ awo nɔ nu ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: This often happens because tiny insects like whiteflies act as transport carriers. They feed on sick plants elsewhere, pick up microscopic bacterial germs like phytoplasma, and inject them into your healthy crops while sucking their sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛfaa. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ hei krokomɛi. Okɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii bibii tamɔ phytoplasma awo otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli be mli ni okɛ amɛ nu lɛ miinu.

english: Do insects harm my crops only by chewing on the leaves, or can they cause other hidden problems?
ga: Ani ŋmeii yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ naagbai krokomɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba?

english: Insects do more than just chew leaves; some act like mosquitoes by sucking plant juices and carrying bacterial diseases from infected plants directly into the fluid system of healthy plants.
ga: Kplukai feɔ babaoo fe baai ni amɛyeɔ. Henɔi komɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛnuɔ ni amɛwoɔ helai amli helatsɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is a plant disease spreading so quickly from one corner of my maize farm across the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela ko miigbɛ eshwa oya kɛmiijɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome nɔ kɛmiiya ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flying insects called vectors move continuously between crops. Every time an insect feeds on a sick plant, it picks up bacterial germs and carries them to the next healthy plant it lands on, spreading the disease rapidly.
ga: Koolooi ni foɔ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ vectors lɛ, nyiɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ be fɛɛ be. Be fɛɛ be ni kooloo ko baaye tso ni hela mɔ lɛ Eŋɔɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ekɛyaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. koni hela ashwã oya

english: If I leave a few diseased plants standing in my farm, will they really affect the healthy ones near them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi tsei fioo komɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Ani ebaana tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, leaving sick plants in the field creates a source of infection. Sap-sucking insects will feed on those infected plants, collect the disease germs inside them, and carry them directly to your nearby healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ yeɔ nakai tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ. Bua helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa yɛ amɛmli. ni otsɔɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Can wild bushes and weeds growing at the edge of my farm make my main crops get sick?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, many wild weeds act as hidden hosts for plant diseases. Insects feed on those infected weeds and then fly into your farm field, transferring bacterial germs onto your main crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, koo mli jwɛi babaoo tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsei ahelai teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ nakai jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Koni okɛ bacteria helai ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops continue to dry up and die even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lolo ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: When insects infect a plant with bacterial germs, the germs multiply inside the plant's internal tubes and block them. This stops water and nutrients from moving through the plant, regardless of how much fertilizer you apply.
ga: Kɛji kooloi kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ wo tsei amli lɛ Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa yɛ tsei lɛ amli tsɔnei lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafata he.

english: Will spraying my farm to kill small hopping bugs actually protect my crops from getting sick?
ga: Miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ koni mikɛgbe kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ Ani ebaabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hela he diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because killing these insect vectors stops them from moving between plants, which breaks the chain of transport that carries bacterial diseases from sick crops to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni agbeɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafã kɛya tsei ateŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ gbɛ ni kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli baa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why is it risky for me to take cassava or yam stems for planting from a neighbor's farm that had sick crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even if a stem looks healthy on the outside, insects may have already injected bacterial germs into it. When you plant that stem, the hidden disease will grow and infect your new field.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ, shi kooloi hu baanyɛ awo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ amli. Kɛ odu nakai tso lɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oyale hee lɛ mli.

english: Can insects carry diseases from my tomato garden to my pepper plants?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ ajie helai kɛjɛ mi-tomato abɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli?

english: Yes, many insect vectors feed on different types of crops. If an insect bites a diseased plant in your tomato bed, it can easily transport those same bacterial germs to your pepper plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii srɔtoi babaoo yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo. Kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ yɛ o-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ nakai kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ amli kɛya o-pepper tsei lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves show disease symptoms weeks after I first noticed insects flying around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jieɔ hela he okadii akpo yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ beni miyɔse kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: When insect vectors transport bacterial germs to a new plant, it takes time for the bacteria to multiply inside the plant's system before the physical signs of sickness appear on the leaves.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni gbeɔ helai lɛ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ tee tsei heei amli lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he hiaa be koni amɛshwere yɛ tso lɛ mli. Dani gbɔmɔtsoŋ hela he okadii baaje kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize stay green and produce larger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas feed the soil by pulling nitrogen out of the air and trapped roots, which leaves natural fertilizer in the ground that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas naa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ shishifãi ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Heavy rains and high dampness cause a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread fast. Trimming overcrowded branches lets sunlight and air dry out the trees, preventing the sickness.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbi. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ helai anaa

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf surface to suck the plant's juice, which spreads viruses that deform the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ shishi koni amɛmu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field for too long, the soil chokes the roots, causing them to drown and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why should I plant my seeds right after a major rain instead of during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe yɛ otsi ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds need wet soil to swell up and start growing. Planting in dry soil leaves the seed helpless, causing it to dry out and die before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ koni amɛfuu ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ nɔ ko amɛfee. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves high into the light and away from rotting ground conditions.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ la mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ kpaa gbee.

english: Extremely hot weather or a sudden lack of water stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save water instead of spending energy forming fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds are allowed to stay, they steal food away from your plants, leaving them weak.
