ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli. ha egbɔjɔ

english: Why do my young cashew trees drop many of their blossoms before producing nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cashew trees often drop early blossoms because they are not yet mature enough to nourish full nuts, or because tiny insects called thrips are damaging the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ mra ejaakɛ amɛdarako bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Aloo yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ thrips lɛ miifite fɔfɔi.

english: How deep should I bury crop seeds in the soil when I am planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds need to be planted at a specific depth—usually about twice their size—so they stay moist enough to sprout without wasting all their stored energy trying to push through too much soil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ waa. (bei pii lɛ, amɛdalɛ feɔ aaafee shii enyɔ) koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi babaoo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ be naa po lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they were stored in hot places, buried too deeply, or if the soil lacks enough moisture to wake the seed up from its resting state.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo la mli, ni afu amɛ tsɔ, loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashi wɔɔhe.

english: What should I look out for when selecting good seeds to start a new crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kɛ́ mihala dumɔwui kpakpai ni mikɛbaaje ŋmɔshi nibii hee shishi?

english: Good seeds should be firm, undamaged, free from pests or mold, and ideally sourced from certified extension centers to ensure high germination rates.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni efiteee, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli. Ni esa akɛ ahe amɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ akɛ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛshwere babaoo.

english: Why do oil palm trees take several years before they start giving fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their early years building strong roots and thick trunks to support heavy fruit bunches later, so they need time to establish before producing yield.
ga: Mu tsei yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni baaye abua aduawai akui ni tsii sɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ be dani atswaa dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell when my crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as fruits changing color, leaves drying up, or palm nuts naturally dropping from the bunch.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ amɛfee klalo, tamɔ aduawai ni amɛhe su etsake, baai ni egbi, loo tso yibii ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster during certain months and slowly in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ekrokomɛi amli lɛ edaa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Crop growth speeds up with adequate rain and sunshine during the wet season, and slows down during cooler or drier periods to conserve water.
ga: Tsei daa oya kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni efee blɛoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of natural aging or disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Natural aging affects only the oldest bottom leaves as the plant grows, whereas disease usually causes spots, curling, or sudden yellowing on newer leaves.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ saa baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa trukaa.

english: What basic steps do I need to take before starting a new crop farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee dani mabɔi tsei ahe ŋmɔ hee?

english: Starting a farm requires clearing weeds, testing soil quality, choosing healthy seed stock, and timing your planting with the beginning of the rainy season.
ga: Okwaafoi ashishijee biɔ ni ajie jwɛi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ he kaa Dumɔwui kpakpai ni ahala ni ato be ni akɛbaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: How long can I keep harvested palm fruits before they lose quality for oil extraction?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ mi-palm yibii ni akpa lɛ ahi shi dani ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mu ni ajieɔ lɛ mli?

english: Palm fruits begin to ferment within a few days of harvest, which increases oil acidity and lowers quality, so processing should happen as quickly as possible.
ga: Palm yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ mli acidity lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ehilɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afee privatisation oya bɔ ni aaanyɛ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested crops raw or process them into products first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo mafee lɛ nɔ ko klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Processing crops—like turning palm nuts into palm oil—increases their shelf life and market value, bringing higher profits than selling fresh produce immediately.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ, tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ awoɔ ŋmei fɔ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei shihilɛ kɛ jarayeli jara yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ baa fe nibii heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm feel so hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa waa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard and compacted when left exposed to hot sun and heavy rains, or when heavily walked on. Without enough plant cover or organic material, the soil particles press tightly together, making it hard for crop roots to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kɛ́ anyiɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ baakpɛtɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃

english: How can I tell if my land is too poor to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ohia tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Signs of poor land include soil that hardens easily, water standing on the surface without sinking in, yellowing crop leaves, and plants that remain small or fail to fruit well despite proper watering.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji shikpɔŋ ni ais feɔ fɛ̃i oya. Nu hiɔ shi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ ni efoŋ, tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii loo amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ po.

english: How can I loosen hard soil so my crop roots can spread easily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo?

english: You can soften compacted soil by adding animal manure or compost, keeping crop residue on the ground as mulch, and planting cover crops to protect the soil surface from baking in the sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ afee blɛoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will leaving very wide spaces between my crop plants help them yield better?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛná yibii kpakpai?

english: Not necessarily. Spacing plants too far apart leaves large areas of bare soil exposed to direct sunlight and rain, which bakes the soil hard and promotes weed growth. Following recommended spacing protects the soil while giving crops enough room.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Gbɛ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo afee nɔ ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ daa. Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa gbɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my young maize plants growing so slowly and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Slow growth usually happens when roots cannot penetrate hard, compacted soil or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Loosening the soil before planting and providing proper plant food helps crops grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji shishifãi nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ mli. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ dani aduɔ nii kɛ tsei niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: What can I do to help my maize mature faster so I can harvest and sell it quickly?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni eye ebua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ oya koni anyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya?

english: To get a fast yield, plant in well-loosened soil, maintain proper plant spacing to preserve moisture, and apply fertilizer early so the young plants have immediate access to nutrients.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná nibii ni anáa oya Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi tsei lɛ ateŋ koni hulutsoo ahi shi. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi Koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant other crops in the open spaces between my main crop?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ he ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting suitable crops between rows helps shade the ground, prevents soil from becoming hard and compacted, suppresses weeds, and gives you extra food or income from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni sa ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waaa ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni ehaa onáa niyenii loo shika kroko kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why is my maize not producing full cobs even though I planted it to make quick cash?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛɛɛ kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ adu koni aná shika oya moŋ?

english: Maize requires nutrient-rich soil and good moisture to produce full cobs. If the soil is poor or compacted, the roots cannot collect enough food and water to form good grain, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ aba. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ abua niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛwo dumɔwui kpakpai. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: How does leaving open ground between my crops affect my harvest?
ga: Te gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Bare ground absorbs heat directly from the sun, which dries out moisture fast and hardens the earth. This restricts root movement and reduces overall harvest yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi oya ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Can I grow maize alongside longer-term crops to earn money while waiting for the main harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmãa titri lɛ?

english: Yes, growing fast-maturing crops like maize alongside slow-growing main crops allows you to earn quick income early on, provided the soil has enough fertility to support both plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ abele yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika oya mra. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsei bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ sũ mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by sap-sucking insects or armyworms. Checking under the leaves helps identify if pests are present so you can apply the right organic or chemical treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu loo asraafoi amli ŋmeii etutua lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi yɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai fee lɛ atsu nii bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot mostly when planted in waterlogged soil with poor drainage, or when infected by fungal root diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and protects the tubers from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ lɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miikwɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, during dry spells, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and adding balanced compost or fertilizer help flowers stay on and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Aloo, kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo tomato.

english: What happens if I bury my maize seeds too deep in the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too deep, a seed burns through all its stored energy before the shoot reaches the surface, leading to weak plants or seeds failing to sprout at all. Planting at a depth of 3 to 5 centimeters ensures quick and healthy germination.
ga: dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui shãa amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo dumɔwui ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ fe sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains before planting my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam seed tubers need reliable soil moisture to break dormancy and sprout roots. If planted in hot, dry soil, the heat can bake and rot the tuber pieces before the rain comes to trigger growth.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛfo ŋmiŋmi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani nugbɔ baanyɛ aha amɛdara.

english: Why does my farmland yield less harvest every year when I plant maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and rot at the stem base shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This issue is caused by a soil fungal condition called damping-off, which thrives when nursery beds are overwatered and overcrowded. Spacing seeds out and avoiding excess water improves air movement and protects young stems.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening, ni baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ nu eyi ŋmɔji akwɛmɔhei lɛ amli fe nine ni amɛyi obɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ amli gbalamɔ kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder and get infested with insects in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ feɔ powder ni helai ewo mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils that multiply rapidly in grains that were not dried completely. Storing thoroughly dried maize in airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps the grain safe.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwereɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa ni egbiko kwraa lolo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives crop roots enough space and nutrients to establish strong growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees or plantains shield young cocoa from intense sun and heat, keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ loo plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruits start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened underground by pests like nematodes or waterlogging. Supporting the stem with a wooden prop stick and mounding soil around the base gives the tree the structural support it needs to hold heavy bunches.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ nematodes loo nu mli ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli kɛ muji ni abua naa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, which stops the fungus from destroying your yield.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii afite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil during long rain periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa he ni agbele lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off hot, wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and results in much larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu lɛ nɔ ni amɛyaaa hei ni edɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need for leafy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores green color and vigor to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly ensures each maize plant gets enough food to grow tall and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water. Keeping the soil moist and mulching around the roots protects the plant from heat stress so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo he. Shishifãi lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. koni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning stiff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by leaf curl virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by severe water stress. Protecting young plants from pests and keeping watering consistent helps prevent curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa ji leaf curl hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local soil and weather, meaning their seeds germinate immediately at the first sign of water. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients meant for your newly planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ edumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nu he okadi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ba. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛha tsei ni odu ehee lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Just like people need proper food to stay strong, plants need extra plant food, like fertilizer or compost, to produce healthy green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Taakɛ niyenii ni sa he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei hu taoɔ tsei niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni afee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cassava tubers so small even though the crop has been in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: If weeds grow around your cassava, they steal the nutrients and water from the soil before the crop can get them. When cassava is starved of soil food, it cannot grow large roots or tubers.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ o-cassava lɛ he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná. Beni ŋmei bɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi wuji loo bulbs.

english: Is it better to start my pepper seeds in a small sheltered nursery before moving them into my main field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooobɔi pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli? He ko ni mahi dani mafã kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Yes, starting delicate seeds in a shaded nursery box keeps young seedlings safe from heavy rain and direct harsh sun. Once the young plants grow strong stems, they can handle the open field much better.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaaje shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli adeka ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tso ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ etsu ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do high-yielding tomato seeds I brought from town fail to grow well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛba lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: New seed varieties brought from outside are not automatically used to your local soil and climate. They require special attention, proper soil preparation, regular watering, and fertilizer to settle in and produce good yields.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni akɛba kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baakɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ daa koni ehi shi ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain shoots grow tall and thin without producing heavy bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii ni tsii bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for nutrients in the dirt while their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Giving each plant proper space ensures every shoot gets enough food and light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ ŋmei naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does leaving grass and weeds around my crops hurt their growth?
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigba enaa edalɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like unwanted guests that eat your crop's food. They absorb the water and soil nutrients meant for your crops, causing your crops to stay small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ ni yeɔ otsei lɛ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha onibii. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose water rapidly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa trees until they grow old enough to withstand the strong sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ebuɔ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defence to protect itself from losing too much water in extreme heat. The plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni cilantro tso lɛ buɔ ehe koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: How does mixing animal manure into sandy soil help my vegetables survive dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Organic materials like manure and decomposed leaves act like a sponge in the soil. They hold onto rainwater and plant food for a long time so your crops can keep drinking even when it hasn't rained for days.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛtoɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ aya nɔ anu nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo po.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that particular plant loves out of the soil. Rotating your maize with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to rest and restores lost nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build healthy leaves. When the soil is low on nitrogen or heavy rain washes it away, the plant moves food to its newest top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ eniyenii lɛ kɛyaa baa hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Heat stress causes the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Heat haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the juices. This damages the leaf tissue and forces the leaves to fold up tightly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ shishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ he okadi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni enyɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ koni ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes right in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests, often called Fall Armyworms, target the tender central leaves of maize to feed on growing tissue. If they eat the core of the plant, it prevents the maize from growing tall and producing cobs.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛye fãji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ amɛye tso lɛ mli fã lɛ Ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sun because their tender leaves dry out easily. Planting shade crops like plantains next to cocoa trees acts like an umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and keeping soil moisture in.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Yam plants need as much sunlight as possible on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves capture light better, stay free from ground pests, and help produce bigger roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Ebɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa shishifãi wuji

english: Why should I space my maize seeds out instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he ko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing makes sure every plant gets enough room and nutrients to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it harmful if I drop fertilizer right against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer has concentrated salts that pull moisture out of living plant tissues. Placing it directly touching the stem causes 'fertilizer burn', which damages the stem and can destroy the root system.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ekɛ ‘fertilizer burn’ baa ni efiteɔ tso lɛ ni ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava field produce plenty of tall leaves but tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai kakadaji babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrition produces large cassava tubers rather than just top leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa moŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai kɛkɛ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots in the soil, it leaves behind free plant food for the maize planted after it.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaashi tsei niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How many bunches of plantain can one person typically harvest from a farm in a single day?
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, plantains ŋmɔji enyiɛ mɔ kome baanyɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ gbi kome mli?

english: A single healthy worker can usually cut about 10 to 15 bunches of plantain a day on their own, as harvesting involves carefully cutting the heavy bunches, carrying them, and clearing the surrounding foliage so young shoots are not damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitsulɔ kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afo plantains 10 kɛyashi 15 daa gbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni fata ŋmaakpamɔ he ji tsei ni afolɔ waa. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ awo mli ni ojie baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafite ŋmeii bibii lɛ

english: If I enter a shared farming agreement with a landowner to grow plantains, how is the harvest normally split in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ fee okwaayeli he kpaŋmɔ ko koni makwɛ plantains lɛ Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ajaa ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, shared farming often uses customary systems like Abunu (split 50/50) or Abusa (split 1/3 to 2/3), where the harvested crops or profits are shared with the landowner according to the terms agreed upon before planting.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli ni akɛ he woɔ mli lɛ kɛ kusum gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ Abunu (50/50 mlijaa) loo Abusa (1/3 kɛyashi 2/3 mlijaa) tsuɔ nii, ni no haa akɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ jaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo sɛɛnamɔi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni amɛkpɛlɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: If I am managing a plantain farm with a partner, how should we organize the work during harvest time?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mihefatalɔ ko kwɛɔ plantain ŋmɔ ko nɔ lɛ Te esa akɛ wɔto wɔnitsumɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ wɔha tɛŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Harvesting works best as a team effort where one partner cuts the heavy plantain bunches from the tree while the other catches or carries them to a collection point to prevent the fruit from bruising on the ground.
ga: Ashɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ akɛ kuu. Fã kome ŋmɔ plantain babaoo kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni mɔ kroko lɛ mɔɔ amɛ loo ekɛ amɛ yaa he ni abuaa amɛnaa yɛ lɛ koni aduawai lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ.

english: Does a plantain stem produce fruit more than once, or do I have to cut it down after harvesting?
ga: Ani plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fe shikome loo esa akɛ mafolɔ amɛ kɛji akpa amɛ?

english: A single plantain stem only produces fruit once in its lifetime. Once you cut down the stem to harvest the bunch, that stem dies, but young shoots (suckers) growing from the underground base will take over and produce the next crop.
ga: Dumɔwu kome baawo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala shihilɛ mli. Kɛji ofo tso lɛ shishi koni okpa ŋmei lɛ Tso lɛ baagbo, shi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishi lɛ baaye egbɛhe ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I see so many small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, which are the plant's natural way of reproducing. However, if you leave too many, they steal water and nutrients from the main plant, so you should prune them to leave only 2 or 3 strong shoots.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Shi, kɛji oshi babaoo lɛ, Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tso lɛ mli ni eshɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong wind and heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and very heavy tops, especially when bearing fruit. Without proper soil mounding around the base or support poles placed under heavy bunches, strong winds can easily pull the entire plant out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ewo yibii Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo sɛɛfimɔ tsei ni akɛwo jwɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain plant turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Old lower leaves naturally turn yellow and die as the plant directs energy to new leaves and the developing fruit bunch. However, if many leaves turn yellow rapidly, it can mean the plant needs nitrogen fertilizer or more moisture.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa baa heei kɛ aduawai niji ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Can I grow plantains together with other crops like cassava or cocoa on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, plantains grow very well alongside crops like young cocoa or cassava. Their broad leaves provide shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, making them an ideal nurse crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei bibii ahe. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfɔɔ bii.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when starting a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ ahe shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Plantain suckers should generally be planted about 3 meters (10 feet) apart. This spacing gives the broad leaves enough room to capture sun and ensures roots do not fight each other for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ akaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do I know when a plantain bunch is fully ready to be cut from the stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaafo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the fingers look full and plump, the sharp angle ridges on the fruit become rounded, and the dried flower tips at the ends of the fruit break off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni oniji tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ naagbee yɛ aduawai lɛ naagbee lɛ fãa mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape before the corn is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli dani abele lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the center, it means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant is moving available nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the growing top leaves and cob.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei miitsi niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my pepper and tomato flowers falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop when the plants experience severe heat or sudden water stress. If the soil goes from very dry to very wet, or if afternoon sun gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ Aloo kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava reaches full maturity, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a longer bare stem. You will also notice the soil around the base of the plant cracking as the expanding tubers push outward.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ashi tso ni kɛlɛ fe fɛɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ. Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni ŋmeii ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to make high soil mounds before planting yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down and require soft, loose soil to expand fully. Mounding gathers rich topsoil together, improves drainage so the seed yam does not rot in heavy rain, and allows the tuber to grow long and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛtaoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Gɔji buaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ anaa. improve drainage No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteee kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural self-defense against drought and heat. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which traps moisture and slows down water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it tired. Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the dark purple flower bell at the end of my plantain stalk once the last fingers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa fɔfɔi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ plantain tsei lɛ anaagbee lɛ beni naagbee inchi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Once the plantain hands have formed, the remaining flower bell consumes nutrients without producing any more fruits. Removing it directs all the plant's energy and water directly into plumping up the existing plantain fingers.
ga: Beni afeɔ plantains lɛ Fɔfɔi aŋmɛlɛtswai ni eshwɛ lɛ baafite niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha plantain niji ni yɔɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs than the original seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent lines to produce strong yields in the first generation only. The seeds saved from those crops lose that special vigor, leading to uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi akui enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ amli. Koni aná yibiiwoo ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly on a clean sheet before putting it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ wolo ni he tse nɔ dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storing maize while it still holds moisture creates a breeding ground for invisible molds that produce dangerous poisons like aflatoxin. Drying grains until they are hard prevents mold rot and keeps the crop safe for consumption and sale.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni anaaa ni jieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni aye ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the branches on my cocoa trees instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner parts of the tree. This gives the tree more energy to grow bigger, healthier cocoa pods instead of wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Will cutting back branches on my cocoa trees make them produce less crop?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo tso lɛ ni mafo lɛ baaha ewo yibii fioo?

english: In the short term, the tree may look smaller, but pruning actually increases your harvest over time by preventing diseases and encouraging the tree to produce more flowering pods.
ga: Yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni efee bibioo. Shi tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛtsɔ helai ni tsiɔ naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: What does proper farm management actually mean for a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Farm management means keeping up with regular maintenance like clearing weeds, pruning excess branches, treating pests early, and harvesting pods correctly so the soil and trees stay healthy for years.
ga: Okwaa nɔkwɛmɔ tsɔɔ daa saamɔ, tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ. niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Ajieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra ni akpaa ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: What causes small holes to appear in the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Small holes in the trunk are usually made by stem borer insects. These pests burrow into the stem wood, weakening the tree's structure and making it hard for food and water to move up from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ tsei akutsei amli. Ehaa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa ewaa akɛ niyenii kɛ nu baajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli aya ŋwɛi

english: Why does the outer bark on my cocoa trees look damaged and chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eshɛre lɛ?

english: Certain insects and caterpillars walk along the outside of the tree and eat the bark for food. Removing this outer layer strips the tree of its natural shield, leaving it vulnerable to rot and drying out.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii komɛi nyiɛɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ kponɔgbɛ fã nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: How can I tell if pests are eating my cocoa tree from the inside without cutting it open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiye kɛmiijɛ mli ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: Look closely at the trunk and branches for tiny holes that have wood dust or wet sticky sap dripping from them. These signs usually mean stem borer worms are tunneling inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona buji bibii. ni yɔɔ tso mli sũ loo latɛs ni mli ewo fɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ stem borers lɛ miifee tunnel yɛ mli.

english: Why is one of my cocoa trees suddenly drying up while the rest of the farm looks green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ eko egbi yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: A sudden drying tree often means stem borers have burrowed completely through the inner trunk, blocking water from reaching the top leaves and causing that specific tree to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso ni egbiɔ trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ ebote tso lɛ mligbɛ kwraa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ni eha nakai tso lɛ gbee shi.

english: How do I stop insects from crawling on my trees and eating the bark?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa ni amɛkaye tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: You can keep pests away by keeping the base of the tree clean from heavy weeds, removing dead wood where pests hide, and applying approved crop protection sprays recommended by your extension officer.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa kɛtsɔ otso lɛ shishi ni oooha ehe atse kɛjɛ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni egboi yɛ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. ni akɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii taakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ.

english: Can damaging the tree during harvest reduce how much cocoa I get next year?
ga: Ani tsei lɛ akpãtãmɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ baaha kookoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, if you tear off pods roughly instead of cutting them cleanly, you can ruin the flower cushion on the bark where future cocoa pods are supposed to grow for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo mli lɛ, Obaanyɛ ofite fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ he ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers pay trained service workers to handle pruning and harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi woɔ sɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ nyɔmɔ koni amɛfolɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛkpa amɛkpamɔ lɛ?

english: Hiring trained workers ensures that pruning is done without weakening the tree and harvesting is done without damaging future pod sites, which saves the farmer time and protects long-term yields.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ ni akɛ amɛ baatsu nii lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni afo tso lɛ mli ni ahaaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni abaanyɛ akpa nikpamɔ ni akpataaa wɔsɛɛ pod he lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ bɛ be babaoo, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa gives them shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa is strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds must point upwards toward the sky; planting stems upside down forces the plant to grow downwards first, which weakens it and reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ. loo fɔfɔii bibii ni shwieɔ shi Ebɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni aaakwɛ shi lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ shi kɛya shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha o-tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the roots. When vines trail on the ground, leaves get shaded and infected by soil diseases, resulting in much smaller yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ wain tsei lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ baamɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build green leaves and grow stem strength. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps green up the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛha tso lɛ shishi hewalɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does putting animal manure on my farm help my soil differently from buying bags of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli ni aheɔ lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly for one season, but animal manure improves the soil itself by building up organic matter. Manure helps sandy soil hold water longer during dry spells and keeps heavy clay soil loose so plant roots can breathe.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya kɛyashi be kome. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni etswaa lɛ nɔ. Manure yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Should I let all the small shoots grow around my main plantain tree, or should I cut some of them away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he loo esa akɛ mafo ekomɛi?

english: You should cut away most of the small shoots (suckers) and leave only one or two strong ones. If too many shoots grow around the mother plant, they compete for water and nutrients, causing the main plant to produce very small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo (ŋmeii), ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii komɛi miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Too mother plant Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii waa.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds from my farm when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have weak, short roots that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs to establish a strong root system.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Ehaa tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etswa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without fruiting when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying dry grass or leaves around the roots as mulch helps keep the plant cool and retains flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and fine powder inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda kpakpa ni yɔɔ mibaa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Spraying approved treatments directly into the central funnel of the plant early in the morning or late evening stops them before they destroy the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from under the leaves and transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or insecticidal soap prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ chili baa baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, scorching sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary living umbrellas and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Should I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes consistent. The first rain often leaves the deep soil dry underneath, which can scorch seeds if a sudden dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves your total yield from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni onáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow big in one section of my land but remain tiny and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Soil quality, depth, and water drainage vary across a single farm. Spreading compost or manure over the poor spots improves soil nutrients and helps all your crops grow uniformly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, emlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo hei ni ehiii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaye ebua onibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ nii lɛ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to cut for planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni afolɔ ni adu?

english: Select the thick middle section of a healthy, mature stem that is about 8 to 12 months old. Avoid the soft green tip at the top and the woody base at the bottom, as the middle portion sprouts the strongest roots.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli tse lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main plantain tree to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to feed the tuber growing under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to light and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa eshɛɔ la he ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms during periods of extreme heat or when the soil gets too dry. Regular watering during dry spells keeps the plants cool and protects the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hidden inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa? ni akɛtee mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments into the central leaf funnels prevents them from destroying your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop because of long dry spells, sap-sucking insects like mirids, or poor pollination. Giving the young trees shade, managing pests early, and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ iris, loo ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ ahewɔ. Tsei bibii lɛ ahe hulutsoo ni akɛhaa Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the middle usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turning black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often because of irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or an recommended pesticide gets rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the ground. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil so your next crops grow much better.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and split during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up during dry hot weather to protect themselves from losing water. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and retains moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nu egbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand downward without hindrance. High mounds keep the soil soft and free of standing water, preventing the seed yam from rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu shwieee nɔ. Etsiɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with small harvests. Proper spacing gives every plant room to yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsu fɛɛ tsu ni miida lɛ ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my young crops grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks gives your young plants all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops inside my plastic crop shelter get so hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ plastic tsei ahe shĩa lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plastic sheets trap heat inside the structure just like a covered pot on a fire. Without proper air vents or cooling nets, hot air builds up quickly and can burn or stress your plants.
ga: Plastic wolo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tamɔ tsɛnsi ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni sa loo ŋmeii ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli jɔɔ lɛ bɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ loo ehao lɛ.

english: What should I do if the plastic cover on my crop house is trapping too much heat?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji plastic ni akɛhaa mi-greenhouse lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ babaoo mli?

english: You can remove some of the plastic and replace it with breathable netting to allow hot air to escape and bring in fresh air for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie plastic lɛ eko ni okɛ tsɔne ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba onibii amli.

english: Can I replace the plastic covering on my crop structure with a net to cool my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋshɔŋlooi atsake plastic ni akɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i?

english: Yes, swapping plastic covers for netting lets air flow freely through the structure, which drops the internal temperature and keeps your crops cool.
ga: Hɛɛ, plastic ni akɛhaa tsɔne lɛ najiaŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are insects still getting inside my crop house even though I installed a shade net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-greenhouse lɛ mli lolo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ shade net lɛ ewo?

english: Shade nets are designed to reduce sunlight, so their holes are often too large to block tiny insects from crawling inside and damaging your crops.
ga: Afee shade netting koni hulu la lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋtayaai amli buji lɛ daraa tsɔ ni amɛhaŋ kooloi bibii akabote mli ni amɛfite onibii.

english: Does a regular shade net protect my crops from insect pests?
ga: Ani shade netting baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Not necessarily. Shade nets mainly block the sun, so if the mesh gaps are wide, insects can easily pass through and ruin your harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Shade nets babaoo tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ mesh gap lɛ mli lɛɛ, kooloi hu baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛfite onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose a net that keeps insects from ruining my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋshɔŋlooi ni baaha kooloi akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Look for specialized insect netting with very tiny mesh holes designed specifically to block small pests, rather than general shade nets with wide gaps.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ shade net ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii.

english: What will happen to my crops if the holes in my protective netting are too large?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ bu ni yɔɔ mihebuu ŋshɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dara tsɔ?

english: If the netting holes are too large, destructive insects will easily enter the shelter, feed on your crops, and destroy your yield despite having a cover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mesh bu lɛ da tsɔ lɛ, Kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ boteɔ hei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ oya. ye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okpãtã oŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ kɛji oyɛ nɔ ni okɛhaa ohe po.

english: Why is seed netting better than clear plastic for protecting young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ahe tsɔne ni hi fe plastic ni mli tse ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Seed netting allows air and gentle moisture to reach young seeds while preventing excessive heat buildup, whereas plastic can easily overheat and damage tender shoots.
