ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. Shi plastic lɛ, ebaanyɛ edɔ fe nine ni efite ŋmeii bibii lɛ oya.

english: Is it a good idea to cover my plastic crop shelter with an extra layer of netting?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ ŋshɔŋloo kroko baaha mi plastic ŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, combining protective netting over a plastic frame can help manage airflow, provide extra shade, and add a barrier against pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ fata plastic lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ha hulutsoo be kroko ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hebuu afata he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: How can I fix a plastic crop structure so it stays cool while still keeping bugs out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake plastic ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ koni eha edɔ shi loloolo lɛ, ŋmeii akabote mli?

english: You can replace parts of the hot plastic with fine-mesh insect netting, which allows cool air to blow through while keeping even the smallest bugs outside.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi bibii ni mli edɔ lɛ ato plastic ni mli edɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii po nyɛɛɛ abote mli.

english: What is the main difference between growing yellow maize and white maize on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Yellow maize contains extra nutrients like Vitamin A that are good for family health and poultry feed, while white maize is traditionally used for local food like banku and kenkey. Both grow similarly under the same soil conditions, but yellow maize often has higher demand from feed manufacturers.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni fata he tamɔ vitamin A, ni hi kɛha weku hewalɛnamɔ kɛ kooloi aniyenii yɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa mli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ akɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ banku kɛ kenkie mli. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ kome nɔ. Shi ŋmãa ni ji yellow lɛ ji nɔ ni mɛi ni feɔ kooloi aniyenii lɛ taoɔ babaoo.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ ema he odase lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and produce uniform, high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over generations and can pass down diseases from the previous season, leading to weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow before the crop is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the plants back their green color and keeps them growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbaa lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the hot afternoon is a defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, saving water from evaporating until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, will I harvest more cassava?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani makpaa ŋmei babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots to expand fully, producing big, heavy tubers instead of many thin, weak roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Efeɔ yitso agbo ni tsii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the big trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeping the soil moist during dry spells.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground. Planting cowpeas after maize naturally restores soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ, heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Cowpeas ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it does not wash away in the rain?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Moist soil helps the plant roots absorb the nutrients quickly before heavy rains can sweep the fertilizer away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaafee nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the deep middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli?

english: Holes in the center of young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl. Treating the plants early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars come out to feed is most effective.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ atsa tsei leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I weed or dig around my groundnut plants once they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi loo mifoɔ sũ ni bɔle mi-peanut tsei lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants send small pegs down into the soil to form the actual nuts underground. Digging or weeding near the stems at this stage breaks these pegs and stops the nuts from developing.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ atsa loo ajie jwɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaakumɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ekpa ŋmei lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay alive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce very little food when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all of them to stay weak and small.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni efeɔ bibioo.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific food nutrients that crop prefers from the soil, while allowing soil pests and diseases that attack that plant to build up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the surface of the land before the plant roots have time to drink it in, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, severe lack of water, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. nu efo mli waa loo tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rain flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for days, it suffocates the roots and causes them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu lɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot stems growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong shoots allows the main tree to focus its energy on growing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niji wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni abɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by viral sicknesses passed on by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ehaa shade kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to circulate, which dries out moisture on the pods and reduces fungal growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni efɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: I found small worms eating deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the growing centers of maize. Applying recommended biological or chemical controls into the funnel of the plant early in the morning helps protect the maize foliage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni abua naa ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same land afterward, the maize feeds on this stored natural fertilizer and grows much stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ato nɛɛ ni ebaada waa babaoo.

english: Is it better to burn dry bush cleared from my land or leave it on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi ni ajie kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut weeds and leaves on top of the soil creates mulch, which keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during dry spells, and turns into rich organic manure as it decays. Burning destroys these nutrients and bakes the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai ni afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛji efite. Shãa fiteɔ nɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ shãa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground, and heavy bunches make the plant top-heavy. Removing extra suckers (shoot branches) and propping up heavy fruiting stems with strong wooden poles prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni niji ni tsii baaha tso lɛ atsii waa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ahe ŋmeii (niji) ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tuber energy through their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground toward sunlight, maximizing photosynthesis and preventing leaf diseases caused by sitting on wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Ha fotosintɛsis aya hiɛ ni otsi baa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ shitaramɔ mli baa lɛ naa

english: Why do I need to clear tall grass away from around my cassava plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava tsei ni akwɛɔ daa

english: Weeds compete directly with cassava for water, plant food, and sunlight. Keeping the base of cassava plants clear allows root tubers to expand fully without competition.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, tsei niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ahã shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the first rainy day of the year means I should start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: The very first rainfall after a long dry spell often only wets the surface soil, leaving the deeper dirt dry. Waiting until you have two or three steady, deep rains ensures the soil holds enough moisture for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ nuɔ pɛ. Ha muji ni mli kwɔ lɛ agbi. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots under the ground are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: When cassava tubers reach full maturity, the lower leaves on the stem naturally turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks often form in the soil around the base of the main stem as the swelling roots push outward.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Bei pii lɛ Amɛfeɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni shishifãi ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip and moving down the central vein usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the root zone helps the plant regain its green color and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yaa shishi kɛyaa fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which cassava stems are best to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yucca tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afo ni adu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Choose mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 18 months old, free from pests or disease spots, and cut pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with at least 4 to 6 active buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe tsɔi bɛ mli lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni tsuɔ nii yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, which prevents proper pollination and causes the plant to shed blooms to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akafee nɔ ni sa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: If I plant groundnuts between my maize rows, will the groundnuts steal nutrients from the maize?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ Ani ŋmeii baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: No, groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, which actually improves soil fertility and helps feed nearby crops like maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the barn even when I want to store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miisumɔ ni mikɛto moŋ?

english: Yams naturally enter a resting phase after harvest, but warmth, light, and high humidity trigger them to break dormancy and sprout. Storing them in a well-ventilated, cool, and shaded barn helps keep them resting longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo, la, kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baawo amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker is best for planting: the short ones with broad leaves or the taller ones with narrow leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui ni nuɔ nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shweremɔ: kuku ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ loo nɔ kakadaŋŋ ni baai lɛ mli etse?

english: The tall ones with narrow, sword-like leaves (sword suckers) are best because they have strong root reserves and grow faster into sturdy, high-yielding plantain trees compared to short suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante (klante ŋmeii) lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni ji enyɔ ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ plantains ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ akɛto ŋmeii kukuji ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce hundreds of flowers, but only a few turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop up to 95 percent of their flowers because the tree cannot support that many pods at once. It naturally selects only the amount of pods it has enough water, shade, and nutrients to feed.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ mlijaa 95 fiteɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmeii babaoo nɔ shikome. Amɛhalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu, hulutsoo, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyeɔ yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin without branching out when weeds are around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ niji be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: When weeds crowd pepper plants, they block sunlight, causing the pepper plants to stretch rapidly upward to reach the light instead of using their energy to grow strong side branches and fruits.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi eyi pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ tsei niji kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What makes the leaves of my okra plants curl upward and turn pale green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi okra baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Upward curling in okra leaves is typically caused by the Okra Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on the underside of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ okra baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji Okra Leaf Curl Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and rot at the ground level right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping off,' a common problem caused by soil fungi that attack delicate stems when nursery beds are kept overly wet, poorly drained, or planted too closely together.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, naagba ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa kɛji ŋmeii akwɛmɔ saatsoi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from heat stress until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore energy and green color to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ebaakwɛ baai ni wa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, and sitting in heavy water starves them of air, causing them to rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo muji lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha mɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ. haa egboɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot, tomato plants get stressed and cannot pollinate their flowers properly, causing the flowers to drop off. Covering the soil with dried grass mulch keeps the roots cool and helps the plant retain flowers.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my corn help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that pulls nitrogen out of the air and puts it naturally into the soil. This enriches the soil with free plant food, helping nearby crops grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do small armyworms hide inside the center whorl of my corn leaves instead of staying on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: The center whorl of a corn plant is soft, moist, and protected from hot sunlight and predators like birds. Pests hide inside this leafy funnel to eat the tender growth in safety.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ okpoi ahe. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ ni eda lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest grow into smaller and weaker plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to yield high harvests, but their offspring lose this combined strength in the second generation. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures high yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming tiny and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap and spread viruses. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the plant from getting stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. small pest control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to produce larger yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to produce the food that swells the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the shady ground, catching maximum sunlight and keeping leaves clean from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni fũuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Egbalaa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni ehaa baa lɛ he tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: Why does my plantain mat produce smaller bunches if I leave all the suckers growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji miha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When too many plantain suckers grow around the main stem, they all fight for the same water, food, and light from the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main stem to make large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green. It can also happen if the roots are standing in too much water for several days.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ damɔ nu babaoo mli gbii babaoo.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to suddenly appear and eat up all the leaves on my crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They eat soft green leaves rapidly to grow, but catching them early with simple traps or approved sprays stops them before they destroy the field.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji oya koni amɛdara. Shi amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ Tsi amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, sucking out the plant's juice and spreading diseases that stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. ni egbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ eshwaa

english: How can I keep my harvested maize from spoiling and getting insects inside the storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-abele lɛ naa koni ekafite ni kooloi akabote mi-nitoo kotokui lɛ amli?

english: Insects and spoilage need air and moisture to thrive. If you dry your maize thoroughly under the sun and store it in airtight bags (like PICS bags), insects cannot breathe or multiply, keeping the grain safe without chemicals.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kooloi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛdara. Kɛji ogbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛshwere. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni tsofai bɛ mli

english: Why do my yam tubers get soft and rot inside after I harvest and put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ mli beni mikpa amɛ ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot in storage when they get bruised during harvesting or when the storage barn is too hot and lacks fresh airflow. Fungi enter through the small cuts on the skin and spoil the tuber from the inside.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛ́ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Fungus boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ yitso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli

english: Why is it bad to leave rotten or fallen fruits lying on the soil in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashi aduawai ni egboi loo ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotten fruits carry pests and fungal diseases that live in the soil. Leaving them on the ground allows those diseases to multiply and spread to your healthy standing crops during the next rain.
ga: Yibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. The plant gets stressed and drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when there are too many tall trees covering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade to survive, adult cocoa trees need direct sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and pods. Heavy shade keeps the trees too damp, encouraging diseases like black pod.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi. Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Shade ni tsii haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Ekɛ helai srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when water settles in the soil for too long without draining away, suffocating the roots and allowing water mold to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu mli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why should I plant legumes like groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, but leguminous plants like groundnuts fix fresh nitrogen food back into the earth through their roots, restoring soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen niyenii heei lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to cut tall wood stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make big tubers underground. Climbing up sticks lifts the leaves off the hot soil and spreads them out to catch light.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni eha bulb lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okwɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni ekɛhere la lɛ atuu.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Soil often lacks enough nitrogen, so adding fertilizer or manure early gives them the food they need.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. E ma ha mɛ niye ní nɛ he hia mɛ ɔ.

english: Why does my maize farm require so much fertilizer compared to my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize grows very fast and is a greedy crop that eats up soil nutrients quickly to build stalks and seeds. Cassava grows slowly and has deep roots that can search for hidden nutrients in poorer soils.
ga: Abɛi daa oya waa, ni eji tso ni yeɔ nii babaoo ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui. Cassava daa blɛoo ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ atao niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull food directly out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural food stays in the soil for your next maize crop to eat.
ga: Peanuts gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets extremely hot or when water is irregular. When the plant gets stressed by heat, it drops its flowers to save its strength and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I have to cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Those extra small shoots steal water and food away from the main mother stem. Removing all but one or two shoots keeps all the energy focused on making one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Nakai tsei bibii ni fata he lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie plantain tsei lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ohewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tsei agbo kome ni tsii lɛ feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and rot if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots soak up extra groundwater like a sponge during heavy rain. If the ground stays too wet for too long, the starch breaks down and fungus rots the roots inside the wet soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi sumɔɔ ni amɛŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu tamɔ sponji yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Starch lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmei lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded water while my maize dies if water sits on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu hi mli lɛ?

english: Rice stems have natural hollow channels inside them that carry air from above ground down to their roots under water. Maize roots don't have these air tubes and drown when submerged.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni amɛshwieɔ nu mli kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or thrips are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, or that they have passed a plant virus to your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhaa tsei amli helai baa onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava right next to my maize on the same small patch of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ emasɛi? Abɛi yɛ he bibioo kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ

english: Cassava and maize both feed heavily on the same soil nutrients and take up a lot of space. Planting them too close together forces them to fight for food and light, which leaves you with smaller maize ears and weak cassava roots.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ nii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛheɔ he babaoo. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmãa toi bibii kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant cassava on the exact same plot without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs a large amount of nutrients from the earth. Growing it continuously in the same soil drains all the food out of the ground, so resting the land or planting legumes like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural way of saving water. By shrinking the surface area exposed to the hot sun, the maize prevents water from evaporating too quickly from its body.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Abɛi tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛtsɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ebaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Giving the plants consistent moisture and keeping the soil cool with grass mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tsei amli daa, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Spraying with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps clear these pests so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. koni baai heei akwɛ̃

english: Why must I weed around my crops before applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will quickly steal the expensive fertilizer you put down. Clearing weeds first ensures your crops get all the food, rather than feeding the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ oya.Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha jwɛi lɛ niyenii

english: Why is it bad for me to water my tomato plants in the middle of the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering in the hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it. It can also shock the roots with sudden temperature changes; early morning watering allows roots to absorb moisture fully.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hu aha shishifãi lɛ akpokpo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu lɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lowest leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the main stem thickens near the soil. Harvesting at this point gives you firm, starchy roots before they turn woody or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛtsɔ tso loo amɛgboi.

english: How do I know if my maize is getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ nu he?

english: If maize leaves roll up tightly like straws, the crop is thirsty. But if the leaves turn pale yellow and the ground stays muddy, the roots are drowning in too much water, which stops them from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abɔle ŋmãa baai lɛ ahe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi lɛ, kumai baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kã he efee muji hu? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli tsɔ. Enɛ haaa mɔ ko anyɛ amu ni enine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to pump water directly from a dam to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ nu kɛjɛ faa ko mli kɛya mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, dam water is generally fine for crops, but you should draw water from near the surface and avoid pulling up heavy mud from the bottom, which can clog your equipment and smother plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi esa akɛ ogbala nu kɛjɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ muji ni tsii ni ooogbala kɛjɛ shishi lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ onibii lɛ anaa ni efolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Does flooding my crop field with water from a pipe harm my plants' roots?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ hose mli ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Pouring heavy water directly onto the soil can wash away topsoil and pack the earth down tight, making it hard for crop roots to spread. Delivering water gently around the base of the plants is safer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ muji fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ewa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã. Light hydration Tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and drop off when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Watering tomatoes every day keeps the roots wet continuously, which rots the root system and creates damp conditions where leaf diseases spread quickly. Tomatoes do better with deep watering a few times a week.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa hulutsoo baa yɛ he ni tso helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ. Tomato tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu ni mli kwɔ shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense mid-day heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Wilting is a natural defense to save water, and plants usually stand back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Wilting ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Ni bei pii lɛ tsei lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu nyɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of big leaves but giving me small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much water or constant fertilizer early on, it puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo awoɔ lɛ ŋmei daa mra. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply water to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Early morning is the best time to water crops because the roots absorb water before the sun gets hot, reducing water loss through evaporation and keeping leaves dry before nightfall.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni oha baai lɛ agbi dani gbɛkɛ aba.

english: How does putting dry grass on top of the soil around my plants help them handle heat?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te mi tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkpee hulutsoo be lɛ naa amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing dry grass or crop leaves around your plants (mulching) acts like a blanket. It shades the dirt from the scorching sun, keeping moisture in the soil much longer so you water less often.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tso lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nu fioo pɛ haa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings struggle to grow when the top of the soil gets dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: A hard soil crust prevents water from sinking down to where root tips are searching for moisture, and it prevents fresh air from reaching the roots, slowing crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ anaa koni eyatao ŋmɔtɔ. ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies; their leaves burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to provide cool cover and keep humidity high while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Baai lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni eha edɔ ni eha hulutsoo aya hiɛ be mli ni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I don't burn all the bush after clearing my land with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Akɛni mikɛ dade shãaa jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ beni mikɛ dade ejie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing without heavy burning leaves organic mulch that decomposes, feeds the soil, and holds moisture for plant roots.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops right after I clear forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie koo lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are very tough. When you clear the land and direct sunlight hits the ground, those seeds wake up and sprout rapidly before your cultivated crop seeds can fully establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛbaate shi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya dani dumɔwui ni odu lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Retaining selected forest trees provides critical shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants are mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ kooi ni ahala mli lɛ haa anáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops look healthier when I leave some trees standing on my farm instead of clearing everything bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ miha tsei lɛ damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trees protect crops from harsh winds, bring up nutrients from deep under the soil through their long roots, and drop leaves that decompose into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi kakadaji anɔ. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and room to expand its tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting if I plant right after the very first short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil without soaking it deep enough. If a dry spell follows, the moist seeds heat up in the soil and rot before full rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hɔmɔ nifeemɔ ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baadɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves turning yellow means the plant is hungry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the central vein is a clear sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make the maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Beans belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and puts it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize growing next to it.
ga: Beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every season when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi daa be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and creates a safe home for crop-specific pests and diseases to build up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni efee shia ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afee.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon heat even if I watered them earlier in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi maŋkpa moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon air causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than the roots can drink it up. Adding dry grass or mulch around the base keeps root zones cool and conserves soil water.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while they are stored in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months to grow new plants. Breaking off the young sprouts as soon as they appear helps the tuber retain its food and stay fresh for cooking or selling.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji bɔɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ tsei heei. Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhaa niyenii hiɔ shi ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ehee kɛha nihoomɔ loo jarayeli.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but why do the flowers fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces stress, such as very hot temperatures, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your crop steady water and avoiding excessive high-nitrogen fertilizer during flowering helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts cracking as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow flowers directly on their thick wooden trunks instead of on the thin twigs?
ga: Why do cocoa trees grow flowers directly on thick tree trunks? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on their thick trunks and main branches because cocoa pods grow very large and heavy. The strong trunk provides the support needed to hold the weight of the ripening pods without breaking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei aniji wuji anɔ. Ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara waa ni amɛtsii. Tsoi ni mli wa haa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛfi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛkuuu.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and remaining small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses. Regular spraying with neem oil or recommended organic treatments helps control these pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii lɛ shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: What causes the bottom part of my garden eggs to rot and turn dark soft patches while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii? ediŋŋ beni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ

english: Dark, sunken spots at the bottom of garden eggs are known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant due to inconsistent soil moisture. Mulching and watering your field evenly prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ashishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo tsei lɛ anɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn pale yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ V-shaped pale yellow yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing at the base of young maize plants is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer around the roots quickly restores the green color and promotes healthy growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ naa amɛ su eŋɔli lɛ oya ni ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest a lot more food from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minine shɛɛɛ minɔ̃ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and very small fruits. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed well and produce a larger, healthier total yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: If the rains stop early in the season, how can I use a nearby stream to keep my crops growing?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can carry water using buckets or use a simple small water pump with flexible pipes to draw water from the stream directly to your farm. Watering your crops regularly during dry spells keeps the soil moist so your plants do not wither and die.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baagi awo nu mli loo okɛ nu pɔmp bibioo ko ni yɔɔ paipii ni nyɛɔ efoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbala nu kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ gbooo ni egbooo.

english: Why do people say water is the most important thing for my crop to produce good yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ nu ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops need water to dissolve food nutrients from the soil and carry them through their stems to their leaves. Without enough water, the crop cannot feed itself, causing it to stunt, drop leaves, or produce tiny fruits.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛjie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ amɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, enɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are stressed from lack of water before they completely dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli dani amɛgbi kwraa?

english: When plants need water, their leaves will start to droop, roll up, or turn yellowish during the hottest part of the day. If you dig a few inches into the dirt and the soil crumbles like dry dust, your crops are thirsty.
ga: Beni tsei he hiaa nu lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔi gbee, amɛbaabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sũ ni egbi. Kuma baaye nyɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: What is the benefit if my fellow farmers and I join together to buy our fertilizer in bulk?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni baaba kɛji mi kɛ minanemɛi okwaafoi lɛ fee ekome kɛhe wɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo?

english: Buying fertilizer and seeds in bulk lowers the price per bag because suppliers give wholesale discounts. It also reduces transport costs per person and helps you get genuine products directly from trusted dealers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ lɛ haa kotoku kome jara baa shi ejaakɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii lɛ baa lɛ haa shika ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi babaoo. Ehaa shika ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛmajeɔ lɛ hu baa shi, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii diɛŋtsɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why does adding fertilizer to my soil make my crops grow faster and greener than using no fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni ehaaa shihilɛ lɛ afite fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works like extra food for plants, supplying key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that might be missing in your soil. Plants absorb these nutrients to quickly build strong stems and leafy green growth.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni akɛfataa tsei ahe. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni ekolɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ koni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni dalɛ yaa oya.

english: Clearing weeds with a hoe takes too much of my energy, so how can I stop weeds from growing around my crops easily?
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ lɛ heɔ mihewalɛ babaoo tsɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, mikpaa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching. This layer blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot sprout, while also keeping soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant them in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every plant enough room to receive sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without choking each other. It also makes weeding, watering, and harvesting much faster and less stressful.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya ni ehaaa haomɔ aba.

english: My elders always burn the bush before planting, but is burning the field actually good or bad for my crops?
ga: Mi onukpai lɛ shãa jwɛi lɛ dani amɛduɔ nii. Shi ani ŋmɔ mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ hi diɛŋtsɛ loo ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, the intense heat destroys natural organic matter and good soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing without burning allows plant residues to rot into rich compost for the soil.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi latsaa ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weakly when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in the field. Switching crops every season allows the soil to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: How does shade from large trees affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Some crops like young cocoa enjoy light shade to protect them from scorching heat, but crops like maize and cassava need full sunshine all day to make food and grow strong tubers or grains.
ga: Tsei komɛi, tamɔ kookoo bibii lɛ haa hulutsoo be fioo ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, Ehe miihia hulu muu fɛɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs loo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Will spraying my cocoa farm with chemicals harm the good insects that help my crops produce pods?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ awui?

english: Approved chemicals target harmful pests like capsids, but spraying at the wrong time or using unapproved chemicals can kill beneficial insects like midges that flowers need to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids, shi tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa fɔfɔii koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: High humidity and continuous rain create a favorable environment for Black Pod fungus to grow and spread rapidly across the pods on your farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungus lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ pods ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What causes the small dark spots on my cocoa leaves and young shoots that make them wither?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Yɛ kookoo baai kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi lɛ anɔ?

english: These spots are usually caused by insects called capsids that suck sap from young shoots, injecting saliva that damages leaves and causes branches to die back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why is it important that I only use government-approved chemicals on my cocoa trees instead of buying any agrochemical from the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe agrochemicals kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ

english: Approved chemicals are tested to ensure they effectively kill pests without damaging the cocoa tree, harming beneficial organisms, or leaving dangerous residues in your harvested beans.
ga: Akwɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ amli koni ana akɛ amɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee cacao tsei lɛ. Ye nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui loo shi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ okɔfi yibii ni okpa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight all day; they need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect their delicate leaves from burning while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer flowers when the branches become very bushy and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ beni eniji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowded branches block sunlight and air movement, causing the tree to spend its energy maintaining heavy leaves instead of forming flowers and pods.
ga: Niji babaoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ ebaa ni tsii lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do many cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop naturally if they are not pollinated by insects or if the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nutrient-starved cocoa trees typically show yellowing leaves, slow growth, small pods, or pale leaf tissue with dark green veins.
