ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii, loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo.

english: How does the government mass spraying program help protect my farm from pests compared to when I spray by myself?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛshwieɔ nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Mass spraying covers entire farming communities at once, preventing pests from simply escaping from an unsprayed farm onto your treated cocoa trees.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa okwaayeli akutsei muu lɛ fɛɛ anɔ shikome. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akajo foi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni afɔɔɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ amli kɛya kookoo tsei ni atsa amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply pest control sprays on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because temperatures are cooler and winds are calm, allowing the chemicals to settle on leaves properly without quickly evaporating.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu mli jɔ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwieee oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow well, especially when they are young and growing quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛmiida oya.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting like a free natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How should I stick my cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava cuttings slanted at a 45-degree angle with the growing buds pointing upward helps roots grow stronger and makes harvesting the tubers much easier later.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji yɛ 45-degree angle mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa. Ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabii yitsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cabbage plants are set too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, which stops them from growing full, heavy heads.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kaabaji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kaabaji lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa kaabii lɛ akwɛɛɛ yitso ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ makɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Planting plantains nearby provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, preventing the flowers from turning into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai

english: What is eating holes in the middle of my young maize plants and leaving small dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni miyeɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mishiɔ muji fioo yɛ mli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They hide inside the central leaves of maize plants, and applying recommended treatments early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Ni tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkpa.

english: Why are my tomato fruits getting black soft spots on the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo diji dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant receives uneven amounts of water and cannot absorb enough calcium.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from the maize I bought at the market to plant in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market maize is often hybrid grain, meaning seeds saved from it will yield much less crop and grow unevenly compared to fresh, certified seeds bought from an agri-dealer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baawo yibii fioo kwraa ni ebaada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay small when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots to spread and grab nutrients so it can grow strong.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛgbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ adara waa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers coming out of the same base steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing extra shoots leaves only one strong follower, allowing the main tree to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shishitoo kome mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear sticks and build tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to spread their leaves and capture direct sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents soil moisture from causing rot and disease, resulting in bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛbai lɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai akafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and easily scorch under harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making them shed their blossoms to conserve energy. Keeping soil moist and mulched helps keep the root zone cool so the plant holds onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato afɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wither and die even when I give them plenty of water every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water smothers their roots by filling all air spaces in the soil. This causes root rot, preventing the plant from taking up food and water, which leaves it wilting despite wet soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: Why does my cassava have lots of big green leaves but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of root tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to direct its energy downward into forming thick roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help the maize crop I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they release natural fertilizer into the soil, feeding the next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upward into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni abɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Treating the crop with neem oil or mild insecticidal soap clears the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ waa tsu onibii ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves when the plants grow thick and bushy close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ beni tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When plant branches are tightly packed, air cannot flow through them and leaf wetness stays trapped. This damp environment creates ideal conditions for fungal leaf spots to spread.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. ni baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baakã shi Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal leaf spot lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or in the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because water sinks deep into the soil before the sun can evaporate it, giving plants the drink they need to survive the hot afternoon heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shwane latsaa be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops need extra water when the rains stop coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo he miihia miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Check your leaves early in the morning. If the leaves are curling up, drooping, or look limp before the heat of the day even starts, the soil is dry and your plants need water.
ga: Kwɛmɔ obaai lɛ amli leebi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi, amɛshwie shi loo amɛfee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ je shishi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni otso lɛ he miihia nu.

english: What happens to my maize plants when rain does not fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Without rain, maize plants roll up their leaves to save water and slow down their growth, which can prevent them from producing full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, abele baafolɔ ebaa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekawo toi ni eyi obɔ

english: How can I keep the soil around my crops wet for longer during dry periods?
ga: Mafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching) to shade the ground and stop water from drying out quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai (mulch) awo tsei lɛ ashishi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu akagbi oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry weather on purpose to reduce water loss, allowing the plant to stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: What causes my vegetable leaves to turn yellow and weak during very hot sun?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: High heat and dry soil make it hard for plants to suck up food and water, causing leaves to lose their green color and look tired.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to do hard farm work early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔtsu nii waa leebi lɛ?

english: Doing field work early protects you from heat exhaustion and allows you to irrigate or spray crops when conditions are cool and plants absorb inputs best.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nitsumɔ mra Ebaabu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli tɔlɛ he. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good to apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the rain has stopped and the soil is totally dry?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: No, fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve and feed the roots; putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn your plant roots or be wasted.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu koni ekɛshwie shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: If my crops start to wilt because of poor rainfall, can I still save them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ hewɔ hu? Ani manyɛ mahere miwala yiwala lolo?

english: Yes, if you irrigate them promptly, trim off dried leaves, and provide temporary shade, many crops can recover once water returns.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okɛ nu wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, gbee baai ni egbi lɛ nɔ ni oha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Nibii ni adu lɛ babaoo nyɛ amɛhiɛ amɛhe beni nu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to just leave a dried-up crop patch unattended on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Abandoned crop patches attract pests and crop diseases, which multiply there freely and then spread to attack your healthy crops nearby.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔji ni ashi lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛ tsei ahe helai. Efɔɔ bii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa koni etutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade during their early growth because direct sunlight overheats the soil and scorches their delicate leaves, so keeping tall shade trees helps retain moisture and protect them.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdaraa mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni eshãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa wɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers, so lifting the vines off the ground spreads the leaves out toward the sun and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ etso lɛ he, ni ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient the plant needs to stay green and build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in that ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains stay on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water sits on the farm without draining, the roots drown and harmful fungi take over, causing them to spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not anchor deeply into the soil, making the plant top-heavy when carrying heavy fruit bunches, especially in wet, soft ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ muji kɛji ewo yibii ni tsii. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent water causes stress to pepper plants, making them shed their flowers to conserve energy for survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How do weeds actually stop my crops from growing big cobs or tubers?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji loo bulbs?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, effectively stealing the food and space your crops need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and spoil so fast during the foggy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni afua ni mli ewo wu lɛ?

english: High humidity and cool fog create the ideal conditions for the black pod fungus to spread quickly, especially if the tree branches are too crowded to let air and sunlight through.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ afua ni mli ejɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale, titri lɛ kɛji tso lɛ niji lɛ amli eyi tsɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la nyɛŋ atsɔ mli.

english: Why is it helpful for me to give simple, memorable names to different sections of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aha fãi lɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hiɛ kpaaa nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he kɛha mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Giving simple names to your plots makes it easy to remember which section produced the best harvest, where you applied fertilizer, and which area had disease problems without getting confused.
ga: Gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakai fãi ni kɛ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ baa lɛ. He ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli kɛ hei ni helai naagbai yɔɔ ni futumɔ bɛ mli?

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantain or cassava during their first two years to retain moisture and build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) around one plantain tree causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main plant to produce larger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Ni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo (ŋmeii) ni bɔleɔ dumɔwu kome he. Enɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛto enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which flows down to feed and expand the yam tuber underground for a bigger harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ niyenii aha ni ekɛ yam ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain floods low or flat ground, water drowns the roots and causes rot; planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu afua shwieɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food element in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure near the roots helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes the ragged holes and little worms inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on leaves that hatch into caterpillars that eat the growing centers of maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel protects your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ tsui lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Onibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Giving plants consistent moisture at the roots and providing light mulch helps keep the soil cool so flowers stay on to produce tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ eyaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ awo tomato.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaves from wrinkling up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in that ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans returns nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist after a light rain, allowing the plant roots to drink it up quickly. Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours causes the water to wash the nutrients away before crops can use them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps them make green leaves and food. It can also happen when too much rain water pools around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai kɛ niyenii eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa tso lɛ amu.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding under the leaves. These insects can also spread plant viruses that make the leaves shrink and twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hu amɛshwãa.

english: Why are there small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnels of my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-corn lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to feed on the tender young leaves inside the stalk. If left untreated, they can destroy the growing point of the plant before the maize ears form.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite hei ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ dani ŋmãa toi lɛ afee.

english: How do I know which way to stick my cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or 'eyes' along the cassava stem. These eyes must always point upward toward the sky so the leaves can sprout easily above ground while roots grow down.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ bibii ni awó nɔ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ hiŋmɛii nɛɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Which plantain suckers are best to cut from an old plant to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain ŋmeii hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ afo kɛjɛ tsei momoi amli koni akɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—the young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They grow much faster and produce stronger stems than shoots that already have wide, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword sucker’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni he wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛtsi latsaa ni naa wa lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants need lots of sunlight on their leaves to make energy that feeds the growing tuber underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground prevents rot and allows maximum sunshine to reach them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa, ni ebaaha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the ground. It blocks direct sun heat, keeps the soil damp longer, and prevents weeds from taking light and water away from your crops.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekagbala la kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What does mixing dried poultry manure into my farm soil do for my crops?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure feeds helpful microbes in the soil, improves how well the soil holds water, and slowly releases essential food that helps your crops grow thicker stems and healthier leaves.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã haa niyenii kɛha nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from shade trees or plantains because direct sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and burns the stems before their roots can establish deep in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ hulutsoo tso loo plantain mli, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi ni eshã amɛshishifãi lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear away extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no baaha dumɔwui bibii aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant lacks the essential nutrient needed to produce green foliage and healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops still perform poorly even after I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb the nutrients; applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn roots and waste money.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã, ni eji shika fitemɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and powdery droppings inside the leaf whorls?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni powder ni mli ewo muji yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing core of the maize plant during the day and feed on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing smaller than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on the sap, which distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ adalɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to survive; when soil stays waterlogged for too long, roots suffocate and fungal rot organisms attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect activity to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce my total crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving them weak and low-yielding.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa oya kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know how much distance to leave between my cassava plants when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awo mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Leaving proper space between cassava plants ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the tubers room to expand underground without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tuber he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and dry up when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender stems and shallow roots that quickly lose water under heavy sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects tender seedlings from burning until they grow stronger.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la he kɛyashiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant roots are soaked in too much water. Adding properly balanced compost or fertilizer helps restore the soil nutrients so leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ

english: How can I tell if my piece of land is fertile enough to start planting vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi aduawai adumɔ?

english: Fertile soil usually looks dark, feels crumbly when moist, and easily breaks apart in your hands. Land that naturally grows thick, healthy weeds during the rains is usually a good indicator that vegetables will grow well there.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ duŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hiɛ. ni efoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ enine mli Hei ni jwɛi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do insects attack one type of crop on my farm but leave the other crops nearby untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shi amɛshiɔ ekrokomɛi lɛ? Yɛ akutso lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako he?

english: Insects are attracted to specific crop smells, soft leaves, or sweet saps. Planting a mix of different crops together confuses insects and stops pests from multiplying and destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni gbalaa kooloi titri ji ŋmɔshi nibii, baai bibii, loo nu mli nu. Tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ooodu lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ futuɔ amɛhe, ni ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ onibii fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli pɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular before planting. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which dries out the soil and kills newly sprouted seeds before they can establish roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba dani odu. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crop yields when I plant the exact same crop in the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously. Rotating different crops, such as legumes after corn, allows the soil to naturally rebuild its nutrient balance.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I add double the recommended amount of fertilizer to my farm, will my crops yield twice as much?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni fa fe bɔ ni awo he ŋaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibiiwoo lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: Excessive fertilizer can burn plant roots and damage soil biology, causing the plants to stunt or die. Applying only the recommended amount provides the exact food plants need without causing root burn.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbɔjɔ loo amɛgboi. Kɛ́ akɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni amɛshãaa amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Do weeds actually steal food from my crops, or do they just take up space in the field?
ga: Ani jwɛi miiju niyenii kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ loo amɛmiiye he ko kɛkɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds actively draw water, sunlight, and key soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's resources so they can grow healthy and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi gbalaa nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii titrii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. So that they grow strong and produce good crops.

english: Why do some of the seeds I put into the ground fail to sprout entirely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deeply in the soil, if the soil is too dry or flooded with water, or if the seeds were stored in hot, damp conditions before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ dani adu.

english: Why is it better for me to get young seedlings from a nursery center rather than planting raw seeds directly into my big field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maná dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ awo ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ?

english: Starting plants in a controlled nursery gives fragile seeds a protected environment to sprout safely away from harsh sun, heavy rain, and soil pests. Buying or receiving pre-sprouted seedlings ensures you only spend effort planting strong, healthy crops in your main field.
ga: Tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ naa he ko ni abuɔ he koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui ni asaa he momo lɛ ahemɔ loo onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ ohewalɛ miiwo tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ pɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cocoa seedlings are mature enough to move from the nursery to my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they are about 4 to 6 months old, have developed a sturdy woody stem, and display at least two full sets of mature, dark green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ beni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa, ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ baai ni edara ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ enyɔ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout even after I water the ground regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa po lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is too packed for air to reach them, or if the seeds were old, damaged by insects, or infected by seed-borne diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni kooloi efite amɛ loo helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ emɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I cover my fresh vegetable seedbeds with palm fronds after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei aha mi dumɔwui eŋɔli lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering seedbeds with palm leaves protects delicate seeds from being washed away by heavy rains and shields the soil from direct sunlight, keeping it moist and cool so seeds can sprout evenly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei aha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ. ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or that the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, prolonged dry weather, or insufficient nutrients in the soil needed to sustain fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ko he, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha aduawai afeemɔ

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow buds after I plant them during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need moisture to awaken their dormant buds. Planting them during extreme heat without enough moisture causes the stem cuttings to dry out and die before roots can form.
ga: Kasava ni afoɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekɛte eshishifãi ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ ashi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings suddenly fall over and rot right at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when the soil stays too wet and air cannot circulate well around the bases of young plants.
ga: Fungal shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle ehe. Tso bibioo lɛ shishitoo lɛ hi.

english: Is it better for me to water my young crop seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo tsei bibii lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it allows plants to absorb moisture before the afternoon heat and lets wet leaves dry during the day, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ baa, ni ehaa tso lɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam seeds rot inside the mounds before they can push shoots above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when mounds are made in poorly drained land or when planted right before heavy rains stall, causing water to pool inside the mound and decompose the seed piece.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ afee amɛ yɛ gɔji amli yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Enɛ haa nu ŋmɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ amli fãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture, giving young cocoa trees shelter while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he ko ni amɛhi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food and grow heavy tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp soil where pests and diseases live, allowing the plant to get plenty of air and sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai hiɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores soil nutrients so the leaves can turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Roots can only take in plant food when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and go to waste, while moist soil helps the roots absorb the food safely and quickly.
ga: Shishifãi baanyɛ aye tso niyenii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai oya.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on the same land helps my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally grabs nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. This leaves nutrient-rich soil behind for crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ekɔɔɔ he eko gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow backward, leading to weak plants and low tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu yucca tsei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why should I wait until the rains set in properly before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting after just one light rain can trick seeds into sprouting, but if dry weather returns immediately, the young seedlings will dry out and die. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures there is enough moisture to keep seedlings alive.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids that feed on plant sap and spread viruses. Protecting the plants with organic oils or pest sprays helps clear the insects so leaves can grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ mu loo kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ bu tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Keeping the plants well-watered during dry periods and protecting flowers from insects helps them turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni abu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce small and poor fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. When weeds overcrowd a farm, they steal resources that the crop needs to make big, healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsɔ Amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important for me to prepare my land around October and November before the minor rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ October kɛ November teŋ, dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ aba naagbee?

english: Preparing your land late in the year lets you clear weeds easily before the ground hardens during the dry season, catches the last rains to keep the soil moist, and sets up your land for early planting when the main rains return.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi lɛ oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Na naagbee nugbɔ lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ titri lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: How can I double the harvest I get from my small farm without buying very expensive equipment?
ga: Mafee nibii ni miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ feɔ lɛ babaoo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee minɔ lɛ shii enyɔ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can double your harvest by planting your seeds in straight rows with proper spacing, clearing weeds early before they steal food from your crops, and adding animal manure or compost to feed the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shii enyɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli Ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when too much water stays around the plant roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle he. tso shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like small babies—they burn easily in full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa provides living shade that protects the seedlings from hot sun and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii bibii. No shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ ehe. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get more harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce maximum yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving the cassava behind to take over the land and grow bigger over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ koni eŋɔ he ko ni eda yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce less food every year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth each season. If you do not add nutrients back using compost, manure, or resting the land (fallowing), the soil becomes tired and cannot feed new crops well.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo hejɔɔmɔ (tillage) nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is fertile enough to support a new crop of yam or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei henɔ hee?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and contains signs of life like earthworms and rotting leaf matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Ni wala he okadii yɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover (mulching). This protective layer shades the ground, keeping the soil moist and cool for much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way for me to manage multiple small farms without getting overwhelmed by the workload?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ ŋmɔji bibii babaoo anɔ ni mikɛ nitsumɔ babaoo baaa?

english: Organize your workload by staggering your planting dates and picking crops with different harvest times. This prevents all your farm work from piling up at the exact same time.
ga: Too onitsumɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ gbii ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ ni oootsake kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kpamɔ bei srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ ni oooha lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni makwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the light and keeps them off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ afee wuji babaoo.

english: Can I cut one big yam tuber into small pieces and plant them to get new yam plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo sweet potato tuber agbo kome mli bibii bibii ni madu koni mafee sweet potato tso hee?

english: Yes, yam tubers have dormant growth buds under their skin. When you cut a healthy tuber into pieces (called seed setts) and let the cut surfaces dry or treat them with ash to stop rotting, each piece with skin can sprout into a completely new yam plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ ni bɛ nitsumɔ yɛ hewolo lɛ shishi. Kɛji ofo tuber ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli bibii bibii, (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ seed set) ni oha nɔ ni ofo lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi loo okɛ sũ atsu nii ni ekpa fitemɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ sweet potato tso hee ni afee.

english: Why does my yam plant produce plenty of big green leaves above ground but gives me very small yams at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ sweet potatoes ni ji bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the yam plant to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems instead of storing food below ground. A balanced nutrient supply encourages the plant to direct its energy into expanding the tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the soil are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. Harvesting too early yields soft, watery tubers that rot fast, while waiting too long leaves the tubers exposed to subterranean pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛbaafite oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and getting light in weight even inside my store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni efee mlɛo yɛ mishwapo lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams remain alive after harvest and naturally try to start growing again when the season changes. Sprouting consumes the stored water and food inside the tuber, which causes the yam to shrink, soften, and lose weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Ni sweet potatoes lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni bei lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ. Sprouting kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛtsiimɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my stored yams rot quickly when I stack them in a big pile on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmeii agbo ko mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Piling yams together traps heat and moisture, creating the perfect warm environment for fungi and rot to spread from one tuber to another. Hanging them on elevated wooden yam barns allows air to flow around every tuber, keeping them cool and dry.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato lɛ to he kome lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ bulb mli kɛyaa bulb mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso ni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe, ni ehaa efeɔ fɛ̃i ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or drop off when the hot afternoon sun hits them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Crops curl or drop leaves to reduce the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, which stops moisture from escaping too fast. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to preserve water inside its stem and roots during dry spells.
ga: Dumɔ bɔni afee ni ebɔle ehe loo efolɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya tsɔ lɛ naa. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crop seedlings die quickly when the bare soil gets extremely hot during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely hot bare soil scorches fragile young roots near the surface and causes soil water to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil around seedlings with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and traps moisture in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baashã shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas alongside my main crops like yam or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with plant food that companion crops like yams can feed on to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei niyenii ni nanemɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aye koni amɛdara waa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some yam varieties take eight months to mature while others are ready in just five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi heɔ nyɔji kpaanyɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different yam varieties have different growth cycles coded into their genetics. Early-maturing varieties grow quickly to finish before dry weather sets in, while late-maturing varieties spend more time building up larger reserves over a long rainy period.
ga: Sweet potato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni edaraa ehaa ni atsɔɔ mli yɛ e-genetic code lɛ mli. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baagbe amɛdalɛ naa oya dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo koni amɛkɛma shikpɔji wuji anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get enough sun, they make more food for the plant, resulting in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why should I space my crops far apart instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants space ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with neighboring plants, leading to bigger harvests.
ga: He ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps moisture in the soil under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that naturally adapt quickly to the environment. They steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than cultivated crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting, curling up, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on cassava are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this damage.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaves. Applying recommended neem seed extract or approved pesticide early protects the young maize plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ neem dumɔ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmãa tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Shrinkage and leaf curling on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying with mild soapy water or approved insecticide helps kill these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Loo, tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just use Urea fertilizer alone on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ urea pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Just like humans need more than one type of food to stay healthy, crops require a balanced mix of nutrients. Urea only provides nitrogen for leaf growth, but crops also need phosphorus for strong roots and potassium to form heavy, healthy grains.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni fa fe ekome he hiaa adesai koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii ni ja hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Urea haa nitrogen pɛ kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Shi fɔsfɔs hu he miihia tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, kɛ potassium hu koni amɛfee dumɔwui ni tsii ni wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are drowning from too much water. Water alone is not enough food for the plant; it also needs nutrients from organic manure or balanced fertilizer to stay green and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho yɛ nu babaoo hewɔ. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha tsei. Shi niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa mli lɛ hu he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I use the exact same type of fertilizer for my crops from planting day until harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni midu kɛyashi be mli ni mikpaa nii lɛ?
