english: Crops have different nutritional needs as they grow. Early in their life, they need nutrients that build strong roots; as they mature, they need nutrients for green leaves, and during flowering, they need high potassium to produce big fruits and seeds.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii mli hiamɔ nii srɔtoi beni amɛdaraa lɛ. mra yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli Niyenii he miihia amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa. Beni amɛdaraa lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia amɛ kɛha amɛbaai eŋɔlii lɛ. kɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Potassium ni fa babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛfee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is cool and slightly moist. Applying fertilizer during the hot midday heat can cause the nutrients to scorch the plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ fioo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii aye tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any tomatoes when water is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant does not get enough water at the right time, it gets stressed and discards its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive, preventing it from bearing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Ehaoɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli. Tsi yibiiwoo naa

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin instead of producing big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to stretch upward for light rather than developing thick stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas returns nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, which thrives in cool, overly shaded, and damp conditions. Pruning dense tree branches allows sunlight and air flow into the farm, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni mli tse lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil cool and provides cover until the young trees are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ ahe waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil, especially during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This competition results in weak stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more food the plant produces to grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ, tsei lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba koni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing smaller than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the plant's sap, or a leaf curl virus transmitted by insects that slows down normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shito baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ thrips loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ he okadi. loo leaf curl virus ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly from the soil, suppresses weeds, and keeps the soil cool during hot weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, with deep roots already established in the soil. They quickly consume available water and nutrients before young, cultivated crop seedlings can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni ehe wa. ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni efu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ Amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya dani dumɔwui bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛhe shi.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during early morning or late afternoon when the plant is actively growing. Avoid applying right before heavy downpours, which wash the nutrients away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ miida. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ aya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any larger plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa trees provides shelter from harsh sunlight and keeps moisture in the soil while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my crops as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food they need to build strong roots and produce high yields before weeds crowd them out.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo dani jwɛi lɛ aye amɛnɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of soil every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up. Switching to legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are getting too much water during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When cassava gets too much water in flooded or waterlogged soil, its leaves will turn yellow and droop, and the roots underground will begin to rot and turn soft instead of expanding into strong tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. You can manage them by hand-picking the insects, spraying natural neem leaf extract, or using safe, approved pesticides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsu amɛhe nii kɛtsɔ onine ni okɛbaakpa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Spray adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Pepper blossoms drop mainly due to stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or small pests like thrips attacking the buds. Mulching around the base and keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi babaoo yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Should I buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer or just plant seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are bred to resist local pests and diseases and give higher harvests. Saved seeds lose their strength over time, making them more likely to produce smaller crops and yield less food.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when the leaves and vines start turning yellow and dry up. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if the milky sap dries white quickly without turning black, it is ready.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki mli nu lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔɔɔ ediŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Why do small insects ruin my harvested maize after I store it in bags for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kpata mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ hiɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils often lay eggs on maize in the field or infest dry storage bags. Drying your maize properly until it is hard, using airtight storage bags, or treating the grain with approved storage dust protects it from weevils.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths lɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo amɛwoɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni egbi lɛ amli. Akɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii ni akɛgbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa loo akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ sũ buaa nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after I spray weedkiller near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers can drift onto your crops or soak into the soil near their roots, stressing the plant and preventing it from making food properly, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛbote onibii amli loo ebote shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ehoo nii jogbaŋŋ. ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: If I put extra chemical fertilizer on my crops, will it make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya fe tsui lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer causes chemical salts to build up in the soil, which burns the plant's roots and can stunt or kill the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda

english: Why is it bad to mix two different farm chemicals together before spraying my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu mli dani mikɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can cause a reaction that destroys their ability to fight pests, creates toxic substances that damage crop leaves, or creates fumes that are harmful to your health.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko aba ni baafite nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ ni okɛwuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Ehaa tsofai fɔji ni fiteɔ tsei ahe baai loo ehaa lasu ni yeɔ ohewalɛ nɔ awui baa.

english: Why are my maize yields so much better this rainy season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hi kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Crop yields change from year to year depending on how well rainfall is spread out across the season, how cool the soil remains, and whether pests attacked during crucial flowering stages.
ga: Esoro ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi. Edamɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ni ani atutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ fɔfɔii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli?

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization; when this happens, the plant drops the flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji enɛ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back to my field even after I spray chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ewo mihe moŋ.

english: Insects can build resistance if you use the same chemical repeatedly, and spraying at the wrong time of day often misses pests that hide under leaves or inside the soil during full sunshine.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ afɔse tsofa yɛ gbi lɛ mli yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning white underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ futafuta yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Curling cassava leaves with white powder underneath are caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or mealybugs sucking the plant's sap, which steals nutrients needed for root growth.
ga: Yucca baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni powda yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with small or empty ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or beans together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that improves crop growth and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei daa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its strength and needs a break or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he waaa ni ehe miihia ni atsake loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When soil loses its strength, your crops grow slowly, their lower leaves turn pale green or yellow early in the season, and the harvest decreases year after year even with good rain.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ he wa lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ni nikpamɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and stay green. This happens when soil fertility is low or when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my corn plants staying very short and refusing to grow tall even after giving them time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku nɛkɛ ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ shi yɛ be mli ni mikɛ be eha lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted corn growth happens when plants are grown too close together, when soil nutrients are exhausted, or when parasitic weeds like Striga attach to the roots and steal the plant's food.
ga: Dwarf corn dalɛ baa kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Beni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fo Aloo be mli ni jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛjuɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining, creating a wet environment where soil fungi thrive. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight and air dry out the farm to protect the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Extra shaded pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off the trees before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack sufficient soil moisture, or when there are too few pollinating insects around to turn flowers into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ faaa tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake fɔfɔii lɛ amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tightly and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is usually caused by a virus carried by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme sun heat and dry soil. Keeping the farm clear of weeds helps reduce the insects that spread this condition.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha kooloi ni gbɛɔ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ eshwa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their small green fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruits when soil moisture changes too drastically, such as going from very dry soil to heavy flooding, or during periods of intense afternoon heat.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ, tamɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or underground stem borers attack and weaken the roots, leaving the plant without a firm grip in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ shishi stem borers lɛ tutua amɛ ni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my cowpea leaves just a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ.

english: Tiny holes on young leaves are signs of leaf-chewing beetles or caterpillars. Checking under the leaves early allows you to control them before they destroy the plant's ability to absorb light.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ahe okadi. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ baai lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛjieɔ la lɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers begin to grow sprouts while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ beni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their resting period and sprout when the air around them becomes warm and humid. Keeping your storage barn well-ventilated, elevated, and shaded keeps the yams dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bote otsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ewo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning red and the stems swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni eshishifã lɛ fũuɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and discolored leaves are major warning signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. This disease chokes the tree's internal sap flow, slowly ruining the plant and drastically reducing its ability to produce pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni etsake amɛhe lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud virus hela lɛ eba. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Efiteɔ tsei fiofio. ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ ni akɛfeɔ pods lɛ baa shi waa

english: Can a cocoa disease really destroy my entire farm if I leave it alone?
ga: Ani kookoo hela baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mishi lɛ?

english: Yes, viral cocoa diseases do not heal on their own. If an infected tree is left on your farm, insects will carry the virus to surrounding healthy trees until your entire farm stops producing pods and dies.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ nyɛŋ aya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kooloi kɛ hela lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Kɛyashi oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baakpa pods feemɔ ni egbo.

english: Why do I need to cut down my cocoa tree if it is still giving me a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso lɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Even if an infected cocoa tree still has a few pods, the virus inside it continues to spread. Keeping it alive puts all nearby healthy trees at high risk, so cutting it down completely is the only way to save the rest of your farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii komɛi lolo moŋ, Shi hela ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ ehi shi lɛ, ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ oshara mli waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ohere oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: Will spraying regular farm chemicals cure a diseased cocoa tree?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji amli daa lɛ baaye abua ni etsa kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: No, chemical sprays only kill surface pests like capsids, but they cannot cure viral diseases inside the tree. Once a cocoa tree gets a viral disease like Swollen Shoot, the only treatment is cutting it down.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ capsids pɛ. Shi enyɛŋ etsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu lɛ, tsamɔ pɛ ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii ji ni afolɔ cacao tsei lɛ.

english: If I cut down an infected cocoa tree, will the disease stay in the soil and ruin new plants?
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ Ani hela lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbe kookoo tsei heei?

english: The virus lives inside the living plant tissue, not in the dirt. Once you cut down and remove the infected trees and roots so they dry out, the soil remains safe for planting new healthy seedlings.
ga: Virus lɛ hiɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli, shi jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, kɛ́ ofo ni ojie tsei kɛ shishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni amɛgbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does cocoa disease move from a neighboring village to my farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kookoo hela gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ akrowa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa viruses are spread by tiny crawling insects called mealybugs, which are carried from tree to tree by ants, strong winds, or on farmers' tools and clothes as they travel between farms.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ gbɛɔ kookoo hela lɛ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybug, ni ŋmeii woɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛyaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. loo yɛ okwaafoi adɛŋdadei kɛ atadei anɔ beni amɛfãa gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ.

english: How far away can disease spread from a sick cocoa farm to a healthy one?
ga: Te hela ko baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: Disease can easily cross farm boundaries if tree branches touch or if winds carry mealybugs over several meters. Clearing a protective border around your farm helps stop the disease from jumping into your field.
ga: Hela lɛ baanyɛ afo ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli mlɛo kɛji tsei niji ta amɛhe loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ wo mealybugs kɛtee jɛmɛ mitai babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie he ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can other wild trees growing on my land give diseases to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba mikookoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, certain native forest trees like the Silk Cotton tree can carry the cocoa virus without dying. Removing these specific host trees near your farm prevents the virus from jumping onto your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ Silk Cotton tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kookoo hela lɛ ni ekɛ gbele baaa. Kɛ́ ojie tsei pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akabote oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How long must I wait to replant new cocoa after clearing out diseased trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo tsei heei beni mijie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: You can replant as soon as the old infected trees and roots are completely dead and dried up, ensuring no living host tissues remain to pass the virus onto your fresh seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ekoŋŋ kɛji tso momo ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ gboi ni amɛgbi kwraa pɛ. Enɛ baakwɛ akɛ fãji ni hiɛ kã ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baagbɛ hela lɛ eshwã odumɔwui heei lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my fresh cocoa seedlings when replanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe beni miduɔ ehee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and will burn in harsh direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and cool soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its first critical years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe titri. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and improving your maize yield.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni oha o-abele yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How do I know if Fall Armyworm is damaging my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji Fall Armyworm miifite mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm leaves ragged holes in maize leaves that look like tiny gunshots and leaves brownish, sawdust-like droppings inside the central leaf whorl of young maize plants.
ga: Fall Armyworm lɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ amli, ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow and green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with yellowish patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread when you plant cuttings taken from infected cassava stems.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ woɔ kɛji ofo tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into white powder after a few months in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi tsu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize turning to powder is caused by maize weevils eating the grain from the inside. Drying your maize properly before storage and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents these insects from surviving.
ga: Abele ni tsɔɔ powda lɛ jɛɔ abele ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto ni akɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and moisture during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine, holds water in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem grows a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off the plant without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress from dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do some of the seeds I planted fail to germinate and sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry, if insects eat them underground, or if the seeds were old and lost their life strength.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji kooloi ye amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Aloo kɛji dumɔwu lɛ egbɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to protect their delicate leaves from heat stress and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the maize plant needs to grow. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when we get heavy rains that don't dry quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔna nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni egbiɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without producing any peppers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy and water. Keeping the soil moist during hot periods helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my land get hard like a rock and make my crop yields drop after I farm it for a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi beni midu nii be fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming and clearing crop leaves remove organic material that keeps soil soft. Adding compost, animal manure, or leaving plant material to rot into the ground restores soil structure so roots can spread.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ kɛ tsei ahe baai ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo tsei ahe nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do you recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize crop that follows.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air so they can catch more sunlight. More sun exposure helps the leaves make more food, resulting in much bigger tuber roots underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around them during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures young crop roots get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and wrinkling, making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Ha tso lɛ akpa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ehe hia ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akakpa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before planting my corn instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout and then run out of water, the young shoots will dry up and die before the main rains return.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nu bɛ amɛhe lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops within just a month of the rainy season starting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli nyɔŋ kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so when heavy rains fall, they absorb nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops. This allows them to quickly multiply and outshine young crop seedlings if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: What happens to my main crops if my field gets completely overgrown with bush?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ jwɛi eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ kwraa?

english: When a farm becomes overgrown, tall weeds block sunlight from reaching crop leaves, starve the roots of soil nutrients, and create hiding places for pests and diseases that damage your yield.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ ji gɔji lɛ, jwɛi kakadaji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anaaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ofee hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi.

english: Is it good to plant my seeds when the heavy downpours have already started?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ waa lɛ?

english: Planting during extremely heavy rains can wash seeds away or cause them to rot in flooded soil. It is best to plant right after the early rains begin when the soil is moist enough to encourage germination without drowning the seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ loo eha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ shweremɔ he hewalɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my plants start rotting or turning yellow when it rains continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high moisture levels around leaves and roots, which prevents plants from breathing properly and encourages fungal diseases like root rot and leaf blight to spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa tsei lɛ ahe kɛbaa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tsei lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Should I space my crops further apart when planting during the wet season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, wider spacing during the rainy season improves airflow between plants, helping foliage dry faster after rain and reducing the spread of moisture-loving plant diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni eha tsei ahe helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi

english: How do I prevent rainwater from flooding my farm and damaging crop roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni ekafite tsei shishifãi lɛ?

english: Digging shallow drainage trenches or furrows throughout your farm helps redirect standing rainwater away from your crop roots and down into safe outlet areas.
ga: Buu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mlifomɔ. Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops while it is actively raining heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Heavy downpours wash fertilizer away from the soil before the roots have time to absorb it, wasting your money and potentially damaging nearby water sources.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to harvest my crops while it is raining heavily?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli?

english: Harvesting during heavy rains introduces excess moisture to mature crops, which causes rapid rot or mold growth, and walking on wet soil hardens it, damaging the soil structure for future crops.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ baaha tsei ni eda lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ nyiɛmɔ baaha tso lɛ mli awa. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I safely dry my harvested crops when the weather remains cloudy and wet?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mikpamɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo atatu lolo ni edɔ lɛ?

english: You can dry harvested crops by building raised wooden platforms covered with clear plastic sheets, which protect the crops from rainfall while using natural warmth and airflow to dry them.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ni okpa lɛ agbi kɛtsɔ tso ni awo nɔ ni oootswa ni okɛ plastic ni mli tse aha nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ he. yɛ be mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛgbi.

english: How should I divide land clearing tasks among my farm workers so the bush doesn't grow back before we finish?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ aja shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ mli mawo ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ateŋ? Koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ dani wɔgbe naa?

english: Dividing the land into smaller, manageable sections and placing teams of two workers on specific plots ensures that clearing, weeding, and planting happen quickly before weeds have time to regrow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlijaa yɛ fãi bibii ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛ nitsulɔi enyɔ akuu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ajie jwɛi lɛ, ni adu lɛ oya dani jwɛi lɛ aná be ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves turning yellow and dying after I water them with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ faa mli nu fɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: River water polluted by heavy mud and mining chemicals chokes crop roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients and oxygen from the soil.
ga: Faa mli nu ni muji ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔji amli lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to use water from a muddy brown river to irrigate my tomato farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baafɔ mi tomato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: No, heavily polluted river water contains thick silt and toxic residues that clog soil pores, burn fragile crop roots, and drastically lower your harvest yield.
ga: Dabi, faa lɛ mli nu ni mli ewo muji waa lɛ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsiɔ sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Shã tso shishifãi ni waaa lɛ. ni oha okpamɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why are my plantain leaves drooping even when the ground feels wet from nearby river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemicals and excess sediment in contaminated water damage the fine root hairs of plantains, preventing the plant from drinking water even if the soil is soaked.
ga: Tsofai ni fa fe nine kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ plantains shishifãi bibii lɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Can dirty river water change the taste or quality of the food crops I harvest?
ga: Ani faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ atsake niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha?

english: Yes, crops absorb harmful substances and excess minerals from polluted water, which ruins fruit development, alters taste, and causes produce to rot faster after harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ minerals ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli. ni fiteɔ aduawai lɛ adalɛ. tsakemɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ

english: Can cassava or yam absorb harmful chemicals if I plant them near an illegal mining site?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo ŋmei baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui? Kɛji midu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he ko ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ akɛ atsu nii yɛ lɛ

english: Yes, root crops like cassava and yam absorb heavy metals and chemicals directly from contaminated soil and groundwater, making the tubers unsafe for consumption.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii.

english: Why are my maize crops stunted and weak when planted on land close to where people dig for gold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Gold digging washes toxic chemicals into the earth and strips away the natural soil balance, leaving crops without the rich nutrients needed to grow tall and produce full ears.
ga: Shika tsuru ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ tsofai fɔji ahe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my farmland no longer grow healthy crops after the surrounding topsoil was scraped away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Topsoil contains all the dark organic matter and nutrients crops need; removing it leaves behind hard, infertile clay that cannot support crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ diŋ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli wa ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly when the ground near my farm turns hard and baked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya beni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ais ni eshãa lɛ?

english: When trees and vegetation are cleared, the bare soil loses its natural sponge-like ability to hold moisture, causing heat to bake the ground and dry out crop roots rapidly.
ga: Kɛji ajie tsei kɛ tsei lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su ni tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ dɔlɛ ni ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees turn brown when covered in thick dirt dust from nearby earth digging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni muji ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ ŋshɔ ni atsa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Thick dust settling on cocoa leaves blocks sunlight, preventing the leaves from breathing and making the food the tree needs to grow healthy pods.
ga: Muji ni mli tse ni shwieɔ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why should I plant a line of trees along the edge of my farm near the riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Tree roots act as a natural barrier and filter, trapping polluted muddy runoff and chemicals before they can flow onto your cropland and ruin your soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii kɛ tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ nu. Emɔɔ muji kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ lɛ dani eboteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field and choke the roots so they cannot take up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii.

english: Why do cowpea plants make the soil richer for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have special tiny nodules on their roots. These nodules take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind in the soil.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or when tiny pests like mirids attack them. Proper shade control and timely spraying help the flowers form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ Mirids tutua amɛ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it risky to cut down all the big shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Big trees protect cocoa bushes from harsh sun and heavy winds, keep the ground cool and moist, and shed leaves that decay into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after growing for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni midu amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand. If the ground is too hard, or if you planted a poor stem variety, the plant spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Aloo kɛji odu tso ni ehiii lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick straight downwards. Raised mounds provide soft, loose soil for the tubers to expand easily while letting excess rainwater drain away so the yam does not rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛmli edɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ ni ehoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Keeping the farm free of weeds helps reduce these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my plantain stem fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by microscopic soil worms called nematodes or stem borer beetles. Staking the stems and planting clean suckers prevents the plant from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem-boring beetles baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni he tse wo tso lɛ mli ni odu lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to survive tough conditions. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your planted crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and lose water quickly. Planting food crops like plantain alongside them provides living shade to protect the young trees until they grow tough enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Will masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba koni ebu tsei bibii ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baaná tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is missing nitrogen, which is an essential soil food. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack open slightly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa fioo.

english: Why do extension officers recommend that I plant beans or cowpeas together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize plant. Planting them together improves soil health and gives you two different harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehaa onine shɛɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and soft caterpillars hiding in the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed rapidly on young crop shoots, but spraying recommended neem solutions or approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening effectively controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii oya. Shi kɛ́ okɛ neem tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves and cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai egbi kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing easily.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when plants already have small roots to absorb it, usually about two weeks after seeds sprout. Applying it when the soil is slightly moist ensures the crop can drink up the nutrients safely without leaf burn.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni eshãaa baai lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from harvested maize lose their natural strength and yield lower amounts of grain in the second season. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures strong growth, disease resistance, and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ baa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa amɛdaraa waa, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and look wilted in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During very hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. The plant intentionally droops to reduce water loss, and it naturally revives as the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ tsei anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebaate shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller cob size and fruit even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ cob dalɛ mli kɛ yibii bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal light, root space, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crop full access to food and water so it can produce large fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their tender leaves dry out easily. Planting shade crops like plantains near them creates a cooler environment that protects the leaves until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛbashi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay dark green and build large, full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo toi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills up all air pockets, leaving roots without oxygen. When cassava roots stay submerged in wet soil for too long, fungal diseases quickly attack and spoil the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Fungal helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress the tomato plant, causing it to shed its flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve water and energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ baai akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo aduawai.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni maha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to capture maximum sunlight so their leaves can create food to grow large underground tubers. Lifting them up on stakes exposes all leaves to light and reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ awó amɛnɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in my young corn leaves with small brown drops inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves inside the central funnel of the plant, leaving behind their waste material that looks like coarse sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep the soil moist longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛfataa pepper tsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil. It blocks direct sunlight from heating up the ground, which drastically cuts down water evaporation from the soil surface.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same farm with my cassava help improve the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, acting as a natural food supply for surrounding crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods develop dark black spots and spoil during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture and continuous rain allow the Black Pod fungal disease to travel in water droplets between pods, quickly destroying the beans inside.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa black pod fungal hela lɛ fãa gbɛ yɛ nu mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my farm just before a heavy rainstorm begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the loose fertilizer from the root zone into nearby streams before the plant roots have enough time to drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up like tight straws during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves roll up in the hot sun, the plant is trying to save water. By curling its leaves, it reduces the surface area exposed to the heat, stopping moisture from escaping into the air.
ga: Beni ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Is a light drizzle enough water for my newly planted groundnut seeds to germinate?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmei dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: A light drizzle only wet the very top layer of the soil and dries up quickly. Seeds need moist soil that stays wet a few inches deep so their first roots can drink water and sprout properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni egbiɔ oya. Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ aaafee 2-3 inch bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Plants send water and food to their new top leaves first when nutrients or water in the soil are low. Yellowing bottom leaves mean the plant is sacrificing its oldest leaves to keep growing new ones.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu kɛ niyenii majeɔ baai heei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ niyenii loo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiŋmɛɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe koni eha baai heei aya nɔ ada.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots remaining thin like pencil sticks while the leaves are very big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ pensil lɛ? Baai lɛ dara ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, sweet potatoes focus all their energy on growing tall stems and green leaves instead of storing energy underground in fat roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ zugba sisi ngɛ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ fɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience temperature stress or lack water. Without enough balance, the plant sheds flowers because it feels it cannot support developing heavy fruit.
