ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ejaakɛ enuɔ he akɛ enyɛŋ ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn dark brown and leathery before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani ekwɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull calcium from the soil into the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering patterns where the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrink while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease caused by fungi that thrive in cold, wet weather. Excess shade and moisture help fungal spores travel in water droplets from leaf to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo haa fungal spores lɛ fãa gbɛ akɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa pod lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves look like someone sprayed white flour on them during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛ powda yɛŋ efɔ amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: That white substance is powdery mildew fungus. It spreads quickly when air is humid and leaves stay wet, feeding off the nutrients inside the plant leaves.
ga: Nakai nɔ yɛŋ lɛ ji powdery mildew tsɛŋemɔ hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni baai lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Training them onto tall stakes exposes more leaf area to the sun, allowing the plant to make food that feeds the growing tuber below the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ atsɔse amɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baa lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees take longer to produce fruit if I leave too many suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Suckers are baby shoots attached to the main plantain mother. If there are too many, they drink the food and water meant for the main mother stem, slowing down its fruit production.
ga: Shoots ji gbekɛbii ashishifãi ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ nyɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ babaoo Amɛbaanu niyenii kɛ nu kɛha nyɛ tso titri lɛ. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce healthy cobs. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus transmitted by them. Controlling these small pests early prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant growing healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed most of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water during dry, hot spells. By losing its leaves, the plant slows down moisture loss and stays alive until the rains return to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo, ni ehiɔ shi aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ ni baa heei baa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell of heat. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young seedlings will dry up and die because the ground lacks deep, steady moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa be ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under intense, direct sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows all leaves to capture sunlight, which leads to bigger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baa fɛɛ baa nyɛɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of wind and insect activity for pollination cause tomato plants to drop flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding extreme dryness helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bɛ kɛha pollination. Ha tomato tsei lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi that rot the tubers, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already wild and adapted to survive harsh conditions in the soil. Once you clear the farm, sunshine and air trigger these dormant weed seeds to germinate long before cultivated crop seeds get established.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ momo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji otsi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Ekwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of thick green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving cowpea too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing big green leaves instead of flowers. Cowpea naturally creates its own nitrogen, so it needs phosphorus instead to encourage pod development.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, fosforo he miihia moŋ koni eha pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes when the weather becomes very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot, dry weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent itself from drying out completely.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni etsiɔ enaa koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: If it rains just a little bit after a long dry spell, will that be enough to save my maize crop?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo pɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ Ani enɛ baafee nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛduɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: A small amount of rain gives the plant temporary relief by cooling it down and moistening the topsoil, but if the dry conditions return quickly, the roots won't get enough water to grow strong grains. Mulching can help retain that little moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ be kukuoo ko kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ oya lɛ Shishifãi lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Mulching baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after the first rain can be risky because early rains are often followed by unexpected dry spells. It is usually safer to wait until the soil is deeply moist and the rainfall becomes more regular.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do some new maize seeds grow better than our local seeds when there is little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shia dumɔwui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Newer improved seed varieties are specifically bred by researchers to either mature faster before the water runs out or to tolerate dry conditions longer than traditional local seeds.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi ji mɛi ni fɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani nu lɛ baaho. aloo koni enyɛ edamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa be kakadaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ.

english: Why does maize need more water when it starts showing silk and tassels than when it is young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa beni ebɔi siliki kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ fe be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: The flowering stage, when tassels and silk appear, is when the plant forms the cob and grains. If the crop lacks water during this period, the cob will not fill properly, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Fɔfɔi afeemɔ be mli ni tassels kɛ silk jeɔ kpo. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei feɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Cob lɛ eyiŋ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: What will happen to my crop if I put fertilizer on the field when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔji amli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so that the plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots and damage the plants.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: Why does maize grown on one section of my field survive dry weather better than maize on another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil types vary across a field. Areas with higher clay content or more rich organic matter hold onto rainwater much longer during dry spells than areas with loose, sandy soil.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ henɔi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe hei ni sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Does planting my maize seeds close together protect the plants from dying during drought?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baabu tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete against each other for the limited water and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough water to survive.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhi shi.

english: Will my maize plants yield good grain if rain comes late when the leaves are already yellow?
ga: Ani mi-abele lɛ baawo dumɔwui kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba sɛɛ ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ momo?

english: Late rain helps save the plant from dying completely, but if yellow leaves mean the plant was severely damaged during its critical growth phase, the final yield will still be lower than normal.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛgboii kwraa. Shi kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efite waa yɛ edalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baakã he ahi shi fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Can planting beans together with my maize help my farm survive when the rains are unreliable?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with leguminous crops like beans covers the bare soil, reducing water evaporation and keeping the ground cooler, which helps the farm handle dry weather better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔji ni amɛkpeɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle strong direct sunlight and can easily burn or dry up. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves, providing living shade and keeping the soil moist to protect young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei lɛ akwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the heavy rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain, but not during heavy downpours. Burying or covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the base of the plant prevents rain from washing it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ futu loo okɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and heavy shade. Pruning excess leaves and branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of young maize plants during the day. Inspecting fields early and using approved treatments or neem oil can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa hei ni tamɔ nɛkɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up competing against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishitso ni mli wa kɛ tso lɛ shishifã agbo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I wait for two good rains before planting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Dry or barely damp soil does not have enough moisture for seeds to germinate successfully, causing them to dry up or rot. Waiting for steady rains ensures the ground has deep moisture to support rapid sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo efɔ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛgboɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Ani amɛyeɔ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled by the lower leaves yellowing and dropping off. Harvesting at the right time prevents the tubers from becoming woody, tough, and difficult to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata okadii lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ tso, ni ewa ni ehoomɔ wa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Sick cocoa trees usually show visible signs like black spots on the pods, leaves turning yellow or drying out prematurely, fungal mold on the bark, or pods rotting before they ripen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ kpo. Fungs yɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: If a disease attacks my farm right before harvest, can I still harvest the healthy pods?
ga: Kɛji hela ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Yes, you can harvest mature pods that show no signs of sickness, but you must harvest them immediately and strictly keep infected pods separate to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii ni eda ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he lɛ. Shi esa akɛ okpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ogbala ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal diseases like Black Pod, which thrive in damp, overly shady farms with high rainfall and poor air circulation between trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal helai tamɔ black pods, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn a deep orange-yellow.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su etsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to sprout or rot, which destroys the quality of the cocoa, lowers selling price, and attracts disease to the farm.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. ni fiteɔ kookoo lɛ kpakpa ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi ni egbalaa helai kɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is the correct way to cut pods off the cocoa tree without hurting the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni afiteee tso lɛ?

english: Use a sharp machete or harvesting hook to slice cleanly through the pod stem, being careful not to damage the bark cushion on the trunk where future flowers and pods grow.
ga: Kɛ kakla loo ŋmei ni naa wa atsu nii ni okɛfo pod lɛ shishifã lɛ mli ni ehe tse. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okafite tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ he ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my crop when it is near harvest time?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain creates damp conditions that allow fungal diseases to spread quickly across mature pods, while making it much harder to properly dry harvested beans.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ akɛ amɛaagbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees droop and turn brown during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves and wilt during dry weather to save water. Planting shade trees alongside cocoa protects them from direct heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why is clearing bush and pruning trees important for crop health?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ahewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning branches and removing tall weeds opens up the farm to sunlight and fresh air, which reduces dampness that causes crop diseases and helps flowers form into pods.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when trees suffer from water shortages, lack nutrients in the soil, or are attacked by insect pests like capsids that feed on young buds.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu ni faaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni yeɔ tsei bibii akɛ niyenii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is missing nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted directly under open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot withstand direct scorching sun. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them creates a living umbrella that protects the seedlings from extreme heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: The small extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha plantain ni tsii ni agbo lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my crop field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi daa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, and they also hide harmful insects that attack plants. Clearing them gives your crops full access to food and reduces pest damage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa tsei lɛ hu teeɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked water for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ awo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can drink it. Morning watering lets the roots soak up the moisture fully so the plant can handle the day's heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu lɛ kwraa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside tiny pods on their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny insects attack the blooms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and spraying natural remedies like soapy water or neem oil helps the plant set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves have holes in them with powdery dirt inside the top funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of the plant to eat the soft leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended pest treatments directly into the plant funnel will stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei ateŋ koni amɛye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit leaf viruses. Removing heavily infected plants and controlling the insects with organic insecticides will keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ, ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ akudɔ kooloi lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow well. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the roots will help fix this.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Root he lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Spraying the leaves with neem oil mixture or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are receiving too much direct sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees getting too much full sun will have brown, burnt leaf edges, dry leaves, and slow growth. Cocoa plants need shade trees or temporary plants like plantains above them to block harsh sunlight while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ babaoo lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛshishigbɛ shãa, amɛbaai ni egbi, ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ blɛoo. Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni baa be kukuoo mli, tamɔ kooyigbɛ plantains, koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become twisted when the soil beneath them is too hard or stony for the roots to push down easily. Making deep, loose soil mounds or ridges allows the yam to expand downwards smoothly without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli shwereɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone and crack open during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil bakes hard and cracks when heavy clay ground loses all its water under bare sun exposure. Covering the soil surface with dried grass or leaves—known as mulch—keeps the soil cooler and holds moisture inside.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni sũ ni tsii lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ fite yɛ hulu la ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ shishi. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli.

english: Young crop seedlings have weak, small roots that cannot win against wild weeds for soil food, water, and space. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ aye koo mli jwɛi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ ŋwɛi. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant goes through dry periods without steady water. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning keeps the soil cool and stops flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ tsɔ be ni nu bɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are my groundnut pods coming out empty with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ jeɔ kpo efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil while the pods are expanding underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting provides the calcium needed to fill the pods.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha calcium ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning black and soft after just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally spoil very quickly once dug up because air enters the cuts and causes rapid decay. It is best to leave cassava in the soil until the exact day you are ready to sell, eat, or process it.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji atsa amɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ he ni afo lɛ mli ni egboɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashi gbi ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ, oye, loo otsu he nii.

english: Why are my plantain stems splitting open near the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli gbalaa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Splitting stems in plantain trees are usually caused by banana stem weevil larvae boring holes inside the trunk, weakening the plant. Keeping the base of the plant clean of old rotting leaves helps prevent weevils from breeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, banana weevil larvae ni tswaa bu yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ mligbalamɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishi he tse kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ ni miifite lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no larger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full sunlight because their leaves are tender. Planting shade crops like plantains protects the tender cocoa plants from heat stress and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa is strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ baai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK gives the maize the food it needs to build strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛ nitrogen fee, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall bushy stems but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given excessive nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients into the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baatsuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually only wet the top surface of the dry soil. If a sunny dry spell follows, the soil heats up and bakes the sprouting seeds; it is safer to wait until the ground is thoroughly soaked by steady rain before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ hulu ni egbi yɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eshãa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress from sudden hot weather or inconsistent watering. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and stay alive rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and waste inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the tight growing tip of the young maize plant, eating the leaves before they open up and leaving sawdust-like waste behind.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ ashishigbɛ. Ye baai lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni oshi ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does leaving dry crop stalks on top of my cleared farmland help my soil stay moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe tsei ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu nɔ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry plant materials on top of the soil creates a protective cover called mulch. This layer shades the soil from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and decays into rich organic plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe nibii ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii babaoo ni jɛ wala mli

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over easily during windstorms when I plant multiple seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight with each other for light and soil water. They stretch upward too fast to catch sunlight, resulting in tall, weak stalks that fall over easily.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu kɛ la yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya tsɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to stay off the damp ground so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to produce food for the roots. Lifting the leaves away from the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases from ruining the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ajie sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants finish growing and decompose, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to naturally fertilize the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni tsei daraa ni amɛfiteɔ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in rainy or humid weather. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to let in light, and removing affected pods early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. weeding Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ mli koni eha la afee mlɛo ni ajie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but only turn a few into pods. Drops happen if tiny insects called midges aren't around to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Drops baa kɛji kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji kɛha pollination. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantain trees or shade trees to protect their foliage and keep the soil cool until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark green powder inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ashiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended biological or chemical treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them best.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with heavy leaves but give me small cassava tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsii shi cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf growth instead of roots. Balance the soil with potassium and phosphorus, and avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen-rich fertilizers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Ehaa sũ lɛ mli potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs lɛ feɔ ekome. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ he fe nine lɛ he.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Should I let all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem keep growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi plantain tsei titri lɛ yaa nɔ edaa?

english: No, you should cut away extra shoots (suckers) and leave only 2 or 3 of different sizes. Allowing too many shoots creates competition for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ (ŋmeii) ni oshi ŋmeii srɔtoi 2 loo 3 pɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is called mulching. Dry grass traps moisture in the soil, prevents weeds from taking over, keeps the root area cool during heat waves, and slowly breaks down into plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni efiteɔ tsei aniyenii lɛ fiofio.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients before my crops start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Warning signs include slow plant growth, pale or yellow leaves instead of deep green, and stems remaining thin. A soil test or observing leaf color patterns helps identify specific missing nutrients.
ga: Kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji: Tso lɛ daa blɛoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa loo baa lɛ su he mfonirifeemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ mli.

english: Can I plant pepper and tomatoes right next to each other on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is better to separate them because peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family. Planting them together allows pests and diseases like blights and wilt to spread rapidly between both crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ weku kome mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because bright, direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei komɛi ni eda loo tsei ni daraa ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid environments. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the trees, which dries out moisture and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen, or that too much water is drowning the roots. Feeding the soil with manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the dark green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of corn plants. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical sprays protects the crop before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei amli baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in flat or heavy soil, or if infected stem cuttings were planted. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Adumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ kɛha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes to lift their leaves into the sunlight. When leaves get plenty of sun, they create more energy, which leads to larger and healthier yam tubers growing under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛje kpo kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat or irregular watering while flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during the flowering period helps the plants set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and causing the plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling insects early keeps leaves flat and lets the plant continue growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Mra Be mli Kooloi Ahe Nitsumɔ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha tso lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry period that can scorch delicate sprouts. Waiting until the rainy season is fully established ensures the soil stays consistently moist so seeds can survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops better over time than chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed crops quickly but do not improve the soil itself, whereas animal manure improves soil structure, helps it hold water longer, and releases nutrients continuously for future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya shi ehaaa sũ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ bei lɛ be fɛɛ be

english: When maize plants do not get enough nitrogen from the soil, they take the nutrients from their older, bottom leaves and send them to the growing top leaves. This causes the lower leaves to turn yellow and die off early.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help my maize grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, giving the next crop free food to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops give me smaller yields when I plant seeds close together instead of giving them space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he ni maha amɛ gbɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete for the same sunlight, soil food, and water. Because none of the plants get enough, they all grow thin and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kome. Ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni náa nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is fresh and strong enough to grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ eyɛ ehee ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A good cassava cutting should come from a healthy plant that is at least eight months old, have hard stems with visible intact buds, and show fresh sap or moisture when you nick the bark.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji kpaanyɔ mli. Eyɛ tso ni wa kɛ fɔfɔii ni anaa jogbaŋŋ. ni etsɔɔ latex loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛji otsi ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get scorched leaves when there are no plantains planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni eshã yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act like umbrellas to shade the young cocoa and keep the surrounding soil moist until the trees are strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni shwereɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and look dead during hot afternoons even when the ground is slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant purposely wilts to reduce its surface area and protect itself from drying out, then recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛgboiɔ koni amɛha amɛhe lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. The stress causes the plant to save its energy rather than feed growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Haomɔ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ amɛhewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaye tomato ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain bunch stay very small even after the main plant has grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso titri lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ?

english: If a plantain tree produces too many sucker shoots around its base, those suckers steal water and food from the main mother plant, leaving it with very little energy to fill out the fruit bunch.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu ko yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle eshishi lɛ he lɛ, nakai ŋmeii lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaawo aduawai akuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars hide inside the funnel of my young maize plants, and how does that affect the grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Those caterpillars (like the Fall Armyworm) eat the tender, young leaves inside the plant's growing funnel where new leaves form. This prevents the plant from making food, resulting in weak plants and empty corn cobs.
ga: Caterpillars (tamɔ Fall Armyworm) yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ gbɛi lɛ amli he ni baai heei miiba lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafee niyenii Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa.

english: Why shouldn't I pour granular fertilizer right against the stem of my cassava or maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer woɔ mi-cassava loo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of plant stems and roots. Putting it directly against the stem can burn and kill the plant tissue, so it should always be placed a small distance away in moist soil.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji ashã ni amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer and smaller pods this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfee bibii afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees peak in production between 10 and 20 years of age. As trees grow older, their soil nutrients become depleted and their root systems grow less efficient, which reduces pod size and total yield unless the farm is fertilized or renovated.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛyibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛye afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha pod lɛ dalɛ kɛ nɔ ni afee lɛ fɛɛ aba shi. Ja awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo asaa lɛ.

english: Does direct sunlight help my cocoa trees grow better, or do they need big shade trees around them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo ehe miihia ni tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ abɔle ehe?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under forest canopies and burn easily under full sun. Shade trees protect cocoa leaves from harsh heat, keep the soil moist, and protect young plants from drying out during hot seasons.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ latsaa be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trunk dry up and drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree lacks water or nutrients, or if tiny pollinating insects like midges are missing. High temperatures or pest damage can also cause unpollinated flowers to fall off naturally.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo, kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ laaje lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔ ni ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn dark brown or black during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and moisture. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight in and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la babaoo abote mli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: How can I know if my farm's soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of weak soil include pale yellow leaves, thin tree trunks, slow growth, and pods that stop growing before reaching full size. If rainfall is good but crops still perform poorly, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he okadii ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso shishifã bibioo lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii ni kpaɔ dalɛ dani eshɛɔ dalɛ he. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ hi shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree, won't I be reducing the number of pods it can bear?
ga: Kɛji mifo niji babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ Ani minyɛŋ mafo ŋmɔtɔi ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ lɛ ayibɔ shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary or unproductive branches actually increases crop yields. It directs energy into pod-bearing stems, allows sunlight to reach the inner trunk, and prevents dark conditions where fungal diseases multiply.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei ni hiɛ pod lɛ anɔ. Ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. ni atsĩ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do strange green bushes grow directly on my cocoa tree branches, and are they harmful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ miida yɛ mikoo tso lɛ niji anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Ni ani amɛhe yɛ oshara?

english: These bushy plants are mistletoe parasites that attach their roots directly into the cocoa tree's stem to steal water and plant food, eventually causing branches to wither and reducing overall farm output.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nɛɛ ji mistletoe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kpãa cacao tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my cocoa plants to turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yellowing leaves during dry spells happen when the tree is trying to save water by dropping foliage. It can also mean the soil lacks moisture or essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do tall weeds under my cocoa canopy slow down the growth of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ mikookoo shishi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crop roots for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. High weed growth also traps humidity near ground level, creating ideal conditions for pests and pod diseases to spread.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hu mɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ pod helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How does a long dry season affect my young crop plants, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsĩ naa?

english: Extended dry periods stress young crops by drying out topsoil roots and scorching tender foliage. Leaving plant mulch—like dried leaves or plantain leaves—around the base of crops keeps the soil cooler and retains moisture longer.
ga: Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ haoɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi ni egbiɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo plantain baai, yɛ otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Flowers fall off when crops experience water stress or high temperatures. When a plant does not get enough rain during flowering, it gets stressed and sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Kɛ tsei lɛ náaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Will hot weather and a lack of rain cause my crop blossoms to drop?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, intense sunshine and hot dry spells cause plants to lose water rapidly. Without adequate soil moisture, the plant cannot support flower growth, causing the blossoms to dry up and drop off.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Is rain really that important when my crops start showing flowers?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he hiaa diɛŋtsɛ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kpojiemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage of crop growth. Water is essential at this stage so the plant can support flower growth, complete pollination, and successfully start forming fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ tso dalɛ mli. Nu he miihia yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ. egbe pollination lɛ naa ni ebɔi yibiiwoo feemɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli

english: Does even a small shower of rain help my crops when they are flowering during a dry period?
ga: Ani nugbɔ fioo po baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, even a small amount of rain helps significantly. A light shower provides just enough moisture to cool the plant and prevent flowers from drying up and falling off.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ fioo ko yeɔ ebuaa waa. Hejuu ni waaa Ha hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ. ni etsĩ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkagbee shi

english: What happens if a dry spell lasts for a long time while my crops are blooming?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ tee nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: If a dry spell lasts too long, the plant will drop most or all of its flowers to stay alive, which severely reduces the number of fruits or pods you will get at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo loo fɛɛ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ baaha aduawai loo ŋmeii ni obaaná yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why are flowers so important for getting a good yield at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ahe hiaa koni aná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Flowers are where fruits, pods, and grains develop. If your plant loses its flowers, it cannot produce the actual crop you sell or eat, such as pepper, cocoa pods, or vegetables.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji he ni aduawai, pods, kɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Kɛji otso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fite lɛ Enyɛŋ hu ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye, tamɔ ŋmeii, kookoo ŋmeii, loo aduawai.

english: Can my crops produce new flowers if rain returns after a short dry spell?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔii heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if the dry period is short and rain returns in time, healthy crops can produce a new set of flowers and continue forming fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ji kuku ni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔii akui heei ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops look weak and drop their parts during prolonged sunny periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During long sunny periods without rain, plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can take from the dry soil, forcing them to drop flowers and weak stems to save water.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔi kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbu nu he.

english: How can I protect my flowering crops if the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa?

english: You can cover the soil around the roots with dried grass or leaves (mulching) to trap moisture, or carry water directly to the plant bases to help them hold onto their flowers until rains resume.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) aha shishifãi lɛ ahe koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Aloo okɛ nu aya tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it normal to lose a few flowers during the dry period if some rain falls?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ fɔfɔi komɛi baafite yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Yes, it is normal to lose a few, but as long as some rain falls to keep the plant hydrated, enough flowers will remain on the plant to give you a reasonable harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ ekomɛi baafite. Shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ ahi shi lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa baakã tso lɛ nɔ koni eha bo yibiiwoo ni sa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am establishing new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist for the young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa and plantain crops, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ plantains adu ŋmei? Aloo ebaafite amɛ?

english: Cassava grows very dense roots and consumes large amounts of water and nutrients from the upper soil, which can starve young cocoa trees and slow down plantain growth.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse waa ni eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do groundnut plants flower above the ground but produce the actual nuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it grows a small stem called a peg that extends downward and pushes into the soil, where it safely develops into the peanut pod away from heat and light.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Ebaaná ŋmei bibioo ko. Atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwereɔ kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaatsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hulutsoo kɛ la bɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve the soil for my other crops later on?
ga: Peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, it leaves enriched soil behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens if I plant my groundnuts too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting groundnuts too close together creates competition for sunlight and moisture, restricts airflow which encourages fungal diseases, and leaves no space underground for the nuts to spread out and grow big.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa, ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Ni he ko bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara.
