english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest without pulling up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikuuu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are generally ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dry out. You can test a few sample plants; if the inside of the pods has developed dark brown or black markings, the crop is mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka tsei komɛi ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara kwraa.

english: My plantain trees are growing many small shoots at the base. Should I leave all of them to grow?
ga: Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Lots at the base Ani esa akɛ mashi lɛ kɛkɛ koni eda kwraa?

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. You should prune them to leave only two or three strong suckers per stand.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi suckers (tsoji) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains shed their lower leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect the main stem and fruit from drying out completely.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ kɛ enɔ yibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong wind and heavy rain compared to cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli kɛ akɛto kookoo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like woody trees. They have shallow fibrous roots and top-heavy stems filled with water, making them vulnerable to strong winds, especially when carrying heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nyɛɔ efiteɔ amɛ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ otere tsɔne ni tsii.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick trunk and big branches instead of the tips of the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji wuji anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei niji lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are large and heavy. The tree naturally flowers on thick bark—a process called cauliflory—so the main trunk and sturdy branches can support the weight of the growing pods without breaking.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛtsii. Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yibii ni mli tse nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cauliflower—no hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri ni wa kɛ eniji lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ nɔ ni efoŋ.

english: Why is it important to measure exact distances between my crops instead of just planting them anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he fɛɛ he

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for food and light, which results in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right planting distance for the crops on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops need different amounts of room to grow; larger crops like trees need several feet between them, while smaller crops like maize or vegetables need less. Following recommended measurements gives roots room to spread and leaves room to catch sunlight.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ he srɔtoi koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nibii ni aduɔ agboi tamɔ tsei biɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee ninetalɔi babaoo. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai biɔ nɔ ko fioo. Susumɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eha gbɛ aha hulu la.

english: Should I clear big stones and old roots from my soil before I plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tɛi wuji kɛ shishifãi momo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu?

english: Yes, removing large stones and hard obstacles allows plant roots to grow deep into the soil easily. It also makes weeding easier and prevents damage to your farm tools when working the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tɛi wuji kɛ gbɛtsii nibii ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa oŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ afite kɛji ootsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my land is fully prepared for sowing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Your field is ready when the soil is cleared of major weeds and heavy debris, loosened up for root growth, and has received enough rain to stay moist so seeds can sprout easily.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo beni ajie sũ lɛ kɛjɛ jwɛi wuji kɛ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ amli lɛ. Gbalamɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ada. ni amɛnáa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my farm damage my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn the roots and leaves of your plants, turning them yellow or killing them. It is always best to apply only the recommended amount so you do not spoil the soil or waste money.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo. Esa akɛ akɛ shika ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ pɛ atsu nii bɔni afee ni akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akafite shika.

english: What happens to my crops if I give them too much water?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli fe nine?

english: Too much water fills up the empty spaces in the soil and starves the roots of air, causing them to rot. Balanced watering keeps the roots healthy and prevents crop diseases.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. haa egboɔ Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baaa amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops changing color from green to yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ eŋɔli kɛmiiya ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that it is getting too much or too little water. It can also be an early warning sign of pest attack or root disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ efee kɔkɔbɔɔ mra hu akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo shishifã hela eba.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop to reduce water loss during intense heat. If they stand back up when the sun goes down, the plant is managing heat normally, but if they stay wilted, your soil needs water.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo efolɔ ehe koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji amɛte shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ he nii bɔ ni sa. Shi kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛgbi Oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nu.

english: How can I keep my land fertile so it continues to produce good harvests for my children in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai eha miwɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ?

english: You can protect your soil by rotating crops, adding organic manure, planting cover crops, and avoiding bush burning. These practices keep the soil rich in food and organic matter for many years.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni dumɔ ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ he Nifeemɔi nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on the same plot of land next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake tsei ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Changing crops breaks the cycle of pests and diseases that attack specific plants, and prevents the soil from running out of one particular nutrient.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tsei komɛi lɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni niyenii kpakpa ko akafee nɔ ko

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds around the tree base and pruning extra branches helps air flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil, it spends all its energy making stems and leaves instead of expanding roots. Giving plants space and using the right balanced fertilizer encourages bigger tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee tsei kɛ baai. yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ najiaŋ Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hegbɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo bulbs wuji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atsu nii ni akɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ kɛha gɔŋkɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tubers underwater. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to capture light while preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ la ni ekɛtsi fungal leaf helai anaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a 'V' shape while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the middle of the leaf in a V-shape means your maize lacks nitrogen. Applying fertilizer like urea or NPK at the early growth stage restores green leaves and boosts cob size.
ga: Yellowing jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have pale yellow streaks and the whole plant stays stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Maize Streak Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called leafhoppers. Planting certified disease-resistant maize seeds recommended by extension officers prevents this condition.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Maize Streak hela, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ leafhoppers Abele dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly when the plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Watering consistently at the root zone during cool morning hours keeps the plant relaxed enough to retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ehe jɔɔ lɛ bɔ ni sa koni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips sucking leaf juices and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil solution controls these insects and helps new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baa nu kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni eye ebua ni baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is the bottom end of my young watermelon turning black and rotting on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it expands rapidly, usually triggered by uneven watering. Maintaining steady soil moisture allows the plant to supply calcium steadily to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ calcium haa amɛyibii lɛ daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, that natural nitrogen remains in the soil to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: What does it actually mean when someone says a farm product is organic?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Organic means the product is made from natural sources like plants, animal manure, or natural minerals rather than synthetic chemicals. It nourishes crops and soil without leaving harmful chemical residues.
ga: Organic tsɔɔ akɛ afeɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ tsei, kooloi amli ŋmeii, loo adebɔɔ mli nibii amli. Yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eshiuuu tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which restores fertility to exhausted soil for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or when excessive rain has flooded the field and prevented the roots from breathing.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed. They drop extra flowers when there is water stress, poor soil nutrition, or simply to preserve energy for the remaining pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji nu hao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Aloo koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Staking allows yam leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which is then sent down into the ground to make the tubers grow large and healthy.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and cracks begin to form in the soil around the base of the stem, typically 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ shweremɔ he kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients as the leaves decompose.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he kɛji baai lɛ fite

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering while the plant is growing fast.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Is it better to spray my crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tsofa leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when it is cool, because afternoon heat causes the spray to evaporate too fast and can burn crop leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni eshãa tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunshine. Without shade plants like plantain or cassava to block intense sunlight, the tender leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it, causing yellowing and scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains loo cassava bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshãa.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops leaves during dry spells as a natural way to save water. When rains return, the plant uses stored energy in its roots and stems to quickly grow fresh green leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ oya.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded soil while my maize rots in waterlogged land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that allow oxygen to travel down to flooded roots. Maize roots lack these air channels and suffocate when trapped in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower maize leaves usually means a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen keeps leaves green and healthy; when it runs short, the plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ amɛho lɛ, tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and yield less every year if I plant them on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when plants cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is growing. Regular watering helps roots carry calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there holes in the leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing centre of maize to feed. The sawdust-like material is its waste, indicating an active infestation that requires early control.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ji jwɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ basabasafeemɔ ko ni ehe hiaa ni akudɔ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a plant virus. These insects feed on young leaves and drain the plant's nutrients, causing deformed growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo tsei amli helai kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ. ni kɛ dalɛ ni efite baa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots rather than deep taproots, making it hard for them to balance heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with bamboo or wooden props prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋmɛ aduawai ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei fi tso lɛ shishi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa eshishifã lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward direct sunlight to create food energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sun while protecting them from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee niyenii hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunlight because intense heat burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a cool environment that helps the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shãa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their branches block sunlight from reaching lower leaves and their roots fight over nutrients in the soil. This overcrowding lowers your total crop yield and makes it easier for diseases to spread between trees.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa onitsumɔ fɛɛ baa shi. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai baagbɛ ashwã tsei ateŋ

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them, or if the tree is experiencing stress from drought, extreme heat, or sap-sucking pests like mirids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miina haomɔ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ pollen mli.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties commonly planted in Ghana begin bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting if they receive proper shade, weeding, and rainfall.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji onine shɛ hulutsoo nɔ, jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp weather. Keeping your farm weeded and pruning dense branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out the pods and reduce the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellow, curled cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by a shortage of key nutrients and water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: These extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's energy and nutrients on useless leaf growth. Removing them allows the main tree to direct its energy into producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Afiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko masɛi?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava directly beside young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and steal nutrients and water, while its wide foliage can completely block necessary light from the cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ la ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ naa kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to plant maize without fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataaa he?

english: Dark, moist soil with plenty of broken-down leaves and earthworms is a sign of good natural fertility. If weeds grow very tall and dark green on the plot, maize will usually grow well there too.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baai babaoo ni ekumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ he okadi. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ dara waa ni amɛyɛ su ni tsuɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi hu baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperature rises too high, pepper plants conserve water to keep themselves alive. Dropping their flowers prevents them from spending energy on fruit production during dry, hot spells.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ toɔ nu koni amɛhi shi. Fɔfɔi lɛ ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ haaa amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii yɛ hɔmɔ be kɛ latsaa ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like pencils during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during intense heat as a natural defense to conserve moisture. Reducing the leaf surface exposed to the sun stops water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ hebuu koni ebu fɛ̃i. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ ajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant my tomatoes directly in wet, swampy land near a river?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tomato yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes directly in soggy ground causes root rot because the roots need air to breathe. It is better to build raised soil beds near the water source so the plants stay hydrated without their roots sitting in excess water.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi ni eshishifãi lɛ akabote nu lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Can I use well water or borehole water to irrigate my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nubu loo nubu mli nu awo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, borehole water is suitable for crops, but applying cold underground water during the hottest part of the day can shock hot plants. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe afee shoo. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig and loosen the ground deeply before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow thick and expand deep underground. Softening and loosening the soil makes it easy for the roots to push through the ground and swell, leading to bigger yields.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfuu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my land weeks before planting cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he otsii babaoo dani adu tsina ŋmei lɛ?

english: Preparing land early allows cut weeds time to decay into soil nutrients, while exposing hidden soil pests to the sun so young cowpea seedlings can germinate safely in clean soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi ni afolɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la bɔni afee ni tsina ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and losing leaves when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that sunburn easily. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, air, and nutrients. They grow tall and weak with few branches, resulting in fewer and smaller peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛniji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow in an upside-down 'V' shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing in an upside-down 'V' pattern on lower leaves indicates nitrogen deficiency. The plant steals nitrogen from its oldest leaves to feed new upper growth, signaling that the soil needs organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ 'V' ni atsake lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and dry up naturally at the end of the season, it shows the plant has finished storing energy into the underground tuber and is ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars target the soft center heart of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miitutua mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ atsuii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms target the central whorl of the maize plant because the tissues there are tender, juicy, and shielded from the harsh sun.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ nu, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn yellow even when I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering can drown root systems and encourage soil fungal diseases like root rot. Tomatoes need moist soil, but soaked roots cannot breathe, causing the plant to wilt and drop lower leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Tomato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Shi shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani mikɛ pepper lɛ du lɛ?

english: Peppers drop flowers when they face extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Without enough phosphorus, the plant cannot support fruit development.
ga: Peppers baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right when they are almost ready for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni eshwɛ fioo ni abaahɔɔ amɛ kɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages split when there is a sudden heavy rainfall or heavy watering after a dry period. The inside grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to burst open.
ga: Kaabaji baatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do my okra plants get sticky white spots under the leaves and stop fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ nɔ tsɔi yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekpa yibiiwoo?

english: The white spots are usually pests like whiteflies or mealybugs. They suck energy out of the plant's leaves and spread viruses that destroy productivity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo mealybugs. Amɛmuɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its power to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include yellowish leaves on young plants, thin stems, slow growth, and crops producing tiny, light fruits despite getting sunlight and rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ, tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and watery even though the leaves look large and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ? He ni baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava plants to put all their food energy into leaf growth rather than storing starch in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen moves to the newest top leaves first, leaving older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen lɛ yaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why shouldn't I grow garden eggs on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up in that plot, while draining the specific nutrients garden eggs need to grow well.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɔɔ mli ŋmeii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too tightly causes overcrowding. The plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves on your farm; their roots grow faster and steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops, starving them during critical growth periods.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Can I successfully grow crops in my small backyard garden, or do I need a large farm to get a good harvest?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mishia bibioo lɛ sɛɛ. Ani minitsumɔ lɛ ye omanye? Aloo ŋmɔ agbo he miihia mi koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: You do not need a large farm to produce good food. Backyard gardens are perfect for crops like peppers, tomatoes, and garden eggs. With proper soil care, regular watering, and good sunlight, a small space can give high yields to feed your family.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oná ŋmɔ agbo dani oná niyenii kpakpa. Abɔɔi ni yɔɔ shia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, tomatoi kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nu daa kɛ hulu la kpakpa He bibioo baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he waa yɛ oweku lɛ tsɔsemɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up in intense heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural defense mechanism. However, if the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, it means the crop is dry and urgently needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi ni nu he miihia amɛ oya.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together in the shade, cassava spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of roots. Proper plant spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage energy to go underground to build big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kasava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eya shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulbs agboi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures are too high, when water supply is irregular, or due to a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil damp and covered with mulch cools the roots and prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds as close together as possible so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe bɔ ni manyɛ koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close causes them to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small yields. Giving crops proper spacing lets each plant spread its roots and grow full, healthy fruits.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa kwraa ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants turning yellow and covered in a sticky film?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni akɛ sini ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with a sticky coating indicate sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies. They suck vital sap from the leaves and leave behind a sugary substance that attracts black mold, which blocks sunlight and weakens the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nɔ ko ni shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies. Amɛmuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii diji. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are hungry for manure or extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your pepper plants have pale green or yellow leaves, grow very slowly, or produce small light fruits, they lack key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure or compost restores vital plant food to make leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko lɛ, no lɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot right after the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ pɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra branches from shade trees and weeding around the farm helps sunlight and breeze dry out wet pods to prevent fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: How do leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural plant food stays in the ground to nourish the next crop, like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the water soaks deep into the soil before heat causes it to evaporate. Watering in the hot afternoon heat wastes water quickly and can shock hot roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nu oya, ni ebaanyɛ etswa shishifãi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ.

english: What actually happens to my maize crop if I spray chemical medicine directly on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Selective weedicides are formulated to target broad-leaved weeds without harming grass crops like maize. However, if you use a non-selective chemical or the wrong nozzle, the spray can burn or kill the maize leaves, severely reducing your plant's growth.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa koni akɛtutua jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ni eyeee jwɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa awui. Shi, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni halaaa mɔ tsu nii loo okɛ nozzle ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, Spray lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbe ŋmãa baai. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why does the type of spray nozzle matter when I am applying weed medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ henɔ he hiaa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different nozzles control the size and spread of spray droplets. A dedicated weedicide nozzle creates larger, targeted droplets that cover weeds directly and prevent the chemical from drifting onto your main crop or blowing away in the wind.
ga: Nozzles sɔrɔtoi kudɔɔ bɔ ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Nozzles pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ feɔ droplets agboi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. ni haa jwɛi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaaa tsofai akafo onibii titri lɛ anɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ kɛya.

english: Why do my young crops look yellow or stressed after I spray weed medicine near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛhaoɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops experience chemical stress when the dosage is too high, when spraying is done during hot midday sun, or when spray drifts onto young leaves. Spraying early in the morning when the weather is cool helps plants handle the spray without getting damaged.
ga: Tsei naa tsofa he haomɔ kɛji akɛ tsofa lɛ fa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashɛreɔ tsofa yɛ shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ. aloo be mli ni afua lɛ shwieɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​tsofa lɛ he nii ni efiteee.

english: Is it safe for my crops to spray weed medicine right before it rains?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: If it rains shortly after spraying, the water washes the medicine off the weeds before it can be absorbed, rendering it ineffective. Most chemicals need a few dry hours after application to work properly.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni afɔ lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ Nu lɛ baajie tsofa lɛ kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ mli dani ebaanyɛ etsɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai babaoo biɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi ni akɛgbiɔ beni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my planted maize in the early part of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmãa ni adu mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native, highly aggressive plants adapted to quickly soak up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because cultivated crops like maize take time to establish roots, weeds will easily overtake and starve them if not controlled early.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye nɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ kɛji akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: At what growth stage is it most important to keep weeds away from my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ?

english: The first two to six weeks after your maize sprouts are critical. During this early growth window, weed competition causes irreversible harm to the crop's development, leading to lower grain production at harvest.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ ni ŋmãa ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ he hiaa waa. Yɛ shishijee dalɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ, jwɛi akaŋshii kɛ naagbai ni hiɔ shi daa baa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ni anáa yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Will using chemical weed medicine stop weeds from ever growing back on my farmland?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weedicides only clear active weeds present at the time of spraying or stop seeds near the surface from sprouting temporarily. Millions of dormant weed seeds remain in the soil and will eventually grow, requiring regular field management.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ pɛ loo amɛtsiɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ anaa yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Jwɛi dumɔwui akpekpei abɔ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Will chemical weed medicine weaken my soil for future crops if I use it every season?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛtsu nii daa afi?

english: Approved farm chemicals break down naturally over time and do not destroy soil nutrients directly. However, relying solely on chemicals without adding organic matter or rotating crops can hurt beneficial soil life over many years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni amɛfiteee niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying medicine before it is safe to harvest and eat my crops?
ga: Kɛ́ awo mi tsofa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa ni maye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Every farm chemical has a required wait period, known as the pre-harvest interval, before harvest. This window allows the plant to safely break down chemical residues so the crop is safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani akpaa nii dani akpaa nii. Samflɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli shweshweeshwe. Koni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii

english: What happens to my maize if it matures on the farm but I don't have the means to harvest it right away?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaakpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Leaving dry maize standing in the field exposes it to rain, field mold, insects, and birds. Delayed harvesting leads to rot and pest damage, which reduces both the weight and market value of your grain.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ, ŋmeii, kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi yeɔ enɔ. Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ jarayeli jara fɛɛ baa shi.

english: My crop leaves are turning brown and the tops are going black, does this mean my plant is dying or is it ready for harvest?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ blɔfo ni amɛyitsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mitso lɛ miigbo loo eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Color changes like general browning and blackening at the top of the crop usually indicate physiological maturity rather than disease, showing that the plant has finished growing and is entering the harvest stage.
ga: Su tsakemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ediŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ dalɛ moŋ fe hela. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe dalɛ naa ni ebote kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What simple visual signs on my farm can I look out for to know that my crop is ready to be harvested?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni anaa. Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: You can tell a crop is ready for harvest when the leaves dry and turn brown, the top section turns dark or black, and the seeds or fruits become firm and dry.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ loo ediŋŋ. ni dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi.

english: Once the top of my crop turns black and brown, what am I supposed to do next on the field?
ga: Kɛ mi tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When your crop shows these maturity signs, you should inspect the farm to confirm the seeds are dry, stop any further watering or spraying, and prepare to harvest immediately before rains ruin the crop.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jie dalɛ he okadi kpo Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi. Kpaa nu ni akɛfataa he loo shwiemɔ. ni asaa he koni akpa nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the black color at the top of my crop is a natural sign of maturity or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ su diŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ edara loo hela eba?

english: Natural maturity blackening occurs evenly along with general yellowing or browning of the plant as it dries, while disease blackening usually appears as random spots, leaves slime, or happens while the plant is still young and green.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli diŋfeemɔ baa pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ diŋfeemɔ fɔɔ kpojiemɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni baa trukaa yɛ muji baai lɛ anɔ loo ebaa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Can I harvest my crop as soon as the top starts turning black, or do I need to wait longer?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji yiteŋgbɛi lɛ je shishi amɛfee diŋ pɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ be babaoo?

english: You can begin harvesting once the top has turned black and the overall crop has dried, as this indicates the plant has stopped drawing nutrients and the yield is fully set.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje ŋmaakpamɔ shishi beni yiteŋgbɛi lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jiemɔ, ni egbe nitsumɔ naa.

english: What simple field tests can I do to confirm it is harvest time besides looking at leaf colors?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee ŋmɔ mli kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni yɔɔ ni maa nɔ mi akɛ nikpamɔ be eba? Kɛfata he lɛ, abaakwɛ baai lɛ ahe su

english: Besides checking for brown leaves and black crop tops, you can test maturity by squeezing or biting the seed to check for firmness, or seeing if the crop easily detaches from the main stem.
ga: Kɛfata he lɛ, obaakwɛ kɛji baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yitsei ni ji ediŋŋ lɛ, Obaanyɛ oka amɛkwɛ kɛji amɛshwere hu kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni ooomimɔ loo ooomɔ nɔ koni ona kɛji amɛma shi shiŋŋ. Aloo kwɛmɔ kɛji tso lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he oya.

english: Why is it recommended for me to harvest my crops between late July and early August in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ akpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ July naagbee kɛ August shishijee teŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Harvesting late July to early August takes advantage of favorable dry windows in the season, ensuring your mature crop is picked before heavy rains rot the harvest or prevent proper sun drying.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni afeɔ yɛ July naagbee kɛyashi August shishijee lɛ kɛ samflɛ ni mli egbi yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ. Aloo bu he kɛjɛ hulu la he ni ogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does getting rain for just one week affect when I should harvest my crop?
ga: Te otsi kome ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baaná be ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A week of good rain provides vital late moisture to fill out your crop grains, but once that rain stops and the crop dries brown, you must harvest quickly before another rainy spell spoils the mature yield.
ga: Nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ otsi kome lɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa waa. Shi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, Ebaabi ni okpa oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ kroko ni baa lɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ.

english: What should I do if the rains stop early while my crops are still in the process of turning brown?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: If the rains end early, your crops will dry out faster than usual; you should closely monitor seed hardness and harvest as soon as the tops turn black to prevent pest damage on the dry field.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee mra Oŋmɔshi nibii baagbi oya fe bɔ ni eji daa. Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ha lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ pɛ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ

english: How do I plan my harvest time if the weather and rainfall pattern keep changing unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato mikpamɔ be lɛ he gbɛjianɔ? Ni kɛji bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ tsake trukaa hu?

english: Watch your crop for physical maturity signs like browning leaves and black tops, and aim to clear your field during dry periods around late July or early August rather than relying strictly on the calendar.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ koni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ, tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ kɛ amɛyitsei diji. Ni okɛ ohe awo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ July naagbee loo August shishijee gbɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture, giving the young cocoa trees the canopy protection they need during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa ŋwɛi ŋta ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ dani miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to grow long and thick. High mounds provide loose earth for the tubers to expand easily while allowing excess rainwater to drain away so the yams do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ ni ehoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests now than it did five years ago on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every growing season. If you continuously farm the same land without leaving it to rest, rotating crops, or adding compost and fertilizer, the soil loses its strength and yields drop.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛji oya nɔ otsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli he nii ni ohaaa ejɔɔ ehe, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning light yellow even though it has been raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes up to a year. Intercropping them allows you to harvest maize first while cassava gradually takes over the space, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmei lɛ, edaa blɛoo ni ekɛ afi tsuɔ nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baa fiofio ni ebayeɔ jɛmɛ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa shii 2 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting pepper on the same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ he yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Switching to a different crop family, like maize or beans, starves those pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Ni atsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii aweku kroko nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nakai kooloi lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi baa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Checking your field early and spraying natural remedies like neem seed extract or recommended treatments into the leaf whorl early in the morning will protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant sap and spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or recommended insect sprays protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ loo kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Which part of a cassava stem is best to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: The strong, mature middle section of the stem makes the best planting material. Extremely green top stems dry out quickly, and very woody bottom stems take too long to sprout.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii. Tsoi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbi oya. ni shishigbɛ ni ji tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Is it better to water my cabbage farm in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha kaabii ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate rapidly and can scorch hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: How do I store my harvested maize so that mold and insects do not spoil it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite.

english: To prevent spoilage, ensure your maize is thoroughly sun-dried before storage, place it off the floor on raised wooden pallets, and keep the storage room dry and well-ventilated to stop humidity and pests from ruining your harvest.
ga: koni ekafite Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Akɛwo shikpɔŋ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ha nitoohe lɛ mli agbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if a room or shed is suitable to use as a warehouse for my harvested crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsu loo tsũ ko ni sa akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ baato?

english: A good storage space must have a leak-proof roof, solid floors without cracks where pests can hide, good airflow to prevent heat buildup, and full protection from direct sunlight and rain.
ga: Esa akɛ he ni hi ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ ahi ŋwɛitsu ni nu nyɛŋ abote mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ koni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko. ni ebuɔ he kwraa kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he

english: What should I do to clean and prepare my storehouse before bringing in my new harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni matsumɔ nitoohe lɛ mli ni masaa he dani mikɛ nibii heei aba?

english: You should clear out all old grains and debris, repair cracks in the walls and floor, and ensure the entire space is dry, as leftover crop residues usually carry hidden pests waiting to attack your new yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie dumɔwui momoi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. Saamɔ he ni etse yɛ gbogboi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ni okwɛ koni he fɛɛ he lɛ agbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei amli nibii ni efite lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni miimɛ koni amɛtutua onibii heei lɛ.

english: What is the best way to transport my fresh vegetables from my farm to the market without them rotting on the way?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ aduawai heei kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa jara nɔ ni amɛfiteee yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Harvest in the cool morning hours, load crops into rigid ventilated crates rather than deep sacks to avoid crushing, and cover the transport vehicle with a tarp to shade produce from hot sun during transit.
ga: Kpaamɔ yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ kotokuhi nɛ a mi kuɔ ɔ kɛ woɔ mi konɛ a ko bua a he nya. ni okɛ tarpaulin aha tsɔnei ni akɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ ahe koni ekɛbu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Is it safe to stack my harvested fruits in large woven bags when carrying them on a tricycle or truck?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaawo aduawai ni akpa lɛ awo mama kotokui wuji amli kɛ́ akɛwo baisikle loo lɔle mli?

english: Stacking heavy soft bags causes severe bruising to fruits at the bottom, which creates wounds where rot sets in quickly; using stackable plastic crates protects the fruit from being crushed during movement.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui ni tsii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ to amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔ waa yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni shwieɔ shi oya baa. Plastic adekai ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akashwie aduawai anɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do my yams start to soft-rot quickly after I harvest and store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikpa ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by skin injuries sustained during digging combined with excess moisture and heat; letting harvested yams dry briefly in a shady spot to heal skin cuts before placing them on raised open racks prevents rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa ji hewolo nɔ pilamɔ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ ni fata he lɛ. Ha sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ agbi be kuku yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni etsa pilamɔi dani okɛwo shwɛmɔhei ni awó nɔ ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: How can I protect my stored cowpea beans from being ruined by weevils without applying dangerous chemical powders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ he koni ŋmeii akafite lɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can store fully dried beans inside triple-layer sealed plastic bags (PICS bags) or mix them with clean wood ash, which cuts off air and naturally prevents weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi awo plastic kotokui ni akɛwo mli shii etɛ (PICS kotokui) amli loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse afutu mli. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my grain is dry enough to be safely stored without testing equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni akɛ nibii ni akɛkaa nii lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: A practical check is to bite a grain seed—if it cracks cleanly with a sharp sound, it is dry enough; if it feels soft or leaves a moisture mark, it needs additional sun-drying before storage.
ga: Nɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ji kɛtsɔ dumɔwu lɛ ni oookɔ lɛ nɔ—kɛji efo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ he okadii yɛ esɛɛ Esa akɛ hulu la kroko afata he dani akɛto.

english: Why do government health officers inspect how farmers handle and store food crops after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ helatsamɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ miipɛi bɔ ni okwaafoi kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛtoɔ he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Health officers check storage and transport conditions to ensure food stays free from harmful molds like dangerous toxins (aflatoxins) and dirty contamination, keeping food safe for consumers across the country.
ga: Helatsamɔ he nitsulɔi kwɛɔ bɔ ni akɛ niyenii lɛ toɔ kɛ bɔ ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ niyenii lɛ mli. (Aflatoxin) kɛ mujiwoo Koni niyenii ahi shi shweshweeshwe aha nihɔɔlɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What steps should I follow right after digging up my cassava to keep it from spoiling before sale?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee kɛji mifo ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil within two to three days; you should either process them quickly into dried products like gari or flour, or keep fresh roots covered in moist sawdust if you need to hold them briefly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi heei baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ oyaiyeli afee nɔ ko ni egbi tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. Aloo okɛ ŋmeii ni mli efɔ aha shishifãi heei ahe kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛto be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting nurse crops like plantains provides living shade and holds soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which direction is right when burying cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the leaf nodes or buds along the cutting; they should point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward first, wasting energy and reducing yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa nitsumɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds or ridges before planting my yam and sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani madu sweet potatoes kɛ yams lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so roots and tubers can easily expand underground without resistance. They also improve water drainage, preventing root rot during heavy rainfall.
