ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help restore the plant's green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer, nourishing the soil and helping neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ abele, koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central whorl of my young maize plants and chewing the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender central leaves of young maize. Spraying approved insecticides or neem leaf extract directly into the central funnel helps control them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ dani efiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plant for water and nutrients. Pruning them down to leave only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big and produces a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii aba.

english: Why is a dry spell so dangerous when my maize crop is producing flowers and tassels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo be lɛ ji oshara be mli ni mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most moisture-sensitive stage for maize. Lack of water during tasseling prevents proper pollination, which leads to cobs with very few or no kernels.
ga: Fɔlɔi ji be ni ŋmãa nuɔ he fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Nu ni bɛ yɛ brɔshi be mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently watered and adding calcium-rich fertilizer prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni calcium eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai akafite.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the tip inward, your maize is short on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so it moves what little it has from older leaves to feed new growth. Adding urea or decomposed manure helps fix this.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni edara lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmeii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their leaves and wilt in the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: During very hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from the soil. If they bounce back by early morning, it is normal heat stress, but spreading dry grass as mulch around the plants helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba leebi lɛ Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ latsaa he haomɔ mli. Shi jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he akɛ mulch lɛ baaye abua ni eshishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or using too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady moisture and avoiding heavy nitrogen application during flowering helps the blossoms turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni akɛhaa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on producing top leaves and stems instead of swelling its roots underground. Crops need potassium (found in wood ash or specific fertilizers) to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, potassium he miihia Tsei. (ni anaa yɛ tso sũ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli) koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse

english: What will happen if I put too many maize seeds in one hole or plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli loo midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stems that fall over easily and produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die when I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ mi-shade tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or companion crops like plantain act like natural umbrellas, protecting the baby cocoa from excessive sun and retaining moisture until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei loo nanemɛi tsei tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu cocoa gbekɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni fe nine lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants staying short and stunted weeks after transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when roots cannot spread due to hard, packed soil, or when the soil lacks phosphorus. Loosening the soil deeply before planting and adding well-aged manure gives roots the room and energy to expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hewɔ. aloo be mli ni fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda fataa he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaalɛɛ amɛmli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, as plants need steady moisture to move calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do pests attack my cabbage much worse when I plant cabbage on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cabbage lɛ waa fe tsutsu lɛ beni miduɔ cabbage yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up in high numbers in the ground. Rotating with crops from a different family, like beans or maize, starves those pests out.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai babaoo ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ wekui krokomɛi amli, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ Ebaaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops turn yellow so much faster than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak roots that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for fertilizer and water. Weeds choke out light and steal soil food before the young crop can establish itself, making early weeding essential.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu. Jwɛi lɛ miɔ la ni amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi. Ha efee nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. lɛ he miihia

english: Why do I need to shade my young cocoa plants when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔlɔ haa kookoo tsei bibii beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Providing shade with crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into making a large fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Which direction should I plant my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds or leaf nodes pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the stems and roots to grow twisted and weak, which reduces your total yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Kwɔ ni oná yitso agbo?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes gives them maximum sunlight, which sends food down to build larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii baa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant moves nitrogen from its older lower leaves to nourish new top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why should I wait for continuous rains before planting maize instead of planting right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔmɛ ni nugbɔ aya nɔ anɛ dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting until rains become frequent ensures the soil stays wet enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛmɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special microscopic organisms in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil nutrients. Nearby maize plants feed on this extra soil food to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ sũ lɛ mli niyenii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from fertilizing and developing into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛfɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the sap, or by a virus spread by insects. Checking under leaves early helps identify pests before they stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ayɔseɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay healthy during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves creates a mulch layer that shields the ground from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cooler, retains moisture longer, and prevents the roots from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbi

english: Is it better for my crops if I burn the bushes after clearing my land or leave them to rot on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ loo miha amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash that helps crops briefly, but it destroys rich organic matter and useful soil life. Leaving the cleared weeds and leaves to rot on the soil feeds the land slowly and helps keep the ground moist during hot days.
ga: Shãa haa sũ lɛ tswaa oya, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: What makes my land lose its power to produce good crop yields after I plant on it for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni haa hewalɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni midu nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take away nutrients from the ground. Planting continuously without giving the soil a rest, adding animal manure, or applying fertilizer drains these nutrients until the land becomes too tired to feed new crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Kooloi aŋmei ni akɛfataa he Aloo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii nɛɛ afite kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more stalks on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ŋmeii babaoo ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stems that produce tiny or incomplete cobs instead of strong plants with large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo eshɛɛɛ he Moŋ lɛ eji tso ni wa ni toii wuji yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with very few leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce their food. When shaded by tall trees, the crop stretches rapidly upward searching for light, using all its energy to grow taller instead of building thick stems and full foliage.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do many farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underground. Planting them together lets you harvest maize early while giving the cassava time to spread out and mature without wasting land.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, nanemɛi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya kɛtsɔ ŋmei lɛ be ni oooha lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ ni efiteee he ko lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases that target tomatoes stay hidden in the soil after harvest. Planting tomatoes in the same spot year after year gives those diseases a constant supply of food, allowing them to build up and ruin your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni amɛtutuaa tomato lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha helai nɛɛ aya nɔ aba. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn pale yellow after heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water floods the soil and pushes out the air that roots need to breathe. It also washes away nitrogen—the main nutrient that gives leaves their deep green color—causing the plant to turn yellow from stress and lack of food.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ nitrogen hu shwieɔ shi. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ kɛ niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know if my land holds enough moisture to grow crops during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a hand-length deep in the ground; if it holds together in a ball without crumbling immediately, it retains moisture well enough to support hardy crops through dry periods.
ga: Mimɔ sũ ni fa fioo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ tso ko ni mli kwɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my crops if there is enough space for all of them to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds are aggressive growers that drink water and absorb fertilizer much faster than your crops can. Even if space looks adequate, weeds steal the essential food and water from under the ground, starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni feɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni he ni eyɔɔ lɛ fa moŋ Shi jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning hard before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe wa dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or passing along a virus that stops the leaves from spreading out flat to make food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ooonu Aloo hela ko ni gbeɔ hela ko ni baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha pepper tsei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen nutrients in the soil or are sitting in too much stagnant water. Adding a balanced fertilizer like NPK early in the plant's life gives it the food it needs to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK fata he yɛ tso ko shihilɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my yam crop growing plenty of heavy green vines above the ground, but the yams under the soil remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves instead of building tubers underground. Using fertilizers higher in potassium helps the plant direct its strength toward growing bigger yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji krokomɛi ni abaakpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and the stems staying very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ kuku nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stunted growth in cassava are signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela baa lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the growing heart of the maize plant. Checking your field early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended insecticides directly into the plant funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ tsui lɛ. Akwɛɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Abaakpa enɛɛmɛi dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist with water and planting shade trees nearby helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look like they are dying in the afternoon heat even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. Covering the soil around the roots with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and prevents this temporary wilting.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why are my young mangoes falling off the tree before they are mature enough to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit trees drop young fruit when they don't have enough water and nutrients to feed them all, or when fruit flies lay eggs in them. Proper watering, feeding the soil, and setting simple fruit fly traps will help the tree hold its fruit until harvest.
ga: Yibii tsei shwieɔ yibii bibii kɛji amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii wo amɛmli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ nii, kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛmɔɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi amɛyibii lɛ amli kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to leave so much empty space between my plantain suckers when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves and wide root systems that need plenty of room to feed. Spacing them properly prevents them from blocking sunlight from each other and ensures every plant gets enough nutrients from the soil to grow big bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni biɔ he babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkatsi hulu la naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ jwɛi agbo.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from producing good yields even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are stronger and faster at drinking water and eating fertilizer nutrients than young crops are. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil nutrients without any competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field without trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade from temporary nurse crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect their delicate leaves from burning while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Enɛ buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot and pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to compete for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which leads to smaller bunches and weak stems that easily blow over in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu he. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for healthy leafy growth, or that heavy rainfall has washed away nutrients from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hia kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kpakpa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leafy bushes on top grow very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Baai ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ lɛ dara waa?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing food below ground in the edible tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ngɛ tsohi nɛ a yeɔ ɔ mi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on a piece of land after harvesting maize from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ beni akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which replenishes nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi aniyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to survive rather than setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo calcium ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do tiny holes keep appearing in the leaves of my cabbage plants just a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Chewing insects like caterpillars and beetles feed on young leaves to grow, which weakens the plant and prevents clean cabbage heads from forming if not managed early.
ga: Kplukai ni yeɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai bibii koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa kaabe yitsei ni he tse afee kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce the final amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, while also harboring pests that can spread plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji shihilɛhe kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture to start planting my seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds its shape without dripping excess water and crumbles easily when gently pressed, the soil has ideal moisture for seed germination.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get full of tiny insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ani ebaafee nɔ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Weevils and grain borers lay eggs inside the maize while it is in the field or during drying. If maize is not dried properly below 13% moisture and stored in sealed hermetic bags, these insects hatch, eat the inside of the grain, and turn your harvest into powder.
ga: Weevils kɛ seed borers woɔ ŋmãa mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ 13% ni akɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ baafɔ. ye dumɔwui lɛ amli ni otsɔ onibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn brown and spoil just two days after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stop receiving water and nutrients the moment they are harvested, causing a natural chemical reaction that breaks the root down rapidly. Processing it immediately into gari, flour, or dried cassava chips removes the moisture and stops it from rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛji akpa amɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ atsu ghari, ashikishaŋ, loo ŋmei ni egbi he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen or suffering in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen gives plants energy to build green leaves; applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli loo eepiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather gets too hot or dry, the plant sheds flowers to save its own energy rather than trying to feed fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha lɛ aduawai

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small instead of long, thick, and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers struggle to expand when planted in hard, compacted soil or stony ground. Planting yams in high, loose soil mounds or ridges gives the growing tuber soft soil to push through easily, resulting in long, smooth yams.
ga: Ewa akɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni etse amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ haa anáa sweet potato kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark, and crowded cocoa farms. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight in and harvesting ripe pods immediately stops the moisture that spreads the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni efɔ, ediŋŋ, ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kroko lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ eshwaa lɛ kpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are these strange purple-flowered weeds growing close to my cowpea plants and making them wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛmiiha amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to your cowpea roots beneath the ground to steal its water and food. Rotating your farm with crops like sorghum or planting Striga-resistant seed varieties breaks this weed's cycle.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa cowpea shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei tsake oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo odu dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ Striga hela lɛ, ebaaku nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes squash and rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting tomatoes in the hot afternoon heat and packing them tightly in heavy sacks causes heat buildup and skin bruising, which speeds up rotting. Harvesting in the cool morning and transporting them in rigid wooden or plastic crates keeps them fresh.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tomato yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni akɛwo kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba ni eha hewolo lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha efite oya. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni okɛwo tso loo plastic adekai ni wa amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested plantains from ripening all at once before I take them to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ shikome dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Plantains give off an invisible natural gas as they age that tells nearby plantains to ripen quickly. Keeping green plantains in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded spot away from direct sunlight slows down this natural gas and delays ripening.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni anaaa lɛ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ha dumɔwui eŋɔlii lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ehoo blɛoo.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my fermented cocoa beans directly on bare plastic or the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ plastic ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans directly on the ground traps dampness underneath, causing mold growth and picking up dirt or chemical smells from the soil. Drying them on raised bamboo mats allows air to circulate under the beans, keeping them clean and premium quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii daa ni ejieɔ muji loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct, full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and shaded until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfee hulutsoo kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this food deep into the earth where roots cannot reach, so adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and boost crop yield.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho niyenii nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough space to grow big roots and produce larger crops.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water fills up all the tiny air gaps in the earth for too long, the roots drown and rot, which stops the plant from absorbing nutrients and kills the crop.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baagbo ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific insects and soil diseases to multiply. Switching your field to groundnuts or beans every few seasons puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and starves out crop diseases.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni atsakeɔ awoɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei mli daa Be fioo komɛi baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni atsĩ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to wake up and begin sprouting. If you plant too early into dry soil, the heat can bake and destroy the seeds before the rains arrive to sustain their growth.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔ aba koni ekɛha amɛdalɛ aya nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water quickly, keeps the roots cool, and gradually breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni egbɛɔ amɛ fiofio ni efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam plants tell you they are ready for harvest when their green leaves begin turning yellow and the vines start to dry up. This indicates that the plant has finished sending energy down into the subterranean tuber and stored its maximum amount of food.
ga: O sweet potato tso lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa be mli ni baai eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu hewalɛ kɛba shi kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ekɛ niyenii ni fa fe fɛɛ eto.

english: Why do insects attack my tomato plants more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa tomato tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, insects seek out juicy plants like tomatoes to get the moisture and nutrients they need to survive. The heat also speeds up how quickly insect eggs hatch, leading to larger bug populations on your crops.
ga: yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kooloi bibii kwɛɔ tsei ni mli edɔ, tamɔ tomato, koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Dɔlɛ hu haa kooloi akui lɛ fɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main plants full access to the resources they need to grow fast and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otso titri lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ oya ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black Pod is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet conditions. When heavy rains arrive, the fungus spreads quickly through water droplets, especially if the cocoa trees are too bushy and lack airflow to dry off.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, Mold gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ŋmeii amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli tse tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni baaha egbi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices from young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects that disrupt normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes inside the central funnel of young corn plants are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on soft leaves before the corn ears begin to form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmeii toi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is short of nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make green leaves, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when the soil experiences sudden dry spells, or when there is a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I do not plant plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first, exhausting the plant and reducing tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant photosynthesize better, which leads to bigger root tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ fotosintɛsis tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi wuji baa.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stalk for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing them allows the main plant to focus all its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aye ehe koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai akui wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally feed the soil and help nearby maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight. Clearing all big trees exposes them to extreme heat and sun scorch, which dries them out and kills them before their roots can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam plants yield bigger tubers when I give the vines tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ haa bulbs wuji beni mihaa lɛ wain tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and make energy, which gets stored underground as the tuber. Staking lifts leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmeii Ajieɔ Staking lifts kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hetsemɔ kɛjɛ helai ahe

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots around my main plantain tree to keep growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Multiple shoots around a plantain tree compete with the main mother stem for water, soil nutrients, and light. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the plant to grow bigger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei babaoo ni bɔle Seedlings lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ adara ni etsɔ kuu wulu.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stems with the buds pointing upwards instead of upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava stem buds naturally sprout upwards toward the light. Planting stems upside down forces new shoots to bend underground, wasting energy, weakening the shoot, and reducing root yield.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛya la lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Hewalɛ ni afiteɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ayibii baa shi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, which can be fixed by adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop finishes, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu nii agbe naa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown, soft, and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wet, humid weather helps the fungal spores that cause black pod disease spread quickly across cocoa trees. Pruning extra branches opens up the canopy so sunlight and wind can dry the pods after rain.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Additional pruning opens the canopy so that sunlight and wind can dry out the pods after rain.

english: Why do the leaf funnels of my young maize plants look like someone shot ragged holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni agbeleɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko tu bu ni elaaje lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside young maize leaves are a common sign of fall armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant stem. Catching them early with appropriate controls prevents them from eating the main growing point.
ga: Buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa mli ŋmeii ni miitao niyenii yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nii yɛ he titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboi dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: Black rot at the base of green tomatoes is caused by blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my hot pepper plants dropping all their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy and water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I process my harvested cassava into gari or flour instead of selling the raw tubers immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mafee gari loo ashikishaŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ yitsei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Raw cassava spoils within a few days after harvest, forcing you to sell quickly at low prices. Processing cassava into gari or flour removes water, prevents rotting, and allows you to store and sell it for a much higher profit over several months.
ga: Kasava ni ahoko lɛ baafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Kɛ́ afee ŋmei ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, ejieɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛtoɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛhaa sɛɛnamɔi ni fa babaoo yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get tiny bugs inside after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Hii mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Maize grains retain moisture after harvest, which attracts insects like weevils that lay eggs inside the seeds. Properly drying your maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags prevents insect damage and keeps the grain whole.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi akafite ŋmãa lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my fresh cocoa beans need to ferment under banana leaves before I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔ kookoo yibii heei anɔ atsɔ banana baai ashishi dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans are naturally bitter and covered in white pulp. Fermenting them under leaves breaks down the pulp and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers demand before purchasing.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei lɛ mli edɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ehà amɛhe. Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ dani amɛheɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes rot so quickly when everyone in my village harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have a high water content and soft skin, making them spoil rapidly in warm heat. When there is a harvest glut, processing fresh tomatoes into paste or drying them helps preserve them so you can sell when prices rise.
ga: Tomatoes have a high water content and soft skin. This causes tomatoes to rot quickly when exposed to warm heat. Kɛji akɛ kpamɔ fa tsɔ lɛ, tomato hee ni ooofee cream loo egbi lɛ haa ehiɔ shi bɔni afee ni onyɛ ohɔɔ kɛji ejara tee hiɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and yellow so fast while I am transporting them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains produce a natural gas that speeds up their own ripening, especially in hot, enclosed spaces. Keeping harvested plantains cool, shaded, and well-ventilated during transport slows down ripening.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshwereɔ oya. Titri lɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested paddy rice straight from the farm or take it to a milling machine first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miŋa ni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling raw paddy rice brings lower returns because buyers have to clean it themselves. Taking paddy rice to a milling machine removes the husk and bran, turning it into clean white rice that consumers pay more for.
ga: Omɔ ni ahoo lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ haaa shika babaoo aba ejaakɛ esa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ atsumɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaajie ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmãa ni he tse ni yɔɔ futafuta ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ woɔ he nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when they are just sitting in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtara mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally try to grow new plants when exposed to warmth and light. Removing early sprouts and keeping your storage barn cool and dark prevents the yam from shrinking and losing market value.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ tsei heei kɛji akɛ amɛwo hulutsoo kɛ la mli. Tsei bibii ni ooojie ni oha otsu lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni efee duŋ lɛ baatsi sweet potatoes lɛ anaa koni ekagbɔjɔ ni ejara bɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to leave my harvested groundnuts in wet piles on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Damp groundnuts on soil easily grow a dangerous, invisible mold that produces poison called aflatoxin. Drying groundnuts thoroughly off the bare ground keeps them safe for eating and acceptable to commercial buyers.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni yɔɔ oshara. Enɛ haa tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ, ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why do people boil and crush shea nuts to make butter instead of selling the raw nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi fɔ̃ɔ shea ŋmeii ni amɛshwieɔ nɔ koni amɛkɛfee bɔta yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Raw shea nuts rot over time and bring low income, but processing them into shea butter creates a long-lasting product used in cosmetics and cooking that sells for a much higher price.
ga: Shea ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛnáaa shika fioo ko pɛ. Shi shea butter ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa anáa nɔ ko ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa mɔ he kɛ niyenii homɔ mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my fresh hot peppers shrink and lose weight when I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpo hiŋmɛi mli ŋmeii heei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes the water inside fresh peppers, which reduces their weight but concentrates their spice and preserves them for months without spoiling.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ chili hee mli lɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi shi ehaa tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni abaanyɛ akɛto nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee.

english: Can I really plant and harvest rice twice in the same year on my land in Northern Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow two rice crops in one year if you have reliable irrigation water, like from a dam or river pumping system. Planting twice allows you to double your total harvest from the same field, but you must plan carefully so the second crop gets enough water during the dry months.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa tsei enyɔ yɛ afi mli kɛji oyɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ faa loo faa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu shii enyɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ onáa yibii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ toi enyɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni oto gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Will planting rice twice in one year destroy my soil's strength?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni aduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ?

english: Growing rice back-to-back can drain the nutrients from your soil if you do not feed it properly. To keep your land strong for two harvests, you need to apply the right fertilizers, return crop residues to the soil, or rotate with crops like cowpea to rebuild the soil's natural strength.
ga: Omɔ ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji okɛ niyenii haaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee shiŋŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔi enyɔ Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii atsake koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How much rice should I expect to harvest from my field if I use good seeds and care for it well?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsu nii ni mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: With high-yielding seed varieties, proper fertilizer application, and good water management, a well-managed farm can produce up to six tons of rice per hectare. If you rely only on rain and low-quality seeds, your harvest will usually be much lower.
ga: kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu he nitsumɔ kpakpa Okwaafoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmãa ni shɛɔ tɔn enumɔ yɛ hectare kome mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni baa shi pɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What does it mean when agricultural extension officers talk about getting a high yield per hectare?
ga: Kɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wie yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo ni anáa yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ he lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: Yield per hectare simply measures how many bags or tons of food you produce from a standard plot of land. Achieving a high yield means your plants are growing healthy enough to yield maximum grain from a small area, rather than needing vast stretches of land to get a good harvest.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni anáa kɛjɛɔ hectare kome mli lɛ ji niyenii kotokui loo tɔn enyiɛ ni okɛbaajɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ he susumɔ kɛkɛ. Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo ni ooona lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ a ná zugba ngua konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a wo ní kpakpahi.

english: Why does rice need so much water on the field compared to crops like maize or sorghum?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special roots and stems designed to thrive in very wet conditions. Water keeps the soil moist for grain development, regulates soil temperature during hot days, and naturally suppresses dryland weeds that try to choke the young crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni afee koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ waa lɛ amli. Nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ naa jwɛi ni yɔɔ hei ni egbi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ anaa.

english: How does the weather in Northern Ghana affect how my rice crop grows?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ saa mi ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Northern Ghana has one main rainy season followed by a long dry period with hot winds. Because rainy periods can be short or erratic, rice plants need continuous moisture during their flowering stage, otherwise the grains will turn out empty or light.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be titri kome, ni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ be lɛ baanyɛ afee kuku loo ebɛ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baafee efolo loo ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some types of rice seeds mature faster than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are bred for different conditions. Short-duration varieties mature quickly in about three months to escape dry spells, while long-duration varieties take longer to grow bigger plants and produce heavier yields if water is available for many months.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Be kukuoo mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ daa oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli koni amɛjo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naa foi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so I do not lose grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ akafite?

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a golden yellow color. Waiting too long makes the stalks brittle and grains fall to the ground, while harvesting too early leaves you with light, undeveloped grains.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishi fãa ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛko.

english: Why do some farmers with very large rice farms end up getting very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji wuji waa lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Large fields require intense management. If a farmer plants a large area without enough labor or money to clear weeds, apply fertilizer on time, and manage water properly, the plants struggle and yield poorly compared to a smaller, well-cared-for farm.
ga: Nitsumɔhe niji wuji biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji okwaafoi du hei wuji ni amɛbɛ nitsumɔ loo shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, Ha amɛdu yɛ be naa ni amɛkwɛ nu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast in my rice field during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds thrive on the same warm weather, sunshine, and moist soil that rice loves. Because young rice plants grow slowly at first, aggressive weeds can easily steal sunlight, water, and soil food unless you clear them early in the crop's life.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni omɔ sumɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ aju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Ja ojie kɛjɛ mli mra yɛ oshihilɛ mli.

english: How can I know if a new seed variety will actually produce good yield on my land before I plant my whole farm with it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can test a small section of your field with the new seed alongside your regular seeds during one season. Comparing how they grow under your local weather and soil conditions will show you if the new variety performs well before you commit your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka fã bibioo ko okwɛ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ dumɔwui heei ni fata odumɔwui ni oduɔ daa lɛ ahe yɛ be ko mli. Okɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ shishi lɛ ato he. Ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji tso hee ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaahe ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some seeds sprout quickly after planting while others from the same bag fail to grow at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ adu lɛ? be mli ni dumɔwui krokomɛi Yɛ kotoku kome mli lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ kwraa?

english: Seeds are living things that can die if stored poorly in heat or damp conditions. Healthy, high-quality seeds sprout uniformly, while seeds damaged by bad storage or old age lose their energy and fail to germinate.
ga: Seeds are living things that can die if stored improperly in hot or humid areas. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Meanwhile, seeds damaged by poor storage or old age lose energy and are unable to germinate.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the young plant is hungry for nitrogen or that heavy rains have soaked the soil too much, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
