ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tsei bibii lɛ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants get wrinkled, curled leaves and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ baa ni egbɔjɔ, ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and spreading plant viruses, or by extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, during dry periods without enough soil moisture, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus during its flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my maize farm during the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ amli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the land for your next crop and breaks the cycle of pests that target maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baafee niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji ŋmãa lɛ oti lɛ.

english: How does covering my vegetable beds with dry grass help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai aŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella that keeps the soil cool, stops sunlight from drying out soil moisture, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield even after I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Ani jwɛi baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they act like thieves—drinking up the water and eating the fertilizer nutrients before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi—amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛwoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Too much rain fills all the small air spaces in heavy soils, causing waterlogging. Without air in the soil, the root tissue suffocates and rots due to water-loving fungal diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. ekɛ nu baa Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hydrophilic fungal helai ahewɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become deformed when planted in hard, unloosened soil that blocks root growth, or when tiny microscopic worms in the soil, called nematodes, attack the skin of the growing tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli tse nɔ, ni no tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ Tutua yitso ni miida lɛ hewolo lɛ.

english: Why do some of the commercial hybrid seeds I buy from the agro-shop have a bright pink or blue coating on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni miheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo bluu ni kpɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seed producers treat the seeds with a safe protective coat containing fungicide and pesticide to prevent insects and soil diseases from destroying them before they sprout. The bright color is added so you know the seed has been professionally treated and isn't meant for eating.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ahe nii koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ akafite amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Bright colors are added so you know the seeds have been professionally cared for and are not meant to be eaten.

english: How can I be sure that the fertilizer granules I buy have not been mixed with fake dirt or impurities?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ kɛ sũ efutuuu loo eyɛ muji ni akɛfee?

english: Genuine manufactured fertilizers undergo strict factory processing where every particle is crushed, blended, and shaped to a uniform size and consistent color. If you open a bag and see unusual dark powders or random mixed grains, it may be contaminated or fake.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee diɛŋtsɛ lɛ atsɔ nitsumɔhe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa mli. Akɛ nibii bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi, afutuɔ ni afee amɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe su feɔ ekome. Kɛji ogbele kotoku lɛ mli ni ona powda ko ni tsuɔ waa loo pellets ni akɛfutu mli trukaa lɛ Ekolɛ muji yɛ mli Aloo eji amale?

english: Why do all the maize crops grown from certified store-bought seeds grow to the exact same height and harvest at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he kome ni akpaa amɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced through clean genetic breeding processes so every single seed carries identical traits. This clean selection ensures predictable crop height, uniform grain color, and equal harvesting time across your whole farm.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛtsɔɔ fɔmɔ nii ni he tse nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu yɛ sui komekomei. Nɛkɛ halamɔ ni he tse nɛɛ haa anyɛɔ atsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ. Omɔ ŋmaa su ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kpamɔ bei ni yeɔ egbɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some new sweet potato varieties have a deep orange color inside while the traditional ones are white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ henɔi heei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ yɛ mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni shishijee henɔ lɛ ji yɛŋ lɛ?

english: The orange color is a natural trait enhanced through plant breeding to provide high amounts of Vitamin A and beneficial proteins. The distinct color shows that the crop contains special nutrients that improve health and boost market value.
ga: Aŋɔli su lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni aha ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei akwɛmɔ nɔ koni vitamin A kɛ protein ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo ahi mli. Su ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli ni haa mɔ he waa ni ehaa jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my fruits like pineapples and mangoes get sweeter and change color as they stay longer on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai tamɔ ŋmei kɛ mango lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As crops mature, the plant naturally converts its stored starches into natural sugars and sweet proteins. This chemical change changes the fruit's skin and flesh color from dull green to bright yellow or orange, signaling that it is fully ripe and rich in flavor.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ starch ni ato lɛ ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ adebɔɔ mli proteins ni ŋɔɔ. Tsofa tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsakeɔ aduawai lɛ ahewolo kɛ loo su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli tseee kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwere kwraa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa.

english: What causes black spots or unusual green patches to appear on my harvested cassava roots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Unwanted colors on harvested crops usually happen when the root is exposed to harsh sunlight before harvest or infected by micro-organisms. Proper harvesting and keeping the roots shaded prevents these dark or green discolorations from ruining your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, su ni ataooo ni yɔɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa ko shɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ dani akpa amɛ loo nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ bamɔ amɛ. Nikpamɔ ni sa kɛ shishifãi ni oooha amɛfee hulutsoo lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ sui ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo eŋɔli nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does processing my cassava into gari make it last for months without spoiling like fresh roots do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ni mikɛfeɔ gari lɛ haa ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee tamɔ shishifãi heei lɛ?

english: Processing cassava mechanically grinds, presses out moisture, and roasts the pulp. Removing water prevents bacteria and mold from growing, turning a easily perishable crop into a stable, dry food that stores safely for long periods.
ga: Bɔ ni afeɔ lɛ ahaa: Akɛ tsɔne shwieɔ ŋmei nɔ, ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli koni efee fɛ̃i, ni ashãa. Nu ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii aya hiɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ feɔ niyenii ni egbi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does a palm oil processing machine extract clean red oil without leaving dirt or fiber mixed inside?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛfeɔ tso mli fɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ ejieɔ fɔ tsuru ni he tse ni eshiuuu muji loo tsɔne ko ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ?

english: The processing machine heats, mashes, and presses the palm fruits, using mechanical strainers and gravity separators to filter out pure oil while keeping the tough fiber and shell completely separate.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛjieɔ fɔ kɛ nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛdɔɔ, amɛshwieɔ ni amɛmiimiɔ tso yibii lɛ koni amɛkɛjie fɔ ni atsake lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tsɔji ni mli wa lɛ kɛ tsitsii lɛ amli gbalaa kwraa.

english: Why do cocoa buyers reject cocoa beans that are purple or gray instead of rich dark brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kpooɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: The rich brown color shows that cocoa beans went through proper fermentation and drying, which develops true chocolate flavor. Purple or discolored beans mean the process was cut short or contaminated with moisture.
ga: Su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afee kookoo yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni egbi. Enɛ haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans ni ji purple loo su ni etsake lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afo gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ mli kuku loo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli.

english: How do modern rice mills sort out bad grains so that only clean white rice ends up in the bag?
ga: Te ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjaraa ŋmãa ŋmãa ni efite lɛ mli, ni ŋmãa yɛŋ ni he tse pɛ eshiɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Modern milling machines use mechanical sorters and light sensors that inspect each grain individually. If a grain is discolored, broken, or mixed with dirt, the machine automatically blows it away so only pure, uniform rice is packed.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa kɛ kane ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ su tsake, egbɛ eshwa, loo ekɛ muji efutu lɛ, tsɔne lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatswa dumɔwui lɛ. Koni ŋmãa krɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa pɛ ahi mli

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. This often happens if heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or if the ground stays flooded for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fresh fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai heei lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or when watering is inconsistent. Sudden changes between dry soil and heavy watering stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa he loo kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni mli wa teŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot primarily when planted in heavy soil that holds too much standing water, or when infected stem cuttings are used. Planting on raised soil mounds helps water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo beni afoɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa plants burn and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect young cocoa trees from heat while keeping soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce tiny harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room for its roots to expand and leaves to gather light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛshɛ amɛhe koni amɛbua la naa.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves off the ground toward sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves away from damp soil diseases and maximizes sunlight exposure, which fuels the growth of large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ. Staking haa baa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my vegetable plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It stops soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, keeps the ground cool, and suppresses weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Helps prevent soil moisture from evaporating in the heat. Helps keep the ground cool and prevent weeds from growing

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my cultivated crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to local conditions. They respond instantly to rain and absorb soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the field, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni amɛha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do green caterpillars attack the central leaves of my maize plants just as they start growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ be mli pɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs inside the tender, rolled leaves of young maize plants because soft leaves are an easy food source for newly hatched caterpillars like armyworms. Checking fields early allows for timely control before damage spreads.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe. Akɛni baai bibii ji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee tamɔ armyworms hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young or unprotected cocoa trees suffer from heat stress under direct sunlight. Sunlight burns their leaves and forces the plant to shed them to save water, which is why shade trees are essential to keep the cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii loo ni abuuu amɛhe lɛ baaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Hulu la shãa baai lɛ ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ he hiaa koni eha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viruses, or by severe heat stress. Excess water alone cannot cure insect-borne diseases or lower high air temperatures around the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. or from severe heat stress Excess water alone cannot treat insect-borne diseases or reduce high air temperatures around leaves.

english: How can I tell from my crop leaves if my farm soil is lacking nutrients before I buy expensive fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: Crops show clear warning signs through their leaves. For example, lower leaves turning pale yellow usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, while purple-tinged leaves mean the soil is low in phosphorus.
ga: Tsei jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside my maize will help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli awa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This provides natural food for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: If I leave my land uncultivated for one season, will the soil recover on its own?
ga: Kɛ mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ be kome mli lɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest allows organic matter to rebuild and soil nutrients to restore naturally. However, you must control weeds so they do not drain the soil's moisture and seed for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ehee ekoŋŋ, ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu feɔ ehee ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okudɔ jwɛi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ dumɔwui lɛ akaho yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin without producing big corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Maize stalks grow tall and thin when plants are placed too close together or lack sufficient sunlight and soil nitrogen. The plants stretch upward competing for light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ, moŋ lɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that collects water and does not drain well. Excess underground water suffocates the roots and promotes fungal diseases that destroy the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu nyɛɛɛ ahi mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it sprouts many side shoots called suckers. If you do not cut back excess suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji ogbalaaa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai ni abua naa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the sun, which maximizes food production and directs more energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni fata staking he ji baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii babaoo baa. ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo aba koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, giving young cocoa trees the cool environment they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo aduɔ tsei ni baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni eha hulutsoo aba ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen runs low in the soil, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to send what little food it has left to the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients and leaves the soil exhausted. Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes water to flow fast across topsoil, washing your expensive fertilizer off the field into nearby streams or pushing it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after mild rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Aloo tsimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ yɛ he ni tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my tomatoes help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-tomato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the hot sun. It traps moisture in the dirt so it does not evaporate quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking light and nutrients from your tomatoes.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekatsɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii kpakpa kɛjɛ tomato mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains collect and sit in the soil without draining, the ground becomes waterlogged, choking the roots and creating conditions where fungal diseases multiply and cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ buaa ehe naa ni eta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Nu baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa babaoo ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ baa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, neighboring plants compete heavily for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Instead of building energy to grow thick stems and big cobs, the plants waste their energy stretching upward to try and get sunlight over each other.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ wa náa he wami konɛ e kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa. Mohu ɔ, tsehi puɛɔ a he wami kɛ guɔ a hɛ mi kɛ yaa hiɔwe konɛ a kɛ hla a sibi hulu la ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on in order to grow big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ bɔni afee ni ekwɛ bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants use sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which is stored underground as tubers. Lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to direct sunlight and keeps them away from soil diseases, allowing the plant to make more food and form larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii Wain tso lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. ni etsĩɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra branches near the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii ni fata he ni bɛŋkɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing tiny side shoots, often called suckers, prevents the tomato plant from wasting vital nutrients on extra leaves and thin branches. This forces the plant to redirect its energy into producing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ niji bibii anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛwo tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my young corn plants and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These pests, often Fall Armyworms, seek out the soft inner leaves inside the central funnel of the corn plant because it offers shelter from sun heat and predators while providing tender plant tissues for them to eat.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛfeɔ asraafoi awuiyelɔi lɛ, taoɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ejaakɛ ehaa mɔ náa abobaahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛ tso mli fãji ni mli tse ni amɛyeɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is suitable for growing maize or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize needs rich, dark, well-drained soil to produce good ears, while cassava is a tough crop that can survive and give tubers even in poor or sandy soil where maize struggles.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ toi kpakpai aba. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋã nɔ po nɔ he ni ŋmeii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer, or the ground is soaked with too much standing water which stops the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: When you plant cassava too close together, the stems fight for sunlight and nutrients, growing tall and thin while producing very small, skinny tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ ohe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Edaa ni ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunshine; they require shade from plantains or taller trees to keep their leaves cool and preserve soil moisture during their early growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛbaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of young corn to feed, reducing the plant's growth if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or lack of water, causing it to save its energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ. Ehaa hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baa moŋ fe nɔ ni ekɛbaajɛ mli aba.

english: Can I plant the maize grains I buy from the local market for cooking, or must I buy certified seed?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛhoo? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Grains bought for food often result in weak plants with small harvests, whereas certified seeds are specially selected to resist local diseases and yield larger, healthier crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni aheɔ kɛhaa niyenii lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal water, space, and soil nutrients quickly, which slows down the growth of your cultivated crops if they are not cleared regularly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso ni adu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji ajieee lɛ daa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and soil diseases to build up, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense sun to reduce the surface area exposed to heat and trap moisture inside the leaf, preventing the plant from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi baai lɛ amli. Koni tso lɛ akagbi

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers when they do not receive enough water, soil nutrients, or insect pollination, saving their energy for the pods they can successfully support.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ ahaaa amɛ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛhaa ŋmeii ni cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet weather. Pruning shade trees to let sunlight reach the trunk helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is running low on nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or that water is sitting too long around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers but no actual peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off without making fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil drops too low in moisture, or when there are no small insects around to pollinate them.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves have small holes all over them like a net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe tsei bibii lɛ? Ogbɔmɔtso muu lɛ fɛɛ tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo?

english: Tiny holes in garden egg leaves are caused by leaf-chewing insects like flea beetles. Clearing surrounding weeds early helps prevent these pests from migrating onto your crops.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ eggplant baai amli yɛ abɔɔi amli lɛ jɛɔ koolooi ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmeii. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafã kɛba onibii anɔ.

english: Why do my okra plants keep growing very tall without producing many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ miida ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Okra plants focus all their energy on growing tall stalks instead of fruit when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or when they are planted too close together in the shade.
ga: Gumbo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Why does my soil dry out and become hard very fast after using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the crops directly but do not improve the soil structure. Adding organic manure or decomposed leaves helps the soil hold water like a sponge.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔ nu tamɔ sponji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family, so they share the same soil diseases and pests. Rotating with a different crop breaks the life cycle of those pests.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ji tsei akuu kome mli bii. No hewɔ lɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaafite nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the afternoon sun even when the wet soil shows I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ nu efɔ nɔ.

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The leaves temporarily droop to protect themselves from burning and usually stand back up in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it out of the ground. Leaves fall temporarily to protect themselves from burns. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local conditions, allowing them to steal sunlight, water, and nutrients faster than farm crops that rely on cultivated care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow and curl when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when pests like the Fall Armyworm are attacking it. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or applying proper pest control early helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm miitutua lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Will spraying crop medicine on my garden make the plants produce bigger fruits or does it only kill pests?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii wuji loo ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Chemical sprays like insecticides only protect crops by killing harmful pests, but they do not feed the crop. To make your crops yield bigger fruits, you must combine pest protection with proper plant food like manure or fertilizer and adequate water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ pɛ ni egbeɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi ekɛ niyenii haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni sa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afata he. kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my cassava stems grow very tall and thin with leaves only at the very top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai pɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants grow tall and thin when they are planted too closely together or are blocked from sunlight by larger trees. Giving each plant enough space allows sunlight to reach all sides, which encourages the plant to grow thick roots underground instead of just tall stems.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la ni kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Ni aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛkɛ.

english: How many years do I need to wait before a new oil palm seedling starts bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani ŋmei tso hee ko aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Good varieties of oil palm usually start producing their first fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after planting, as long as you keep the farm clear of weeds and supply adequate fertilizer and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni hi lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa aha

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when the plant lacks key soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and feeding the soil helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do seeds from certified government packets grow better than the seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ paketii ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested in laboratories to give high yields and resist local crop diseases. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose these strong qualities over time, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ yɛ laboratori mli koni ana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ tsei ahelai ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops that catch nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plant dies and rots, that nitrogen stays in the soil, serving as free plant food for the maize you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my yams if I plant the seed yams too close to each other in the mound?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli?

english: Yam tubers need plenty of room underground to stretch and grow big. If planted too close, the roots fight each other for food and water, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of large, heavy ones.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he babaoo koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara. Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitso agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon sunshine, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can draw it up from the soil. Placing dry grass around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant stay upright.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛaabɔle Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind steals moisture from cocoa leaves and soil, placing the trees under intense heat stress. To survive the dry season, the tree sheds its flowers and leaves to conserve the little water it has left.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all shade trees exposes them to heat stress and quick drying, which damages or kills the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha amɛhe afee hulutsoo he haomɔ babaoo ni amɛbaagbi oya. ni baanyɛ afite tsei bibii loo efite amɛ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cool, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which dries out the moisture and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight, better airflow, and protection from ground fungal diseases, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil because they need air to breathe. Excessive water causes fungal root rot, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain water away from the root system.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛmu. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside or after maize, they naturally fertilize the soil and improve maize yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha ŋmãa yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and causing the plants to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaves or pass along plant viruses. Spraying early with appropriate organic or recommended treatments controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ loo helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Akɛ organic spray ni sa loo mra be mli tsofafeemɔ he ŋaawoo haa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots and cause the fertilizer to waste away into the air.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers with broad, wide leaves grow weaker than the ones with thin, needle-like leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ yɔɔ oshara fe baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Thin, needle-leafed suckers (maiden suckers) are strongly attached to the main plant's root system and store more energy, whereas broad-leafed suckers (water suckers) receive little nourishment from the mother plant and produce weak bunches.
ga: Baai bibii (tsobii bibii) lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, broadleaf shoots (tso bibii) lɛ naaa niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ panicles ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some fast-maturing maize seeds reach harvest in three months while local seeds take five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaa ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji enumɔ.

english: Fast-maturing seeds are bred to complete their life cycle quickly so farmers can harvest early during short rainy seasons. While they mature faster, they need early feeding and proper care to reach a good size before harvest time.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ akpa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdaraa oya moŋ Shi ehe miihia ni aha amɛ niyenii mra. kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa koni anyɛ ana dalɛ kpakpa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ aba.

english: If I plant short-duration crop varieties, do I need to apply fertilizer differently than I would for long-season crops?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, because short-duration crops grow and mature in a shorter timeframe, they need ready access to soil nutrients very early in their growth so they can feed rapidly before flowering and fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kukuoo mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. Koni enyɛ eye niyenii oya dani ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: My cassava plants look green and healthy above ground, so why are the tubers under the soil so small when I harvest?
ga: Mi yucca tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy leaves show the plant is doing well above ground, but small tubers usually mean the soil lacks specific nutrients like potassium, or the ground is too hard and compact for the roots to expand properly.
ga: Baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ potassium, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: What basic conditions do I need to check on my farm to make sure my vegetables grow to a good size?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee shihilɛi esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-aduawai lɛ dara kɛyashɛ dalɛ kpakpa he?

english: You need to monitor key growth parameters like adequate sunlight, good soil moisture, proper plant spacing, weed control, and essential soil nutrients so the crops have everything required to reach full size.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ dalɛ nibii ni he hia tamɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kpakpa Tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Jwɛi akudɔmɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eda kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall and thin under my tree crops without producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ mi tsei lɛ ashishi ni fɔfɔi bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes require direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. When shaded by tall trees, the plants waste all their energy stretching upward to search for light instead of producing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Beni eyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi Tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni etaoɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee tomato.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of leaves but very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ baa babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. This stress causes the plant to focus on growing leaves to reach light rather than setting flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa efoji lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ koni ená la moŋ fe ni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai baawo nɔ.

english: How does hard, packed soil affect how my yam tubers grow?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ saa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard soil acts like a wall underground, making it difficult for root crops to push down into the earth, which results in short, thin, or misshapen yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi gbogbo. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ feɔ kuku, eyɛ mlɛo loo efiteɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is missing nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay dark green and grow well. It can also happen if heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: If my harvested vegetables are smaller than usual, does that mean they are low quality for buyers?
ga: Kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ ehiii kwraa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Crop size is often determined by water and plant spacing, but quality is about firmness, good color, lack of disease, and freshness. Small crops can still be very high quality if they are healthy.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ. Shi bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ shiŋŋ, ehiɛ su kpakpa, hela ni bɛ mli, kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ehee lɛ nɔ. Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my crops so they don't spoil on the field?
ga: How can I tell the right time to harvest my crops? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when they reach maturity, such as maize silks turning dry and dark brown, bean pods turning yellow-brown, or tomatoes changing color, indicating peak quality before decay sets in.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa siliki ni baatsɔ asarasu ni egbi. Bean pods lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. loo tomato ni tsakeɔ ehiɛ su Enɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ dani egboɔ.

english: If I clear land that has been untouched for a long time, why do my crops grow well at first but then start struggling after a few harvests?
ga: Kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Land left untouched accumulates rich organic nutrients over time. The first crops quickly consume these natural nutrients, but continuous farming exhausts the soil unless you replenish it with compost, manure, or fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako nɔ lɛ baabua niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Klɛŋklɛŋ tsei lɛ ye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ oya. Shi okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: What crops grow best if my cleared plot has heavy, hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ni mijie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli wa?

english: Hard clay soil holds water well but makes root growth difficult. Crops with strong taproots like cassava, or shallow-rooted crops like leafy greens, perform best in clay, especially if you loosen the dirt and mix in compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ji shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ shi ehaa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmei, loo tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Titri lɛ kɛji ojie muji lɛ ni okɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds come back so quickly right after I clear and weed my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the dirt for years. When you clear or dig up the land, you expose those hidden seeds to sunlight and rain, which triggers them to sprout rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ loo otsa Nakai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. This usually happens when the soil lacks nutrients or after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli beni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ ni niyenii lɛ elaaje.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers heat stress, gets too much or too little water, or lacks key soil nutrients. Very high heat damages the pollen, making flowers fall off before fruiting.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? loo niyenii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin with few fruits when planted near shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ waa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need full sunlight to produce energy for flowers and fruit. When shaded by big trees, they stretch tall to search for light, wasting energy on stems instead of producing fruits.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu ni fa bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ aha amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii lɛ. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao la. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni afiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my sweet potato plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by viral diseases carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow very well together. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows more slowly and takes over the remaining space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii 2 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops stay small and produce tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ji bibii ni ewoɔ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce full-sized ears.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee toi ni dalɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil holds enough water for crops to survive brief dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil into a ball in your hand. If it holds its shape without crumbling immediately, it has enough clay or organic matter to retain moisture during short dry periods.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ko nɔ ofee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni efoŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why are some of my harvested yams very big while others from the same farm stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi dara waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yam size depends on how much food and water the plant gets while growing. Rich soil, proper spacing, and healthy leaves allow the plant to store more weight in the tuber, while poor soil or crowded planting results in small tubers.
ga: Bɔ ni o-sweet potato lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ muji babaoo toɔ bulb lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baaha bulbs bibii aba.

english: Why do some corn cobs on my field grow big with full grains while others remain small and half-empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi ji bibii lolo ni fã ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn cobs need adequate plant nutrients and water during the flowering stage. If a stalk lacks sufficient food, sunlight, or water, it cannot develop the grains fully, leaving the cob small.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔji biɔ tso mli niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, hulu la loo nu ni fa lɛ Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ aba kwraa. ni ofee ŋmei lɛ bibioo

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and light even after growing for a long time in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to swell up properly. Hard soil prevents the roots from expanding, and a lack of soil nutrients keeps them thin regardless of how long they stay in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfu jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Ni niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee bibii, ekɔɔɔ he eko be abɔ ni amɛbaahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to measure fertilizer in exact small amounts like grams instead of just throwing a handful on each plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, tamɔ gram, moŋ fe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo tso komekomei lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops require specific amounts of nutrients to grow well. Giving too little food leaves the crops small, but giving too much can burn the plant roots and ruin the crop, much like an overdose of medicine.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni fa fioo baaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aba. Shi kɛ́ akɛ babaoo ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Etamɔ tsofa ni fe nine ni oooye.

english: How can I measure small gram amounts of fertilizer for my plants if I do not have a weighing scale on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ gram mli? Kɛji akɛ sɛkɛn ko bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can use simple everyday containers like standard plastic bottle caps. Extension officers can show you how many grams a full bottle cap holds so you can give each plant the exact measure it needs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɛnsi ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. yɛ daa gbi shihilɛ mli, tamɔ plastic tsɛnsii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsii amli ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo gram enyiɛ tsɛnsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ otsɔɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko dalɛ pɔtɛɛ.

english: Does planting a big seed guarantee that I will harvest a bigger crop than planting a small seed?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji ni miduɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo fe dumɔwui bibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Bigger seeds hold more stored energy, giving the young plant a stronger start. However, the final weight of your harvest still depends on the nutrients, water, and sunlight the crop receives throughout its life.
ga: Dumɔwui wuji toɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ, shi kɛlɛ, naagbee shwiili ni obaakpa lɛ damɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ eshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ lolo.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger fruits when I leave more space between them instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii wuji beni mishiɔ gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants have enough space, their roots do not fight each other for soil nutrients and water, and their leaves receive full sunlight to feed the growing fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Ni amɛbaai lɛ naa hulu ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some pepper plants produce many small peppers while another plant produces just a few big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tso kroko lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji fioo komɛi pɛ?

english: Different crop varieties distribute their food differently. Some varieties spread their energy across many smaller fruits, while others concentrate their energy into producing fewer, heavier fruits.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi jaa niyenii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Henɔi komɛi jaa hewalɛ yɛ aduawai bibii babaoo amli. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa aduawai fioo ni tsii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I remove some of the small young fruits from my tomato plant, will the remaining ones grow bigger?
ga: Kɛji mijie aduawai bibioo ko kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ Ani aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ baafee agbo?

english: Yes, removing a few weak or extra fruits allows the plant to redirect all the water and nutrients it absorbs into the remaining fruits, making them grow larger and heavier.
ga: Yes, removing a few weak or surplus fruits allows the plant to reroute all the water and nutrients absorbed by the plant to the remaining fruit. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛtsiiɔ.

english: Why do crops growing under big trees on my farm stay small while crops in the open sun grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ ji bibii, yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Crops rely on direct sunlight to manufacture the food needed for growth. Trees block sunlight and their strong roots steal water and nutrients from the smaller crops underneath.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara. Tsei tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisting up and developing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: That is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. When leaves twist and turn yellow, the plant cannot catch enough sunlight, which prevents the roots from growing into big, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in dark, wet, and overly shaded farms. Pruning heavy tree branches to let in sun and clearing infected pods early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ waa lɛ haa hulu la baa ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes and dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ ni eshi bu bibioo ko? kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ su diŋŋ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing part (the funnel) of the maize plant during the day, so treating them early before the maize flowers is very important.
ga: The damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide in the middle growing part (cone) of the corn plant during the day. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ amɛ mra. Before corn flowers, it is therefore very important.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs for leaves to stay green and healthy. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure will fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land drains the exact same soil nutrients every year and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to search for sunlight. Staking gets the vines off the wet ground to catch maximum sun and prevents leaves from rotting, which helps the plant store more food in big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛyatao hulu la. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ akafite. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii babaoo toɔ bulb agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.
