english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck up moisture from the soil. The plant wilts to protect itself from losing more water, but it usually revives by evening once the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni baafite amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Watering regularly and providing light shade during extreme heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: How do I know that my sweet potatoes are ready for harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the vines start turning yellow and dry out. You can test by digging up one plant; if you cut the tuber open and the milky sap dries white rather than turning dark quickly, the crop is mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ wain tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ofo yitso lɛ ni nu lɛ gĩ ni efee yɛŋ moŋ lɛ etsɔɔ duŋ oya. Nibii ni adu lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted directly in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense direct sunlight while their roots establish. Planting plantains or shade trees nearby creates a humid canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and retains soil moisture.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ etswa shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli hulutsoo hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines require tall wooden stakes to yield good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to turn sunlight into food that gets stored in the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes exposes maximum leaf area to sunlight and keeps the stems away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. ni ehaa tso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and promotes healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce large leafy bushes above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to direct energy down into building thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛmɔ he nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni mli tse.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly a day after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without organic material lacks the ability to hold water like a sponge. Spreading dried grass or leaves as mulch around crop stems helps trap moisture in the earth and shields the roots from heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ bɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaamɔ nu tamɔ sponji. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi afɔ tso lɛ shishi akɛ mulch, ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer heat stress or dry soil conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the flowering stage prevents flower drop and gives the plant enough water to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ ashwiemɔ naa, ni ebaaha tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines flower, and does that affect the sweet potatoes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miikwɛ lɛ? Ni ani no saa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ahe?

english: Flowering takes away energy that the plant could otherwise send to the underground roots. Pruning excessive flowers allows the sweet potato plant to direct its nutrients toward growing larger, sweeter tubers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛmaje eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha sweet potato tso lɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ fɔfɔii wuji ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my maize plants while ignoring nearby cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ yucca ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer cereal crops like maize because the soft center leaves provide safe hiding spots and tender food. Cassava leaves contain natural chemical defenses that deter armyworm caterpillars from feeding on them.
ga: Autumn cutworms sumɔɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ yɛ ŋmeii baai amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling insect pests early and pulling up severely infected plants prevents the virus from spreading to neighboring crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to dust inside the crib after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize weevils bore inside stored grain kernels to eat and lay eggs, leaving behind empty dusty shells. Properly drying maize before storage and using clean containers or safe grain treatments protects the harvest from insect damage.
ga: Abele ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo amɛwui. ni ashiɔ sũ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ Abele ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ kɛ tsɛnsii ni mli tse loo ŋmaa nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baafite lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient found in fertilizers. Applying nitrogen fertilizer early helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller cassava roots now compared to when I first cleared the land five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shishifãi bibii fe beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the ground every season. If you farm the same plot repeatedly without adding fertilizer or allowing the land to rest, the soil loses its nutrients, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji otsu okwaayeli he nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that can burn the stem and shallow roots of the plant if touched directly, which can cause the crop to wither or die.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbi loo egbo.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they struggle against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes the plants to grow tall and weak with small or no fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii ko kwraa.

english: Does leaving weeds in my field really reduce the amount of food my crops will produce?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds compete heavily with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. If weeds are left unchecked, your crops will starve and produce much lower yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping new fruits from coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai heei ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves, or transmitting a virus that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and drying up? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the internal channels carrying water from the roots up into the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo bacteria mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa trukaa yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ mligbɛ gbɛi ni kɛ nu yaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: If the main rains delay in my region, should I go ahead and plant my seeds in dry soil?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ titri ni nɛɔ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Planting in completely dry soil is risky because if a tiny rain comes and stops, the seeds may absorb just enough water to swell and decay underground before the real rains arrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ dumɔ yɛ oshara mli kɛji nugbɔ fioo nɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa. Dumɔwui baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfuu ni amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the main leaves start turning yellow and shedding. You can also pull up one plant to check if the inside of the pods has dark markings and firm seeds.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso kome hu kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ kɛji hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa.

english: Why do some flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when they fail to get pollinated by insects or wind, often due to extreme heat or dry conditions. Keeping the soil damp and allowing good airflow helps the flowers pollinate properly and turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi. Bei pii lɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How long does a cocoa flower usually stay open for pollination before it dies?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ agbeleɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli dani amɛgboi?

english: A cocoa flower usually stays open and ready for pollination for only one to two days. If tiny insects called midges do not pollinate it during this short time, the flower wilts and drops off the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha pollination gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ atswaaa kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be kukuoo nɛɛ mli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I pollinate my crops by hand if I do not see enough bees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi nine awo tsei amli pollen? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: Yes, for crops like cocoa, pumpkins, or passion fruit, you can gently transfer pollen from the male parts of the flower to the female parts using a small soft brush or cotton swab to help the fruit develop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, pumpkin loo passion fruit lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ brɔsh bibioo ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo cotton swab atsu nii ni okɛ pollen lɛ ajɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya yei lɛ amli fiofio koni eye ebua tso yibii lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop has successfully pollinated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-abele lɛ eye omanye yɛ pollination mli?

english: When maize pollinates successfully, the fresh silks hanging out from the young corn cob turn dark brown and dry out, showing that pollen has travelled inside to form the kernels.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ye omanye yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ Siliki hee ni fĩɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pollen lɛ efã kɛtee mli koni efee dumɔwui.

english: Does heavy rainfall during flowering hurt my crop's ability to produce fruit?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii lɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, heavy rain can wash pollen away from flowers and stop bees or midges from flying around, which leads to fewer flowers getting pollinated and lower fruit yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni eha ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii akafo kɛbɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii fioo pɛ shwieɔ amɛhe, ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant quickly grows new leaves and continues developing its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ ewo shishifãi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce hundreds of flowers but only a few pods mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. Many unpollinated flowers fall off naturally, and the tree drops extra young pods if it lacks enough nutrients or water to grow them all.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi babaoo ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni tso lɛ baajie ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ kwraa bɛ lɛ.

english: What kind of plants can I grow nearby to bring more pollinators to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni mikɛ pollinators babaoo aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting flowering crops like cowpea, sunflowers, or wild flowering herbs along your farm borders attracts bees and midges, which will then visit your main crops and improve fruit set.
ga: Fɔfɔi tsei tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, hulutsoo loo koo mli fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ husui lɛ ahe lɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Enɛ baaye abua ni oyasara onibii titrii lɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha aduawai akuu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do garden egg plants produce some flowers that never grow fruit even when pollinated?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ abɔɔi amli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni wooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Some garden egg plants produce 'male' flowers meant only to provide pollen, alongside hermaphrodite flowers that actually produce the fruit. The pollen-only flowers naturally drop off after releasing their pollen.
ga: Abɔɔ mli eggplants komɛi woɔ ‘hii’ fɔfɔi, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ pollen pɛ aha. Kɛfata fɔfɔi ni ji hermaphroditic ni woɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ahe lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni pollen pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛjie pollen lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many months after pollination does it take for a cocoa pod to mature for harvest?
ga: Yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani cocoa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: After successful pollination, it takes about 5 to 6 months for a cocoa pod to fully grow and ripen from green or red to a yellow or orange color.
ga: Yɛ pollination ni ye omanye sɛɛ lɛ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛshwereɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ mli.

english: Maize plants need a nutrient called nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves up to the young top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves, but the tubers in the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny nodes on their roots that pull nitrogen fertilizer out of the air and put it into the ground, leaving rich soil behind for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the shade of the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the plant to grow big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa tsei kwɛɔ bulb agboi

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they fight each other for water and plant food in the soil. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu he ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and cannot pull up enough water to match what hot sunlight bakes out of their leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a protective canopy while the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shãa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves roll up and wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves curl up to reduce their surface area and save moisture, usually recovering when the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha amɛhiɛ aba shi ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, dry soil, or sudden stress because they do not have enough water or energy to convert those flowers into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo haomɔ ni ba trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha nakai fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii ni atsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or a virus they spread, which damages the leaf tissue as it expands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo ani helai komɛi yɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa? Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are there holes and chewed leaves right in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu kɛ baai ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which crawl into the soft central whorl of the maize plant where it is moist and tender to feed on the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni mli efɔ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ koni eye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ niyenii.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees dying off suddenly after producing well for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ gbo trukaa yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛwo yibii kpakpai sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often decline or die due to viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, extreme soil nutrient depletion, or root rot. As trees age, they become more vulnerable to pests and diseases if the soil is not replenished with nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ kookoo bud virus lɛ ahewɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa loo shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Tsei hu baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small insects cause my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: Insects like capsids feed on cocoa pods and create small wounds. Fungal spores, such as those causing Black Pod disease, enter through these wounds and spread quickly, especially in wet and shaded conditions.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids yeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ pilamɔi bibii. Fungal mli tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ. Eboteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks the nutrients my cocoa trees need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil runs out of nutrients, crops show warning signs such as yellowing leaves, slow growth, small pods, or flowers falling off prematurely. Adding compost or balanced cocoa fertilizer restores these missing nutrients.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fite lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni edaa blɛoo, ŋmeii bibii, loo fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why am I getting fewer cocoa pods this year even though I weeded my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ kookoo ŋmeii fioo nɔ afi nɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding removes competition for sunlight and water, but trees also need adequate soil nutrients, proper pruning, and pest protection to produce pods. High yields require a combination of weeding, fertilizing, and disease control.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ hulu la kɛ nu he lɛ kɛyaa. Shi niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa hu he miihia tsei yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ koni akɛfee pods Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo biɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni akɛfee ekome.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and turn brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves are sensitive to intense heat and strong direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense sun dries out moisture from the leaves faster than the roots can drink water from the dry ground.
ga: Cocoa baai nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop to the ground without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: During periods of drought or severe heat stress, cocoa trees drop their flowers to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Keeping shade trees and mulching ground around the tree base helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: yɛ hɔmɔ loo latsaa be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Tsei ni akɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: When trees are planted too close, their branches block sunlight from reaching lower leaves and their roots fight over water and nutrients. Dense foliage also traps moisture, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra side shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo sɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra side shoots, known as chupons or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its energy into growing healthy flowers and large pods.
ga: Side shoots ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I start replanting a new cocoa farm on land where old trees have stopped producing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔ hee dumɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei momoi ekpa yibiiwoo nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Replanting old land requires clearing diseased wood, improving soil fertility with compost, and planting temporary shade crops like plantains before introducing new, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings.
ga: Hei momo ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ dani akɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest green or half-ripe cocoa pods alongside fully ripe ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmɔŋ loo fã ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ masɛi?

english: Unripe pods contain underdeveloped beans with low sugar content. When fermented, unripe beans turn flat or bitter, lowering the overall quality grade and market price of your entire cocoa yield.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ pods ni edako lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni edako ni sugar faaa yɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni eshɛko lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛmli edɔ. Enɛ haa o-cocoa fɛɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. Shade trees act as blankets that protect young cocoa from leaf burn, conserve soil moisture, and keep the plant cool during dry spells.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ baai ni shãa amɛ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small flies. The disease weakens the leaves so they cannot produce food, resulting in smaller cassava roots underground.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Hela nɛɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown waste inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and eat new growth, which can kill the growing point if not controlled quickly.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei heei ni eda lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbe he ni shwereɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow at the tips while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves inward in a V-shape means your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main plant food responsible for green leaves and strong vegetative growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa mli ni efeɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or excessive fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ebaai lɛ anɔ fe eyibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall sticks (stakes) so their leaves can spread out in full sunlight to make energy, which is sent down underground to feed and expand the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ niji ni kɛlɛ. Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ ni amɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and damp air cause Black Pod disease, which is a fungal infection. High humidity allows the fungus to travel across the wet pods and rot them quickly if trees are not pruned for airflow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amli ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil food. Cutting away extra shoots leaves one or two strong stems, allowing the plant to yield a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaajie tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ plantains kuu ko ni da kwraa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This soft black rot at the bottom is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant doesn't get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering that prevents roots from absorbing minerals from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ minerals kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This competition leaves you with tall, weak stems that produce very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo ni elaaje.

english: What is the main difference between dwarf and tall crop varieties when I am starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni ji dwarf kɛ tall lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Dwarf varieties stay much shorter and start producing fruits earlier—often within 3 to 4 years—making harvesting easy, while tall varieties take longer to mature but usually live and bear fruit for a much longer period.
ga: Dwarf henɔi lɛ wala be kukuoo kwraa ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra—bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli—ni no haa amɛkpamɔ feɔ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ fe nakai.

english: People keep telling me to buy F1 hybrid seeds, but what actually is an F1 hybrid?
ga: Mɛi babaoo kɛɔ mi akɛ mihe F1 hybrid dumɔwui, shi mɛni tuuntu ji F1 hybrids?

english: An F1 hybrid is created by breeding two carefully chosen parent plants to get the best traits of both, such as faster growth, higher yields, and better resistance to common farm diseases.
ga: Akɛ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ F1 hybrids lɛ koni anyɛ ana tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ amɛdaramɔ oya. Nibii ni anáa babaoo kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Can I save seeds from my harvest of hybrid crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not advisable to save and plant seeds from hybrid crops because the second generation will not grow uniformly and will result in much lower yields and weaker plants compared to the original hybrid seeds.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ato ni adu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ji hybrid dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi kwraa kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahe.

english: Why do dwarf tree varieties produce fruit much earlier than traditional tall varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dwarf henɔi lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa fe blema tsei srɔtoi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Dwarf varieties spend less time and energy building tall trunks or thick branches, allowing them to redirect their food nutrients quickly into flowering and bearing fruit.
ga: Dwarf henɔi lɛ biɔ be kɛ hewalɛ fioo dani amɛfee tsei ni kɛlɛ loo niji ni mli tse. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: How do I know if foreign crop varieties like Sri Lankan dwarf will survive in Ghana's weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko ni yɔɔ srɔto tamɔ Sri Lanka dwarf lɛ baahi shi yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli?

english: Varieties like Sri Lankan dwarf are bred for tropical climates similar to Ghana's, so as long as they receive adequate sunlight, water, and rich soil, they adapt very well and yield heavily.
ga: Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi tamɔ Sri Lankan dwarf kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tamɔ Ghana nɔ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni amɛnaa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, amɛbaashwere. Amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ mli waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii waa.

english: How does planting dwarf crop varieties help me save money on farm labor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ shika ato ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he?

english: Dwarf crops remain short enough that workers can pluck the produce directly from the ground or with short tools, eliminating the need to pay expensive labor to climb tall trees.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi kuku bɔ ni sa ni nitsulɔi baanyɛ ajie nibii ni amɛwo lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛkɛ nibii kukuji atsu nii. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni awo nyɔmɔ ni jara wa koni akɛkwɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ.

english: Do dwarf crop varieties need more fertilizer than the local tall varieties?
ga: Ani tsei bibii srɔtoi lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, because dwarf varieties produce heavy yields early in life and have smaller root systems, they need steady organic manure or fertilizer to support their heavy fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ dwarf henɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ bibioo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni baaye abua yibiiwoo ni tsii.

english: Are hybrid crop varieties less likely to get attacked by diseases on my farm?
ga: Ani helai nyɛŋ atutua tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most hybrid varieties are specially bred to withstand common local pests and diseases, giving them a better chance of survival compared to traditional non-resistant seeds.
ga: Atsɔse tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ anɔ kunim. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant a dwarf crop today, will it continue producing fruit for as many years as a traditional tall variety?
ga: Kɛ midu tso bibioo ko ŋmɛnɛ Ani ebaaya nɔ ewo yibii afii babaoo tamɔ blema tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Dwarf varieties typically have a shorter productive life span—around 20 to 30 years—whereas traditional tall varieties can continue bearing fruit for 50 years or more.
ga: Dwarf henɔi lɛ fɔɔ wala be kukuoo, aaafee afii 20 kɛyashi 30, yɛ be mli ni blema henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 50 krokomɛi loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: How do I choose whether to plant a dwarf variety or a hybrid variety on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kɛji madu dwarf loo hybrid henɔi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If you want quick early income and easy harvesting, a dwarf variety is ideal; if your priority is getting the highest total crop yield and strong disease protection, a hybrid variety is usually the better choice.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná shika oya ni okpa nii oya. Dwarf henɔi lɛ hu hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni he hiaa bo fe fɛɛ ji ni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛ helai ahebuu ni mli wa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛfee tsofa lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops like leafy green vegetables make my children grow strong bones while cassava mainly gives them energy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ, haa mibi lɛ wui ni wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji nɔ titri ni haa hewalɛ?

english: Different crops take up different minerals from the soil. Green leafy crops like kontomire soak up high amounts of calcium and iron, which build strong bones and rich blood in children, whereas root crops like cassava mainly store starch for energy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi kɛ shika tsuru srɔtoi ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji tamɔ contomires lɛ shwieɔ calcium kɛ dade babaoo. ni maa wui ni wa ni lá eyi mli obɔ yɛ gbekɛbii amli Yɛ be mli ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei titri toɔ ŋmei kɛhaa hewalɛ.

english: Which specific crops can I grow on my farm to help pregnant women in my family stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni yei ni hiɛ musu ni yɔɔ miweku lɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ?

english: Growing legumes like cowpeas and dark greens like cocoyam leaves provides rich sources of iron and folate. These essential nutrients help pregnant women produce enough healthy blood and support the developing baby's bone growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli tamɔ kookoo baai lɛ ji dade kɛ folate babaoo jɛɛhei. Niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa yei ni hiɛ musu lɛ ni amɛfeɔ lá ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eyeɔ ebuaa abifao lɛ wui lɛ adalɛ.

english: How do plants collect nutrients like iron and calcium from the ground so that humans can get them when we eat?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛbuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ dade kɛ calcium naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Bɔni afee ni adesai anine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔye amɛ.

english: Plant roots act like small straws that drink up water dissolved with minerals from the soil. The plant moves these nutrients up into its leaves and fruits, converting them into natural forms that our bodies can digest.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ paipii bibii. Nu ni anuɔ ni akɛ minerals ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efutu. Tsei kɛ niyenii nɛɛ yaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. ni etsake lɛ efee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni wɔgbɔmɔtsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ

english: Will adding manure to my soil make the crops I harvest more nourishing for my family?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miweku lɛ?

english: Yes, adding well-decomposed animal manure enriches the soil with vital minerals. Healthy, well-fed plants absorb these extra nutrients, making their harvested leaves and fruits richer in essential vitamins and minerals.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ aya hiɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni fa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ aduawai ni akpaa lɛ feɔ vitamini kɛ mineral ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why do my green vegetable plants wilt and stop growing well during hot afternoon sun in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants lose moisture quickly through tiny pores in their leaves when exposed to intense heat. If the roots cannot drink water fast enough from dry soil, the plant wilts to conserve moisture and temporarily slows its growth.
ga: Aduawai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. yɛ baai amli kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ oya bɔ ni sa lɛ, Tso lɛ baagbo kɛkɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster when I plant them right at the start of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The warm soil combined with early rains breaks seed dormancy and triggers roots to expand rapidly. Rain water also dissolves nutrients trapped in the dry soil, making food immediately available for young seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya. Nugbɔ nu lɛ hu shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ mli. Feemɔ niyenii kɛha tsei bibii ni esa akɛ aye amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough good food for my crops without buying expensive testing kits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni miheee kaa nibii ni jara wa?

english: Soil that is dark, moist, and crumbles easily usually contains rich organic food. If young crops planted in it develop deep green leaves and thick stems without yellowing, your soil has healthy nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni edɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji tso bibioo ni kwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize help my maize grow tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Nearby maize plants feed on this natural nitrogen to grow strong leaves and large cobs.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick green leafy vegetables so they have the highest nutrition?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni okɛbaakpa o-greens lɛ koni onine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo nɔ?

english: Harvest green leafy vegetables when the leaves are fully expanded, firm, and deep green, but before the plant starts producing flowers. Once flowering begins, the plant sends its best nutrients into the seeds instead of the leaves.
ga: Kpãa baai eŋɔlii beni baai lɛ egbɛ eshwa kwraa, eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ. Shi dani tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ Be ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔi shishi Tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ amɛbaai lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I keep my harvested vegetables from spoiling quickly so buyers coming home late from work in Accra can still buy them fresh?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite oya? Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni jarayelɔi ni kuɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔ mli yɛ Accra lɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ anyɛ ahe aduawai heei lolo.

english: Harvest early in the morning before the sun gets hot, store the produce under shade, and keep the roots moist. Gently sprinkling clean water on leafy greens keeps their cells full of water, preserving freshness until evening market time.
ga: Kpaa nii lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ ashɛ. Too nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi. ni eha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni mli tse ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛmli wala yibii lɛ amli eyiɔ kɛ nu. Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ jarayeli be.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn brown when I plant them directly under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shelter them from heat and maintain moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and soft on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and high-humidity environments. Moisture staying on the pods allows the fungus to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in your soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, turning the lower leaves yellow.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abele juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three heavy rains before planting my maize seeds in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ April mli lɛ?

english: Planting after just the first light shower can trick seeds into sprouting before the soil has deep moisture. If a dry spell follows, the tender seedlings will dry up and die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ wuji lɛ aba.

english: Why do my stored harvested maize grains end up with small holes and fine powder after three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kɛ powda kpakpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils. These tiny pests feed on the inside of dry maize grains and multiply rapidly in storage if the grain is not properly treated or kept in airtight containers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mli ŋmeii. tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather favors cassava mealybugs and green spider mites. These small insects attach to the undersides of leaves and suck out sap, causing leaf curling, stunting, and premature leaf drop.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa cassava mealybug kɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ sumɔɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaa mra.

english: Why do my yams develop bent, thin, and crooked tubers instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yitsei ni ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ mlɛo, ni ebɔle ehe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni etse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deeply cultivated soil or raised mounds to grow properly. Hard or compact clay soil resists tuber expansion, causing the root to twist into misshapen shapes as it tries to grow.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baate shi awo tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat or irregular watering. High temperatures can cause pollen to dry up, preventing fertilization so the plant sheds the unproductive flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green pepper fruits turn dark brown and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ashishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Irregular soil moisture prevents the plant from transporting calcium to the developing fruits.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakɛ calcium aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I cut it down completely with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishia lɛ mli beni mikɛ dade efo jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has strong underground stems called rhizomes that store energy beneath the soil surface. Simply clearing the leaves leaves the roots intact, allowing the grass to shoot up quickly again.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ojie baai lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from harsh direct sunlight. Keeping big shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa creates a cooler, humid environment that helps the young trees survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Which way should I bury cassava stems in the ground so they produce big roots?
ga: Te esa akɛ afu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛŋŋ koni ehiɛ shishifãi wuji?

english: Cassava stems grow best when planted at a slanted angle with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down stops them from sprouting properly, while planting them slanted gives the roots enough room to swell into big tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ koŋ ko nɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need full access to sunshine to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tso lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the rolled center leaves (the funnel) of young maize. Checking your farm early and applying the correct control measures into the funnel helps protect the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai (cones) ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tip ni miida lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Clearing weeds around the farm and managing these tiny insects keeps the leaves healthy and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi kɛ kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Niyenii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small plantain shoots to grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛbɔleɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only two or three strong shoots of different ages ensures bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Tsofai lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ okpa tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okwɛ jwɛi wulu ko.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seed right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the real rainy season starts. Planting too early means the seeds might sprout and then wither away in the dry soil before the steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants to lose water faster than they can absorb it, which stresses the plant and makes it drop its flowers to save energy. Providing shade or adequate watering during hot periods helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ha yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some farmers plant food crops on the same piece of land where they plant young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops like plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa provides essential shade for delicate cocoa seedlings while maximizing land use, allowing you to harvest food to eat or sell while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni akwɛɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii bɔ ni sa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni oyeɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: If I plant different types of crops together on one piece of land, will they fight each other for food in the soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsei babaoo fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, Ani amɛbaatswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When you combine the right crops—like deep-rooted tree crops with shallow-rooted food crops—they draw nutrients from different soil depths, allowing them to thrive together on the same plot without competing heavily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ tsei ni shishifãi mli kwɔ kɛ niyenii ni shishifãi bɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, Tsei nɛɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Ehaa tsei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: How can planting multiple crops on a single plot help reduce the money I spend on hiring farm laborers?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ aha shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ahemɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: When your crops are combined on one piece of land, routine work like weeding, land clearing, and fertilizing handles all your crops at the same time, saving you the extra cost of hiring separate labor teams for different fields.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Ebaakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ekɛ shika kroko ni fata he ni okɛbaahe kui sɔrɔtoi kɛha nitsumɔhe niji srɔtoi lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it easier for a single farmer to manage one mixed field or several separate fields for each crop?
ga: Ani ewaaa akɛ okwaafonyo kome baakwɛ ŋmɔji ni efutu loo ŋmɔji babaoo nɔ? Ajara ŋmɔji amli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Managing one mixed field is usually much easier because all your daily care and monitoring happen in one location, saving you travel time, energy, and the extra labor needed to oversee separate farms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ kome ni efutu lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ waaa kwraa. Ejaakɛ daa gbi nibii ni okwɛɔ kɛ nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa nɔ yɛ he kome. Enɛ haa gbɛfaa be, hewalɛ kɛ nitsumɔ kroko ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does growing cashew trees differ from growing cocoa when it comes to farm care?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro cashew tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ kookoo akwɛmɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ he?

english: Cashew trees are hardier and can tolerate drier weather with less constant attention, whereas cocoa trees require more shaded environments, regular pest control, and active field management.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei biɔ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ babaoo. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui daa kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ

english: What happens to food crops planted alongside cashew trees as the cashew trees grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni baa niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi lɛ nɔ beni ŋmei tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As cashew trees mature, their branches create a thick overhead leaf canopy that blocks sunlight; because food crops need direct sun to yield well, they are usually grown alongside cashews only during the first few years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cashew tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛniji lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli edɔ ni baai yɔɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, akɛ cashew ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2-3 lɛ pɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast in open tree crop farms, and how does intercropping help control them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds flourish when direct sunlight hits bare soil; growing food crops or cover plants between young trees covers the exposed ground and blocks sunlight, which slows down weed growth and saves you weeding labor.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ loo tsei ni akɛhaa tsei bibii ateŋ Ha hei ni agbele naa lɛ ni otsi hulu la naa. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ fioo, ni ehaaa okɛ be babaoo akatsu jwɛi lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die so easily during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight or dry soil; they need shade plants around them to trap moisture and protect them from severe sun heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he.

english: Why should I consider planting tree crops like cashew or cocoa alongside my regular food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu tsei tamɔ cashew nuts loo cocoa dumɔ he lɛ? Yɛ mi daa niyenii tsei lɛ ahe

english: Food crops give you fast returns and food security within months, while tree crops like cocoa and cashew act as long-term investments that yield income for decades on the same piece of land.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ haa anáa nibii oya kɛ niyenii ni anáa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ cashew ji nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika mli be kakadaŋŋ ni haa anáa shika afii nyɔŋmai abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: If I mix plantains or cassava with my cocoa trees, will pests from the food crops destroy my cocoa?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ plantain loo cassava futu cacao mli lɛ, Ani niyenii mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite mi-cacao lɛ?

english: Most crop pests prefer specific plant families; plantains, root crops, and cocoa trees attract different types of pests, so growing them together generally does not cause disease outbreaks between them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo sumɔɔ tsei awekui pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Plantains, shishifãi, kɛ kookoo tsei gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ekɛ helai baaa amɛteŋ.

english: Why do the rain patterns and planting times change when I move my farming from the south up towards Techiman or Wenchi?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛ́ mijie miŋmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ anaigbɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi kɛtee Techiman loo Wenchi lɛ?

english: Techiman and Wenchi lie in a transition zone between the southern forest and northern savanna. This middle belt gets a unique mix of weather, meaning rainy seasons start at different times and require adjusted planting schedules compared to the south.
ga: Techiman kɛ Wenchi yɛ tsakemɔ he ni yɔɔ kooi ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ teŋgbɛ bɛlt nɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto ni efutu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. ni esa akɛ atsake be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛ akɛto kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ he

english: How can I tell if the very first rain of the year is safe for planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: The very first rain is often a 'false rain' that leaves the soil dry again quickly. It is best to wait until you get two or three steady rains so the ground stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale’ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ekoŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food it needs to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts gives the soil a rest.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe.

english: Why did my young crops start wilting after I placed chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to the stem or applying it when the soil is dry can scorch the plant's roots, drawing water out of the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. kɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaawo mli

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop planted there.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hei ni mɛi yɔɔ ni mɛi yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need tall shade crops like plantains or tree canopy cover to protect them from heat and keep humidity high while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground allows them to catch more sunlight to feed the tuber underground, while keeping the leaves away from wet soil that can cause fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ he.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if I leave them in the ground too long after they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If cassava stays in the ground past maturity, the tubers lose starch, become woody and hard to cook, and can easily rot if heavy rains arrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋmei lɛ baafite ŋmei. Etsɔɔ tso ni ehoomɔ wa. Ni ebaanyɛ egbo oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli ewo muji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of the plant and chew through tender leaves as they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are tested in specialized laboratories to make sure they sprout reliably, resist common local diseases, and produce uniform crops, whereas seeds saved from past harvests often lose their strength and yield less over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ laboratorii pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are damaged, stored incorrectly in high heat, infected with fungi, or planted too deep in the soil where they cannot get enough air.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛfite. Akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ waa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ he ni enyɛŋ ená kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if a specific crop seed will perform well in my region's weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu pɔtɛɛ ko baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ?

english: Crops are adapted to different rainfall levels and temperatures, so using seeds approved by regional agricultural leaders ensures the variety has been proven to handle your local climate.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo bei srɔtoi anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he hiɛnyiɛlɔi ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa anaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops producing bigger yields than mine when we live in the same area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ, be mli ni wɔyɔɔ he kome lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest size usually come down to using better-quality seeds, properly feeding the soil with fertilizer or manure, spacing plants correctly, and clearing weeds early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ja gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil and cannot absorb food.
