ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves above ground but tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agbo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves on top instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai ni tsii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before any fruit or pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔii dani aduawai loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aba lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience sudden stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or pest attacks, causing them to protect themselves instead of reproducing.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mli trukaa lɛ kpe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei afã amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafɔ bii.

english: Why do some of my crops survive dry spells while others wither quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root systems; deep-rooted crops can reach hidden underground water during a drought, while shallow-rooted crops dry out as soon as the topsoil dries up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi srɔtoi. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩ pɛ.

english: Does planting my crops in straight rows really help them grow better?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, straight rows ensure every plant gets an equal share of sunlight, air, and water, while also making it easier for you to weed without damaging root systems.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi lɛ ni ofiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do crop diseases spread so quickly across my field once one plant gets sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ be mli ni tso kome hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Plant diseases caused by fungi or bacteria spread easily through wind, splashing rainwater, or insects moving from one closely planted leaf to another.
ga: Tse helai ni fungi loo bacteria kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi loo kooloi bibii ni jɛɔ baai ni adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even when I clear and weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Clearing and weeding removes competition, but crops still need food from the ground. If the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, the plants cannot grow strong no matter how clean the land is.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Shi niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lolo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus. Tsei nyɛŋ adara waa bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ha.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives leaves their rich green color and helps the plant produce energy to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and leafy but fail to produce good fruit or grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing stems and leaves instead of fruit. Plants need a balance of nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to produce healthy seeds, grains, or tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potassium fata he koni ekɛ dumɔwui, dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: What is fertilizer and how does it actually help my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mitsei lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated plant food. It adds missing nutrients back into the soil so your crops have the energy to grow faster, fight off diseases, and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Fertilizer ji tsei aniyenii ni mli eyi obɔ. Ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Wuu helai ni okɛ yibii babaoo aba

english: Will putting fertilizer on crops that are already stunted automatically save them?
ga: Ani tsei ni egbɔjɔ momo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer helps, but it is not a magic cure for sick plants. If crops are stunted due to drought, pests, or disease, applying fertilizer without fixing those main issues might stress the plant further or waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua, shi jeee majik tsofa ni akɛtsaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo hela hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni atsuuu nakai naagbai titrii lɛ ahe nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ kroko loo efite shika.

english: Can I use the exact same fertilizer for all crops like maize, cassava, and vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛpɛɛpɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai anɔ?

english: Different crops need different nutrients. Leafy vegetables need more nitrogen for leaves, while root crops like cassava need more potassium to grow thick tubers. Using the right type for each crop gives the best results.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ biɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛha amɛbaai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei biɔ potassium babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: What happens if I just throw a handful of fertilizer directly on top of my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly on the plant stem or leaves can burn them. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the base of the plant in the soil so the roots can drink it up safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi loo ebaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best time to put fertilizer in the ground so the crops can feed on it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa awo tsei amli koni amɛfee nɔ ni ayeɔ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so roots can absorb it. The best time to apply it is when the soil is already moist or right before expected light rain.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ.

english: Where can a local farmer go to ask about government-supported fertilizer programs?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi baanyɛ aya koni amɛyabi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔyeli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ he saji?

english: You can visit your district office or local Department of Agriculture extension office. They manage government fertilizer subsidy programs and assist local farmers in getting inputs.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ loo maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe lɛ. Amɛkwɛɔ nɔyeli lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ koni amɛná nibii ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is completely exhausted before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efo mi dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: If previous crops on the same land yielded less food every season, grew very slowly, or had pale leaves, your soil is likely exhausted and needs nutrients added back before the next planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ afata he dani tso kroko lɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast when I store them at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto shia lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. When stored in hot, dark, or poorly ventilated places, moisture builds up and creates a perfect environment for rot-causing fungi. Storing them on raised wooden racks in a cool, airy barn helps them stay fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛto tsei ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: How does mold get into my stored maize even when I thought the grains were completely dry?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii bote mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ misusu akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa moŋ?

english: Even if grain feels dry on the outside, internal moisture can cause mold if stored in hot places or non-breathable bags. Drying your maize on clean tarpaulins until the grains make a sharp cracking sound when bitten ensures they are dry enough to prevent mold from developing.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ, shi Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa aba kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo awo kotoku mli ni mumɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ amɛye. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa akafee.

english: Is it good to keep fresh cassava in water or a cool shaded place after harvesting to stop it from spoiling?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, ani esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa hee awo nu mli loo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ koni ekafite?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest because exposure to air triggers internal rotting. Submerging them in clean water or burying them in moist sawdust can extend their freshness for a few extra days, but processing them into gari or flour is the best long-term solution.
ga: Cassava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo nu ni mli tse mli loo ofu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli efɔ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe ahi shi gbii fioo komɛi, shi kɛ́ okɛ amɛ fee gari loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, no ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsu he nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black spots on their leaves and dry up just as they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal diseases like blight, which thrive in wet and humid conditions. Rain drops splash soil onto lower leaves, spreading fungal spores up the plant. Giving plants enough space and trimming lower leaves near the soil keeps them dry and prevents disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ, ni yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ sũ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Egbɛɔ fungal spores eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ofolɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni tso lɛ akagbi ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Can diseases from last season's crop stems infect my new crops if I plant in the same field?
ga: Ani stem hela ni ba yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa mitsei heei lɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo saatso kome nɔ?

english: Yes, many fungal and bacterial crop diseases survive in old plant remains left in the soil over the dry season. Clearing out diseased plant remains and rotating your crop families, such as planting legumes after maize, breaks the disease cycle and starves the pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ tsei momo ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ anɔ. Tso ni hela emɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ otso wekui lɛ atsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a reaction to tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies that multiply rapidly in hot weather. These insects suck the nutrient sap from the underside of leaves, causing the leaves to curl up to protect themselves from water loss while spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baashwere oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ be mli ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave my ripe maize on the farm for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving mature maize in the field exposes it to rain, field insects like weevils, and birds. Wet maize on the stalk easily develops mold that produces toxins, making the grain unsafe to eat or sell at the market.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ okpoi baashɛ he. Abɛi ni efɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jieɔ tsofai fɔji baa lɛ baa mlɛo. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay close to the soil surface. When heavy rains soften the soil, strong winds easily dislodge the roots, especially when carrying heavy bunches. Heap soil around the base and prop the stems with sturdy bamboo poles to keep them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ootere tsei niji ni tsii lɛ, too muji obɔle shishigbɛ ni okɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do imported vegetable seeds from overseas sometimes fail to perform well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, aduawai dumɔwui ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds imported from foreign climates are often bred for cooler conditions and may lack natural resistance to local tropical heat, dry spells, or soil pests. Planting certified seed varieties adapted to West African conditions ensures better yields and stronger pest resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli lɛ kɛha shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ. ni ekolɛ ebɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ hulutsoo be, hulutsoo be, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni akɛtoɔ Afrika Anaigbɛ shihilɛi ahe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibii kpakpai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe wa.

english: Why do my traditional cocoa trees live longer than the new fast-growing hybrid cocoa I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kusum cacao tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni akɛfee tsofai ni shwereɔ oya ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to yield heavy crops early in life, which drains a lot of their energy. Traditional cocoa varieties grow more slowly and build deeper root systems, allowing them to withstand harsh droughts and live longer, even though they take longer to produce pods.
ga: Afɔ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee nibii babaoo lɛ koni akɛfee nibii babaoo yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra. ni fiteɔ hewalɛ babaoo Kusum kooloi srɔtoi lɛ daaa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaa hɔmɔ ni naa wa naa, ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ ajieɔ pods moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil. Nitrogen is the main food leaves need to stay green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the heat is too high or when the soil gets too dry suddenly. The plant gets stressed by the heat and drops its flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ trukaa. Tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava field has a sickness or is just suffering from dry weather?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ hela yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛkɛ?

english: Dry weather makes all leaves droop evenly across your field, but a disease usually starts on a few plants first, causing twisted leaves, yellow spots, or dark patches even when there is some moisture in the ground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa baai shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ baa tsei fioo komɛi anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. ni kɛ baai ni etsilɛ baa Ayɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi. Aloo okadii diji yɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why should I plant my plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and cooler air for the cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting in straight rows gives every crop enough room to get sunlight and root space. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm without stepping on crops.
ga: Ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ onaji akashwieee ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to save and plant seeds from my harvest instead of buying fresh ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from modern crop varieties lose their strength over time. Planting saved seeds often results in weak plants, smaller yields, and less resistance to local pests compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, yibiiwoo baa shi, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Early morning is best because the roots absorb water before the hot sun dries up the ground, and wet leaves dry quickly in the daytime, which prevents fungal diseases from starting.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baagbi oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akabɔi baa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer off the topsoil and carry it away into drains before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to change the type of crop I plant on my land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Rotating crops starves out pests and diseases that like a specific plant, and it helps the soil stay healthy because different crops take and give different nutrients back to the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kɛyaa. tamɔ tsei komɛi Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize or rice get moldy and ruined inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain spoils in bags when it is not dried properly before storage. Trapped water creates heat inside the bag, which makes mold grow fast and attracts storage insects like weevils.
ga: Ŋmaa fiteɔ yɛ kotokui amli kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni ato, tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger plants like plantains or shade trees to survive. Direct, intense sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out the soil around their roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Which plantain sucker is the best kind for me to remove and plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ majie ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers, which have narrow leaves and a large base shaped like a bulb, are best. They grow faster and produce stronger stems and bigger bunches than water suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii kɛ shishi agbo ni tamɔ bulb lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni wa kɛ jwɛi wuji fe nu mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden sticks to stake my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunshine so the plant can make food efficiently. This extra energy is directed underground, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps green up the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni jwɛi gboi kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, holds water in the soil during hot dry days, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Should I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a dry hot week, which can dry up and kill young seeds that have just sprouted.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ kɛkɛ lɛ agboi.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars chewing holes inside the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-abele lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in maize crops. Catching them early and applying recommended organic sprays like neem extracts into the central leaves helps protect the yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu nibii ni anáa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes in the exact same soil plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same spot allows soil pests and diseases to build up and drain the specific nutrients tomatoes need. Rotating with crops like cowpeas helps clean and rebuild the soil.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛjieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tomato lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ ni etswaa ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. Watering regularly during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can grow.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: How do I choose the right stem cuttings when planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso nine ni sa kɛ́ midu ŋmei?

english: Select thick, healthy stems from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, cutting from the middle of the stem where the buds are firm and healthy.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ mli tso ni mli tse ni mli wa, ni ofo kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the tiny buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and leaves struggle to sprout properly, leading to poor growth or plant death.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight to make food. Using tall stakes lifts the leaves off the ground into full sunlight, which helps the plant store energy and build much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛhoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei kakadaji tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shade and traps moisture to protect young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo aba ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on the ground around their vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating too quickly, and stops weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very beneficial. Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper repeatedly in the same spot allows soil diseases and insects that target pepper plants to multiply. Rotating with a different crop like maize or cassava starves the pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni ji pepper tsei lɛ ayiŋtoo lɛ aya hiɛ. Nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebaaha hɔmɔ agbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent during flowering helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaves sawdust-like dust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ sũ ni tamɔ sũ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that burrow into the central leaves. Applying neem seed oil extracts or recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening kills these caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them in the middle of the afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli shwane loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during the hot midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and water droplets on hot leaves can cause leaf burning.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baa ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baa lɛ ashã.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction are meant to turn into pods. The tree naturally sheds unpollinated or weak flowers to conserve its energy for the pods it can successfully feed.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ No sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ pod. Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha fɔfɔi ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ.

english: Why do the young leaves on my cocoa tree start out soft and reddish before turning hard and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: New cocoa leaves produce red pigments to shield their delicate tissues from intense sunlight while they develop. As the leaves mature, they develop chlorophyll, which turns them green so they can start making food for the tree.
ga: Kookoo baai heei jieɔ su tsuru ni buɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Amɛbaafee klorofil. ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji. Bɔni afee ni oje niyenii feemɔ shishi oha tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branches during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal spores (black pod disease) to spread. The fungus attacks the damp pod skin, causing it to rot rapidly if there is not enough air circulating through the farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores (black pod hela) lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Fungi lɛ tutuaa pod hewolo ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees producing only male flowers and no fruit bunches yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso bibioo lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Young oil palms usually produce mostly male flowers in their first few years to build up stem and root strength. Once the tree reaches maturity, it will start producing female flowers that grow into oil-bearing fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ji hii lɛ babaoo yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebɔi fɔfɔi yei ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm turning yellow and drooping down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: As an oil palm grows taller, it naturally sheds its oldest bottom leaves to redirect water and nutrients to the growing top leaves and fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Beni mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ hu shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii aya ŋwɛi baai lɛ kɛ aduawai akui ni miida ehee lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm bunches end up with tiny, empty fruits that have no oil in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ hiɛ aduawai bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni fɔ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the female flowers are not properly pollinated by insects or wind. Without proper pollination, individual fruitlets on the bunch fail to develop kernels and palm oil.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ fɔfɔi yei ahe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ Yibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui kɛ ŋmei fɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with plenty of leafy branches, but the tubers under the soil remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing upper stems and leaves instead of storing starch in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why is my plantain sucker taking so long to produce a flower bunch after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ fɔfɔii akui baa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of soil moisture and nutrients to build a thick false stem before they can push out a flower. If the soil lacks food or water is low, the plant delays flowering until conditions improve.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni efee pseudostems ni mli tse dani ebaanyɛ eshɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baaha fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm roll up tightly into tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tight to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down the amount of water the plant loses through evaporation during the heat of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa nu ni tsei lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, pepper plants experience heat stress and shed their flowers to save water and keep the main stem alive rather than trying to feed new fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai heei aba

english: Why do useful medicinal plants grow on my farm bush even when I never planted seeds for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduko dumɔwui ko pɛŋ moŋ?

english: Seeds from wild plants and herbs are naturally spread across farmland by wind, rain, and birds. Many of these natural plants are hardy and naturally sprout in farm bushes to cover the soil and provide natural remedies.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi gbɛɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ koo mli tsei kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei nɛɛ ateŋ babaoo wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei bibii amli akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa.

english: Is it safe for me to leave wild bushes and herbs growing around the borders of my cocoa farm?
ga: Ebaafee shweshweeshwe kɛha mi akɛ mashi koo mli tsei kɛ tsofai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving natural plants along farm borders is safe. They act as windbreaks, keep the soil cool, and attract good insects that help pollinate your main crops while providing useful herbal remedies.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli husui ahe. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni amɛgbalaa kooloi kpakpai kɛbaa jɛmɛ. No yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ pollination woɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa tsofai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava crop drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather as a natural defense trick to save water inside its roots. Once the rains start again, the stem will quickly sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ko ni haa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ yitso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun is very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense sun to hide their surface from the heat. This helps the plant trap moisture inside itself so it does not dry out before evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛha nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ dani gbɛkɛ shɛɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines always search for sticks or trees to climb upward instead of growing on the flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ taoɔ tsei niji loo tsei ni ekwɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb upward naturally to reach maximum sunlight. The sun gives the leaves energy to make food, which is then stored underground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛha hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu lɛ haa baai hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow even though there is water in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is missing essential food like nitrogen from the soil, or that the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen or prevent insects from visiting the flowers. Without pollination, the plant cannot form fruit and simply drops the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo etsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkasara fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ baashwie shi kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce better crops after I leave it to go back to bush for two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni mishi lɛ yɛ koo lɛ mli ekoŋŋ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When land rests, wild plants and bushes grow deep roots that bring up trapped minerals, rot into rich natural manure, and restore life to tired soil naturally.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ miihe ejɔ ehe lɛ, koo mli tsei kɛ tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛjie shika tsuru ni emɔ mli lɛ. Rotting ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni ekɛ wala aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni etɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow better and faster when I plant them together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni eyaa oya kɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ du lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and maize help each other; cowpeas pull natural nitrogen food from the air into the soil to feed the maize, while maize offers support and light shade.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe. Cowpeas gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa haa hulutsoo ni ehaa hulutsoo.

english: How can I know if a wild plant growing near my crops is feeding the soil or stealing from it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ loo amɛmiiju amɛ?

english: Plants with soft green leaves that decay easily usually feed the soil with manure, while aggressive weeds with thick spreading roots tend to steal water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni baa eŋɔli yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants roll their leaves inward during peak afternoon heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and reduce water loss through their leaf pores.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava drops leaves in hot, dry weather to reduce its water needs and protect its roots until rains return to stimulate new leaf growth.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ nii shi ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ eba koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or water is scarce, causing heat stress that prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Enɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee aduawai baa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize indicates nitrogen deficiency, as the plant moves limited nitrogen from older leaves to support newer top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ yɛ tsei heei anɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow much better when I plant groundnuts or beans on the field first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil with food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn under intense direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain leaves act as a living umbrella to provide the necessary shade and moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ baashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa aha.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking spreads out yam leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight, allowing the vine to produce more energy that gets stored in the growing underground tuber.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds together in the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ ŋmãa bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the roots and shoots to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are typically caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on young leaves, or by a viral infection carried by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when rain sits on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to breathe; standing water drowns the root system and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungal rots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomatoes right next to my garden eggs in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs (eggplants) belong to the same plant family, like close siblings. Because they share the same weaknesses, planting them together allows pests and diseases to spread easily between them, destroying both crops.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii (eggplants) ji tso weku kome mli bii tamɔ nyɛmimɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa. Ejaakɛ amɛ hu amɛyɛ gbɔjɔmɔi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baagbɛ amɛshwã amɛteŋ. Akpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land right after harvesting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously starves the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs. It also allows soil diseases and pests that target cassava to multiply, causing your second harvest to produce weak and small tubers.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ ŋmei lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa okpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest produce weaker plants than the certified seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui ni mihe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: When crops cross-pollinate with close genetic relatives in the same field generation after generation, their offspring lose strength and yield potential. Certified seeds are specially bred from distinct parent lines to give the crops high vigor and strong yields.
ga: Beni tsei kɛ amɛwekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ feɔ cross-pollinate yinɔi kɛ yinɔi. Amɛbii lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo he nyɛmɔ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi akui srɔtoi amli. Koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: If I plant sweet cassava close to bitter cassava, will my sweet cassava turn bitter?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ lɛ masɛi Ani ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baafee ŋmei?

english: The tubers you harvest from the sweet cassava this season will not change taste. However, if seeds form from cross-pollination between the two and you grow new plants from those seeds, the new plants may inherit the bitter traits.
ga: Tubers ni okpaa kɛjɛɔ sweet cassava mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsakeŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛ cross-pollination ni tee nɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ mli ba ni okɛ tso hee ko jɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei Heei hu baanyɛ aná su ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and yam in the exact same mound to save space on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ koni mikɛ he ko akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava and yam both feed heavily on the same nutrients and need space for root development. Placing them in the exact same mound forces them to fight each other, resulting in stunted plants and very weak tubers for both.
ga: Cassava kɛ sweet potato yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔŋŋ babaoo ni ehe hiaa he ko ni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛwu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ bulbs ni bɛ hewalɛ waa kɛhaa amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant beans together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and maize work together as good companions. Beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the tall maize stalks support the bean vines as they grow.
ga: Bean kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii akɛ nanemɛi kpakpai. Beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ. be mli ni ŋmãa tsei kakadaŋŋ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ŋmãa tso lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—their leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as living umbrellas until they are old and strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and die when I move them straight from the nursery bed into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings grown in a sheltered nursery get shocked by sudden heat and direct sun. They need to be gradually exposed to sun for a few hours each day before transplanting so they become strong enough to survive the main field.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ he feɔ amɛ yaa. Esa akɛ amɛfee fiofio Get hulu la ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi daa gbi dani adu amɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete aggressively with each other for light and nutrients. They stretch upward fighting for sunlight instead of spending energy to produce strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatswa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ tsei agboi.

english: Why does Striga weed destroy my sorghum field, but does not harm my groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miifite mi ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi eyeee mi-peanuts lɛ awui.

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that only recognizes chemical signals from cereal crops like sorghum. Groundnuts belong to a completely different plant family, so Striga cannot attach to their roots or feed off them.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni nuɔ tsofai ni jɛɔ ŋmaa tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ pɛ he. Peanuts yɛ tso weku ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa mli, no hewɔ lɛ Striga nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ shishifãi ahe loo eye amɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need proper soil moisture, warmth, and correct planting depth to germinate. If the soil is too dry, too hard, or if pests eat the seeds underground, they will not sprout.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ, dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ewa tsɔ, loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings grow tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee shwiili moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow long and weak (leggy) when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. They stretch upwards searching for light, which weakens their main stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ (naji) kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer or if the soil is already good enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ momo?

english: If your crops have light green or yellow leaves and grow very slowly, the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Healthy green growth usually means the soil currently has enough food for the plant.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edaa blɛoo waa. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific plant to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. It reduces the plant's ability to make food and grow large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves and how does it affect the crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te enaa tsei anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Small holes are caused by caterpillars and beetles eating the leaves. Damage to the leaves reduces the plant's ability to absorb sunlight and form a solid, healthy cabbage head.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Baai lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛjieɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ kaabe yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun heats up. Afternoon watering leads to fast evaporation and can stress hot plant roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ adumɔ he?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to smaller yields and faster spread of diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination. High temperatures make the pollen inactive, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni bɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa pollen ŋmaa lɛ tsuuu nii. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for dry grain harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and paper-dry, and a small black mark appears at the base of the grain kernels.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni efee tamɔ wolo lɛ. ni eyɛ okadi diŋ bibioo ko Jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and leaves that cannot withstand direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to block the harsh heat, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it, causing them to dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to make green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted poultry manure or the right fertilizer will help the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I find small caterpillars hiding inside the center of my maize plants eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on maize leaves. The caterpillars crawl into the central funnel where the softest leaves are to feed; catching them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ, he ni baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down into the root tubers. A balanced soil nutrient approach helps the plant build bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatsu nii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that goes down into building large yams. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and giving them full access to sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni niyenii ni yaa mli lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when a strong rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can become weak if there are too many young suckers growing around the main stem or if pests damage the roots. Cutting away extra suckers leaves the main stem strong and well-anchored in the soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe. tso titri lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli awa ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or irregular watering because the plant gets stressed and tries to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Wrinkled or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by severe water stress during hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and leave it in the soil, which acts as natural food for whichever crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the light, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need to thrive, effectively starving your crops even if rainfall is good.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ kpakpa nɛ po.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient that helps plants stay green and build food. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep into the ground where the roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get dark, rotten spots at the bottom of the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi waa, ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Why do my bean plants grow very tall with many leaves but fail to produce bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo bean ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the bean plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves and stems instead of spending energy on flowering and forming bean pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Bean tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee fɔfɔi ni efee bean pods lɛ,.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the farm for long periods, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the farm for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sunlight. More sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down to grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishitoo mlai anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a special way of growing where flowers bloom above ground, but after pollination, the stem bends downward and buries itself in the soil so the nuts can safely grow underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ yɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and wither when there are no plantains planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide wide shade leaves that act as protective umbrellas for young cocoa plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as excessively hot dry winds, sudden drops in soil moisture, or a lack of nutrients needed to nourish developing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha aduawai ni miida lɛ aná hewalɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have tiny round holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves. As they eat, they weaken the plant's ability to form a strong, solid cabbage head.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ Hewalɛ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ kaabe yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and fast-growing. Their roots quickly drink up water and fertilizer before young crop seeds have enough time to establish their own roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshishifãi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings grow better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo kookoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the damp ground so they can catch direct sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make food to grow larger tubers, while keeping leaves off the ground protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out completely. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The leaves wilt to protect themselves from the heat, but they usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers that drop off without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the soil lacks sufficient moisture or nutrients, or if tiny insects called midge flies haven't pollinated them. Maintaining proper shade trees helps retain moisture and encourages pollination.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ŋmeii lɛ eshɛko amɛhe lolo. Tso ni yɔɔ shade lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa pollination yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer or animal manure before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your previous crop had pale yellow leaves, thin stalks, or produced small ears, your soil is low on nitrogen and other nutrients. Rich soil usually looks dark, feels crumbly, and contains earthworms.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo toi bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ duŋ, enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does planting cover crops like beans or cowpeas make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii? No hewɔ lɛ eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.
