english: Legume crops like beans pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plants die, they decay and release natural fertilizer into the ground while keeping the soil moist and weed-free.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, egboɔ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi hu bɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get dark spots on their leaves and die when I plant them in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot continuously allows crop-specific diseases and fungal spores to build up in the soil. Rotating your plot with maize or cassava starves out these diseases between tomato seasons.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tomato yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe kɛ ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsakemɔi ni okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baafee lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai nɛɛ anaa yɛ tomato be mli.

english: What is eating the middle of my young maize leaves and leaving holes and waste inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ni eshiɔ bu kɛ jwɛi yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended bio-pesticides or local controls can protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ yi loo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my hybrid maize harvest produce smaller crops than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed from two distinct parent plants to produce maximum yield only in the first generation. Saving and replanting those seeds breaks that special genetic combination, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ foɔ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni abuɔ he ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ gbalaa fɔmɔ nii krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom upward when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth, or when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do people advise planting groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that catch nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, providing free natural plant food for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ eji adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool under the hot sun, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn in direct sunlight and dry winds; they require temporary shade plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas and keep the soil damp.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds early before the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ato mra. Dani wain tsei lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam plants use up massive amounts of soil energy in their first few months to build vines and tubers; early weeding ensures weeds do not steal that food before the yam becomes established.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli koni amɛkɛfee wain tsei kɛ ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akaju nakai niyenii lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of friendly insects like bees to transfer pollen between flowers to trigger fruit growth.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni eha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why does my plantain stand give me small bunches even when the main stem grows tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ.

english: Allowing too many shoots, or suckers, to grow around the main plant causes them to fight for the same water and soil food, leaving less energy for the main plant to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, no haa ehe bahiaa ni amɛwu koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe, ni no haa tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers come out thin and woody instead of thick and starchy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn woody if planted in hard soil that prevents tubers from swelling, or if left in the ground too long past harvest time, causing the plant to convert its stored starch back into tough wood fibers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafu. aloo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in flooded water while my maize rots and dies in the same conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice stems have natural air tubes inside them that transport oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots have no air tubes and suffocate when submerged in water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi lɛ. Shi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ, ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do small worms gather inside the center leaves of my young maize and chew ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu ni elaaje lɛ?

english: These pests, called Fall Armyworms, seek out the tender, moist funnel of young maize leaves because it offers soft food and shelter from heat and predators while they feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ taoɔ hei ni ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhaa niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ wɔɔhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a major food plants need to grow green and healthy. This happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa ni ehe miihia ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist and the crop is actively growing, usually 2 to 3 weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer on dry soil or during heavy rainfall causes it to evaporate or wash away before the plant can feed on it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la loo nu lɛ baaho dani tsei lɛ aye.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the exact same soil nutrients every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin plants with small fruit and a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, aduawai bibii kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit near the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting them with strong wooden props (forked sticks) helps anchor them against wind damage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni no haa amɛ ŋwɛigbɛ tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa (chopsticks) fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when rain water stays on the field for too long without draining, causing fungi in the wet soil to attack the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants twisting up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. As the whiteflies feed on the leaf sap, they infect the plant, causing leaves to curl up and stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly yɛ be mli ni whiteflies yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Amɛbaatswa tso lɛ hela. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the branches without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they experience water stress, severe insect attack, or if there are not enough tiny insects present in the farm to pollinate the flowers into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nu afua. Kplukai tutuaa kɛ yiwalɛ Aloo kplukai bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying small and refusing to grow taller after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get stunted if their delicate root system was damaged during transplanting, or if the soil is too hard, too wet, or lacks compost to encourage root spreading.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo ebɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately after receiving rain water, absorbing available nutrients faster than young crop seedlings that need time to settle.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛna nugbɔ nu. Enɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni he hiaa be koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to mix different chemicals and household liquids together when pests attack my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi baafutu lɛ? kɛ shia nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ekomefeemɔ beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals or liquids can burn your crop leaves, kill the good insects that naturally fight pests, make the pests immune to real medicines, and leave harmful chemical residues on food you sell or eat.
ga: Tsofai loo nu ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi kpakpai ni kɛ kooloi bibii wuɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɛɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni ohɔ̃ɔ loo oyeɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do pests like armyworms know when my maize crops are weak and ready to be attacked?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be mli ni mi-ŋmã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaatutua mi?

english: When crops are stressed by lack of water, bad soil, or extreme heat, they release subtle odors and change leaf colors that insects can sense from far away, signaling that the plant has low defenses.
ga: Kɛji nu ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tsei miihao lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ko ni bɛ faŋŋ ni etsakeɔ baai lɛ ahe su ni kooloi baanyɛ ana kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hebuu babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo ni potassium loo fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium, as the plant tries to save water and energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle full sunlight, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and hold moisture in the soil until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do yellow patches appear on my cassava leaves, making them curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow patterns and curling leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies or spread when you plant cuttings taken from infected stems.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whitefly bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ko ni hiɛɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Aloo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ ofo tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does leaf rot and black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ pod black hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases thrive in high humidity; raindrops splash microscopic disease spores from the soil and infected leaves onto healthy pods, allowing the rot to spread rapidly when weather stays wet.
ga: Fungal helai yaa hiɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ amli kɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fitemɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves usually show that the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the plant nutrients deeper into the ground where the roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop yields to drop even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, allowing them to steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your plants before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting in the barn even when they looked healthy during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Tiny cuts or scratches made during harvesting allow invisible rot fungi into the tuber, and if the storage barn is warm and lacks fresh air, those germs multiply and turn the yam soft.
ga: Nibii bibii ni afolɔ loo afolɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ Nakai helatsɛmɛi lɛ baafa babaoo ni amɛha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do international buyers reject my crops even when they taste very good to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ waa kɛha mi moŋ?

english: Foreign buyers check for strict appearance criteria like uniform size, lack of blemishes, and absence of chemical residues, because crops must survive long transit times and match standard grocery store requirements overseas.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ nihɔɔlɔi kwɛɔ bɔ ni ehiɛ yɔɔ ha tamɔ dalɛ ni yɔɔ daa, tɔmɔ ko bɛ he kɛ tsofa ko ni eshwɛɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ gbɛfaa be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛshɛ taomɔ nii ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ shwapoi ni ahɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: If I spray more chemical pesticides on my crops, will that make them look cleaner and easier to sell for export?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: Using excess pesticides leaves invisible chemical residues on crops that overseas inspectors test for and reject, so following strict spraying schedules and chemical limits is necessary for export sales.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsofai ni anaaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni maŋsɛɛ kwɛlɔi kaa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛkpooɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ ahe husui kɛha nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so quickly before I can get them to the buyer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops continue to breathe and generate heat after harvest, so keeping them in direct sunlight or crammed tightly in unventilated sacks speeds up breakdown and rotting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite ni amɛfite oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive harsh direct sunlight and need living shade from larger trees or crops like plantain to maintain soil moisture and protect their tender leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crop leaves become very green and bushy after I put fertilizer, but fail to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli lɛ sɛɛ, shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: High-nitrogen fertilizers encourage leaves and stems to grow, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to trigger flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni eha amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii adalɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing short and thin when I plant them close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crowding plants forces them to compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller, weaker plants and lower overall yields.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my land yield less cassava every season when I grow it on the same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, which is why rotating crops helps restore natural fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crop plants turning yellow and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are common signs that sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids are feeding on the plant, or that the crop is infected with a plant virus.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids miiye tso lɛ. aloo tso lɛ mli hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ tso lɛ

english: Why do the roots of my crops turn black and soft when I water them frequently during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo nɔ shii abɔ lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Overwatering fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful fungi to breed and cause root rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crop plants more during hot, dry weather than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dry weather causes water stress in plants, making them weaker and easier for insect pests to feed on, while many sap-sucking insects reproduce faster in warm, dry conditions.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Yɛ be mli ni koolooi babaoo ni nuɔ nu lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ,

english: How can I calculate if my cocoa farm will actually make a profit this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he akɔntaa kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baaná sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: To calculate profit, you write down all money spent on labor, fertilizers, and spraying, and subtract that total from the total money you receive after selling your harvested cocoa beans. If the money from sales is bigger than your expenses, you made a profit.
ga: Bɔni afee ni obu sɛɛnamɔ he akɔntaa Obaa ŋma shika fɛɛ ni ofite yɛ nitsumɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ojie shika fɛɛ ni onáa kɛjɛ shika fɛɛ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ beni ohɔ̃ɔ kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji shika ni jɛɔ jarayeli mli baa lɛ fa fe shika ni afiteɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ oná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: What main things should I look at before deciding whether to plant mangoes or cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu mango loo kookoo?

english: Look at your land's soil type, rainfall in your area, how many years you can wait before the trees start fruiting, the upfront cost of inputs, and whether you have a ready buyer or market near you.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Be enyiɛ obaanyɛ omɛ dani otso lɛ aje yibii womɔ shishi? Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni esa akɛ awo kɛtsɔ hiɛ Ni okwɛ kɛji oyɛ mɛi ni baahe nii loo jarayeli hei ni bɛŋkɛ bo.

english: How long does it take for a new cocoa seedling to start producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, but newer hybrid cocoa varieties developed in Ghana can start producing pods in just 2 to 3 years if cared for well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo tsei lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii, shi kookoo tsei heei ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii awomɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose water rapidly in dry wind and heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain and regular watering to survive harsh weather.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa ba amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good beans for me?
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo kɔfe yibii kpakpai. Afii enyiɛ obaanyɛ oha mi?

english: A healthy, well-managed cocoa tree can produce profitable yields for 25 to 30 years, with its peak production years usually occurring between ages 10 and 20.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni bei pii lɛ, afii ni amɛwoɔ nii babaoo lɛ baa yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 teŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa farms in my community yield so many pods while others yield very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ woɔ pod yibii babaoo ni ekrokomɛi hu woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come from using improved seed varieties, maintaining correct soil fertility with fertilizers, regular pruning, effective control of pests like capsids, and managing shade levels properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ shade ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: How many years will I wait before my new mango tree gives me fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mango tso hee awo yibii?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start fruiting within 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown directly from a mango seed can take 6 to 8 years before producing their first fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛyibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers due to dry spells without enough water during flowering, fungal diseases like anthracnose, or insect attacks. Proper spraying and watering help flowers stay attached.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii yɛ hulutsoo be ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose hewɔ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my young mango trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant annual crops between young tree rows during the first two years to feed your family and earn income, as long as you keep the food crops a few feet away from the tree stems so they don't steal nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni akɛkwɛ weku lɛ nɔ ni akɛfee shika. Shii abɔ ni okɛ niyenii tso lɛ toɔ tso lɛ he ninetalɔi fioo komɛi koni ekaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ,

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant big mango trees inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu mango tso agbo ko yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is generally not recommended because fully grown mango trees create dense, heavy shade and compete aggressively for water, which reduces the amount of sunlight and nutrients cocoa trees need to form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ afee enɛ ejaakɛ mango tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my mango trees seem to get sick mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ he yeɔ be pii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases, especially fungal infections that affect mangoes, need moisture to grow. Rain helps disease spores travel from leaf to leaf and provides the wet conditions the disease needs to infect the fruit.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo Titri lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mango nɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i he miihia koni ekwɛ̃. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni hela lɛ he hiaa koni ekɛwo aduawai lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Can rain actually harm my fruit trees instead of helping them grow?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baanyɛ aye mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: While rain gives plants the water they need, excessive moisture also creates the ideal environment for plant diseases to appear and spread rapidly across your farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ haa tsei lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ moŋ, shi hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni sa baaha tsei ahe helai aba ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does plant disease spread so fast across my farm after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops splash disease germs from infected leaves onto healthy ones. The high moisture after a storm also allows these germs to quickly enter and infect the plant tissue.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ shwieɔ helai ni jɛɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa yɛ ahum ko sɛɛ lɛ hu haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ amli fãji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it so difficult for me to get a good yield from my mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii kpakpai anɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ mango tso lɛ nɔ ani ewa kɛha mi?

english: Mangoes are sensitive to widespread diseases that attack during wet weather. These diseases spoil the fruits early, making it very challenging to achieve a successful harvest without proper management.
ga: Hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni tutuaa mɛi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa mango. Helai nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, eji kaa kpele akɛ aaakpa nikpamɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my mangoes to rot or develop spots right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mango lɛ fiteɔ loo enáa ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa?

english: This damage is usually caused by rain-triggered diseases. Moisture on the skin of the developing fruit allows fungal infections to take hold, causing spots and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli kɛbaa lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahewolo nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Are mango diseases a problem everywhere in Ghana or just on my farm?
ga: Ani mango hela ji naagba yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he loo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Mango disease is a major issue faced by farmers all across Ghana and in many parts of the world, especially in areas that experience heavy rainfall.
ga: Mango hela ji naagba wulu ko ni okwaafoi kɛkpeɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ kɛ je lɛŋ hei babaoo. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ.

english: Who can I talk to when I cannot figure out what is killing my crops?
ga: Namɔ mikɛ lɛ baanyɛ agba sane? Akɛni mileee nɔ ni gbeɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: You can consult agricultural extension officers or plant doctors. They are trained to identify specific crop diseases, explain how weather affects them, and recommend treatments.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo nitsumɔhe datrɛfoi lɛ agba sane. Atsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛyoo tsei ahe helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ saa helai ahe ehaa lɛ mli. ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa hela lɛ

english: How does the weather in Ghana affect how plant diseases behave?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ saa tsei ahe helai lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ghana's warm temperatures combined with rainy seasons create warm, humid conditions. This climate is what helps plant diseases thrive, multiply, and attack crops most effectively.
ga: Ghana dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni haa tsei ahe helai daa, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Should I care for my mango trees differently when the rainy season starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Yes, because rain helps diseases appear, you need to protect your trees early by pruning branches to allow sunlight and wind to dry the leaves quickly after it rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ helai. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni obu otsei lɛ ahe mra. Kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aye abua baai lɛ ni amɛgbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is there a way to prevent rainy weather from ruining my fruit crop?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While you cannot stop the rain, you can protect your crop by spraying approved preventatives before the rains start and keeping the ground beneath your trees clean of fallen, diseased leaves.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ onyɛɛɛ okpa nugbɔ lɛ moŋ Shi obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ nugbɔ lɛ naa lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi lɛ nɔ. Ni ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he atse kɛjɛ baai ni egbee shi ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the weather becomes too sunny and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and need protection from intense sunlight. Providing shade trees or intercropping with plantains protects them from heat stress and helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ha tsei ni miida lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off due to lack of water, excessive heat, pest attacks, or poor pollination. Ensuring proper shade, spraying for pests, and keeping the farm clear helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Nu ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi. hulutsoo ni fa fe nine Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔ loo pollination ni ehiii Shade ni sa He ni akwɛɔ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse Ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aaaha efee faŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my growing cocoa trees if they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni miida lɛ niji komɛi kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches so the tree focuses its energy on producing larger cocoa pods. It also opens up the canopy to let sunlight and air pass through, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ. Egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ hu naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to plant maize without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni miheee ŋmãa ni jara wa?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels moist, and has earthworms or rotting leaves in it. If natural weeds grow thick and dark green on the land, it shows the soil has good nutrients for crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni miigboi yɛ mli. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to yield a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them if spaced correctly. Maize grows and matures quickly, so you harvest it first while the cassava is still young, preventing them from competing for resources.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofo amɛ kɛji akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja. Abɛi daa ni edaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Koni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekaye nibii ahe akaŋshii

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Weeding regularly and pruning trees allows air and sunlight to dry the farm and slow the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Tsei ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa hela lɛ shishijee baa shi.

english: Why are small worms eating the leaves of my maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ leebi lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the plant leaves during the heat of the day and come out to feed when it is cool. Checking your crops early allows you to catch and spray them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso. Nibii ni adu lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ dani nibii ni adu lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally stronger and better adapted to local soil conditions, so they absorb rain and nutrients faster than crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food they need.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How does long dry weather affect my cocoa trees, and how can I keep them alive?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi?

english: Dry weather causes trees to lose water fast, leading to leaf drop and small pods. Covering the soil around the tree base with dry leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps water longer.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii bibii feɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting maize before the rains start?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa?

english: Good soil preparation involves clearing weeds and tilling the earth so it is loose. If you dig up a handful of soil after a light rain and it crumbles easily without forming a hard, sticky lump, it is loose enough for seeds to sprout easily.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ koni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji otsa shikpɔŋ ko yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ, Ni efiteɔ oya ni efeee ŋmeii ni wa ni shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves usually turn yellow due to a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, severe dry weather, or sap-sucking pests like green mites. Adding well-rotted manure or compost to the soil helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On very hot days, tomato plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The leaves temporarily curl or wilt to reduce water loss, and they usually stand back up once the sun goes down and temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe loo amɛbaagboi be kukuoo ko koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms lay eggs on young leaves because the soft shoots are easy for their caterpillars to feed on. Inspecting your field regularly and applying natural neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides at the first sign of damage keeps them under control.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ mlɛo. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under the harsh sun. Keeping mature shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides the cool shade and soil moisture needed for survival.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe Ebaaha hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season before planting my maize instead of planting right after the first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli dani adu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: A single early rain is often followed by dry weeks that can dry out and kill germinating seeds. Waiting for the established rainy season ensures that young roots get a steady supply of water to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome lɛ nyiɛɔ otsi ni mli egbi sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu daa koni amɛdara waa.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the bed?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso nɔ?

english: When pepper plants grow too close together, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients, and their leaves block each other's sunlight. Spacing them properly ensures each plant grows thick stems and produces bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa tso lɛ shishi ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni da.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops each year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns vital nitrogen to the soil and restores its natural fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my crops grow better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds beneficial soil organisms and improves the soil's structure, allowing it to hold onto water and nutrients longer. This gives crop roots a constant supply of food even during short dry spells between rains.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã ji niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii be fɛɛ be yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ po mli.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when they are bruised during harvest or stored in warm, airless spaces where fungal spores thrive. Storing undamaged yams on raised bamboo racks in a well-ventilated, shaded barn prevents dampness and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ he ni ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko to ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good for crops if I have never planted anything on this land before?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Eji miduko nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ dã kulɛ

english: New or unused land often has rich dark topsoil filled with organic material, but clearing weeds, checking how fast water drains, and loosening tight soil ensures young crop roots can easily breathe and search for nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei heei loo akɛtsuuu nii lɛ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ. Shi jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ muɔ mlɛo ni amɛnaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives plant-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa.

english: What signs should I look for to know my young maize plants are making good progress?
ga: Mɛɛ okadi esa akɛ matao koni male kɛji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy maize shows deep green leaves, thick stems, and steady, uniform height across the field, which indicates the roots are successfully taking up water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii ni tsuɔ, eshishifãi lɛ mli tse, ni elɛɛmɔ yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How can I tell if my newly transplanted plantain suckers have taken root properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei ni midu ehee lɛ miiwo shishifãi jogbaŋŋ?

english: When a plantain sucker establishes good roots, the old outer leaves may dry up while a new, bright green leaf unfurls from the center stem within two to three weeks.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ, amɛfeɔ shishifãi kpakpai. Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi, yɛ be mli ni baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baaje kpo kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to handle crop seed sprouts so carefully when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei amli dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: The early sprout contains the tiny root tip that feeds the growing plant; if this tip snaps or bruises during planting, the sprout will die or grow into a weak, stunted plant.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni haa tso ni miida lɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa fã loo ekpɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaadara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply too much fertilizer thinking it will speed up growth?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii ni misusu akɛ ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Excess fertilizer acts like salt on plant roots, burning them and pulling water away from the plant, which causes leaves to turn brown, dry up, and die.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni fa fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo yɛ tsei shishifãi anɔ. Shã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ojie nu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ asasu, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I catch diseases on my cassava plants early before my whole farm gets ruined?
ga: Mamɔ hela lɛ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ mra. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ efee dani akpata ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ?

english: Look regularly for unusual leaf curling, yellow spots, or stunted leaves at the tip of the branches; removing affected leaves early prevents insects from carrying the sickness to healthy plants.
ga: Kwɛmɔ daa akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo baai ni egbɔjɔ yɛ tsei niji lɛ anaagbee Baai ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ mra Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ helai kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops curl and droop under intense afternoon sun to shrink their leaf surface area and slow down water loss when the air is hotter than what the roots can pump up.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi koni ekɛba baai lɛ anɔ shi ni ekɛba nu ni hoɔ fiofio lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛhe.

english: Can giving my crops too much water cause them to die?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe tso lɛ?

english: Yes, waterlogging fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots so they rot, which turns the leaves yellow and kills the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why does crowding my seeds close together lead to a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛmiimiɔ amɛhe lɛ haaa kpamɔ kpakpa aba lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground moisture, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii loo dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the maize, acting as a free natural fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize farm turn light yellow after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away important plant food like nitrogen deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach, making the leaves lose their dark green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads grow bigger when I mix dry chicken droppings into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe yitsei lɛ feɔ agboi kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is high in nitrogen and natural plant food, which gives leaf crops like cabbage the rich nutrition they need to form dense, heavy heads.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ baai, tamɔ kaabe lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee yitsei ni mli etsii ni tsii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding and eating deep inside the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛyaa mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer the hidden central leaves (the whorl) because the plant leaves there are soft to eat and offer protection from heat and rain.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ (rings) ejaakɛ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ayeɔ ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and produce a white powder during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni powda yɛŋ yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather when cool air and moisture get trapped under thick tree branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ekpɛtɛ tsei aniji ni mli tse lɛ ahe lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants roll up and shed during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops some leaves and rolls others up during hot, dry spells to save water, allowing the plant to sleep and protect its roots underground until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ baai yɛ be mli ni edɔ, be mli ni nu egbi koni ekɛbu nu he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewɔɔ ni ebuɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the middle of the day even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, causing the stems to temporarily bend until the sun lowers.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ ahi shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the stem instead of turning into hot pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper yibii ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or lack of water, letting the flowers fall so the plant saves energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni tso lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ehi wala mli.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: When the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season, it means the plant has stopped feeding and the tuber underground is fully mature.
ga: Beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii yeli ni eshishifãi lɛ edara.

english: How can I tell if the farm medicines or chemicals I am buying are safe and not fake?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni jeee amale?

english: Fake or poor-quality farm chemicals often lack proper regulatory approval stamps, batch numbers, or clear manufacturer details. Buying from certified and tested agro-dealers ensures the chemicals have been properly vetted and won't ruin your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni ji amalei loo nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ mla he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkpɛlɛ nɔ. Nifeemɔ kuu yibɔ loo nifeelɔ mlitsɔɔmɔ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ Hemɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ haa akwɛɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee onibii.

english: Is it safe to mix different crop medicines together in the same sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baafutu? afee ekome yɛ sprayer kome mli koni akɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing unapproved farm chemicals can cause bad reactions that make the medicines useless or burn your crops. Always check product labels or ask an expert before combining chemicals in one spray tank.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔji ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii gbohii aba ni baaha tsofa lɛ afee nɔ ni he ehiaaa loo eshã oŋmɔshi nibii. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be loo bi mɔ ko ni le nitsumɔ nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ tsofai awo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops like tomatoes need calcium, and how does it help them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato he hiaa calcium lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa?

english: Calcium strengthens plant cell walls, acting like bones for the crop. It prevents problems like fruit cracking and bottom rot on tomatoes, keeping the produce firm and healthy for market.
ga: Calcium wajeɔ tsei amli wala yibii lɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli wui. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ naagbai tamɔ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ tomato ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa jarayeli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the plant is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too wet or dry for the roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Plants rest and curl their leaves during extreme afternoon heat to reduce water loss. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will bounce back when the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ yaa wɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: What causes fruits on my farm to split open before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dani esa akɛ akpa?

english: Fruits split open when there is a sudden intake of heavy rain after a dry spell, or when the plant lacks calcium to make the skin flexible enough to expand.
ga: Yibii lɛ tswaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ calcium ni baaha hewolo lɛ afee mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my farm even after I spray chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ewo mihe moŋ.

english: Pests return if the wrong chemical is used, if spraying is done at the wrong time of day, or if neighboring farms carry pests that re-infest your clean crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii. Kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ onibii ni he tse lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a disease or just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii loo nu efo mli?

english: A thirsty crop wilts evenly across the field during dry heat, while a diseased crop shows isolated symptoms like spots, mold, rotting parts, or stunting on specific plants.
ga: Nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ hei ni egboi lɛ akpo. loo sɛɛkuu yɛ tsei komɛi amli

english: How can I get an agricultural officer to visit my farm and check my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha okwaayeli he nitsulɔi abasara miŋmɔ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You can request farm visits by contacting your district Department of Agriculture office, joining a local farmers' group, or reaching out through community agriculture platforms.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi ni ayasara bo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtsɔ okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ ni oootswa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ohe awo akutsoŋ okwaafoi akuu mli loo otswa kɛtsɔ akutsoŋ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it important to test my soil before buying fertilizers and chemicals for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ dani ohé ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Soil testing reveals exactly what nutrients your land is missing so you don't waste money buying unnecessary fertilizers or applying medicines that your crop does not need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo faŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa loo tsofai ni he ehiaaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade trees or quick-growing crops like plantains around them creates a natural umbrella that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves stay healthy and feed the growing ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha niyenii aha toi ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up my cassava so the tubers do not spoil?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ atsa ŋmei? Koni yitso lɛ akafite?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. Leaving them in the ground too long past maturity turns the tubers woody, hard, and lose their starchy quality.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe tseee.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry up the ground and kill young seedlings. Waiting until the major rainy season fully settles ensures the soil stays consistently wet enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii lɛ agboi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baaho lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center of the maize plant where it eats new leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the plant whorl controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli he ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii koni akɛkudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin without giving me many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are planted too close together, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight instead of growing wide branches. Leaving proper space between plants allows sunlight to reach the lower stem and encourages the plant to branch out and produce more flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaakpã mli koni ekɛ hulu la atswa akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ niji ni mli kwɔ lɛ eshwa. Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni ewo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛje niji amli ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani bei lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same nutrients out of the soil and lets maize-specific pests and diseases build up in the earth. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nitrogen to the soil and starves out crop pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hɔmɔ baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly even if I clear the weeds later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the water, light, and soil food during the crop's most critical early growth stage. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks gives your crops a strong start before weeds can stunt their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ akpa shweremɔ.

english: Why do I need to make high soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards underground and require loose, soft soil to expand without resistance. High soil mounds provide a deep, well-drained bed of soft soil that allows the yams to grow long, thick, and smooth while preventing root rot from trapped water.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛdaraa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt quickly. It keeps the plant roots cool, conserves soil moisture during hot days, and stops weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akajie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do I know which way to point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni matsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems will struggle to emerge properly, wasting the plant's energy and reducing root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seedlings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When pepper plants are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, air, water, and nutrients. This competition makes them grow tall and weak, producing fewer and smaller peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii fioo kɛ bibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up during bright sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to them provides shade and holds moisture until the young cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ adumɔ baaha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from environmental heat stress, insufficient soil moisture, or a lack of plant nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shihilɛ mli dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ bɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops look limp and wilted during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. This temporary water loss causes wilting, but the plant usually recovers by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni laajeɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ haa ŋmeii baa. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.
