english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize plants usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when roots stay flooded in trapped water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ bote nu mli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the soil of specific nutrients that maize needs to grow. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha abɛi lɛ adalɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are ragged holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaf funnel are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. The caterpillars hide inside the funnel during the day and feed on the soft, fresh leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ.

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal fertilizers and water from the soil before your crops can reach them. They also block sunlight from reaching crop leaves and can host harmful farm pests.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ tsei ahe baai ahe, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni ekɛyaa tuber lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: How do I tell if oil palm nuts are good quality before I plant them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ oil palm ŋmeii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good quality oil palm seeds (such as the recommended Tenera variety) come from certified suppliers, germinate uniformly, and produce fruits with a thick outer pulp and smaller inner nut, yielding much more oil than wild seed varieties.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ (tamɔ Tenera henɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ) jɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ adɛŋ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii bibii. Ehaa mu babaoo fe koo mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ.

english: How long does an oil palm tree take to start producing fruit bunches after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ko jeɔ yibii akui feemɔ shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Oil palm trees generally begin producing their first harvestable fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the main field, and they can continue yielding every year for up to 25 to 30 years with proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii afi fɛɛ afi kɛyashi afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce plenty of fruits in one season but very few in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ fioo yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm yields depend heavily on rainfall and soil nutrients. Extended dry periods or lack of fertilizer cause the tree to produce fewer female flowers, resulting in a lower fruit yield several months later.
ga: Mu tso ni anáa lɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii nɔ waa. Hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yei fioo. Enɛ haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: How often during the year can I expect to harvest fruit bunches from my mature palm trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa aduawai akui kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ mli?

english: Mature oil palm trees yield fruit bunches year-round, but harvesting usually peaks during the rainy season when moisture is plentiful and slows down during the main dry season.
ga: Mu tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni ebaa shi yɛ hulutsoo be titri lɛ mli.

english: How can growing maize on my farm help me feed my chickens?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni makwɛ kooloi?

english: Maize is rich in carbohydrates and serves as the primary energy source in poultry feed. Harvesting and drying your own maize allows you to crush it and mix it directly into chicken feed, reducing your overall feed costs.
ga: Carbohydrates babaoo yɛ ŋmãa mli, ni eji hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri yɛ kooloi aniyenii amli. Bo diɛŋtsɛ o-ŋmã ni okpaa ni ogbiɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛfutuɔ okɔɔŋtso niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi aniyenii he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy waterlogging around the roots, which prevents the plant from taking up essential nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What steps do I need to take to get a strong maize harvest every year?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maná ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ daa afi?

english: To ensure a reliable maize harvest every year, use improved certified seed varieties, plant right at the onset of the rains, apply fertilizer at the correct growth stages, and keep the field free of weeds during the first month.
ga: Enɛ haa anáa ŋmãa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ daa afi. Kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli ni atsake lɛ atsu nii. Dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni oha jwɛi akafee he ni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Can I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting maize on the same plot every year rapidly exhausts nitrogen from the soil and builds up crop-specific pests. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or peanuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my young tree seedlings dry up and die shortly after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often suffer from transplant shock due to root damage, high heat, or lack of water immediately after moving them to the field. Providing shade and mulching around the roots helps retain soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shishifãi ni efite, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli beni ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How does growing different crops like maize and palm trees on the same farm protect my business?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ abu mi nitsumɔ lɛ he?

english: Growing multiple crops spreads your risk; if poor rainfall or pest attack damages one crop like maize, the year-round yield from stable crops like oil palm ensures you still have income and food support.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ afee srɔtoi. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa hiɛ. Afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ tamɔ mu tso mli lɛ baaha ona shika kɛ niyenii yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do I need to put stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce leaves along their vines to catch sunlight. When you stake the vines off the ground, the leaves get maximum sunlight to make food, which feeds the roots and creates larger yam tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛmaa baai yɛ wain tso lɛ he koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Kɛji odu wain tso kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ naa hulu la fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa shishi.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers drop their lower leaves after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ shiɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ sɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ?

english: Transplanting disturbs the roots, making it temporarily hard for the plantain to absorb water. The plant sheds its lower leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself until new roots grow to support new leaf growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ gbaa shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu yɛ be kukuoo mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe he kɛyashi shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃ koni amɛye amɛbua baai heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is dry and the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that need water to dissolve safely. If applied to dry soil in heat, the fertilizer draws moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing root burn and wilting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni biɔ nu koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants stress, which damages the pollen inside the flowers. When pollination fails, the plant sheds the unproductive flowers to conserve its energy and moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rain saturates the soil, cutting off oxygen to the roots and allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ nu. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɛŋeɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my vegetable bed make my crops grow small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that fight directly with your crops for soil nutrients, ground water, and sunlight. When weeds surround your crops, they steal the vital food your plants need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ onibii lɛ wuɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli. Ebaaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack the dark center leaf funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miitutua mi-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant contains tender, juicy young leaves that are easy for young caterpillars to eat, while also offering a shady, hidden shelter from heat and predators.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli ewo nu ni ŋmeii bibii yeɔ oya lɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the same bed where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ saatso ni mifolɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Planting them continuously in the same soil allows pests and diseases from the previous harvest to attack the new crop immediately.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot easily germinate.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsĩ hulu la lɛ naa koni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in a wide open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and cannot handle direct heat from the hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa leaves and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK near the base of the plant will help restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How should I cut and position cassava stem cuttings in the ground so they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmei niji ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cut mature cassava stems into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with several visible buds. Plant them at an angle into raised mounds or ridges, ensuring the buds are pointing upward toward the sky so the stems grow correctly.
ga: Kpãa ŋmei momo lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni ŋmeii babaoo ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Dumɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛya gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central growing funnel of the maize. Applying appropriate recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme sun heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Mulching around the plants and keeping the soil consistently moist helps protect the flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching around Plants kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better to plant yam and cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu sweet potatoes kɛ cassava yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Raised mounds loosen the soil, allowing tuber crops to expand easily underground without hitting hard soil. Mounds also keep roots elevated so they do not rot in standing water after heavy rainstorms.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔji hu yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ yaa ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my seeds after the first rain arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Avoid planting immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is often still dry and warm. Wait for two or three steady rains to deeply soak the ground so your seeds have enough lasting moisture to germinate.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so much during their first month of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first four weeks, young crops are weak and easily overwhelmed by weeds competing for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Keeping your farm clean during this early period allows your crops to establish strong roots and grow faster.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse yɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛdara oya.

english: Which shoots should I take from an old plantain tree to plant a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ dumɔwu momo lɛ mli esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which are shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves and a large bulb at the base. They grow much faster, stronger, and yield heavier plantain bunches compared to shoots with broad, wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ bulb agbo ko yɛ shishigbɛ. Amɛ daa oya. much stronger Ni ewoɔ plantain ŋmeii ni tsii kwraa kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: When is the safest time of day to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, but ensure the plant leaves themselves are dry. If chemical fertilizer granules stick to wet leaves under hot sun, they can scorch and damage the foliage.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ baai lɛ agbi. Kɛji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ ahe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛha baai lɛ ashã ni amɛfite.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and refusing to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and tall. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer early gives the plant the energy it needs to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi yibii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Crops often drop flowers without making fruit when they are stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. When a plant feels thirsty or overheated, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu kumai he loo edɔ tsɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to give me a high yield before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo yibii babaoo dani madu nii?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and has earthworms inside. If the soil is pale, hard, or sandy, it lacks nutrients and needs compost or manure to support crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse, ewa, loo ŋã yɔɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aye abua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Will using a heavy tractor to plow my field harm the way my crops grow later?
ga: Ani trakta ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkpaa ŋmɔji lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard soil so crop roots can spread easily, but using heavy machinery on wet soil packs the ground too tight below the surface, making it difficult for roots to reach deep water later.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Shi tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaayashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even after leaving them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand into large tubers. If the dirt is packed too hard or lacks potassium, the plant cannot store energy underground and the roots will remain skinny.
ga: Kassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei wuji. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ato hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo lolo.

english: Can I grow two different crops on the same small piece of land without them killing each other?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ he bibioo ko. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nakai nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbeee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting complementary crops like legumes alongside tall crops works well because legumes naturally put food back into the soil, helping nearby crops grow better in a limited space.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛfataa he tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ niyenii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally built to survive on very little water and bad soil. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your planted crops have time to spread their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ nu fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ naa be ni ekɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetables dry up and die even when I water them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun causes water to dry up instantly before roots can drink it, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch them. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening allows roots time to soak up moisture.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu.

english: How does heavy rainfall change the way my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsakeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Moderate rain helps crops grow quickly by dissolving soil nutrients so roots can eat, but continuous heavy rain washes those nutrients away deep into the ground and rots roots by cutting off their air.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ aye amɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear old stems and dead plants away from my growing crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni egbɔ kɛ tsei ni egboi kɛjɛ mitsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaving rotting plant waste near healthy crops creates a damp home for insects and diseases that quickly jump onto your living crops and destroy them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei amli jwɛi ni egboi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai feɔ shĩa ni mli ewo fɔ. koni okɛ ohe awo oŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ anɔ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. This often happens when the soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash the nutrients away beyond the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: If I plant corn on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my harvest get smaller each time?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Corn pulls specific nutrients out of the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot wears out the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack corn to build up in that field.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni ehaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm alongside my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This acts like free fertilizer that feeds your corn and improves soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava stay alive during long dry spells while my other crops wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hi shi lɛ? Minɔ lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ?

english: Cassava has very deep root systems that reach underground moisture. During dry periods, it conserves water by dropping its upper leaves and resting until rain returns, making it very drought-resistant.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ebuɔ nu he kɛtsɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ nɔ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ. Ehaa enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa waa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that lose moisture quickly and burn under harsh sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the air humid while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe shwieɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni ebu kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why did my corn seeds rot underground after I planted them following the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by hot, dry days that dry out the topsoil. Without follow-up rain, the warm, damp soil suffocates the seeds, causing them to rot before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbi ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What is making holes in my corn leaves and leaving brown, sawdust-like powder in the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the growing top of the corn plant, chewing the soft leaves and leaving behind droppings that look like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ayiteŋ. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, too much water, or uneven soil moisture. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu babaoo, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local environment. Their roots spread fast and absorb water and nutrients quicker than crop seeds, giving them an advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui. ha sɛɛnamɔ ko

english: How can I keep tiny insects from eating and destroying my harvested corn while it is stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye ni mafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Insects need air and moisture to survive and multiply inside stored grain. Drying your corn thoroughly until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight bags will suffocate insects and keep your grain safe.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kooloi koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it. Planting plantains or cassava next to cocoa gives them temporary living shade, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Akɛni amɛbaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná la ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Does it matter which direction I push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots and roots grow in the wrong direction, causing weak growth and very small or zero cassava tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ Tsoi kɛ shishifãi baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. kɛ dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa yɛ loo eko kwraa bɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves catch enough light, the vine produces plenty of energy and stores it underground, resulting in larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Wein tsei lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, poor soil water, or a lack of insects like bees to move pollen within the flower so the fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli koni aduawai aba lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape, it means the soil lacks enough nitrogen food. The plant is taking stored food from its lower leaves to feed the growing corn cob at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛ V-su yɛ naagbee lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ ebaai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ akafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist, ideally after a light rain or early in the morning, and cover the fertilizer lightly with soil. Applying it on dry ground or right before heavy downpours will cause the rain to wash the food away from the crop roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. loo leebi maŋkpa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni ashiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the leaf funnel during the day to feed on soft tender leaves, leaving behind sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii pɛ eshwɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap beneath the leaf, or by a plant virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nibii lɛ amli

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot and turn soft when rain stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe in the soil just like humans need air. When heavy rain sits on the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant too many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, they fight with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important nutrient for plant growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the soil the boost it needs to turn the leaves green and help cobs grow fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that traps nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa yɛ oŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: What is causing my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and crowded farms. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ mli Efɔ tsɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ŋmɔmɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli.Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my tomato leaves, and will it stop my plants from producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ tomato baai anɔ Ni ani ebaatsi tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii loo ebaatsi amɛnaa?

english: Insects like caterpillars and beetles chew those holes to feed on the leaves. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot catch enough sunlight to make food, which reduces the number and size of tomatoes it can grow.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ nakai bu lɛ mli koni amɛye baai lɛ. Beni baai lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa tomatoi ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense, direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries them out. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a protective umbrella while they are young.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã ni amɛgbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he aba be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough space and nutrients to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: When is the right time to plant my cassava cuttings after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to plant cassava stems right after the rains become steady and the soil stays soft and wet. This allows the stem cuttings to sprout roots quickly before any short dry spells occur.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmei tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shishifãi shwereɔ oya dani hulutsoo be kuku ko baa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they face heat stress, dry soil, or lack specific nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil moist during hot weather and adding compost helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni amɛfee amɛhe.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves curl up and look like they are wilting during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. If the plant recovers by evening when temperatures drop, it is normal, but if it stays wilted, the crop needs extra watering.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi kɛji akɛ egbo lolo lɛ, Tsei hu he miihia ni aha amɛ nu kroko.

english: How can I tell that my yams are completely mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines on top of the soil begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally. This shows the plant has finished growing and stored all its energy in the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow heavy cobs, so applying fertilizer like NPK or urea helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the ground, naturally restoring fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool. Applying it in intense afternoon heat can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry earth around my crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil around crops with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds sprout and the heat returns, the hot dry soil will kill the tender seedlings before regular rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Hot, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread a virus, or by extreme heat. Controlling insects early helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mra Be mli Kooloi Ahe Nitsumɔ Yeɔ Ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli waa

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from irregular watering, intense heat stress, or a lack of nutrients in the soil needed for fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yams to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni ŋmeii akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food that makes the tubers underground grow big. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing rot and getting maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ afee agbo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking from root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can burn easily. Planting fast-growing plantains provides essential shade, lowers soil temperature, and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and produce food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base of the maize can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛwo niyenii Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ Corn cones lɛ ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess water. Pruning tree branches and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and dry out moisture faster.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni nu babaoo hu yɛ jɛmɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests build up in that field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my pepper plants before turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding over-spraying chemicals that kill bees helps fruit set properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ falɛ faaa Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛma shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if I am mixing the right amount of chemical pest spray in my knapsack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ miifutu misɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Using too little spray fails to kill pests, while using too much burns your crop leaves and wastes money. Always check the recommended dosage on the container label or measure with the standard measuring cap provided.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, egbeŋ kooloi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni efite shika. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni akɛha lɛ asusu he.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt during hot afternoons even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: During intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the dirt. Covering the exposed soil around the crops with dry leaves or straw helps retain ground moisture and cool the roots.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's maize harvest yield less than newly bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially bred for high yields, uniform growth, and protection against common regional pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni mi dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early prevents them from crowding out your crops during their critical growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo onibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop survive long dry spells better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and energy in its deep underground tubers and drops its upper leaves to conserve water during dry weather, whereas maize has shallow roots and loses water quickly.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ eŋwɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya.

english: Why should I clear and flatten my land properly before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mawo mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Flat, well-cleared land ensures that rain and farm water spread evenly across the soil so every crop gets equal moisture. It also prevents heavy rains from sweeping away topsoil and fertilizers.
ga: He ni ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ he ni ajie lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to my crop roots if I plant directly into hard, unbroken ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etseee nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Hard soil acts like a stone wall that stops tender young roots from pushing deep into the earth. When roots cannot spread out, the crop grows weak and starves quickly whenever there is a short drought.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ tɛ gbogbo ni tsiɔ shishifãi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ oya be fɛɛ be ni hɔmɔ ni heɔ be kukuoo ko baa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage making raised mounds or ridges instead of planting flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he hewalɛ moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges create soft, loose soil that lets roots breathe easily and helps root crops like yam, cassava, and sweet potato expand smoothly into big, healthy tubers.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ mlɛo. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes, cassava, kɛ yams ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: My plot stays waterlogged and muddy after rain; will crops like maize grow well there?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu kɛ muji beni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ. Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Most dryland crops like maize, pepper, and tomatoes choke and suffer from root rot if left standing in wet soil. Their roots need air to breathe just like human lungs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsei babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tomato, baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaaná shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Taakɛ adesa fɛ̃i ji lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛshishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu.

english: What crops are best suited for planting in swampy or low-lying land that holds water?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, sugarcane, and swamp-adapted vegetables thrive in wet, swampy soils because their root systems are naturally built to handle standing water without rotting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ ŋmei nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he nii ni amɛfiteee.

english: What simple step can I take if rain water collects in the middle of my farm plot?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ okwaayeli ŋmɔji ateŋ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mlɛo?

english: Digging simple drainage channels around your farm beds lets excess water run off smoothly, protecting crop roots from drowning while keeping the soil damp enough for growth.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ ahe lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa mlɛo. Buu tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛkabote nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my soil holds enough water to keep my crops alive during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil holds moisture like a wrung-out sponge when squeezed. If leaves wilt or roll up tightly by midday, it shows the soil lacks moisture and your crops are stressing for water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni jieɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gboi loo amɛbɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane teŋgbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu miihe nu.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are squeezed too tightly together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with very small fruits or yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa tsei waa tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa.

english: If I leave wider spaces between my crop plants, won't I end up harvesting less food?
ga: Kɛji migbala gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli Ani makpa niyenii fioo?

english: Not at all. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow stronger, absorb maximum soil nutrients, and yield bigger fruits, which often results in a heavier harvest than a crowded field.
ga: Jee nakai kraa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ yibii wuji baa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni tsii fe ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Does the direction I lay out my crop rows affect how my plants grow?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Laying out rows to follow sunlight and wind direction ensures every crop gets full light to make food and adequate airflow, which dries wet leaves quickly and stops diseases from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully grown underground without digging all of them up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the earth outward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together to try to fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete heavily for water and soil nutrients while their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in weak, slender plants and a poor yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers, but the flowers fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the daytime weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water during flowering, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo be mli ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ Kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by small sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, which feed on leaf sap and can transmit plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, maximizing sunlight capture and reducing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la nine shɛɔ nɔ babaoo ni oha baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ aba shi

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than my main crops when the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing their seeds to sprout instantly and take quick advantage of early rains and soil nutrients before domestic crops fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya dani shia tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why does the insect spray I buy stop killing the pests on my farm after I use it repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii ni mihe lɛ kpaɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbemɔ beni mikɛtsu nii shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Using the exact same chemical repeatedly allows the strongest insects to survive and reproduce, creating a new generation of pests resistant to that specific spray. Switching between different approved treatments prevents this.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Ehaa kooloi bibii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai heei ni nyɛɔ nakai tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Tsamɔi srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my orange trees produce plenty of sweet fruit one year, but almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ babaoo yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ewaaa akɛ ebaawo yibii kwraa?

english: Fruit trees like citrus can exhaust their stored energy and soil nutrients after producing a massive harvest, requiring a rest season to rebuild nutrients before they can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Yibii tsei tamɔ citrus baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmaa babaoo ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ biɔ hejɔɔmɔ be koni ekɛtswa niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani enyɛ ewo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that create protective shade and retain soil moisture while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and drying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from severe heat and water loss, or because tiny insects like whiteflies have spread a virus to the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli hewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to make healthy green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni wa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, causing them to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Tired soil shows signs like slow crop growth, pale yellow leaves, thin stems, and very small yields compared to previous harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ kpo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ yibii fioo ko pɛ ni anáa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and damaging the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni efite tso lɛ mli fã lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing center of maize plants and chews through new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ ni ekɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots by blocking air and allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. kɛ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa yitso lɛ

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans make the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil, providing free natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which produces the energy the plant needs to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire cocoa farm at once or plant new sections every year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo madu fã hee daa afi?

english: Planting your farm in stages every year spreads out your workload and costs. It also ensures you have trees at different ages, giving you a steady yearly income rather than waiting for all trees to mature at the same time.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni ooodu yɛ be kɛ bei amli Daa afi lɛ egbɛɔ onitsumɔ kɛ shika ni ofiteɔ lɛ eshwaa. Ehaa onáa tsei ni eye afii srɔtoi hu. Shika ni anáa daa afi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛhaa bo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tsei lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli lɛ,.

english: If I plant new cocoa seedlings near older trees, will the big trees prevent the young ones from growing?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ tsei momoi ahe Ani tsei wuji baatsi kookoo tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Older trees can block sunlight if trees are planted too close together. While young cocoa needs shade to survive, you must keep proper spacing—about 3 meters apart—so the young seedlings get enough light and nutrients to thrive.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la naa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi moŋ, shi Esa akɛ Okɛ amɛhe akabɔ bɔ ni sa. Ha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do some cocoa farms have crops of different heights and sizes across the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi duɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ amɛdalɛi srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Farms with mixed tree sizes usually practice phased planting, where the farmer plants new trees every year or replaces dead ones. This creates a continuous cycle of young, growing, and full-producing trees on one farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni tsei lɛ dalɛi efutu mli lɛ feɔ dumɔwui yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Okwaafoi lɛ baadu tsei heei daa afi loo amɛbaatsake tsei ni egboi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yaa nɔ amɛyaa nɔ amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ baa. ni miida ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli

english: How can I tell how old my cocoa trees are if I did not write down the date I planted them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afii abɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ eye? Kɛji miŋmaaa gbi ni adu lɛ

english: You can estimate a cocoa tree's age by its height, stem thickness, canopy width, and whether it has started flowering. Usually, cocoa trees start producing their first flowers and pods between 2 and 4 years of age.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu afii abɔ ni kookoo tso eye lɛ he kɛtsɔ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ nɔ. trunk thickness Canopy lɛlɛ ni okwɛ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shishi kɛji amɛye kɛjɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 4.

english: What changes should I expect to see in my cocoa trees during their first three years of growth?
ga: Mɛɛ tsakemɔi esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni ekɛbaadara lɛ mli?

english: In year one, cocoa trees focus on roots and soft green leaves. In year two, the stem hardens and branches out (forming a fork called a jorquette). By year three, trees grow thicker canopy leaves and begin forming their first flowers and pods.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ shishi wa ni niji jeɔ kpo. (Ebafeɔ fɔk ni atsɛɔ lɛ jorquette) yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baaná baai ni mli tse. ni ejeɔ shishi enáa klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi

english: Why is it important for me to know the exact age of the cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ male afii pɔtɛɛ ni kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eye lɛ?

english: Knowing tree age helps you give the right care at the right time. One-year-old trees need sun shade and weed protection, three-year-old trees need flowering support, and older trees require heavier pruning and pod disease management.
ga: Kɛ́ ole afii abɔ ni otso lɛ eye lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tso ni eye afi kome lɛ he miihia hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe. Tso ni eye afii 3 lɛ he miihia ni ewo fɔfɔi. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ waa kɛ pod helai ahe nitsumɔ.

english: At what age do cocoa trees produce the highest amount of cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ afii amli cacao tsei lɛ woɔ cacao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Cocoa trees usually reach their peak production between 10 and 20 years of age. Before 3 years they produce very little, and after 25 to 30 years, their pod production naturally starts to drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ lɛ he fe fɛɛ beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Dani afii 3 baashɛ lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, ni yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, amɛ pod ni amɛfeɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How should I care for a one-year-old cocoa tree compared to a three-year-old tree?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ kookoo tso ni eye afii 1 lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto kookoo tso ni eye afii 3 lɛ he?

english: A one-year-old cocoa tree needs temporary shade trees like plantains to protect its tender leaves from the hot sun. A three-year-old tree has stronger leaves and roots, so it needs more direct sunlight, regular weeding, and fertilizer to start bearing pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eye afi kome lɛ he miihia amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei ni eye afii etɛ lɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ ehe tɛ̃ɛ babaoo. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛje pods lɛ shishi

english: How can I know if my young cocoa trees are growing healthy or if something is wrong with them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ loo nɔ ko miigba amɛnaa?
