english: Healthy young cocoa trees frequently sprout bright reddish-brown or soft green new leaves and have strong stems. If the leaves turn yellow, dry up, or stop growing, the young tree may be getting too much sun, too little water, or lacks soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ baai heei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse kɛ tsei ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, loo amɛkpa dalɛ lɛ, ekolɛ hulu la babaoo eshɛ tso bibioo lɛ he. nine shɛ nu fioo tsɔ nɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: What should I do when my older cocoa trees stop producing good pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpa ŋmeii kpakpai feemɔ?

english: When old cocoa trees produce fewer pods, you can gradually cut them down and replant new seedlings in those spots, or use a method called side-grafting to grow fresh, high-yielding branches on the existing trunk.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Obaanyɛ Ofo amɛ fiofio ni odu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei lɛ. Aloo okɛ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ side grafting lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key food that helps plants grow green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the field and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are growing big tubers underground or just lots of leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji loo baai babaoo?

english: If your cassava stems are thick with many leaves but the soil around the base is not cracking or bulging after six months, the soil may have too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, causing the plant to put its energy into leaves instead of roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai babaoo, shi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ egbako loo ebɔleko ehe yɛ nyɔji 6 sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but drop them if the tree lacks water, if tiny insects like mirids damage the blossoms, or simply because the tree is saving energy for the few pods it can safely feed.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ miikwɛ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii fioo ni tso lɛ baanyɛ awo nɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ hewɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my yam seed pieces take so long to sprout after I plant them in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. They will only wake up and sprout when the soil reaches the right temperature and receives steady rain.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛbaate shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni sa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a sickness living in the soil that clogs the water pipes inside the stem. Once infected, water cannot travel up to the leaves, causing the plant to dry out quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ mli. Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ lɛ Nu nyɛŋ abote baai lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by whiteflies. Checking under the leaves early helps stop them from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji whiteflies vectors Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the ground. If seeds sprout during this dry period, the hot sun will dry out and kill the weak young roots before regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ shishifãi bibii dani nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the roots of my crops help them survive the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents rainwater from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and soft trunks that easily bend under heavy weight. As fruit bunches grow heavier, strong winds can pull the roots out of the ground unless you prop the tree up with sturdy wooden sticks.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ muji ni tsii shishi. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsiimɔ fa babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hu baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests even if I feed the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves; they quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them, leaving your plants weak and unable to form big fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi hiɛjoolɔi. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why should I consider growing my vegetables inside a greenhouse instead of in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu aduawai adumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse protects your crops from severe Ghanaian weather like intense scorching sun and torrential rainstorms, keeping temperatures steady so plants suffer less from stress and diseases.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe. ha hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi daa No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ naaa haomɔ kɛ helai babaoo.

english: How does heavy rain damage my vegetable crops, and can a simple farm shelter help?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ mi aduawai lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔ mli shĩa folo ko baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away topsoil nutrients, breaks delicate flowers, and spreads fungal diseases. A covered structure or greenhouse blocks heavy raindrops while still giving your plants sunlight.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni egbɔjɔ ni ekumɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsu ko ni aha nɔ loo ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ehaa hulu la haa otsei lɛ lolo.

english: Why do my plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ miha lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po?

english: Extreme heat forces plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water. Using shade structures or ventilated greenhouses keeps the air cool enough for plants to retain moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo ŋtayaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Does our hot weather in Ghana require a specific type of greenhouse design?
ga: Ani wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ biɔ ni afee ŋwɛitsu pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Yes, tropical heat requires taller greenhouse structures with wide side ventilation vents so that trapped hot air can escape, preventing your crops from heat stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, tropical dɔlɛ biɔ greenhouse tsu kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ esɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo. koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ anyɛ ajo foi Tsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli.

english: How does the height and size of a greenhouse structure affect crop growth inside it?
ga: Te ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa kɛ elɛɛmɔ saa tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The overall size determines airflow and heat management. Taller and wider structures hold more air volume, which prevents rapid temperature spikes and allows crops to grow without wilting.
ga: Dalɛ fɛɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo. Nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni elɛɛ lɛ hiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa ni amɛgbooo

english: Why is good air ventilation so important when growing plants under plastic roofs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ he hiaa beni aduɔ tsei yɛ plastic ŋtayaa shishi lɛ?

english: Without proper airflow, trapped heat and humidity build up quickly, causing crop leaves to rot and fungal diseases to spread fast among your plants.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i lɛ buaa amɛhe naa oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ otsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do I know if a greenhouse structure is strong enough to handle our local weather conditions?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ greenhouse tsɔne ko mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsu wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ he nii?

english: A well-designed greenhouse uses durable framing materials and proper roof angles tailored to resist local strong wind gusts and heavy seasonal downpours without collapsing.
ga: Greenhouse ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni enyɛ edamɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli lɛ naa ni ekuuu shi lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Which specific crops do best when grown inside a controlled farm structure?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni akudɔɔ mli?

english: High-value and delicate vegetables like tomatoes, sweet peppers, and cucumbers perform best because they are vulnerable to direct sun, excess rain, and heavy pest attacks in open fields.
ga: Aduawai ni jara wa, ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato, bell pepper, kɛ kukumba tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ oya. Nugbɔ miinɛ waa tsɔ. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Can building a net house or greenhouse help keep pests off my crops without heavy chemical spraying?
ga: Ani trellis shĩa loo greenhouse ni ama lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mikɛ tsofai ni tsii shwieee nɔ?

english: Yes, installing insect-proof mesh netting on the sides of a structure creates a physical barrier that stops damaging pests like whiteflies and thrips from reaching your vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ kooloi bibii ahe ŋshɔŋlooi wo otsu lɛ he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ thrips naa koni amɛkashɛ o-vegetables lɛ ahe.

english: Is it worth investing in a crop shelter if I only farm on a small scale?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ mikɛ mihe baawo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe mli kɛji akɛ mikwɛɔ he ko bibioo pɛ?

english: Yes, because a small, properly constructed shelter protects your yield year-round, allowing you to harvest high-quality crops off-season when market prices in Ghana are highest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ shĩa bibioo ko ni ama jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabu onibii ahe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni jara wa fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my new cocoa trees burning and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ nɔ lɛ shã ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves are very tender. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or banana next to them provides a natural umbrella that protects the cocoa from sun scorch while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa, tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ haa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-based fertilizer will help bring the green color and growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of building roots. Loosening the soil before planting and avoiding heavy chemical fertilizers encourages the plant to grow large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu nii, ni ajie tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil and takes away nutrients. Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the earth through their roots, which refreshes the soil for the next planting season without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: Abele haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii babaoo ni ejieɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii amli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa.

english: If I plant my tomato seeds very close together, will I get more harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and small fruits. Giving plants enough space allows fresh air to flow through and results in bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a long hot spell, which can dry up the soil and destroy your seeds before their roots grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe odumɔwui lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu.

english: How can I tell if armyworms are attacking my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji parasaiti miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Look inside the central funnel of the corn plant for ragged holes in the leaves and small sawdust-like droppings. If you spot these early, spraying organic neem leaf solution or recommended bio-pesticides can stop them before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni ona bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni shwieɔ shi. tamɔ ŋmei ni atsɛɔ lɛ sawdust lɛ Kɛji oyɔse nibii nɛɛ mra lɛ, Organic neem tso lɛ mli tsofa loo bio-insecticide ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the weather is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra branches from your cocoa trees lets sunshine and wind inside, which dries off the pods and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ duŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot dry weather, lack of water, or poor soil. Covering the ground around the plant with dry grass (mulching) helps keep the root area cool and moist so the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛtsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your main plants need. Clearing weeds early while they are still small ensures your crops get all the nourishment to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for green growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the younger growing leaves on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on dry soil when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve properly. Applying it to dry soil concentrates the chemicals, which can scorch or burn the crop's tender roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã loo eshã tsei ashishifãi bibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Excessive soil moisture starves the roots of air and allows harmful fungi to infect and destroy the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ helai ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my corn leaves and dark powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ powda ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of the corn plant and chew through young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to produce a good harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass on the ground around their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around plants is called mulching. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool under the hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade trees to protect them from extreme heat and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients like calcium in the soil.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up safely in that soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa shweshweeshwe yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops look weak and stunt their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa edalɛ miitsi enaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil food, and water away from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I leave space between my crops instead of planting as many as possible in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? Nɔ kome ni fe fɛɛ

english: When plants are crowded into a small space, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and light to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei bua amɛhe naa yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to small crops when they are growing under the shadow of larger plants?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Crops trapped under taller plants do not get enough direct sunlight to make their food. They become weak, grow slowly, and often produce smaller yields compared to plants in open space.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ náaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Amɛbɛ hewalɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni amɛfɔɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in neat rows rather than putting seeds wherever there is space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows creates orderly paths that let light and air reach every crop. It also makes it easier for you to walk through the farm to weed and tend to plants without damaging them.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ahe. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ofiteee amɛ.

english: Why is good air movement through my crop field important for my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ he ni mikwɛɔ lɛ he hiaa mi tsei lɛ?

english: Fresh air flowing between plants dries up excess rain and dew from leaves. Good ventilation prevents moisture build-up, which stops mold and fungal diseases from multiplying on your farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ jieɔ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbi lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops tend to rot quickly when the field becomes too crowded and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi tsɔ lɛ?

english: A tightly packed, bushy farm traps heat and dampness because wind cannot pass through. Fungi and bacteria thrive in wet, stagnant air, causing leaves and crops to rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. Mold kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I trim or prune off extra leaves and low-hanging branches from my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower foliage creates space for air to move freely around the base of the plant. It allows sunshine to reach the ground and keeps the plant dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ amɛhe. tso lɛ shishi lɛ heyeli Ehaa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How does proper spacing help protect my crops during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During rains, proper spacing allows wind and sun to dry off wet leaves rapidly. Without trapped dampness between plants, dangerous diseases cannot easily jump from plant to plant.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la agbi baai ni efɔ lɛ oya. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ Helai ni yɔɔ oshara nyɛŋ ajɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli mlɛo.

english: Why is keeping the farm clean and removing dead leaves important for my crop health?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni makwɛ koni ehe atse kɛ baai ni egboi ni mijieɔ lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ lɛ?

english: Good farm sanitation removes breeding grounds for pests and diseases. Clearing out dead plants and tight clutter reduces the moist places where dangerous insects and fungi hide.
ga: Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa jieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai fɔɔ yɛ lɛ kɛyaa. Tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens if I stack my harvested crops on top of each other in a small, tight storehouse?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔi lɛ to nitoohe bibioo ko ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli hu?

english: Piling produce tightly without space causes heat and humidity to build up inside the pile. Crops at the bottom get squished and heat up, causing the whole harvest to spoil and rot quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akudɔɔ ŋtayaai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni he ko bɛ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋtayaai lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni awoɔ mli la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya.

english: Why does taking care of tightly packed crops require so much extra time and physical labor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together without proper paths, workers cannot move easily and must spend hours bending down carefully to avoid stepping on crops, which slows down work and requires more workers.
ga: Kɛji tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo ni gbɛi kpakpai bɛ nɔ lɛ Nitsulɔi nyɛŋ aya he fɛɛ he mlɛo. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni akɛkotoɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni akanyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaabi nitsulɔi babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow and dry leaves on young cocoa often mean the plant is getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade, or it lacks essential nutrients in the soil like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or because there are no bees and insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo akɛni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. fɔfɔi ni feɔ pollen

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out thin and hard instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small and hard when the soil is packed too tightly for the tubers to expand, or when the ground lacks potassium, which helps the plant store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on to give good yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni ená ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sticks so their leaves can reach maximum sunshine. Sunbeams allow the leaves to make food, which is then sent down underground to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ niji koni amɛba lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow very fast at first but then suddenly stop growing before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara oya yɛ shishijee mli shi trukaa lɛ? Akpa shweremɔ dani akpa?

english: Crops often stall in growth because they have used up all the nutrients easily available in the top layer of soil and need extra fertilizer to keep building stems and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kpaa shweremɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing maize leaves need fertilizer or if they just need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmei baa ni ji yellow lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu kɛkɛ?

english: If maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the middle tip of the leaf, it lacks nitrogen fertilizer; if the leaves roll up tightly and wilt, the plant is thirsty for water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, je shishi kɛjɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ naagbee. tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen fertilizer bɛ Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle shi shiŋŋ ni egbo Kui ye tsei lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles eating the leaves to grow, which weakens the plant and prevents a tight head from forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ekɛ bulb lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever there is strong wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are not deep enough, which happens if the soil was plowed too shallowly or if pests have chewed through the underground root base.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii tsɔ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops even when my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Even small weeds beneath tall crops drink up water and steal fertilizers from deep underground, leaving less food and drink for your crop's roots.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ enuɔ nu ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nii ni anuɔ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after producing just one bundle of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo plantain kuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once; after fruiting, it dies so its energy can pass to the young suckers growing around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ́ amɛwo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, amɛgboiɔ bɔni afee ni hewalɛ aya ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my fruit tree if they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mitso lɛ mli kɛji amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Trimming some healthy branches, known as pruning, allows light and air to reach the inside of the tree. It forces the plant to send its food and water to the remaining branches so they can produce bigger and more plentiful fruits instead of just growing leaves.
ga: Ale tsei niji komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu amaje tsei niji ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni fa babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I leave old branches that no longer produce fruit on the tree?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi niji momo ni wooo yibii dɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Branches that do not bear fruit still steal water and soil nutrients away from the rest of the tree. Removing these unproductive branches frees up valuable food for the healthy parts of the plant to produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛjuɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ. Niji ni wooo yibii nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni jara wa jeɔ kpo kɛhaa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why does trimming a branch that already has fruit on it help me get a better harvest later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii momo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: If a branch carries too many small fruits, the tree becomes weak trying to feed them all, resulting in small or poor-quality crop yields. Trimming back fruiting branches helps the tree focus its strength on developing fewer, much larger, and healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛji nine kome yɛ aduawai bibii babaoo tsɔ Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha amɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi loo nɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi. Niji ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni afoɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii fioo, ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some branches on my cocoa tree dry up and stop bearing fruit while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ niji komɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Branches stop fruiting when they do not get enough sunlight, suffer pest attack, or become old and weak. When a branch stops contributing food to the plant, the tree slowly cuts off nutrients to it, causing it to dry out.
ga: Niji kpaɔ yibiiwoo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ loo egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ Beni tsei niji lɛ kpa niyenii ni amɛhaa tso lɛ Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiofio, ni no baaha egbi.

english: Why are the fruits on my mango tree smaller this year even though the tree has grown much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa afi nɛɛ? Nɛgbɛ mango tso lɛ kwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ?

english: As a tree grows larger without being cut back, it creates too many branches competing for the same amount of food in the soil. Because the nutrients are spread thin across many branches, the individual fruits end up smaller.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da ni afolɔko lɛ Ebɔɔ niji babaoo tsɔ ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii ni falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlijaa bibioo yɛ tsei niji babaoo amli. No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my fruit trees need direct sunlight inside their branch canopy to produce well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Leaves use sunlight to manufacture the food that grows flowers and fruits. If the outer branches are too thick and shade the inner parts of the tree, those inner branches will not get enough light to produce any fruit.
ga: Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ niyenii ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ niji lɛ mli tse tsɔ ni amɛha tso lɛ mligbɛ hei lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ, Nakai mligbɛ niji lɛ naaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my mature tree crop still need regular clearing and care even when it is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso ni eda lɛ he hiaa ni ajie lɛ daa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni edara kwraa po lɛ?

english: Even fully grown trees constantly compete with weeds and pests for soil food and water. Regular farm maintenance ensures that all available nutrients go directly into fruit production rather than feeding weeds or disease.
ga: Tsei ni eda po kɛ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miitswa akaŋ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa aduawai afeemɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha jwɛi loo hela niyenii

english: How does removing dead or infected branches prevent my whole farm from getting ruined?
ga: Te aniji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ akafite lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Dead and sick branches attract insects and plant diseases like black pod or fungi. Cutting them off early removes the source of infection before it can spread to healthy trees across your farm.
ga: Niji ni egboi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii. Ofolɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ejie he ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can an old fruit tree that has stopped producing well start bearing again if I cut it back hard?
ga: Ani tso ni egbɔ ni ekpa yibiiwoo lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji wɔfo lɛ waa?

english: Yes, heavy pruning on old trees can wake them up by encouraging fresh, young shoots to grow. Once the tired old wood is removed, the root system pushes stored energy into these new shoots, which can start producing fruit again.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei momoi ni afoɔ. Heavy baanyɛ ateshi tso lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ewoɔ amɛmli lɛ adalɛ nɔ kɛji ajie tso ni egbɔ ni etɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛyaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii heei nɛɛ amli. ni baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do some tree crops take several years before they give their first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops spend their first few years building strong underground roots and a sturdy trunk. Only after the tree has established a solid base can it store enough extra energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Beni tso lɛ etswa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ kroko ni fa bɔ ni sa ato koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my rice plants need to sit in standing water during their early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ata nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ amɛmra be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet soil, and keeping a layer of water in the field smothers weeds that compete for light and food while giving young rice roots the continuous moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ni nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ nuɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do some improved rice seeds mature much faster than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ oya fe mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Improved rice varieties are specifically bred by scientists to grow quickly and produce grain within a shorter rainy season, helping you harvest before dry weather sets in.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests each year even when I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant every season without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and depleted of those nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu nii daa be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni nakai niyenii lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that excessive water or drought is stopping the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo amɛkɛɛ akɛ nu babaoo loo hɔmɔ haaa shishifãi lɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I space out my cassava cuttings instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ abɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Giving cassava plants proper spacing ensures their underground roots have enough room to expand into large tubers without fighting neighboring plants for sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture.
ga: Cassava tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ hulu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ awuu

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden stress, causing the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛ yashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔnyɛɛ trukaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: How do I know the ground has enough moisture for sowing seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the top part of the soil is wet deep down to your hand's depth after two or three steady rains, ensuring seeds won't dry up if the rain pauses for a few days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ onine he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my field than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water and food faster than crop seeds until you clear them away.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaajie amɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects attack my stored grains even when I keep them inside a covered barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni aha nɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Insects thrive in grains that still hold moisture from the field; drying your crop thoroughly under the sun before storing it removes the dampness insects need to survive and multiply.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lolo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa yɛ hulu shishi dani okɛto lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kooloi koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii lɛ.

english: Why do buyers at the market pay less for my rice when it contains broken grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni ekumɔ lɛ?

english: Broken rice grains cook unevenly and spoil faster during long storage, so market buyers pay higher prices for whole, unbroken grains that look clean and attractive to consumers.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa ni ekumɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa ni eye emuu ni akumɔko mli ni tamɔ nɔ ni he tse ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ lɛ jara babaoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves scorch and dry up after I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Big trees protect young crops from extreme direct sunlight and keep moisture in the soil. When too much land is cleared at once, fragile crops get sunburned and the soil dries out faster than the roots can drink.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ ajie he ko babaoo shikome lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baaná hulutsoo. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me not to burn the bush after clearing my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkashã kooi beni amɛjie okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms that feed your plants. Leaving cleared weeds to decay naturally creates mulch, which keeps soil cool, holds water, and acts as free fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without bearing good cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ ŋmei fɛfɛo ko beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its stalk to grow thick and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive feeders that steal plant food and water from the soil before your main crop can reach it. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji niyenii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii titrii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will turn the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When mixed with maize, they naturally feed the soil and fertilize surrounding crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa futu mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant's leaves during the day to feed on young tissue. Checking leaves early and applying targeted treatments stops them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe tee tso lɛ baai amli yɛ gbi mli koni eye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from tiny sap-sucking insects. Watering regularly and providing light cover keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ kane ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mikpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots are underground food stores for the plant. If left in the soil too long, the plant uses up the starch in the tubers to stay alive, making the roots fibrous and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii shwapo kɛha tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tsei kɛ starch ni yɔɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ewaa akɛ amɛhooɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain accumulates in poorly drained soil or when small soil insects wound the tuber, letting fungus enter. Building well-drained mounds helps protect the roots from decaying.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua yitso lɛ. ni ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii aboteɔ mli Gɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni abu shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight over food and water in the soil. Pruning away the weaker shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which makes the main plant produce bigger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are there small holes and worm droppings inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni vermikɔmpost?

english: This damage is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm. The worms hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant during the day and chew through tender leaves, which creates holes as the leaves unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yitsei amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. kɛ baai bibii ni ayeɔ Enɛ haa buji baa kɛji baai lɛ gbele amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juices during dry conditions, causing the leaf to twist and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up when the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that enters the plant's roots and blocks water from traveling up the stem, making the top of the plant dry out quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho kɛya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ yiteŋ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but give me tiny tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, ani mikɛ ŋmeii bibii haa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems up top instead of storing food in roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my land grow better maize next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, working like free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where pests live and spreads them out toward the sun.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds eat from the same plate as your crops. They steal the fertilizer and soil nutrients that your crops need to stay green and strong, leaving your plants hungry.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry season often tricks farmers because the ground is still very hot underneath. If another rain doesn't fall immediately, the hot dry soil will scorch and ruin the germinating seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli edɔ waa lolo. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ baashã ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I get a higher yield from my yellow maize crop so I have plenty of grain to process into farm feed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mi-yellow corn lɛ mli bɔni afee ni maná ŋmaa babaoo ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛfee kooloi aniyenii?

english: To get higher maize yields, plant certified seeds at proper spacing (about 75 cm between rows and 25 cm between plants), apply fertilizer when plants are knee-high, and keep the farm free of weeds during the first four weeks of growth.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná ŋmãa yibii babaoo Dumɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli (aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ 25 cm yɛ tsei ateŋ). Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛkuɛ he lɛ. ni eha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest for processing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa koni akɛtsu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. Harvesting at this stage ensures the roots have maximum starch content and low water content, making them ideal for drying and milling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa starch babaoo ni nu hu faaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize and sorghum grains develop mold and spoil quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa oya ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain mold develops when crops are stored before they are fully dry. Grains must be sun-dried until they crack cleanly when bitten (around 12% moisture content) before being stored in airtight bags or dry cribs to prevent spoilage and toxins.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛgbi kwraa. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaakumɔ kwraa kɛji akɛ emɔ lɛ. (Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aaafee 12%) dani akɛto vacuum bags loo cribs ni egbi mli koni akafite kɛ tsofai fɔji.

english: Why does planting soybeans or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybeans loo cowpeas ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soybeans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in root nodules. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, this natural plant nutrient remains in the soil to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Soybeans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso mli niyenii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip and spreading along the center stem indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it fine to plant cassava and maize together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows slower and expands after the maize is cleared, allowing you to maximize yields from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is eating the fresh young leaves inside the central funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi akɛ ayeɔ baai bibii heei yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant's funnel to feed on young leaves. Applying recommended insecticides or neem extract directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo kooloi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop plants roll up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use during hot weather to reduce water loss through their leaves, helping the plant conserve moisture until temperatures drop.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ aba shi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately with the first rain. Clearing weeds early within the first month gives your crops a fair chance to establish strong roots without competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: How can I safely process cassava peels after harvest so they do not harm my farm animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu ŋmei ŋmɔji lɛ ahe nii shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Koni ekaye miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ awui.

english: Raw cassava peels contain natural cyanide compounds that are harmful. Washing, fermenting, squeezing out the water, and sun-drying the peels thoroughly removes these toxins, making the dried product safe to mix into feed.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ cassava hewolo mli. Kɛ́ afɔ he jogbaŋŋ, afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ajie nu lɛ kɛjɛ mli, ni agbi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ nɔ ni egbi lɛ futuɔ kooloi aniyenii mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How many cobs of maize can I realistically expect to harvest from a single plant?
ga: Abele ŋmeii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ tso kome mli?

english: A healthy maize plant typically produces 1 to 2 fully formed cobs. Under good soil fertility, sufficient rainfall, and proper weed control, the plant has enough nutrients to fill out both cobs completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo ŋmãa 1 kɛyashi 2 ni efee jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ shishi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ awo mli kwraa.

english: Why do some cocoa trees in my farm have over thirty pods while others nearby have less than ten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nyɔŋmai etɛ lɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Ashɛɛɛ pods nyɔŋma ni bɛŋkɛ?

english: Yield per tree varies depending on soil nutrients, sunlight exposure, tree age, and pest management. Trees in richer soil with good shade management produce more flowers and sustain more pods to maturity.
ga: Yibiiwoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, hulu la, tso lɛ afii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How many healthy cassava tubers should I expect from a single stem planting?
ga: Cassava ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli?

english: A single healthy cassava stem normally yields between 4 to 8 good tubers. The exact number depends on how loose and rich the soil is for tuber expansion, as well as rainfall during early root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmei kpakpai ni fa fe 4 kɛyashi 8. Yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni fata he ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shishijee bei ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does weather condition affect the number of mature seeds inside crop pods?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi saa dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat or dry weather during flowering causes plant stress, leading to poor pollination. This results in pods that are either stunted or contain far fewer fully developed seeds.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ tso lɛ haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pollination ni ehiii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ loo dumɔwui ni eda kwraa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why are my vegetable plants shedding their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping usually happens when plants face sudden water stress, extreme heat, or a shortage of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen needed to nourish young fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni akɛha aduawai bibii lɛ niyenii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes some fruits on the same tree grow very large while others stay small and flat?
ga: Mɛni haa yibii komɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ daraa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Trees prioritize nutrients to branches that receive the most direct sunlight and water. Fruits growing on weaker or shaded branches receive fewer resources and remain smaller.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛhaa tsei niji ni hulu la kɛ nu shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Yibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ naaa nibii fioo komɛi ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: How can I estimate my overall harvest quantity before actual harvesting day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ he akɔntaa dani ŋmaa lɛ gbi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba?

english: You can estimate yield by counting the average number of mature pods or cobs on a few sample plants across different areas of your field and multiplying that by your total plant count.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni edara ni yɔɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ enɛ abɔ otsei lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ he.

english: Why does a buyer pay less money for some bags of harvested crops than for others from the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmaa kotokui komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ fioo fe mɛi krokomɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Buyers assess crop condition, including seed size, dryness, insect damage, and fullness. Bags containing fully developed, undamaged seeds attract higher market prices.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ, egbi, koolooi fitemɔ, kɛ dalɛ fata he. Baagi ni dumɔwui ni edara kwraa ni efiteee lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbala jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a bigger total yield at harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo kɛji akpa?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This usually results in many weak plants with low-quality yields rather than a larger total harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibii ni ehiii baa moŋ fe ŋmaa fɛɛ ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my pepper pods look fully grown on the outside but feel light and empty inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper pods lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edara kwraa kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi ani onuɔ he akɛ oyɛ mlɛo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: Empty or light pepper pods happen when there is incomplete pollination or low soil calcium, preventing the inner seeds and seed walls from fully forming.
ga: Pepper pods ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ eshɛɛɛ he loo calcium faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui gbogboi lɛ efeee kwraa.

english: Is our traditional local rice good for my family's health?
ga: Ani wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ hi kɛha miweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, local rice is very nutritious, making it a healthy choice for your household, even though it behaves differently in the field compared to newer varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa. Ha efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oshiabii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ efeɔ enii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto henɔ hee lɛ he moŋ.

english: Why do farmers avoid planting local rice even though it is nutritious?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ? No yɛ niyenii kpakpa mli sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Even though local rice is full of nutrition, its long cultivation cycle means it stays in the soil for too long, leading many farmers to stop planting it.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii kpakpai moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe bahia ni okwaafoi babaoo akpa nidumɔ.

english: Why are farmers in my community choosing not to plant local rice anymore?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ halaa akɛ amɛduuu ŋmãa yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Farmers are moving away from local rice mainly because it takes a long time to complete its cultivation cycle from planting to harvest.
ga: Okwaafoi miitsi amɛhe kɛmiijɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he ejaakɛ eheɔ be babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli.

english: How does the long growing time of local rice affect my farm operations?
ga: Te maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni miduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A long cultivation cycle means your land is tied up for a extended period before harvest, which is why many farmers prefer faster-growing alternatives.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akpɛtɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ dani akpaa. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaafoi babaoo sumɔɔ gbɛi krokomɛi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why is perfume rice becoming so popular among buyers and farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: Perfume rice is popular because it grows bigger than local rice varieties and is highly demanded by consumers in the market.
ga: Mɛi sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa ejaakɛ eda fe ŋmãa srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ waa.

english: Does perfume rice actually grow bigger than our traditional local rice?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ agbo fe wɔmaŋ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, perfume rice has the growth ability to develop bigger than traditional local rice varieties.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni da fe ŋmãa srɔtoi krokomɛi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Which rice variety should I choose if I want my crop to grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi esa akɛ mahala kɛji miisumɔ ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: You should consider planting perfume rice, as it naturally grows bigger than local traditional rice.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ dumɔ he ejaakɛ eyɛ adebɔɔ mli akɛ eda fe ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why did my recent plot of local rice produce a small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Local rice varieties often yield smaller harvests compared to popular varieties like perfume rice.
ga: Kuu mli ŋmãa fɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it normal to get a small harvest when planting traditional local rice?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ aaaná yibii fioo ko kɛ́ adu maŋ lɛ mli kusum mli ŋmãa?

english: Yes, traditional local rice crops typically result in a smaller harvest size compared to larger-growing varieties like perfume rice.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa bibioo baa. Kɛ akɛto ŋmãa henɔi wuji tamɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ he

english: How does perfume rice compare to local rice in terms of plant growth?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa yeɔ egbɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ tsei adalɛ he?

english: Perfume rice is able to grow bigger than local rice, making it a popular choice for farmers looking for better crop development.
ga: Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ adara fe maŋ lɛ mli omɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni okwaafoi ni miitao ni amɛdu nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ halaa waa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are sick before they start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani amɛgboi?

english: You can look for early signs like yellowing or swollen shoots, dark brown patches on the pods, or leaves that grow in strange, distorted shapes. Spotting these symptoms early helps you stop diseases from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao mra be mli okadii tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni efuu. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. loo baai ni hiɛ sui ni etsake ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Okadi okadii nɛɛ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni otsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Regularly removing infected pods and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must a whole cocoa tree be cut down if only a few branches look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Certain serious illnesses, like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, live inside the tree's internal sap system. Even if only a few branches show symptoms, the virus is already throughout the roots and trunk, so cutting the tree completely is the only way to protect nearby healthy trees.
ga: Helai komɛi ni naa wa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ jieɔ hela lɛ he okadii akpo po. Shi hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ amli momo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my new young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist while they grow.
