ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei bibii ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ lɛ.

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for water, soil food, and sunlight. This overcrowding also traps humidity, making it much easier for crop diseases to spread from tree to tree.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ tsei ahe helai baajɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Can I just pick seeds from my harvested cocoa pods to plant a new field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli koni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: It is best to get certified pods or seedlings from approved Cocoa Board nurseries. Seeds saved from regular harvests often produce weaker trees that yield fewer pods and are more easily affected by diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona pods loo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli kɛjɛ Cocoa Board lɛ ŋmɔ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli daa lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni helai yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why is it important to trim or prune the extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ loo afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach the lower branches. This dries out extra moisture that causes mold and helps the tree direct its strength into growing bigger pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji lɛ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: Is burning my farmland the best way to clear weeds before I plant new crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashãa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli dani aduɔ tsei heei?

english: While burning is quick, it destroys valuable soil nutrients and kills helpful earthworms that keep the soil rich. Clearing weeds by hand or leaving cut weeds to rot back into the soil creates a healthier environment for your crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa oya moŋ Shi efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Who am I supposed to talk to if I think there is a dangerous disease on my farm?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mikɛ lɛ agba sane kɛji misusu akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should contact your local agricultural extension officer or a representative from the Ghana Cocoa Board. They can inspect your farm in person, confirm what is wrong, and help you get the official support needed to manage it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ loo Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko abɔ. Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ma nɔ mi akɛ nɔ ko ejaaa. ni eye ebua bo ni oná yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa bo ni okɛkwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients from the soil, such as nitrogen, or that pests are attacking the roots beneath the ground, preventing the crop from absorbing food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: How can I keep my farmland strong so that it does not lose its fertility after every harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can maintain your soil's strength by rotating your crops, applying animal manure or compost, and leaving crop residues on the field to decay into organic matter instead of burning them.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji afata he. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni egbo akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ashãa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam mounds break down and wash away so easily when heavy rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato pile lɛ fiteɔ ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose topsoil when there are no roots or plant covers to bind the earth together. Mulching your mounds with dry grass or leaves creates a protective shield that holds the soil structure in place.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ he beni shishifãi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome lɛ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for growing maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, naturally enriching the soil strength for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nodes bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that excess water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ ehe. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaye niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ shã amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing upper stems and leaves instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifã kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when the plant suffers from extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling inward and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Is there any advantage to doing my transplanting early in the morning rather than during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he leebi maŋkpa moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Transplanting early in the morning prevents young seedlings from losing too much water through their leaves, allowing their roots to settle safely into the cool soil before heat stress sets in.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo akaje tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ shweshweeshwe dani dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds around my crops when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the land's strength without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ amɛ awuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is my maize turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to grow tall and produce large cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans helps my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize feeds on this stored natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ato nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, healthy leaves but very thin roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni mli wa lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi?

english: When crops are planted too close together or get too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its food making stem and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build thick cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen fa tsɔ Tsei kɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee ŋmei shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot temperatures, dry soil, or too much water. The plant discards the flowers to survive the stress rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi yɛ haomɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots from my tomato plants when they are growing so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ be mli ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Removing small side branches forces the tomato plant to send its water and soil nutrients directly into growing larger, healthier fruit instead of spreading energy across too many leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji bibii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ hewalɛ babaoo eshwa baa lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense sunlight or dry conditions alone. Plantains or shade trees planted nearby shield young cocoa from direct sun and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ pɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa shade ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hide inside the leaf funnel and feed on the soft plant tissue before the leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli dani baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt during the afternoon heat even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: In hot weather, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Soil with low organic matter loses moisture quickly, so adding compost helps soil hold onto rainwater longer.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does leaving weeds in my field lower the amount of food my crop produces?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act as thieves in the farm—their roots drink the soil water and steal fertilizer away from your crops, leaving your crop weak, small, and unable to give a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibioo, amɛbaafee bibii, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest give a smaller yield than certified seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni shwapoi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strong traits in the next generation, resulting in uneven plant growth. Certified seeds are specially bred to give high yields and resist local pests and diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛha yibii babaoo aba ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋbii helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to survive the intense heat. Without protection from direct sunlight, the leaves burn, dry out, and fall off because the young root system cannot draw enough water to cool the plant.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ abuuu he kɛjɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaagbee shi ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in high humidity and moisture. During heavy rains, fungal spores from the soil or infected pods splash onto healthy pods and spread rapidly if shade is too dense or ventilation is poor.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Fungal spores ni jɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural protective response to severe heat and drought. By rolling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and traps moisture inside to keep from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ. kɛtsɔ shwiemɔ nɔ Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes in the leaves and center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a major pest in West Africa. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars feed heavily on the growing shoot and tender leaves, which can stunt or destroy the crop if untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ Afrika Anaigbɛ lɛ. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida kɛ baai bibii waa. Enɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii akpo loo efite kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling into thick tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if planted in overly compacted or hard soil where roots cannot easily expand, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium. Poor soil preparation and harvesting too early also prevent tubers from filling out.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. ni eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ bulbs lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant, which is then transported underground to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la babaoo aba tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboi dani efee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by inconsistent watering. When water levels fluctuate violently, the plant cannot transport calcium properly to the bottom of the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ nu lɛ mli shwereɔ waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall with lots of green leaves, but produce very few flowers and peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil. High nitrogen encourages bushy leaf and stem growth, but discourages the plant from producing the flowers needed to grow peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji. Shi enɛ baaha tso lɛ akawo fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only two or three strong shoots, directing energy into growing larger bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa hewalɛ yaa plantains wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that have natural bacteria in their roots capable of taking nitrogen gas from the air and changing it into a form plants can use. When they grow, they naturally fertilize the soil for future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli helai ni baa mɔ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsake lɛ efee nɔ ko ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why does a fruit tree I planted from a sweet market mango end up giving bitter or bad fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tsei ni mikɛ jarayeli mango ni ŋɔɔ lɛ du lɛ woɔ aduawai ni mli edɔ loo ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Seeds carry mixed traits from both parent flowers, so a seed taken from a sweet fruit will not always grow into a tree with the same sweet fruit. To get the exact same taste and quality, farmers use grafted seedlings instead of planting seeds directly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ji fɔlɔi fɔfɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛfutu. No hewɔ lɛ, jeee be fɛɛ be dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso ni hiɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni aná ŋmɔlɔ kɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ Okwaafoi kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaadu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of the fruit trees on my farm grow very tall but never produce any fruits at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: A tree might not bear fruit because it was grown from a poor-quality seed, lacks essential soil nutrients, or suffers from internal diseases. Buying certified seedlings ensures the tree is bred specifically for high fruit production.
ga: Ekolɛ tso lɛ wooo yibii ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii kwraa jɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hela ko ni yɔɔ emli lɛ yeɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ akwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do fruit trees that grow naturally by the roadside sometimes look healthier than the ones I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, aduawai tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe nɔ ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild roadside trees only survive if they happen to land in a spot with ideal conditions and have strong naturally selected genes. However, their fruit yield is unpredictable, whereas planted crops need proper spacing, nutrients, and protection to give consistent yields.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ he tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi pɛ kɛji eba akɛ amɛba shi yɛ he ko ni shihilɛ ni sa kɛ adebɔɔ mli halamɔ mli wala yibii ni mli wa yɔɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ yibii amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná he ko ni sa, niyenii, kɛ hebuu koni amɛwo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: How can I tell if my tree is not bearing fruit because of a disease or because of poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ ni mitso lɛ wooo yibii lɛ?

english: Diseased trees usually show visible signs like yellowing or spotted leaves, dying branches, or sticky sap coming from the trunk. If the tree looks green and leafy but still brings no fruit, the problem is likely poor seed quality or a lack of specific nutrients that trigger flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ. nine ni miigbo loo latex ni shwieɔ shi ni miijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo yibii lolo. Ekolɛ naagba lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni woɔ fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do some planted fruit trees catch sickness easily while wild trees seem to survive on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni woɔ yibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Many planted crop varieties are bred to focus their energy on producing large, sweet fruits rather than fighting off pests. Because of this, they require regular monitoring and care, unlike wild trees which naturally prioritize survival over high fruit quality.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akwɛɔ koni akɛjwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ ni anáa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawu amɛshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛnɔ daa. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ mli wala ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he hiaa fe aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What causes a fruit tree seedling to grow into a diseased plant even when I care for the soil properly?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai tsei amli dumɔwui daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: The seedling itself may have been infected while still at the nursery or inherited a disease from the parent plant. Starting with clean, disease-certified seedlings from trusted agricultural officers prevents you from spending years taking care of an infected tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ aná hela be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo amɛŋɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Je shishi kɛ dumɔwui ni he tse, ni hela yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Ebaatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ afii babaoo akakwɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it a good idea to collect seeds from a good wild tree by the road to start my new farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ abaabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ koo mli tsei kpakpai amli? Yɛ gbɛ lɛ naa koni mije miŋmɔ hee lɛ shishi.

english: It is risky because wild seeds do not reliably copy the good traits of the parent tree. You might wait several years only to find the new tree yields poor fruit or no fruit at all, wasting your time and land.
ga: Oshara ko yɛ ejaakɛ koo mli dumɔwui nyɛŋ afee sui kpakpai ni yɔɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ he mfoniri yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ omɛ afii babaoo dani ona akɛ tso hee ko wooo yibii kpakpai loo ewooo eko kwraa. Ehaa ofiteɔ be kɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: How can I be sure that the fruit tree seedlings I buy will actually produce the fruits I want?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai ni miheɔ lɛ baawo aduawai ni misumɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can ensure good results by purchasing grafted seedlings from certified nurseries. Grafting takes a branch from a proven, high-producing tree and attaches it to a strong root base, guaranteeing the exact fruit quality you expect.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ni hi baajɛ mli aba kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ ji tso ko ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ niji ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishitoo ni wa he. Koni oná nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ji nɔ ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do two trees planted side by side on my farm perform differently, with one fruiting and the other remaining barren?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei enyɔ ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ lɛ? He ni tso kome woɔ yibii ni tso ni eshwɛ lɛ hu wooo yibii lɛ?

english: Even trees planted together can differ if they came from different seeds with different genetic traits, or if one tree's root system was damaged or attacked by underground pests and diseases.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he kome po baanyɛ afee srɔtoi kɛji amɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi amli ni amɛyɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. aloo kɛji akɛ tso kome shishifãi lɛ efite loo shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai etutua lɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce plenty of green leaves every year but fails to bring out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ baa eŋɔli babaoo daa afi shi ebɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage with no flowers often happens when a tree gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or water, causing it to focus only on leaf growth. It can also be caused by using uncertified seed varieties that have weak flowering genetics.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo nɔ. Ha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ pɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni bɛ odaseyeli ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ahe nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu aba.

english: How do I choose the best seed stock to buy for the upcoming planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mahe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Look for certified seeds from recognized extension officers or dealers that match your region's rainfall pattern. Certified improved seeds usually offer higher yields and better resistance to local diseases compared to saved grain from previous harvests.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ extension agent loo jalɔ ni ale lɛ ni kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from my current corn harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted local open-pollinated seeds, you can save the healthiest seeds for next season. However, if you planted hybrid seeds, the crop grown from saved seeds will be weak and produce much lower yield, so fresh certified seeds should be bought.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ato koni okɛtsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ, Tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli.

english: How do I know when my maize crops have moved from the vegetative growing stage to the flowering stage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-abɛi lɛ eshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ mli kɛtee fɔfɔii agbɛfaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize enters the flowering stage when the tassels appear at the very top of the plant and soft silks emerge from the young cob ears. At this stage, the plant stops growing taller and shifts all its energy toward producing grains.
ga: Abele boteɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli beni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ atoi lɛ amli lɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ mli kɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply fertilizer at the wrong growth stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa akɛ amɛdaraa lɛ mli?

english: Applying fertilizer too early when roots are small causes nutrients to wash away in the rain, while applying it too late means the plant misses the crucial growth surge needed to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ beni shishifãi lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akaná dalɛ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii loo ŋmaa wuji lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. If the leaves uncurl once the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they remain curled overnight, it signals water stress or pest damage.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ Etsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lush green leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: This happens when soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend all its energy growing foliage above ground. To grow big roots, cassava needs soil rich in potassium rather than excess nitrogen.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Cassava moŋ fe nitrogen ni fa fe nine.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cowpea plants before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ dani pods baa lɛ?

english: Flower shedding is usually caused by small insect pests like thrips feeding on the buds, or severe water stress during the flowering stage. Managing pests early ensures flowers stay on the stem to turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Mra be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How far apart should I space my tomato plants when transplanting them into my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing tomatoes about 50 to 60 centimeters apart gives each plant enough soil space to pull nutrients and water without competing, while allowing air to flow freely to stop fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50 kɛyashi 60 kã tomatoi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ekɛ ehe akaŋ akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi fungal leaf helai anaa.

english: Why is early weed clearing so important during the first month after my crops germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are fragile and grow slowly at first. Weeds grow much faster and will steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from the young crop, permanently stunting its development if not removed early.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa. ni ebaaju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli Enɛ baatsi ehiɛyaa naa kɛya naanɔ kɛji ajieee lɛ mra.

english: How can I tell if my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are mature when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally. You can also dig up one test tuber and cut it—if the sap dries clear without turning dark brown, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa kaa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki lɛ gĩ ni etsɔko ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young leaves from scorching.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua akɛ wɔɔhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: Planting maize too close together causes the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller or empty corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. ni ŋmãa lɛ ji bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same soil with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally release it into the soil. This enriches the ground and helps neighboring crops like corn grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is missing essential nutrients from the soil, such as nitrogen, or that the roots are suffering from lack of water or pest damage.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant faces stress from irregular watering, excessive heat, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and healthy soil keep the flowers attached until fruit forms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push downward easily. Hard or compacted soil stops the roots from growing deep, causing the tubers to become stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant at the very start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early planting allows young roots to establish while the soil is warm and full of moisture. Plants started late often run out of rain before they finish growing, leading to lower yields.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii shwereɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ náaa nugbɔ ko dani agbeɔ amɛdumɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves so fast during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Hot, dry conditions speed up the breeding cycle of armyworms while weakening the maize plant, making it easier for pests to consume the leaves before the crop can recover.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa cutworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Removing extra branches directs the plant's energy and water away from useless leaves and straight into producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so fast if I leave them on the field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rapidly break down once detached from the main plant stem because they lose water and react to air exposure. Processing or selling them within two days prevents natural rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fãa oya kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli be mli ni amɛlaajeɔ nu ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome lɛ. Kɛ́ atsu he nii loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are vine plants that need to climb up towards the sunlight. Staking them helps the leaves catch light better to produce food, which results in bigger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing long leaves instead of forming a tight, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa kakadaji yɛ yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages usually fail to form heads when the weather gets too hot or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaf growth rather than wrapping into a solid head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kaabe nyɛɛɛ afee yitsei kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee yitso ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplant lɛ nɔ lɛ baai lɛ eyi lɛ?

english: Small holes in garden egg leaves are usually caused by small insect pests like flea beetles feeding on them. Keeping the field clear of weeds and using appropriate pest control can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eggplant baai amli yɛ abɔɔi amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies, which can also pass viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã tsei hu amli

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing in plantain leaves often points to lack of water during dry spells, low soil nutrients like potassium, or fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa, tamɔ potassium loo fungal leaf helai.

english: Why is it helpful for my soil when I plant beans on my farm before growing other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots break down, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers come out short and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow misshapen when the soil is too hard, stony, or compacted, which prevents the tuber from expanding downwards easily. Planting in high, loose mounds helps them grow long and straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni nɔ kwɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested tomatoes from getting crushed and rotting quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite ni efite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Harvest tomatoes when they are just starting to change color from green to pink, store them in sturdy wooden or plastic crates instead of deep sacks, and keep them in a cool, shaded area.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomatoi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa pinki nɔ lɛ. Okɛto tso loo plastic adekai ni wa amli moŋ fe kotokui ni mli kwɔlɔ. ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or late in the evening using my water pump?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nu pɔmp baafɔ tsei anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so your crops can absorb moisture before the hot sun arrives. Watering late at night leaves leaves wet for too long, which encourages fungal diseases to spread on the plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu leebi koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water with my irrigation setup?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe nine yɛ bɔ ni mitoɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots drown from lack of air. You will notice the leaves turning yellow, wilting even when the soil is wet, or soft rotted spots developing near the base of the stem.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Obaana akɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Egboɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. aloo he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbo eba yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing smaller and weaker in areas where heavy machines drive through my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hei ni tsɔnei ni tsii tsɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery squashes the soil particles tightly together, causing soil compaction. This creates a hard ground layer that makes it difficult for crop roots to penetrate deep to find water and nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛ baa bote mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛ na nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Does plowing my farm with tractors help crop roots grow better?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ trakta tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plowing loosens the upper layer of soil, making it easy for young root seedlings to spread. However, doing it repeatedly when the soil is wet can create a hard layer underneath that stops deep root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ atsu he nii shii abɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni wa.

english: What happens to my crops if someone plants seeds too close to my existing plants?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mɔ ko du dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mi tsei ni miyɔɔ momo lɛ tsɔ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the plants grow thin, weak, and produce much lower yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my crops under the shade of big trees grow tall but produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ shi amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food for fruits or seeds. Under tall shade, plants waste all their energy stretching upward toward the sun instead of spending energy on flowering and fruiting.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii amɛha amɛyibii loo amɛdumɔwui lɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ hulu lɛ he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo he lɛ

english: Leaf rolling is a survival mechanism. The crop rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing precious water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu ni jara wa lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat or water stress, it tries to save its own life by dropping flowers and tiny fruits so it doesn't waste energy trying to nourish them without enough moisture.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehere ehe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akafite hewalɛ ni akɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni akɛha tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my vegetable plants producing lots of green leaves but no fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: This usually means the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages leaf and stem growth. To get fruits, plants need balanced feeding that includes nutrients like phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. ni haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium fata he koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my crop turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in dry or poor soil, it moves the remaining nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha nɔ hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are some of my seeds failing to sprout after I plant them in the moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are old, damaged by insects, planted too deep, or if the soil is too hot or flooded. Using high-quality, certified seeds ensures that most of what you plant will sprout healthy and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ŋmeii ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ efite loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ mli babaoo baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe wa.

english: What is the advantage of buying certified seeds from an agricultural dealer instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specifically tested and bred to grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and yield a higher volume of crops. Saved seeds often lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli pɔtɛɛ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛdara daa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: How deep under the soil should I bury my seeds during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi be mli ni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: A general rule is to bury a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its width. Planting seeds too deep prevents the young sprout from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow exposes them to birds and dry heat.
ga: Mla ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni afu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛlɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ooodu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi lɛ aná la ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks vital nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen. It can also mean the soil is holding too much water, which suffocates the plant roots and prevents them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Crops drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate the blooms. Consistent watering and shade during hot periods can help plants hold their flowers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop plants stretch out thin and tall instead of growing thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɛ amɛhe ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee shwiili ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plants stretch and grow tall when they are searching for sunlight. If crops are planted too close together or under dense shade, they spend all their energy reaching upward for light rather than building strong stems.
ga: Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛdaraa be mli ni amɛtaoɔ hulu la lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni etao la kɛya ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeetswa tsei ni wa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close to each other in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough resources to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my healthy green crops to suddenly wilt and collapse overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Sudden wilting is usually caused by pests like cutworms chewing the roots underground, or bacterial and fungal diseases inside the soil that block the plant's tubes from carrying water upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. aloo helai ni jɛɔ bacteria kɛ fungi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tsei paipii anaa koni amɛkawo nu kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives crop-specific pests a permanent place to live. Rotating with crops like beans restores nutrients and starves the pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hiɔ shi daa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: How should I store my harvested seeds so they stay healthy until the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds should be dried completely and stored in clean, airtight containers in a cool, dark, and dry room. Keeping moisture and heat away prevents seeds from rotting or losing their ability to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli egbi mli. Kɛ́ ahiɛ fɛ̃i kɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their green color and keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okpa ni otsiii amɛ fɛɛ?

english: When cassava is ready for harvest, the lower leaves on the stem naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the base of the plant begins to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat without enough shade, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Keeping adequate shade trees helps keep the farm humid and protects the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or water consistently while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aná calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain tree give smaller bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe.

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main tree for food and water. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother tree to direct all its food into producing a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the roots grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper field early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs water before the heat of the day, and excess water on the leaves dries off quickly, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi oya. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that extract nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there holes in the middle leaves of my young corn and small caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves inside the plant funnel. Applying recommended neem extract or chemical spray directly into the plant funnel early in the morning stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by small insects even when I tie the sacks tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotokui lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects and their eggs are often already on the maize during harvest or enter through small gaps in regular sacks. Thoroughly drying the grain and storing it in airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates insects and preserves the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo amɛboteɔ ŋmãa bibii amli yɛ kotokui ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli (vacuum) lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I start my seeds in a seedbed instead of planting them directly in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A seedbed protects small, delicate seeds from harsh weather and pests, giving them soft soil and steady moisture so they can sprout safely before being moved to the bigger farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe. Eyɛ mlɛo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔ agbo ko mli.

english: What exactly is a seedbed and how does it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni diɛŋtsɛ ji dumɔwui? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A seedbed is a special area of fine, soft soil prepared to give tiny seeds ideal warmth and moisture, ensuring a higher chance of seeds sprouting successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui atsu ji he ko krɛdɛɛ ko ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɔɔ nɔ ni asaa he koni dumɔwui bibii akwɛ̃. Eyɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni sa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hegbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How long do my seeds usually need to stay in the seedbed before they sprout and are ready to move?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ?

english: Most vegetable seeds take around one week to sprout in a well-watered seedbed and build initial strength before they are ready for transplanting.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui babaoo heɔ aaafee otsi kome dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni etswa shishijee hewalɛ ema shi dani efee klalo akɛ abaawo mɔ kroko mli

english: Why is it necessary to add water to the soil as soon as I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ?

english: Water softens the hard outer shell of the seed and wakes it up, giving it the moisture it needs to burst open and push roots into the soil.
ga: Nu haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eteɔ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa koni akɛgbala ni akɛtsi shishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Should I wet the seedbed before or immediately after putting my seeds in?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo mli loo beni mikɛwo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Adding water when sowing keeps the soil moist around the seed, preventing it from drying out and helping it germinate faster.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu fata he beni aduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akwɛ̃. dumɔwui ni mli efɔ Etsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: What does transplanting mean, and why is it done for certain crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ kroko mli lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ afeɔ tsei komɛi nakai lɛ?

english: Transplanting means growing young plants in a small nursery first and then moving them to the main field; this ensures only strong, healthy plants are grown in your main plot.
ga: Tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aaadu tsei bibii klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe bibioo ko mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ajie amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to plant cabbage directly into the main farm soil or start it in a seedbed first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kaabaji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Cabbage grows best when sown in a seedbed first and then transplanted, as young cabbage seedlings are delicate and need careful monitoring in their first week.
ga: Kaabaji daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ adu lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kaabe dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa, ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii lɛ amli.

english: Can watermelon seeds be started in a nursery bed before moving them to the farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu watermelon dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akɛwo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, watermelon seeds can be sown in a seedbed to guarantee good germination and protect young shoots before carefully transplanting them to the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu watermelon dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe dani akɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some vegetable crops take up to a week to show growth after being planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tsei komɛi heɔ otsi kome dani amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the first week, seeds are busy absorbing water underground and developing roots before their leaves finally break through the soil surface.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ŋmɔmɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi dani naagbee lɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if a crop like cabbage or watermelon is suitable for transplanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko tamɔ kaabe loo watermelon sa akɛ adu?

english: Crops with small seeds and sensitive young shoots, like cabbage and watermelon, benefit from being sown in a nursery bed first to establish strong roots before facing open field conditions.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ kaabɛji kɛ watermelon. Obaaná dumɔwui adumɔ he sɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni oma shishifãi ni wa dani okɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli tse lɛ akpee.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away from your fields into streams or push it too deep into the ground before your crop roots have time to drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed and scorched under direct hot sunshine. Shade trees block intense sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and protect your cocoa plants from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: How does leaving proper space between my plantain suckers help me get bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni mashi yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná tsei wuji?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their leaves block sunshine from each other and their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central growing funnel of maize. They feed on soft young leaves and can destroy the growing point if not caught early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛji amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and crinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses, causing leaves to twist and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, creating soggy conditions where root-rot fungi multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya lɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress, which prevents proper pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or during the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the heat of the day causes water to evaporate rapidly.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aha nu lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mifo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests, which multiply in the soil if you don't rotate with a different crop like maize or beans.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Enɛ baafee babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeee.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly in the basket while other farmers' tomatoes stay fresh for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato ni mikpa lɛ miifite oya yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaafoi krokomɛi atoma lɛ hiɔ shi otsii babaoo.

english: Just like good feed makes strong animal products, proper plant nutrition—especially calcium and balanced watering—builds strong skin walls in tomatoes, making them stay firm and fresh much longer after harvest.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa haa kooloi anibii feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tso mli niyenii ni sa—titri lɛ calcium kɛ nu ni sa—haa hewolo nɔ gbogboi ni mli wa baa tomato mli. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunches start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ miihe afee shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that get top-heavy when fruiting. Without propping them up with wooden bamboo stakes or if root-eating pests are present, wind easily knocks them down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsii kɛji amɛwo yibii. Ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fioo ko pɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi yɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crop turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ kpakpa.
