english: Why does my cassava farm have huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its food energy growing top leaves instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does adding organic compost or animal manure help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Compost acts like a sponge in the soil, holding moisture near the plant roots and releasing steady nutrients so crops stay healthy even when rain is scarce.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kpo daa. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ faaa po.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that provide vital shade and cool moisture during the cocoa trees' first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Overcrowded plants fight each other for limited sunlight, root space, soil nutrients, and water, causing all of them to grow thin and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. kɛ nu fioo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, erratic watering, or pest attacks, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ Enɛ tsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and draining the plant's juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal fertilizer, root space, and sunlight away from your main crop before your plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli dani amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I keep using saved seeds from my own maize harvest year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Reusing seeds from the same farm harvest causes crops to lose their vigor over time, leading to smaller yields and higher vulnerability to diseases. Buying fresh certified seeds or getting seeds from a different, healthy source introduces strong traits that keep your harvest large and healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ajɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni helai hu baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli loo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ he kroko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ sui ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa okpamɔ nii lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and need shade to survive their early development. Intercropping them with fast-growing plants like plantains creates a natural protective canopy that shields the young cocoa from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛtaoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛshwere yɛ amɛshishijee bei amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains du amɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli ŋtayaa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers get smaller every season when I use stem cuttings from my previous farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii daa be mli ni mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Taking stem cuttings continuously from old farms can transfer hidden diseases and accumulated weakness to the new field. Using fresh, disease-free cuttings from an improved stock source ensures strong plant growth and bigger tubers.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ ahe tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ bɔjɔmɔi ni abua naa lɛ kɛya ŋmɔji heei amli. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni hela bɛ mli ni jɛ tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: What causes the bottom leaves of my maize plants to turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize relies on to build green leaves. Applying organic compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth and supports grain development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa biɔ koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba Kɛ akɛ organic compost loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my land produce less yield when I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop on a plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake o-corn lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture and occasional shade during the hottest parts of the dry season helps flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Will I harvest more crops if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and lower yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce maximum harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your plants' root zone. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to rain and fertilizer so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Koni tsei lɛ adara waa

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground exposes their leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food to feed the tubers underground, while also preventing leave rot from damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha efoji lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually a sign of fungal root rot caused by excess water sitting around the roots. Improving field drainage and using disease-resistant seed varieties prevents roots from rotting and dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji shishifãi lɛ ahe okadi, ni nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afee ŋmɔ mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa plants can survive their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy treated hybrid seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni atsa amɛhe lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du wuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose their vigor and disease resistance over time. Hybrid seeds are specially bred to fight off local pests and diseases right from germination, giving you a stronger crop and better yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ mli baa lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni onáa yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to use a large seed piece when planting yam instead of a tiny cutting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ dumɔwui wuji atsu nii kɛ́ midu sweet potatoes yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The seed yam stores energy for the sprouting plant. A larger piece provides enough food reserves to support the vine until it grows enough roots and leaves to feed itself from the soil.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ toɔ tso bibioo lɛ he. Nibii ni dara lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaakwɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaye nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil without good drainage, the roots suffocate from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing organisms to attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa bɔɔ nii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that clogs the internal water pipes of the plant stem. Even if water is present in the soil, the plant cannot pull it up to its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala lɛ kɛyashɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water and keeps the root zone cool, helping your crops stay hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Eyeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ anáa nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is a reaction to tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or a virus spread by insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ baa lɛ adalɛ naa bɔ ni sa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the tassels at the top of my maize plant appear before the cobs develop lower down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: The tassels produce pollen, which is carried by the wind to fertilize the cobs. They mature first so that pollen is ready to drop as soon as the silks emerge on the young cobs to form maize grains.
ga: Tassels lɛ feɔ pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Amɛdaraa klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaagbee shi kɛji siliki lɛ je kpo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ nɔ pɛ koni ebatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming removes parts of the plant that consume energy without producing fruit. It directs the plant's food supply straight into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Trimming jieɔ fãi komɛi. ni ji tsei ni kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ Etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for next season's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This leaves free natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops, like plantain, to block harsh sun and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a key sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires high amounts of nitrogen to grow full green leaves and produce large cobs, which can be fixed using manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa ni ewo ŋmãa wuji. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest feeds on the soft inner leaves of young maize, leaving behind ragged holes and fine waste material as it eats.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai lɛ. Amɛshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ nibii bibii beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: How can I tell from looking at the plant that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the bottom leaves yellow and shed, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack as the expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to gather energy efficiently, which drives the growth of large tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo he. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛbuaa hewalɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. ni tsirɛɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before any small fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when plants face extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and protecting roots helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled, distorted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, which can also pass along stunt-causing plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni haa amɛjieɔ amɛnyɛmɔi akpo lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees tend to fall over so easily when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread horizontally near the surface rather than deep underground. As heavy fruit bunches grow, the top-heavy trees easily tip over in soggy soil and strong winds unless supported by wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu ni mli tse lɛ dara lɛ Tsei ni tsii waa lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ nɔ oya. ja tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry gap before the main rains fully settle. Seeds planted immediately may germinate and then die from heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui ni adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural plant food in the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantains around them, the hot sun scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil, causing the leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã tsei lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce big green leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing energy in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do fall armyworms cause my young maize plants to break and fall over?
ga: Te fall armyworms lɛ haa mi-babi corn tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Fall armyworms burrow deep into the central growing tip (the funnel) of young maize, chewing through delicate leaf tissue and weakening the main stem so it snaps easily in the wind.
ga: Fall worms lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ (cone) lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. ni eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni efo oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Is it true that planting beans in the same farm as my maize will help my soil?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nitrogen-hungry maize growing nearby.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ nitrogen ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛkuɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the water channels inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves no matter how wet the soil is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ha.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their parent plants' special vigor in the next generation, leading to weak plants, uneven growth, and much lower yields compared to fresh seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni fa ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahe.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or drought stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve water and energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my yam crop so much more during the first two months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young yam sprouts grow slowly at the start and cannot cover the ground, allowing weeds to easily steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients needed to form strong roots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ daaa fiofio yɛ shishijee mli ni anyɛɛɛ awo amɛmli. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What happens if a heavy downpour of rain falls right after I put fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away granular fertilizer from the soil surface into drainage paths before crop roots can absorb it, wasting your fertilizer and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe kɛyaa nu homɔ gbɛi amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa o-fertilizer kɛ oshika lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Growing cassava continuously in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows pests and root diseases tailored to cassava to build up in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kpo. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni etsake amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my young green oranges falling off the trees before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Orange trees shed young fruit when they don't get enough water during dry spells or when fruit flies damage the small fruits. Keeping the soil moist and clearing dropped fruits from the farm floor helps prevent this.
ga: Citrus tsei woɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii kpata aduawai bibii lɛ ahiɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ajie aduawai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my orange trees turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the tree lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil around the roots is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my orange trees produce flowers at different times of the year instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees flower whenever rain comes right after a long dry period. Unpredictable weather tricks the tree into flowering multiple times in a single year.
ga: Orange tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shii abɔ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Why is my maize staying short and yellow even though I planted it right when the rains started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ? Adu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Young maize needs quick access to soil nutrients. Pale and stunted growth means the soil lacks nitrogen or that weeds are stealing water and nutrients from the young crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo jwɛi miiju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen but not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why did my fruit trees yield a huge harvest last year but almost nothing this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi afi nɛɛ, ani afeee nɔ ko kwraa?

english: Trees use up vast amounts of energy to produce a large crop. Without extra fertilizer and water after a big harvest, the tree gets exhausted and takes a year to rest and recover.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kroko fataaa he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ wulu ko sɛɛ lɛ No lɛ tso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ekɛ afi jɔɔ ehe ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot or dry. The plant drops its flowers to save water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my oranges have dark brown patches and hard spots on their skins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni wa yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard patches and dark spots on orange skins are caused by tiny pests or fungal diseases attacking the skin while the fruit is still small and soft.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa hewolo lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tso yibii lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ blɛoo lolo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahewolo nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do we heap soil into large mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔbuaa muji babaoo naa dani wɔduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into large, smooth tubers. Heaping soil into mounds provides deep space, prevents soil compaction, and protects the tubers from rotting in standing water.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato gɔŋ ko he koni efee he ko ni mli kwɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides temporary shade and keeps the air humid until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This nitrogen acts as free fertilizer that helps nearby maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow starting at the bottom when the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top young leaves to survive, leaving the lower leaves to starve.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ he hiaa nitrogen lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Shi shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni eegbo?

english: The cassava is not dying; dropping leaves is its way of saving water during drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and safely rests until the rains return to sprout fresh shoots.
ga: Kasava gbooo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ekɛ tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients cause heat stress. When stressed, the pepper plant drops its flowers because it knows it does not have enough energy to raise those flowers into full fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Kɛji akɛ haomɔ ba Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ amɛle akɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee nakai fɔfɔi lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do I get much smaller yields when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii bibii babaoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes your crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because the resources are shared among too many plants, none of them get enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ajaa nibii ni yɔɔ tsei babaoo ateŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves. Their roots grow faster than your crops, stealing the water and natural food in the soil before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Eshishifãi lɛ daa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Ejuɔ nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus or by severe heat stress, which damages the leaf cells and stops normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii ni ehaa amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaa lɛ mli

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so roots can soak them in. Putting fertilizer on bone-dry soil can burn and destroy the plant's root tips, killing the plant instead of helping it.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. ni haa tso lɛ gboɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Leaves often turn yellow and drop when young cocoa trees receive too much direct sunlight or not enough water. Providing shade crops like plantains and keeping the soil moist helps protect the delicate young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when I plant them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ato kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees should typically be planted about 3 meters apart in rows. This gives their roots and branches enough room to grow, allows light to penetrate, and prevents diseases from spreading easily between crowded trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3, ni eha shishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃. Ehaa la tsɔɔ mli. ni atsĩ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu kookoo?

english: If crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or produce small yields, your soil is likely low on nutrients. Adding organic manure or recommended fertilizers before planting ensures your trees get the nutrients needed to establish strong roots.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko lɛ Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eshishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cool, rainy weather when trees are dense and humid. Pruning branches to let in air and light, and removing infected pods, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ebaakpa hela gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree lacks water, suffers pest damage, or lacks beneficial insects like midges to pollinate them. Proper watering, pest control, and maintaining light shade encourage flowers to set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii efite loo ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, nu ni akɛhaa, kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni bɛ Ni kane ni sa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches and leaves so sunlight and fresh air can circulate through the tree. This directs the plant's food and energy straight into growing healthy cocoa pods rather than useless foliage.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni ataooo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ kudɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: How long should my cocoa seedlings stay in the nursery before transplanting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu amɛ?

english: Cocoa seedlings should stay in the nursery for about 3 to 6 months until they develop several strong leaves and a sturdy root system. Planting them at the start of the rainy season gives them the best chance of survival.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 kɛyashi amɛbaaná baai babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa mɔ náa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛhiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ yucca yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: While plantains provide great shade for young cocoa, crops like cassava compete heavily for soil nutrients and water, which can stunt cocoa growth. It is better to keep aggressive feeder crops away from cocoa root zones.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantain haa kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo moŋ, shi esa akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmei lɛ atswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ kɛjɛ he ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa pod is ripe and ready to pick when its skin completely changes color from green or red to a deep yellow or orange. Harvesting at this time ensures the beans inside are fully formed and rich in quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ahe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ koni kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a huge harvest one year and a very small harvest the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa babaoo afi kome mli, ni ewoɔ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees use a tremendous amount of stored energy during a heavy harvest year, leaving them exhausted for the following season. Consistent fertilizing, weed control, and pruning help trees stay healthy and produce balanced yields every year.
ga: Cacao tsei yeɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato yɛ kpamɔɔ afii ni mli wa lɛ amli. ni oha hewalɛ lɛ afite kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ jwɛi amli daa Ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa daa afi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods for several months after the main harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔji babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow natural climate cycles tied to rainfall and dry periods. After producing a heavy crop during the main harvest, the trees enter a resting phase to conserve energy, grow new leaves, and recover before starting a new flowering cycle when the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni kɛ nugbɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ sɛɛ. Beni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baabote hejɔɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he, amɛkwɛ̃ baai heei, ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛje fɔfɔi heei ahe nitsumɔ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: When is the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans inside don't spoil?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii koni kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite?

english: You should harvest cocoa pods when the pod color turns completely from green or deep red to solid yellow or orange. Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to germinate or rot, while picking them green results in poor quality beans.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa cocoa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ ahe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaabuamɔ baaha aná kɔfi ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What short-term crops can I plant on my farm to get food and money during the months when cocoa is out of season?
ga: Mɛɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ nyɔji ni kookoo be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and vegetables such as peppers or garden eggs alongside your main farm. These crops grow and mature quickly, providing continuous food and extra income during the quiet cocoa months.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa, kɛ aduawai tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ obɔɔ lɛ mli. yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ masɛi Tsei nɛɛ daa ni amɛdaraa oya. Ha niyenii ni yaa nɔ kɛ shika kroko yɛ kookoo nyɔji ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce smaller tubers when planted right before the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii kɛji akɛ adu dani hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs consistent moisture during its early growth stage to establish strong, thick roots. If planted right before the dry season, the lack of water causes the plant to stunt and focus on survival rather than expanding its tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ koni ená shishifãi ni wa ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ adu dani hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ Nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama wala nɔ moŋ fe bulb lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree experiences water stress and poor soil nutrients. Keeping shade on your farm creates a safe environment for pollinating insects and keeps the tree hydrated.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa kɛha kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are some of my young green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot feed, or by fungal infections like Black Pod disease. Clearing thick weeds and pruning crowded branches improves airflow and reduces pod loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha pod ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and hot sun cause cocoa trees to drop leaves to save water and protect their main stems from drying out completely. Shade trees help reduce leaf loss by shielding cocoa trees from direct dry winds.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi kwraa. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ haa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How do shade trees help protect my crops during the hottest months of the year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Shade trees act as living shields by blocking direct sun, lowering air temperature, and preventing soil water from evaporating quickly. Their deep roots also bring up moisture from deep underground, keeping the farm cooler.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulu la ni tsiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i

english: How does pruning my cocoa trees help them grow more pods in the coming season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛshwere yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or extra branches so sunlight and air can reach the lower trunk where flowers form. It forces the tree to direct its food and water straight into growing strong flowering buds and large pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe he ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ lɛ. Enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkudɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm soil needs fertilizer to help the trees produce better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: If your cocoa trees show pale green or yellowish leaves, drop their flowers early, or produce smaller pods despite good rainfall, the soil is low on essential nutrients. Applying approved cocoa fertilizer or organic manure restores tree strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya Aloo ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Even with enough water, if the soil loses its nutrients after years of planting without replenishment, the plants cannot feed properly and will turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akwɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni akɛ nu fataaa he lɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every year when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating your crops or allowing the soil to rest helps restore its fertility and boosts future harvest yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ ni eha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaakpa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I add dried animal manure or compost to my farm instead of relying only on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi aŋmeii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi afata miŋmɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give plants a quick boost, but manure feeds and improves the physical structure of the soil. Manure helps the soil retain moisture longer and keeps it fertile for future planting seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Manure yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my pepper plants to suddenly rot from the roots and wilt during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by fungal diseases that thrive in soggy, waterlogged soil. Ensuring proper farm drainage and planting on raised soil beds prevents excess water from suffocating and rotting the roots.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni efite.

english: How do tiny worms get inside my maize stems and cause the top leaves to dry up?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii boteɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbiɔ?

english: These worms are stem borers, which are caterpillars hatched from invisible eggs laid on the leaves by moths. They burrow deep into the stem and eat the plant from the inside, preventing water and nutrients from reaching the top leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛfoɔ bu kɛyaa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets in sunshine and airflow, which dries up the moisture the disease needs to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa hela lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and weak with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and nutrients to produce strong branches and abundant fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo niji ni wa kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: How does covering the ground with dry leaves around my crops help them during hot periods?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi ebɔle he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and keeps moisture around the roots during heatwaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ Roots lɛ he lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting beans together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ajieɔ Nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of planting saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops often lose their strength and disease resistance in the second generation, leading to smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases and produce uniform, high-yielding crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees around them to shield their leaves from severe heat and retain moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning from excess standing water. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la ni ashiɔ koni eha ŋmei lɛ ada blɛoo ni eshwere sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield small, thin roots instead of big tubers when I plant in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose earth to expand easily under the ground. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to grow large, which is why forming raised soil mounds or ridges helps increase yields.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tubers lɛ shweremɔ wa. Enɛ hewɔ ni gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ ni afee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep chewing holes in my vegetable leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-vegetables baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates damp conditions where moths lay eggs on leaf undersides, hatching into caterpillars that feed on crops. Clearing weeds and spraying safe neem oil or recommended control remedies protects the foliage.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be baa. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ neem fɔ loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and yellow leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows the plant to focus its energy on growing bigger fruits rather than feeding extra leaves. It also improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebote baai krokomɛi amli lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three steady rains have thoroughly wet the ground so seeds do not dry out in the soil, but avoid planting right before heavy downpours that might wash the seeds away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my main crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough plants designed to capture light, water, and soil nutrients quickly. Clearing land uncovers weed seeds in the soil, so early weed clearing gives your main crops a head start to grow taller.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛmɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aje shishi eda.

english: How can I prevent insects from destroying my stored grains after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive on leftover moisture inside harvested grains. Drying your grains thoroughly in the sun until hard and storing them in airtight bags prevents weevils from breeding and spoiling your harvest.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafɔ ni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of adding animal manure to my farm instead of relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Animal manure improves long-term soil structure and helps the soil hold moisture during dry spells, whereas chemical fertilizers give plants a fast nutrient boost but do not build soil quality over time.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya lɛ, amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How long after planting maize will I start seeing the flowers and ears forming?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani abɔi fɔfɔii kɛ toii ni miida lɛ anaa?

english: Maize usually begins flowering—producing tassels at the top and silk on the side—about 6 to 8 weeks after planting. Once the silks appear, the cobs develop rapidly over the following weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi. Amɛbaaná ŋmeii yɛ amɛyiteŋ kɛ siliki yɛ amɛsɛɛ aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 yɛ be mli ni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ Cob lɛ baaya hiɛ oya yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my pepper plants have reached their peak production time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni amɛwoɔ nii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants usually start flowering about 6 weeks after transplanting and reach their peak harvest period around 8 to 10 weeks. During this peak, you will notice heavy flowering and many firm, mature peppers ripening at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi aaafee otsii 6 sɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ. Nikpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ji aaafee otsii 8 kɛyashi 10. Yɛ nɛkɛ yitso nɛɛ mli lɛ obaana fɔfɔii ni tsii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit because of extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or poor pollination. Giving the plants steady water and planting at the right time helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ nu daa ni adu amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: How many months does cassava take before the tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months to mature fully. Harvesting too early results in thin tubers with low starch content, while leaving them too long can make them woody.
ga: Kasava ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu faaa. Kɛji ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ eha yitso lɛ afee tso.

english: At what age does a new hybrid cocoa tree start producing pods?
ga: Mɛɛ afii mli kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa trees usually start producing their first flowers and pods around 2 to 3 years after planting, reaching their peak pod production after about 7 to 10 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhe fe fɛɛ yɛ aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10 sɛɛ.

english: Why do new small shoots grow around the base of my plantain tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ nibii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, which are natural offspring of the main plant. You should prune away weaker ones and leave only 2 or 3 strong shoots so they do not steal food from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. ni ji tso titri lɛ adebɔɔ mli seshibii Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni akajie niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops to get a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: For most grain crops like maize, apply the first portion 1 to 2 weeks after sprouting to aid early growth, and the second portion around 4 to 6 weeks when the plant is growing fast before flowering.
ga: Kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli yɛ otsii 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ koni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ oya. ni okɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 beni tso lɛ miida oya dani ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up in hot weather as a natural defense to reduce water evaporation. However, if they stay curled in the early morning or evening, it could be a sign of pest damage or dry soil.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji amɛfo amɛhe leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi.

english: How many weeks should my garden egg seedlings stay in the nursery before transplanting them?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ mi abɔɔ mli eggplant dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani adu amɛ?

english: Garden egg seedlings are usually ready to be transplanted to the main farm about 4 to 6 weeks after sowing, once they have developed 4 to 6 strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ahe dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to buy fertilizer for my cassava farm if plants already grow in the soil naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ? Be mli ni tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Crops are like growing children—wild plants in the bush only grow enough to survive, but farm crops need extra food (nutrients) to produce big tubers. Fertilizer replaces the food that previous crops have pulled out of the ground so your soil stays rich.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tamɔ gbekɛbii. Dalɛ—Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa pɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi. Shi ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii krokomɛi (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji. Niyenii ni tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii gbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ. Koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: Why do my pepper plants produce tiny fruits when I plant many of them close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be ni midu babaoo Dumɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni he akafite?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other under the soil for water and food, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Giving each plant its own space allows it to feed properly and grow larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa amɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and burn when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—their leaves are soft and burn easily under the hot afternoon sun. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Ebaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ he ko ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow first, it means the plant is starving for a key soil food called nitrogen. To survive, the plant pulls whatever food it has left from its old lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ. koni ehi shi Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but then the flowers drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme sun heat, lack of water, or pest attacks. The plant drops the flowers to save its own life when it senses conditions are too harsh to feed growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ shihilɛi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ. Ehe wa tsɔ ni ekɛfiɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the yam crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe sweet potato tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild survival experts that have adapted to drink water and steal nutrients from the soil much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early removes this competition so your yams get all the water and food.
ga: Jwɛi ji mɛi ni le bɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi amɛhaa yɛ koo lɛ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ mli ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ nine shɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer plantains now compared to three years ago when I first cleared the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo plantains fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii etɛ ni eho nɛ beni mifo ŋmɔji lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they carry away nutrients from the earth. Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains the soil of its specific food until the soil becomes exhausted and yields drop.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii krɛdɛɛi lɛ baa shi, ni no haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leafy branches from my tomato plants when I want more fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato tso niji komɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli be mli ni miitao aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: When a plant has too many branches, it wastes its strength feeding extra green leaves instead of making tomatoes. Trimming excess branches forces the plant to redirect its energy into growing bigger, heavier fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Ehewalɛ baaje edɛŋ kɛji eye baai eŋɔli yɛ tomato najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsake hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya aduawai wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from the maize I harvested last season to plant for my next farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength and disease resistance over time, leading to uneven growth. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures every plant grows strong, resists pests, and gives a higher yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha tso fɛɛ tso ada jogbaŋŋ. Enyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Why do my vegetable leaves sleep and drop down during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi veggies lɛ ka amɛsɛɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛkaaa lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the middle of the day, the hot sun makes water evaporate from crop leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant folds its leaves down to protect itself from drying out, and it stands back up once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni ebaate shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.
