english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowers and pods. Using fertilizers higher in phosphorus helps the plant shift energy toward producing healthy pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsakeɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops now than when I first cleared the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared bush land has rich organic matter built up over years. Continuous farming drains those natural nutrients out of the ground, so you must replenish the soil using compost, manure, or fertilizers to keep harvest yields high.
ga: Brɔshi he ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ yɛ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ebua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil. When excessive rain gathers around the roots without draining away, it cuts off air supply to the roots and causes underground rot to set in.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, ebuaa ehe naa kɛbɔleɔ he. shishifãi ni nu ejeee mli Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi nibii lɛ agbo

english: Why does my maize crop produce small cobs with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni dumɔwui komɛi elaaje?

english: Missing grains on a maize cob usually happen when dry weather or heat stress occurs during pollination. If pollen falls off or dries out before reaching the silks, the kernels will not form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ ba yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollen lɛ gbee shi loo egbi dani eshɛ siliki kpãai lɛ ahe lɛ Dumɔwui efeŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and out of shape underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand straight downward. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tuber struggles to push through and bends around obstacles as it grows.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛkoto nɔ ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ lɛ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Maintaining consistent moisture and providing light shade during very hot weather helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How can I know if my tomato plant is thirsty or has a disease when it wilts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai miiye mi-tomato tsei lɛ loo hela yɛ amɛmli beni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: A thirsty plant wilts in the hot afternoon sun but recovers and stands up straight in the cool evening after watering. A diseased plant stays wilted even at night and may develop yellowing leaves or dark spots.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaahe ewa ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi gbɛkɛ po. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees are like babies—they burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need during their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii—amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad to plant the same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating your crops keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet potato leaves look pale green with yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pale and spotted leaves usually show that the soil lacks essential plant foods like potassium or magnesium. Mixing well-rotted compost into the soil around the plants helps balance the nutrients they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ futuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tsei baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the middle of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the central shoot of the maize plant to feed. Spraying natural neem extracts or recommended crop remedies early in the morning or late evening helps clear them out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem mli nu loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow in patches and curling up out of shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni amɛkpɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck leaf sap. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing affected plants early stops the spread to healthy crops.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ baai amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ekpaa gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant suffers from heat stress or from a virus transmitted by small white insects called whiteflies. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from insect bites prevents leaf curling.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ mli loo hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei bibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe; Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, allowing soil fungi to attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold together tightly in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants fold their leaves during the hottest hours of the day as a natural protection trick to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly from their leaves.
ga: Peanut tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off without turning into small peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Giving the plants consistent water and applying compost helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden poles to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce the food that builds large tubers underground. Staking the vines gets them off the wet soil, increases light exposure, and prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ okɛ wein tsei lɛ fĩ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha la aya hiɛ, ni ebaaha baa helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during light wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall when tiny underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers destroy the root foundation. Planting clean suckers and adding organic manure strengthens the root anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite shishifã lɛ shishitoo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni he tse ni akɛ ŋmeii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves on top look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves grow using sunshine, but cassava tubers need loose, well-drained soil and potassium nutrients to expand. If the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant spends energy growing big leaves instead of expanding its roots underground.
ga: Baai lɛ daa kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni ji potassium lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do new plantain shoots grow from under the ground without me planting seeds?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni miduuu dumɔwui?

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds like maize. They reproduce through underground stems called corms that push new shoots, called suckers, up through the earth right next to the main mother plant.
ga: Plantains jeee dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ anɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii heei, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ, kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I clear and plant on land that has rested for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ehi shi afii fioo komɛi ni eho lɛ nɔ ni midu nɔ lɛ?

english: Resting land allows natural leaves and roots to rot and decay into the soil, restoring essential nutrients and organic matter. This rich soil feeds your new crops much better than land that has been continuously farmed without a break.
ga: He ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ haa baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɛɛ baaye abua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko bɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need space underground to stretch and grow big. If mounds are built too close together, the roots fight each other under the soil for water and food, resulting in smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ato lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Can I harvest seeds from my hybrid maize crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ hybrid corn mli koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to buy fresh hybrid seeds every season. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their vigor and will produce uneven plants with smaller yields when planted a second time.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid daa be. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaawo tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni wooo yibii babaoo kɛji adu shii enyɔ nɔ.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots spread in the soil, they feed the maize plant and make the soil richer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does Striga weed keep coming back to attack my cereal crops even after I pull it out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni ebatutua mi ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ migbala kɛtee moŋ

english: Striga, or witchweed, attaches its roots directly to the roots of your crop beneath the soil to steal nutrients. Its tiny seeds can lie hidden underground for years waiting for crop roots to grow near them again.
ga: Striga, loo Witchweed lɛ, kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Edumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ ni tso shishifãi akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in strong afternoon heat is the plant's way of protecting itself. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces sunlight exposure and stops water from evaporating too quickly until the sun cools down.
ga: Baai ni efoɔ yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baaha hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt for a few days right after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock. Moving a young plant breaks its delicate root hairs that drink water, so it wilts until its roots recover and start growing into the new soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso bibioo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ akumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Tall shade trees or plantain plants shield them from intense heat and help keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raising the soil into mounds creates soft, loose earth that allows cassava roots to expand easily into large tubers, while also preventing rainwater from sitting around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ awó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up before the ears are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani toi lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant has run out of nitrogen in the soil. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the food it needs to keep its leaves green and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like a rock after a few hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ gbii babaoo ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses its moisture quickly to the heat and wind, causing the ground to bake hard. Leaving crop leftovers or dried grass on top of the soil shields it from the hot sun and keeps it soft and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewɔ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects cause small dark patches on my cocoa pods that spread until the whole pod dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shĩɔ okadi bibii diji yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are mirids (capsids) that pierce the skin of the pod to suck sap, causing black lesions that destroy the pod. Clearing bush around the trees and spraying at the right time helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji merids (capsids) ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo nɔ koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa okadii diji ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Too tsei bibii ni ebɔle he lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ Tsei kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap and spread plant sicknesses. Removing severely sick plants early prevents the problem from spreading across the rest of your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ waa lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ebaatsi naagba lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures and dry air cause tomato blossoms to drop off before they can produce fruit. Giving the plants steady water at the root level and light shade helps them keep their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce lots of thick leaves above ground but very small roots beneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni mli tse waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When plants get too much water or excess nitrogen late in the season, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of expanding their underground roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When planted too close, maize plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough energy to build a thick stalk and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the ground better for next season's maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, those nutrient-filled roots stay in the ground and feed the next crop like maize naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai shishifãi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii, taakɛ ŋmãa feɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shishi pɛ

english: Cassava leaves grow fast when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. The plant spends all its energy on top instead of sending nutrients down to build fat roots.
ga: Kasava baai lɛ daa oya kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the tip down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps the plant stay green and build food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots work with tiny friendly microbes in the soil to pull nitrogen out of the air, leaving natural fertilizer in the ground for your next crop.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves curl up and dry out during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves lose water quickly in dry winds. Without shade trees above them, the sun bakes the leaves and the plant curls them up to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: When the air gets too hot and dry, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy until the weather cools down.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaajie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my corn seeds rot in the ground if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up the dry soil without soaking it deep enough, creating a warm, damp environment that causes seeds to spoil before full rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli awo mli bɔ ni sa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines keep sending out thin shoots looking for sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛɔ tsei bibii ni etaoɔ niji ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally grow upwards toward sunlight. Climbing stakes keeps their leaves open to light and off the damp ground where diseases live.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsoi ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe kɛhaa la, ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ ahi lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the heavy fruit bunch comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread out near the surface. When heavy fruit grows, rain softens the topsoil and wind pulls the top-heavy plant right out.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara babaoo lɛ Nugbɔ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ni amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa ni egbala nɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree give me plenty of fruit this year, but almost nothing the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi babaoo yɔɔ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ani ebaatsu nii kwraa?

english: Producing a massive harvest takes a lot of energy, so the tree spends the entire next year resting and re-building nutrients before it can flower heavily again.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo biɔ hewalɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ heɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ dani enyɛɔ efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my cleared land than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that react instantly to sunshine and soil food, making them faster at taking up water and nutrients than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, small tubers when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water just like people sharing a small plate of food. When cassava is planted too close together, the leaves block each other from getting sunlight and the roots do not get enough room or nutrients to expand into large tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, taakɛ gbɔmɛi jaa niyenii tsɛnsii bibii lɛ. Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baabu ehe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Ni shishifãi lɛ bɛ he ko loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants stretch very tall and fall over instead of producing plenty of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need direct sunlight to grow strong stems and produce fruit. When planted in shady spots or under dense trees, they stretch upwards searching for light, which makes their stems thin and weak, leaving them with little energy to bear heavy fruits.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ewo yibii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi. baatsɔ ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Ehaa enáa hewalɛ fioo ko ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why does hard, unplowed soil slow down the growth of my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko he nii lɛ haaa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward into soft earth. If the soil is hard and compacted, the roots and tubers struggle to penetrate the ground, resulting in small, stunted, or misshapen tubers because of the physical resistance.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ewa akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii, ni egbɔjɔ loo ni esaaa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shitee-kɛ-woo hewɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if a small motorized water pump will be enough to irrigate my whole maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu pɔmp bibioo ko ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli nu?

english: Every water pump has a specific power limit for how much water it can push across a distance. If your field layout is large, a small pump will not have enough strength to deliver water to the far end of the farm, so the machinery size must match the total size and layout of your land.
ga: Nu pɔmp fɛɛ pɔmp yɛ hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni ekɛbaatsu nii kɛha nu abɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛtsɔ he ko ni jɛkɛ. Kɛji akɛ ohe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ da Pɔmpɔi bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ nu baaya ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsɔne lɛ dalɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Is it better to use a small walking tiller or hire a big tractor to prepare my large field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii loo mikɛ trakta agbo aha koni mikɛsaa miŋmɔ agbo lɛ he?

english: The size and power of farm machines must match the total land area you are working on. A small tiller is good for small garden spaces, but for a large farm, a bigger tractor works faster and has enough power to plow deep without breaking down under a heavy load.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ kɛ he fɛɛ he ni otsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ akpã gbee. Mini tillers lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha abɔɔ mli hei bibii. Shi kɛha ŋmɔji wuji lɛ Traktɔi wuji lɛ yaa oya ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii yɛ shɔŋŋ ni amɛkuuu yɛ jatsui ni tsii shishi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for essential soil food, especially nitrogen, or that the ground is flooded with water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving land drainage helps the plant make chlorophyll, which restores its green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye sũ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔŋ su kɛ dalɛ kpakpa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during hot afternoons but stand up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: On hot afternoons, crops lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. Drooping is the plant's natural way of saving water during intense heat, and it recovers in the evening as the air cools down and root water intake catches up.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Ebaatsa ehe yɛ gbɛkɛ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni nu babaoo ni shishifãi lɛ baa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they face extreme heat stress, severe lack of water, or an overdose of nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for basic survival rather than spending energy to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. nu ni faaa waa loo nitrogen fertilizer ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Even with good rainfall, weeds absorb the available soil nutrients first, leaving your crops hungry and growing slowly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛdara fiofio.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil pests and diseases to build up in that field. Rotating with legume crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and cleans out pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has the special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the soil without costing extra money for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni afite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to shield them and keep the ground moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nuɔ la he waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small and thin even though the stems above ground grow tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ ni baai lɛ hu kɛlɛ moŋ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together or receive too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground tubers. Proper spacing gives the roots room to expand.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ loo amɛná nitrogen babaoo. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ, Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa gbɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flower from forming fruit, so consistent watering and light shade during hot periods can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil to prevent disease and ensures the leaves capture enough sun to grow large tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni hela akabote mli. Ni ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulb agboi baa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when many young shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii bibii lɛ? Beni tsei bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for food, water, and sunlight. Cutting away extra shoots—leaving only one or two strong ones—allows the mother stem to put all its energy into growing a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Plantains lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii ni he wa 1-2 pɛ eshwɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda ni etsɔ panicle agbo.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te pepper tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves on the soil surface is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation after rain, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots into rich soil organic matter.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young corn leaves with soft dirt packed in the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji fioo ni eyi obɔ yɛ mfoniri lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the funnel of young corn plants and eats the leaves before they unfold. Detecting them early allows you to control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ amɛnɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these pests. Managing insects early prevents the leaf twisting from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ. Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi anɔ Enɛ baatsi baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their roots cannot absorb enough water under strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains, hot sunshine scorches the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei loo dumɔwui ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps plants turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin stems with very small, thin tubers underneath instead of big, thick roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi lɛ feɔ shishifãi wuji ni mli tse.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating holes into the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to feed on the tender young leaves inside the maize funnel. They grow quickly and need early treatment with recommended sprays or neem extracts before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ mra. kɛ neem spray loo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi dani akpataa tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoot suckers to grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain stem causes them to steal food and water from the main mother plant. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only one or two leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce big bunches.
ga: Ni aaana ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle Dumɔwu kome pɛ he lɛ baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ ato, ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tso titri lɛ baanyɛ afee panicle agbo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can take it up from the ground. This temporary wilting is the plant's way of protecting itself from drying out, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why is it risky to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the ground season after season. Alternating with crops like maize or legumes breaks this cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, efoɔ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch sunlight with their leaves to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awó sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɔ hulu la lɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: How do weeds lower the amount of food I harvest from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and aggressively consume the fertilizer, water, and space that your crops need. This starves your crops, making them small and reducing the final yield at harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei, nu, kɛ he ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii, ni ehaa naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from sprouting around your crop.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil gets flooded with water, plant roots cannot breathe or take up nitrogen. This causes the leaves to turn yellow and curl, showing that the plant is starving for air and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my yam tubers are getting enough water underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miiná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: When yam plants lack water, the vines will start wilting during the afternoon sun and the lower leaves will turn yellow prematurely before the harvest season.
ga: Beni nu bɛ sweet potato tso lɛ he lɛ Wein tsei lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do some new seed varieties mature faster than the traditional seeds I usually save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ oya fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mifɔɔ kɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to complete their growth cycle quickly so they can yield crops before short rainy seasons end or before major pests arrive.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ aná ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee loo dani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni he hiaa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but give me small underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in heavy shade, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of expanding its roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai kakadaji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods can start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face sudden stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or the sudden removal of overhead shade trees that protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔi ni baa trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ trukaa lɛ kpe.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop growing new branches after I pick the first crop of peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ niji heei kwɛ̃mɔ beni mikpa klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants use up most of their food energy to produce their first fruits. Without adding extra manure or fertilizer after harvest, the plant lacks the strength to grow new flowers and branches.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔii kɛ niji heei.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get black spots and dry up starting from the bottom leaves first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil disease called blight, which splashes from the wet ground onto the lowest leaves during watering or rain and slowly spreads upwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ late blight lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nu loo nugbɔ be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi fiofio.

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer to attack my maize crop when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua mi ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, sweet leaves that are easy for young caterpillars to eat, and the small leaves create a safe hiding place in the central funnel of the plant.
ga: Abɛi bibii tsei yɛ baai ni ŋɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aye, ni baai bibii lɛ feɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots. If planted too close together or in loose soil, their roots cannot grab the ground firmly enough to hold up the heavy weight of the fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfi aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my rice plants turn thin and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than rice and steal the fertilizer, sunlight, and water from the soil before the rice roots can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni amɛjuɔ ŋmãa, hulu la kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: What is mpampuro, and why do some farmers cover their entire piece of land with it?
ga: Mɛni ji mpampuro ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi haa amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mpampuro (bamboo) grows very fast and spreads quickly across bare ground. Farmers plant it to cover entire fields to control severe soil erosion, build live fences, restore overworked soil, or harvest the stems later for farm stakes and building materials.
ga: Mpampuro (bamboo) daa oya waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni agbele naa lɛ fɛɛ. Okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa jɛmɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkɛku shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ nɔ. ma gbogbo ni hiɛ ka Ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsu nii fe nine lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Aloo akpa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei kɛ tsumaa nibii.

english: Why do some plants spread so fast across the land compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Certain spreading plants and cover grasses put out underground runners and quick surface roots. This allows them to grab water and spread quickly across the surface, blocking out weeds faster than standard upright crops.
ga: Tsei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ jwɛi srɔtoi komɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shishifãi baa oya. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa oya fe tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: If I plant a fast-spreading cover plant across my whole farm, will it choke my soil or make it better?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Ani ebaafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ loo ebaaha efee nɔ ni hi?

english: In the short term, cover plants protect topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains and keep the earth cool. When their leaves fall and rot, they enrich the soil with organic matter, though you must clear them back properly before planting new food crops.
ga: Yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafo lɛ. ni eha je lɛ afee fɛ̃i Beni baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni ojie lɛ ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ dani odu niyenii hee moŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant trees along the edges of farm roads and pathways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsei yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ahe kɛ ŋmɔji amli gbɛjegbɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Trees along pathways serve as windbreaks that shield your crops from strong storm winds. They also mark property boundaries clearly, provide shade for farmers walking to the farm, and prevent road dust from settling on your crop leaves.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ahum ni naa wa he. Ekadiɔ shikpɔji ahe husui hu yɛ faŋŋ mli. Ha okwaafoi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ hulutsoo. ni otsi gbɛjegbɛ nɔ sũ lɛ naa koni ekamɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe.

english: Will planting big trees right beside my farm pathway take away water from my crops inside the field?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ gbɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Tree roots reach deep down into the soil to find water that shallow food crops cannot reach. As long as you keep a small space between the roadside trees and your field crops, they will protect the land without stealing crop moisture.
ga: Tso shishifãi shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu ni niyenii tsei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Shii abɔ ni obaaha gbɛ bibioo ko ahi gbɛjegbɛ he tsei kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ Tsei nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛjuuu nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: How do shade trees along the farm border affect food crops growing close to them?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji husui lɛ ahe lɛ saa niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Border trees reduce hot afternoon sun and keep humidity in the air, which helps crops like cocoa or young plantains stay fresh. However, if they grow too thick, you must trim high branches so your food crops still get enough light.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu lɛ baa shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo plantains bibii lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ amɛmli tsɔ lɛ, Esa akɛ Ofolɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli koni oniyenii tsei lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo.

english: Why do government forest officers encourage farmers to plant forest trees on agricultural land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli onukpai woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu koo mli tsei yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji anɔ lɛ?

english: Forest trees help bring back rainfall, improve soil fertility through leaf drop, and shade crops during extreme heat. Officers distribute them so farmers can grow crops and valuable timber together sustainably.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ. ni amɛha tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa Amralofoi lɛ jaa amɛ koni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei ni jara wa yɛ gbɛ ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant tree seedlings given to us by forestry officers from my main food crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu tsei bibii ni koo mli onukpai lɛ kɛha wɔ kɛjɛ miniyenii titri ni miduɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should plant forest trees at least 10 to 12 meters apart from light-sensitive food crops like cassava or corn. This spacing gives crop roots enough room to grow without being overcrowded by tree shade.
ga: Esa akɛ odu koo mli tsei kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 10 kɛyashi 12 kɛjɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa hulu kpɛɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhaaa tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe nine.

english: Can planting shade trees on my farm help my crop soil stay wet during the dry season?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, shade trees lower ground temperatures by blocking direct sunlight. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly into the air, helping the ground stay moist for much longer during hot, dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How do tree roots deep in the soil help the smaller food crops growing on top?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii tsei bibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Deep tree roots pump water and underground minerals up to the surface leaves. When those leaves fall onto the ground and decay, they deposit those rich nutrients right where the shallow roots of your food crops can feed on them.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ pɔmpiɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shika tsuru kɛyaa baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nakai baai lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛgboi lɛ Ekɛ nakai niyenii kpakpai lɛ toɔ he ni oniyenii tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I harvest my cocoa pods by roughly pulling or beating them off the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛtsɔ amɛ ni mikɛgbalaa loo mikɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Roughly pulling or beating pods damages the flower cushions on the trunk. This creates open wounds that can attract diseases, weaken the tree, or even cause the cocoa tree to die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ogbala loo otswa pod lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni mli tse ni baanyɛ agbala helai srɔtoi aba. egbɔjɔ tso lɛ loo eha kookoo tso lɛ po agbo.

english: What is the best way to pluck cocoa pods off the tree without harming it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni ayeee amɛ awui?

english: You should use a sharp tool like a cocoa sickle or cutlass to cut the pod stem cleanly, leaving the bark and flower cushion on the tree intact so it can grow pods again.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ dɛŋdade ni naa wa, tamɔ kookoo kakla loo kakla kuku, afo pod lɛ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shi tso lɛ he tsitsii kɛ fɔfɔii akushin lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can bad harvesting methods really kill a full-grown cocoa tree?
ga: Ani gbɛi ni ejaaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbe cacao tsei ni eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, if you strip off the bark or break the flowering points while harvesting, you wound the tree severely, which stops future growth and can lead to the tree dying.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ojie tso lɛ yibii lɛ loo ogbala fɔfɔii lɛ amli hei lɛ beni okpaa nii lɛ. Obaapila tso lɛ waa. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa wɔsɛɛ, ni ekolɛ ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Can I harvest my cocoa pods whenever I have time, or is there a specific right time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii be fɛɛ be ni be loo be ni sa baashɛ?

english: There is a specific time to harvest cocoa pods. Harvesting at the right time ensures the beans are mature and prevents damage to the tree's natural flowering cycle.
ga: Be pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ daa, ni ehaaa tso lɛ fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ afite.

english: Does cocoa produce pods all year round or does it happen in seasons?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ woɔ yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo amɛbaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli?

english: Cocoa production follows a two-phase cycle each year, usually consisting of a major harvest season and a minor harvest season.
ga: Cocoa feemɔ yɛ fãi enyɔ ni yaa nɔ daa afi. Bei pii lɛ, shishijee kpamɔ be kɛ kpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to go back to harvest my cocoa farm in phases rather than all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maku misɛɛ kɛya ni mayakpa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ shikome shikome moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods do not all ripen at the same time. Cocoa yields in two distinct phases, so you must harvest periodically as pods reach maturity.
ga: Jeee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kome mli. Afeɔ kookoo yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okpa be kɛ bei amli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How does a cocoa tree produce flowers again after I finish harvesting?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ akpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees bloom from small spots on the trunk called flower cushions. If these cushions are kept safe during harvest, the tree naturally flowers and blooms again for the next season.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ hei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ fɔfɔii akutsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ kushɛnii nɛɛ to shweshweeshwe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa trees fail to bloom again after a harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If the flowering points on the trunk are damaged or scraped off during harvest, the tree loses its ability to produce new blooms in those spots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ efite loo ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Tso lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi heei yɛ nakai hei lɛ.

english: What naturally causes cocoa trees to flower again after plucking the ripe pods?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni ajie amɛ ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have an inherent growth pattern where removing mature pods gently allows the tree to direct energy into its next blooming phase.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ yɛ bɔ ni edaa ehaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ pods momo lɛ mligbalamɔ blɛoo nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ kɛya fɔmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: My cocoa farm looks very green and healthy, so how do I keep it productive for long?
ga: Mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ minitsumɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Keeping a cocoa farm productive requires harvesting at the correct mature stage, avoiding damage to the tree trunk, and respecting its two natural harvest phases.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ ni akpa yɛ be ni sa mli ni edaa lɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni efiteɔ lɛ he. ni abu adebɔɔ mli ŋmaakpamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I remove all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Big shade trees protect them from harsh heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the growing center of the corn plant where leaves are soft. Catching them early with appropriate control measures keeps them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ. Amɔmɔ mra Gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning watery and rotting if I leave them in wet ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays soaked with water for too long during heavy rains, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ egbo ni egbo.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when they face extreme heat stress or lack water. When the plant feels stressed by bad weather conditions, it drops flowers to conserve energy so it can survive.
ga: Tomato baafɔ fɔfɔii ashwie shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo latsaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni esaaa lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots to anchor them in the soil; their roots grow shallowly. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, so you need to support the stem with a wooden prop stick to keep it upright.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaha amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ dara fioo. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ bafeɔ tsiimɔ lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ tso afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground, also called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil, protects plant roots from hot sun, and stops weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛmɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Buu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii.

english: Yam leaves need to catch maximum sunlight to make food that builds the big tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves off hot ground and spreads them out to collect sun easily.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaagbɛ eshwa mlɛo koni hulu la ashɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested corn grains turn into fine powder after sitting in my store room for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa beni mita nitoohe lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects called weevils eat into the dry corn and lay eggs inside. Storing corn in airtight bags or treating grains with safe storage protectants stops these pests from destroying your harvest.
ga: Picker kooloi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmãa toɔ vacuum kotokui amli loo akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ ŋmãa lɛ he nii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ. Ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it safely. Put on dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer sucks water out of roots instead of feeding them, which burns and damages the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ koni ejie nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni oooha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ashã ni efite nii.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rain season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu nii beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil is still hot underneath and can dry out quickly. Wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains so there is enough moisture trapped in the ground to help your seeds sprout and stay alive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni ebaanyɛ egbi oya. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants native to the soil, so their roots are already established and ready to drink water instantly. Your cultivated crops need extra time to adapt, so clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to drink the water and nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ etswa shi momo ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaanu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei ni okɛwo mli lɛ he miihia be kroko koni amɛtsake amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when the hot sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides early shade to shield the young leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantain loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba mra. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp soil, exposing them to light while preventing ground diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Feemɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ la ni oooha ehi shi lɛ nɔ, ni otsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing large, heavy plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over so easily whenever a rain storm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are too shallow or the soil around the base is too soft. Heap extra soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) when the plants are knee-high to build a strong anchor against wind and rain.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ. Okɛ sũ kroko abɔle tso lɛ shishi (shwie shi) beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaneshi lɛ koni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa ni baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the tuber, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there is an imbalance of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on the stem and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Sprinkling wood ash or using appropriate organic sprays can help keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ shwie nɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why is my maize growing tall dark green leaves but producing very tiny cobs?
