ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi toi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Giving maize too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus entirely on leaf growth instead of grain growth. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium gives the plant the right food to build big, full cobs.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ moŋ fe dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are tiny flies on my pepper plants making the leaves curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ mi pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Those small insects, often whiteflies or aphids, suck the sap from your plants and transmit viruses. As they feed, they weaken the leaves, causing them to curl and turn yellow like an infection spreading across the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii. Emuɔ tsei amli nu ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ mɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Baai lɛ efee blɛoo. Enɛ haa ebɔleɔ ehe ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does one diseased cassava plant cause the rest of my farm to get sick so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni hela emɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yeɔ hela oya lɛ?

english: Crop diseases like cassava mosaic are spread by insects that feed on the sick plant and then fly to healthy ones. Rain droplets and wind can also carry disease spores from one plant to another very quickly.
ga: Tsei ahe helai tamɔ yucca mosaic lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfoɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko nɔ oya.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear in huge numbers on my corn farm right after a short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay hidden eggs on the undersides of leaves before the rains. When the air becomes warm and moist, hundreds of eggs hatch at the exact same time into hungry caterpillars like the fall armyworm.
ga: Kplukai woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛteeɔ baai ashishi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ohai abɔ feɔ ekome kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli.

english: Why do black spots on a few cocoa pods spread to the rest of the pods on the tree so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo komɛi anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ oya lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp conditions. Raindrops bouncing off an infected pod splash invisible fungal spores onto neighboring pods, causing the rot to spread rapidly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei mli ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ anɔ kɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi amɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Plants behave this way when the soil has too much nitrogen, which promotes stem and leaf growth, but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are the nutrients plants need to build large, healthy corn ears.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa Shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem instead of turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato flowers cannot pollinate properly. The plant sheds the unfertilized flowers to conserve its energy and water during stressful weather.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and dry up when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective canopies that keep the ground moist and shelter cocoa leaves from heat burn while their roots are still small.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together so I can get more harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from each other, leaving all the plants weak and producing smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than the cassava crop I planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmei tso ni miduɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants designed to survive harsh conditions. Their root systems absorb available water and fertilizers much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder inside the storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils burrow inside dry maize kernels to lay eggs. The growing larvae eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind only damaged husks and powdery dust.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwuji. Lala ni miida lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo ni efite lɛ kɛ sũ pɛ.

english: I heard mango farming brings a lot of quick money, so can I just plant the trees and leave them to yield without much daily work?
ga: Minu akɛ, kɛ́ afee mango lɛ, anáa shika oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu ni ashi ni ewo yibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsu nitsumɔ babaoo daa gbi?

english: Mango farming requires continuous physical labor and active management, including regular pruning, pest monitoring, weed clearing, and dry-season watering. Without effort and sweat, the trees will yield low-quality fruit or get destroyed by pests.
ga: Mango okwaayeli biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ daa kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ. Nɔ ni fata he ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asɛɛdii jwɛi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli Kɛji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ latsaa bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baawo yibii ni ehiii loo nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants take longer to produce big roots when I plant stem cuttings taken from very young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani shishifãi wuji shwereɔ beni miduɔ tso bibioo ko ni afolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cuttings from soft, young cassava plants lack the stored food energy and mature buds needed for fast growth, whereas stems taken from mature plants aged 8 to 12 months have stored nutrients to sprout strong roots quickly.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ni darako lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni eda ni he hiaa koni amɛdara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ daraa oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or too much water around the roots, both of which stop the plant from producing the green food-making pigment it needs to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection behavior where the plant shrinks its exposed leaf surface to stop water from evaporating too quickly under extreme sun and heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ koni nu lɛ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young orange trees drop tiny green fruits onto the ground long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop occurs when a tree faces water stress, extreme heat, or pest attack, forcing the tree to shed excess fruit it cannot support with its limited supply of food and water.
ga: Yibii ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ jieɔ yibii ni fa fe nine ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in full sunlight, which is why fast-growing shade plants like plantains are needed to protect them during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni shade tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ abu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I plant my tomato seedlings very close to each other, won't I get a bigger total harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo ni da fe no nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stems with few small fruits instead of a heavy, healthy harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: What happens if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients completely and allows soil pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛfa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even after I apply expensive fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can, so adding fertilizer to a grassy field feeds the weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ aye nii moŋ fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying even when the soil is wet and there are no insects visible on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni kooloi komɛi ejeee kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Underground pests like root-knot nematodes or soil fungi may be attacking the root system beneath the dirt, preventing the plant from taking up water from the soil to feed its leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ root knot nematodes loo shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha amɛbaai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside them keeps the soil moist and protects the tender leaves from burning until the trees are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover and naturally restores nutrients.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛ ehe baawo mli ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil if I do not harvest them before the heavy rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess rain makes the soil waterlogged, which prevents air from reaching the cassava roots. Waterlogged roots easily attract rotting fungi and bacteria, so harvesting mature cassava before severe flooding occurs prevents losses.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ abua ŋmei ni eda lɛ naa dani nu afua ni naa wa aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɔ ko.

english: Yams are climbing plants, and lifting their leaves off the ground allows them to catch maximum sunlight. This extra sunlight helps the plant produce more energy to grow bigger underground tubers, while keeping leaves away from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato ni kwɔɔ tso nɔ Ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Nɛkɛ hulu la ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets excessively hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Ensuring consistent watering during the flowering phase helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na be ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. Controlling these pests early stops leaf damage and protects fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebuɔ aduawai lɛ adalɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops the sun from evaporating soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during heat, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ latsaa be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, won't I get more total yield from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni jɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mliyaa?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop fully and produce a larger overall harvest.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts together with maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When groundnut roots rot in the soil, they release this extra nitrogen, naturally fertilizing neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kpo. Enɛ baaha tsei ni tamɔ nakai tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ aha kooloi niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why can't I just save seeds from my harvest to plant next season instead of buying new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Improved or hybrid seeds are bred for high performance in their first generation. Replanting saved seeds causes the crop to lose its strength, grow unevenly, and produce significantly lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni ooodu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahe ajɔ amɛ. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni eha nibii ni afee lɛ ba shi waa.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year when I keep replanting seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaai ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Over successive seasons, saved seeds naturally lose their genetic purity and accumulate hidden seed-borne diseases, causing the crop's vigor and yield to decrease over time.
ga: yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii ahe tsemɔ ni amɛbuaa helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is there really a difference between seeds bought from certified dealers and grains bought from the local market?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaraa ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ kɛ ŋmaa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, certified seeds are scientifically cleaned, tested for high germination rates, and treated against pests, whereas market grains may have poor germination or carry diseases into your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsumɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe yɛ jeŋ nilee gbɛ nɔ. Kaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ akwɛ ni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo ekɛ helai aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean when people say a crop variety has been modified by researchers in a lab?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɔ akɛ niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ laboratori ko mli lɛ tsake tsei ahenɔi lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: It means scientists have introduced specific helpful traits into the plant's makeup—such as resistance to a destructive pest or extreme heat—so it can grow better in your field.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ sui ni he hiaa ewo tso lɛ mli, tamɔ bɔ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Bɔni afee ni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɛŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat food crops that come from scientific research centers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee ni jɛ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ?

english: Yes, crop varieties developed by researchers undergo strict health and environmental safety tests to ensure they are nutritious and completely safe for human consumption before reaching farmers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ tsɔɔ shihilɛ mli hewalɛnamɔ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kaai ni mli wa mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛhe yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha adesai niyenii dani akɛmajeɔ okwaafoi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and hang down during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in intense heat to reduce their exposure to sunlight and minimize water loss. If they bounce back in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Shi ni egbee shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive dry spells better than my local traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ hɔmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Certain improved varieties are selected for deep root systems or efficient water usage, allowing them to draw moisture from deeper in the soil when rains stop unexpectedly.
ga: Ahala tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo bɔ ni amɛkɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: How do improved crop varieties naturally fight off pests without heavy spraying?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ awuu ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofa ni mli wa shwieee nɔ?

english: Breeder varieties are selected to have natural defense traits, such as thicker leaf surfaces or natural repelling compounds, making it harder for insects to feed on or damage the plant.
ga: Ahalaa fɔlɔi kɛha adebɔɔ mli sui ni buɔ mɔ he, tamɔ baa hewolo ni mli wa loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ hela naa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa koolooi akɛ amɛaaye loo amɛfite tsei.

english: How can I check if seeds saved in my barn will actually grow before I spend energy planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni ato yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani mikɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛdu amɛ?

english: Place ten seeds in a moist cloth in a warm area for five days; if at least eight sprout, the seeds are healthy, but if fewer sprout, it is best to get fresh certified seeds.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma awo mama ni mli efɔ mli yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii enumɔ. Kɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, 8 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ shweremɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored crop seeds even when I keep them inside dry sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni egbi amli moŋ?

english: Microscopic insect eggs are often already inside the seeds before you harvest them. Unless seeds are treated or stored in airtight hermetic bags, those eggs hatch and destroy the grain from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli momo dani okpa amɛ. ja atsu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii loo akɛto vacuum bag mli. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong; when it runs short, the plant pulls whatever nitrogen it has left out of its old bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ efo mli lɛ, tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tso hee ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people say I should plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds your maize crop without you needing to spend extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni okɛ shika kroko tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll up tightly into straws during the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against heat and drought. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its surface area from the hot sun, trapping moisture inside and reducing the amount of water lost through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehiɛ fã ko teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flower blossoms without growing any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air gets too hot or when soil water suddenly drops. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming tiny, crinkled, and bunched together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii, ebɔle ehe, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves. As they suck out the juices, they inject viruses that stop the leaves from expanding normally.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ahewɔ. Beni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ Akɛ hela ko woɔ amɛmli koni ekpa baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my mature cocoa pods turning black and hard right on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, shaded conditions. When heavy rain stays trapped under thick branches without air movement, the fungus infects and ruins the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiimɔ bɛ mli lɛ ahe. Fuji lɛ tsɛŋeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around the roots for too long in heavy, poor-draining soil. Excess water cuts off air to the roots, allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ daa tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put up wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni mato niji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers by using sunlight captured through their leaves. Lifting the leaves high on tall stakes exposes them to maximum sunlight while keeping them safe from pests and damp soil diseases below.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why did the seeds I buried very deep in the soil fail to sprout and come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛfu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ekwɛko lɛ?

english: Seeds have a limited amount of stored food energy inside them. If buried too deep, the young sprout runs out of energy pushing through the heavy soil before it reaches the surface light, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ niyenii hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ baaho dani eshɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are my orange trees dropping young green fruits before they get the chance to grow big and ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli dani enáa hegbɛ ni eda ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop excess young fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them, or when attacked by fruit flies. It is the tree's way of lightening its load so it can survive.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo yibii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua lɛ Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jatsu ni kã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains around them acts like natural umbrellas, protecting the young leaves from scorching heat and keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer upper leaves to survive, leaving the older bottom leaves starved of nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Shi shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of pushing them straight down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at an angle helps the roots spread out sideways near the surface where the soil is soft and fertile, making it easier for the plant to produce larger and longer tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ, ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛ baawo bulb agbo ni kɛlɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just growing along the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight to feed the tuber underground, while also keeping the leaves away from wet soil where diseases and rot spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he he ni hela kɛ fitemɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main plantain tree. Pruning them away leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring the main tree gets enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It damages the plant's leaves, preventing it from making food properly and leading to a much smaller harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Efiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ahoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Ni ekɛ kpamɔ bibioo kwraa baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my groundnut plants push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. Once the flower on top is pollinated, it grows a small stem called a peg that burrows down into the soil where the actual nuts can safely develop.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaafee ŋmei bibioo ko. ni atsɛɔ lɛ pins Enɛ baafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without turning into any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: When the temperature gets too high and moisture is low, tomato plants experience heat stress. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water, which prevents new tomatoes from forming.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Enɛ baatsi tomatoi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in heavy moisture and cool shade. Pruning surplus branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ mli kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the soil too fast, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why do some farmers cut or trim the husk of a coconut seed nut before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi foɔ loo amɛfoɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔi dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming the outer husk near the soft spot (the eye) allows water to reach deep inside the nut more easily, helping the coconut absorb moisture quickly and sprout much faster.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ he ni egbɔjɔ (hiŋmɛi lɛ) lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo akɛ nu lɛ baashɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa.

english: What are the small dark spots or 'eyes' on a coconut nut used for when growing new trees?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii diji bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛduɔ tsei heei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The eyes are the natural soft points on the hard shell where the new sprout emerges. Exposing or cutting near these eyes helps water enter the seed to trigger growth.
ga: Hiŋmɛii ji adebɔɔ mli he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni wa lɛ nɔ he ni tsei heei baa lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi loo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ hiŋmɛii nɛɛ baaha nu abote dumɔwu lɛ mli koni eha eda.

english: Is it safe to cut into the outer husk of my coconut seed, or will I spoil the plant inside?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafolɔ ŋmei ŋmei kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli? Aloo ebaafite akokoso tso lɛ?

english: It is safe as long as you only trim the fibrous outer husk near the eye area without damaging the inner seed. Slicing that spot actually helps the seed drink water and develop faster.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ ofo fibrous kponɔgbɛ fã ni bɔle ohiŋmɛii ahe lɛ pɛ. ni efiteee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ He ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How should I prepare dry mature coconuts before placing them into my seedbed?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ dani mikɛwo ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Slice off a small portion of the husk at the top end near the eyes, which allows the dry nut to drink enough water when you irrigate, helping it sprout quickly.
ga: Shĩmɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii. yɛ ŋwɛi naagbee ni bɛŋkɛ hiŋmɛi lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ nuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ okɛ nu wo amɛmli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How can I get my coconut seed nuts to sprout faster in my nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: You can trim a piece of the husk right over the eye of the coconut. This allows the nut to take in water much faster, which speeds up the whole germination process.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo ŋmei lɛ ŋmei lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ oya kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ yaa oya.

english: How does a coconut seed manage to drink water through such a hard outer shell?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei dumɔwui nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Water enters primarily through the soft 'eye' of the coconut shell. When you cut open the thick husk above the eye, water travels deep into the nut much more easily.
ga: Nu baatsɔ ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ nɔ titri. Kɛji ogbe ŋmei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hiŋmɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ baabote ŋmei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why is regular watering so important for my newly prepared coconut seedbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔji heei ni asaa he lɛ?

english: Coconut seeds need water to penetrate deep through the eye area; getting sufficient moisture directly to the inside allows the nut to develop its shoot rapidly.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmei dumɔwui koni amɛbote hiŋmɛii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli tɛ̃ɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: Why do some of my planted coconuts take months to sprout while others come up quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ ekomɛi heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, ni ekomɛi hu daa oya lɛ?

english: Coconuts sprout at different speeds based on how easily water reaches the germinating eye. Seeds prepared by cutting the husk near the eye absorb water better and grow much faster than untreated ones.
ga: Kokooi baakwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni nu baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmeii ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ ahe mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni asaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni atsuuu he nii.

english: What actually happens inside the coconut seed after water reaches deep into the eye?
ga: Mɛni baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli beni nu ebote hiŋmɛi lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Once water gets deep through the eye, it hydrates the young embryo inside, softening the environment so the plant can grow and push its first green shoot upward.
ga: Kɛ nu bote hiŋmɛii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ Ebaaha fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli aná ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ yaa ŋwɛi.

english: Does trimming the husk of my coconut seed nuts help them survive during hot dry spells?
ga: Ani akooshi dumɔwui ahe tsɔi ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cutting near the eye allows the seed to drink in maximum water whenever you water the nursery, keeping the internal plant hydrated and growing even when weather is warm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofolɔ dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ nu babaoo be fɛɛ be ni obaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔhe lɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa nu ni amɛshwereɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ po.

english: Why do my mango tree flowers keep falling off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers can drop due to strong winds, insect pests, or a lack of water during flowering. Keeping the soil moist during blooming and protecting young trees from wind helps flowers stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ, ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves near the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore green leaves and improves yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Underground cassava rot usually happens when water gets trapped around the roots in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw calcium up to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: How does heavy rain cause my cocoa pods to turn black and spoil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kookoo diŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ?

english: Heavy rainfall and damp conditions allow fungal spores to spread rapidly, causing Black Pod disease. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets in sunlight and wind to dry the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Ekɛ black pod hela baa Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa pod lɛ mli gĩɔ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crops compete with one another for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper field spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to mature and produce larger harvests.
ga: planted too close Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does covering the ground with dry leaves help my crops during the hot season?
ga: Te baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around crops with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, shields the earth from the burning sun. This keeps the soil moist longer and reduces the amount of water your crops need.
ga: Mulching ni bɔleɔ Dumɔwui ahe kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ye obua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do small caterpillars appear on my crop leaves mostly after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain triggers many adult moths to lay eggs on fresh green foliage, which hatch into caterpillars shortly after. Scouting your fields regularly after rain helps you catch and remove pests before they cause widespread damage.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ eha ŋmeii babaoo ewo amɛwuji yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmɔji ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni ojie amɛ dani amɛfite nii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing when the field gets too crowded with weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your pepper plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Can I prune my fruit trees to encourage them to produce more yield next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ koni mawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, removing dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches allows sunlight to reach inner leaves and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy new shoots and extra fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii heei kɛ aduawai krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or water. When nutrients are low, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo nu. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do some farmers put dry grass around the base of their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing around your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: Cassava plants spaced too closely will fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants with small, poor roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii ni ehiii yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller trees like plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Taller plants provide shade and humidity, acting as protection while the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Ebuɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight. More sunlight on the leaves helps the plant create more energy, which grows bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotting inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when the soil stays too wet due to poor drainage during heavy rains, allowing fungal diseases to attack and decay the roots underground.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my chili pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa chili pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on the leaves and pass viral diseases to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does removing weeds around my vegetable crops help them grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Removing them ensures your vegetables get all the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha o-vegetables lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunshine because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from heat stress and keeps the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2-3 lɛ mli

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and high humidity. Clearing weeds and pruning extra shade trees helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ahe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores this vital nutrient to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they release this free nitrogen into the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛtsu nii.

english: Why is my farm yielding less food every year even though I plant on the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting year after year without adding manure, crop rotation, or resting the land leaves the soil empty of nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Dumɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsake loo okɛ sũ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akafee sũ lɛ.

english: What is causing small worms to chew holes in my maize leaves and leave green dirt in the centers?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ekɛ bu ko shwie mi-corn baa lɛ mli ni eshi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They hide deep inside the growing leaves of maize plants, requiring early application of recommended treatments or neem liquid to control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ̀i ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Aloo okɛ neem nu atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants get dark spots and wither away early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is leaf blight, a disease caused by fungi in the soil. Raindrops splash soil onto the bottom leaves, spreading the fungus. Mulching around the base with dry grass helps prevent rain from splashing soil onto the leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji blight, hela ko ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwie muji lɛ nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ Sũ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of straight upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ moŋ fe ni ooodamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanted angle encourages roots to spread shallowly and horizontally. This gives the tubers room to grow larger and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ ŋwɛi fɛɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and produce very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Leaving weeds in your farm deprives your crops of what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know if the ground is wet enough for planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall usually only wets the top surface. You should wait until steady rains soak the top layer of soil thoroughly so seeds have enough deep moisture to sprout without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be, ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why can't I just save seeds from my current harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from high-yielding or hybrid crops lose their special strength in the next generation. Planting harvested seeds will result in weak plants, mixed quality, and much smaller harvests. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures you get the same strong, high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ, nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni mli wa, ni nɔ kwɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a seed variety requires me to buy new seeds every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi?

english: Look for seed packets labeled 'Hybrid' or 'F1'. These varieties are specially bred to produce a high yield for only one season, so you must purchase new certified seeds each planting time to keep getting that high performance.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ 'Hybrid' loo 'F1'. Atsɔse nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli be fɛɛ be ni obaadu lɛ koni oya nɔ owo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it always better to buy store-bought seeds instead of getting seeds from my neighbor's farm?
ga: Ani ehi be fɛɛ be akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli fe dumɔwui ni jɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are tested to be clean, disease-free, and high-yielding. Seeds taken from a neighbor's harvest may carry diseases or have lost their original strength, which can lead to poor growth and smaller crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛhe tse, hela bɛ mli, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko kpamɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná hela loo amɛshishijee hewalɛ lɛ baaje mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aba.

english: Why do certified high-yielding seeds cost more money at the agro-dealer shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odase lɛ jara wa yɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds go through years of scientific breeding, testing, and quality control. They are also treated with protective coatings to prevent insect damage and disease during germination, which makes them produce far more food than untreated local seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ jeŋ nilee mli fɔmɔ, kaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli afii babaoo. Agbɛnɛ hu, amɛnáa nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe koni kooloi bibii kɛ helai akafite amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni atsuuu he nii.

english: How can I test if the high-yielding seeds I bought are healthy before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth or moist newspaper for a few days. If 8 or 9 seeds sprout, the seed batch is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ loo adafitswaa wolo ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: What makes these improved seed varieties give a much bigger harvest than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi maŋbii akusum dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred by scientists to focus their energy on producing large grains or fruits, growing faster, and resisting common local pests, whereas traditional seeds spend more energy just surviving.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi baadu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ. shwereɔ oya ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni blema dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest, why do the plants grow tall but produce very small cobs?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daa shi amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens because hybrid seeds lose their special genetic balance after the first harvest. The second-generation plants break down, leading to uneven growth, empty husks, or very small cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ nii krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ gbee shi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do high-yielding crop varieties need more fertilizer and care compared to my old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto midumɔwui momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: High-yielding crops grow very fast and produce heavily, which means they consume nutrients much faster than local crops. They need proper fertilizer and water to fuel that rapid growth and reach their full yield potential.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei nɛɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni sa koni ewo amɛdalɛ oya kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my traditional crop varieties survive dry weather better than the fast-growing high-yield varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishijee tsei srɔtoi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni daa oya lɛ?

english: Traditional varieties have adapted over many decades to survive tough local conditions like drought, but they yield less. High-yielding varieties are designed primarily for food production, so they need steady water to perform well.
ga: Kusum mli tsofai srɔtoi lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai tamɔ hɔmɔ mli, shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Afee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ titri kɛha niyenii feemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ nu atsu nii daa koni yibii kpakpai aba.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I mix saved seeds with newly bought certified seeds in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui heei ni ahe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ futu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: The plants will grow at different speeds, flower at different times, and produce uneven yields. This makes it difficult to apply fertilizer, manage pests, or harvest your crop efficiently.
ga: Tsei daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli ni yibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ loo onibii ni akpaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together on my land, won't I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo ejaakɛ tsei babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and tiny ears of corn. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and yield the maximum amount of grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ oha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni edara waa ni ewo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: How do I know the right amount of maize seed to buy for my one-acre farm here in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa dumɔwui ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Every crop has a maximum density that one acre can support without overcrowding. For maize, recommended spacing requires about 8 to 10 kilograms of seed per acre. Buying and planting more than this wastes money and reduces your overall harvest quality.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe fɛɛ ni acre kome baanyɛ ashɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ mli. kɛha ŋmãa He ni atsɔɔ akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ biɔ aaafee dumɔwui kilogram 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ acre kome mli. Kɛ́ mɔ ko he ni edu nɔ ni fe enɛ lɛ, ebaafee shika ni efiteɔ. ni okɛ okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ mlihilɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I pull out healthy seedlings when two or three grow out of the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Beni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ bu kome mli

english: This practice is called thinning. When multiple seedlings grow in one hole, their roots tangle and starve each other of food and water; removing all but the strongest seedling leaves one healthy plant that produces much more food than three struggling ones would.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ, ja nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo niyenii babaoo fe tsei etɛ ni miibɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin like sticks without producing much fruit when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei niji shi ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make energy for fruiting. When shaded by big trees, the tomato plants stretch upward looking for light instead of using their strength to produce flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo. Kɛji akɛ amɛyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛtao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ tomato.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to tie tomato plants to wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps plants upright so every leaf gets enough sunlight and fresh air. It also lifts fruits off the wet ground, protecting them from soil diseases, rot, and insects.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe. fitemɔ kɛ kooloi bibii hu

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow even though there is plenty of land space around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani he ko babaoo ebɔle ehe?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or that the roots cannot access water. Just like farm animals, crops need enough nutrients in the soil to stay healthy and green.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛna nu. Nakai eji yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi hu ahe. Tsei hia niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: Why did my groundnut yield drop this season even though I used the same piece of land as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut yibiiwoo lɛ eba shi yɛ afi nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific plant foods from the soil. Rotating your crops or adding organic manure restores soil nutrients so future crops can yield well.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei aniyenii komɛi aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the yam plants I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe sweet potato tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to fight aggressively for nutrients, water, and space. If you do not clear them early, they steal the soil food meant for your yams, causing your tubers to stay small.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe esa waa yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko he tawuu mli kɛji ojieee amɛ oya. Ebaaju niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Ha oyitso afee bibioo.

english: Can I plant pepper and cassava on the same small patch of land without them spoiling each other?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani obaanyɛ ofee nakai nɔŋŋ ni ofiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them if spaced correctly. Because pepper matures quickly and cassava takes longer and grows tall, planting them together works well as long as the cassava leaves do not shade the pepper plants too early.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofo amɛ kɛji akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja. Ejaakɛ pepper daa oya hewɔ lɛ, Cassava heɔ be babaoo ni ekwɛɔ. Hefatalɔi adumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ haaa ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and look tired during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a natural survival defense. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss from direct heat, helping it save moisture until cooler evening hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ wala mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ

english: How are modern farming methods different from the traditional ways my family has always used in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ blema gbɛi ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: Modern farming uses planned techniques like soil testing, precise plant spacing, crop rotation, and controlled watering rather than relying solely on traditional hand tools and unpredictable rain patterns, helping crops produce higher yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ okwaayeli kɛ gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ kaa kɛ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Nibii ni aduɔ atsakeɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ blema nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, Eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do crops grow better when planted in neat rows instead of scattering seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every crop its own space to get enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with nearby plants, while also making it easier to weed and manage water.
ga: Row planting haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe ni ekɛnáa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu he nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Does adopting modern farming practices mean I have to rely only on expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ anɔ?

english: No, modern farming also emphasizes improved natural methods like crop rotation, using compost, and planting nitrogen-fixing crops to feed the soil alongside or in place of commercial fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli hu maa adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni aya hiɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ mi. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen fiɔ shi lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe loo yɛ amɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I invest in a water management system instead of just waiting for the rain to fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shika awo nu he gbɛjianɔtoo mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛkɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa?

english: Rains in Ghana can be unpredictable, but managing your own water source ensures your crops get steady moisture when they need it most, allowing you to farm year-round and harvest even during dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ko ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ. Shi bo diɛŋtsɛ onu jɛɛhe lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni okpaa nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: How can I prepare my land to retain more water in the soil during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni ehiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, which shields the earth from direct sunlight and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaaa nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How can I store rainwater on my farm so I have water available when the rain stops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Koni oná nu ni okɛtsu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: You can dig simple farm ponds, create water retention pits, or use catchment tanks to collect heavy rainfall runoff so you have a backup supply during dry weeks.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Tsɔɔmɔ nutoohe Aloo okɛ nu ŋtayaa atsu nii ni okɛbua nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Bɔni afee ni oná nu jɛɛhe ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is drip irrigation and how does it work for small-scale crop farming?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? Ni te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Drip irrigation uses thin pipes or hoses with tiny holes to deliver water directly to the base of each plant drop by drop, delivering moisture right to the roots without wasting water.
ga: Drip irrigation kɛ paipi loo hose bibioo ko ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ nu lɛ yaa tso fɛɛ tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ, ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛhaa shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu fiteee lɛ nɔ.
