english: What preparations should I make on sloping land to prevent heavy rains from washing away my topsoil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ masaa yɛ mi gɔŋji lɛ anɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig contour trenches or plant grass strips across the slope to slow down running rainwater, giving it time to soak into the ground instead of sweeping away fertile soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa ŋmeii loo odu jwɛi yɛ gɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ nu lɛ akafee mlɛo. Ha lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from too much water versus not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni fa babaoo loo nu ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Crops with too little water will have dry, curling, or wilting leaves, while crops sitting in too much water will develop yellowing leaves, soggy stems, and rotted roots due to lack of air in the soil.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbi, amɛkpãtã, loo amɛgbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ baaná baai ni tsuɔ, amɛshishifãi ni efɔ, kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon heat even if I water them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon sun, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil; watering deeply at the root level early in the morning or late in the evening helps reduce heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni oooha kɛyashɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded areas while cocoa trees die in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei gboiɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal channels that allow oxygen to reach their roots even when submerged in water. Cocoa roots need oxygen directly from well-drained soil, so standing water suffocates the roots and causes rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ shɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli po. Cocoa shishifãi biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if water stays trapped on my land after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nu ŋmɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: When excess water stays on the field without draining, it starves crop roots of oxygen, yellowing the leaves and creating an ideal environment for fungal diseases like black pod in cocoa.
ga: Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant rice on dry, high land where cocoa usually grows?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu omɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nɔ kwɔ ni aduɔ kookoo yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Most rice varieties require low-lying, swampy land or heavy soil that retains moisture. Planting wetland rice on high, dry cocoa land will cause the plants to dry up and fail to produce grain unless you plant specialized upland rice.
ga: Omɔ henɔi babaoo biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui. Ja odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: Why is it so hard for me to maintain three or four different farm plots at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Different crops require unique care schedules for weeding, spraying, and harvesting. Splitting your time across too many fields makes it difficult to manage pests and weeds promptly, leading to lower yields on all plots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ, jwɛi ni ashwieɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa. Be babaoo ni akɛyeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: How do I decide how many crops I should grow in a single season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ tsei enyiɛ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ be kome mli lɛ he?

english: Focus on the amount of labor, water access, and money you have available. It is often more profitable to fully care for one main crop like cocoa and one food crop like rice than to overstretch your effort across many plots.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nitsumɔ babaoo nɔ ni onáa nu kɛ shika ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo fe mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ shikpɔji babaoo anɔ.

english: Why do weeds take over my crops so fast when I split my time between cocoa and rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya beni mijaraa mibe lɛ mli miwoɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and take advantage of any delay in farming activities. If you are away tending to rice fields, weeds quickly steal nutrients, sunlight, and water from your cocoa trees.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛkɛ sɛɛkuu yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji oje kpo oyakwɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and dry up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or food crops around them to protect them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo niyenii tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe. Koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take several years to give me any income?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani sɛɛnamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its first three to five years developing strong trunks and deep root systems before producing pods. Farmers often intercrop with short-term food crops to earn income while waiting.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ lɛ feɔ shishifã ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani ekɛ ŋmeii baa. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi duɔ niyenii ni heɔ be kuku koni amɛná shika be mli ni amɛmiimɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant permanent crops like cocoa on land with unresolved ownership issues?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baahi shi daa, tamɔ kookoo, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔtsɛyeli he saji ni asaaa he lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa takes years to yield, requiring long-term investment. If land ownership or sales agreements are disputed, you risk losing access to the farm or harvesting rights after spending years caring for the trees.
ga: Cocoa heɔ afii babaoo dani enyɛɔ efeɔ. Ebiɔ ni akɛ shika awo mli be kakadaŋŋ Kɛji béi ko yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔyeli loo jarayeli he kpaŋmɔ he lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo oshara mli akɛ obaafite hegbɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ loo kpamɔ hegbɛi amli yɛ be mli ni okɛ afii babaoo ekwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do land ownership disputes affect my ability to sell or manage my harvest?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe béi saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ loo makwɛ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When a farm plot is in dispute, buyers may refuse to trade with you, and local authorities may freeze activities on the land. This leaves your crops stuck unharvested or unsold, wasting your effort.
ga: Kɛji béi ko ba yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ he lɛ Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpoo akɛ amɛkɛ bo baajara nii. ni maŋ nɔyelɔi baanyɛ akpa nitsumɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni akpaaa loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ. Ehaa ofiteɔ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the first rain falls?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry. Wait until you get a few steady rains that wet the soil deep enough so your seeds do not dry up and die after germinating.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baatsi odumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right before a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ dani otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Young seeds need continuous moisture to germinate and establish roots. If dry weather strikes right after planting, the fragile seed sprouts cannot find water and will dry out completely underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ sɛɛ Fragile dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ ana nu. ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbi kwraa

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip and moving down the center in a V-shape mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ ni feɔ V su lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl inward during intense afternoon heat to shield themselves from direct sunlight and reduce water loss from the plant, which is a natural defense to save moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ aba shi Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Young and growing cocoa trees get scorched easily by intense heat. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist, which protects cocoa trees from dying during the dry harmattan season.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii ni eda lɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cowpea together with my maize, and how will it help my soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpea with maize improves soil fertility because cowpea is a legume that captures nitrogen from the air and releases it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei ji ŋmei ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking due to expanding tubers underground, typically 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my yam plants growing lots of leafy vines but producing very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miida yɛ wain tso ko ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes yam plants to put all their energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ehaa sweet potato tso lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsei ahe tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when water supply is irregular, which prevents proper pollination and stops the flower from developing into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa, ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less crop than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their high-yielding strengths in the second generation, leading to uneven plant growth and lower harvests compared to fresh certified seeds from approved dealers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ ŋmaa bibii ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when it hasn't rained for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko lɛ? Gbii babaoo nɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tightly to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss through evaporation during dry spells, helping the plant survive until the next rainfall.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my pepper plants alive during the dry season when rain is scarce?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha pepper tsei ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can use mulching by covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves, which traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. tsei ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli ni baaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ amɛ shii abɔ lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out entirely before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ haomɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is my cassava harvest smaller when I plant a huge field compared to a small, well-kept plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ faaa kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu nɔ fe shikpɔŋ bibioo ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When a farm is too large to clear and maintain, weeds compete with cassava for soil nutrients and water, whereas a smaller, properly weeded plot allows each plant to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔ ko da tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ bibioo ni jwɛi yɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso akwɛ bulbs wuji ni mli wa lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Trees planted too closely fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, and the dense shade creates humid conditions that encourage fungal diseases like black pod to spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni hulutsoo be ni mli ewo wu lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs turning yellow with web patterns underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ wɛb mfoniri yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by tiny pests called red spider mites, which suck the sap from the underside of leaves during hot, dry weather, turning the foliage yellow.
ga: Nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ Red Rider. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my dying crops are suffering from drought or from a insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ loo kooloi bibii etutua miŋmɔshi nibii ni miigbo lɛ?

english: Drought stress makes the whole field wilt evenly, while insect attacks leave clear physical evidence like leaves with holes, dark droppings, or localized patches of damaged plants.
ga: Hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa hei muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ, yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ odaseyeli ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ bu yɛ baai amli, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ loo tsei ni efite lɛ ahe fãi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers often destroy the root system unnoticed, leaving the plant unable to anchor itself firmly in the soil when wind blows.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers. Bei pii lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yɔseee. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ema shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa.

english: Why did the maize seeds I bought at the local market fail to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Market grain sold as seed may have been stored in hot, damp conditions or treated improperly, which kills the living embryo inside the seed and prevents germination.
ga: Ekolɛ akɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ gbeɔ fɔmɔ kotoku ni hiɛ kã ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaaa ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting underground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when excess water stays in heavy soil, or when soil insects bite the tuber, allowing fungal infections to enter and decay the yam before maturity.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu babaoo yɛ sũ ni tsii mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ amɛyitsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa egboɔ dani edaa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves of maize plants to feed, which can destroy the plant if not controlled early with proper pesticides or natural controls like neem oil.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei ahiɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛyeɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and dry up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal diseases like blight, which thrive in wet and warm weather. Rain drops splash fungi from the soil onto the leaves, so removing lower leaves near the ground and spraying suitable fungicides can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal helai tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ, ni shwereɔ yɛ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni akɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die and decompose, that natural nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a free fertilizer for the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why is burning my bush before planting bad for my soil in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter, kills helpful insects and worms in the soil, and leaves the earth bare and exposed to erosion from heavy rains, making the soil poorer over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small stems and thin roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough room and food to grow thick, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense sun and heat. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees during their first two years to keep cool and hold soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce energy for tuber growth through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, giving leaves maximum sunlight and preventing ground diseases from damaging the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ haa tuber dalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Ni tsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main plantain stem. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder and get full of holes in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ etsɔ sũ ni eyi obɔ kɛ bu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils eat the grain from the inside out when maize is stored with too much moisture or without protection. Drying maize thoroughly until it is hard and using airtight storage bags prevents weevil attacks.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ni abuuu he. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akatutua bo.

english: Why is cassava better to plant than maize if the rains stop early in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hi fe ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a drought-tolerant crop with deep roots that store water, allowing it to survive long dry spells, whereas maize needs regular rainfall at critical growth stages to produce grain.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni toɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia nugbɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni edaa waa lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmãa aba.

english: Why do I need to cut and trim the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy to let sunlight and air circulate, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to put its energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to prune my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: It is best to prune before the heavy rains begin or right after the main harvest season so the tree can recover quickly and grow strong new leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tsei lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ oya ni ená baai heei ni mli wa.

english: Is there a specific way I should cut the branches so I do not hurt my cocoa tree?
ga: Ani gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei aniji koni akafite kookoo tso lɛ?

english: You should use clean, sharp tools to make smooth cuts close to the main branch without peeling or tearing the bark, which helps the tree heal faster.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ dɛŋdade ko ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛjieee loo ogbalaaa tso lɛ shishi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsaa oya.

english: How does trimming my cocoa branches affect how the pods grow and hang on the tree?
ga: Te kookoo ni afoɔ lɛ saa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trimming removes unnecessary branches so that sunlight reaches the main trunk and primary branches, where cocoa flowers bloom and pods develop comfortably.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji he ko ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: I see ants crawling on my cocoa trees and sucking liquid from them. Are they harming my crop?
ga: Mina ŋmeii ni miihoso yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiinu nu ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ. Ani amɛmiiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, ants feed on the tree's sweet sap and often protect smaller insects like mealybugs, which weakens the cocoa tree and reduces pod production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, ni haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa pod ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is sap leaking from my cocoa branches, and why does it attract insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu miiho kɛmiijɛ mikookoo niji lɛ amli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ egbalaa kooloi bibii?

english: Sap leaks when insects bite into the bark or when branches are damaged, creating a sweet fluid that attracts ants and other harmful pests to feed on the tree.
ga: Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ loo kɛ́ tsei niji fite. Ehaa nu ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ baa. koni eye nii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ

english: Can pruning my cocoa trees help get rid of pests like ants?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛya?

english: Yes, cutting away extra branches lets direct sunlight into the tree canopy, creating a drier environment that ants and other moisture-loving pests dislike.
ga: Hɛɛ, ajieɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I leave them unattended without regular care?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ daa?

english: Neglecting your farm leads to dense shade, pest infestations, and unmanaged growth, which weakens the trees and drastically lowers your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oku ohiɛ oshwie oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be mli baa. tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ kɛ dalɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my neighbor's cocoa trees yield more pods than mine even though we planted around the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ akutsoŋnyo lɛ kokoo tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe kokoo tso ni wɔdu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa health depends heavily on constant maintenance; trees that are regularly pruned, weeded, and protected from sap-sucking pests produce significantly more pods.
ga: Cocoa hewalɛnamɔ lɛ damɔ ekwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni afoɔ amɛhe daa, ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ nu lɛ ahe lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo kwraa.

english: What simple maintenance steps should I take to keep my cocoa trees healthy all year round?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo komɛi anɔ. Mɛni esa akɛ ofee koni okkoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You should regularly trim overgrown branches, clear weeds from around the base of the trunk, check for sap-sucking insects, and remove diseased pods promptly.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up fighting for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough distance lets the roots spread out and gather enough food to grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso fɛɛ tso ni oooha ekɛ ehe abɔ he shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa Shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbaabua niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa aba.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide leafy shade and keep the soil moist, acting as natural umbrellas to help young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a major plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to survive, showing you that it needs extra fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Etsɔɔ bo akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be kpe. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves. This damages the leaves and can spread plant viruses, which stunting the crop's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ashwã. ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ kpaa

english: Why does my plantain farm produce smaller bunches when many young shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Beni tsei bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, drain water and nutrients away from the main fruiting stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing all the plant's energy to go into making one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ kui agboi ni tsii.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops each year even though I plant on the same land at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land every season strips the soil of the exact same nutrients over and over. Rotating crops, especially by planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start to rot and turn dark just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni efee duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a natural thick skin or dormant period after harvest, so they react quickly with oxygen and spoil. Processing them into gari or flour right away, or only harvesting what you can sell immediately, prevents this rapid decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa loo be ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ feɔ ekome ni efiteɔ oya. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ. Aloo kpamɔ nɔ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni yaa oya nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do small insects turn my stored dried maize into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsakeɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside maize kernels, and when they hatch, the insects eat the inside of the grain. Thoroughly drying your maize until it is very hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags starves the insects of air and stops them from multiplying.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui amli Ni kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ Kooloi yeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ahe loo. Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa waa ni akɛwoɔ vacuum bag ni atsĩ naa mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ashwie kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing green shoots in the barn before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break their resting state when exposed to warmth and moisture in storage. Storing yams in a well-ventilated, shaded, and cool yam barn delays sprouting so the tubers stay firm and edible longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i he yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni ayeɔ be babaoo.

english: How often should I water my garden eggs and tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-egg kɛ mi-tomato lɛ nu yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Vegetables like garden eggs and tomatoes need consistent moisture to form healthy fruits. Watering them deeply two to three times a week early in the morning or late in the evening helps roots absorb water without losing too much to heat evaporation.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ abɔɔ mli wɔji kɛ tomato he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli waa shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ nu ni amɛhaaa hulutsoo babaoo aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause heat stress in tomatoes, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers. Supplying consistent water to the soil and providing light shade during peak sun hours helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ haaa pollen lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my vegetable crops turn yellow after I start irrigating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mibɔi nu shwiemɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is getting too much water at once, which drowns the roots and prevents them from taking in nutrients, or that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo shikome. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon even when the soil has water from irrigation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu jɛɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: On hot days, crop leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. This daytime wilting is a self-defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss and plants usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why does it take many years for tree crops to start giving full harvests?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e heɔ jehahi babauu loko tso ko jeɔ yiblii womi ɔ mi ɔ?

english: Perennial trees spend their first few years developing deep root networks and thick trunks so they can support heavy yields. Once their frame is strong, they shift their energy into producing flowers and fruit consistently for decades.
ga: Tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ baa koni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji frem lɛ mli wa Amɛbaatsake amɛhewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like tomatoes between my young tree crops while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tsei, tamɔ tomato, yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops between young trees makes good use of space and sunlight. As long as you leave enough space around the base of the young trees, the short-term crops will provide food and income until the trees mature.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, be kukuoo mli dumɔ yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ. Abaakɛ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la atsu nii ni ená he sɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha ana niyenii kɛ shika kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to support long-term tree crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ afi mli tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Good soil for tree crops should be deep, well-drained, and rich in dark organic matter so the deep roots can spread without rotting in trapped water during heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ tsei lɛ mli kwɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli edɔ babaoo Enɛ ji koni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni amɔmɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can keeping farm animals benefit the crops I grow on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure is rich in natural plant nutrients. When dried and mixed into your field soil, it improves soil texture, helps the ground hold water better, and provides steady food for growing crops.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ tsei amli niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji egbi lɛ ni okɛfutu oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aha kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ.

english: Why do crops grow so quickly right after the first rains of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rains wake up beneficial soil microbes that break down trapped organic matter, releasing a sudden wave of nitrogen into the soil which gives plants a natural growth boost.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ shi. Ejieɔ nitrogen ni hoɔ trukaa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe

english: How do agricultural officers determine the best time of the year for farmers to start planting?
ga: Te okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ aaafee tɛŋŋ amɛle afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okwaafoi lɛ baanyɛ aje dumɔ shishi?

english: Agricultural officers monitor regional weather patterns and soil moisture levels to identify when rains will be steady enough to keep seeds wet continuously until they sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi kwɛɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛna be ni nugbɔ lɛ baaná shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi be fɛɛ be kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will help restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining regular watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap beneath the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Treating the plants with neem oil spray or an appropriate insecticide controls these sap-sucking pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ nɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crop chemicals in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during the hottest part of the day causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air before it can protect the plant, and the bright sun mixed with the chemical can scorch the leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when it is cooler.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛbuɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops like maize consume a large amount of soil nutrients. Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, making the field fertile again for the next crop season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha jɛmɛ afee he ni baa nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, depriving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ha shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ akumɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help them grow bigger and produce more yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Removing weeds ensures that your crops get all the food and water they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop pole helps bear the weight of the fruit and keeps the tree upright during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their outer skin turns completely yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Harvesting pods at this stage ensures the beans inside have fully sweet pulp, which is necessary for proper fermentation and quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akpaa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. Enɛ he miihia kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of leafy growth above ground but very few nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need loose, well-drained soil and calcium to push their flowering pegs into the dirt to produce pods. If the soil is too hard or packed down, the pegs cannot enter the ground properly to form full nuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ calcium he miihia ŋmeii koni ekɛtsi fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Peg lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nut ni eyi obɔ baafee.

english: Why do my crops keep wilting or falling over even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes might be attacking the roots. When roots are damaged or broken by these pests, the plant cannot hold itself firmly in the ground or suck up water and nutrients.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fite shishifãi loo amɛkumɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii.

english: What are nematodes, and how do they affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Nematodes are microscopic, worm-like pests that live in the soil. They bite and feed on plant roots, causing them to swell, rot, or break, which starves the plant of essential food and water.
ga: Nematodes ji kooloi bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛ ŋmɔɔ ni amɛ yeɔ tsei shishifãi, ni no haa amɛ fuɔ, amɛ fiteɔ loo amɛ fãa, ni no haaa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hia lɛ.

english: How can I check if bad soil pests are damaging the roots of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Carefully dig up one of your weak plants and look at the roots. Healthy roots are long and clean, but roots damaged by pests like nematodes look short, broken, swollen with knots, or rotted.
ga: Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome ni okwɛ shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tse. Shi shishifãi ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ efite lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ kuku, ni ekumɔ, ni efuu, ni ebɔle ehe loo ni efite.

english: What causes a crop's roots to break easily under the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi lɛ fãa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya?

english: Roots break easily when soil pests like nematodes feed on them or when fungal diseases cause root rot. A weak root system loses its flexibility and strength, making it crumble easily.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes ye amɛ loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Shishifã ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ. ha efee mlɛo akɛ oookumɔ

english: Why do my plants dry up so fast in the hot weather compared to my neighbor's plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: If soil pests have destroyed your plant's roots, the plant loses its main 'drinking straws.' Even if the soil has moisture, damaged roots cannot lift water up to the leaves, so the plant dries out quickly in the sun.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fite otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ‘enumɔ jwɛi’ titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ awo nu nɔ kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to completely uproot a diseased crop instead of just cutting the top off or spraying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ loo oooshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: When root pests like nematodes infect a plant, the damage happens underground. Cutting the top off leaves infected roots in the soil where pests continue to multiply and spread to surrounding healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ ye tsei lɛ Nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baaba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, eshiɔ shishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: What should I do with a plant after I dig it up because of root damage?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tso lɛ beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ efite?

english: You should remove the infected plant completely from your field and burn or bury it far away. Never leave infected plants on the farm or throw them in your compost, as pests like nematodes will survive and infect new crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oshã loo ofu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Kaashi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ.

english: How can I help my young crops build a strong root system from the start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛjɛ shishijee?

english: You can build strong roots by adding rich organic manure or compost to the soil before planting, watering deeply rather than shallowly, and making sure the soil is loose enough for young roots to spread easily.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma shishifãi ni wa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani odu lɛ nɔ. Nu lɛ mli kwɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: How do microscopic soil pests like nematodes spread from one side of my farm to the other?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Nematodes move across fields through contaminated soil stuck to farm tools, boots, or tractor tires, as well as through running rainwater that carries infected soil from one area to another.
ga: Nematodes lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni akɛkpɛtɛ okwaayeli nibii, bɔɔtu loo trakta tai ahe lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni fata he ji nugbɔ nu ni holeɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ he kome kɛyaa he kroko lɛ nɔ.

english: How does rotating my crops every season help protect roots from pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Soil pests like nematodes usually prefer specific crop roots to eat. When you rotate and plant a different crop that the pests do not like, they starve and die out, leaving the soil safer for future crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ nematodes lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye tso shishifãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Beni otsakeɔ ohe ni oduɔ tsei srɔtoi ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ. Hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛgboi. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain inside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Yes, growing food crops alongside young cocoa provides helpful shade for the young trees while providing quick food and income for your family before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika oya dani aje kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Which food crops can I safely plant to eat while waiting for my cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe koni maye be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Crops like plantain, cocoyam, and cassava are commonly grown because they give quick harvests and provide temporary shelter for young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Aduɔ tsei tamɔ plantains, cocoa, kɛ cassava koni amɛwo oya kɛ be kukuoo mli wɔɔhe kɛha kookoo dumɔwui.

english: Why should I remove mature food crops from my farm after my cocoa trees grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie niyenii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mi-cacao tsei lɛ eda lɛ sɛɛ?

english: As food crops grow mature and large, they start competing with your cocoa trees for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which can delay or reduce your cocoa yield.
ga: Kɛ niyenii tsei lɛ dara kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he ni amɛbatsɔ wuji Amɛbaabɔi akaŋshimɔ kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha o-cocoa lɛ aya hiɛ loo eba shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing slowly when I plant cassava very close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ daa blɛoo beni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ duɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cacao tso lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spread widely and feed heavily on soil nutrients and water, which starves nearby young cocoa trees if they are planted too close together.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni eyeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye cacao tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I leave old food plants in the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi niyenii tsei momo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving old or overgrown food plants blocks too much sunlight, traps unwanted dampness, and steals nutrients that your cocoa trees need to bloom and make pods.
ga: Niyenii tsei ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine ni ashiɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa lɛ Mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo lɛ mli ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Does uprooting root crops like cassava or yam harm my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi amli lɛ yeɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ awui?

english: Uprooting root crops can break the delicate roots of nearby young cocoa trees if you dig too close, so it is important to harvest carefully and keep proper spacing.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji otsi ohe kɛbɛŋkɛ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akpa ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: How do I recognize when a food crop in my cocoa farm is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Food crops usually show maturity when their leaves start turning yellow, stems dry up, or tubers push near the surface, signaling it is time to harvest them and give space to the cocoa.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛbaai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ, loo amɛ bulbs lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Etsɔɔ kpamɔ be ni ehaa kookoo lɛ hegbɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade from my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ miniyenii tsei lɛ amli?

english: If cocoa trees grow thin and tall without spreading out, or if their leaves look pale green, they are getting too much shade and need surrounding crops to be cleared.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da ni efee bibioo ni ekwɛɛɛ shi ni egbɛ eshwaaa Aloo ebaaji lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulutsoo babaoo ni ehe miihia ni amɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do food crops that helped my cocoa trees when they were young become a problem later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii tsei ni ye ebua mi cacao tsei lɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ bafeɔ naagba yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive hot sun, but older cocoa trees need full sunlight to produce flowers and pods, so shade crops become competitors over time.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Shi cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii, no hewɔ lɛ shade tsei lɛ bafeɔ akaŋshilɔi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does clearing old, mature crops out of my cocoa field help increase my harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni egbɔ lɛ ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing mature crops allows fresh air and bright sunlight to reach the cocoa canopy, which encourages flowering and ensures all soil food goes directly into making cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ kookoo lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli nibii fɛɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How many new yams can I usually expect to harvest from one big yam using the traditional planting way?
ga: Sweet potatoes heei enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ sweet potato agbo kome mli kɛtsɔ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: With traditional farming practices, planting one large yam tuber typically yields only about 20 additional yams over the course of a full year.
ga: kɛ blema okwaayeli gbɛi Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei agbo kome lɛ, ŋmei aaafee 20 pɛ baafata he yɛ afi muu fɛɛ mli.

english: Is it possible to get more seed yams from just one single yam tuber?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ana dumɔwui babaoo kɛjɛ yam tuber kome pɛ mli?

english: Yes, by adopting rapid multiplication techniques, a farmer can use just one single yam tuber to produce over a thousand new seed yams instead of relying on old traditional methods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwereɔ oya lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛkɛ sweet potato tuber kome pɛ afee sweet potato dumɔwui heei ni fa fe akpe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ehe aaafɔ̃ kusum gbɛ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: If I want to expand my yam farm, do I have to buy hundreds of heavy yams to start?
ga: Ani oosumɔ ni okɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli alɛɛ? Ani ehe miihia ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii ohai abɔ dani obɔi nitsumɔ?

english: No, you do not need to buy massive amounts of seed yams. With improved multiplication methods, a single healthy yam can generate over a thousand new seed yams to stock your farm.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii amli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui heei ni fa fe akpe ni akɛto oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How long does it normally take for a yam crop to complete its growth cycle?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ gbeɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa?

english: Under standard traditional farming practices, a yam crop takes a full year (12 months) to mature and complete its harvest cycle.
ga: Yɛ blema okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, Sweet potato tsei lɛ heɔ afi muu fɛɛ (nyɔji 12) dani amɛdaraa ni amɛgbeɔ amɛkpamɔ be lɛ naa.

english: Can I produce new seed yams in less time than a full year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ afi muu fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, standard traditional farming takes a whole year, but improved propagation methods allow you to produce abundant new seed yams in under six months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kusum mli okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shi gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ ni etee hiɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmeii heei babaoo ni woɔ dumɔwui baa yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli.

english: Why does my traditional yam harvest take so long just to give me a small reward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kusum mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ he be babaoo dani ekɛ nyɔmɔwoo fioo ko ba mihe lɛ?

english: Traditional methods focus on growing large whole tubers slowly over 12 months, which naturally limits production to about 20 extra yams per plant per year.
ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa sweet potato tubers agboi ni akwɛ̃ɔ fiofio yɛ nyɔji 12 mli lɛ nɔ, ni no haa sweet potato krokomɛi ni afeɔ lɛ feɔ aaafee sweet potato 20 yɛ tso kome mli yɛ afi mli.

english: Why do I lose so much of my harvest every year just keeping yams to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ nibii babaoo ni miduɔ daa afi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛtoɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Traditional planting relies on using large portions of your harvest as seeds, which yields very few new yams (around 20 per tuber). Improved methods drastically change this ratio so one yam produces over a thousand.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi damɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni akpaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa sweet potato hee fioo ko pɛ (aaafee tubers 20 kɛha mɔ kome). Gbɛ ni atsake lɛ tsakeɔ nɛkɛ mlijaa nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, yam kome baanyɛ awo nɔ ni fe akpe.

english: How can I produce enough planting material quickly without spending a fortune?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee nibii ni akɛduɔ nii oya ni mikɛ shika babaoo efiteee?

english: By switching from traditional whole-tuber planting to rapid multiplication methods, you can turn a single yam tuber into over a thousand viable seed yams in just six months.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsakemɔ ni afeɔ kɛjɛɔ blema sweet potato tuber ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa oya lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ otsɔ sweet potato tuber kome nɔ ofee sweet potato dumɔwui ni fa fe akpe yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli.

english: What makes improved yam production methods different from how our fathers used to farm yams?
ga: Mɛni haa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ bɔ ni wɔblematsɛmɛi lɛ duɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he?

english: Traditional farming takes a whole year to turn one big yam into about 20 extra yams, while improved techniques produce over a thousand new yams from one tuber in less than six months.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli heɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani anyɛɔ atsakeɔ ŋmei agbo kome aaafee ŋmei krokomɛi 20, yɛ be mli ni ŋaai ni atsake lɛ haa ŋmei heei ni fa fe akpe kɛjɛɔ ŋmei kome mli yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli.

english: How can I increase the speed at which my yam crop multiplies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee mi-sweet potato lɛ oya?

english: You can increase multiplication speed by moving away from whole-tuber yearly planting and adopting fast-propagation techniques that reduce the cycle to six months while producing over a thousand new yams from one tuber.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shweremɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya kɛtsɔ bulbs muu ni ooodu yɛ afi mli lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni haa be lɛ feɔ kuku kɛyashɛɔ nyɔji enumɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei ni fa fe akpe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kome mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn under direct, intense sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let air and sunlight through, alongside frequent harvesting of ripe pods, helps prevent the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli Kɛfata ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa shii abɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need their leaves exposed to direct sunlight to make food for the growing underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, increasing sun exposure and protecting the plant from ground diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in their growth gives them the necessary nutrients to regain green leaves and produce strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha ebaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They feed inside the young leaves and central shoot, so early detection and applying recommended sprays or neem extracts is key to protecting the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli ni ana Ni okɛ neem spray loo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii mra. No hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ titri ni haa abuɔ nibii ni afee lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat or water stress. Maintaining consistent moisture in the soil through regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its blossoms to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper planting distance ensures each plant gets enough space and nourishment to yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field when the ground is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a rain. Water helps dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can absorb it, whereas applying it to dry soil can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your main crops a fair chance to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Yellow leaves are a sign that the plants are starving because too many stalks are sharing the same small space.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi babaoo tsɔ miijara he bibioo ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting light green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white flies. The virus attacks the leaves and stops the plant from making food properly, which leads to smaller tuber yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ni hiɛɔ Virus lɛ tutuaa baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa tuber lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: What happens if I bury my maize seeds very deep in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: A seed only has a small amount of stored energy to sprout. If planted too deep, it will use up all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before it reaches sunlight, causing it to rot or die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. ni haa egboɔ loo egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is the plant's way of protecting itself. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, which helps it save water and stop from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei baaha baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so fruit cannot form, causing the plant to shed the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai efeee. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my watermelon vine have many yellow flowers but very few fruits growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers. Bees must carry pollen from the male flowers to the female ones; if there are no bees around to do this, the female flowers will fall off without making watermelons.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli. Kɛji ŋmeii bɛ he lɛ Fɔfɔi yei lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo melon.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants producing huge green leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving sweet potatoes too much rich fertilizer or animal manure forces the plant to focus all its strength on growing big leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to swell the tubers below.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha sweet potato lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, atsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shishigbɛ yitso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green sprouts while resting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ be mli ni miheɔ mihe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A harvested yam is still alive and goes into a natural sleep period. Once that period ends, heat and moisture in the air signal to the yam that it is time to use its stored energy to start growing a new plant.
ga: Yam ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebote adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be mli. Kɛ nakai be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛje tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: How do weeds harm my groundnuts if they are not directly covering the leaves?
