ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi ŋmeii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛhaaa baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Even if weeds are not shading your groundnuts, their aggressive roots grow underground and steal water and soil nutrients away from your crop, leaving your groundnuts weak and low-yielding.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, jwɛi lɛ haŋ o-peanuts lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars crawling inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Kpãa emli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. These pests eat the growing heart of the maize plant, reducing yields if not controlled early with appropriate bio-pesticides or recommended spray treatments.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela ko eba. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra. kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaf tips of my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until their canopy develops.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ko baaje shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow along the middle vein while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the midrib of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in your soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure will help restore green growth.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋgbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ bulbs bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its root tubers. Potassium-rich fertilizer helps balance growth for bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifã lɛ mli alɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulbs wuji lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I prune away the extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and light with the main plant, resulting in smaller bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures bigger yields.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii babaoo haa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii, nu kɛ la yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ niji bibii baa. Kɛ́ ashi suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔse sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets the leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make more food for tuber growth, while also keeping the leaves away from wet soil to reduce fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe hulu la bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii babaoo kɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Mulching around the roots helps hold moisture and lowers soil temperature to keep flowers on the stem.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Mulching around Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning dark brown and rotting on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo baa ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize crop naturally and keeps the soil fertile for longer periods.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I test if the ground has enough moisture for me to safely sow my crop seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a hand-deep hole into a ball; if it holds its shape without dripping excess water or crumbling away easily, there is enough moisture to plant.
ga: Okɛ oniji amɔ sũ ko ni yɔɔ bu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi loo egbeeee shi mlɛo lɛ, no lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off some of the healthy-looking branches on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra branches, known as pruning, helps the crop direct its energy and food toward producing bigger fruits rather than wasting resources on unnecessary leaves. It also allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents diseases.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite nibii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe, ni no tsiɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do I need to spend so much time and effort clearing and weeding my farm at the start of the season compared to later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo kɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: At the beginning of the planting season, young crops are small and weak, so they need maximum space, light, and nutrients to establish strong roots. Once the crops grow larger and develop a thick canopy, they naturally shade out many weeds, requiring less intense labor until harvest time.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená he ko babaoo, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni enyɛ efee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ tso lɛ mli lɛɛ ni eyɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse lɛ Amɛbaafee jwɛi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ biɔ nitsumɔ fioo kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops affect how the crops produce fruit?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves in your farm by stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from the soil before your crops can reach them. This leaves your crops weak, stunted, and unable to produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe feɔ shoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni he ko akafite?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for nutrients, water, and sunlight. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems, producing smaller fruits or fewer pods overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii loo pods fioo pɛ baa fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves rot and turn black when the farm becomes very bushy during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ beni ŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enáa jwɛi babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a farm is overgrown with leaves and weeds, air cannot flow freely between the plants, trapping damp, humid air inside. Fungal diseases thrive in dark, humid environments, causing leaves and fruits to rot quickly.
ga: Beni baai kɛ jwɛi ehà ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya. ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ mli Fungal helai shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ejɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai kɛ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops require different types of care as they grow from seedlings into mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛyaa tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Just like growing children, young crops need protection from harsh sun and weeds to build strong roots, while mature crops need branch trimming and nutrient boosts to support heavy flowers and fruit growth.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛ ni miida lɛ ji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ jwɛi ahe koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ, ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli ni akɛ niyenii afata he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara waa lɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my fruit trees fall off before turning into actual pods or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miiho dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant becomes stressed due to a lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or having too many overgrown branches to support. Proper trimming and timely feeding help the tree retain its flowers until fruit matures.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine babaoo ni baanyɛ aye abua lɛ. Tso lɛ ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ daa.

english: Why should I remove old, dead crop stems and rotten pods from my farm after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ashishifãi ni egboi kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni egboi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Old crop residue and rotten pods act as hiding places for pests and plant diseases during the dry season. Removing them cleans the field so that your new crops will not be infected when the next rain starts.
ga: Nibii ni egbɔ ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ ji hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai teɔ shi yɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli tseɔ koni be kroko ni nugbɔ baaje shishi lɛ, hela akamɔ onibii heei lɛ amli.

english: How does sunlight reaching the lower branches of my crop help increase my harvest?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni hulu la ni shɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ?

english: Leaves use sunlight to make food for the entire plant. If upper branches block all the light from reaching the lower section, those lower branches become unproductive and die off, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji ŋwɛi nine lɛ tsi la fɛɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ Nakai shishigbɛ niji lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the best time to do major work like branch trimming on my farm?
ga: Male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nitsumɔi ni he hiaa, tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Major maintenance like trimming is best done right before the rainy season or immediately after harvesting. Doing it at these times prepares the plant to direct fresh rainwater and nutrients straight into growing new, healthy fruiting branches.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba loo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afee enɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii heei kɛya niji heei ni woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field under direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa creates a living shield that keeps the soil cool and provides the damp environment cocoa needs to mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Kɛfata kookoo he lɛ, efeɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa kookoo lɛ naa he ko ni mli ejɔ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of stay deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer brings back the green color and helps the crop produce heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo toi ni tsii.

english: Is it better for me to plant cassava on raised soil mounds or flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava on raised mounds loosens the soil so the roots can expand easily without running into hard dirt. Mounds also prevent rainwater from collecting around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli oya ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔji hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with many leaves but gives me tiny roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stem tops instead of sending nutrients down to build large tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane mli ni nu egbi lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from intense heat and trap moisture inside. It is the plant's natural way of saving water during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into tomatoes when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When air temperatures get too hot, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from extreme heat stress. Mulching the soil with dried grass helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight into the farm to dry out moisture and stop the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai kpaa.

english: How come fall armyworms are able to destroy my maize crop without me seeing them early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms baanyɛ afite mi ŋmãa ni minaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms lay eggs and hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize stalk. They eat the tender leaves from the inside out, so inspecting the inner leaf fold early helps catch them before damage is severe.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ mligbɛ fãi lɛ amli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ amɛ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Overcrowding forces pepper plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with very small fruits. Proper spacing lets sunlight reach all branches and improves yield.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni enɔ yibii lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso nine fɛɛ nine he ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot quickly after I bring them to the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if their skin gets cut during digging or if they are stored in hot, unventilated rooms. Storing undamaged yams on raised, airy wooden shelves in the shade keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afo hewolo lɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to adeka ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the bottom up even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow well. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil away from roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the plants will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: My cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but why do most of the small pods dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mikoo tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ pods bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, emli babaoo gbɛ́ɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa?

english: This is often caused by cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree cannot support all its pods, but it can also be triggered by black pod disease or mirid insect attacks. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to let air flow through, and applying recommended treatments will help save your young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cherel tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Shi black pod hela loo glass beetle ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba. weeding Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛ o-pods bibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten just as they begin to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ beni ekwɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when the soil gets too dry or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist using grass mulch and adding agricultural lime to the soil before planting helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli, ni bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo afɔɔ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and eat the central leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ba trukaa ni amɛye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the center funnel of maize plants during the day and feeds on the leaves at night. To control them, spray a recommended insecticide early in the morning or late in the evening directly into the center funnel as soon as you see small holes on the leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ. Kɛha nɔyeli Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli kɛji ona buji bibii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ pɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curled up with yellowish patches, and the roots staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Your plants have Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and by taking stem cuttings from sick plants. You cannot cure a plant once it is infected, so you should pull out infected plants and only plant improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: O tsei lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Onyɛŋ otsa tso lɛ kɛji hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni odu ŋmei henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crop protection medicines during the hot sun at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ shwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Spraying during the hot midday sun causes the liquid medicine to evaporate quickly into the air before the plant or pest can absorb it. The intense heat combined with chemicals can also burn your crop leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon gives the treatment time to work safely.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer directly on top of dry soil without burying it or waiting for rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni afuuu lɛ loo emɛɛɛɛ nugbɔ lɛ?

english: When fertilizer sits exposed on hot, dry ground, the sun and wind cause much of its food nutrients to escape into the air as gas before the roots can reach them. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and cover it lightly with soil near the root zone.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, edɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa niyenii mli nibii babaoo joɔ foi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oshi ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and maize on the exact same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slower and stays in the ground much longer. Proper spacing ensures both crops get enough sunlight and nutrients without crowding each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land right after I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil and germinate as soon as direct sunlight and rain reach them. Removing the tree shade opens the soil to full sun, which triggers rapid weed growth. Planting cover crops or covering bare soil with mulch blocks sunlight and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ amɛhe pɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ sũ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them after keeping them in a plastic bag for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo plastic kotoku mli nyɔji fioo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storing seeds in plastic bags without drying them thoroughly traps moisture and heat, which kills the tiny living embryo inside the seed or causes mold to grow. Seeds must be dried completely in the sun and kept in a cool, dry, well-ventilated space to stay healthy for planting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui wo plastic kotokui amli ni ogbiiee lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mli. ni gbeɔ fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ. yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli loo eha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ Ehe miihia ni agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: What fast-growing plants can I sow along my farm boundary to discourage stray cattle from entering my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe koni mikɛtsi tsinai ni elaaje lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: You can plant dense hedge plants like jatropha or thorny acacia around your borders. Livestock like cattle avoid eating jatropha because it has a bitter, unpalatable sap, creating a natural living fence that protects your food crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tso ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ jatropha loo akasia ni ŋmeii ebɔle he lɛ. ohusu lɛ Kooloi tamɔ tsinai tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ jatropha yeli he ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbogbo ko ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ oniyenii tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, causing the lower leaves to yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their leaves during sudden dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni ba trukaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their leaves as a natural defense to conserve moisture when water is scarce. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass or leaves retains moisture and stops the plant from dropping leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji nu faaa. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains grown right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into plant food in the soil. This enriches the ground naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without exhausting the soil.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava crop curling up and developing pale green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches indicate cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings for planting prevents this sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela, ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ odumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes drastically from wet to very dry. Keeping soil constantly damp with regular watering helps the flowers turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they expend all their stored energy trying to push up through the heavy dirt before reaching sunlight, causing seeds to rot or produce weak, spindly shoots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛje kpo kɛya hulu la lɛ mli, ni no baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛniji ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: If stray livestock trample my young maize field, will the stems grow back or should I replant?
ga: Kɛji tsinai ni elaaje lɛ nyiɛ mi-ŋmei bibi lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ loo esa akɛ madu ekoŋŋ?

english: If the main growing point near the base of the young shoot remains unbroken, the maize plant will recover and push out new green leaves. If the stem is snapped off right at ground level, that stalk will die and needs replanting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tso bibioo lɛ shishi lɛ efoko lolo. Abɛi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ekɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baaje kpo. Kɛji tso lɛ fã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbo ni ehe baahia ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting early and rotting inside the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ mra ni amɛmiifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when they sense heat and moisture, which signals to the tuber that it is time to grow again. Keeping yams off the ground on raised bamboo racks in a shaded, well-ventilated barn stops premature sprouting and decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ naa akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ekoŋŋ. Kɛ atomo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmei shɛlɛf ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ fitemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and turning brown during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight because their root systems are not yet deep enough to draw sufficient moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from severe sun damage during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during intense sunshine as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. By reducing the surface area exposed to the heat, the plant retains moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield heavily during one part of the year and produce very little pods a few months later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ fã mli, ni nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to rainfall patterns and seasonal changes. Rain triggers flowering, and it takes about five to six months for those flowers to mature into full cocoa pods, creating natural peak and low harvest seasons.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ be mli tsakemɔi ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ. Nugbɔ haa fɔfɔi baa. Ni eheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani nakai fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yeɔ emuu. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli kpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ kɛ be ni baa shi baa.

english: Why do some cassava varieties take eight months to produce tubers while others take over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nyɔji kpaanyɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi?

english: Different crop varieties have different biological clocks. Early-maturing varieties are bred to store starch in their roots much faster, allowing farmers to harvest earlier compared to traditional long-term varieties.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswai srɔtoi. Afɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛkɛ starch ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya kwraa. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii oya kɛ akɛto blema nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do high-yielding maize varieties like Sikavita produce bigger yields than the regular seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ Sikavita lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe daa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are carefully selected and bred for strong roots, disease resistance, and efficient nutrient intake, which guarantees stronger stalks and larger grains compared to saved seeds that lose vigor over time.
ga: Ahalaa tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni shishifãi ni wa, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi wa kɛ dumɔwui wuji kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops produce mostly leafy branches instead of flowers and fruits when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ tsei ni ji baai babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into leafy growth rather than fruiting. Crops need a balance of different nutrients, like phosphorus and potassium, to trigger flowering and pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Tsei hia niyenii srɔtoi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa. Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ he hewalɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ bulb bibii waa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of storing food in their tubers or fruits, they stretch upward to reach daylight.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii loo aduawai amli lɛ Ebaakpã mli kɛyashi ebaashɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread. Removing infected pods and trimming excess branches improves air movement and keeps the crop healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating crops or letting the land rest restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni enáa ebɔɔ nii ni baa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds thoroughly before I put my seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your newly planted seeds need to sprout and grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ oya koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does my maize grow so tall and green when I plant it on freshly cleared bush land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ waa beni midu yɛ tsei bibii ni agbele ehee lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared bush land is rich in organic matter and nutrients that have built up over years. This gives young maize a strong nitrogen boost, helping it grow fast, leafy, and deep green.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ eyi tsei ahe hei ni agbele ehee lɛ babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa abifao ŋmãa ni enáa nitrogen babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni edaa oya Eyɛ baai ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does burning dry grass and fallen branches before planting hurt my soil?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egboi kɛ tsei niji ni egbee shi ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning gives a short-term ash boost, but it destroys essential organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that keep the ground moist and fertile over time.
ga: Shãa haa sũ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant maize on the same piece of land where young tree saplings are planted?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, young trees and maize can grow together during the first few years. Maize grows quickly and feeds near the surface, while young tree roots go deeper, allowing you to harvest food without harming the tree seedlings.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Abɛi daa oya ni eyeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni ofiteee tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does planting legumes like groundnuts alongside maize make the land better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots decay in the dirt, they feed the soil with natural fertilizer that helps crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the maize plant moves whatever food it has left from its older lower leaves to keep its new top leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants shadow one another from sunlight and fight over soil water and food, leading to weak, thin stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ hulu la. ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my maize cobs sometimes have missing or patchy grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni elaaje lɛ?

english: Patchy cobs usually happen if the maize plant suffers from heat or drought while flowering and tasseling, which prevents full pollination of every grain on the cob.
ga: Cob that is patchy Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ na hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ fɔfɔi amli ni eyɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ naa kwraa.

english: How do I know when the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rain dampens the soil down to at least the depth of your hand, ensuring the seed gets continuous moisture to germinate without drying out in the sun.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛyashɛ onine mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do some crops produce a heavy harvest in the first year but yield less in the second year on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy-feeding crops like maize pull large amounts of nutrients out of the earth during their growth, leaving the soil tired and hungry unless you add fertilizer or rotate crops.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni hɔmɔ hu miiye lɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I let my maize stalks dry in the field before picking the cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mafo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Drying maize naturally on the stalk lowers the moisture content inside the kernels, which stops mold from growing and protects your harvested grain from grain-boring insects during storage.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to stay green and grow. It often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that nitrogen stays in the dirt, acting as natural food for the corn you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaafee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for roots to drink it in safely. When applied to dry soil, concentrated chemical salts draw water out of the roots, causing the plant to burn and wither.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can spread out in full sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines off the damp soil also prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ koni amɛha niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain baai lɛ ahe

english: Each small shoot drinks water and eats food from the ground. If you leave too many shoots, they steal energy from the mother tree, resulting in small bunches of plantains instead of one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa plantains bibioo ko. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kuu agbo kome pɛ ni tsii.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need to be planted under plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hɔɔŋ kɛ fɛ̃i aha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that sit under the leaves and suck out the sap. They also transmit viruses into the plant, which distorts the leaves and stops fruits from forming.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni taraa baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ muawai hu yaa tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa aduawai feemɔ.

english: Why do my young corn plants have small ragged holes in the leaves with tiny dark specks inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden central leaves of the corn plant to feed and leaves behind small dark droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry conditions. When the weather gets too hot, the pollen dries out and cannot fertilize the flowers, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ pollen koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen inside the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded for too long, water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do cassava plants have so many different variety names like 'Uncle' or 'Maurice', and how do I choose the right one for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi, tamɔ ‘Tsɛkwɛ’ loo ‘Maurice’, ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala gbɛi ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava varieties differ in yield, maturity time, disease resistance, and culinary qualities. Choosing the right variety depends on your local rainfall, soil conditions, and whether you plan to boil the tubers or process them into gari.
ga: Esoro cassava henɔi yɛ yibiiwoo, dalɛ, kɛ helai ahewalɛ. kɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa Nɔ ni sa lɛ halamɔ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaashã ŋmeii lɛ loo okɛtsu nii ni okɛfee ghari.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant two different cassava varieties on the same farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting multiple varieties can protect your farm against total crop loss from specific pests, diseases, or changing weather, while also allowing you to harvest early-maturing and late-maturing varieties at different times.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ akafite yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra kɛ nɔ ni shwereɔ sɛɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do the stems of some cassava varieties look dark or black while others look light or white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ashishifãi lɛ feɔ diŋ loo ediŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛŋ lɛ?

english: The color of cassava stems and leaf stalks varies naturally from variety to variety due to plant pigments. Stem color is simply a physical trait farmers use to tell varieties apart and does not mean the plant is sick.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ baai lɛ ahe su srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ tso lɛ mli sui lɛ ahewɔ. Stem color ji gbɔmɔtsoŋ su ko kɛkɛ ni okwaafoi kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛyoo srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ. Ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants mature in six months while others take up to a year or more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi heɔ afi loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have distinct genetic growth rates. Early-maturing types grow quickly to produce tubers in 6 to 9 months for quick harvest, while late-maturing types take 12 to 18 months, usually accumulating higher starch content over time.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii ni haa mɔ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ srɔtoi. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 mli kɛha ŋmaa oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛbuaa starch babaoo naa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some cassava plants grow straight up while others spread out with many branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jaŋŋ ni ekrokomɛi hu gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ?

english: Branching habit depends on the cassava variety. Spreading varieties cover the soil with dense leaves, which naturally suppresses weed growth, while straight-growing varieties allow you to plant stems closer together in the field.
ga: Niji ahe su lɛ damɔ ŋmei henɔ lɛ nɔ. Henɔi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei ni etse ehe banee. ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi srɔtoi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do tubers from some cassava varieties spoil quickly after harvesting while others stay fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi komɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally deteriorate quickly after harvest, but varieties with high dry-matter content and specific genetic traits hold up better, slowing down post-harvest rotting and discoloration.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Shi henɔi ni nibii ni egbi babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ fɔmɔ nii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ahi shi. Kɛtsɔ fitemɔ kɛ su ni tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How early in the rainy season should I plant my cassava cuttings for the coming year's harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei mra tɛŋŋ kɛha afi ni baa lɛ kpamɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to plant cassava stem cuttings right at the start of the main rainy season so the roots can establish deeply in moist soil before any dry period begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: How do I choose the best stem cuttings from my current harvest to plant for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ amli koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from strong plants that produced good tubers and showed no leaf disease. Cut pieces from the middle section of the stem with at least 4 to 6 healthy buds for planting.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ bulbs kpakpai ni foliar hela bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 yɔɔ mli kɛha dumɔ.

english: How can I know which cassava variety is best for making gari and which is best for boiling to eat as fufu?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha gari feemɔ kɛ ŋmei henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shãa ni ayeɔ akɛ fufu?

english: Varieties with high starch and high dry matter produce heavier yield when processed into gari, whereas soft-cooking varieties with lower dry matter and good texture are better suited for boiling and pounding into fufu.
ga: Henɔi ni yɔɔ starch babaoo kɛ dry matter babaoo lɛ tsii fe tsutsu lɛ kɛji akɛ afee lɛ gari. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ahoɔ amɛ mlɛo, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli ni egbi ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni ashãa kɛ ŋmeii ni atswaa kɛfeɔ fufu lɛ.

english: Do all cassava varieties require the same amount of soil fertility, or can some grow in poorer soils?
ga: Ani ŋmei henɔi lɛ fɛɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa? Aloo ani henɔi komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kwraa nɔ?

english: While all cassava crops need nutrients, traditional or hardier varieties can survive in poorer, sandier soils, whereas high-yielding commercial varieties require more fertile soil or added organic matter to produce large tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa henɔi fɛɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ moŋ Shi blema ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni wa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni ohiafoi yɔɔ nɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akɛheɔ jara ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to block direct sunlight and keep the soil cool and moist while they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizer restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the center of my young maize plants so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides deep inside the growing leaves of young maize. They eat quickly and can destroy crops unless caught early and treated with recommended pest sprays or neem solutions.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ nii oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii. Ja amɔ lɛ oya ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsa lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpea together with cassava on the same farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baafata he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, cowpeas and cassava grow very well together. Cowpea roots naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the cassava grow bigger without draining the soil of goodness.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpea shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ daa ni efiteee shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save hybrid maize seeds from my harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give a high yield only in their first harvest. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength, leading to poor yields, weak plants, and uneven growth the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baaa shi jogbaŋŋ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛdaraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When weather gets too hot, tomato pollen dries up and cannot fertilize the flowers. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy until cooler temperatures return.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and hard instead of growing fat tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa yɛ cassava ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin when the soil is packed too hard for tubers to expand, when there is not enough potassium in the dirt, or when weeds compete with the plant for food and water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni jwɛi kɛ tsei miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the plant and spreading a virus. This virus stops the plant from growing properly and reduces fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ pepper tsei ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ haaa tsei adara jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the shells shows dark brown or black markings, the nuts are mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ ahoo ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with strong root systems that absorb rain and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni shwieɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to put fresh animal manure or waste directly onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei loo sũ ni fiteɔ nii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal waste produces excessive heat as it breaks down and contains harmful bacteria that can burn plant roots and spread crop diseases. It should always be fully composted and cured before applying it to your fields.
ga: Koolooi ahe jwɛi heei kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine baa be mli ni efiteɔ ni helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni egbɛ tsei ahelai ashwã lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni etsa dani akɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Tight spacing also traps humidity, which allows fungal diseases like black pod to spread quickly between trees.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni mli wa lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ateŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or banana trees around my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain loo banana tsei yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the main dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural self-defense mechanism cassava uses to conserve water during dry weather. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing its roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eshishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or pest attacks. Keeping soil moisture consistent and protecting the plants from tiny sap-sucking insects helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize plants so quickly before I even notice them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi-corn tsei lɛ oya dani miyɔse amɛ po lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hatch in large numbers and immediately crawl inside the central funnel of the maize plant where they feed on soft growing tissues, hidden from sight until visible leaf damage appears.
ga: Fall worms lɛ fɔɔ babaoo ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. he ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Amɛteeɔ shi koni mɛi akakwɛ amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ efiteɔ faŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and turn sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck plant sap and excrete a sticky liquid, which can also spread viral diseases to your tomato crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛjieɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi ni baanyɛ agbala helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛbaa o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold even after I dried it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ?

english: Maize molds if the grain still contains hidden internal moisture when bagged, or if it is stored in a room without proper airflow, allowing trapped moisture to create a habitat for fungus.
ga: Abɛi baaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lolo yɛ mli beni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ afee shihilɛhe kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is too hard and compacted for them to expand, or when rocky ground blocks their natural downward growth path.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe kɛyashɛ he ko ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their roots are still small and lose water faster than they can draw it from the soil. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to act as living umbrellas during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon but look fresh again in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss. Once the sun goes down and temperatures cool, the plant recovers its water balance and leaf shape.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ afee bibioo ni amɛha nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nu ni sa kɛ ebaa lɛ su ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for deep green, healthy growth. The plant is pulling nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli waa Tso lɛ miigbala nitrogen kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni eha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year if I plant cassava in the exact same field repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava continuously pulls specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Growing it in the same spot without adding compost, manure, or rotating with crops like beans drains the soil's fertility and allows crop-specific diseases to build up.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be daa be. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ yɛ he kome ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ aba.

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess rainwater sits in the soil for too long, it pushes out all the air, suffocating the cassava roots and causing them to rot under the ground.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It blocks the direct sun from baking the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ shãaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: Why do I need to clear tall bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that produce tubers based on how much sunlight their leaves catch. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves get full sunlight while staying safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni damɔ hulu la ni baai lɛ náa lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha tsei ahe tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs if I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for limited light, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, all of them remain weak and form tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme hot temperatures, dry soil, or a lack of wind and bees to transfer pollen inside the flower. Unpollinated flowers automatically drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo be, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ shwieɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars always attack the tender top funnel of my young maize plants first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the central funnel (whorl) because it contains the softest, newest, and most nutritious leaf tissues. Hiding deep inside the funnel also protects the pests from sun and heavy rain.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ (whorl) ejaakɛ no ji nɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ehee, ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko tee ehe ewo ŋtayaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the roots are drowning from too much standing water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ nu lɛ ekã shi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Can I put fresh cow dung directly on my farm right after clearing the animal pens?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee afata miŋmɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ beni mijie tsina ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fresh animal dung is too strong and generates heat that can burn young plant roots. It is best to let the dung rot and dry into dark compost first, which breaks down the nutrients into a safe form your crops can easily digest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbo ni amɛgbi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ gbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli ewoɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why should I plant my corn in straight rows with measured spacing instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja ni asusu gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ
