english: Planting in straight, well-spaced rows makes sure each corn plant gets its fair share of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. It also makes weeding and harvesting much faster and easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant cassava and cowpeas together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai beni mikɛ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the heavy-eating cassava plants. Ground-covering plants also protect the topsoil from drying out in the sun.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmei tsei ni yeɔ loo ni tsii lɛ Cover crops hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like small tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing moisture when the sun is very hot. It is the plant's natural defense to save water until the cool evening comes.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ akɛ ebaabu nu he kɛyashi fɛ̃i be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why is rain so critical when my corn starts showing tassels at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ he hiaa waa beni mi-ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The tasseling stage is when the corn flowers and starts forming kernels on the cob. If the plant lacks water during this stage, the cobs will turn out small with missing or empty kernels.
ga: Be ni abuaa naa lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ebɔi dumɔwui feemɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii ni dumɔwui ni elaaje loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How does leaving dry corn stalks on top of my field after harvest help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry plant matter on the soil creates a protective layer called mulch. This layer shades the earth from direct sunlight, keeping the soil moist for longer and slowly decomposing into rich organic food for your next crops.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni hulu la akashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni ji niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I test if the corn seed I saved from my last harvest is still good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: You can place ten saved seeds on a wet rag inside a container for a few days. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are strong enough to plant in your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshi dumɔwui 10 ni ato lɛ yɛ mama ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ owui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns in the centers of my maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are common pests like fall armyworms that hide inside the tender center leaves of young maize. Catching them early by inspecting your farm weekly allows you to control them before they damage the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ fall flukes ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii amli. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ daa otsi lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni otsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do you advise us to try a new crop variety on a small garden plot first before planting our main fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ wɔka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko wɔkwɛ yɛ abɔɔ bibioo ko mli dani wɔdu yɛ wɔŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Testing a new seed on a small plot lets you see how it reacts to your local soil and climate without risking your main harvest and food supply if the season turns out bad.
ga: Dumɔwui heei akamɔ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ Ehaa ona bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he. ni ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji be lɛ ehiii

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil around their small roots. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains next to them protects the young cocoa until they grow strong enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Ebuɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if the very first heavy rain in April means it is safe to start sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ April mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaaje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi?

english: The first rain of the season is often a short rain followed by days of scorching heat that can bake planted seeds in the dry earth. It is safer to wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains within a short time so the ground stays moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ feɔ kuku. Gbii ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ agbi lɛ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my green maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize show that the crop is running low on nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining food to the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers very small and light when I plant them too close to my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same limited supply of soil food, water, and sunlight. This competition prevents the cassava from getting the nutrients it needs to swell and produce large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfu ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am pushing a cassava stick into the mound?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei miiwo gɔŋ ko mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ aya?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the new shoots have to grow around the stem inside the dirt to find light, which wastes energy and leads to poor yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ tsei heei akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Tsoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ena la Enɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Which young shoot should I take from my plantain tree if I want to plant a strong new crop?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii ni jɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: You should pick a sword sucker, which has thin, pointed leaves like a sword and a thick base attached deep to the parent stem. These suckers grow faster and produce heavier plantain bunches than water suckers that have broad leaves very early.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala klante sucker, ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tamɔ klante, kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse ni akɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ plantain panicles ni tsii fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce tiny tubers if I let them trail along the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji miha efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetswa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need high wooden stakes to spread their leaves into the air where they can catch sunlight to produce plant food. Vines trailing on wet soil get shaded easily and suffer from fungal diseases that reduce tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi koni amɛkɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni baanyɛ aná hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli Wein tsei ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ hulutsoo he oya, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa bulb lɛ dalɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why are my green peppers curling up tightly at the tips instead of opening into broad leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili eŋɔli lɛ ebɔle ehe yɛ naagbee yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. Their feeding damages leaf tissue and can spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ eshwa.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to chew holes inside the central funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli?

english: This destruction is caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the hidden inner leaves of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft new tissues. Left untreated, they destroy the heart of the plant before it can flower.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Amɛbaakpata tso lɛ tsui lɛ hiɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why are my green tomatoes getting flat, dark, rotten patches on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is developing. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates sharply, preventing roots from steadily absorbing calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if the holes in my crop leaves are caused by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ba?

english: Insect damage usually leaves clean holes or chewed edges on the leaves, and you might see the bugs or their droppings nearby. Disease damage often starts as discolored spots, yellowing, or powdery growth before the leaves die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji ni he tse loo ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni ekolɛ obaana kooloi bibii loo amɛmli ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni fiteɔ mɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ he ko ni ehiɛ su. Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ dani baai lɛ gboiɔ.

english: What should I look for when inspecting my farm to know if pests are damaging my plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii miifite mitsei lɛ?

english: Check under the leaves, inside the flowers, and around the stem for crawling insects, webbing, sticky residues, or unexpected yellowing and wilting of the leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi, fɔfɔi lɛ amli, kɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛkwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ, ŋmeii, nibii ni eshwɛ ni shwieɔ shi, loo baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ yɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions, causes cocoa pods to rot. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight helps prevent this.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ, ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves in dry weather to conserve water and survive. As soon as the rains return, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue its normal growth.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling up during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat to reduce water loss, but persistent yellowing and curling usually mean stem borer insects are attacking the inside of the plant or the soil lacks nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ni yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ stem borers lɛ etutua tso lɛ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny pests like thrips that feed on the delicate parts of the blossom.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutua amɛ.

english: People talk about buying crop 'medicine' for pests, but how do I choose the right one for my farm?
ga: Mɛi wieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ‘tsofa’ ni akɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala nɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You must first identify the exact pest causing the damage. An extension officer can help you identify the pest and recommend a safe, government-approved chemical specifically made to control that pest.
ga: Esa akɛ oyɔse tsɛŋemɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Extension agents baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oyoo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni amɛtsɔɔ bo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni afee pɔtɛɛ koni akɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: If the pest medicine recommended for my crop is not available in my town, what should I do?
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli? Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Consult your extension officer for alternative approved products that contain the same active ingredient, or use natural methods like neem extract sprays while waiting for official supplies.
ga: Bi o nibii ahe hiɛyaa najiaŋdamɔlɔ kɛha nibii krokomɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ yɔɔ mli. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tamɔ neem extract spray atsu nii be mli ni omɛɛɔ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together so I can spray my farm faster?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ baafutu koni manyɛ mashɛre miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya?

english: No, mixing different chemicals without professional guidance can destroy their effectiveness, burn your crops, or release hazardous fumes that are dangerous to your health.
ga: Dabi, tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii Kɛ́ ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. shã onibii loo ojie lasu ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aye ohewalɛ nɔ awui lɛ kpo.

english: How can working with an agricultural extension officer help me protect my crops better?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitsumɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers visit your farm to inspect crop damage firsthand, correctly identify pests or soil issues, and guide you on the safest and most effective ways to treat your farm.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni owo bo ŋaa yɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow big enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la shɛɔ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why must I wait for my cocoa pods to turn yellow before harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa?

english: Harvesting green, unripe cocoa pods results in underdeveloped seeds that will not ferment properly, leading to flat, poor-quality cocoa beans that buyers will reject.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover my cocoa seeds with banana leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ banana baai aha kookoo yibii ahe gbii fioo komɛi dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Covering the cocoa seeds creates heat, allowing them to ferment. Fermentation develops the chocolate flavor and turns the inside of the seed brown instead of bitter and purple.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ baa ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsokolate mli ŋɔɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ amli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: What makes cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet weather and excess shade. Clearing weeds and harvesting infected pods early helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akpamɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the nutrient it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bote mli lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil gets thoroughly soaked by two or three heavy rains. Planting after the first light drizzle can cause seeds to germinate and dry up if the rain stops.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, while legumes like beans pull nitrogen from the air and restore it to the soil, naturally fertilizing your land for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying an approved pesticide or placing wood ash in the center funnel of the plant early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ tso sũ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested cassava roots from spoiling two days after digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava spoils quickly when exposed to air after harvest. Leave cassava in the ground until you are ready to sell, or process it immediately into cassava flour or gari.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Shi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ. loo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afee lɛ ŋmei ashikiŋsha loo gari

english: How can I protect my stored dried maize seeds from being destroyed by weevils?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ he koni ŋmeii akafite?

english: Ensure the maize is dried thoroughly until hard, then store the grains in airtight bags or treat them with safe grain-protectant powder before storing them in bags.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ powda ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu he nii dani okɛwo kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why should I test my farm soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil testing acts like a health checkup for your land. It reveals what nutrients your soil already has or lacks, helping you spend money only on the right fertilizers and pick crops that will thrive in that specific soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛnamɔ he kwɛmɔ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ loo ebɛ lɛ kpo. Ehaa okɛ shika tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa pɛ ahe. ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing mangoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mangoes need deep, well-draining soil so their long roots can spread out without rotting in trapped water. Inspecting the land and testing the soil depth and composition will tell you if mango trees will survive and yield well there.
ga: Mango he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi kakadaji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oka bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji mango tso lɛ baahi shi ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops rot when rainwater stays on the land for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long without draining away, it chokes the roots, causing them to drown, turn black, and rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, amɛbote nu mli, amɛfee ediŋŋ, ni amɛgboi.

english: Is it better to plant my fruit tree seedlings right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tso yibii dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, planting at the beginning of the rainy season gives young seedlings steady moisture to build strong root systems deep in the ground before the dry harmattan period arrives.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei bibii lɛ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani harmattan be ni egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why can't I plant many mango trees very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haaa yibii wuji aba lɛ?

english: If mango trees are planted too close, their mature branches block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients. Spacing them properly ensures big, healthy trees with maximum fruit yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu mango lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Niji ni eda lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ mango tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Gbɛjegbɛ ni sa haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why does a grafted mango seedling produce fruit much faster than one grown from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: A grafted seedling uses a branch taken from a mature tree that is already old enough to flower. A seed must start its life from scratch, taking many extra years just to mature before it can produce its first fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Esa akɛ dumɔwu ko aje wala shishi kɛjɛ shishijee. Eheɔ afii babaoo dani ekwɛɔ dani ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally drop unpollinated flowers, but severe flower drop is usually caused by sudden dry spells, insect pests, or lack of soil nutrients during the flowering period.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa baa ji shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ trukaa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, which gives leaves their rich green color and helps the plant make food.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii.

english: How do weeds hurt my young crops even if I give the crops enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal essential soil food and sunlight away from your crops. Even with water, your crops will struggle because the weeds are taking the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ nu po yɔɔ mli lɛ, onibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Does cutting off some healthy branches from my fruit tree actually help it produce more fruit?
ga: Ani niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mifoɔ yɛ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes crowded inner branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the whole tree. This directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, sweeter fruit rather than just growing extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ baai kpahi kɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that your soil is low in nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient too deep into the ground where the plant roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How does adding animal manure or dried leaves to my soil make my crops yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Organic matter like manure and leaves acts like a food store and sponge for the soil. As it breaks down, it slowly releases rich nutrients to feed your crops while helping the soil hold onto water during hot, dry weeks.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei kɛ baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ kɛ sponji kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Beni efiteɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii babaoo fiofio koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes root strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. yɛ be mli ni kookoo wajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines rely on sunlight to manufacture the energy needed to grow large tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum light exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha tsei lɛ aná la babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain stem, they steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two healthy shoots, allowing the main stem to produce a much bigger and heavier plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee plantain ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms usually drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of wind and insects to pollinate the flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ kooloi ni haa tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves, resulting in larger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Planting maize in the same spot season after season drains the same nutrients from the soil and encourages corn-specific pests to live in your soil. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns vital nitrogen back into the earth naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ewoɔ abele pɔtɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded for too long, water fills these air gaps, smothering the roots and allowing harmful fungi to attack and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei nɛɛ amli obɔ. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani akpaa.

english: What is eating tiny ragged holes in my young corn leaves, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tiny ragged holes are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on the soft leaves inside the whorl. If left unchecked, they destroy the plant's growing point, preventing it from producing a healthy ear of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ amɛhe, ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. ni no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni wa aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees require partial shade from companion plants like plantains to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and extreme heat, which cause severe moisture loss and leaf scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa waa kɛ baai ni shãa lɛ baa.

english: How does applying fertilizer help my mature cocoa trees yield more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer restores essential nutrients like potassium and phosphorus that mature cocoa trees draw out of the soil over time, giving the trees the strength to form more flowers and carry healthy pods to maturity.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus baa ekoŋŋ. Cacao tso ni eda lɛ jieɔ enɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune extra branches and water shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive shoots that siphon energy away from pod production and opens the tree canopy to airflow and sunlight, which lowers humidity and reduces fungal disease risks.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they lack sufficient soil moisture, balanced nutrients, or pollinators like midges, ensuring the tree only retains what it can support.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. niyenii ni ja loo nibii ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi, tamɔ midges, koni tso lɛ ahi nɔ pɛ ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli dani odu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Maize seeds need consistent moisture in the soil to germinate evenly and develop deep root systems; planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry out or get destroyed by insects.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo ŋmeii baafite amɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle encourages roots and tubers to form near the soil surface in a compact layer, making harvesting much easier and improving overall yields.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ woɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ koni amɛfee nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the weather is very rainy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, high-humidity conditions; regular harvesting of ripe pods and clearing excess farm shade helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in the central whorl of young maize are typically caused by destructive caterpillars like Fall Armyworm, which eat the growing point of the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help them grow faster?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, so removing them leaves all essential resources available for your crops to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does rainwater stand on my farm land for days without soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soils have tiny spaces between soil particles that trap water and slow down drainage, requiring raised beds or drainage channels to protect crop roots from waterlogging.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. shikpɔŋ mli nibii bibii ni hiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa nu hoɔ oya lɛ ateŋ Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ saatsoi ni awo nɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛi atsu nii koni akɛbu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves whatever nutrients it has left from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new top growth, causing the lower leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Curled and wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding on the undersides of the leaves. As they feed on the leaf juices, they distort the leaf tissue and can also spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ hu amɛshwã.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rotting is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto low pods, causing them to turn black and ruining the beans inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛfiteɔ kɔfe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does this purple-flowered weed keep weakening my maize even after I clear the grass around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli nɛɛ miigbɔjɔ mi-abele lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ moŋ?

english: This weed is called Striga (or witchweed), and it is a root parasite. Before it even shoots above the ground, its roots attach directly to your maize roots underground, stealing water and vital food directly from the maize plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Striga (loo abɛi jwɛi) ni eji shishifã mli tsɛŋemɔ hela. dani etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ o-corn shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as temporary living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need abundant sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground to capture maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves off damp soil, which prevents leaf rot diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa shwiemɔ hela naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of small pollinating insects. When the plant senses unfavorable conditions, it drops its flowers to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii bibii ni haa tsei lɛ nuɔ shihilɛi ni ehiii lɛ amli lɛ mli. Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why does my cocoa tree shed most of its tiny flowers without them developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ehe wooo pod mli?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands more flowers than it can physically feed into full pods. The tree naturally drops most unpollinated or weak flowers to preserve energy, relying on tiny biting midges (insects) to pollinate the few flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni amɛfa babaoo tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aye akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen loo ni bɛ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Bite koni ekɛ fɔfɔi fioo komɛi ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ awo mli.

english: How can I know that my cassava roots are big enough to harvest since they grow hidden under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtee amɛhe?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months of age, its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the soil surrounding the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Why does swamp rice grow better when the field stays covered in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers out competing land weeds that would otherwise steal light and fertilizer from the rice. The water also keeps the root zone consistently moist and warm, encouraging the rice plant to produce more tillers and grain heads.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Nu hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen or sitting in too much stagnant water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or draining flooded soil helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can grow strong corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo eyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt during the sunny hot afternoon even though I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni esa akɛ mafee nakai lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu ewo mli?

english: When pepper plants wilt in wet soil, it usually means soil fungi or pests have damaged the root system. The damaged roots cannot suck up enough water fast enough to keep up with the hot afternoon heat, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛye shwane mli latsaa lɛ nɔ. gbee tsei ashwie shi

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture changes rapidly between very dry and very wet. Consistent watering and giving crops light shade during high afternoon heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ be ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my cabbage leaves, and will that stop the cabbage head from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani ebaaha kaabe yitsei lɛ afeemɔ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by chewing caterpillars. Leaves act as the plant's solar panels to create food; when insects destroy too much leaf area, the plant lacks the energy needed to form a firm, heavy cabbage head.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii lɛ amli. Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ hulu hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kpata baai babaoo ahiɛ lɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee kaabe yitsei ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are growing big roots underground or just growing tall stems and leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo shishifãi kɛ baai kakadaji kɛkɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, it wastes energy growing tall stems and lush foliage instead of roots. Loose, well-aerated soil and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to direct its energy into fattening the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaafite hewalɛ ni ekɛmiida tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to keep weeds away from my yam mounds while the vines are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsi jwɛi kɛjɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni wain tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young yam vines need maximum sunlight and nutrients to feed the underground tuber as it develops. Early weeds act like thieves, stealing water and fertilizer from the soil and choking the vine before the tuber can form properly.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Mra be mli jwɛi lɛ fee amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɔɔ dani bulbs lɛ baanyɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the air cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and falling over easily in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants stretch thin and weak as they compete with each other for light. Giving each seed proper distance ensures thicker, stronger stalks that can withstand wind.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables taste bitter and produce seed heads early during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables flower early and turn bitter when stressed by heat and water shortages. The plant senses harsh conditions and rushes to produce seeds to reproduce before it dies, which stops leafy leaf growth.
ga: Aduawai fɔɔ mra ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei nuɔ shihilɛi ni esaaa he ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have natural helpers on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When the cowpeas are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmei Nitrogen ni emɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This usually means your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crop regain its strength and produce healthy leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ, ni baai lɛ hu baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients from the soil. Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains those exact nutrients and allows soil pests to build up, whereas rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with tiny fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper spacing allows their roots to spread and leaves to capture enough light to produce big harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni baai lɛ naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines onto stakes spreads the leaves out in the sun and air, preventing leaf rot and growing larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Tsi baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni okwɛ sweet potatoi wuji.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: The main plantain tree shares its food and water with every sucker attached to its root. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant focuses its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu mli ni eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii agboi ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ he nii.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or dead leaves on the soil around my vegetables help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-aduawai lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture. This mulching keeps the root area cool and wet for a longer time, reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ mulching nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during harsh sunny days helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo gbii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the juice under the leaves and transmitting plant viruses. Clearing surrounding weeds and applying neem oil or organic pest controls early helps stop leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ mites loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When rain water sits on flat ground without draining, it suffocates the roots and causes rot, which is why planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds protects the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ akɛ nugbɔ nu fɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ.

english: Tender young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Young cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba, hulutsoo ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot retain enough water under direct, intense heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their early years to protect their leaves from sunscald and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni shãa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions with poor air circulation. Overgrown weeds and low tree canopies trap moisture, which helps the fungus infect the pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei kukuji lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do new leaves on my cocoa trees come out looking reddish or pink before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tsuru loo pinki dani amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: This leaf growth stage is called flushing. The bright red pigments protect the young, tender leaves from sunlight damage until they mature and produce green chlorophyll for food production.
ga: Atsɛɔ baa lɛ dalɛ fã nɛɛ akɛ leaching. Pigment tsuru ni kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai bibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build healthy green leaves and fill out big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps it save water and prevent severe moisture loss during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa nu ni mli edɔ waa lɛ afite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ baai beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings will not sprout if they are planted upside down, cut from old or dried stems, or planted in soil that lacks basic moisture during the first few days.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Afolɔ niji ni egbɔ loo ni egbi lɛ amli. Aloo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishijee ŋmɔtɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves. Proper sunlight exposure allows the vine to feed the plant and produce large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛbaa lɛ. Hulu la ni sa lɛ haa wain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away the smaller suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the parent plantain for water, nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning them leaves more energy for the main tree to produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between wet and dry, preventing successful pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Etsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, which damage the leaves and can spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei ahe helai ni haaa amɛdara lɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my rice plants need so much standing water in the field compared to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in shallow water because their root systems are adapted to wet soil, which also acts as a natural barrier to stop weeds from choking the crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice crops turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth, or that the field is either too dry or completely waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my tall rice stalks fall over flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when heavy rain or wind pushes down tall crops, or when applying too much fertilizer makes the stems weak and top-heavy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shĩa, ni baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amɛshwie shi. Aloo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli, ni no haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant my crops too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaa nii bibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster in my field after rain than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants fully adapted to local soil and conditions, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for planting rice instead of cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Rice needs heavy soil like clay that holds water for long periods, whereas root crops like cassava need loose, well-drained soil so their roots can expand easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ yucca lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why should I buy certified project seeds instead of replanting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe nitsumɔ mli dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to produce high yields and resist diseases, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations and yield less crop.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why can't I just cook and eat my paddy rice straight from the field right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahoo ni maye ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Harvested paddy rice is a raw material covered by a hard outer shell called a husk, which must be dried and milled to reveal the soft, edible grain inside.
ga: Paddy ni akpa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ chaff ehà nɔ. Esa akɛ agbi enɛ ni atsɔ mli koni ajie ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested grain on a clean tarpaulin instead of bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying on a tarp keeps soil, rocks, and bird droppings out of your crop while reducing moisture so the grain does not rot or mold during storage.
ga: Kɛ́ oogbi yɛ tarp nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji, tɛi, kɛ okpoi afɔfɔi akashɛ onibii ahe. kɛfata hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ he No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ egbooo loo amɛhe efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do buyers pay less money for my harvested rice if it contains moisture or dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo muji lɛ?

english: Buyers treat wet or dirty grain as raw material that requires extra time, labor, and fuel to dry and clean before it can be milled into food.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ buɔ ŋmaa ni efɔ loo ewo muji lɛ akɛ eji nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni biɔ be, nitsumɔ, kɛ tsofa kroko koni egbi ni etsumɔ he dani abaanyɛ atsɔ mli afee niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and crop vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in the middle of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni etse yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common insect pest. They hide in the central growing funnel of young maize plants and chew the leaves, which can reduce your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do some farmers in my community plant cassava and groundnuts together in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the crops, while cassava grows deep roots. Planting them together keeps the soil healthy and gives you two different food crops from one piece of land.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ Nibii enyɔ lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops still wilt during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In very hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the dirt. Light morning watering only wet the top surface, so the deep roots stay dry.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ fioo leebi lɛ Ha ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ afɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baagbi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or sudden changes in water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. be kakadaŋŋ ni nu lɛ mli egbi loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ nu mli Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How does leaving dried grass or dry leaves around my plants help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Te mitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the dirt around your crops with dry plant leaves acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil water, stops weeds from growing, and rots over time to feed the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsei ahe baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by tiny microscopic fungi that thrive in damp, heavy shade. Trimming dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gboo bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, shade ni mli wa mli kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to make high mounds of earth before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick under the ground, so they need soft, loose dirt to expand easily. High mounds also prevent water from standing around the yam seeds and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can die if they were stored with moisture inside them or damaged by tiny insects like weevils. Drying seeds properly until they are hard and storing them in sealed containers keeps them alive for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fite amɛ. Dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the crops I planted after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots designed by nature to quickly grab water and food from the dirt. Your planted crops need extra help and clear space so they don't get choked out by weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni adebɔɔ fee koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. O tsei ni miida lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛ he ko ni agbele koni jwɛi akaye amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops shoot back up and sprout even after I have cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mifo amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Certain plants store food and energy in their underground roots. Even when the upper part is cut, these resilient root systems allow the plant to shoot fresh stems back up once moisture or favorable conditions return.
ga: Tsei komɛi kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ afo ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ po Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe nɛɛ hu haa tso lɛ náa shishifãi heei kɛji ŋmɔtɔ loo shihilɛi kpakpai ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: How can I prepare my land so my crops survive when the dry season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the ground and shields the plant roots from direct heat during hot dry periods.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ŋmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?
