english: Plants drop their leaves during dry conditions as a survival trick to conserve water, because leaves naturally release moisture into the warm air.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do crop diseases usually enter and spread across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai boteɔ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases enter farms through airborne spores, rain splashing infected soil onto leaves, contaminated cutlasses or boots, or when insects carry sickness from farm to farm.
ga: Helai boteɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai amli. Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ baai anɔ. Kpoji loo bɔɔtui ni mli ewo muji Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: What simple everyday habits can I practice to keep diseases away from my crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ sui ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni esa akɛ afee daa gbi koni helai akabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: You can protect your crops by pulling out and burning infected plants immediately, washing your farm tools after use, leaving space between plants, and changing the types of crops you plant each season.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya ni oshã amɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe kɛji okɛtsu nii sɛɛ. Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni otsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops more likely to catch diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds create a damp, overcrowded environment that traps humidity around your crops, creating the exact conditions plant diseases and pests need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai koni amɛshwere lɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us not to plant our seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each crop gets enough sunlight, soil food, and airflow, which prevents fungal diseases from jumping quickly between touching leaves.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni sa nɔ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ atswa oya yɛ baai ni taa he lɛ ateŋ.

english: How can I tell by looking at my crops that they are healthy and free from sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli?

english: Healthy crops usually have rich green leaves, strong upright stems, smooth fruit or pods without dark spots, and consistent growth across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni yeɔ emuu. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Yibii loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tse, ni ŋmɔtɔ diji bɛ he. ni eyɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Is it harmful to plant the exact same crop on the same field every single year?
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be. Ani afi lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up permanently in your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli daa.

english: Why did my farm give a huge harvest last year but very little produce this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli shi ewo fioo kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: A heavy harvest uses up a lot of the soil's natural strength; if you do not replenish the soil with manure or rest the land, the crop yield will naturally drop in the following season.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni tsii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my maize crops if I plant the seeds too close together on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in small cobs and low yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why should I measure and plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni madu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ.

english: Planting in organized rows ensures each crop gets equal room, air, and sunlight to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to a randomly scattered field.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛ akɛto hei ni egbɛ eshwã trukaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Without shade crops like plantains to shelter them, the harsh sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil around their young roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall and weak with very few flowers under my large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbɛ fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ yɛ mitso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need direct, full sunlight to generate energy for flowering and fruiting. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upwards searching for light, making the stem long and thin while reducing fruit production.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Beni eyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ena la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, bushy green leaves but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes plants to direct all their energy into growing foliage above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei tsɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips that move down the middle vein indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and produce food for healthy growth.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ niyenii aba koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks the cycle of soil exhaustion.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ fitemɔ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the bunches are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily loosen in wet soil, especially under the weight of heavy fruits or when root pests attack them. Removing excess suckers and propping up heavy trees prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ oya. Titri lɛ yɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ashishi loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni ayeɔ abuaa Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop growth even when my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ awui lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground and steal water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Even if tall crops get sunlight, root-level competition from weeds drains the nutrients essential for crop development.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ naa hulu la moŋ, shi shishifãi akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi amli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wither so quickly during dry spells even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: When bare soil is exposed to direct heat, moisture evaporates rapidly from the surface before plant roots can drink it. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves holds moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots grow small and twisted when I plant them in hard ground without softening the soil first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni efiteɔ waa kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni afeee shikpɔŋ lɛ blɛoo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are swollen underground stems that need soft, loose soil to push outward easily. When soil is hard, the roots struggle to expand, resulting in thin, misshapen, and woody tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni efuu ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛtsi kɛya kponɔgbɛ oya. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa lɛ, ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa yitsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni ehiii, ni tamɔ tsei baa.

english: Why do seeds take much longer to sprout when I plant them directly into unplowed land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a mix of air, moisture, and soft earth to crack open and push up through the surface. Tight, unplowed soil holds less trapped air and creates a hard crust that delicate young sprouts cannot easily push through.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛfee ekome koni amɛgbala ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo. ni efeɔ ŋmei ni wa ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds come back much faster when I clear my land by cutting with a cutlass compared to digging up the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ amɛ lɛ to shishifãi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ he?

english: Cutting weeds off at ground level leaves their underground root systems alive, allowing them to bounce back quickly after rain. Digging deeper removes the roots entirely, slowing down weed regrowth and giving your crops time to establish.
ga: Jwɛi ni afoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahi shi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ atsa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Ehaa jwɛi heei daa blɛoo. ni ehaa tsei lɛ be koni amɛhi shi

english: Is it better for my maize if I burn the dead bushes on my field after clearing, or leave them to rot on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi ni egboi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni mijie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo aha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Leaving cleared plant material to rot acts like a protective carpet that keeps the soil cool and retains rain moisture. Burning gives a quick ash boost but leaves the soil exposed to hot sun, causing it to dry out quickly and starve crops of water.
ga: Tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbo lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli baa lɛ hiɔ shi. Shãa haa sũ lɛ yaa hiɛ oya shi ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli nu faaa.

english: What happens to my corn plants if I plant them late after the main rains have already started?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Late-planted corn misses the wet period when its roots are developing, forcing it to grow during hotter, drier weeks. This causes stunted growth, yellow leaves, and small, incomplete cob development.
ga: Abɛi ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ beni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Nyɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu shwereɔ ni eshɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and wilt by midday even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ amɛ moŋ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: When soil lacks rotted plant material, it cannot hold water like a sponge. Rain drains through too fast or evaporates under direct sun, leaving plant roots dry and unable to absorb nutrients, which turns leaves yellow.
ga: Beni tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu tamɔ sponji. Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya tsɔ loo efoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves block each other's light and their roots fight for the same soil water. The plants waste energy growing tall to reach light instead of building strong stems and big ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe la naa. ni tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ mli koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tue nguahi.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops more than older, fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and few leaves, so they are easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds stealing sunlight and soil water. Older crops have deep roots and larger leaves that shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ enɔ oya. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which crops grow best if I am unable to dig deep into my land before planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mafo amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Shallow-rooted crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or pepper can thrive on shallow, hand-tilled soil because their main feeder roots stay near the top layer, unlike yams or sweet potatoes which require deep, soft soil.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ. Amɛjeee tamɔ sweet potatoes loo yams, ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas between my other crops help keep the soil healthy?
ga: Beans loo cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ateŋ Te mine lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas extract nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots decay, they release natural fertilizer into the earth, which feeds the neighboring crops without needing chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni yeɔ naagbai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii

english: Why do crop prices drop so low when everyone in my village harvests at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests simultaneously, the market becomes flooded with produce. Because buyers have so many choices and crops can spoil quickly, farmers are forced to reduce their prices just to sell what they have before it ruins.
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi fɛɛ fee ekome kɛkpa nii lɛ Jarayeli lɛ baayi obɔ kɛ nibii ni amɛbaakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ nibii babaoo ni amɛbaahala, ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afite oya. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛba jara shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛkɛ dani efo.

english: Why does having a very huge harvest sometimes end up causing me to lose money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nikpamɔi wuji haa bei komɛi lɛ mifiteɔ shika lɛ?

english: A bumper harvest can lead to market gluts where supply far exceeds demand. When prices crash below what you spent on fertilizers, labor, and transport, you can end up losing money despite having grown plenty of crops.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ aya hiɛ fe nine, he ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ kwraa. Kɛ́ nibii ajara ba shi fe nɔ ni ofiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nitsulɔi, kɛ gbɛfaa he lɛ, obaanyɛ ofite shika yɛ be mli ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo po sɛɛ.

english: What can I do with my extra produce when the market price is too low to make a profit?
ga: Mɛni mikɛ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ kɛji jara nɔ jara lɛ baa shi tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: When raw crop prices crash, you can preserve or process your produce—such as drying cassava into gari or milling maize—or place durable crops in proper storage until market supplies decrease and prices rise again.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ ajara ba shi Obaanyɛ okɛ onibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ ato loo otsu he nii, tamɔ ŋmãa ni ooogbi ni ofee gari loo ŋmãa ni oootsɔ ŋmãa mli. aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ awo he ko ni sa kɛyashi jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛjara baaya ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ.

english: How can proper crop storage help me get a better price for my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Good storage protects crops from insects, mold, and rot. By keeping your produce safe for a few months after harvest, you can wait until market shortages occur and sell at much higher off-season prices.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ahe. Kɛtsɔ onibii ni oooha ehi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ omɛ kɛyashi be mli ni nɔ ko baashɛ jara nɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa yɛ be ni be lɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to buy certified seed varieties or just plant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odase lɛ loo madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yields, disease resistance, and uniform growth. While saving your own seeds saves money initially, saved seeds often lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Eyɛ mli akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui ni ooobua naa lɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ shishijee mli moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ bibioo.

english: Why do seeds brought in from another region or country sometimes fail to grow well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ kpokpai loo maji krokomɛi anɔ aba lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds are adapted to specific climate conditions, rainfall levels, and soil types. A crop variety that performs well in a different region may suffer from local heat, drought, pests, or nutrient differences in your soil.
ga: Atsakeɔ dumɔwui kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. Tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ aná dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii mli nibii amli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do market buyers prefer paying higher prices for certain crop varieties over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Traders and consumers pay top price for crop varieties that match specific preferences, such as better taste, faster cooking times, longer shelf life, or higher oil and starch content for processing.
ga: Jarayelɔi kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ hiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe nii, tamɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Hoomɔ be ni yaa oya Shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ loo fɔ kɛ starch ni fa babaoo kɛha nitsumɔ

english: How do I calculate whether my crop sales actually made a profit or a loss?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he akɔntaa kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ miihe sɛɛnamɔ loo miifite nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Subtract all your production expenses—including land prep, seeds, fertilizers, chemical sprays, hired labor, and transport—from the total money you received from buyers. If the remaining amount is positive, you made a profit.
ga: Jiemɔ shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ he saamɔ fata he Dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, nitsulɔi ni awoɔ amɛ nyɔmɔ kɛ gbɛfaa kɛjɛɔ shika fɛɛ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hɔlɔlɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ shika ni eshwɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi Obaanyɛ oná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How much money should I put aside after selling my harvest to prepare for the next season?
ga: Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni adu lɛ agbe naa lɛ, shika enyiɛ esa akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛsaa he kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: A good practice is to set aside at least 30% to 40% of your earnings immediately after sales to cover essential inputs like certified seeds, land preparation, and emergency costs for the next planting season.
ga: Nifeemɔ kpakpa ji ni kɛ hoo lɛ, okɛ shika ni oná lɛ mlijaa 30 kɛyashi 40 ato he yɛ jarayeli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ koni okɛwo nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ, kɛ oyaiyeli he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: How does processing my raw crops into packaged goods increase my farm earnings?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ni mikɛbaafee nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni mináa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Processing adds value by making crops cleaner, easier to store, and ready for immediate consumption. Value-added products last longer, attract urban market vendors, and command higher, more stable prices than raw crops.
ga: Nitsumɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ ni ehaa ehe tseɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaato ni asaa he kɛha niyeli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ fata he lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Gbalamɔ jarayelɔi kɛba maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ ni okwɛ jara nɔ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong leaves, or when there is too much water choking the roots.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa loo kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ shi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer off the top of the soil before the plant roots can drink it up, wasting your time and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ. Eji obei kɛ oshika fitemɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines up on stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight and prevents ground diseases from attacking the leaves, which helps the crop grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni amɛkatutua baai lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry, when the tree lacks nutrients, or when tiny pests like mirids attack the delicate blooms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the mother plant for food and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excessive water prevents air from reaching the roots, causing harmful soil fungus to infect and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu babaoo haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies passing a virus to the plant, or by extreme heat and inconsistent watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii? dani eda

english: Pepper plants drop young fruits when they experience water stress, such as sudden dry spells after heavy rains, or when the soil gets too hot.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ trukaa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the soil and provides free nutrients for your maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops wilt faster during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the little water and food stored in the soil, leaving your main crops weak and thirsty.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu fioo kɛ niyenii ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kumai yeɔ bo.

english: Why are the top leaves of my maize plants spreading out wide like a fan instead of staying upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tamɔ fan yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Spreading leaves help the maize plant catch as much sunlight and rain as possible to feed the growing corn ears, though drooping leaves during hot afternoons can also mean the plant is stressed from lack of water.
ga: Baai lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha toi ni miida lɛ niyenii. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ po baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni faaa amɛmli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know when the ears on my maize stalks are completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa toi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize ears are ready for harvest when the outer leafy husks turn dry and brown, and the silk threads coming out from the top become dark brown and dry to the touch.
ga: Abɛi toi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni siliki ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he.

english: Is it helpful to trim or cut off some leaves from my crop plants while they are growing?
ga: Ani eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trimming excess or damaged leaves allows the plant to send its water and nutrients directly to growing fruits or grains instead of wasting energy on leaves that no longer help the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine loo ni efite lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni yeee ebuaaa tso lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the large leaves on my plantain trees droop down during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally fold or droop under intense sun to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which keeps the plant from losing too much moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and stay alive, while continuing to safely store food in the tubers underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni akɛbu nu he ni wala ahi shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii lɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender like human babies and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight; they require shade trees or fast-growing plantains to shield them during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni enyɛŋ eŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, and blocks airflow between leaves, which creates damp conditions where diseases easily spread.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli oya.

english: Flowers drop off without forming fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot, when the soil lacks essential nutrients, or when the plant does not get steady water.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from young leaves, or by viral diseases carried into the field by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli

english: Why do my maize plants fall over sideways right when the ears start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛyaa afã beni toi lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are too shallow, when they are planted too close together, or when the soil lacks potassium, making the lower stem too weak to support heavy ears during strong winds.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ haa shishigbɛ tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi toi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and drop to prevent water loss during dry spells. Planting banana or plantain trees nearby provides living shade that blocks direct heat and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Banana loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baatsi dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil is slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: During peak heat, plant leaves lose moisture into the hot air faster than roots can pull water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and conserve moisture until the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which often happens after heavy rains wash nutrients away. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ elaaje sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas partner with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water fills these air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei nɛɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in standing water while my other crops die in flooded fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ marsh rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow air passages inside their stems and roots that carry oxygen down from the air, allowing the roots to breathe underwater.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic pests like mites or aphids sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by viruses spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: High daytime temperatures or extreme moisture changes stress tomato plants, damaging the pollen so flowers fail to form fruit and fall off early.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tsakemɔi ni naa wa yɛ hulutsoo haomɔ mli tomato tsei. efiteɔ pollen Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are frequently weakened by soil-borne pests like nematodes or weevils, making the plant top-heavy and vulnerable to strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo weevils lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I stake them high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ be mli ni mikɛ amɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward maximum sunlight so they can produce more plant energy, while keeping the leaves away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How often should I be visiting my field to make sure my crops stay healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya miŋmɔji lɛ amli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: You should check your farm at least two to three times every week. Regular visits help you spot insect pests, weeds, and early signs of disease before they spread and destroy your whole field.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ daa otsi. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, jwɛi, kɛ helai ahe okadii ni tsɔɔ mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave rotted crops lying on the soil inside my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ashwieɔ lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving rotted crops on the farm leaves disease spores and pests in your soil. These spores will jump onto healthy neighboring plants or infect your next crop as soon as you plant.
ga: Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔshi nibii fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eshiɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ baatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ loo amɛbaatswa onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe hela kɛji odu amɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables suddenly start rotting on the stems within just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rapid stem rot is usually caused by fungal or bacterial infections that thrive in warm, damp weather. When fields are not checked often, excess humidity and standing water accelerate the decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ fitemɔ oya jɛɔ fungal loo muawai ni yeɔ omanye yɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli. Kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli shii abɔ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do tomato fruits rot on the plant before they even get a chance to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei anɔ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ po ni amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit rot often happens due to fungal blights spread by splashing rainwater, or a lack of calcium in waterlogged soil. Clearing infected leaves early prevents the rot from reaching the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii fitemɔ baa yɛ fungal leaf blight ni nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hewɔ. loo calcium ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe ni ooofɔ mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting my pepper crops too close together cause them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close blocks air from moving freely between leaves. This traps heat and dampness around the stem, creating the perfect conditions for rot and leaf mold to spread.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms have entered my maize farm before they destroy the entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ebote mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Look inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants for small holes and brownish sawdust-like droppings. Catching these signs early lets you treat the plants before the growing tip is eaten away.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo ko baa lɛ teŋgbɛ. koni ona bu bibioo ko kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli Omɔ okadii nɛɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tso lɛ dani ayeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds unchecked for just two weeks cause my crop leaves to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi otsii enyɔ pɛ ni mikwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Without enough nutrients, your crop leaves lose their green color and weaken quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Otso lɛ baai lɛ baafite amɛhe oya ni amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: What is the simplest way for me to keep my soil moist during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—blocks direct sunlight, traps soil moisture, and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni oha shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i ahi shi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate water stress or low nitrogen in the soil. Checking soil moisture levels regularly helps you adjust drainage or add compost before the plant stops growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ loo nitrogen ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ otsake nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani tsei lɛ akpa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ.

english: How does clearing old crop residues help prepare my soil for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei momo ni etse amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Clearing old stalks and rotting debris removes hidden pest eggs and fungal spores, giving your fresh seeds a clean, safe environment to germinate and grow strong.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei momo kɛ sũ ni egbo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa odumɔwui heei lɛ naa he ko ni he tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and produce very little when the rains don't come on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Crops rely on water to dissolve nutrients in the soil so their roots can drink them up. When rainfall is low or comes late, the crops cannot feed properly, which slows down their growth and prevents fruits or grains from forming fully.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni amɛjie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ fioo loo eba sɛɛ mli lɛ, anyɛɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo ni ehaa aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ shɛɛɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu he.

english: How does unpredictable weather affect how much harvest I will get from my farm?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ saa nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need steady water at specific growth stages, especially during flowering and fruiting. If rains stop suddenly at these key moments, flowers can drop off and pods won't fill, drastically reducing your total yield.
ga: Tsei biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ amɛdalɛ be pɔtɛɛ mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ nɛkɛ bei ni he hiaa nɛɛ amli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ni ŋmeii lɛ eyiŋ obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Is there a simple way to keep soil moist for my crops when rainfall is very light?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried leaves, straw, or weed cuttings—called mulching—helps trap moisture in the soil, preventing the sun from drying it out quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi ni afo lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ—ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching—eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. ni ehaaa hulu lɛ agbi oya

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon even if it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. This temporary wilting is a protective behavior where the plant curls up to preserve its remaining water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji subaŋ ni buɔ mɔ he. He ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbua nu ni eshwɛ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield heavily in some years but produce almost nothing in other years on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii komɛi amli, ni eshɛɛɛ kwraa yɛ afii krokomɛi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop yields change year to year based on weather conditions, soil nutrient depletion, and pest presence. If one year brings less rainfall or more heat stress, the crop puts its energy into basic survival rather than producing heavy yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ afi kɛyaa afi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛji afi ko kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ babaoo baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa shishijee wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee babaoo lɛ

english: What causes my plants to produce small fruits or small tubers instead of big ones?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ?

english: When crops experience water stress or high heat during their main development phase, they cannot generate enough sugar through their leaves to expand their fruits or underground tubers to full size.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ beaŋ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha aduawai loo ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops flower well but drop their blossoms before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ shi amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Crops drop flowers when they sense extreme heat or a sudden lack of water. It is a defense mechanism to save energy and protect the main plant from dying during severe dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ he. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ hewalɛ he ni abuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops right at the beginning of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to germinate in warm, moist soil and build deep roots while water is plentiful. This gives crops the strength to withstand short dry spells later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdamɔ be kuku ni nu hɔmɔ baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much faster during dry spells than during wet seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally tougher than farm crops and absorb scarce underground water much faster. During a dry spell, weeds quickly steal the limited soil moisture that your crops need to stay alive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ, ni amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni anaaa lɛ oya. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fioo ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ oya.

english: What happens to crop yield if I delay clearing weeds because I don't have enough help on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie shi ejaakɛ mibɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni fa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If weeds are allowed to grow alongside young crops for too long, they steal essential soil nutrients and sunlight. Even if you weed later, the crop may remain stunted and never produce its full potential harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei bibii ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po. Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni akpaaa kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. Even with plenty of water, plants need solid food from rich soil or fertilizer to stay healthy.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa tso lɛ su eŋɔli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɔɔ lɛ, Tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni wa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does fertilizer that I scatter on top of dry ground actually get into my yam roots underground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ayashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: Fertilizer granules dissolve in water from rain or dew, turning into a liquid solution. The roots then drink up this liquid nutrient water from the soil like a straw.
ga: Fertilizer pellets lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli. ebatsɔ nu mli tsofa No sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ jwɛi.

english: Why does leaving cleared weeds to rot on my field make the crop yield better the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni he tse ni mikɛhaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Decaying plants break down into rich organic matter, which acts like a sponge to hold water and slowly releases trapped minerals back into the soil for new crops to eat.
ga: Tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ebuaa nu naa ni ejieɔ shika tsuru ni emɔ mli lɛ fiofio kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei heei aye.

english: Why does burning crop leaves on my field give good harvest at first, but leave the soil weak after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ani ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Burning turns plant material into ash, releasing quick nutrients like potassium all at once. However, the heat destroys the living organic matter and beneficial organisms that keep the soil soft, moist, and fertile for the long term.
ga: Shãa haa tsei amli nibii feɔ sũ. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium oya shikome Shi kɛlɛ, dɔlɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, edɔ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my young maize plants droop during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ete shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: On hot days, plants lose water into the hot air through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it out of the ground. Drooping reduces leaf exposure to sunlight to save moisture until the cooler night arrives.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Foji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How does water from deep in the ground move all the way up to the high leaves of my plantain trees?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yaa kɛyaa mi-plantain lɛ baai kakadaji lɛ anɔ fɛɛ?

english: Plants have microscopic tubes inside their stems. As water evaporates from the leaves into the atmosphere, it creates a continuous suction force that pulls fresh water up from the roots, similar to drinking liquid through a straw.
ga: Tso lɛ yɛ tsɔnei bibii yɛ eshishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ nu jɛ baai amli kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli Ehaa nu ni yaa nɔ ejieɔ nu kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Etamɔ nu ni anuɔ kɛtsɔɔ jwɛi nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper roots rot and die when rainwater stays flooded on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water fills all the tiny pockets of air in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate and decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield very few pods when planted directly under dense forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ashishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops use direct sunlight as energy to manufacture their food and grow fruits. Dense shade blocks this light, leaving the crop with too little energy to produce abundant pods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛduɔ aduawai. Shade ni mli wa tsiɔ kane nɛɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yams grow small and crooked when planted in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are soft root tissue that expands under the ground. Hard soil acts like a wall that presses back against the root, stopping it from expanding wide and forcing it into twisted shapes.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni miimɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa egbɛ eshwa babaoo ni enyɛ enɔ ni efee nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why does heavy clay soil stick together when wet and turn hard like stone in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni tsii kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji edɔ ni ebafeɔ wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ he ni egbi lɛ?

english: Clay is made of tiny soil particles pressed very close together. When wet, water locks these small particles into a sticky mud; when dried by the sun, the water leaves and the particles pack tight into a solid mass.
ga: Sũ mli nibii bibii ji nɔ ni akɛfee sũ. No ji nɔ ni akɛfee ekome waa. Kɛ́ nu lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, emɔɔ nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ ni etsɔɔ amɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Nu lɛ baai kɛ nibii bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out easily in full sun. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them until their roots and leaves grow strong enough to handle hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni ebu he kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting too close causes trees to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water. Overcrowded trees grow weak, stay small, and end up producing fewer pods than trees given enough space.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛji bibii ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛwooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. Removing them allows light and air to reach the main trunk, directing all the tree's food straight into growing larger and healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the secret to getting a consistently high harvest across a large cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa anáa yibii babaoo yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji amli be fɛɛ be?

english: High yield is not based on a single trick, but on combining basic practices regularly: clear weeds on time, prune trees properly, apply fertilizer when needed, and control pests before they spread.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ damɔɔɔ ŋaa gbɛ kome pɛ nɔ. Shi moŋ, ejɛɔ nifeemɔi ni afeɔ daa, ni ji shishijee nibii, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa lɛ mli. Tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ Ha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do weeds on my farm make my crops produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, plant food, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds grow thick, your crops suffer from hunger and produce smaller fruits or fewer pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by tiny organisms that thrive in cold, damp conditions. Too much shade and trapped moisture allow the disease to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pods ji hela ko ni nibii bibii kɛbaa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How do long dry spells without rain affect the way my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni afeɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During severe drought, cocoa trees drop their flowers and young pods to save water and stay alive. This reduces your harvest because the tree cannot support new growth without moisture.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ehee kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing the nutrients my crops need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crop leaves usually turn yellow instead of deep green, growth becomes slow or stunted, and the plant produces very few flowers or fruits.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Dalɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ehiɛ kpaaa nɔ. ni tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi loo aduawai fioo ko pɛ

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects to carry pollen between them before pods can form. If there are few insects around, or if the weather is too dry, unpollinated flowers naturally dry up and drop.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ koni amɛwo pollen yɛ amɛteŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee. Kɛji kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How do I know the exact time a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvesting when its skin changes color completely, turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety, showing that the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ ahe su tsake kɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmɔŋ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Can I plant seeds or crop varieties brought from another region of Ghana, like Kumasi or Kintampo, on my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu dumɔwui loo tsei ni akɛba kɛjɛ Ghana kpokpai krokomɛi tamɔ Kumasi loo Kintumpo. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can, but you must ensure your local soil type, temperature, and rainfall (or irrigation) match the conditions where that variety originally grows best.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ, shi ehe miihia ni ona nɔmimaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, bɔ ni edɔ ha, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Nu (loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi) ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni nakai tso lɛ daa yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why do different varieties of the same crop grow and produce differently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different varieties have unique genetic traits. Some are bred to grow faster, some produce bigger fruits, and others are designed to resist pests or dry weather better than others.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe sui srɔtoi. Afɔ kooloi komɛi koni amɛdara oya. Henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii wuji. Ni afee ekomɛi koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best suited for my land before I spend money buying the planting material?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ? Dani ooowo nyɔmɔ koni ohe nibii ni akɛduɔ nii

english: You should check your soil type, local rainfall patterns, and water access, and then consult an extension officer to match those conditions with a variety bred for your specific environment.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ̃ lɛ mli. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni anáa lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sɛɛkpee nitsulɔ ko agba sane koni ekɛ nakai shihilɛi lɛ ato srɔtoi kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why might a crop variety yield very well in one town but perform poorly on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ kome mli shi etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react strongly to local climate, soil nutrients, and pest presence. A crop variety that thrives in cooler or wetter regions might struggle in a different area unless it gets additional water or fertilizer.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii waa yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei krokomɛi. ja aná nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi

english: How does having a reliable water supply change what types of crops I can plant on my farm?
ga: Te nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni miyɔɔ lɛ baatsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A reliable water supply allows you to grow crops during the dry season and cultivate delicate, water-sensitive crop varieties that would normally dry up and fail under regular rainfall.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni okwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ shishi.

english: Do crops grown with manual watering or irrigation perform as well as crops grown during the main rainy season?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe nu loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, as long as you provide sufficient water consistently and supply proper soil nutrients, irrigated crops can perform just as well—or even better—than rain-fed crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oooha lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa ni okɛ niyenii ni sa aha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei ni afɔɔ amɛ nu lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai nɔŋŋ. Ekɛ tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ loo ehi fe no po.

english: Why do some crop varieties require regular watering while others can survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi anɔ nu daa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Some varieties have deep root systems or thick leaves that store moisture, while high-yielding or soft-fruited varieties have shallow roots and lose water quickly, requiring frequent watering.
ga: Henɔi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli tse ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo tsei ni woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya, ni ebiɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu shii abɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant two different varieties of the same crop next to each other on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ ni ji henɔ kome ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, but they may flower at different times or need different amounts of water and fertilizer, so it is often easier to separate them into small plots to manage them properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli loo amɛbaabi nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ewaaa akɛ abaajara amɛmli awo shikpɔji bibii amli koni akɛkwɛ amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does it actually mean when a crop variety is described as drought-tolerant?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ atsɔɔ tso ko mli akɛ enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa?

english: It means the plant has physical traits that allow it to stay alive and produce food even when there is little rainfall or a delay in watering.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui ni haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ po.

english: How can I safely test a new crop variety on my farm without risking my whole harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tsei srɔtoi heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ mikpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: Set aside a small test plot on your land to grow a few plants of the new variety first. Watch how much water it needs and how well it grows before planting it on your entire farm.
ga: Saamɔ he bibioo ko ni akaa mɔ akwɛɔ. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni odu tsei heei fioo komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ. Taomɔ nu abɔ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa dani odu amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing food crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield their leaves from heat and keep the surrounding soil cool while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ niyenii tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo ephemeral tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why is my mature cocoa tree growing plenty of thick leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli tse waa lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When a cocoa tree has too many dense branches, it uses all its energy to grow leaves instead of flowers. Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air into the canopy, which encourages the tree to produce blossoms and pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fa tsɔ Kookoo tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires plenty of nitrogen to build strong, green leaves, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside or in rotation with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why should I spread dried grass or leaves on top of the soil around my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a shield. It keeps the sun from evaporating soil moisture quickly, keeps root temperatures cool, and blocks weeds from taking light and nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrink on the branches during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Black Pod disease, a water-loving mold that multiplies rapidly in cold, damp conditions. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning branches to improve airflow helps dry out the pods and reduce infections.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the tubers of my cassava rotting inside the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the ground with water, air cannot reach the roots. Prolonged waterlogging smothers the cassava tubers and encourages soil fungi to attack and decay the roots before harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni damɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agboi dani akpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves or passing along plant viruses. Spraying natural neem oil or insecticides helps eliminate these pests so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei akwɛ̃

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to look for light. Providing stakes lifts the leaves off the wet ground where pests live and spreads them toward sunlight, allowing the plant to generate more energy to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtao la. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of natural wind and insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and keeping the root area cool helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa loo adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni baahã fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa ni ahaa shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for a longer time so my crops do not dry out quickly during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice known as mulching. This mulch acts like a protective shade that prevents the sun from quickly evaporating moisture from the ground, keeping water available for your crops much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo jwɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my sandy farm soil require much more frequent watering than my neighbor's clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ nu shii abɔ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has coarse particles with large gaps, allowing water to drain straight down very quickly. Clay soil has tiny, packed particles that hold onto water like a sponge, keeping moisture around plant roots for many days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi oya waa. Shikpɔŋ yɛ nibii bibii ni ekpɛtɛ nu he tamɔ sponji. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo

english: Why did my crop leaves scorch and wither after I applied fertilizer during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?
