english: Chemical fertilizer is made of concentrated salts that require plenty of water in the soil to dissolve safely. When the ground is dry, the fertilizer draws water out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, which burns the roots and causes the leaves to dry up.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu babaoo ni biɔ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ feɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ baa shã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from heat and water loss. By curling the leaf, less surface area is exposed to the harsh sun and dry winds, helping the plant conserve its internal water until temperatures drop.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ haa hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow when my farm stays flooded with water after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ nu eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on your farm for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, suffocating the roots so they can no longer absorb essential nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ baatsi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ dɔŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon even when the soil around them still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ lolo?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it up from the ground. As long as there is moisture in the soil, the plant will recover and stand upright again once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Be abɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before forming any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience extreme heat stress and shed their flowers to save energy and moisture. High heat can also dry out the flower's pollen, preventing it from forming fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ mli muji lɛ agbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa

english: Why does cassava stay green and survive the long dry season much better than vegetables like garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe aduawai tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cassava develops deep, powerful roots that reach far down into the subsoil where moisture stays trapped deep underground. Garden eggs have shorter roots near the surface, where the sun dries out the top layer of soil very quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ emɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Hulu la lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya waa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin with small cobs because I planted them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ejaakɛ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants stretch upward fast to reach the sunlight before their neighbors, using up energy that should have gone into developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya koni amɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ aba, ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni kulɛ esa akɛ amɛya koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do crops I plant at the very start of the rainy season grow stronger than crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rains of the season trigger a natural release of nutrients trapped in the dry soil, giving early crops a rich boost of nitrogen. Planting early also gives your crops a longer period of consistent rainfall to build deep, healthy root systems before the dry weather returns.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ jeɔ kpo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nitrogen ni naa wa waa yɛ shishijee mli. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa onibii lɛ hu náa be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni etswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which gets washed away from crop roots during heavy rains, or too much standing water suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni baaho kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillar droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the central growing tip of young maize plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ni daraa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell or dry gap that can scorch and kill newly sprouted seeds before the actual rainy season stabilizes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't turn hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa ni efee tso?

english: Cassava roots are generally best harvested between 9 and 12 months after planting; leaving them in the ground too long makes them fibrous, dry, and tough to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii, amɛgbiɔ, ni ewaa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make enough food to feed and swell the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot, when watering is irregular, or when small pests attack the flowers before they can form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, which damage the leaves or transmit plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete aggressively for light and air, stretching upward quickly instead of growing strong stems and thick foliage.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Amɛheɔ oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my crops after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants in the soil equally, and weeds naturally absorb nutrients faster than crops, which is why clearing weeds before fertilizing is necessary.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni jwɛi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do people cover the soil around crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the ground cool, prevents weeds, and adds soil nourishment as it rots.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yaa hiɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: I saw information online about new crop seeds from other countries like Kenya—can I just buy them and plant them directly on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mina saji ni kɔɔ tsei dumɔwui heei ahe yɛ Intanɛt lɛ nɔ. Kɛjɛ maji krokomɛi tamɔ Kenya lɛ, ani manyɛ mahe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Seeds brought from other countries may not be suited for Ghana's soil, rainfall patterns, or local heat. They can easily fail, produce low yields, or accidentally introduce new pests and crop diseases to your soil. It is always safest to plant approved local varieties.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ esaaa Ghana maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo dɔlɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite oya, amɛwo yibii fioo, loo amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai heei aba. ba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ ooodu maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid crop to plant again in the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Harvested seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation. If you plant them, the crops will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields, so it is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu tsei nɛɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the hot dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during severe dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to save water and reduce heat stress. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni akɛbaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of leaves and flowers but failing to produce any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ebɛ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer causes crop plants to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of fruit. Extreme high temperatures can also prevent proper pollination of the flowers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: If a strange bug or creature appears on my crops, should I immediately buy chemical spray to kill it?
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii loo bɔɔ nii komɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ je kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛgbe lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not all insects harm crops; some actually eat harmful pests or help pollinate plants. You should first identify the insect with an extension officer to choose the right control method, as spraying blindly can destroy good insects and waste money.
ga: Kplukai komɛi yeee ŋmɔshi nibii awui. Henɔi komɛi yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛwoɔ tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ o-extension agent lɛ ayɔse kooloo lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ohala gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko shwie tsofa lɛ nɔ shwilafoi lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite kooloi kpakpai ni efite shika.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded farms. Pruning thick tree canopy leaves allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce fungal infection.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni edɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ amli. Tso lɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support a good maize yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, retains moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms or decaying organic plant materials.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain standing on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out oxygen, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots time to soak up water before the hot sun causes evaporation, whereas afternoon watering wastes water to heat and can scorch tender leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛha dɔlɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai bibii.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing much slower than the ones on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Growth rates depend on soil nutrients, access to water, and root cleanlines. Suckers infected with tiny soil pests like nematodes or planted in poor soil will grow very slowly compared to healthy, well-nourished shoots.
ga: Bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. nu ni anáa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsemɔ Suckers ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes emɔ amɛ loo ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo waa kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning or removing excess branches allows light and air to move freely through the tree. This reduces humidity that breeds fungal diseases, deters pests, and helps the tree direct its energy into growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my tree or crop is getting sick just by looking at it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso loo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ hiŋmɛi nɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: You should check the entire plant from leaves to stem. Signs of disease include yellowing leaves, dark spots, stunted growth, or leaves curling up, which often show that pests or diseases are attacking the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ baai kɛyashi shishifãi anɔ. Hela he okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, hei ni tsuɔ, dalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ, loo baai ni ebɔle ehe, ni bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ko miitutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when the ground is waterlogged and drowning the roots. Adding proper fertilizer or improving drainage helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or pest damage. When the plant is stressed, it sheds its blossoms to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ efiteee Kɛji tsei lɛ miihao Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ehi shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: When is the right time to clear weeds from my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeding should be done frequently during the first three to four months after planting. Once the cassava canopy grows dense and shades the ground, weeds will naturally stop growing aggressively.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii abɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3-4 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni ŋmei jwɛi lɛ daa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ. Jwɛi lɛ baakpa yiwalɛ shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist right after a rain and the crop is actively growing. Applying fertilizer during dry soil conditions can burn the plant roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 and 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling, and the soil around the base of the stem starting to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: What brings armyworms into my maize field, and how do they attack?
ga: Mɛni kɛ cutworms baa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛtutuaa?

english: Fall armyworm moths fly into fields at night and lay eggs under the leaves. Once hatched, the caterpillars crawl into the central leaves of the maize plant to feed, creating holes and damaging the growing point.
ga: Katerpillar ŋmei lɛ foɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli gbɛkɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ashishi. Kɛji amɛfɔ pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Enɛ haa buji baa ni efiteɔ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are some of my maize plants growing tall and green while others in the same farm stay short and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, amɛfeɔ kukuji ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Soil nutrients and water are not spread evenly across a field. Plants in spots with poor soil or tight crowding struggle to find food, causing them to turn yellow and stay small while healthier neighbors thrive.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ ejaraaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛkutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning bright yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a cry for help showing the crop lacks nutrients like nitrogen or sufficient water. The plant sacrifices its older lower leaves to send what little food it has left to keep the top leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he tsɛmɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ niyenii fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ aha koni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ahi shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of a larger harvest, you will end up with weak, thin stems that yield very small cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa babaoo Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and look stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than domestic crops. If left unchecked, weeds will starve your crops and choke their growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni ama amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe shia tsei. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ehee leebi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in heat to slow down water loss and protect themselves from burning. Overnight, when it cools down, they draw moisture from the damp soil to recover.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa mli koni nu lɛ akafite ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ Amɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when grown under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants require bright, direct sunlight to convert energy into fruit. Under tree shade, the plant gets stressed and drops its blossoms to save energy just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsake hewalɛ amɛwo aduawai. tsei ashishi Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow and stop growing when rainwater stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe and drink nutrients. Standing water drowns the roots, stopping them from feeding the plant and causing the leaves to turn pale and sick.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ aha tsei niyenii ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling and covered in sticky liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nu ni mli tse ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids attach to the undersides of leaves to suck out the plant's food juices. They secrete a sweet, sticky waste that ruins the leaves and weakens the whole crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu tso lɛ mli niyenii. Amɛjieɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer right at the moment I plant my seeds into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Seeds carry their own food energy to sprout and don't need outside fertilizer immediately. It is better to wait until the young plant forms roots and true leaves so it can actually take in the nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui heɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ kponɔgbɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi tso bibioo lɛ baaná shishifãi kɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ dani enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year without replacement. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores essential nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsakeee. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong green leaves. Applying an NPK or urea fertilizer at the right time restores the green color and helps the plant grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele he miihia baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are little caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that attacks the growing tip of maize. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening reaches the worms while they are actively feeding.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yitsei lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baashɛ kooloi lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot dry spells to protect itself from losing too much water. Once the rains return, the plant naturally sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni efiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too closely, their branches block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and food to produce maximum pods.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ niji tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Once the afternoon temperature cools down, the leaves will stand up straight again.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the maize seed from the agro-dealer mature faster than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Agro-dealer seeds are certified hybrid or improved varieties specifically bred to mature early and survive shorter rainy seasons, whereas saved seeds lose vigor and take longer to produce.
ga: Okwaafoi ajarayeli dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko loo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the bushes on my plot before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the useful organic matter and living organisms in the soil that naturally feed your crops. Clearing without burning allows the dead grass to decompose into natural manure that keeps the soil rich.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni egboi lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaagbala jwɛi ni egboi lɛ amli ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why does striga weed keep appearing only around my corn and sorghum crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa pɛ he lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose seeds wake up only when they smell the roots of cereal crops like corn or sorghum. Rotating your field with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts stops striga seeds from growing.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi pɛ kɛji amɛnu ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ahe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔji lɛ. Ehaa striga dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rainwater collects around the roots in heavy soil, creating conditions for rot-causing fungi. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ baa. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the topsoil or when water stays trapped around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why do extension officers recommend that I plant cowpeas on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpea yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special crops that can capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores the soil fertility that the hungry maize crop took away.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ, ni abele ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ejie kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop stems with dry bush grass help them stay alive in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from stealing moisture from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves up to catch more direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to feed and grow large tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off the damp ground where rot and diseases spread.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛtaoɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulb agboi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ ni helai gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ la mli, ni amɛjieɔ be babaoo kɛyaa, ni tso ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady for about two to three weeks rather than sowing after the very first rain. Planting too early can cause your seeds to sprout and then die if a short dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shi aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by a plant disease spread by tiny whiteflies. When these insects feed on your tomato plants, they pass on a virus that stunts the leaves and prevents the plant from setting good fruit.
ga: Tso hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye o-tomato tsei lɛ Egbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tomato tsei lɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and rot in the ground when left in very wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked with water, air cannot reach the roots. The roots suffocate, and naturally occurring fungi in the wet soil quickly attack and rot the softening cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni ŋmeii ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii shishifãi ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if they experience water stress, extreme sun heat, or damage from sucking pests like capsids. Maintaining good shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ. Hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids ni nuɔ nu lɛ efiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the small flowers and young fruits falling off my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers and small fruits when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings rapidly between very dry and very wet. Regular watering and partial shade during hot afternoons help protect the crop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomatoes splitting open and bursting at the bottom before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes burst when their water supply changes suddenly, like heavy rainfall after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows too fast for the skin to stretch, causing it to crack open. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering prevents this.
ga: Tomato tswaa kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni ehewolo lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe. cause rupture Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Flowers drop when the plant is under stress, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Without insects to transfer pollen or enough water to support growth, the plant cannot form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing big green leaves but no cassava tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi cassava shishifã ko bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or very rich soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf growth above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ babaoo wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do the roots of my maize plant carry fertilizer from the wet dirt up into the leaves?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Plant roots act like drinking straws. They suck up water dissolved with soil nutrients and pull it up through tiny veins inside the stem all the way to the leaves.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ. Amɛmuɔ nu ni haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni amɛtsɔɔ lá fãji bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables grow poorly in hard red clay soil compared to dark forest soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa mli kɛ akɛto koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Hard red clay soil gets packed tightly, making it hard for soft roots to push through and search for food. Dark soil has rotted leaves that hold air and water better for easy root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa ni ebɔle ehe Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛna niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ baai ni fiteɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot starting from the bottom tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shaded conditions. Rain drops splash the fungus onto the pod's bottom, causing it to rot and ruin the beans inside.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni efiteɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are tiny red insects causing my cowpea leaves to turn brown and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ ha mi-cowpea baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: These are red spider mites. They hide under leaves and suck out the plant's juices during dry weather, causing the leaves to lose moisture, turn reddish-brown, and die.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii tsuru. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ-ŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ.

english: What causes the base of my pepper stem to turn soft and wet right at the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is stem rot caused by excessive water sitting around the base of the plant. Poor soil drainage creates conditions where soil fungi attack the outer skin of the stem.
ga: Enɛ ji shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni sũ mli ŋmeii tutuaa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baa.

english: Why are my vegetable seeds failing to sprout after I buried them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the soil dries out completely, or if the soil is too wet and suffocates the seed before it can break open.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtswaa.

english: Why does sticky liquid leak out of my orange tree stem when I cut off a dead branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ejɛ mi-orange tso lɛ shishi beni mifo tsei lɛ aniji ni egboi lɛ.

english: The liquid is sap, which is the plant's food and water transport system. When a stem is wounded, sap leaks out until the plant hardens the spot to seal the wound.
ga: Nu lɛ ji nu, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo. Kɛji tso lɛ pila Nu lɛ mli nu lɛ baajɛ mli aahu kɛyashi tso lɛ baafee shiŋŋ koni ekɛtsi pilamɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden sticks to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight. Staking the vines keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allowing the plant to make more food and produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai eshwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and heavy bunches at the top. Propping them up with sturdy wooden Y-sticks supports the extra weight and keeps wind from uprooting them.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋtayaai ni wa ni tamɔ Y fi esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua muji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekajie lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as very hot weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist and using mulch to cool the ground helps save the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in cold, damp weather. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunshine in and removing infected pods helps keep the tree healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo abote mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist allows the roots to carry calcium to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ calcium baa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up. Rotating your land with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to be harvested underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open from the tubers expanding underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my crops yield so much more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing them early removes that competition so your crops get all the energy they need to produce a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ojie amɛ mra. Enɛ baajie nakai akaŋshii lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its strength and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my farm right before it rains or after the rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain. If you put it on dry ground right before a heavy downpour, the rain can wash the fertilizer away before the crop roots get a chance to soak it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo he ko ni egbi dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tso shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkuu nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can harvest more from my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow bigger and produce a heavier harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves catch plenty of sun, they make food that travels down to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Amɛfeɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes small caterpillars to chew holes in the centers of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on corn plants. Catching them early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides into the plant funnel will protect your corn from being destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɛɔ lɛ bio-insecticide ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baabu o-ŋmã lɛ he kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of rainfall for all plants on the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa nugbɔ babaoo?

english: Even if water is plenty, weeds steal the hidden food in the dirt that your main crop needs. Weeds also attract plant diseases and pests that can easily move over to damage your main crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi hu baanyɛ aju niyenii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni hereɔ bo lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ mli. Jwɛi hu gbalaa tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya koni amɛfite onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants steady, moderate water helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi kɛ baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat. As the grass rots, it also turns into rich food for your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Ebafeɔ niyenii babaoo hu kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Will my cassava rot if I leave it in the ground after it is mature?
ga: Ani mi-cassava lɛ baagbo kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava is unique because the roots stay fresh underground for several months even after they mature. The soil acts like a natural storage place until you are ready to dig them up for food or sale.
ga: Cassava yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ po sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaafo mli ni okɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii loo okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: If I spray my vegetables with pest medicine, how long must I wait before harvesting them to sell at the market?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie aduawai anɔ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani akpa ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: You must observe what is called a 'pre-harvest interval' or waiting period, which usually ranges from 3 to 14 days depending on the specific chemical. Selling crops immediately after spraying can poison consumers with harmful chemical residues.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘dani ŋmaakpamɔ’ loo mɛmɔ be lɛ fɔɔ baa kɛjɛɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14, ni enɛ damɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ lɛ awo mɛi ni yeɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: Are the more expensive crop medicines always better than the cheaper ones available at the agrochemical shop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛduɔ nii ni jara wa lɛ hi fe tsofai ni jara waaa ni yɔɔ agrochemical shwapoi amli lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not necessarily. What matters most is the active chemical ingredient and whether it targets your specific pest or disease. A cheaper medicine with the correct active ingredient will work much better than an expensive one designed for a different problem.
ga: Jeee nakai kwraa. Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji kɛji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ o-pest loo hela lɛ nɔ. Tsofa ni jara waaa ni nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsofa ni jara wa ni afee aha naagba kroko.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease needs chemical treatment or if the plant will just heal on its own?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko he miihia ni akɛ tsofa atsu he nii loo tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa?

english: Crop diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, or heavy pest attacks rarely heal on their own and can quickly spread across your whole farm. If you notice spreading spots, rotting leaves, or wilting, you should identify the cause and apply the right treatment early before the crop is ruined.
ga: Tse helai ni ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa kɛbaa. Efɔɔɔ kaa akɛ eyaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji ona hei ni egbɛ eshwã, baai ni egbo, loo egbɔjɔ Esa akɛ oyoo nɔ ni kɛba ni okɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ja lɛ atsu nii mra. dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and leaf curl in tomatoes are usually caused by plant viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or sometimes by a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo bei komɛi lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess leaves and clearing weeds to let sunlight and air into the farm helps prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize plants roll up their leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to reduce surface area and stop water from evaporating too fast in extreme heat. It is a natural survival trick, but if the leaves stay rolled in the cool morning, it means the crop desperately needs watering.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso hu? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nu babaoo he miihia tso lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very big leaves but refusing to produce any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji waa shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo pepper ko lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus only on leaf growth. To produce flowers and fruits, the plant needs balanced nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ pɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm eating the plant. If you check inside the central funnel of the plant, you will often find the worm hiding there.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni egbee shi ni eye tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji okwɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo jɛmɛ.

english: Why are my young mango fruits falling off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Young fruits drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks critical soil nutrients, or is attacked by pests like fruit flies. The tree also naturally sheds extra fruits it cannot support.
ga: Yibii bibii baagbee shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ Tsei hu woɔ aduawai krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ aye abua yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I use the same weedkiller chemical on both my cassava farm and my maize farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ fɛɛ mli?

english: No, because different crops tolerate different chemicals. A weedkiller designed for broad-leaf weeds might safely clear a maize field but will kill or severely damage cassava plants.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi kpɛɔ tsofai srɔtoi anaa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee aha jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli shweshweeshwe. Shi ebaagbe ŋmei tso lɛ loo ebaafite lɛ waa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain or banana trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain loo banana tso yɛ emasɛi? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch and die in full, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have very large leaves that provide living shade and keep the air damp, helping the cocoa survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai wuji waa ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Eye ebua kookoo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if I am putting my cassava stem cuttings into the ground the right way up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ mi yucca niji lɛ miiwo gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds or nodes along the cassava stem cutting; these tiny bumps should point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and shoots struggle to grow, leading to very low yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ he lɛ, esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛi shishi lɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to chew holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmei bibioo ko ŋmɔ bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the soft center leaves of maize plants during the day and eats them. Checking your farm early and using recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ amɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up dry soil without soaking deep enough, creating a warm, damp environment that rots the seeds. It is safer to wait until the ground is thoroughly soaked by two or three steady rains before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plants face stress from extreme hot afternoon heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their pepper plants with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material—called mulching—protects the soil from the harsh sun, traps water so you water less often, and stops weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkaná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad to let weeds grow close to my young crops even if the weeds are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe, kɛji amɛji bibii po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water that your young crops desperately need. Clearing them early gives your main crops a head start to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ he hiaa waa lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii titrii lɛ aje shishi amɛda waa.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni amɛkɛkwɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make the food required to grow big underground tubers. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni eha niyenii ni he hiaa koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akafite tsei.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and rot after putting it inside sacks for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite beni mikɛ otsii fioo komɛi ehi kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize rots if it is put into sacks while it still holds dampness from the field. Drying your corn kernels thoroughly on tarpaulins under the sun until they are hard before bagging prevents fungi and mold from spoiling your harvest.
ga: Abɛi baagbo kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku mli be mli ni nu ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ lolo. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarp nɔ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why are my yams harvesting so small even though the leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sometimes yam plants put all their energy into growing leaves instead of tubers if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Balanced soil nutrients and proper staking ensure the leaf energy goes down into growing big tubers.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Sũ mli niyenii ni ja kɛ ŋmeii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kudɔɔ baai lɛ ahewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Do I really need to build high mounds before planting yams, or can I plant directly on flat ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu sweet potatoes loo manyɛ madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into large tubers. Making high mounds loosens the soil, improves water drainage, and gives room for the tuber to grow big without hitting hard earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I select the right yam seeds to make sure I get a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato dumɔwui ni sa koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose clean, healthy seed tubers without soft spots, mold, or insect holes. Using clean seed sets prevents carrying soil diseases into your field and gives your crops a strong start.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ŋmei, loo kooloi abu bɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni oha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do yam vines need to be trained on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and helping the leaves catch light.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa baai lɛ náa la.

english: What causes my yams to rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Underground tuber rot is usually caused by excess water sitting in the soil combined with fungal or bacterial infections. Planting on well-drained mounds and using undamaged seed pieces protects tubers from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni abua naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli loo bacteria mli lɛ fataa he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu bulb lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: When is the best time of year to plant my yams to get the highest yield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu sweet potato koni ená yibii babaoo?

english: Yams are best planted towards the end of the dry season or at the very start of the early rains. Planting early allows the seed tubers to sprout naturally as rains begin, giving them the maximum time to grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu sweet potato yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ayitsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ haa anáa be ni fa fe fɛɛ ni akɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell if my soil lacks the nutrients needed to produce heavy yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii?

english: If your crops produce pale, yellowish leaves or thin vines and tiny tubers season after season, your soil is low in nutrients like potassium and phosphorus, which tubers need to build mass.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo wain tsei bibii kɛ be mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tubers he hiaa koni amɛma mass

english: Why do my harvested yams start shrinking and sprouting while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni ekwɛ̃ beni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up and use their internal water to sprout after a few months. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn slows down water loss and delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Can I plant beans or cowpeas between my yam mounds, or will they choke my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe lɛ ateŋ? Aloo amɛbaafite midumɔ nii lɛ.

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas between mounds actually helps your yams. Legumes capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, while also covering the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: What is making dark, ugly holes in my yam tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu diŋ ni yɔɔ mi shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato tuber lɛ mli lɛ ba?

english: Yam beetles and soil worms feed on tubers as they develop, leaving holes and dark scars. Changing the crop location every year and treating seed pieces before planting keeps these pests away.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa bu kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ baa. Kɛ́ atsake he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa afi, ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ fãi komɛi anɔ dani aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing bent and crooked instead of standing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems often grow crooked when they are planted too shallowly, exposed to strong winds, or planted in shady areas where they have to bend toward the sunlight.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ kɛji adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why do my young maize stalks bend over crookedly towards the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ekoto shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks bend over, or lodge, mainly due to strong winds, shallow root development in hard soil, or stem borer insects weakening the base of the stalk.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ ebɔle loo eje kpo. Nɔ titri ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ sũ ni wa mli loo kooloi ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli, ni haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Can I grow healthy tomatoes without using chemical medicines to kill insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can manage pests naturally by spraying solutions made from neem leaves or wood ash mixed with soapy water, and by planting strong-smelling herbs around your tomatoes to repel insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsa tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai loo tso sũ ni akɛ nu ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ baashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni aduɔ yɛ Tomatoes he koni akɛshwie kooloi bibii lɛ nɔ

english: What natural alternatives can I use instead of chemical medicine to protect my cabbage from worms?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛtoɔ tsofai ahe lɛ manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mikɛbu mi-cabbage lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Crushed hot pepper mixed with water and mild soap, or neem seed extracts, can be sprayed on cabbage leaves to repel caterpillars without using harsh synthetic chemicals.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ nu kɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem dumɔwu mli nu efutu mli Abaanyɛ akɛshwie kaabe baai anɔ koni akɛshwie ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why is it bad if I put too much chemical medicine on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ ehiii lɛ?
