english: Excessive chemical medicine can kill friendly insects like bees and midges that pollinate cocoa flowers, weaken soil health over time, and leave dangerous chemical residues.
ga: Tsofa lɛ babaoo baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ni amɛshi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ sɛɛ

english: How do plantain trees help young cocoa trees grow better in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist for cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ aha kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do older farmers plant legumes like cowpeas alongside their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ duɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops grow stronger.
ga: Legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the silks at the top turn dark brown, and the kernels become hard when pressed with your thumbnail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko nyɛ nɔ.

english: What signs show that my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko eshɛ klalo akɛ abaafo?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is my citrus tree taking several years without showing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ yaa afii babaoo ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Fruit trees like citrus need to establish strong root systems and sturdy branches before they can bear fruit. Depending on the variety, it requires patience as it can take 3 to 5 years to start producing.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ citrus lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa dani amɛwo yibii. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Eheɔ tsuishitoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ ebaahe afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani aje nitsumɔ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before I plant maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize uses this natural fertilizer to grow strong without you needing to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why should I leave dried leaves and cut grass on top of the soil around my vegetables instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni afo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Aduawai moŋ fe ni abaashã?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and slowly turns into rich plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without plantains or shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect the tender cocoa from high heat and keep the surrounding air humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden sticks to climb on to give me bigger tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to capture sunlight and turn it into energy, which is stored in the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sunlight and don't rot from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli lɛ Staking baaye abua ni ewó tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni egbooo kɛjɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli

english: Can my cassava crops survive on my farm if the rains stop for two or three months?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ?

english: Yes, cassava is naturally built for dry spells. When water is scarce, it drops its outer leaves to conserve moisture and relies on its deep, thick root system to pull water from deep underground until the rains return.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, abɔ cassava yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha e-dry spell lɛ. Kɛ nu faaa Ebaatsɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller maize cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibii loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a signal that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. To keep growing, the maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to move whatever nitrogen it has left up to the fresh top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni eya nɔ eda Abɛi tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ aya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center funnel of my young maize plants and eating holes through the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which target the softest, newest leaves growing in the middle of the plant where it is dark and safe from birds and heat. Catching them early with recommended sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ enɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ɔ baai bibii ni fe fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni yɔɔ duŋ ni okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ bɛ he lɛ anɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die right after they start showing green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛjeɔ tomato eŋɔli kpojiemɔ shishi etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters through the roots and blocks the water pipes inside the plant stem. Once blocked, water cannot reach the leaves, causing the plant to dry up while still green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ mli ni etsĩɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ atsĩ naa lɛ, nu nyɛŋ abote baai lɛ amli. Gbimɔ tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before the fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani yibii lɛ po jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, drought, or nutrient stress. The plant aborts the blossoms to conserve its energy and survive rather than trying to produce fruits it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ kpe. Tsei baafo fɔfɔii amli koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee nɔ ko ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ.

english: Why did my maize farm give me a very poor yield this year even though I did the exact same work as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa afi nɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nitsumɔ ni mitsu yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Crop yields change because soil loses nutrients over time if they are not replaced, and weather patterns like rainfall timing can vary greatly from year to year even if your farming effort remains the same.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ kɛji akɛ atsakeee lɛ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake kwraa kɛjɛ afi kɛya afi. Eyɛ mli akɛ okwaayeli he mɔdɛŋbɔɔ lɛ kã he eji nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Why do crops on one side of my farm grow very tall while the ones on the other side stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Soil quality is not uniform across a farm; variations in soil depth, water drainage, shade, or past nutrient depletion can cause uneven crop growth on the same plot of land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ ejaaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni elaaje yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How does unpredictable rainfall affect the development of my cocoa pods?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ saa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irregular rains confuse cocoa trees during their flowering and pod-filling stages, which can lead to flower drop, smaller pods, or higher susceptibility to fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ futuɔ fɔfɔi be lɛ kɛ be ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ teŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite, ŋmeii bibii, loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off before the tubers are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani bulb lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Premature yellowing and dropping of cassava leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil or an infection like Cassava Mosaic Disease, which starves the plant of energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo oyɛ hela ko tamɔ cassava mosaic hela ni haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Flower drop in peppers is often caused by heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, chili ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wilt and die under the hot afternoon sun even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Young seedlings have shallow roots and tender stems; intense direct heat causes water to evaporate from their leaves faster than their small roots can suck water from the ground.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni ejɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Can diseases from my neighbor's crop field spread to my healthy crops?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, and pests like fall armyworms can easily travel between farms through the wind, flowing water, insects, or shared farming tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai ni ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworm kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kooloi bibii loo okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so that I can harvest more crops from a small space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaaa nii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a good crop harvest before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa dani madu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, smells rich and earthy, holds moisture well without staying soggy, and contains visible life like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, eyɛ sũ ni mli wa ni sũ yɔɔ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli hu yɛ ni abaanyɛ ana, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even after I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than crops, so they steal the fertilizer and water from the soil before your main plants can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otsei titrii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help keep the foliage green and improve your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the exact plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, while legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating these crops naturalizes the soil food supply and reduces soil-borne pests for the next planting season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ atsake tsei nɛɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei ni miida lɛ amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist and the young crops are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tsei bibii lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Leaving some large trees or planting plantains beside them creates a canopy shade that protects the young cocoa plants until they grow sturdy enough for direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why must I erect tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible so they can manufacture food. Lifting the vines off the ground allows the plant to produce larger and healthier yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Plantain shishitoo lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy cluster of fruit.
ga: Tsobii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii akui wuji ni tsii.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaf whorls of my young corn crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Small holes in the upper leaves of corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender inner leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem leaf extract can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mligbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early using soapy water or neem oil spray protects the leaves and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water cuts off air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is an uneven water supply in the root zone. Watering your tomato plants consistently and mulching around the roots helps hold moisture and lowers soil temperature.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ sũ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi.

english: How many years after planting does a young oil palm tree start bearing palm nut bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu mu tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually begin producing their first fruit bunches between 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the field, reaching maximum yield when they are around 8 to 10 years old.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 teŋ beni ajie amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Ni amɛbaaná yibiiwoo babaoo beni amɛye aaafee afii 8 kɛyashi 10 lɛ.

english: Why does oil palm grow and produce better in heavy rainfall areas like the Western Region compared to drier parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? kɛ akɛto Ghana hei ni nu egbi lɛ ahe.

english: Oil palm trees require continuous high moisture and high humidity all year round to develop heavy fruit bunches; dry conditions cause the tree to stop growing fruit and produce only male flowers.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo aya nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ.

english: How much space do I need to leave between my oil palm seedlings when planting them in the field?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miidu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ ehe baahia ni matsɔ mu tso dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Oil palm trees should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern so their large leaves have enough room to capture sunlight without crowding or shading neighboring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni baai wuji lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa loo amɛtsiii hulu lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees during the first year?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi mu tsei ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops between young palms for the first two years, but you must keep the crops at least 2 meters away from the base of the palm seedlings so they do not steal water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ tsei lɛ ahi shi kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 2 kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ ashishi koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my oil palm tree producing only male flowers and no palm nut bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ ni ŋmeii akui ko bɛ lɛ?

english: When an oil palm tree experiences extreme stress—such as a long dry season, severe weed competition, or poor soil fertility—it conserves energy by producing male flowers instead of female fruit-bearing flowers.
ga: Kɛ́ mu tsei kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Weeds kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa. aloo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Oil palm tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi hii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ fɔfɔi yei ni woɔ yibii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of the small palm nuts on my fresh bunches turning black and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ miniji ni hiɛ ka lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop and blackening are usually caused by poor pollination, water shortages during the fruit development stage, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium and boron.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ yibii ni fiteɔ oya kɛ ediŋŋ baa ji ŋmeii ni ehiii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Nu ni faaa yɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ boron.

english: How can I tell that a bunch of palm nuts is completely mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sugar palm dumɔwui lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A palm nut bunch is fully ripe when its outer fruits turn a deep reddish-orange color and at least 5 to 10 loose fruits naturally fall off the bunch onto the ground around the tree trunk.
ga: Nuts kuu ko ekwɛ̃ kwraa beni kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai 5 kɛyashi 10 ni etse amɛhe lɛ baajɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower green leaves on my palm trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: While it is normal for the oldest leaves at the very bottom to age and dry up, widespread yellowing of leaves usually indicates a nutrient deficiency in the soil, particularly nitrogen or potassium.
ga: Baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ po baagbɔ ni amɛbaagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ, nitrogen loo potasium.

english: Should I cut off all the lower leaves of my oil palm trees during farm maintenance?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ be mli?

english: You should only prune dry, dead, or diseased lower fronds; cutting off healthy green leaves reduces the tree's ability to make food and leads to smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbi, egbo, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa yibii lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: What causes small brown and orange spots on the leaves of my young palm trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa? Mitso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Leaf spots are typically caused by fungal infections that spread easily when young trees are overcrowded, shaded by tall weeds, or when there is too much standing moisture on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji tsei bibii eyi obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. Jwɛi kakadaŋŋ ayɛ ni haa hulutsoo. aloo kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: My old cocoa trees are not producing as many pods as they used to years ago, even though I care for them the same way. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi cacao tso momo lɛ ewooo ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ lɛ yeɔ nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Cocoa trees have a peak productive age, usually between 10 and 25 years. As they grow older, their internal systems slow down and they yield fewer pods, meaning it might be time to prune heavily or replace them with new hybrid seedlings.
ga: Cocoa tso lɛ ji nɔ ni eyeɔ afii babaoo fe fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi kɛjɛɔ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Emli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baafee mlɛo ni ebaaha pods fioo pɛ aba. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ be ebashɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli waa loo akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ atsake.

english: My oil palm trees have grown very tall and produce very few fruit bunches now. Can I make them yield heavily again, or do I need to cut them down?
ga: Mi-oil palm tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ bianɛ. Ani ebaanyɛ ewo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ loo esa akɛ afo mli?

english: Oil palms reach their peak yield limit around 20 to 25 years. Beyond this age, yield permanently drops and harvesting becomes difficult, making clearing and replanting with improved dwarf varieties the most profitable choice.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baashɛ he ni ekɛbaatsu nii fe fɛɛ lɛ he aaafee afii 20 kɛyashi 25 yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa ni ŋmaakpamɔ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa. Enɛ haa dwarf henɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop setting new fruits after harvesting them a few times, even when the bushes are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ kpa yibii heei womɔ yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lolo moŋ

english: Tomatoes are short-term crops with a natural lifecycle. Once they complete their main flowering and fruiting phase, the plant's energy naturally runs out, signaling that production has reached its end and it is time to replant.
ga: Tomato ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ. Beni amɛgbe fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo fã titri lɛ naa lɛ. Tso hewalɛ baaho yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nifeemɔ eba naagbee. Ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: If I leave my cassava tubers in the ground for a very long time after they mature, will they keep growing bigger and yield more food?
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmei shishifã lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, beni egbɔ lɛ ebaatsɔ agbo ni efee agbo. Ni onine ashɛ niyenii babaoo nɔ loo onine shɛɛɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava roots reach their best starch quality around 9 to 12 months. Leaving them in the soil too long causes the roots to turn woody, fibrous, or rot, reducing their useful yield even if the tubers look large.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛ starch ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ tso, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni anáa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara moŋ.

english: I noticed that my plantain farm produces smaller bunches after a few harvest cycles from the same stool. Why does the yield drop over time?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kome mli lɛ shii 2-3 sɛɛ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ?

english: Over successive harvest cycles, the underground root system gets crowded and exhausts the surrounding soil, leading to weaker shoots and smaller bunches unless old suckers are thinned out and fresh soil nutrients are added.
ga: yɛ kpamɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Ja ajie ŋmeii momo lɛ bibii ni akɛ niyenii heei efata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of big leaves for months before the tubers inside the ground actually start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai wuji babaoo nyɔji babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants spend their early months building leaves and vines to capture sunlight. Once the leafy top is full, the plant redirects its stored energy underground to build the tuber during the second half of its life cycle.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ nyɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ maa amɛbaai kɛ wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhere hulu la lɛ atuu. Kɛji baai lɛ eyi tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii yɛ ewala be lɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants flowering while they are still very small during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni eji gbekɛ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants face severe heat or drought stress, they trigger early flowering as a survival mechanism to produce seeds before dying, even if the plant itself is too small to carry a big crop.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ mli haomɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa fɔfɔii fɔɔ mra akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ji bibioo tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ tso agbo moŋ, shi.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow and dry from the bottom up while the ears are drying. Is my crop dying from a disease?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni toi lɛ miigbi lɛ. Ani hela miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: As maize reaches full maturity, it naturally pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to fill out the seeds, causing the lower leaves to dry up. This is a normal sign of maturity rather than a disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ mɔ ko miida moŋ fe hela.

english: Why does my maize yield less grain every year when I plant it on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Repeatedly growing the same crop on the same spot drains those specific nutrients completely, leading to poorer growth unless you rotate with legumes like beans or apply fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baaho kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni ehiii kwraa Ja okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fata he.

english: I planted orange trees from seeds, but after four years, they still have not borne any fruit. Why are my trees taking so long?
ga: Mikɛ dumɔwui du akutu tso ko. Shi afii ejwɛ eho. Amɛbako yibii lolo. Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ heɔ be babaoo nɛkɛ?

english: Fruit trees grown directly from seeds go through a long youth phase that can last 6 to 10 years before fruiting. Grafted seedlings fruit much sooner—usually in 2 to 3 years—because the grafted stem comes from a mature branch.
ga: Yibii tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsɔɔ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni baanyɛ ahi shi afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 ejaakɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ tso nine ni eda lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hottest part of the day even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Crops lose water rapidly through their leaves in high midday heat to cool themselves down. If they lose water faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil, they temporarily wilt to save moisture, but they usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛhe. Kɛji amɛlaaje nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ebaagbo be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: How does installing irrigation pipes and water pumps help my farm perform better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu shwiemɔ paipii kɛ nu pɔmpii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ nu pɛ ni mikɛaafɔ̃ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pipes and pumping stations deliver a steady, controlled supply of water directly to your fields year-round. This prevents crop stress during dry spells and allows you to farm and harvest even outside the normal rainy seasons.
ga: Paipii kɛ pɔmpii kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni akudɔɔ lɛ baa oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni otsi haomɔ ni baa oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli ni okpaa nii yɛ nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ daa lɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water sits on my farm field for several days without draining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo ni efooo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns the roots by blocking air from reaching them. Without oxygen, the roots stop working and cannot feed the plant, causing the leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eeetsi amɛnaa koni ekashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive when I plant them in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow under the canopy of large forest trees. Direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out their roots, so they need shade plants like plantains to protect them in their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do small black spots start appearing on my cocoa pods after a period of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ ji lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ebɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa be ko sɛɛ.

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and leaves wet droplets on cocoa pods, which encourages fungal diseases like Black Pod. The fungus thrives in wet conditions and spreads fast if the farm lacks proper air movement.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni eshiɔ nu ni mli efɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ hewalɛ. Fuji lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava alongside my young cocoa trees, or will they harm the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe? Aloo amɛbaaye kookoo lɛ awui?

english: You can plant temporary crops alongside young cocoa for shade and food, but if planted too close, cassava will compete heavily with cocoa roots for soil nutrients and water. Proper spacing is necessary so both crops survive.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo tsei bibii adu be kukuoo mli tsei kɛha hulutsoo kɛ niyenii. Shi kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ cocoa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa he miihia koni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Does heavy rainfall or excessive watering wash away the fertilizer I apply around my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaje mli?

english: Yes, heavy water flow causes runoff that washes surface fertilizer away before roots can drink it, or pushes it too deep into the ground where roots cannot reach. Applying smaller amounts of fertilizer closer to root zones helps avoid this.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shwiili ni hoɔ lɛ feɔ nu ni hoɔ ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Aloo tsimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafee naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why does the soil in some parts of my farm dry out fast while other parts stay muddy for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi hu feɔ muji gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Soil composition varies across fields; sandy soil has large spaces that let water drain quickly, while clay soil holds onto water like a sponge. Understanding your soil type helps you know how much and how often to water.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Kɛ́ onu shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli kɛ shii abɔ ni esa akɛ okɛwo mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the dry Harmattan season even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ?

english: The Harmattan brings dry, dusty winds and low humidity that pull moisture out of plant leaves very quickly. Crops slow down their growth process as a defense mechanism to conserve energy and survive the dry air.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa. sũ kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi ni gbalaa hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ hewalɛ he ni ahiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why does soil on sloped ground seem to lose its moisture much faster than soil on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on sloped land, gravity pulls the water downhill across the surface as runoff before it has time to soak deep into the soil. Flat land allows water to settle and sink down into the root area.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ, Gravity lɛ gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ nu ni hoɔ dani enáa be ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ kɛyaa shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my yam farm need tall wooden stakes for the vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight allows the plant to produce food, which is then stored underground to form big, healthy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee tsɔnei wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away from the root zone, or the soil itself may be worn out and need fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every season if I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously exhausts the specific nutrients that crop relies on. Rotating your maize with nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore the soil's natural strength.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Okɛ nibii ni haa nitrogen-fixing tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Very high temperatures damage the pollen, causing the plant to shed the blossoms instead of setting tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomatoi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their small pods and flowers during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods and flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture during droughts. When water is low, the tree preserves its main body rather than spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ, tso lɛ buɔ eshishigbɛ fã lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Curled leaves are commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides. They can also transfer viruses that cause the leaves to deform and stop growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni fiteɔ baai ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa lɛ hu amɛshwã.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil where excess water prevents air from reaching the roots, encouraging fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine nɛɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to one another, the growing crops fight for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The season's first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil and can be followed by several dry weeks. Seeds may sprout with that initial rain but will dry out and die before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni hɔmɔ baanyɛ aba otsii babaoo sɛɛ. Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Shi ebaagbi ni ebaagbo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle intense heat and full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to shield them from harsh light and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which then feeds the tuber growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while protecting them from rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ eyeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small and skinny when I plant the stem cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close to each other, their root systems compete for soil nutrients, water, and space. Giving each cassava stem enough distance allows the roots to expand freely into thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off before the harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that it has been infected by cassava mosaic disease. Without enough nitrogen or healthy leaves, the plant cannot produce green pigment to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ cassava mosaic hela emɔ lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen loo baai ni mli wa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni amɛkɛye amɛhe.

english: Why is my maize crop growing very tall green stalks but failing to form big, full corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii wuji ni eda lɛ?

english: Maize plants need adequate soil nutrients early on and plenty of water right when the silks appear to form full kernels. If water or nutrients drop during the flowering period, the plant puts its remaining strength into keeping the stalk alive instead of filling out the cob.
ga: Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra. Ni nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ kɛji siliki lɛ je kpo akɛ dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ba shi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ cob baafata he lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my crop field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilization requires moisture in the soil to dissolve the chemical granules so plant roots can safely drink them in. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil leaves concentrated salts directly on the roots, which can scorch and burn the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aya shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ni ashã amɛ

english: What causes small worms to eat ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms, a pest that burrows deep into the tender central leaves (the whorl) of young maize plants. They hide inside the plant canopy during the daytime to escape heat, eating the leaf tissues before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛjo latsaa lɛ naa foi. Amɛyeɔ baa mli fãji dani cob lɛ feɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruits even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani aduawai lɛ po shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. When soil moisture swings rapidly from dry to soaked, the plant cannot move calcium to the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their blossoms without growing any pepper pods during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni miduuu pepper pods yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can physically knock delicate flowers off pepper stems before pollination occurs. Additionally, overly wet soil stresses roots and restricts oxygen, forcing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ajɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ faaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and pale even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal fertilizer, soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Even with good rain, the crops suffer because the weeds consume the vital soil minerals first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kudɔɔ onibii. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from full sun to survive their early months. Plantains grow quickly with large, broad leaves that shield the delicate cocoa shoots while providing extra food or income for your household while the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu ni naa wa waa lɛ he hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshia lɛ náa niyenii loo shika kroko be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green tissue. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant early in its growth will help keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia babaoo koni ekɛfee fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know which direction to point cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ atsɔɔ beni okɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Look for the small buds on the stem where leaves used to grow; those buds must point upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new roots and shoots to fight gravity, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ koni amɛwu amɛshi hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: What makes my tomato leaves curl up tightly and stop producing fresh fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibii heei ni amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil spray and pulling out severely damaged plants helps protect the rest of your garden.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Control Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ ni ojie tsei ni efite waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu obɔɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize hurt my main crop's growth?
ga: Ani cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaná ŋmãa titri lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Cowpeas actually help your maize because legumes trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. As long as you leave enough space between rows so they do not overcrowd each other, this mixed planting keeps your soil richer naturally.
ga: Cowpeas baanyɛ aye abua o-corn lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni obaashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ koni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, Nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ baaye abua oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily and spreads them out to capture maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help during hot, dry days?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass on the soil creates a barrier called mulch that keeps soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly into the hot air. Over time, the dry grass also rots and enriches the soil with natural organic matter.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Be ni be hoɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the central funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of young maize. Checking your field regularly and applying targeted treatments directly into the plant funnels early will prevent major leaf damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii amli baai lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa ni okɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, erratic watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weeks helps the plant keep its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ amɛ ŋmeii.

english: How do weevils get inside my dried, stored maize grains even when kept in closed sacks?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi ni ato lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto kotokui ni aŋã mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid inside the grain while the maize is still drying in the field before harvest. To prevent them from destroying stored grain, dry your maize thoroughly until hard and store it in airtight bags or with safe grain protectants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miigbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa. Enɛ ji koni akafite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or when the ground is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ baai ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan or dry season, hot winds and intense sun cause cocoa trees to lose water quickly, making leaves dry out and drop as a survival reaction to protect the tree.
ga: Yɛ harmattan loo hulutsoo be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi koni ekɛbu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni niji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that get heavy at the top; tiny pests like nematodes can also weaken the underground roots, causing the plant to tip over easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underwater when soil drainage is poor and heavy rain collects around the roots, allowing fungal rots to develop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Proper spacing ensures that plants do not compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, while allowing air to flow and prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa tsei amli helai baa.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long heat spell; if seeds sprout immediately, the hot ground can dry out and kill the young seedlings before main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, hei ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe tsei bibii dani nugbɔ aba.

english: What is eating small holes in the soft center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-babi ŋmãa lɛ baa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing whorl of young maize plants to feed on the fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and grow aggressively to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛdaraa oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: How can I test if the seeds I bought are good quality before planting them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can do a simple water test by putting a sample of seeds in a bowl of water; seeds that sink to the bottom are generally healthy and good for planting, while floating seeds are usually dry or damaged and won't grow well.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nu lɛ okwɛ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni akɛwoɔ nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni sa kɛha dumɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi loo efite ni amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the best crop variety that buyers in Ghanaian markets prefer to buy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛhe lɛ?

english: Market preferences depend on traits like crop size, taste, color, and shelf life, so consulting local extension officers or market traders helps you identify certified crop varieties that attract higher prices and quick sales.
ga: Jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ damɔ sui tamɔ tso lɛ dalɛ, ŋɔɔmɔ, su kɛ shɛlɛf wala nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli shweremɔ he nitsulɔi loo jarayeli jarayelɔi lɛ gba sane lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oyoo tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni gbalaa jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ jarayeli oya.

english: Why do some crop varieties grow better on my neighbor's farm than on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli fe minɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific soil types, rainfall levels, and resistance to local pests, meaning a variety suited for one specific area or soil condition might underperform if planted elsewhere.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni sa kɛha he ko loo shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he kroko.

english: How does a crop grow step-by-step from the time I put the seed in the soil until it is ready?
ga: Te tsei lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛda fiofio kɛjɛ be mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛbaafee klalo lɛ?

english: Crops start by sprouting roots downward for water and shoots upward for light, followed by a vegetative leaf stage, flowering, and finally fruit or grain production, with each stage requiring specific water and nutrient care.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ shishifãi ni baa shi koni amɛbahe nu kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha la. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji baa lɛ fã, fɔfɔi, kɛ naagbee lɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui afeemɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai krɛdɛɛi.

english: Why are my crops growing very slowly even though I planted fresh seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ dumɔwui heei yɛ?

english: Slow growth often happens when soil lacks necessary nutrients, when weeds compete with the young plants for sunlight, or when roots do not receive enough water during the early vegetative stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni jwɛi lɛ kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ miitswa akaŋ loo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I tell the exact time my crops are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show distinct physical signs when mature, such as leaf yellowing, fruit color changes, drying stalks in grain crops, or firmness, indicating the crop has stopped growing and reached full yield potential.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, aduawai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni egbi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli, loo bɔ ni ekã shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baa.

english: How many times can I harvest from the same crop plant before I need to clear the land and plant again?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dani ehe baahia ni mafo jɛmɛ ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Some single-season crops like maize yield only one harvest before dying, while continuous crops like peppers, tomatoes, or cassava can be harvested multiple times over several months if fed and watered properly.
ga: Nibii komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii kome pɛ dani amɛgboiɔ. be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ tamɔ pepper, tomato loo cassava Abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shii abɔ yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli kɛji akɛ aha lɛ niyenii ni aha lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers in Ghana get very small harvests even when they plant on a large piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ náa yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji amɛduɔ shikpɔji wuji po lɛ?

english: Small harvests usually result from simple issues like poor seed selection, wrong fertilizer timing, overcrowding plants too close together, or failing to protect crops from early pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ naagba bibioo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui ni ahalaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli baa ji nikpamɔ bibioo. Be ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ejaaa. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ loo ni abuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: What is the correct way to apply fertilizer so I do not destroy my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer should be applied in specific amounts placed a few centimeters away from the plant stem in moist soil, rather than directly touching the plant or burning the roots during hot weather.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa. Akɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli tɛ̃ɛ loo oshã shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow or look burned shortly after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etamɔ nɔ ni eshã amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ awo mi tso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Leaf burn happens when too much fertilizer is applied at once or placed directly against the stem, causing salts to pull water out of the plant roots rather than feeding them.
ga: Baai shãa baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ be kome mli loo awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Do my maize crops stop growing or rest at night like human beings do?
ga: Ani mi-abele lɛ ekpa shweremɔ loo ehiɛ edɔ nyɔɔŋ kome tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ?

english: Crops never truly rest or sleep. Even at night when there is no sunlight, plants continue using the energy they created during the day to build roots, stems, and leaves continuously.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ejɔɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛwɔɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ po ni hulu la bɛ Tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli.

english: Are the roots of my cocoa trees always working underground even when I cannot see new leaves growing?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be fɛɛ be, kɛ́ minaaa baai heei ni miida po?

english: Yes, plant roots are active around the clock. They continuously draw water and essential minerals from the soil to support the tree, even when there is no visible growth above ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛ nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ anaaa dalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: What actually happens to my cassava plants if weeds are stealing all the food from the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Because crops and weeds consume nutrients continuously, weeds will greedily drain the soil dry if left unchecked. Without food available in the soil, your cassava plants will starve, stop growing, and produce very small tubers.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ jwɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Jwɛi kɛ hiɛjoomɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ O-cassava tsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ, amɛbaakpa dalɛ, ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants become weak and thin if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they constantly compete for the exact same water and soil nutrients. Since none of the plants get enough food to feed their non-stop growth, they all turn out weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛha edalɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko kpaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil become completely empty of nutrients after every harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Throughout their entire lifespan, crops are feeding on soil nutrients 24 hours a day. By the time you harvest, the plants have pulled most of the available food out of the ground, which is why you must restore the soil with manure or fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 daa gbi yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Beni okpaa Tsei lɛ ejie niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up so fast during the hot harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains constantly lose water through their broad leaves throughout the day and night. During the harmattan, the dry air pulls moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can drink it from dry soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ mli. Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly when the sun shines intensely for many hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo lɛ?

english: Sunlight forces plants to work at high speed to make food. During this continuous process, they pull up groundwater and release it into the air; if the soil runs out of water, the plants collapse from dehydration.
ga: Hulu la nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛtsu nii oya koni amɛná niyenii. Yɛ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛgbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei baagbee shi yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do insect pests keep attacking my vegetable farm both in the daytime and during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest activity is continuous across your farm because different insects operate on different schedules. While some pests feed during the day, nocturnal pests wake up and feed all night long, putting your crops under constant attack.
ga: Pest nitsumɔ yaa nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii yɛ be srɔtoi anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baahi shi ni amɛye nii gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ha onibii lɛ atutua be fɛɛ be.

english: How do weeds grow so much faster than the tomato seeds I planted?
