ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tomato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally built to grab soil water and nutrients continuously without needing ideal conditions, whereas domesticated tomatoes grow at a slower rate and need extra care to feed properly.
ga: Abɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛya nɔ amɛŋɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shihilɛ kpakpa bɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tomatoi ni yɔɔ shĩa mli lɛ daaa blɛoo ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I apply fertilizer to my crops, how long does it take for the roots to start feeding on it?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ niyenii yeli shishi?

english: Roots begin absorbing nutrients almost immediately as long as there is moisture in the soil. Since roots feed continuously, dissolved fertilizer gives them an instant supply of food to boost growth.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ŋmɔmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves are thin and delicate. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava grown nearby to protect them from direct sun, keep the air humid, and shield them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ni obu he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa

english: Why is it bad if I plant too many maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you put too many maize seeds in one hole, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall, thin, and weak, producing very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɛɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ko kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: As cassava reaches maturity, the lower leaves on the plant naturally turn yellow and shed. You will also notice the soil around the base of the main stem cracking and lifting slightly as the expanding tubers push upwards.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Obaana shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ mligbalamɔ ni ewo ehe nɔ fioo be mli ni tso lɛ ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aduɔ nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark specks inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɔ ni etse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibioo ko yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the center of the young maize plant during the day, eating the soft leaves before they unfold and leaving behind dark droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ.

english: How does mixing dried chicken manure into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in natural nitrogen and organic matter. When mixed into the soil, it acts as plant food that releases slowly, while also helping the soil hold water longer during short dry spells.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmei mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ fiofio. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts alongside my maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of plants called legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the surrounding maize plants.
ga: Peanuts fata ŋmeii akuu ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or inconsistent watering. If the soil gets too dry while flowers are blooming, the plant discards its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miifɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and dry out during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds are dry and strip moisture from leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. Covering the soil around the pepper base with dried grass or leaves helps retain soil moisture and protects the roots.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie pepper shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale even when it is raining heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have aggressive root systems that steal food and water from your crops before the crops can use them. Even with plenty of rain, crops suffer from hunger if weeds dominate the field.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu yeɔ hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi ye ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni akɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are given rich manure at the wrong time, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to put fertilizer on my maize farm so it does not go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekafite?

english: The best time to apply the first round of fertilizer is about two to three weeks after planting when the maize is knee-high, because that is when the roots are strong enough to drink up the nutrients before weeds or rain take them away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani jwɛi loo nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves and passing a virus to the plant, which distorts how the leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips, ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛhaa muawai kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni haa baai lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is forming, causing the bottom tissue of the tomato to collapse and turn black.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai miifee lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap at the base and fall over easily during light winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa oya yɛ shishigbɛ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer insects often burrow into the underground root base of the plantain stem, destroying the anchor roots so the heavy plant can no longer hold itself up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo trunk borers lɛ shwieɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishitoo shishitoo lɛ mli, ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, ni no haa tso ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ adamɔ shi dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender leaves until the cocoa plants grow older and tougher.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa ni ehe waɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers before producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas often shed their flowers when small pests called flower thrips attack the blossoms, or when the weather becomes extremely hot and dry, causing stress that forces the plant to abort the flowers to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ale amɛ akɛ fɔfɔi thrips, ni amɛtutuaa fɔfɔi. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛfo fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots in the storage barn before I am ready to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go to sleep after harvest, but warm temperatures and high moisture in the storage area wake them up from dormancy, signaling to the tuber that it is time to sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpa amɛ. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ baate amɛ shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe. Etsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ wain tsei heei.

english: Why does spear grass keep coming back on my farm even after I clear it completely with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade jie fɛɛ po?

english: Spear grass stores food in strong underground stems called rhizomes that spread deep under the soil. Clearing the top leaves with a cutlass leaves these underground stems alive to shoot up fresh grass again.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ toɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ dade tswa ŋwɛi baai lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei nɛɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi hee ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are tender and lose water quickly. Retaining shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, providing shelter, lower temperatures, and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ ji bibii ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni ebaaha wɔɔhe, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a shortage of nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil below the reach of roots or flood the ground so roots cannot breathe; applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea after excess water drains will restore leaf color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo ekɛ nu abɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii, beni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield only tiny root tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant directs all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of food storage. Balancing soil nutrients and avoiding excessive nitrogen ensures the plant shifts energy down into expanding the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Yɛ niyenii ni abua naa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I collect and replant seeds from my previous harvest of hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ anaa ni miduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce a high-yielding crop in the first generation. Replanting saved seeds results in offspring that lose that uniform strength, yielding uneven plant sizes and significantly lower harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛfee tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa seshibii lɛ ahewalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛi lɛ feɔ ekome ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep forming new flowers and pods for weeks instead of ripening all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ? yɛ otsii babaoo mli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikome

english: Some cowpea varieties have an 'indeterminate' growth pattern, meaning they continuously produce new vines, flowers, and pods as long as moisture is available. Planting 'determinate' or bushy varieties ensures uniform flowering and a single, synchronized harvest.
ga: Cowpea henɔi komɛi yɛ ‘erratic’ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaawo wain tsei heei, fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. ‘Definitive’ loo bushy henɔi ni aduɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ aba yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomato fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination inside the flower. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and applying grass mulch around the base protects flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ni aaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishi buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits develop flat, dark, rotten patches at the bottom end before turning ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplants lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the developing fruit during erratic watering cycles. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps roots steadily absorb soil calcium and move it to growing fruit tips.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa yɛ aduawai ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛkɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do dark black spots spread across my plantain leaves and cause the leaves to dry up prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ miigbɛ eshwa mi plantain baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni eha baai lɛ miigbi oya lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Sigatoka, a fungal disease that thrives in hot, humid weather and spreads via wind and rain splashes. Pruning affected leaves and maintaining proper spacing allows air to dry the leaves quickly, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Black Sigatoka ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɔ Baai ni ena hela lɛ ni afolɔ mli kɛ sɛɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi baai lɛ oya. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my yam vines turn black and die back rapidly during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This rapid blackening is caused by Yam Anthracnose disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, warm conditions. Spacing yams properly for ventilation, using clean seed yams, and avoiding working in wet fields helps stop the fungal spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ diŋ ni yaa oya nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji anthracnose ni baa mɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Okɛ sweet potato lɛ awo he ko jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Yam ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my pepper plants stop them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from reaching the soil, reducing water evaporation and keeping plant roots cool. This steady supply of root moisture prevents pepper plants from wilting during hot dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ Shishifãi lɛ ni akɛ nu woɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pepper tsei lɛ akagboi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves green and boosts grain size.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abele tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with many leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or excess water, it puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of roots. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers late in the season encourages the plant to store energy in the soil to form thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛto hewalɛ amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Does my yam crop really need tall wooden stakes, or can the vines just trail along the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato lɛ biɔ tso ni kɛlɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo wain tsei baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to produce food for tuber growth. Leaving vines on the ground increases leaf diseases from damp soil and results in significantly smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa tsei ahe helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee bibii kwraa.

english: Should I allow all the new shoot suckers to keep growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei heei akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe? Mi dumɔwu titri lɛ loo daabi?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plant for food, water, and sunlight, leading to small plantain bunches. Keeping only the main stem, one medium follower sucker, and one small shoot yields the largest fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no baaha ŋmeii bibii aba. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ pɛ ni abua naa Follower sucker ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kome kɛ tso bibioo kome baawo yibii ni da fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers they cannot support, but poor pollination by tiny midges also causes flower drop. Maintaining moist leaf litter on the soil creates a breeding ground for these beneficial insects, helping more flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni anyɛɛɛ aye abua amɛ. Shi pollination ni midges lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee lɛ hu haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ aná he ko ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ pods babaoo.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady and adding crushed eggshells or agricultural lime to the soil prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni atswa loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing fresh shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves. Spraying the plant with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil controls these insects so normal leaf growth can resume.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai lɛ anyɛ adara bɔ ni sa

english: Why is my cabbage starting to flower early instead of forming a hard, compact head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra yɛ yitsei ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When cabbage experiences severe heat or lack of water, it gets stressed and triggers early flowering to reproduce before dying. Regular watering and providing light shade during hot spells keeps the plant cool enough to form a dense cabbage head.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa loo nu ni faaa yɛ mli lɛ baaha kaabe lɛ aná haomɔ ni awo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ oya dani egbo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ kaabe yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: Can I plant vegetables directly in soil where I currently keep my backyard chickens and goats?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mishia sɛɛ kooloi kɛ tooi lɛ toɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Animal droppings make excellent natural fertilizer, but fresh manure is too hot and can burn delicate crop roots. It is best to collect the animal waste, let it dry and decompose for a few weeks, and then mix it into the soil before planting crops.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Shi ŋmeii heei lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaabua kooloi ashishifã naa. Ha ni egbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okɛ tso lɛ adu.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the crop is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas before maize helps put nutrients back into the soil so the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo ni aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa tsei aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why does covering the ground around my crops with dried grass help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil shaded and cool. It traps moisture in the ground so roots stay hydrated longer and prevents weeds from taking light and water from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni eha jwɛi lɛ akaná la kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and heat, which scorch their leaves and dry out the roots. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides living shelter that blocks strong sun while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow very tall and weak with few fruits when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops compete against each other for light, water, and soil food. Giving each crop enough space allows sunlight to reach the stems and lets roots spread out to absorb the food needed to yield heavily.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la ashɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ.

english: If I leave my cassava in the ground long after it is ready, will the tubers keep getting bigger and better?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni efee klalo sɛɛ hu? Ani yitso lɛ baaya nɔ agbo?

english: No, keeping cassava in the ground long after maturity causes the roots to become hard, woody, and lose starch quality. Harvesting cassava on time ensures you get soft, heavy tubers that cook well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei wo shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni edara sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tsei, ni amɛmli ŋmei lɛ hu baaje mli. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmei yɛ be naa lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsii ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will trimming off extra branches from my pepper plants hurt them or help them produce?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye amɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii?

english: Trimming unnecessary lower branches and leaves, known as pruning, actually helps pepper plants because it redirects food and energy away from leaves and into forming bigger, healthier peppers.
ga: Niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ooofolɔ, ni ale lɛ akɛ pruning lɛ baanyɛ aye abua o-pepper tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe. Ni ebafeɔ chili ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to grow the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to build up over time. Rotating crops restores nutrient balance and stops pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni esa akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: What causes small holes and chewed edges on my vegetable leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in crop leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, beetles, or worms feeding on young foliage. Checking under leaves early in the morning and applying insect remedies protects leaves so the plant can gather sunlight to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ kɛ bu baa tso baai amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ abua hulu la naa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce a lot of flowers but fail to form heavy palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees have separate male and female flowers. If insects like pollinating weevils or wind do not move pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers, the flowers drop off without forming fruits.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsiii ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɛɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ nɔ kɛyaaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my sorghum crop help both plants thrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-sorghum tsei lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Nearby crops like sorghum can feed on this natural nitrogen, improving crop yield without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ aye nitrogen yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do the roots of my crops turn black and soft when heavy rains fall on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains soak the ground, standing water pushes out the air that roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots drown, causing rot and decay to spread through the whole plant.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli, ni ekɛ fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ baaba tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has too much water for planting trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha tsei ni baakwɛ̃?

english: If rainwater stays pooled on top of the soil for days or the ground stays muddy and smells sour, your land is waterlogged, which will cause sensitive trees to rot.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee atatu lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo.

english: What can I do on my farm to protect my crops from water damage during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nu akafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels or build raised soil beds so extra rainwater flows away from crop roots, keeping them safe from rot and decay.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Aloo feemɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Ni aaaha ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting even though the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water around crop roots smothers them, preventing them from taking up plant food. This starves the plant, making leaves turn soft, yellow, and eventually decay.
ga: nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tse shishifãi babaoo baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ŋmɔŋ, ni naagbee lɛ amɛbaagboi.

english: What causes the bottom of my crop stems to turn soft and rotten near the soil level?
ga: Mɛni haa tso lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is stem rot, which happens when excess moisture sits around the base of the plant. Wet conditions allow harmful fungi to thrive and decay the stem.
ga: Enɛ ji shishifãi ni fiteɔ, ni baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If my farm floods and my crops start rotting, can they survive once the sun comes back out?
ga: Kɛji nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi fitemɔ Ani amɛbaahi shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi?

english: Plants can recover if the water drains away quickly, but if the roots have already rotten completely, the crop cannot save itself and will die even after the soil dries.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji nu lɛ ho oya. Shi kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo kwraa Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ atsa amɛhe ni amɛbaagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ po.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant crops on soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Planting on mounds lifts the crop roots above standing rainwater, allowing air to reach the roots so they do not rot and decay during heavy downpours.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nugbɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, egbooo ni egbooo.

english: Can I plant any type of crop or tree in low-lying, wet areas of my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tso loo tso srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, many crops and trees dislike too much water and will quickly rot in swampy ground. Only specific water-loving crops like rice can thrive in low, wet soils.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei babaoo sumɔɔɔ nu babaoo. ni ebaafite oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni sumɔɔ nu titri, tamɔ ŋmãa pɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best location on my farm to plant young tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ tsei bibii tamɔ kookoo?

english: Choose elevated or well-drained ground where rainwater flows away easily, because tree crops dislike excess water and will rot if their roots sit in waterlogged soil.
ga: Halamɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ loo he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ sumɔɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine, ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ afu amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings die when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Giving seedlings too much water smothers their delicate roots and causes root rot. Young trees need moist soil, but soaked soil causes decay before the roots can grow strong.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛshifãi lɛ agbo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia tsei bibii. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha egbo dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to grow well when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid varieties or improperly stored grains lose their vigor over time, leading to poor germination. Using fresh, certified seeds or properly drying and storing saved seeds in airtight containers keeps them healthy for the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ hybrid srɔtoi amli loo dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii Aloo, dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield much less food when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow big and produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ, niyenii, kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and protect themselves from extreme heat. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High daytime and night-time temperatures stress tomato plants, causing the pollen inside the flowers to dry up, which makes the plant drop its blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Gbi kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants look fresh in the morning but drop and wilt under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ehee leebi lɛ? Shi egboɔ kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ shɛ enɔ shwane mli?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crops every year even though I work hard on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsu nii waa kɛha lɛ?

english: Every time crops grow, they pull nutrients out of the soil. If you do not put nutrients back using compost, animal manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni tso ko baakwɛ̃ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are leguminous crops that capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps feed companion crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni fata ehe tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the tender leaves of my young maize plants suddenly filled with holes and small worms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the tender central leaves of young maize plants before they can fully grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains develop tiny insects and turn into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ miifee kooloi bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Insects like grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside or on grains before and during harvest. If the grain is not dried properly before storage or kept in airtight bags, the insect eggs hatch and consume the grains from the inside.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli loo nɔ dani akpaa kɛ be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto loo akɛwo vacuum bag mli. Kooloo wuji lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my cultivated crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: I applied fertilizer to my field, but pests are still eating the leaves. Why is the fertilizer not helping my crops grow well?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔji amli. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ lolo. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for your crops, but if insects are damaging the leaves and roots, the plant becomes too weak to absorb those nutrients. You must clear the pests so the crop can actually use the fertilizer to grow.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kpata baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nakai niyenii lɛ. Esa akɛ ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Should I apply fertilizer first or spray my farm for insect pests first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ loo mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to control the pests first. If insects are currently eating your crops, applying fertilizer just creates lush leaves for the pests to destroy, which wastes your expensive fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji kooloi miiye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afite lɛ baa. Enɛ baafite o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ.

english: Can insects and weeds steal the benefits of fertilizer away from my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi baanyɛ aju sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli baa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, weeds will quickly absorb the fertilizer from the soil before your crop roots can get it, and pests will eat the lush leaves that the fertilizer helps produce, wasting your money.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baaye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Why are my harvest yields still very low even though I spent a lot of money buying chemical fertilizer this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer alone cannot guarantee a big harvest. If you do not also control pests, remove weeds, and plant with proper spacing, pests and diseases will destroy the extra growth that the fertilizer provided.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ aha ŋmaa babaoo aba. Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ oye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni odu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai fiteɔ dalɛ kroko ni ŋmɔshi nibii haa lɛ.

english: How do insect pests harm my crops if the plants already look tall and green?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛ ŋmɔji momo?

english: Even if a plant looks tall, insects suck out its internal juices and bite holes in leaves, taking away the energy the crop needs to produce big grains, healthy cobs, or large tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ moŋ Shi kooloi bibii nuɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli ni amɛkpãa baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo dumɔwui wuji. cob ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo yitso agbo lɛ bɛ

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are sickly because they lack plant food or because pests are attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ejaakɛ tso niyenii bɛ amɛhe loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua amɛ?

english: Lack of plant food usually causes leaves to turn pale yellow evenly across the field, while pest attacks leave visible holes, chewed edges, spots, or tiny insects under the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei aniyenii ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ bu, ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli, ŋmeii, loo kooloi bibii baa. ni abaanyɛ ana yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Is it necessary to follow all the farm training steps like proper spacing and pest spraying, or can I just rely on fertilizer?
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ, tamɔ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Aloo ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: All farming practices work like a team. Fertilizer feeds the plant, but correct spacing gives it room to breathe, and pest control protects it. Skipping any step weakens the final harvest.
ga: Okwaayeli nifeemɔi fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuu. Fertilizer ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ Shi gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa gbɛ ni amɛmuɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do insects still attack my farm even when I clear all the weeds and water the crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding and watering make your crops healthy and attractive, but healthy crops also draw in hungry pests. Good watering and weeding must be paired with active pest monitoring and control.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ nu ni oooha lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo ni amɛfeɔ fɛo. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ nu kpakpa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ afata kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ he.

english: Why does my agriculture officer keep telling me to kill fall armyworms before adding fertilizer to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ magbe cutworms dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms destroy the growing central leaves of maize. If you fertilize while armyworms are active, you end up feeding plants that the worms will completely eat before corn cobs can form.
ga: Fall cutworms fiteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋ baai lɛ. Kɛji ofɔ bii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ Ehe baahia ni oha tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye lɛ niyenii dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I decide to skip pest management for just one farming season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mafo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mli yɛ be kome pɛ mli?

english: Skipping pest control for even one season allows insect populations to multiply rapidly, which can result in pests destroying most of your crop yield despite all your other hard work.
ga: Kɛ́ atsɔ be kome po ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi afa oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã ko ni da. Kɛji akɛ ootsu nii waa yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ po.

english: Why should I clear a small circle of weeds around the base of my young tree crops instead of clearing the whole field at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli lɛ? Ebɔle mi tso bibioo lɛ shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafolɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli shikome

english: Clearing a circle around the stem removes weeds that directly steal fertilizer and water from the plant's main roots, while saving you time and money compared to weeding the entire farm right away.
ga: cutting circles around Stalks ji jwɛi ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okɛ be kɛ shika toɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli jwɛi ni oootsi shikome lɛ he.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my maize plants if there is enough rainfall?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Even with enough rain, weeds grow faster than crops and steal important soil nutrients like nitrogen, while also block sunlight and hide crop-damaging insects.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛkɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do older farmers always tell me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide temporary umbrella-like shade and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, stealing energy and nutrients from the main tree. Removing them ensures the main tree grows a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize ears turn out small and weak when I plant seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ ji bibioo ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for space, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough strength to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my sweet pepper plants turning pale yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi bell pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have flooded the roots, preventing the plant from taking up food to feed its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii ni baaha baai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy-feeds on specific nutrients in the ground; planting it repeatedly exhausts the soil and allows cassava diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their vegetables with dry grass and cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ kookoo ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water loss from the heat, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't become woody and hard?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafee tso ni amɛhe wa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, around 9 to 12 months after planting; leaving them in the ground too long turns the roots fibrous and unpalatable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans get full of small holes and white powder after a few weeks in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay hidden eggs inside the beans before or during harvest, and once they hatch inside your storage bags, the larvae eat through the seeds.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni akɛtee ŋmeii amli dani akpaa loo yɛ be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ. kɛ beni amɛfɔ yɛ onitoo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ Lala lɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I plan my farming so that I am harvesting crops continuously from January to December?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ January kɛyashi December?

english: By using crop rotation and intercropping short-season vegetables with long-term crops like cassava or plantain, you can stagger your planting dates. This ensures different crops mature at different times, giving you food and income throughout the entire year.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ kɛ be kukuoo mli aduawai ni akɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo plantains adumɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ otsake gbii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it good for my land if I grow the exact same crop on the same plot year after year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: No, planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating your crops every season keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Dabi, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in the same field with my maize instead of growing maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei pɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as free fertilizer for your maize, improving soil fertility while giving you two different harvests from the same land.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛɔ he kome lɛ hu baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when I plant them in an open field without shade crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and harsh winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler microclimate and protects the young trees until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ baa, ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to conserve water. As long as the stems remain healthy, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves quickly as soon as the rainy season returns.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he teemɔŋ sane koni akɛbu nu he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin, but only yield small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak when planted too close together or when they lack sufficient nutrients like nitrogen. Overcrowding makes them compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, leaving little energy for the plant to form large, full cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli. Kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before any fruit grows on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to stress caused by sudden extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and ensuring proper plant feeding helps flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa trukaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants start wilting and dying even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that attack the plant's roots, preventing them from taking up water properly. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava helps clean the soil of these hidden diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungi loo muawai hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e ngɔ nu saminya. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to sprout as well as certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mito kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ? Tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vitality over time if stored in warm or humid conditions, or if they carry hidden diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are treated and tested to ensure high germination rates and uniform crop growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ be mli kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ anɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni tsei lɛ daa daa.

english: Does it matter which way I point my cassava stem cuttings when I push them into the soil?
ga: Ani mitsɔɔ yucca tso lɛ nine lɛ gbɛ nɔ beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the stem buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to bend upward, which weakens the plant and significantly lowers your tuber harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei abɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which generates the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the wet soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why shouldn't I clear away all the large shade trees when setting up a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ kɛji miito kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched and killed under full, harsh sunlight. Retaining larger canopy trees or planting plantains alongside baby cocoa provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋwɛitsu agbo ko nɔ loo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ baby cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore the leaves and increase corn yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes large amounts of nutrients from the soil, while groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize cobs only half full of kernels instead of being packed to the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mawo nɔ lɛ?

english: Incomplete corn cobs usually happen due to poor pollination, which occurs when plants are spaced too far apart, or when severe drought hits right as the silk and tassels are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni edako lɛ mli baa ji ŋmãa ni bɛ ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko ba beni siliki kɛ ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily even when there is no heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when pests like banana weevils or tiny root worms weaken the underground root system, making the stem unable to support the heavy weight of growing plantain bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji agbe kooloi bibii tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi bibii. Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ plantains ni akwɛɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ ni tsii waa lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown and black during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This condition, known as Black Pod disease, is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions when trees are overcrowded and air cannot circulate freely through the farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ hela nɛɛ akɛ black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any pepper fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or insect attacks on the buds. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits develop soft, black rotten patches before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering where the soil flips between being too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better when I plant them at the start of the June rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu nugbɔshiimɔi yɛ June mli lɛ?

english: Planting with the early June rains ensures young seeds receive continuous moisture to build strong root systems before any dry spell hits, leading to high germination rates and healthier crop growth.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ June shishijee gbɛ lɛ baaha amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my maize crops if I plant them too late after the main rains have passed?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Late-planted maize misses the critical rain supply needed during its flowering and cob-filling stages, resulting in small cobs, undeveloped grains, and a higher vulnerability to pests.
ga: Abɛi ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibioo ko. dumɔwui ni edarako kɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, direct sunlight, or lack of water. Maintaining shade trees and soil moisture helps flowers stay attached and develop into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, while dark red or purple pods turn orange. Harvesting at this point ensures full seed development and proper bean fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-kokoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches, allowing sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity around the trunk, preventing fungal infections like black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tsei lɛ ashishi. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Tired soil shows signs through your crops: leaves turn light green or yellow, growth becomes slow and stunted, and crop yields drop significantly despite getting enough water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehiɛɛɛ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi waa yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they spread. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves open so the plant can make food and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele koni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni eda.

english: How does covering the ground with dry leaves help my young crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the ground—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so roots don't dry out quickly in the heat, and stops unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants that yield very little food.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haaa niyenii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my farm plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa miŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal fertilizer, water, and space away from your crops, leaving your farm plants starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko oya kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Can I grow any crop I choose on any piece of land I own in Ghana?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. ni mihala yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ Ani manyɛ maná eko yɛ Ghana?

english: No, crops have specific needs regarding soil type, rainfall, and climate. For example, cocoa thrives in humid forest zones, while other crops prefer drier areas, so planting in an unsuitable location will lead to poor growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ taomɔ nii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kookoo shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli edɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Sumɔɔ hei ni egbi fe No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni esaaa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable before I start clearing it for a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa dani mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ kɛha ŋmɔ hee?

english: You should examine the soil's texture, depth, water drainage, and the natural plants already growing there. Consulting an extension officer to test or evaluate the land helps ensure your target crop can thrive on that specific site.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha, bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha, bɔ ni nu hoɔ ehaa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ momo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ extension official ko gba sane koni eka shikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ loo ekwɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsei ni okɛmamɔ ohiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do certain crops perform very well in some regions of Ghana but fail when planted in other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ, shi kɛ́ adu yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ, amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Different regions have varying rainfall patterns, temperature ranges, and soil qualities. A crop adapted to high rainfall and rich forest soil will struggle in drier regions unless provided with irrigation and specialized soil treatment.
