ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, bɔ ni dɔlɛ yaa nɔ ehaa, kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsake amɛhe kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ koo mli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Ja nu krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ko yɛ.

english: Why do farmers refer to crop chemicals as 'medicine', and how do they help my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi tsɛɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ akɛ ‘tsofa’ ni te amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua mi tsei lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Farmers call chemicals 'medicine' because, like health treatments, they protect crops from diseases, kill destructive insect pests, or destroy weeds that steal food and water from the plant.
ga: Okwaafoi tsɛɔ tsofai akɛ ‘tsofa’ ejaakɛ amɛji nɔ kome kɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔkwɛmɔ. Tsofai nɛɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe. Egbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. loo ekpãtãa jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I safely mix crop chemicals with water so I do not destroy my farm by mistake?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afutu nu shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: You must strictly follow the measurement instructions on the product label and use clean water. Using too much chemical can burn and kill your crop's leaves, while using too little will fail to solve the pest or weed problem.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ nu ni mli tse atsu nii. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu tsɛŋemɔ hela loo jwɛi naagba lɛ he nii lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers mix different crop medicines together before spraying their field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsei ahe tsofai srɔtoi futuɔ amɛhe dani amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Combining compatible chemicals—like mixing a weed killer with an insect spray—allows a farmer to solve multiple farm issues in a single application, saving time and labor costs.
ga: Tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ futumɔ Yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛtsuɔ naagbai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii yɛ nitsumɔ kome pɛ mli Enɛ haa be kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi.

english: Where should I buy my farming chemicals to ensure they are safe and genuine?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mahe mi okwaayeli tsofai lɛ yɛ koni mana akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛji anɔkwale?

english: You should buy crop inputs from registered, certified agro-dealers rather than unverified sellers to avoid counterfeit, expired, or dangerous products that can harm your health and ruin your crop yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Yɛ mɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ nii ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ Enɛ ji koni ajie amalei, nibii ni efite loo nibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aye ohewalɛ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the best way to care for young crops when starting them from the early nursery stage?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tsei bibii anɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Young plants require consistent moisture, gentle shade from hot sunlight, and protection from insects. Providing a shaded nursery bed and regular watering builds strong roots before moving them into the main field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli hulutsoo blɛoo yɛ jɛmɛ. ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ha kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, ebaatswa shishifãi ni mli wa dani adu kɛya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them to the open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to transplant shock, strong heat, or dry soil. Planting during early morning or late afternoon, and ensuring the ground is wet, helps young seedlings adapt without dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ tso ni atsakeɔ lɛ he shoofeemɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hewɔ. Dumɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbooo.

english: What steps should I take immediately if I notice leaves on my young plants turning yellow or dying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso bibioo ko nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛmiigbo?

english: First inspect the plants closely for insects or fungus spots, then ask an extension officer for the exact cause so you can treat the issue quickly with the right chemical spray or practice before it spreads.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛji kooloi loo ŋmeii yɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, bi mɔ ni kwɛɔ hiɛyaa nɔ lɛ koni ele yiŋtoo diɛŋtsɛ ni ha eba lɛ nakai. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ otsu naagba lɛ he nii oya kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsamɔ ni sa nɔ dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and moisture escapes quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides living cover that traps moisture and protects the young cocoa until it grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ekɛ nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ teeɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year when I plant it in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes nutrients like nitrogen from the dirt. Planting it repeatedly in the same field exhausts the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally restores nitrogen back into the soil, keeping it fertile.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ha efee babaoo

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings from recommended sources prevents the virus from taking over your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right next to the seed on the day I sow it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ emasɛi? Dumɔwui yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Freshly sown seeds do not have developed roots to absorb fertilizer, and concentrated fertilizer directly touching a seed can burn and kill it. It is best to wait a few weeks until roots develop before applying fertilizer slightly away from the stalk.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni miida koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii 2-3 kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he fioo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around my crops help them survive during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he lɛ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ye ebua amɛ ni amɛje Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass over the soil is called mulching. It acts as a protective blanket that traps water in the ground, reduces evaporation from the sun, and keeps root zones cool during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha hulu la ni jɛɔ mli lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower branches and stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ shishigbɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing small, non-fruiting side branches forces the tomato plant to send its nutrients directly to developing fruit instead of wasting energy on excess foliage, resulting in larger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: niji bibii ni afoɔ Yibii ni bɛ lɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje yibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas between my rows of maize, and how does it help my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is a great practice called intercropping. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, while also spreading low across the ground to suppress weeds and protect the soil from drying out.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishi koni egbe jwɛi ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give me less yield than certified seeds bought from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and can carry over pests and diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially selected and bred for high yields, uniform growth, and resistance to common local diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ashwã. Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents fungal diseases that spread on wet, shady soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: How do small insects get into my stored maize bags, and how can I stop them from eating my harvest?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote ŋmãa kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Weevils often enter maize when grain is not dried properly before storage because moisture creates ideal conditions for them to multiply. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until they are hard, and storing them in airtight, hermetic bags, starves insects of air and stops infestation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmãa mli kɛ́ agbiko ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ baa. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni akɛtoɔ vacuum bag mli Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni ekpaa haomɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot absorb enough water to keep up with intense heat. Direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries them out before they can grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi dani amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves fold or roll up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants roll their leaves during the hottest part of the day as a survival mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which stops them from losing too much water.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akafite fe nine.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential food from the soil, especially nitrogen. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot produce the green color it needs to grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of storing food in its roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii toɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the soil, while their leaves fight for sunlight, leaving no single plant with enough strength to grow thick.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu ko shishi lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, known as suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plant. Removing them allows the main stem to focus its energy on producing a big cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or tiny pests attacking the young flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ. koni amɛtutua fɔfɔi bibii lɛ

english: Why does a cocoa tree take years to yield while my maize gives food in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei woɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a short-term plant designed to complete its entire life cycle quickly, whereas cocoa is a long-term tree crop that must build a strong wood trunk and root system before it can bear fruit year after year.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni egbe ewala shihilɛ naa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ená shishifã kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa dani ewo yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do black spots spread across my cocoa pods whenever the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: The rainy season creates damp, humid weather that allows fungal diseases like black pod rot to live, multiply, and spread quickly through water droplets landing on the pods.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ hiɔ shi, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does putting dry leaves around the base of my crops help them stay healthy in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi fata mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket that shades the ground, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas out of the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant in that spot next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai he ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to grow green and strong, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the leaves on top look healthy and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdara moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of expanding its root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines roll up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves curl during intense afternoon sun to protect themselves from losing too much water to the air, though severe curling can also mean sap-sucking insects are attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ miitutua baai lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before any actual peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or when tiny pests like thrips feed on the delicate blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ye fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shade-heavy conditions. Trimming excess tree branches lets sun and wind dry out the pods to prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade ni mli wa waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha egbi kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi be mli ni edara lolo lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which usually happens when watering is uneven and the plant cannot pull calcium up from the soil consistently.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops when my crops are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even small weeds have roots that steal food, fertilizer, and water away from your crops under the soil, which reduces the total amount of harvest your crop can produce.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Shishifãi yɛ ni juɔ niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantain to block direct sun, the leaves burn and the soil dries out quickly, causing the seedlings to wither.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ latsaa he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ shãa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground, helping your next crop of maize grow greener and stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ye obua o-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings yield huge tubers while others only grow leaves and thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ bulb agboi lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi bibii pɛ.

english: Cassava roots depend on how mature the stem cutting is and which way it is planted. Using mature, healthy stems cut to the right length and planting them with the buds facing upward ensures the plant focuses energy on swelling the root tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ damɔ bɔ ni afoɔ lɛ ahaa kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛyashɛ he ni sa ni adu amɛshishifã lɛ fã kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha shishifã lɛ afuu.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and tall. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the crop and restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii ni eha efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and protects them from rot and pests that live in damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same piece of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. If you plant them back-to-back, pests left in the soil from the tomatoes will immediately attack your new pepper plants.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛji odu tomato yɛ ohe lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ tomato mli ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua o-pepper tsei heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my maize and leaving dirt that looks like sawdust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the funnel helps destroy the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni ji bio-insecticide loo neem ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ funnel lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni efite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Pruning them away leaves only one or two strong replacement suckers, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers loo shoots babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ baaná plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, be mli ni mi hu shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Under intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the bare soil. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, which acts like food for green leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough food and room to produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it helpful to plant beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally put essential nutrients back into the soil that maize takes away. Rotating your crops keeps the soil fertile so future harvests remain high without spending as much on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi babaoo ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii babaoo.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up for my family to eat?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ koni oweku lɛ aye?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the main stem darkens. You can carefully dig around the base of one plant to check if the roots are thick enough to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ bafee duŋ Obaanyɛ otsa he fɛɛ he. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atswa tso kome shishifãi koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, take away water and nutrients that the main plantain tree needs to produce food. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to grow a larger, healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa dumɔwu titri lɛ koni ená niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in my barn before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Yams naturally wake up from their resting state when storage temperatures and moisture change. Keeping them in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated yam barn slows down sprouting so the tubers stay good to eat for longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ tsake. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ blɛoo. Bɔni afee ni aye sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your field, quickly stealing the water, sunlight, and plant food that your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oyale mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Very hot sun or dry soil stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop their flowers to survive. Keeping the soil consistently moist with water or mulch helps the plants hold onto their flowers and grow peppers.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear on my crop leaves right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rains cause crops to grow tender new leaves, which attract moths that lay eggs on the plants. When the eggs hatch into caterpillars, they quickly begin eating the soft green leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ehei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ Amɛbaabɔi baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeli oya.

english: This black rot at the bottom of the fruit is caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is forming. Watering your tomatoes evenly helps prevent the fruit from spoiling before harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite dani akpa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or Gliricidia nearby creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning removes excess, dead, or diseased branches so that sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like Black Pod from spreading and directs the tree's energy into growing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay healthy and green. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure helps the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same field every season exhausts specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops or planting legumes like cowpeas helps restore natural nutrients and allows the soil to recover its fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and starves the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ naa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives steady rain for several days in a row before planting, rather than planting after the very first light rain. Using early-maturing seed varieties also helps ensure your crop reaches harvest before the dry season starts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ gbii babaoo dani odu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ hu haa onibii lɛ shɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize crop, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting beans with maize is very beneficial because beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. The maize gets extra nutrients to grow strong, while the bean plants use the sturdy maize stalks for support.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi nine shɛɔ niyenii krokomɛi anɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni bean tsei kɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa tsuɔ nii akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants with strong roots that quickly take up sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can grow. Weeding early within the first three weeks after planting gives your crop a strong advantage to grow tall and shade out competing weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ kpele yɛ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hidden in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that eats young maize leaves. Applying neem leaf extracts or recommended pesticides early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get eaten by tiny insects inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils multiply quickly if maize is stored while it still contains moisture. Thoroughly drying your harvested maize under the sun until the grains are hard, and storing them in airtight hermetic bags, starves the pests of air and protects your grain.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo. Okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Eshwieɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ odumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or gliricidia planted beside them to shield them from intense sun and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the middle of the leaf down to the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so adding compost, poultry manure, or NPK fertilizer will help the crop recover and produce large cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains cause water to pool around the roots, it deprives them of air and attracts soil fungi that make the tubers rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ amɛmli ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, making it hard for the plant to transport calcium from the soil into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies that feed on the sap underneath the leaves. As they suck the juice, they damage the leaf tissues and can spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ latɛ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to hide inside the tender funnel of young corn. Spraying recommended botanical or chemical treatments early in the morning or late evening targets them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa amɛ ehiɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farmland better for next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves high up off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell before the real rainy season begins. Planting too early means the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die due to lack of moisture in the scorching sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do plantains refuse to grow or yield well on certain parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ miikpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaawo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains need deep, rich, moist soil that drains water easily. If the soil is hard, shallow, sandy, or gets flooded with standing water, the plantain roots cannot breathe or feed properly, causing the crop to stunt or die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo lɛ he miihia plantains. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Plantain shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is naturally fertile enough for farming before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: Fertile land usually has dark, soft soil rich in decaying leaves, holds moisture well, and has earthworms or healthy wild vegetation growing on it, which shows the soil is alive and full of food for crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni baa nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo koo mli tsei ni he wa yɛ ni miida. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so small and weak even after I clear all the weeds from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for light and water, but if the soil underneath is exhausted and lacks nutrients, your crops still won't have the food they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ la kɛ nu he lɛ kɛyaa. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ efo kwraa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Can applying chemical fertilizer actually ruin my crops instead of making them grow?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, if you apply fertilizer directly against crop stems, use too much, or apply it on very dry land, it creates a harsh salt effect that burns plant roots and can kill the entire crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ, okɛtsu nii babaoo tsɔ, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo hei ni egbi waa. Enɛ baaha ŋmei ni naa wa aba ni baashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ekolɛ ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why did my crops dry up and die right after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to mix into the soil safely. When applied on dry ground or too close to the plant, the fertilizer pulls moisture out of the root system, causing the plant to dry out as if burnt by heat.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo hei ni egbi loo he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la eshã lɛ.

english: Is chemical fertilizer supposed to work on every type of soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi fɛɛ anɔ?

english: No, if soil is completely worn out or too sour (acidic), chemical fertilizer alone cannot fix it and may make things worse. Damaged soil often needs organic manure or lime first to restore its balance before commercial fertilizer can work.
ga: Dabi, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ (acidic) lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ asaa lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eha ehiɛ afee shoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni efite lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How does animal manure help tired land differently than chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifã yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly for a short time, while animal manure slowly rebuilds ruined soil by adding organic matter, holding moisture, and feeding useful soil organisms over many years.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ fiofio kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii afii babaoo.

english: What does it mean for farm land to be 'balanced'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ‘ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee’ lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Balanced soil has the right mix of natural nutrients, air spaces, moisture, and beneficial microbes. This balance allows crop roots to drink water and absorb nutrients easily without getting stressed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ja lɛ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii, kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni efutu. Nɛkɛ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu mlɛo ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What causes healthy farm soil to become ruined over time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Soil becomes ruined when it is farmed continuously without resting, burned repeatedly during clearing, or washed away by heavy rains, which strips away the top layer containing natural crop food.
ga: Afiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli, ni ashãa shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baajie ŋwɛi fã ni tso niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do crops perform very well on my neighbor's land but fail on mine right next door?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eshɛɛɛ mishikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change within just a few meters. Your neighbor's plot might have deeper topsoil, better water retention, or less previous damage than your land, even if they look similar on the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ mitai fioo komɛi pɛ mli. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ fe no. Eyɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ fioo fe oshikpɔŋ lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ amɛhe yɛ hiɛ moŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is well-prepared before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Properly prepared land has loose, weed-free soil with good drainage, allowing crop roots to easily spread out, breathe, and drink up water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse. jwɛi bɛ mli Nu kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to the soil at the same time I am planting my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Applying a small amount of starter fertilizer during planting gives seeds the early food they need, but you must place it slightly away from the seed so it does not burn the delicate roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shishijee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛto he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo koni ekashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Can I dissolve my granular fertilizer in water before applying it to my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ granular fertilizer awo nu mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, mixing water-soluble fertilizer with water helps the plant roots absorb the nutrients much faster and prevents dry fertilizer from burning the crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi kɛ nu futu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kwraa, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves burn when I apply fertilizer to dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa kɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are rich in salts that need water to dissolve; without enough moisture in the soil, the concentrated fertilizer pulls water out of the plant roots, causing the leaves to dry up and burn.
ga: Nuŋtsɔi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ehe hiaa nu dani etsɔ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I applied if a very heavy rain falls right after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash top-applied fertilizer away from your crops before the roots absorb it, which is why it is best to apply fertilizer when soil is already moist rather than right before a big storm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ top dressing ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ he dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo mi loko ahumi ngua ko maa ba.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough water after I fertilize them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ?

english: Healthy crops with enough water will have firm, upright, green leaves, whereas plants lacking water will wilt, curl up, or turn yellow during the hot afternoon hours.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaná baai ni mli wa, ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ baagboi, amɛbaakpãtã, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening reduces water loss from heat evaporation, allowing the crop roots maximum time to soak up moisture and nutrients.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be babaoo ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does water sink into the soil very fast in some parts of my farm but sit on top in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi etaa ŋwɛi yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has larger air spaces that let water drain quickly, while packed or clay soil holds water on the surface, which can suffocate plant roots if it does not drain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui wuji ni haa nu hoɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu yɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji ajieee nu lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Too much fertilizer can shock the crop, cause root damage, make leaf edges turn brown, or cause the plant to grow bushy green leaves without producing fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ he afee shoo. efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa baai eŋɔlii akui ni amɛwooo yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Why are my crops still looking weak and yellow even though I gave them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot uptake fertilizer without adequate soil moisture, so if the soil is too dry—or if the roots are damaged by pests—the plant will still show signs of starvation.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii efite shishifãi lɛ. Tso lɛ baajie hɔmɔ he okadii akpo lolo.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves available nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth, showing that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Yellow, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ahe koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves but gives me tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of storing food in the roots. Using potassium-rich soil or balanced fertilizer helps build bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni afee bulbs wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the wet ground onto stakes gives them maximum sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ babaoo, ni etsĩɔ tsei ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow and get top-heavy once fruit bunches grow. When rain softens the soil, heavy winds can easily uproot them unless you support the stems with sturdy bamboo props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsii be mli ni kuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. Ja okɛ nibii ni akɛ ŋmei ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and humid weather. Regular pruning lets sunlight and air in, which helps keep the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nibii ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking juices from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do many of my cocoa tree flowers fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed extra flowers if they don't get pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by heat and drought. Shade trees and moist soil help keep flowers intact.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi titri kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Shade tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to come up when I plant immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up dry soil without soaking it deep enough. If a hot dry spell follows, the seeds get baked or dry out before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛgbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for fruit to set. The plant naturally drops useless blossoms to save its energy and moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers begin to rot in the ground if heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills all underground air pockets with water, cutting off oxygen to the tubers. Without air to breathe, the tuber tissue dies and rots under the wet soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ amli kɛ nu. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa yitso lɛ he Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni akɛmuɔ Tuber fãji lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but very few of them turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges (or human help through hand pollination) to transfer pollen. If there are not enough natural insects on your farm, many flowers will simply dry up and drop off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii (loo adesa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛtsɔ nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ nɔ) koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi lɛ aya. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbi kɛkɛ ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: I hear people talking about hand pollination for cocoa—how does it work and will it help my farm yield more?
ga: Minuɔ mɛi ni wieɔ kookoo ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ he—te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ ni ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination means using small tools or your fingers to move pollen from one cocoa flower to another. Doing this manually ensures that flowers get fertilized, which can greatly increase the number of pods your trees produce compared to relying on insects alone.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ nibii bibii tsuɔ nii. loo onine ni okɛjie pollen kɛjɛ cacao fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Enɛ ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Kɛ akɛto kooloi bibii pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: What causes healthy-looking cocoa flowers to suddenly dry up and fall off the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo fɔfɔi ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛjɛɔ tsei akutsei amli amɛgbeeɔ shi?

english: Flowers drop when they fail to get pollinated, or when the tree experiences stress from prolonged dry heat or lack of soil nutrients. Assisting with pollination and keeping good farm shade can help save these blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollin. aloo kɛ́ tsei naa haomɔ kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Pollination ni ayeɔ abuaa kɛ ŋmɔ mli hulutsoo kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu fɔfɔi nɛɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time of year to start clearing and preparing my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔji lɛ ashishijee kɛ amɛhe saamɔ?

english: In Ghana, main farm preparation should start right before the major rainy season (around March/April) or minor rainy season (September). Clearing weeds and pruning early allows your cocoa trees to absorb maximum moisture and nutrients when the rains arrive.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ titri lɛ aje shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aba. (aaafee March/April) loo nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ (September) jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ tsei ni afoɔ Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why do some trees on my farm give me plenty of cocoa pods while the trees right next to them yield almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi kookoo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ haaa mi lɛ? No haaa yibiiwoo ko kwraa aba?

english: Differences in yields across the same farm are usually caused by uneven shade, differences in soil fertility, tree age, or localized pest attacks. Ensuring uniform shade, pruning, and soil feeding helps all trees produce abundantly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ yibiiwoo sɔrɔtoi ni baa ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi afii ni tso lɛ yɔɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atuatsemɔ He ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to learn and try new cocoa farming methods instead of keeping to the traditional ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makase gbɛ hee ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ kookoo lɛ ni maka lɛ makwɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Modern techniques like structured shade control, targeted pruning, and hand pollination are designed to increase yields on the exact same size of land, helping you harvest more cocoa without needing a larger farm.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Targeted pruning kɛ hand pollination Afee lɛ koni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa kookoo babaoo ni obɛ ŋmɔ agbo.

english: If bad weather or poor roads delay transport, how can I keep my harvested cocoa pods from rotting on the farm?
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo gbɛjegbɛi ni ehiii ha nibii ni akɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Store harvested, unopened pods on a raised platform off the bare ground under cool shade. Keep them covered from heavy rain, and do not break the pods open until you are ready to start the fermentation process.
ga: Too ŋmeii ni akpa, ni agbeleee lɛ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni agbele yɛ hulutsoo be shishi. Ha nɔ koni nugbɔ ni naa wa akanɛ. Ni kaagbele ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaaje ŋmɔtɔ nitsumɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. They require temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them from harsh heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do green cocoa pods on my trees turn dark black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overgrown farms. Pruning overcrowded branches improves airflow and sunlight, which dries out moisture and stops the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo fɔ ni efee basabasa lɛ amli. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need extra food or fertilizer to bear more fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia mi-cacao tso lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: If cocoa leaves look pale or yellowish, tree growth slows down, or pod production drops despite good rainfall, the soil has run out of nutrients and needs organic manure or cocoa-specific fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi loo pod feemɔ baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔ kookoo he lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them creates living umbrellas that retain moisture and protect the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ hulutsoo tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce food. More sunlight on the leaves directly increases the size and weight of the tubers growing underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Hulu la ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dalɛ kɛ emli tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip towards the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛyashiɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower leaves usually indicates that your soil is lacking nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea early in the plant's growth helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning them away leaves only the main plant and one strong replacement, ensuring you get large and heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ amɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ pɛ kɛ tso kome ni he wa ni baaye najiaŋ lɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ baaha onine ashɛ plantains babaoo kɛ babaoo nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop leaves during prolonged dry spells to reduce water loss and protect the tubers underground. If the leaf curling happens alongside tiny white insects under the leaves, it could be a viral disease carried by whiteflies.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ekolɛ eji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: My tomato plants are producing plenty of flowers, but why are the flowers dropping off without forming fruits?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is excess nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to grow leaves instead of holding fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my pepper fruits turn dark brown and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to absorb and carry calcium throughout the plant.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji blossom end rot ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa, ni baa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ calcium ni amɛkɛyaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars creating ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee bu ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide in the central funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the funnel protects the plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ bio-insecticide loo neem extract ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo funnel lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why can paddy rice survive in flooded lowlands where my maize and cassava would rot and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔji ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ anɔ, he ni mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baafite lɛ?

english: Rice plants possess specialized air channels in their stems and roots that transport oxygen from the leaves down to the submerged roots, allowing them to breathe underwater where other crops drown.
