ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hei krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ emuɔ yɛ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi shwieɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Officer, which crops are tough enough to survive if the rainy season stops early in my area?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛɛ tsei baaŋmɛ amɛtsui shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava and cowpeas are naturally resilient and can withstand dry spells because of their deep root systems, whereas crops like tomatoes or cabbage are more delicate and suffer quickly without regular water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji nɔ ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ hulutsoo bei amli yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato loo cabbage lɛ waaa kwraa ni amɛyeɔ amanehulu oya kɛji nu bɛ mli daa.

english: Why is my cassava growing fine in poor weather while my maize field next to it is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli lɛ? be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ Ani eegbo?

english: Cassava is a highly resilient crop that stores water and energy in its roots, making it tough against stress. Maize is much more sensitive and requires strict, regular care and rainfall to thrive.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi waa ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi amli. Ehaa enyɛɔ eshiɔ haomɔ naa Abele lɛ nuɔ he waa ni ebiɔ kwɛmɔ ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ koni enyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: As a beginner farmer in Ghana, which vegetable is forgiving if I make small mistakes in caring for it?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo hee yɛ Ghana Mɛɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma kɛ esha keɔ kɛji mitɔmɔ bibioo ko yɛ ekwɛmɔ mli?

english: Okra and garden eggs are resilient crops that can tolerate minor mistakes in watering or soil quality, making them better choices for beginners than delicate crops like sweet peppers or tomatoes.
ga: Okra kɛ abɔɔ mli eggplant ji tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ tɔmɔi bibii ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛhaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ bell peppers loo tomato.

english: Can I skip clearing the weeds on my cocoa farm for a few months to cut down on expenses?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi koni shika ni mifiteɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: There are no shortcuts in farming. Leaving weeds unchecked allows them to steal vital nutrients and water from your cocoa trees, which will eventually cause your harvest yields to drop significantly.
ga: Gbɛ kukuji komɛi bɛ okwaayeli mli. Kɛ́ akwɛɛɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni okpa lɛ aba shi kwraa yɛ naagbee.

english: Is it okay if I don't apply fertilizer to my maize on time and just put it all at the end of the season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji mikɛ mi-abele lɛ wooo mli yɛ be naa ni mikɛwoɔ mli fɛɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Timing is crucial for crop nutrition. Trying to take a shortcut by applying fertilizer late means the plants miss their key growth period, resulting in weak stalks and very small corn ears.
ga: Be he hiaa kɛha tsei aniyenii. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ gbɛi kukuji anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akashɛ dalɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds directly into hard ground without tilling the soil first?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni mikɛtsuuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Skipping soil preparation makes it hard for young roots to penetrate the ground and absorb water. Taking this shortcut will cause stunted crop growth and poor harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ ni afoɔ mli lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛŋɔ nu. Gbɛ kuku nɛɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: If I forget to water my vegetable nursery seedlings for just one day, will it destroy them?
ga: Kɛji mihiɛ kpa nɔ akɛ mawo aduawai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu gbi kome pɛ lɛ, ani amɛbaafite?

english: Missing a day once or twice might not kill tough seedlings immediately, but continuous irregular watering creates weak plants that will eventually fail when transplanted to the main farm.
ga: Ekolɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ ni elaaje lɛ egbeŋ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaafite.

english: Why do I need to walk through my crop field every single day even if the plants look fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ ko mli daa gbi eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Daily inspection helps you spot pest attacks and diseases before they spread. Consistent routine care is essential because ignoring the field for days often leads to sudden crop loss.
ga: Daa gbi kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ. dani egbɛ eshwa Hekwɛmɔ daa he miihia ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie jɛmɛ gbii babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ trukaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural behavior where the plant reduces its leaf surface to conserve moisture during heat stress. If the plant is properly watered, it will recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Baai lɛ shwiemɔ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni tsei shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji okɛ nu ha tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ he waa kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow even though I water them heavily every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli waa daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water smothers their roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients. Consistent, balanced daily care is required because overwatering can hurt crop health just as much as underwatering.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tso ko nu babaoo lɛ, ebaatsi eshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu loo amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Daa gbi kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ja lɛ he miihia. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni nu ni okɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ awui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps the leaves turn green and stay strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce so many leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing bushy leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the soil, so they do best with minimal fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ maa ŋmɔ mli baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii fioo bɔ ni aaanyɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my farm turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and air dry out the crop, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips living under the leaves. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil water or an approved insecticidal spray clears these bugs and lets fresh leaves open up normally.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu, neem fɔ, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai heei lɛ agbele bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom end rot, happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots carry calcium to the growing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium baa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive the heat. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rains return, fresh new leaves will sprout from the stem.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. No mli lɛ tso lɛ gboko, ni beni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience heat stress or lack water. Maintaining shade trees on your farm helps lower the field temperature and keep moisture in the air so flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the soil surface, making them easy to uproot. Mounding extra soil around the base of the plant and supporting heavy bunches with wooden props keeps them standing upright during storms.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaawo shishifãi Akɛ muji krokomɛi ni abua naa awoɔ tso lɛ he ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ he lɛ afiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around them without draining away. Planting yams on high soil mounds or raised ridges keeps excess water away from the tubers and prevents rotting.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akaboteɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni ehaaa egbo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and absorb rain and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your young crop seedlings the space and sunlight they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Without taller shade plants like plantain trees nearby to shield them, the sun scorches the leaves and dries out the roots before the cocoa can establish itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ ni baaha nɔ lɛ, Hulu lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani kookoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why is my maize crop looking pale yellow instead of deep green even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks essential nutrients or organic fertilizer, the maize leaves cannot produce the green chlorophyll needed for strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ ajie klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground during heavy rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Standing water cuts off air supply to the roots, causing underground rot-causing fungi to thrive and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbáa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting during periods of extreme heat or dry weather. High temperatures stress the plant, which prevents successful pollination and causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ waa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he

english: What will happen to my yam crop if I do not provide wooden stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haaa?

english: Yam leaves need to reach upwards to catch daylight. Without stakes, the vines trail on the humid ground where leaves shadow each other, catch fungal leaves diseases more easily, and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ. Wein tso lɛ baakplekeshi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsei ahe tsei ni ŋmei bɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooona fungal leaf hela. ni amɛwoɔ yitsei bibii kwraa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the soft, growing funnels of young maize. If left unchecked, they destroy the developing leaf tissues and drastically reduce harvest yields.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ekpãtãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When corn is planted too closely, the individual plants compete fiercely for sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients. This competition makes the stalks grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ waa Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa tsei bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. The feeding damages the leaf structure, causing leaves to twist and reducing fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni edaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry foliage or straw (mulching) acts like a protective cover over the soil. It stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple young suckers steal valuable nutrients and water from the main plantain plant. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only the strongest one, allowing the main stem to focus energy on producing large bunches of plantain.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, niji ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ plantains babaoo ni ekɛbaa lɛ he nii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves regain their green color and support healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my maize seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground is thoroughly soaked and rains become steady rather than planting after the very first light rain. Planting too early during an isolated shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot, dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli eja lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ba.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn woody and tough to cook if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants mature past their optimal harvest time, they stop storing soft starch in the roots and begin building tough woody fibers. Harvesting your cassava at the recommended age for the variety—usually between 9 to 12 months—ensures the roots stay soft and easy to boil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa lɛ amamɔ shishi. Kpaa ŋmei yɛ afii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmei henɔ lɛ ye lɛ mli. Be nɛɛ (bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) baaha shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee mlɛo akɛ aaaho.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. You can protect your cocoa by pruning excess branches to let sunlight in and removing affected pods immediately so the fungus does not spread to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ obu kookoo he kɛtsɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ koni hulu la aba mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛbaafata he Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are tiny insects drilling holes into my maize stalks and causing them to fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ni amɛshwieɔ mi shi lɛ?

english: These are stem borer caterpillars, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and eat their way into the center of the stalk. Intercropping maize with crops like cassava or legumes, and applying approved bio-pesticides early in the season, helps reduce stem borer damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji stem borers ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛyaa stem lɛ teŋgbɛ. Abele ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade with their broad leaves, protecting the young cocoa trees from heat and preserving soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo kɛha baai lɛ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared weeds and grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter, earthworms, and beneficial soil microbes that feed your crops. Allowing cleared weeds to rot into the soil or using them as mulch improves soil moisture and natural fertility over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce smaller cobs than certified seeds bought from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield and disease resistance in their first generation. When you save seeds from that harvest, the offspring lose those high-performing traits, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Seshibii lɛ baafite nakai sui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken patches on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eboteɔ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit while it is growing, usually because of irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit from developing these dark spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi nɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain loo cassava yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Planting food crops like plantains provides temporary shade to protect the young cocoa leaves from scorching while giving you food and extra income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko dani kookoo lɛ agbɔ.

english: Why are many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii bibii Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods. Excessive flower drop can happen due to dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination, so keeping proper shade and soil moisture helps save more flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ bafeɔ pod. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni ehiii ni shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi babaoo ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy-looking branches on my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air. This reduces dampness that causes diseases like black pod and ensures the tree directs its energy into making big, healthy pods rather than extra leaves.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai tamɔ pod blackening baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ pods wuji ni mli wa moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while they are still growing on the branch?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overcrowded farms. Clearing weeds, pruning extra branches for airflow, and removing infected pods quickly will help stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. weeding Nibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Cocoa seedlings should generally be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing keeps mature trees from overcrowding each other so they do not have to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei wuji lɛ afee ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni atswa akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are not getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Trees lacking soil nutrients usually show pale or yellowing leaves, slow growth, and small or weak pods. Adding compost or applying the right fertilizer helps restore leaf color and improves pod production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ kpo. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha pod lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave some large forest trees on my land when preparing it for cocoa farming?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi koo mli tsei wuji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni misaa mihe koni madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving a few large shade trees helps protect mature cocoa from extreme afternoon heat, keeps the soil moist during dry spells, and provides a home for beneficial insects that pollinate cocoa flowers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ Tsei fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baabu kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa kookoo fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan weather affect my cocoa trees and how do I protect them?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ Harmattan lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the soil and leaves, causing leaves to curl, turn brown, and drop. Leaving fallen leaves on the ground as mulch helps trap moisture in the soil around the roots during dry periods.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbee shi. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. shishifãi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting too early results in undeveloped beans, while leaving them too long can cause the seeds inside to start germinating.
ga: Efee klalo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do straight green shoots keep sprouting out from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni ja lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These fast-growing shoots are called water shoots or 'chupons.' They steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk without producing pods, so you should cut them off while they are still small to keep the main tree productive.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛɛ akɛ nu tsei loo 'chupons'. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ awo yibii lolo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, so applying NPK or urea fertilizer, or adding well-rotted animal manure, will help the plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea fata he loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry fertilizer; their roots can only absorb nutrients when they are dissolved in water. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil can burn and damage the roots, so it is best to apply it when the soil is moist after a rainfall.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long, which smothers the roots and causes fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my maize and leaving dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ ŋmãa baa ko teŋ ni eshiɔ muji yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing part of the maize plant. Spraying recommended insecticides or neem extracts early in the morning or late evening directly into the center funnel helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves twisting up and curling into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ ni atsɔ mli awo kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding under the leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or approved sprays prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the plant growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni egbɔ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Giving your tomato plants steady, regular water and adding lime or organic compost to the soil prevents this damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ lime loo organic compost wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and soft trunks that struggle to balance heavy fruit bunches, especially during strong winds. Propping up the main stem with a strong bamboo pole or wooden fork gives the plant the support it needs until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛha aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ afee ekome. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant generate energy to build large underground tubers. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the trees suffer from severe heat, drought, or attacks by insect pests like mirids (capsids). Keeping shade trees on your cocoa farm lowers the temperature and protects the blossoms so they can form healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutua tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo hulutsoo be mli yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings collapse and die right at the ground level soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is a fungal problem called damping-off, caused by soil that is kept too wet and seedlings planted too close together. Giving seedlings good air movement, using clean soil, and avoiding overwatering prevents the fungus from attacking the soft stems.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii ahe naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui amli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ okpa nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekatutua tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Feeding the plant with the right fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores its nutrients and helps it grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ha tso lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does feeding fertilizer to my crops help them produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ yibii babaoo nɔ?

english: Just like good food gives a person energy to work, crops need proper nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium from fertilizer to build strong roots, stems, and leaves so they have the strength to produce bigger fruits and higher yields.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa haa gbɔmɛi hewalɛ koni amɛtsu nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni sa hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛma shishifãi, tsei, kɛ baai ni wa. Koni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛwo yibii wuji kɛ yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the agricultural inputs or chemicals I buy on the market are good quality or bad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji okwaayeli mli nibii loo tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi loo ehiii?

english: Good quality agricultural inputs come in sealed packages with clear manufacturer labels and registration numbers from official agricultural dealers. Bad or fake inputs often have no brand labels, look discolored, or are sold cheaply in unsealed bags.
ga: Nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ okwaayeli mli lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli ni mɛi ni fee lɛ ahe okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ gbɛi aŋmalamɔ nɔmbai ni jɛɔ okwaayeli nibii ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa loo amalei lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, etamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe su etsake, loo ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩii mli lɛ amli ni jara waaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants lose water rapidly through their leaves in strong sunshine to keep cool. If the soil is dry, they droop during peak sun hours to save water, but usually recover when temperatures cool down in the evening if moisture is present.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ kɛji hulutsoo be yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings bend and grow tall and thin towards one side of my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛyashɛ mi saatso lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean and stretch toward sunlight because they need light to make their own food. If nearby trees or structures shade them, seedlings stretch unnaturally long and thin to reach the sun.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ la he miihia amɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛji tsei loo tsũi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsi hulu lɛ naa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛbaafee mlɛo yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of essential plant food, causing the plant to drop its flowers because it lacks energy to nourish the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaahã aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the mature tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bare trunk left Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni eda lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops slow down in growth even when I am watering them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water allows plants to transport food from the ground, but if the soil lacks essential plant nutrients or is packed too tightly for roots to get air, water alone will not keep the crop growing well.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ hu? Nu pɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of flowers but very little actual produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo shi nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Crops need wind or insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower so fruit can form. If heavy rains wash away pollen or bad weather reduces insect activity, flowers drop off without turning into produce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ koni aduawai aba. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie pollen lɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ ha kooloi ayibɔ ba shi lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbatsɔŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid crops give me weaker plants this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ gbɔjɔ afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created to produce a strong yield for only one generation. Saving seeds from that crop causes the next generation to lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ afite nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to put fresh chicken droppings directly onto my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee baawo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken droppings are too strong and hot for young plants, which can burn their roots and ruin the crop. You need to heap the droppings and let them dry and break down (compost) for a few weeks before mixing them into your farm soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ kɛha tsei bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato ni oha egbi ni efite (compost) otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop stray cattle from destroying my cassava farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsinai ni elaaje lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant a hedge of living plants like thorny Jatropha or Gliricidia around your farm boundaries to create a strong barrier, or build simple wooden fences. Clearing livestock paths away from crop field borders also prevents cattle from wandering into your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei bibii ni hiɛ ka tamɔ jatropha loo glicidia ni ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he husu koni ofee gbɛtsii nii ni wa. Aloo ma tso gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kooloi agbɛi ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni tsinai akafã gbɛ kɛbote oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot direct sunshine, dry winds, or insect attacks like capsids. Keeping tall shade trees in the farm shelters the cocoa flowers and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo kooloi tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ ni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my plantain leaves drooping and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in strong heat. The leaves droop or dry up naturally to help the plant save water in its main stem until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks the small tubes inside the plant stem. Because water cannot move up through the blocked stem, the leaves wilt and die rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ paipii bibii anaa. yɛ tso ko shishi Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsi lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why do cassava tubers rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When farm soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate. Waterlogged conditions allow fungal diseases in the soil to attack and decay the soft cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ Shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my yam leaves and causing the vines to wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa wain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads in hot, humid weather. Staking your yam vines up on tall sticks keeps them off the damp ground and reduces disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni ebaaha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the soil?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen gas out of the air and trap it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, the cowpeas leave behind rich soil nitrogen that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Cowpeas lɛ, eshiɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow big and bushy with leaves but produce no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai lɛ? Shi chili bɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the pepper plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves instead of flowers. Giving the plant balanced nutrients containing phosphorus encourages it to blossom and bear fruits.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it a good idea to plant two different crops like cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, yɛ he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together helps you maximize your land. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant recover and produce bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe waa ni amɛnáa toi wuji.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves and spreading viruses. Clearing weeds around the farm and using early pest control protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the dry weeds and bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys the beneficial living organisms in the ground and burns off natural organic nutrients. Leaving cleared weeds to rot back into the soil keeps the ground cool, holds rainwater better, and feeds your crops naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ toɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after waiting for almost a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ be mli ni mimɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to swell into big tubers. If the soil is packed hard like rock, the roots cannot push through to expand, causing them to stay thin regardless of age.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfu ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛje kpo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ekɔɔɔ he eko afii ni amɛye.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in heavy shade and humidity. Pruning overgrown shade branches lets sunlight and fresh air dry the trees out, stopping the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi bibii ni kɛbaa Ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli lɛ. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aha tsei lɛ agbi. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa hela lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rains even when the wind is not very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa tsɔ moŋ?

english: Tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borer insects often eat the plantain roots underground, destroying its anchor so the heavy plant easily tips over in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ yeɔ plantain shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. break e anchor No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack consistent water. Keeping the soil damp and using mulch around the roots keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know if the first early rains are enough for planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛdu dumɔwui?

english: First rains often only wet the surface soil. Dig down into the dirt with your hands—if the moisture goes deep below your wrist and stays damp for days, the soil has enough water to safely sprout seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Okɛ oniji atsu nii ni okɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tee onine shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehi shi ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to grow. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves to survive, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the tiny tubes inside the stem that transport water. Even if there is water in the soil, the plant cannot drink it, causing it to dry up quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ paipii bibii anaa. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu yaa Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. egbi oya

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from lack of water or lack of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli?

english: Water-stressed plants usually droop or curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day but recover in the cool evening. Nutrient-deficient plants change color—such as turning yellow, pale green, or purple—and do not recover at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaatsa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli. Tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su, tamɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, loo ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Vine ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛkwɔɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the vine produce the food that goes down into the ground to make big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: The young shoots, called suckers, steal food, water, and soil nutrients from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother tree to focus all its energy on making a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii, ni atsɛɔ amɛ young shoots lɛ, juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni eshwɛɔ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ha tso nyɛ lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ahi tso agbo ko ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before they can form pods. If the weather is too dry, if shade is lacking, or if chemical sprays have killed those helpful insects, the flowers cannot form pods and will drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollination dani amɛfee pods. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be bɛ, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ nakai kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tougher and better adapted to the local environment. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop roots have a chance to spread.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I even harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in heavy soil starves the cassava roots of air and allows fungal germs to grow. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akahi nu lɛ mli ni amɛkafite.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves and centers of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni etse ehe ni yɔɔ mi-bi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center of the maize plant during the day and chews through the fresh young leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni amɛyeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii heei amli

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them in the new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ kɛhaa be hee lɛ?

english: Saved seeds die if they were stored with too much moisture or kept in a warm place where insects and mold could attack the living embryo inside the seed before planting day.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ dani gbi ni akɛduɔ lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, acting as a protective canopy while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛitsu ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores soil nutrients so the maize can regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ŋmãa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to build energy and grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases and helping the plant catch more sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes in the very middle of my young corn shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn shoots lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the central whorl of young corn plants. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash prevents them from destroying the growing tip of your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas extract nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, helping the maize grow better without exhausting the ground.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long, cutting off oxygen and allowing underground fungi to thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium during flowering. Keeping soil consistently moist and applying compost helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer directly onto dry soil during a warm week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can absorb. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves it concentrated on top, which can burn plant roots or evaporate into the air before the crop benefits.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaná baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my seeds after the first early rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry out newly sprouted seeds. It is safest to wait until two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the soil before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients right from underneath your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni mijieɔ tsei wuji kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight. Leaving some shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains provides shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough to survive direct heat.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: How do I know if I am planting my cassava stems too close to each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ miidu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cassava is planted too close, the leaves fight for sunlight and the roots fight for water, leading to thin stems and tiny tubers. Giving them about 1 meter of space allows the underground tubers to grow full and large.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai kɛ hulu la he akaŋ ni shishifãi kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni miihe ashɛ mita kome ha lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ agbo.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks next to my yam vines as they start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi kɛ́ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high to catch sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to manufacture food and build large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests if I plant cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it becomes exhausted. Rotating with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restock nutrients in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu lɛ baaya nɔ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaafite. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing, but avoid applying it right before a heavy rainstorm. Placing it near the plant roots and lightly covering it with soil keeps it safe.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum ni naa wa aba. Kɛ́ okɛma tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ sũ fioo ko ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch delicate new sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the young roots always have moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ana ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their blossoms to save energy. Watering regularly at the roots and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool and preserves the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant beans in the same field where I planted my tall maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, it is very good! Beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil to feed the maize, while the tall maize stalks provide extra support for trailing bean varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi waa diɛŋtsɛ! Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ baaha yelikɛbuamɔ kroko aha ŋmãa henɔi lɛ.

english: I noticed tiny worms eating the inner leaves of my young corn; will the plant survive this?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ yeli. Ani tso lɛ baahi shi?

english: Those worms target the growing center of the plant where new leaves form, which can stunt or kill the maize if left unchecked. Treating the funnels of the plants early protects the growing heart of the crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he ni baai heei jeɔ kpo yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ afee mlɛo loo egbe kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tso gbɛi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves receive full sunlight, they produce more food, which leads to larger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems, producing very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves too much standing water in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu babaoo ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii kpakpai.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out their sap, or by a virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the daytime temperature gets too hot or when the plant suffers from a sudden lack of water. Heat and water stress prevent the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli nu fite trukaa. Dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.
