english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I wait for the rain before applying fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ dani mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before crop roots can drink it in. If you apply dry fertilizer on dry ground under full sun, it can burn the plant roots or lose its power into the air.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you clear the farm, that left-over nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ojieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, akɛ nakai nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are strong plants that steal the food, water, and root space meant for your crop. Even with plenty of rain, your crop will struggle because the weeds are drinking the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛha onibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baanu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How can I test if a new crop will grow well on my land before I spend money planting a big field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ shika awo mli koni mikɛdu ŋmɔ agbo ko?

english: You can plant a small test patch in your backyard first. If the crops grow healthy and produce well in your soil on a small scale, it shows that your local climate and soil are suitable before you invest in large-scale farming.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa ŋmɔ bibioo ko. Obaanyɛ okɛwo abɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji tsei lɛ dara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fioo fioo mli. Kwɛmɔ pɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sa dani okɛ shika awo okwaayeli wulu mli.

english: Is it safer for me to try farming a small backyard garden before expanding to a large farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee shweshweeshwe akɛ maka abɔɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ makwɛ? dani egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmɔ agbo ko

english: Yes, starting in a backyard allows you to observe how the plant behaves, learn its water and sunlight needs, and handle pest issues with minimal financial risk before spending money on huge land and inputs.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oje shishi yɛ oshia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni otsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa. Kasemɔ nu kɛ hulu la he hiamɔ nii ahe nii. ni amɛtsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ahe nii kɛ shika he oshara fioo ko pɛ. Dani abaafite shika yɛ shikpɔji wuji kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my onion plants grow tall green leaves but fail to make big bulbs under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ aŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ efee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Onions need plenty of direct sunlight, well-drained loose soil, and proper spacing to swell into big bulbs. If the soil is too hard or plants are crowded together, the bulb cannot expand even if the leaves look healthy.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sabolai tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hoɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee agbo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tsei ni ebua amɛhe naa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Bulb lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ eshwa eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get eaten by insects before the plant can form a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ dani tsei lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ yitsei ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves are soft and attractive to caterpillars and pests. If pests attack the young outer leaves, the plant becomes too weak to fold its leaves tightly into a solid head.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua baai bibii ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee gbɔjɔmɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efolɔ baai lɛ amli shiŋŋ ni efee yitso ni wa.

english: What happens to my vegetable crops if I plant them too close to each other in a small space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he ko bibioo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants thin and weak, resulting in small fruits or vegetables.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛnáa aduawai bibii loo aduawai.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up root crops from underground so they do not rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo tso shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkafite?

english: Root crops usually show readiness above ground when their leaves begin to turn yellow and dry naturally. Leaving them in the moist soil too long after maturity makes them vulnerable to soil pests and rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi tsei jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ hesaamɔ kpo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can get them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are high in water and have thin skin, making them spoil quickly in hot weather or when bruised during harvesting and transport. Picking them when they just start changing color helps them last longer.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ tomato mli, ni ehewolo lɛ mli tseee. Tomato fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ kɛ gbɛfaa be mli. Kɛ́ ohala amɛ beni amɛjeɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔ shishi kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do market buyers suddenly refuse to buy my vegetables even when the harvest is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kpooɔ trukaa akɛ amɛbaahe mi-vegetables lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: When many farmers in the same area harvest perishable crops like tomatoes or cabbages at the exact same time, the market gets flooded. Supply becomes higher than buyer demand, causing prices to collapse or crops to go unsold.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya tamɔ tomato loo kaabe yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nu baaho jara lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ taoɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ajara baa shi loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If nobody is buying my harvested vegetables, what can I do with them so they do not go to complete waste?
ga: Kɛji mɔ ko mɔ ko heee aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ Mɛni mafee kɛ nakai aduawai lɛ koni amɛkafee yaka?

english: You can feed fresh excess vegetables to farm animals or plow them back into your soil as green manure. As they decay, they return rich nutrients to the soil for your next planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine aha ŋmɔ mli kooloi loo okɛ amɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ amɛfite Ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which fast-growing vegetables can I plant around my house to quickly feed my family and children?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? shia koni akɛ niyenii aha weku lɛ kɛ gbekɛbii lɛ Mi oya?

english: Leafy green vegetables like local spinach, amaranth, and short-cycle backyard vegetables grow rapidly and can be harvested within a few weeks to provide healthy meals for your household.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach, spinach, kɛ sɛɛgbɛ aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli koni ekɛ niyenii ni hi aha oshia lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ mihe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their delicate leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow healthy green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa afee baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso lɛ ni ekwɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize crop without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni nɔ ko nɔ ko fataaa he.

english: Why do I need to put long bamboo poles next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ awo ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high toward the sun so their leaves can catch light and make energy. When the vines climb well on poles, the plant can direct more food down into the ground to grow large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ atere niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming out around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni jeɔ kpo kɛbɔleɔ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant grows big and produces heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle puts part of the stem deep enough in the soil to grow strong roots while keeping buds above ground to sprout quickly into stems.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ fã ko abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi ni wa aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni eda oya kɛbote tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs and pepper roots rot when water stands on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive; when stagnant water fills all the soil spaces for days, roots drown and harmful fungal diseases attack them, making the plant wilt and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara baatutua amɛ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are small green caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young maize and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai amli ni amɛmiiye bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, pests that feed on the soft growing centers of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying organic or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnel stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This rot at the bottom of the tomato is blossom-end rot, caused when the plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up the nutrients it needs to make firm fruit.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi nɛɛ ji blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick even when I buy fresh seeds to plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛji mihe dumɔwui heei ni mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po.

english: Crop diseases and pests can stay hidden in the soil long after harvest. If you plant the same crop in the same spot, those pests are already waiting in the soil to attack your new plants.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ miimɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtutua otsei heei lɛ.

english: How do I clear crop diseases from my farm soil without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can clear soil diseases by switching to a completely different type of crop, like planting beans after maize. The diseases that attack maize cannot survive on beans, so they die out naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ ahi ŋmãa mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying because of diseases in the soil or just because of poor rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛkɛ hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi lɛ?

english: Soil diseases often cause young plants to yellow, wilt, or rot at the roots even when the soil is wet, especially if you have grown the exact same crop on that land recently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai haa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni egboɔ loo egboɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land immediately after harvesting my old cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikpa ŋmei momo?

english: It is better not to plant the same crop immediately. Instead, plant a fast-growing crop like beans for about three months first to clean the soil and break the cycle of cassava diseases before planting cassava again.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooodu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei aaafee nyɔji etɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛtsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efo ŋmei hela lɛ mli dani odu ŋmei ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my land if I keep planting tomatoes in the same spot season after season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows tomato-specific diseases to build up, leading to lower yields and sickly plants every year.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ helai ni abua naa ni kɔɔ tomato pɔtɛɛ he lɛ baa Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: If I want to clear disease from my land, can I plant any crop as my next crop?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni majie hela kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ madu tsei komɛi akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, you must choose a crop from a different family. For example, if you grew cereal crops like maize, switch to a legume like beans, as diseases from one plant family usually cannot survive on another.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ weku kroko mli. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu ŋmaa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ tsei aweku kome mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ ŋmãa weku kroko mli.

english: What is a short-term crop, and why should I plant one on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A short-term crop is a plant like beans or quick-growing vegetables that matures in about three months. Planting them helps break disease cycles on your land while giving you a quick harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ji nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai ni shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Dumɔ baaye abua ni helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa oya.

english: Why do extension officers always advise farmers to plant beans between main farming seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans grow quickly in about three months, fix food back into the soil, and starve out diseases that attack other crops, leaving your field healthier for your next main crop.
ga: Beans lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ejieɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛyaa. Ha oŋmɔji lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How many months do I need to grow a quick crop to clean my soil of plant diseases?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makwɛ tsei koni manyɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe?

english: Growing a quick crop like beans for about three months is usually enough time to starve out disease pests and prepare the land for re-planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ oya aaafee nyɔji etɛ ji be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛjieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ kɛsaa he lɛ kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: Is it better to leave my land empty to rest, or should I plant beans for a few months?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mihe ajɔɔ mihe loo esa akɛ madu ŋmeii nyɔji fioo komɛi?

english: Planting beans for three months is better than leaving the land empty because the beans protect the soil from rain damage, add good nutrients, and clear out diseases at the same time.
ga: Beans ni aduɔ nyɔji 3 lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ejaakɛ beans lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Okɛ niyenii kpakpai afata he ni ojie helai kɛjɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and can dry out quickly. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the young cocoa moist and protected while its roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛ baanyɛ agbi oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the ground, providing natural nutrients that help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their dark green color and strength, so yellow leaves mean the crop needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. If the ground gets too dry or too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How do I know which direction to insert a cassava stem cutting into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the cassava stem. The buds must point upwards toward the sky so the stems and leaves grow up easily while roots develop below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kpɛtɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why must I tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp ground to prevent fungal disease and allows the plant to catch sun, resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why will planting my crops too close together reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi náa aduawai bibii loo bulbs.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops before adding fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds first ensures your crops get all the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny green caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender leaves. Detecting them early allows you to spray recommended treatments before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani ofiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my pepper plants with cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ aha shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with cut grass or dry leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot weather and stops weeds from sprouting around your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my corn seeds need fertilizer placed near them at the time of planting instead of waiting until they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ masɛi beni aduɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃?

english: Applying fertilizer at planting time ensures that as soon as the seed germinates, its fresh root can immediately feed on essential nutrients, giving the young crop a strong start to grow fast and resist early pests.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ kɛkɛ ni Eshishifãi heei lɛ baanyɛ aye niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Can putting fertilizer directly on top of my corn seed burn it before it sprouts?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, raw fertilizer directly touching a seed can draw moisture out of the seed and burn it, preventing it from germinating. Fertilizer should be placed close to the seed so roots can reach it, but not directly touching it.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni eshã amɛ. tsiɔ shweremɔ naa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ dumɔwu lɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he. Shi kaata dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does planting my corn seeds at the exact same depth across the field make harvesting easier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted at the same depth, they receive equal warmth and moisture from the soil, allowing them to germinate on the same day and mature uniformly across the entire farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tight into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up in strong sunshine as a natural defense to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping the plant conserve water and survive hot, dry conditions.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko aha koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my growing maize plant turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen; the maize plant responds by taking food from its older bottom leaves and sending it up to protect the fresh new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ haa hetoo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ebu tso hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop need so much extra water when it starts showing flowers at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo beni ebɔi fɔmɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Flowering is the time when the maize plant shifts its energy into forming cobs and filling kernels, so any lack of water at this stage will cause cobs to turn out small or missing grains.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be ni ŋmãa tso lɛ tsakeɔ ehewalɛ lɛ ewoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ eyiɔ obɔ ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afee bibioo loo ebaaje mli.

english: Why does my corn turn pale and stay small if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ bibioo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, individual corn plants compete heavily against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, leaving every plant weak and stunted.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Abɛi tso fɛɛ tso kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why does fertilizer work better when covered with soil instead of left scattered on top of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi amɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer left exposed on top of the ground loses its nutrients to the hot sun and can be easily washed away by heavy rain before the crop roots ever reach it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he.

english: How do weeds harm my young corn plants before the corn even gets tall?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital food, sunlight, and moisture directly from the soil, starving the young corn when it needs nutrients most.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha ŋmãa afee gbekɛ yɛ be mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why can heavy rain right after planting cause my corn seeds to rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall saturates the soil and blocks oxygen from reaching the buried seeds, causing them to drown and rot before they have a chance to germinate.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ koni ekashɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around its roots. Adding fertilizer like NPK or compost gives the plant the nutrients it needs to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very short and thin this season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida kuku ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ be nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Stunted maize growth happens when soil nutrients have been washed away or exhausted from continuous farming without adding manure or fertilizer. It can also happen when the soil is too hard for roots to spread out and feed.
ga: Abɛi mli dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ loo efiteɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and drop their flowers during hot afternoons even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up, causing stress that makes them shed flowers. Providing light shade or placing mulching grass around the stem keeps the root area cool and helps protect the flowers.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi baa. ni haa hulutsoo be fioo Aloo akɛ jwɛi abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large broad leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cassava harvest if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close together causes the roots to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, small tubers instead of big, thick roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if the insects eating my corn field are fall armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloo ni yeɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ji ŋmei?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged, chewed holes in the leaves and leave behind dark, sawdust-like waste inside the center funnel of the corn plant. Spotting these signs early helps you spray before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Cutworms ni egbee shi lɛ shĩɔ bu ni ashɛre yɛ baai lɛ amli. ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa afɔ dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which dries out the moisture and slows down the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha hela lɛ shishijee aba sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look yellowish and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties for planting is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni etsake ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ni akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally and keeps it fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain can be deceptive and is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent so your seedlings have continuous water to survive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ baanyɛ afee amale Ni bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã lɛ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to clear and weed my bush completely before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie mi-hedgerows lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ ni mafo mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Clearing the land removes weeds that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your young crops, giving your plants the best chance to grow strong without competition.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ooojie lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the heavy rains to settle before planting seeds instead of planting after the very first shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first short rain can trick seeds into germinating, but if a dry period follows immediately, the tiny seedlings will dry up and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku yɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aje shishi.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely forces them to fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, leading to tall, thin trees that produce fewer pods and easily pass diseases to one another.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni ehaa ŋmeii fioo pɛ feɔ, ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa amɛhe oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow after days of continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes key nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil past the roots and fills up air pockets in the ground, causing the crop to turn yellow from lack of food and air.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain leaves are drooping from normal afternoon heat or if the plant is actually dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain baai lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ shwane mli latsaa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli? Aloo tso lɛ miigbo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally curl or droop in the hot afternoon sun to conserve moisture, but if they remain limp and dry during the cool morning, the plant is severely lacking water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi kɛji akɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tsei lɛ amli waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients, as they try to save their energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi wala mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take nearly a year to bear fruit while my maize is ready in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ aaafee afi ni mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a short-term crop designed to grow rapidly and produce seeds quickly, while plantains are large long-term plants that must build thick stalks to support heavy fruit bunches before flowering.
ga: Abɛi ji be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni eda oya ni ewo dumɔwui oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, plantains ji tsei wuji ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni esa akɛ amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same piece of land where I have planted maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the cassava behind to use the remaining space to mature slowly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi yucca lɛ ni ekɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ fiofio.

english: Why do my cassava plants yield large roots in loose soil but small roots in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need soft soil so they can easily expand outwards, whereas hard clay soil physically restricts root growth and holds excess water that can rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ mlɛo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fee lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ, ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to leave old crop leaves on the farm soil after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi tsei ahe baai momoi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry plant matter on top of the soil forms a protective cover that slows down water evaporation, keeps the ground cool, and slowly decays into natural manure.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo lɛ baa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct heat from the hot sun burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture around their young roots before they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay close to the surface and heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over if the roots are not firmly supported or staked.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso nine lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa nɔ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ loo akɛ tso etswaaa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking an important soil nutrient called nitrogen, or the soil has too much standing water which prevents the plant roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi babaoo Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood the farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and creates the perfect environment for harmful fungi in the soil to rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛgboi.

english: Why must I put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akakwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big and healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts together with maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are legumes that can take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally enriches the land and provides free food for the maize crops growing alongside them.
ga: Peanut tsei ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why is it harmful to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers need moisture to dissolve into the soil; applying dry fertilizer on dry land concentrated around plant roots acts like salt and burns the roots, which can stunt or kill your crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ hei ni egbi ni tsei shishifãi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni eshãa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, dry weather, or stress, because the plant feels it does not have enough water or strength to support growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, loo haomɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛbɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaye amɛbua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the dry hot season than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, crops get thirsty and weak, making them easy targets for insects that are actively searching for moisture and food contained inside plant leaves and stems.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaye kumai ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small harvests even when I give the crops water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your plants, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: If my cocoa farm land is small, how can I still get a large harvest from it?
ga: Kɛji mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: You can maximize a small farm by proper pruning, maintaining the correct tree spacing, and using recommended crop boosters or pod-setting sprays. These practices help each tree produce more pods than usual, giving you high yields even on limited land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ahi he ni sa. ni okɛ tsofa ni haa tso lɛ yaa oya loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ pod mli lɛ atsu nii. Nifeemɔi nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ nyɔmɔwoo babaoo nɔ yɛ he ko fioo po.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when trees lack nutrients, face water stress, or lack proper pollination. Using pod-setting products and foliar feeds helps the tree retain flowers and turn them into healthy, full-sized cocoa pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. kɛ nu mli haomɔ loo pollination ni sa ni bɛ lɛ kpeɔ Kɛ akɛ pod setting product kɛ folier feeding tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛ amɛfeɔ cocoa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni dalɛ eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees smaller than they used to be in previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni amɛji nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods become small when soil nutrients are depleted over time or when trees are stressed. Feeding the trees with proper fertilizers and applying pod-boosting sprays supplies the necessary food for the pods to grow large and heavy.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha otso lɛ ni okɛ pod spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ podi wuji ni tsii.

english: Can I plant cocoa on land that was previously cleared for small-scale mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie kɛha shika tsuru ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Land affected by small-scale mining loses its fertile topsoil and may contain harsh chemicals. Before planting cocoa, you must treat and restore the soil using organic compost, cover crops, and soil conditioners to make it healthy again for crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shika bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa ehe lɛ baafite eshikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ, ni tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ ahi mli. Dani obaadu kookoo Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi atsu nii koni efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain carry away topsoil from my cocoa farm, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Rain washes away topsoil when the land has no cover plants or leaf mulch to trap water. You can prevent soil erosion by planting cover crops, leaving leaf litter on the ground, and creating soil barriers to keep nutrients in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha nu amɔ mli. Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi baai yɛ shikpɔŋ. ni efee shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi

english: Why should I spray liquid products on cocoa tree leaves instead of just putting fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ mli ba lɛ afɔse kookoo baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Spraying directly onto leaves (foliar feeding) allows the tree to absorb nutrients quickly through its pores. This is especially helpful during critical growth stages or dry spells when roots struggle to pull nutrients from the dry ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ (Foliar feeding) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ he hiaa waa titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa loo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Beni shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical products on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the evening. During the hot afternoon, liquid sprays evaporate too fast or can scorch the leaves under intense sunlight before the plant absorbs them.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse ji leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaho oya tsɔ loo ebaanyɛ eshã baai yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi dani tso lɛ aŋɔ.

english: How do crop booster products actually help my cocoa trees produce more beans?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni haa tsei yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Crop boosters act like extra vitamins for plants. They supply quick essential minerals that stimulate flower production, prevent young pods from drying out, and help the tree direct energy into filling out cocoa beans.
ga: Nibii ni haa tsei tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ vitamini ni akɛfataa tsei ahe. Amɛhaa minerals ni he hiaa ni haa fɔfɔi feɔ oya. Etsiɔ pods bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow when trees lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from dry soil. Providing shade trees, mulching around the roots, and using moisture-retaining sprays help cocoa trees stay green and healthy through dry periods.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, kɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do I need to remove the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, consume food and water that the tree needs for producing pods. Cutting them off ensures all plant nutrients go directly into flowering and pod development on the main trunk.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa fɔfɔii kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small green worms inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize stem, feeding on young tissues and weakening the plant before it can produce ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ dani enáa toi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss. Once the rains return, the stem sprouts fresh new leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ baai heei ni eyaa nɔ edaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and look light green even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Light green and stunted leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Water alone is not enough; adding well-rotted animal manure or suitable fertilizer gives plants the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for leaf growth. Staking keeps leaves off the wet soil, preventing damp-leaf diseases and allowing the plant to direct energy into growing larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni baai lɛ adara. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela naa ni oha tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is given irregularly, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ aha nu ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots or suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain stem for nutrients, light, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring bigger stems and larger bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara ni plantains lɛ hu adara.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get easily scorched and damaged under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa oya ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with natural fertilizer for the maize plant while providing an extra harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmãa tsei Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the main stem thickens, lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open due to growing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do dark brown spots appear on my groundnut leaves after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is leaf spot disease caused by fungi that spread easily in high humidity and wet weather. Proper plant spacing allows air to dry leaves quickly and cuts down fungal growth.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa he tsɔi baa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow lots of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees use energy for both growing branches and producing fruit. When trees get too much shade or aren't pruned, they spend all their energy growing tall and making leaves instead of flowering and setting cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ niji kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ. Kɛ tsei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ ni ekɛ baai aba yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii awo mli.

english: What causes cocoa flowers to fall off the branches before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ amɛniji anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off mainly due to stress from a lack of water, extreme heat, or poor pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping the farm properly shaded and moist helps these beneficial midges survive and keeps flowers on the tree.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni faaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and die before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and unpruned farms. Regular pruning lets sunlight and air into the farm, drying up excess moisture and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ kɛbaa. ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ baagbi. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my crops dry up and die faster during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds suck moisture directly out of the soil and plant leaves. Without shade trees or organic mulch covering the ground, plants lose water faster than their roots can drink, causing them to wilt and dry out.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds leaves all the food in the soil for your cocoa trees, allowing them to grow strong and yield more pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛhaa o-cacao tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling me to cut off the extra branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extra branches block sunlight, trap excess moisture, and waste tree energy. Removing non-producing branches and suckers allows air to flow, lets light in, and directs the tree's food straight into making big, healthy pods.
ga: Tso niji ni miida lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ he waaa Niji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baawo kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Ha la lɛ atsɔ mli. ni okɛ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: What other crops can I plant on my farm to give me income while waiting for the main cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo kpamɔ titri lɛ?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, or cocoyam alongside cocoa. Plantains provide immediate cash and necessary shade for young cocoa trees, while food crops ensure you have food and income throughout the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain, cassava loo kookoo kɛ kookoo atsu nii. Plantains haa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo tsei bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if insects like mirids are damaging my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ myrids miifite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Mirids suck sap from young shoots and pods, leaving dark, blasted spots that look like brown burns. If you see dead, dry leaves at the top of your trees or dark spots on young pods, mirids are likely feeding on your crop.
ga: Mirids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni efite ni tamɔ shãa he okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji ona baai ni egbi ni egboi yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ loo ŋmeii diji yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ atatui miiba koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce fewer cocoa pods now than it did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo kookoo ŋmeii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, cocoa trees pull nutrients out of the earth with every harvest. If you do not replenish the soil with organic compost, leaf mulch, or fertilizer, the soil gets exhausted and cannot feed the trees well enough to produce high yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ organic compost, mulch, loo fertilizer fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to burn weeds and old crop leaves on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei momo ahe baai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter that acts as natural food and a moisture sponge for the soil. Leaving weeds and leaves to rot naturally creates rich mulch that keeps the soil cool, holds water, and feeds your crops over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ jwɛi kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize crops yield so poorly if I miss the first rains of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ kɛji mikpa klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the first major rains ensures seeds get enough moisture during critical early growth stages, helping them establish deep roots before dry spells occur.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be ni he hiaa waa ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi baa.

english: How long does my cassava crop need to stay in the soil before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-cassava lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most cassava varieties take between 9 to 12 months to mature, and harvesting too early results in small roots with low starch content, while waiting too long makes the roots woody.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛdaraa, ni kɛ́ akpa amɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii kɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tamɔ tso.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the cassava with full access to space, sunlight, and nutrients later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Ha ni ŋmei lɛ aná he ko babaoo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small bunches when I leave many of them attached to the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni mishi amɛteŋ babaoo ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ he hewɔ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for food and water in the soil; cutting away extra suckers so only two or three remain allows the plant to send its energy into bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ekomefeemɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need steady water to absorb plant food from the soil; without enough moisture in the dry season, the plant starves, turns yellow, and slows down its growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia nu daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛjie tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ baaye hɔmɔ, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni ehaa dalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the air gets too hot or when they lack sufficient water, which signals to the plant that it does not have enough resources to support fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii lɛ bɛ.

english: How often should I weed my vegetable farm so that my plants grow fast?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ koni tsei lɛ adara oya?

english: Weeding every 2 to 3 weeks during the first two months keeps unwanted plants from stealing water, light, and nutrients from your young vegetables while they are establishing.
ga: Kɛji okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi tsei ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables bibii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiiya nɔ amɛmiitswa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get white powdery spots on them during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are caused by a fungal infection that thrives when plants are grown too close together, blocking fresh airflow and trapping moisture around the leaves.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni baa kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ powdery yɛŋ baa. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil mounds to expand freely; if the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers cannot push through easily, resulting in crooked and small yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia sweet potatoes koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ yitso lɛ mli mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efite ni amɛfee bibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing good pods after many years on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii kpakpai yɛ afii babaoo ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, they exhaust essential soil nutrients and become shaded by thick canopies, requiring soil feeding through compost or fertilizer and regular pruning to restore yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. They require fast-growing shade plants like plantains or shade trees to act as living umbrellas, keeping the plants cool and preserving soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil because the roots cannot breathe without air in the soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests and diseases to build up. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nutrients in the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baajɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting it with dry grass mulch helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ jwɛi ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they are forced to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds out properly gives every plant enough room, light, and food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Abaanyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the ground around my plants with dry leaves or straw?
