ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents sun heat from evaporating water quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ naa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii fiofio be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out to catch maximum sunlight for energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from soil diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests. Inspecting leaves early and controlling insects keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra Ni akudɔ kooloi bibii lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil creates a harsh concentration of chemicals that can burn plant roots and damage the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai babaoo baa. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, intense sun burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture before their root systems can establish deeply.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry palm leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduawai ni akɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ewo mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool during hot days, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing of the lower maize leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves and the developing cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai ni miida kɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to build up. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems with very small tubers underground instead of large, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bulbs bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off my plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do I find ragged holes and greenish powder inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ powda eŋɔli yɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is characteristic damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar eats the tender leaves inside the central funnel of the plant and leaves behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he susumɔ. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy, allowing sunlight and air to reach inner branches. Good airflow lowers humidity around the tree, preventing black pod disease and encouraging more flower production.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, etsĩɔ black pod hela naa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look droopy in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. As long as the soil is moist, the leaves will bounce back and stand tall once the weather cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛsɛɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops whenever the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baabɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to survive under harsh conditions. Their roots grab water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to sprout rapidly as soon as moisture returns.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: How many years after planting my young cocoa trees should I expect to harvest my first pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa takes time to establish itself on the land. Most improved cocoa varieties in Ghana start bearing fruits about three years after planting, so patience and consistent care during these early years are essential.
ga: Cocoa heɔ be dani ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cocoa henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii etɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsuishitoo kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua. No hewɔ lɛ enɛ he miihia.

english: Why is it important to care for my cocoa farm step-by-step rather than trying to do everything in one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fiofio moŋ fe ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ofee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa farming is a long-term investment. Taking maintenance bit by bit—such as regular weeding, pruning, and spraying—prevents fatigue, reduces costs, and allows you to give proper attention to your crops at each stage of their growth.
ga: Kookoo dumɔ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nibii bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Ebaatsi tɔlɛ naa, ebaaha shika aba shi ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ aha onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ shishijee?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, well-drained soil rich in organic matter that can hold moisture. It should also be in an area with adequate rainfall and natural shade trees to protect the young crops.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli. Esa akɛ ehi he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ, ni tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up so easily under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly in direct sun. They require shade trees or temporary crops like plantains to shelter them until their own foliage creates a canopy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ tsei bibii, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛyashi amɛbaai lɛ baafee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Heavy rain, dry winds, or nutrient stress can also cause extra flowers to drop.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi krokomɛi agbɔjɔ.

english: Does a cocoa tree produce pods continuously all year round?
ga: Ani cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: No, cocoa follows a seasonal cycle. In Ghana, there are two main harvest periods: the main crop season (October to February) and the minor or light crop season (May to August).
ga: Dabi, kookoo nyiɛɔ be ko sɛɛ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ be titrii enyɔ yɔɔ: ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri (October kɛyashi February) kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ loo fioo. (Manyawale kɛyashi Manyawale)

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds cause cocoa trees to lose moisture quickly, leading to leaf drop. Mulching the soil around the base of the tree and maintaining shade helps preserve soil moisture during this period.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ hulutsoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to trim branches off healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that breeds black pod disease and encourages the tree to direct energy into producing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee black pods.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing or curling leaves are usually a sign of stress caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids, lack of soil nutrients, or diseases such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which require prompt treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji haomɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ capsids, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo helai tamɔ cocoa bud virus ni biɔ ni atsa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi.

english: How long can a single cocoa tree keep producing good yield on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: With proper soil management, disease control, and regular pruning, a cocoa tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more before it needs to be rehabilitated or replaced.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa, helai anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani ehe baahia ni aha amɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ loo atsake amɛ.

english: Can I just save seeds from my maize harvest this season and plant them again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: While you can replant harvested seeds, many modern varieties lose their strength after one season. Replanting saved seeds often leads to smaller harvests, weaker plants, and lower yields compared to buying fresh, certified seeds.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ekoŋŋ moŋ, Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be kome sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibii, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests every time I use seeds saved from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over many seasons lose their vigor and vigor through continuous self-pollination. They also accumulate hidden diseases from the soil and parent plants, which slowly reduces crop yield year after year.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Amɛbuaa helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ hu anaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ amli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi fiofio afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What is the difference between the seeds my grandfather used and the improved seeds extension officers bring?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni minaa kɛtsu nii lɛ kɛ dumɔwui amlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ kɛba lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional seeds are hardier against local weather but grow slowly and give lower yields. Improved seeds are scientifically selected to mature faster, fight off common diseases, and produce much larger harvests on the same amount of land.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli jogbaŋŋ. Shi edaa fiofio ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. Atsɔ jeŋ nilee nɔ ahala dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Tao helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni owo yibii babaoo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: How can I test if the seeds I stored at home are still good before I spend time planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ hi lolo dani madu?

english: You can perform a simple water test or rag-doll test. Put 10 seeds in a wet cloth for 3 to 5 days; if 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and good for planting in the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee nu kaa loo atade kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall with big leaves but producing very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen or too much shade, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of flowering. Balancing your fertilizer and ensuring enough sunlight will force the crop to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛbaawo lɛ najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil where they cannot breathe. Adding manure or proper drainage can fix this.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ emɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli aahu akɛ amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my harvest get easily eaten by insects in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ yeɔ mlɛo yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often carry invisible insect eggs from the field or contain too much moisture. Without proper drying and treated storage bags, pests hatch and destroy the seeds quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli kooloi bibii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ kotoku ko bɛ lɛ, ha ehi shi ni egbi ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafɔ oya ni amɛbaakpãtã dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too close creates competition. The crops will fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with very small yields overall.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I plant the exact same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field. Rotating different crops restores soil health.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Is it better to follow traditional farming advice from elders or the modern methods from agriculture experts?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooonyiɛ blema okwaayeli he ŋaawoi ni jɛ onukpai adɛŋ loo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni jɛ okwaayeli he nilelɔi adɛŋ lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Combining both works best. Traditional knowledge helps you understand local weather and soil conditions, while modern agricultural advice provides scientifically proven methods for disease control, seed selection, and higher yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ ekome fata he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Kusum nilee yeɔ ebua bo ni onuɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaawoi kɛ gbɛi ni jeŋ nilee etsɔɔ mli ni akɛyeɔ helai anɔ lɛ haa. Dumɔwui ahalamɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Is it necessary for me to burn my field before planting crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mashã ŋmɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is not always necessary to burn your farm. While burning clears land quickly, leaving the land unburned or burning less frequently protects helpful soil organisms and keeps natural nutrients in the ground.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni ashã ŋmɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi hei ni ashãaa loo ashãaa shii abɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my soil if I burn my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishã miŋmɔ lɛ daa afi?

english: Burning your farm every year destroys organic matter and kills tiny insects in the soil that help keep it fertile, which weakens the land over time.
ga: Kɛ́ oshã oŋmɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ, efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How often can I burn my farm without destroying the soil quality?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mashã miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii?

english: Instead of burning every year, reducing fire use to once every two to four years—or avoiding fire completely—gives the soil and beneficial soil creatures time to recover and nourish your crops.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ daa afi lɛ, abaaba sarawa hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ daa afii 2-4 loo abaatsi la he kwraa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛsaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛha amɛ niyenii.

english: Are all the tiny insects crawling in my farm soil harmful to my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, many tiny soil insects are beneficial. They help break down plant materials in the ground and loosen the soil so crop roots can grow well and absorb nutrients.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii. Henɔi babaoo he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Efoɔ tsei amli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do I see so many tiny insects in soil that hasn't been burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo yɛ sũ ni ashãko lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unburned land preserves moisture and natural organic matter, creating a healthy home for beneficial insects to live and thrive.
ga: Hei ni ashãko lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Bɔɔ shia ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere yɛ mli.

english: How do small soil creatures help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Tiny soil insects digest natural material in the ground and turn it into simple food that your crop roots can easily feed on.
ga: shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii Efoɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ amɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni ayeɔ oya.

english: How do poultry droppings help improve my farm soil?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry droppings act as a rich organic fertilizer that adds essential nutrients back into the soil, feeding your crops without harming beneficial soil life.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Ha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni okpataaa shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Is using poultry manure better for my land than burning bush to clear it?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi fe jwɛi ni ashãa koni akɛjie nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, poultry manure adds valuable nutrients and supports living organisms in the soil, whereas burning destroys nutrients and kills helpful soil insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ashishifã kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa he ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ wala. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni egbeɔ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use poultry manure on crops if I decide not to burn my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ? Kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mishãŋ mishikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Yes, combining a non-burning practice with poultry manure creates very rich soil, as the manure supplies strong nutrients while the unburned soil protects beneficial insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ nifeemɔi ni akɛshãaa nii kɛ kooloi ashishifã fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ashishifã haa niyenii ni mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ashãko lɛ buɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Are poultry droppings good for special or sensitive crops?
ga: Ani kooloi afɔfɔi hi kɛha tsei krɛdɛɛi loo tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Poultry droppings provide a gentle, nutrient-dense organic boost that helps special or delicate crops feed well and yield better results.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fataa he blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei krɛdɛɛi loo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato seeds need to start in a nursery bed before I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ajie kɛya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are very small and produce delicate sprouts. A protected nursery bed allows you to easily shade, water, and shield the young seedlings from pests and harsh heat until they are strong enough to survive direct weather on the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nursery saatsoi ni abuɔ he lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ hulutsoo, nu ni obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ he mlɛo. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on tomato plants are usually caused by insect pests like whiteflies that transmit viral diseases, or by heat stress and inconsistent watering. Controlling pests early and keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli. Mra Be mli Nibii ni Yeɔ Gbɛjianɔtoo Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil is too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving plants adequate water and avoiding heavy nitrogen when flowers appear keeps them attached to grow into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli bɔ ni sa kɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛji fɔfɔii je kpo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi ji ediŋŋ ni egbo lɛ?

english: Black, rotten spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture fluctuates from wet to dry.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common crop pest. Inspecting fields early and applying appropriate control measures inside the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akwɛɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to harvest so it does not rot after picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa lɛ koni ekafite beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard. Drying the harvested grains on raised mats in the sun before storing prevents mold growth and insect infestation.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ tsɔji ni awó nɔ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akadara.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to compete with each other for light, ground water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick stems and bigger fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crop when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to thrive easily on rainfall and light nutrients. Removing weeds while your crops are still young prevents the weeds from taking away essential water and nutrients meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi be mli ni onibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekajie nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because water sinks deep into the soil for the roots before the afternoon sun can evaporate it. It also lets wet leaves dry quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eshishifãi aba dani shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa ni efɔ lɛ hu ni egbiɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: How can I tell if my crops need animal manure or plant food added to the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni mikɛ kooloi aŋmei loo tsei aniyenii afata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: If your crop leaves look pale green or yellowish instead of dark green, and the stalks grow very thin, the soil is low in nutrients. Mixing decomposed manure into the soil restores essential nutrients for healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Ni shishifã lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the essential shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, maximizing light exposure while preventing leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni otsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa baai lɛ amli lɛ hu naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green and grow. It often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning their roots work with beneficial soil microbes to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. After harvest, this leftover nitrogen feeds whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Abaaha nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why will I get a smaller harvest if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the dirt. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough resources to produce large fruits or roots.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii loo shishifãi wuji.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. When stress occurs, the plant drops flowers to conserve its energy for basic survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔ ni haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ ni mifooo shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, leaving mostly top leaves. You can confirm by carefully digging around just one plant stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ pɛ eshwɛ babaoo. Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsɔ hiɛ okwɛ kɛji tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my chili pepper plants curling up and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaves fold up to protect themselves from further fluid loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu kroko ni baaje mli lɛ he.

english: Can I put chemical fertilizer directly into the hole with my seeds when planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata bu ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: Putting raw fertilizer directly on seeds can burn the delicate young roots as soon as they sprout. It is safer to apply fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem after the seeds have germinated.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi sɛntimitai fioo komɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if they are small and not touching my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji bibii ni amɛtaaa mitsei lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: Underground, weed roots spread very fast and steal soil moisture and fertilizer long before your crop's roots can reach them. Small weeds also act as hiding spots for insects that spread crop diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi jwɛi shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi bibii hu tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves need to stay green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even when I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Without resting the land or adding fertilizer, the soil gets tired and hungry.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Leaving taller trees creates shade and keeps the air cool and moist, protecting young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull free nitrogen food out of the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize growing next to them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When too much rain sits in the soil without proper drainage, it drowns the roots by taking away air, allowing fungal rot to grow and destroy the tubers.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers onto the ground before growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ eshwie shikpɔŋ dani mikɛ pepper lɛ du lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, choosing to save their strength rather than feed new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Amɛhala akɛ amɛbaahiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ aduawai heei.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground into full sunlight so they can make food faster, while keeping the leaves away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. koni amɛhoo nii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ shɛɛɛ ebaai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Crowding seeds causes the plants to fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow a large cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tight like small cups during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling can be a plant's natural reaction to conserve water in hot weather, but it is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus to the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ko ni tsei feɔ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my stored sweet potatoes start growing green sprouts inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are living roots; when exposed to warmth and small amounts of humidity in the air, they receive a signal that it is time to wake up and grow new plants.
ga: Atomɔ ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka. Kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa fioo ko pɛ mli lɛ. Amɛbaaŋɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛdu tsei heei.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up and harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa ni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready 8 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving caterpillars inside the plant funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni mishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats young maize leaves and stalks. Applying recommended insecticides or neem extract early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why is my crop yield smaller when I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs stakes to lift its leaves off the ground toward sunlight. This helps the leaves make food for the plant and prevents ground rot, leading to bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or dry leaves on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sunshine, keeps moisture in the ground for longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks like mirids. Keeping adequate shade trees, watering when possible, and managing pests help flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ, tamɔ hulu la, tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo ni sa Nu kɛji ebaahi. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heat spell that can dry out the ground and kill fresh sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains are regular before sowing your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ po lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the benefit of growing delicate crops inside a shade house instead of an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: A shade house protects sensitive crops from extreme heat, heavy downpours, and large pests that you cannot easily control in an open field, allowing you to produce healthier crops throughout the year.
ga: Shade greenhouses lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni onyɛɛɛ oye nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ he, ni no haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do pests attack my vegetables more in an open field than under a protective net structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe ŋshɔŋlooi ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: In an open field, insects can freely fly in from nearby weeds and bushes. A protective net structure creates a physical wall that keeps destructive insects out while still allowing sunlight, air, and rain to reach the crops.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, koolooi baanyɛ afã kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛba mli. Mesh ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote mli. yɛ be mli ni ehaa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nugbɔ shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up and drop their flowers when the sun gets too hot in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save energy. Giving plants shade during the hottest hours helps keep flowers attached so they can grow into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ wo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after prolonged heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up air spaces in the soil and washes away essential nitrogen. Without oxygen and nitrogen around the root zone, the plant cannot feed properly, turning its leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nitrogen bɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why is it better to water my crops directly at the roots instead of wetting the leaves from above?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni majɛ ŋwɛi mafɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu lɛ?

english: Watering at the root zone places moisture directly where the plant drinks. Keeping leaves dry prevents dangerous fungal diseases from breeding and spreading on the foliage.
ga: Nu ni oooha shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi he ni tso lɛ nuɔ nu yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Kookoo tsei bibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ Ha ehi shi kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few peppers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing strong branches. Spacing them out allows light and air to reach all sides, producing more fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaafee kakadaŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaana niji ni mli wa. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava heavy feeds on specific nutrients in the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those nutrients completely, leading to poorer soil quality and smaller tuber yields over time.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ajɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii, ni tuber yibiiwoo hu baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal fertilizer and water away from your crops. Clearing weeds before fertilizing ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the lower leaves and stems of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Trimming lower foliage directs the plant's energy into growing larger fruits rather than extra leaves. It also improves airflow near the ground and prevents diseases from splashing up from the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji moŋ fe ni ebaaná baai babaoo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged and stopping the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Aloo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough strength to produce big fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛaawo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather when water stays on leaves and pods for long periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Nu lɛ baahi baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied a few weeks after planting when the soil is damp from fresh rain, allowing the young roots to absorb the nutrients quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ hee mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight; plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the cocoa trees and keep the ground moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted failing to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry, or if insects ate the seeds under the soil before they could shoot up.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do weeds in my field slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your crops weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-vegetable baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Tiny holes on leaves are caused by chewing pests like beetles and caterpillars eating the leaf tissue, which reduces the plant's ability to make food from sunlight.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baa lɛ amli tamɔ ladybugs kɛ caterpillars ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo maŋɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree, which keeps diseases away and directs energy into producing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ajieɔ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hela naa ni ekɛ hewalɛ feɔ pods.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, causing the plant to drop flowers to save itself from dying.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots to spread and gather enough food to produce bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ebuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, which rain alone cannot provide. Adding organic manure or fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to stay green and grow large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ aha lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my young cocoa trees make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your cocoa trees. Clearing the base of the trees stops this competition so the cocoa gets full nourishment to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-cacao tsei lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha foidamɔ nɛɛ akpa. Enɛ ji koni kookoo lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, no haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people say planting beans alongside my other crops helps the soil yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts like natural fertilizer for the neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why is it important to cut off dead or spotted leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ baai ni egbo loo ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ?

english: Removing dead or spotted leaves prevents diseases from spreading to the healthy parts of the plant and allows the tomato to direct its energy into producing good fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli. ni ehaa tomato kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and droop so fast during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of the leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Covering the base of the plant with dry grass or leaves keeps moisture trapped in the soil longer.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the extension officer yield better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist common field diseases and withstand tough weather, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength and produce lower yields over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Hewalɛ baa shi fiofio ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Providing steady moisture and shade during very hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable garden during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu ni mikɛhaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on leaves can magnify heat and scorch the tender plants.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ aya hiɛ ni eshã tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture and warmth to wake up. If the soil is too dry or packed down too hard, the seed stays dormant or lacks the strength to push through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. aloo nɔnyɛɛ ko bɛ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: What happens to my cassava plants if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete under the ground for nutrients and water. This competition results in small, thin tubers instead of heavy, fully formed roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni yeɔ emuu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do certified hybrid seeds give better yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are bred specifically for strong growth, disease resistance, and high yield. Saved seeds often lose these strength traits over generations, making the crops weaker and yields smaller.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara waa, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hewalɛ sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my crops actually need fertilizer or if my soil is fine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi diɛŋtsɛ loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi?

english: Crops show hunger through their appearance. If your plant leaves look pale or yellow, or if growth is slow and stunted, the plant is lacking soil nutrients that fertilizer provides.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛhefɛo nɔ. Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kɛji akɛ edalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen, a main food for leaf growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nitrogen to the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa lɛ Tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ yɛ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes water-soluble fertilizer off the field surface and away from root zones before the plants can absorb it, wasting your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or low soil phosphorus. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that lose water rapidly in full sun. Without taller shade plants like plantains to protect them, the young trees burn and dry out before their roots can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ekãa lɛ ebuuu amɛhe lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How do weeds growing next to my crops slow down crop growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mitso lɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal these resources and leave your crops starved.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. Amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ ni amɛhaa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy when I pack it into bags immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture. If bagged before drying properly, trapped dampness creates a warm environment where mold and fungi grow rapidly, spoiling the stored grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani egbi Trapped moisture haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ oya Enɛ baafite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly showing small ragged holes and looking eaten up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ bu bibii trukaa, ni amɛgbala ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni aye fɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize during the day to feed, and you need to catch them early with recommended treatments before they ruin the entire stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye nii. Ni esa akɛ omɔ amɛ mra. kɛ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them shields them from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning light yellow with twisted, curly shapes instead of remaining broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, baai ɔmɛ a mi wa nɛ a ngɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: This shape change is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. The twisted yellow leaves cannot capture sunlight properly, which stops the cassava roots underground from growing big.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsakemɔ ni baa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela baa. ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsake lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara.

english: Why does my farmland produce big crops in the first year after clearing, but gives me very small yields by the third year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli?

english: Clearing fresh bush provides accumulated natural nutrients for the first crop, but continuous harvesting removes those nutrients without replacing them. Soil gets tired and exhausted unless you add compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi heei ni afoɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ato kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ kpo. Shi nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ni ekɛtooo najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni egbɔjɔ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off to the ground instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Without consistent moisture and food, the plant discards its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots inside my barn even when I haven't planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduuu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yams naturally go to sleep after harvest, but once warm weather and humidity indicate that the rainy season is near, the tubers automatically wake up and use their stored energy to grow new shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes yaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpa amɛ. Shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ. Bulbs lɛ teɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves rolling upwards like little cups and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo lɛ? ni ekpa tso lɛ shweremɔ

english: Leaf rolling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves. This sap loss damages the leaf tissues and stunts the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat spell that lasts for weeks. Seeds that sprout during this short wet period will dry up and die before the main, continuous rains actually settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ-gbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ otsii babaoo sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli He ni efɔ nɛɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during moderate windstorms right when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni mli wa waa mli kɛ be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak root systems that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a mature fruit bunch. Supporting the stem with strong wooden prop poles prevents the roots from pulling out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni ekɛfi aduawai akui ni edara kwraa lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ Kɛ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my lowland rice plants turn yellow and stop forming heavy grains when the mud dries out completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dumɔwui ni tsii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ beni sũ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Rice plants need steady soil moisture, especially during flowering, to transport food throughout the stem. If the field dries out completely at this stage, the plant gets stressed and cannot fill the grain husks properly.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ hia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ahi shi daa. Titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli koni akɛ niyenii aya tso lɛ shishi fɛɛ Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ edumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmãa lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there are no plantain trees grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa plants can survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rain stops for just a couple of weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?
