english: When water is scarce, maize plants cannot draw key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. The leaves turn yellow because the plant is struggling to make food without enough water and nutrients.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ, Abɛi nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfee niyenii ni nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does planting my crops early with the first rains help them grow better than planting late?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rains trigger a natural release of rich nutrients trapped in dry soil. Planting early allows your crops to consume this boost of plant food right away, helping them grow stronger before pests increase later in the season.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ haa niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ jeɔ kpo. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa onibii lɛ yeɔ tsei niyenii krokomɛi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ye obua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa dani tsɛŋemɔ helai aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but no fruits are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Very hot weather can damage tomato pollen so flowers drop off before forming fruits. Lack of nutrients like potassium or uneven watering also causes the plant to drop its flowers instead of fruiting.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite tomato mli ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and loose instead of growing into firm round balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ bɔɔlu kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages need steady water and high soil nitrogen to form tight heads. If the soil lacks food or dries out often during growth, the leaves will grow loosely instead of wrapping tightly together.
ga: Nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli he miihia cabbage be fɛɛ be koni ekɛfee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai loo bei pii lɛ, egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ he waa lɛ

english: Why are small holes appearing in the leaves of my yam plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Rainy weather creates good conditions for leaf-eating beetles and caterpillars to multiply. They eat the tender parts of yam leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to make food for its underground tubers.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Amɛyeɔ sweet potato baai lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps feed the maize growing next to them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wither and drop off after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni mikɛ fɔ wo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer or putting it too close to the stems burns the plant's roots. Damaged roots cannot take up water, causing the leaves to dry up and fall off.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo loo akɛma tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show yellow patches during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, spread by tiny whitefly insects. These insects multiply quickly during warm weather and suck juices from leaves, damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ faa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can soak up the moisture before the sun gets strong. Afternoon watering causes much of the water to evaporate quickly into the air, wasting your effort.
ga: Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu la lɛ mli awa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Without temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them, high heat drains their moisture and damages the foliage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ ni efite tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes through the center leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of young maize. Applying the recommended insect treatment into the leaf funnels early in the morning stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa koni akɛtsa kooloi bibii lɛ awo baai lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do black rot spots spread so quickly across my cocoa pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal organism that thrives in cool, humid, wet weather. Splashing raindrops carry the fungal spores from the damp soil up onto low-hanging pods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but produces very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much foliage-building nutrient (nitrogen) relative to root-building nutrients (potassium), cassava plants direct all their energy into leafy top growth rather than storing starch in the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ maa shi (nitrogen) babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ maa shi (potassium) lɛ he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, long periods without water, or lack of pollination. The plant sheds flowers to conserve its remaining strength.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu efo mli be kakadaŋŋ loo pollination ni bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I harvest tiny, thin cobs when I plant maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crowding seeds forces plants to compete intensely for limited light, soil nutrients, and ground moisture, leaving each stalk without enough resources to form full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshi akaŋ waa kɛha kane fioo. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ sũ mli nu ni mli edɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko bɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee cob ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I recognize if yellowing on my maize leaves is caused by nutrient hunger?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ?

english: A distinct yellowing that starts at the tip of the lowest leaves and moves inward along the central vein in a 'V' pattern is a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen.
ga: Su ni mli tse ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fe fɛɛ ni eyaa mli kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ‘V’ gbɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my soil producing weaker yields when I plant maize on the exact same patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients faster than they can recover and allows crop-specific pests and soil pathogens to accumulate year after year.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii komɛi fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ana ekoŋŋ. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do selective weed-killing chemicals clear weeds without destroying my crop leaves?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ baagbe jwɛi lɛ ni efiteee mitsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Selective herbicides are formulated to target specific plant structures present in certain weeds while passing through crops like maize or cassava without being absorbed in harmful amounts.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala koni akɛtutua tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ jwɛi komɛi amli lɛ be mli ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli lɛ. ni akɛwooo mli yɛ shika ni yɔɔ oshara mli

english: Why does covering the soil around my young crops with dry palm leaves keep them green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei tsei ni egbi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Mulching with dry plant material forms a barrier that shields soil from direct sun, keeping root zones cool and preventing groundwater from evaporating quickly.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves scorch and wilt during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive intense direct sunlight without enough soil moisture, they lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up, causing them to wilt and scorch.
ga: Beni tsei nine shɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa.

english: How does allowing a little sunlight through shade trees benefit my underlying crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni miŋmɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hulutsoo?

english: Allowing partial sunlight to filter through tree canopies provides crops with enough light energy to grow while protecting them from extreme heat that dries out the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni hulu la ko tsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it good for wind to pass through my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Air movement between plants lowers moisture levels on leaves, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading and helps strengthen plant stems.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi fungal helai anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni eye ebua ni ewaje tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough air circulation in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If the lower leaves of your crops stay damp for long periods or show mold spots, your plants are too crowded and need more airflow passing through them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi baai lɛ mli edɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ ebɔle ohe tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo atsɔ mli.

english: How can I get a good harvest if I have only a very small piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nikpamɔ kpakpa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant tall crops alongside short, shade-loving crops on the same plot so that every small piece of land receives proper light and space to produce food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei kakadaji yɛ tsei kukuji ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Koni afee shikpɔŋ bibioo Shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ naa la kɛ he ni sa kɛha niyenii feemɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay small when I plant too many seeds together in a small space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ?

english: Overcrowded plants fight each other for the little sunlight, air, and soil nutrients available, which stops all of them from growing to their full size.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la fioo, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ adara kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What basic steps should I take when my crops start showing signs of dying back?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi gbele he okadii jiemɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: First check if the plants are getting blocked from sunlight or airflow, then clear weeds and cover the soil around them with dry grass to hold moisture.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji hulu loo kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ tso lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ. kɛ jwɛi koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi

english: What basic inputs or materials do I need to protect my young crops from harsh weather?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii loo nibii he hiaa mi koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe?

english: You need organic mulch to cool the roots, simple wooden stakes for support, and temporary shade palm fronds to reduce direct sun exposure.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ organic mulch atsu nii ni okɛha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Tso tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ be kukuoo mli tsei ahe tsei ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do crops growing near the edge of my farm look healthier than those in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops on the outer edges naturally get more exposure to sunlight and breeze, which promotes better leaf development compared to shaded inner crops.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔi lɛ baaná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ahe.

english: How should I space my plants if my farm is in a very windy area?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mitsei lɛ amli kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa waa?

english: In windy areas, plant your crops slightly closer in rows that block the main wind direction, or plant tall boundary trees to slow the wind down before it reaches your crops.
ga: Yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yɔɔ lɛ Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fioo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli koni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ titri lɛ gbɛ. Aloo dumɔ tsei kakadaji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo dani eshɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and crop cleared bushes on top of my soil help my crops survive the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, stops soil water from evaporating quickly into the hot air, and slowly rots to feed the soil with natural plant food.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant cassava on the exact same piece of farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the soil. Planting the same crop on the same land continuously drains those specific nutrients until the soil becomes exhausted, leading to poor yields over time.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaya nɔ ajie nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafo. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow greener and faster on spots where I burned dry brush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ he ni mishãa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning plant material releases ash into the soil, which contains quick-acting nutrients like potassium that plants love. However, over-burning can eventually damage the living richness of the soil if done every season.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni ashãa lɛ jieɔ sũ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni niyenii ni tsuɔ nii oya tamɔ potassium ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ naagbee kɛji akɛ afee lɛ daa afi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, less leaf surface is exposed to direct sunlight and wind, reducing water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers onto the ground instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed, usually due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its strength for survival instead of spending energy on fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with many bushy leaves but refuse to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Too much leaf growth with no fruit often happens when the soil has too much nitrogen (often from raw manure or excessive fertilizer) and lacks phosphorus, which is the nutrient needed for flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo (bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo mli) ni ebɛ phosphorus, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer cocoa pods when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their branches block sunlight from reaching all leaves, and their roots fight for the same soil food and water. Proper spacing allows every tree enough light, air, and soil to produce full pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la fɛɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ kome nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for my main crops if I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are natural soil fixers. They capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which helps enrich the soil with free nitrogen fertilizer for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers need shade from big trees when I first plant them in the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ ahe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji amli beni midu amɛ yɛ jwɛi mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plantain shoots do not have strong, fully established root systems yet to drink enough water. Heavy direct sunlight dries them out faster than their small roots can pull water from the ground.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yeɔ emuu. Shi loloolo lɛ, nu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya fe shishifãi bibii. amɛteŋ ekome ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do insect pests appear in large numbers on my vegetable leaves right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: The warm, wet conditions after the first rains trigger pest eggs lying dormant in the soil and bushes to hatch. At the same time, young green leaves start growing, providing abundant food for the newly hatched pests.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ehiɛ edɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ jwɛi ni afɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ mli lɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛha kooloi ni fɔɔ ehee lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I don't plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kooloi bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has left from older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves, turning the bottom ones yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist before putting fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer is like powder that needs water to dissolve before plant roots can drink it in. If you put fertilizer on dry soil, the roots cannot absorb it, and the strong chemicals can burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ powda ni esa akɛ atsɔ nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ni tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water and cannot drain away, it starves the roots of air. Without air, roots weaken, allowing soil fungi to infect the cassava and cause root rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ nu ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming seeds and fruit. When a flower fails to get pollinated due to heat, the plant naturally drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee. Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollin yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small harvests when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough space and food to grow thick stems and full crops.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda.

english: Why does my harvest drop when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves out of the soil. It also allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to multiply in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and steal nitrogen and phosphorus directly from the soil surrounding your crop roots, robbing your plants of food regardless of how much rain falls.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛjuɔ otsei lɛ niyenii bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ waa ha.

english: What is eating small holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep into the central funnel of the growing stem to eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest perform worse than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified commercial seeds are carefully bred hybrids designed for maximum yield in their first generation. Saved seeds lose those special yield-boosting traits in the second generation, producing weaker plants and smaller ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ sui ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ toi bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and dry harmattan winds. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to cover them, the leaves scorch, turn yellow, and drop off because the plant is losing more water than its small roots can drink.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baashã. tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni amɛshwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu babaoo fe eshishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ anu.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sunshine, heat, or irregular watering. When the heat is too high, the plant drops flowers to save its energy and survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa, dɔlɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V' down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ‘V’ yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of lower maize leaves means the soil is running out of nitrogen. Nitrogen is the food maize needs to stay green, so when soil food is low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green manure, cassava puts all its energy into making leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients tell the cassava plant to slow leaf growth and send food down to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ kɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ baai lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shi koni eha ŋmei lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread dry fertilizer on my field when the ground has no moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ashwã miŋmɔji amli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Ani ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops can only drink food through their roots when it is dissolved in water. Putting dry fertilizer on bone-dry soil can scorch or burn the crop roots and waste the fertilizer, as the plant cannot absorb dry grains.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata wui ni egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ dumɔwui ni egbi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji aha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the air so they can catch full sunshine to produce food for the root. Keeping the vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from soil-borne diseases and rot.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers act like hungry children competing for the same plate of food. Cutting away extra suckers ensures the main plant gets all the water and soil nutrients needed to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Mɛi babaoo ni nuɔ nu lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛmiiwu yɛ niyenii kome he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rainy season becomes very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji momo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water-loving fungus that multiplies in high humidity and spreads through rain splashes. Pruning extra tree branches to let air and sunlight through helps dry out pods and prevents fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni fɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread a virus. Controlling these small sucking insects early prevents the virus from stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land for three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific soil nutrients maize needs and gives maize-loving pests a permanent home. Rotating with groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and starves corn pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni abɛi lɛ he hiaa lɛ mli. Ni ehaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Sir, why is it that some fertilizers work well for my maize but don't seem to help my cocoa trees?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa mi ŋmãa lɛ? Shi etamɔ nɔ ni eyeee ebuaaa mi cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Different crops have different nutrient demands. Food crops like maize need rapid nitrogen for leaf growth, while perennial tree crops like cocoa require balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium over a longer period to develop strong roots and healthy pods.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ niyenii mli hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, he miihia nitrogen oya koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ biɔ niyenii ni ja tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiɔm. yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba

english: Is there a general type of fertilizer I can use across all my crops to make them thrive?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛshwere?

english: Yes, balanced compound fertilizers like NPK provide the three primary nutrients—Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium—that almost all crops need to build healthy roots, green leaves, and good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ NPK lɛ haa niyenii titrii etɛ: nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: Should I apply fertilizer directly onto the leaves of my plants or put it in the soil near the stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should generally be applied to the soil around the base of the plant where the roots can absorb it, rather than on the leaves, which can burn if high-strength fertilizer touches them.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishi, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ kɛ fɔ tso ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ e ma nyɛ maa sã ke ngma nɛ he wa wawɛɛ ɔ kɛ mɛ kpe.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its strength and needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If your previous harvests were smaller than usual, or if young plants grow slowly and turn yellowish, your soil has run low on key nutrients and needs plant food to regain its fertility.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni okpa tsutsu lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji tso bibioo lɛ daa blɛoo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa, ni ehe miihia ni ená tsei aniyenii koni eku esɛɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I use dried plant waste and farm manure to feed my soil instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, compost made from animal dung and crop waste is great for your soil. It improves the soil's structure, helps it hold water, and slowly releases essential nutrients to your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ kooloi ashishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ lɛ hi kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa onibii amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and lose their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate, shallow roots and burn easily in harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains during their early years to keep the soil moist and reduce heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni amɛmli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi

english: Sir, why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree suffers from pest damage, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Giving the tree proper fertilizer and controlling pests helps the flowers mature into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui efite tso lɛ, nu bɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts producing its first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start producing pods within 2 to 3 years under good farm management, whereas older varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are the leaves on my crop turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Rain provides water, but plants still need nutrient feeding to keep their leaves green and active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii koni amɛ baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni efee ehee.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after light rains. Avoid applying it during heavy downpours, as torrential rain can wash the fertilizer away before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and strong. Heavy rains can wash this food deep into the dirt where roots cannot reach it, or weeds might be stealing it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho niyenii nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo jwɛi baanyɛ aju lɛ kɛya.

english: Why do I need to cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry palm fronds or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or palm fronds, called mulching, acts like a shield for your soil. It traps moisture so the soil stays wet during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and prevents heavy rain from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field alongside my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ titri, ni ji ŋmei lɛ masɛi?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull natural food out of the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them next to maize helps feed the soil naturally so your maize can grow bigger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni aduɔ yɛ Abɛi masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni o-abele lɛ adara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during the dry season to protect itself from losing water through its leaves. It goes into a resting state to survive the heat, and once the main rains start again, it will quickly sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Eboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ, baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do I need to build a wooden frame with palm leaves over my pepper nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa ŋmei tso ko yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Baby pepper plants have very tender leaves that easily burn and die under direct sun. The palm-frond structure creates a shaded canopy like an umbrella, protecting the seedlings until they grow strong enough to be moved out into the full field.
ga: Pepper tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Palm tso lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ haa hulutsoo baa tamɔ ambrela. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants drying up and falling off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani tomato lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil gets very dry and then suddenly gets too much water. The plant feels stressed and drops its flowers to save its strength just to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa trukaa. Got too much water Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away from the base of my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young cocoa trees for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving weeds around your cocoa stems also creates a hiding place for dangerous insects and fungal diseases that can easily spread and kill the young tree.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu feɔ hei ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni egbe tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to turn soft and rot inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when they get cut or bruised during digging, or when they are stored in a hot place without good airflow. Fresh air keeps the stored tubers dry and cool, which stops rot from starting and spreading to other yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji afo loo atswa yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. aloo kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekabɔi fitemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmeii krokomɛi amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains when they are carrying heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii yɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the top of the soil and do not go very deep. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the tree becomes top-heavy, so strong winds and rain can easily push it over unless you prop it up with a sturdy bamboo pole.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ tsɔ tsii Tso lɛ baafee tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre lɛ oya. Ja okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa fiɔ esɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from my last maize harvest to plant for the new farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛduɔ kɛhaa ŋmãa shweremɔ be hee lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength and yield potential in the next planting cycle. Using fresh, certified seeds from agricultural stores ensures your crop grows uniformly, resists diseases better, and gives you a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ hybrid kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii yɛ dumɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni okpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to full sunlight and burn easily. Providing shade using fast-growing crops like plantains acts as a natural umbrella, protecting the young trees from harsh sun until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Ni akɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii kɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and droop when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants droop or fold their leaves in intense heat to reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to shelter itself and conserve moisture during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Will my yam plants grow well if I plant them under big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ du tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: No, yam plants need direct sunlight to make energy and grow large tubers underground. Planting them under heavy shade starves them of sunlight, resulting in weak vines and small yams.
ga: Dabi, sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la akashɛ ehe. Enɛ haa wain tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills up air pockets in the soil, which prevents crop roots from breathing. Without air, the roots cannot take up nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato fruits right after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ feɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil containing fungal spores onto the leaves and fruit. The wet conditions create the ideal environment for these spores to sprout and cause disease spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baaha nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ helai aba.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall flat on the ground after a heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ ahum wulu ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain softens the topsoil around the roots, and strong winds push against the tall stalks. When the wet soil loses its firmness, it can no longer hold the root system steady, causing the crop to fall over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ tswaa tsei kakadaji lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebɛ shiŋŋ. Anyɛɛɛ aha shishifã lɛ ahi shi dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ gbee shi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer shortly after heavy rains begin in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away valuable topsoil nutrients deep into the ground where young roots cannot reach. Applying fertilizer replaces these lost nutrients so crops have food to grow rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni jara wa lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ koni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with organic material acts like a protective blanket. It shelters the ground from extreme sun heat, keeps moisture in the soil, and prevents heavy rain from washing topsoil away.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without forming fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to preserve water and survive. Giving plants light shade or watering during hot spells helps them retain their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ otsei lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli loo okɛ nu ha amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers plant tall trees along the borders of their crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsei kakadaji yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall border trees act as wind shelters. They break strong storm winds before they can snap crop stems, strip off leaves, or dry out the soil across your farm field.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ abobaahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Amɛfiteɔ ahum ni naa wa dani amɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, amɛfoɔ baai, loo amɛhaa sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my crops fall off without ever turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Many crop plants produce separate male and female flowers. Male flowers naturally drop off after releasing pollen, while female flowers will drop off without forming fruit if they are not properly pollinated by wind or insects.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ tsei babaoo woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛjie pollen lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔfɔi yei lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do small cocoa flowers actually turn into big pods on the tree trunk?
ga: kookoo fɔfɔi bibii Te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ tsei akutsei anɔ?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from male flower parts to female flower parts. Once pollination occurs, the base of the flower swells and gradually develops into a full cocoa pod over several months.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination ba lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shishi baafu ni ebaada fiofio. Etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli.

english: What is a hybrid crop variety, and how is it different from my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome? Ni te esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ mishishijee maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ahe eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A hybrid (or high-breed) variety is produced by carefully crossing two different parent plants with strong traits in a research station, resulting in crops that grow faster, resist diseases better, and produce higher yields.
ga: Afeɔ Hybrid henɔi (loo henɔi ni kɛlɛ) kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni yɔɔ sui ni mli wa ni akɛfoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni daa oya. Helai ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: If I save seeds from my best hybrid cocoa pod and plant them, will they give me the same high yield?
ga: Kɛ mibua hybrid cocoa yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ anaa ni midu lɛ, Ani cocoa yibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Not usually. Seeds collected from a hybrid tree often lose their special combined traits in the next generation, which is why it is best to get fresh, certified planting materials from a research station.
ga: Enɛ jeee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ sui krɛdɛɛi ni feɔ amɛ ekome lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona dumɔwui ahe nibii heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko lɛ.

english: Can a farmer manually move pollen between flowers to help crops produce more fruit?
ga: Ani okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, this is called hand pollination. By manually transferring pollen from male flower parts to female flower parts, farmers can increase fruit setting on their trees, especially when natural pollinating insects are few.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ pollen ni akɛ niji jieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi baanyɛ aha yibii ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa.

english: Why is it important to follow exact instructions when mixing spraying chemicals for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifutu lɛ?

english: Mixing chemicals in the correct ratio ensures pests and diseases are controlled without burning the plant leaves, damaging delicate flowers, or weakening the crop's long-term health.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai jeɔ kpo. Abaaye nɔ ni ahaaa tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ loo ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can spraying pesticides on my crops while they are flowering harm my pod output?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye mi-pod lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ awui?

english: Yes, heavy chemical spraying during the main flowering period can damage open flowers and kill or scare away beneficial insects like midges that are needed to pollinate the flowers and form pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔii ni agbele lɛ. ni egbeɔ loo egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii ni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What actually happens at an agricultural research station, and how does it help local farmers?
ga: Mɛni ba diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Okwaafoi Ahe Nibii Amli Taomɔ He lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua okwaafoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Scientists at research stations study crop behavior over many years to develop stronger crop varieties, test safe pest control methods, and discover the best planting practices to help farmers increase their yields.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ni yɔɔ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ kaseɔ tsei asui yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛfee tsei srɔtoi ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Kaa gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ okwɛ ni ona gbɛi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua okwaafoi ni amɛha amɛŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why do officers recommend special training for cocoa farming if my family has farmed it for generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ tsɔsemɔ krɛdɛɛ ko he ŋaa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni miweku lɛ etsu kookoo ŋmɔshi nii kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Training introduces modern, science-backed methods—such as proper tree pruning, correct chemical mixing, and flower management—that build on traditional experience to significantly boost farm productivity.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni jeŋ nilee fiɔ sɛɛ, tamɔ tsei akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kpo. Tsofai kɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Etswaa blema niiashikpamɔ emaa shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ mli.

english: Is getting high cocoa yields mostly about heavy physical work, or does technical knowledge play a bigger role?
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa ji nɔ titri ni haa anáa kookoo babaoo. Aloo ani ŋaa he nilee tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ wulu ko he nii?

english: While physical work is needed for clearing and harvesting, obtaining consistently high yields relies mostly on technical knowledge—such as controlling pests, timing chemical applications, and managing soil health.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ he miihia kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ moŋ, shi yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni anáa be fɛɛ be lɛ damɔ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ nilee, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ babaoo. Tsɔɔmɔ be ni akɛ tsofai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ he nitsumɔ baatsu nii

english: Why is it bad to leave heavy bushes and undergrowth growing around my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oshi jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi cacao lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Undergrowth steals water and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees. It also creates a dark, damp space where pests and diseases like Black Pod disease can easily hide and destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Ehaa jɛmɛ hu feɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ he ni kooloi kɛ helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ atee amɛhe ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya.

english: How does clearing the grass around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing the undergrowth allows direct sunlight to reach the lower leaves and fresh air to circulate around the trunk. This helps the plant dry quickly after rain and reduces crop diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, ni ehaa tso helai baa shi.

english: If I clear all the weeds on my farm, won't the sun dry out the soil around my cocoa roots?
ga: Kɛji mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la lɛ haŋ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ agbi. Ani kookoo shishifã lɛ egbi?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for moisture, but to keep the soil cool, you should leave a layer of dry leaves (mulch) on the ground or plant recommended shade trees instead of letting wild bushes grow.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Shi bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Esa akɛ Oshɛrɛ baai ni egbi lɛ ashwie. (Mulch) yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha koo mli jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us to plant permanent shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees protect cocoa leaves from being scorched by strong sunlight, reduce wind damage, and drop leaves that rot and turn into natural fertilizer for your cocoa.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni hulu lɛ akashã amɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi Ni enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-cocoa lɛ.

english: How do I know the right space to leave between my young cocoa trees when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ ashi yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cocoa trees need proper distance—usually 3 meters apart—so their branches have room to spread and capture light without fighting each other for soil space as they grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná he ko ni sa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 (bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3) no hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ niji lɛ ná he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmɔmɔ la ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye he ko he akaŋ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is my cocoa tree taking so long to grow and produce its first pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani edaa ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Slow growth usually happens when cocoa trees are planted too close together, choked by weeds, or left completely without shade when they are young.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo. jwɛi ehà nɔ Aloo ashi lɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if I use fire to clear the weeds?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ la gbe jwɛi?

english: Fire burns the shallow feeder roots of cocoa trees, kills useful soil insects, and removes the natural topsoil nutrients, causing severe long-term damage to your crop's output.
ga: La lɛ baashã kookoo shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ fiteɔ onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I clear my farm land without damaging my existing crop trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie midumɔi lɛ ni mifiteee tsei lɛ?

english: Use cutlasses or light tools to manually clear weeds away from the tree bases instead of aggressive digging or fire, ensuring you do not strip the bark or cut the roots of your crop.
ga: Kɛ cutlass loo dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii ni okɛ onine ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu loo oooshã waa Enɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ ojieee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ loo ofolɔɔɔ onibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor get a higher cocoa harvest than me even though our farms are side by side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ kookoo babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe moŋ?

english: Higher yields come from good management practices like clearing undergrowth regularly, proper tree spacing, pruning weak branches, and protecting young trees from harsh sun.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ ni akpaa daa lɛ mli. Tsoi ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Afolɔ tsei aniji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are often a sign that the young plant is getting too much harsh, direct sunlight or that its roots are struggling due to poor soil nutrients or weed competition.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ naagbai yɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to remove the plastic wrapper around my seedling before planting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie plastic ni akɛbɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing the plastic polybag allows the plant's roots to spread freely into the farm soil to search for food and water. If left on, the plastic will trap the roots, preventing growth and eventually killing the plant.
ga: Polybag lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli oya koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji oshi lɛ Plastic baamɔ shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when transplanting a young tree crop like mango?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tso bibioo ko tamɔ mango lɛ, te esa akɛ atsa bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should dig a hole deep enough so that the entire root system fits straight without bending, and cover it so the soil level reaches the exact same height the plant had in its nursery bag.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ. ni okɛha nɔ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ashɛ he ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to press the soil down firmly around a newly planted crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atswa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ni adu ehee lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pressing the dirt down firmly removes air pockets around the roots, ensuring the plant stays upright against strong winds and allowing the roots to make direct contact with moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ onyɛ muji lɛ nɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens if the bottom root of my young seedling gets cut or broken when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi shishifãi lɛ afo loo amɛkumɔ beni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: If a taproot is slightly trimmed, the plant can still survive if well-watered, but severe root damage can cause shock, wilting, or stunt the plant's length and overall growth.
ga: Kɛji ofo taproot fioo Tso lɛ hu baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu bɔ ni sa. Shi shishifãi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akpokpo, egbo, loo eha tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ edalɛ fɛɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why must I cover all the roots with fresh topsoil after putting the crop into the hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sũ hee aha shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni midu tso lɛ yɛ bu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Exposed roots will dry out and die under the hot sun. Covering them completely protects them from heat and holds soil moisture close to the plant so it can settle quickly.
ga: Shishifãi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha tso lɛ he kwraa lɛ, ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ he bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi oya.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to measure straight lines when planting mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ asusu line ni ja kɛji akɛ adu mango lɛ?

english: Planting along straight, measured lines ensures every tree gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without crowding each other as they expand in length and width.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ linei ni asusu he lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛtsiii amɛhe naa kɛji amɛmiigbɛ amɛlɛɛmɔ kɛ amɛmlilɛɛmɔ mli amɛshwã

english: How can I tell if a young tree seedling has settled well in the farm soil after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ miimɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A well-planted seedling will stand firm in the dirt, keep its green leaves without heavy drooping, and start pushing out fresh green shoots within a couple of weeks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu jogbaŋŋ lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Buu baai eŋɔli lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbee shi waa. Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ tsei eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why does the root length of a tree crop matter so much during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Longer and deeper root systems reach water buried deep underground, allowing the tree to survive long dry spells when topsoil moisture dries up.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eshɛɔ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi.

english: What causes a newly planted crop to wilt even when the soil looks moist?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni adu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This often happens from transplant shock or root distress caused by improper handling during planting, which briefly stops the roots from drawing up water efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛjɛɔ tso ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli shoofeemɔ loo shishifãi ahe naagbai ni jɛɔ nitsumɔ ni ejaaa mli kɛbaa yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How do field demonstrations by agricultural officers help me avoid mistakes on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ fee lɛ ye ebua mi ni mitsi mihe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ahe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Field demonstrations show you practical, hands-on techniques—like proper planting depth and safe bag removal—so you can practice correct crop handling directly on your farm.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nifeemɔi baatsɔɔ bo ŋaai ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii tamɔ dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kotokui ni akɛshwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni ja atsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their root systems are not fully grown to suck up enough water. They need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them from direct heat until their leaves grow tough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ edako kwraa bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi baai lɛ baafee ais.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves exposed to light and prevents damp leaves from decaying on the wet ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli, ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant takes the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to support new green growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tso lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it in. In dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer draws moisture out of the roots instead, burning and killing the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ. shã tsei ni efite amɛ

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block light from each other, resulting in weak plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. Without oxygen in the soil, bacteria and fungi thrive and cause the cassava tubers to rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi daa ni amɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering. When the plant experiences dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering, it cannot move calcium evenly to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ trukaa, ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmeii bibii?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attack. The tree drops flowers to conserve its strength so it can survive harsh conditions.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ha amɛhao. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni tutuaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why is my plantain sucker taking so many months to produce a bunch even though the trunk is thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tse moŋ?

english: Plantains require a specific number of healthy, functional leaves to store enough energy before they can push out a flower stalk. Pest damage to leaves or roots delays this energy storage process.
ga: Plantains he miihia amɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni fiteɔ baa loo shishifãi lɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by insects, which weakens the leaf tissues as they expand.
