ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their delicate leaves burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a cool microclimate that protects the seedlings until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii woɔ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into high mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ ŋmɔtɔ naa dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Creating high mounds loosens the soil so yam tubers can easily expand underground without hitting compacted earth. It also improves water drainage, which keeps the tubers from rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ hu, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: You should use the mature, woody middle portion of a healthy cassava stem, cut into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with visible growth buds. Avoid using the soft green top, which dries out quickly, or the extremely hard bottom base.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni hiŋmɛii lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbiɔ oya lɛ he. Aloo okɛ shishigbɛ shishitoo ni wa waa atsu nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant takes stored nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it to feed the newer growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni amɛye ŋwɛi dalɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land for three consecutive seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that target maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my soil help crops grow better than using raw soil alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfutuɔ sũ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni ŋmɔŋ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter that acts like a sponge, helping the soil retain moisture and nutrients longer. It also feeds beneficial soil organisms that break down nutrients so crop roots can absorb them easily.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji fataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni gbálaa niyenii mli nibii amli lɛ hu niyenii bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark, sawdust-like powder in the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest burrows deep into the growing tip of the maize plant to feed on leaves, leaving behind its droppings, which look like coarse sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the plant roots from taking up calcium consistently from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays prevents leaf damage and protects fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ hu ashwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ebuɔ aduawai ni baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden forks supports the weight of the fruit and prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ kɛ muji babaoo baa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni tsii lɛ, ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (called mulching) acts like a blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in dark, cool, and damp air. Pruning overgrown cocoa branches allows sunlight and air to dry the trees, which stops the fungus from destroying your pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tsei lɛ agbi. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by tiny bacteria or fungi in the ground that block water flow inside the stem. Rotating your crops every season and avoiding planting tomatoes in the exact same spot helps prevent these diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai bibii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good for your soil. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which gives free plant food to your maize while protecting the soil from heavy rains.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ náa tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are grown too close together or have too much shade, they spend all their energy growing leaves toward the sun instead of storing food in their roots. Spacing them properly allows the stems to get sunlight and build bigger tubers.
ga: Beni aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛhe yɔɔ hulutsoo tsɔ. Ebaafite ebe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaawo baai lɛ amli yɛ hulu la mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni eha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulch helps the flowers stay on and turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli loo tsei aniyenii ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal light, water, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early while your crops are small ensures your plants get all the nutrition they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ yeɔ obua amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my yams under the ground are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the green vine above the ground starts to turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season. This signals that the vine has finished sending all its energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ bo akɛ amɛfee klalo beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear old crop remains from my farm before planting new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii momoi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Old stems and leaves left from previous harvests often hide pests and plant diseases. Clearing or composting old plant remains cleans your field so new seedlings can start growing without immediately getting infected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ashishifãi momoi kɛ baai ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai teeɔ. Tso momo ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oootsi loo okɛwo mli lɛ baaye abua ni otsumɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei abɔi dalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela baaa amɛnɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and cannot tolerate full direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides essential shade to protect young cocoa roots and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Tsei kakadaji loo plantains ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni ebu kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the stalks fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed the plant nutrients deeper into the ground where young roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: If I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant next season, why do I get much smaller crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii babaoo nɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one single harvest; planting saved seeds from that harvest causes the plant's genetic strength to break down, resulting in weaker stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ baafite tso lɛ mli fɔmɔ nii ahewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl up their leaves and stop producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛmiikpa fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada lɛ mli

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot while the fruits are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or overly rich soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in storage before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in warm, unventilated places. Storing them off the ground in shaded, well-ventilated yam barns prevents early decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite oya.

english: Why do my maize plants produce thin stalks and small ears when I plant four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ toi bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which weakens all the plants instead of letting healthy ones thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ Moŋ lɛ, ha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my plot help my maize crop grow better the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, replenishing nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ehaa niyenii ni tsei ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce many flowers in the dry season but shed them before fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Heavy flower shedding in mango trees can be caused by dry spells without water, fungal diseases like anthracnose during high humidity, or a lack of pollinating insects.
ga: Nu ni faaa, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa yɛ mango tsei amli lɛ aba. loo kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. This often happens when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash the soil food away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies and cannot survive under harsh, direct sunlight. Big trees provide shade, keep the air cool, and hold moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo. haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do you recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take natural food called nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This feeds your maize naturally, keeping the soil rich without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa kooloi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over as soon as they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji ebɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the soil, making the plant top-heavy when a large bunch grows. Propping the tree with strong wooden stakes supports the weight and keeps wind from blowing it down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ egbɛ eshwa kui wuji. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua etsitsinɔnii lɛ, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits when the heat is high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, making it impossible for flowers to develop into fruits. When the weather gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save water and survive the heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ aduawai. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that spreads in damp, shaded conditions. Trimming extra tree branches lets sunshine and airflow into the farm to dry out the moisture.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsoi krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out long and watery instead of big and starch-filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛyɛ starch lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to form heavy, starchy tubers. Hard soil stops tubers from swelling, and too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch. Shikpɔŋ ni wa baaha bulb lɛ akafu. Ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need. Even with good rain, crops suffer if weeds are stealing their soil food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam tubers are ready when the green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. This shows that the plant has finished sending all its food into the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii fɛɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ baa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass help my vegetable crops during hot weather?
ga: Te mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing dry grass around crops acts as a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root zone cool under hot sun, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Nibii ni adu lɛ baatsu nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first application of NPK fertilizer should be done about two weeks after sprouting to support early root growth, followed by a second application of Urea when the plants reach knee-height.
ga: Esa akɛ afee NPK ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ aaafee aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni eshishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mra. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ urea ni akɛwoɔ mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purple instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ green ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus or the roots are too cold and wet to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the tender growing core of maize plants; catching them early with targeted treatments prevents total crop loss.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli fãji lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite kwraa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and falling off early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Early yellowing in cassava is often a sign of nutrient deficiency in the soil or infection by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmei Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmei yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to split or grow into odd shapes under the ground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miigba loo amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ?

english: Yam tubers deform or split when growing in hard, stony soil, or when heavy rains suddenly follow a long dry spell while the tuber is swelling.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛmli gbalaa kɛji amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni trukaa, be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi yɛ be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efuu lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three heavy rains before planting my maize seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture deep in the soil to germinate and build strong roots. Planting after just one light rain leaves seeds vulnerable to drying out and dying if the rains stop for a few days.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under harsh direct sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool environment and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant uses all its food to grow leaves and stems above ground instead of storing energy in the roots to build large cassava tubers.
ga: Be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a kɛ pee tso ɔmɛ a wuji.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its nutrients without sending soil to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyaaa laboratori?

english: You can tell by observing your crops: if the leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green, stems remain thin, or yields are much lower than in previous years, the soil nutrients are running low.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ nɔ: kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. loo nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa fe afi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miiho.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and gives pests and soil diseases a permanent home to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli lɛ náa shihilɛhe ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why are there small holes in my corn leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Checking crops early and applying neem extracts or approved insecticides controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ dani akpataa tsei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi attacking the roots and stems. The disease clogs the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even when water is present in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early when my maize plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Akɛni mi-abele tsei lɛ faaa kwraa lolo hewɔ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants grow slowly and easily get overpowered by fast-growing weeds, which steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crop.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ enɔ kunim oya Enɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight where they can manufacture food efficiently, and keeps leaves off hot soil, leading to much larger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ adara yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ni amɛtsi sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ yitso ni da kwraa baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and rotten at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwere kwraa lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or inconsistent watering, which prevents the plant from moving nutrients evenly to the developing tomatoes.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛya tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less grain every year even though I keep replanting seeds saved from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui heei ni mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ toɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, recycled seeds lose their vigor and genetic strength, making them weaker against pests and drought. Buying certified fresh seed varieties periodically restores high yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ nyɛɔ eyeɔ nɔ oya. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baaba.

english: What happens to my yield if I mix two different types of maize seeds together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi enyɔ futu mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Mixing seed varieties causes uneven crop growth because each type grows at a different speed and needs different care, making harvesting difficult and lowering overall yield quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa oya, ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if an old crop seed variety I have been using for many years is no longer good for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui momo ni mikɛtsu nii afii babaoo lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: If you notice smaller cobs, poorer survival during short dry spells, or more pest damage compared to past years, the seed variety has likely degraded and needs replacement.
ga: Kɛji ona cob bibioo ko Ehiii shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii babaoo kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he Dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ hu fiteɔ oya ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ.

english: Why didn't many of the seeds I saved in my barn sprout when I planted them this rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ, kɛ́ midu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui babaoo ato ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved in warm or damp storage lose their life energy or suffer insect damage, which reduces their ability to germinate once placed in wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baafite amɛwala hewalɛ loo kooloi baafite amɛ. Enɛ baaha nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its root tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni abu eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without producing big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and food, causing them to stretch thin instead of producing full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry wind, or irregular watering stress the crop, causing it to drop its blossoms to save energy rather than set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa tsei ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why did my crops turn dark green and bush out after fertilizing, but didn't produce many fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ? Shi ewooo yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into making heavy leaves and stems instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why does my field produce weaker crops when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific plant food from the soil and gives pests a permanent home. Rotating with beans or groundnuts heals the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do young crops stop growing when weeds are left around them during their first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ beni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ he lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Young crop roots are small and easily get choked out by weeds, which steal water, fertilizer, and light needed for early root development.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ mra.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green growth, or that waterlogging is suffocating the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Aloo nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant, or by extreme heat and underwatering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu shishi ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize improves soil fertility because cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak stems and smaller yields.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade from plantain or forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantain loo koo mli tso ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight, so shade plants protect them from sun damage and keep the ground moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Staking allows yam vines to spread their leaves toward sunlight to make food efficiently, which helps the plant grow larger tubers below the ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why did many of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were planted too deep, if the soil dried out completely, or if soil pests like ants and fungal diseases destroyed the seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Should I plant all my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for steady rains to settle, because a single early rain is often followed by hot dry spells that can dry up and kill young seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikome lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ agbe tso bibioo lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too high, when the plant experiences water stress, or when small insects attack the delicate stems of the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and cracks begin to appear on the soil surface around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or mixing organic manure into the soil gives the plants the food they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I mix dry animal manure into my farm soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Dry animal manure acts like a rich, long-lasting food for the soil. It adds nutrients, improves how well the ground holds water during dry weather, and creates a soft soil structure that young crop roots can easily spread through.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. add nutrients Te ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eha tɛŋŋ? ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tsei bibii ashishifãi baanyɛ atsɔ mli agbɛ ashwã mlɛo lɛ baa

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe without air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves droop down during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the hot afternoon sun beats down, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. Providing mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist, reducing afternoon wilting.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ tso lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulch ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ha tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he okadii lɛ aba shi yɛ shwane mli

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny water fungus that spreads easily in dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight reach the trees and allows wind to blow through, drying off the pods and stopping the disease from growing.
ga: Fungi ni yɔɔ nu fioo mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji ni egbo lɛ baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa helai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying the leaves with soapy water or neem oil drives away these pests and allows fresh, flat leaves to grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ hee lɛ ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if worms are hidden inside my young corn plants destroying the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii komɛi ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ni miifite baai lɛ?

english: Look for small holes chewed through the young leaves and dark, sawdust-like waste inside the central funnel of the corn stalk. Spotting these signs early lets you apply natural treatments or recommended pest controls before the worms destroy the growing point.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni atsɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ baaha okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akpãtã he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it directly into the soil. This natural soil food stays in the ground and helps feed your maize plants without you having to buy extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn tsei lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily when exposed to full, bright sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the gentle shade and humidity young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce the energy required to swell the large tubers under the ground. Staking the vines keeps the leaves off the damp earth, giving them full sun exposure and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Small ragged holes in maize leaves are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments will prevent them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai babaoo aba. Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees developing strange swollen lumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen lumps on cocoa branches are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees must be cut down to stop the disease from spreading to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Kookoo niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving inside the stem. Rotating your field with crops like maize or sorghum helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower leaves indicates that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when they do not get enough water, or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from dying. Once the rains start again, the plant will quickly produce fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ ŋmɔtɔ naa dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to grow deep and wide. Mounds loosen the soil, make it easier for tubers to expand, and keep excess water from rotting the crop.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmli alɛɛ. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. ni etsĩ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekaha ŋmɔshi nibii fite.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and tall with tiny ears instead of full ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiya ŋwɛi kɛ toi bibii yɛ toi wuji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize grows thin and weak when planted too close together because the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows full ears to develop.
ga: Abɛi feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa toi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is soaked with too much water, which stops the roots from taking in nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing grains or empty spaces on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the corn silks do not get enough pollen during flowering time, often caused by hot dry winds or planting the corn stalks too far apart.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa siliki lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi loo abele tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why does one corn plant produce two big cobs while another stalk nearby produces only one tiny cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele tso kome woɔ ŋmeii wuji enyɔ yɛ be mli ni tso kroko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji enyɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ekome pɛ?

english: Corn plants give more and bigger cobs when they get enough water, sunshine, and manure without having to fight weeds or nearby crops for food.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants blossom flowers above the ground, but the nuts develop inside the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After the groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a long peg that bends down and pushes itself into the soil, where the nut can safely swell and grow underground.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ko ni shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be harvested from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can test maturity by pulling up a few plants and opening the pods; if the inside shell has dark brown or black spots and the seed skin is full, they are ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ Ni dumɔwu lɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do dark brown spots appear on my groundnut leaves and make them drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miije kpo yɛ mi-peanut baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called leaf spot that spreads during rainy weather. Planting clean seeds and moving groundnuts to a new plot each season helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf spot ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛyaa saatso hee nɔ daa afi lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Will planting groundnuts on the same land where I grow my corn help my corn crop grow better?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull food from the air and deposit nitrogen into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for your next corn crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough to pack into bags for storage without it getting spoiled?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli koni akɛto ni efiteee?

english: You can check dryness by biting a grain or shaking it in a glass jar with dry salt; if the kernel is hard and no salt sticks to the glass, the corn is dry enough to store.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji egbi kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni oooye loo okɛ ŋmei ni egbi awo glase tsinsii ko mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni ŋmei bɛ glase lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto.

english: What brings small insects with hard shells to bore holes into my stored corn, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: These are grain weevils that hatch inside damp or warm corn. You can prevent them by drying your corn completely, using clean storage bags, or using safe storage dusts.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni fɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ loo ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni ooohã egbi kwraa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ kotoku ni mli tse ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ sũ ni ato he shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is it important for me to spread my freshly dug groundnuts in the sun to dry right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-peanuts ni mifo ehee lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes wetness from the pods so dangerous molds called aflatoxins do not grow on the seeds, keeping your harvest safe to eat and valuable for sale.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Fuji ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin lɛ kwɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ, ni ejara wa kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why are my maize plants remaining small and yellow even after I applied the fertilizer I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ ewo mli po lɛ?

english: Fertilizer only works well if it matches the specific nutrients your soil is missing and if there is enough soil moisture. If the soil is too dry, missing other key nutrients, or if the fertilizer was applied incorrectly, the plant roots cannot absorb it to grow healthy.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akɛ ekɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ kpãa gbee, ni sũ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Niyenii nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ lɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is rich enough for planting without paying for expensive laboratory tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwooo laboratori mli kaai ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: Look at the wild plants growing naturally on the land—thick, dark-green weeds usually indicate fertile soil. You can also dig up a handful of earth: dark, crumbly soil that holds some moisture and breaks apart easily in your hand is generally good for crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Obaanyɛ okɛ muji fioo ko hu atsu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni efiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly as soon as the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very fast under the sun. Adding a layer of dry leaves or grass (mulch) around the base of your plants shields the ground from heat, trapping water in the soil for your crops during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (Mulch) fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he. Amɛhaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the cassava plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from water stress, or being attacked by sap-sucking pests like mealybugs under the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. aloo ni ŋmeii tamɔ mealybugs ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ miinu nu

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their blossoms before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of moisture, or poor shade. Growing temporary shade plants like plantains helps protect young cocoa trees and keeps the blossoms cool and hydrated.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa miimɔ amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo ebɛ hulutsoo be kpakpa Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do my tomato plants have plenty of green leaves but very few fruits growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-heavy fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Switching to a fertilizer balanced with phosphorus and potassium encourages fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out small and twisted instead of growing big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deeply tilled soil to expand downward smoothly. If the soil is hard, stony, or the mounds are too shallow, the growing tubers meet resistance and become stunted or bent.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo gɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Growing bulbs lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi.

english: Why are white powdery spots covering the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ehà mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a leaf disease called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, crowded, and humid conditions. Spacing your plants further apart allows air to flow through and keeps the leaves drier.
ga: Powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Amɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hulutsoo, mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Gbɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni baai lɛ mli egbiɔ babaoo.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize field so much faster during some seasons than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ mra fe bei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on young maize leaves, and their caterpillars multiply rapidly when warm dry spells follow early rains. Checking your farm weekly allows you to catch and treat young caterpillars early.
ga: Katerpillar ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmei baai bibii anɔ. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ. Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii ni otsa amɛ mra.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas together with my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they share this natural plant food with the soil, helping your maize grow better without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: How long does it usually take for different crops to mature and feed my family?
ga: Bei pii lɛ tsei Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mida ni makwɛ miweku lɛ?

english: Crops mature at different speeds. Fast crops like maize or vegetables can be harvested in 3 to 6 months for quick food, while crops like cassava take up to a year or more but provide steady long-term food security.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 mli kɛha niyenii ni ayeɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei heɔ afi loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Shi ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ haa.

english: Why do some crops stop producing after one harvest while others keep bearing fruit year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kpaɔ yibii yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Seasonal crops like corn or beans complete their lifecycle in a few months and die after yielding, whereas perennial crops like oil palm or cocoa continue growing and producing yields every year once established.
ga: Be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ewala be lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli ni egboɔ beni ewo ŋmãa ko sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii tamɔ oil palm loo cocoa Eyaa nɔ edaa ni ewoɔ yibii daa afi kɛji ato shishi pɛ.

english: Which crops can give me quick cash to support myself while waiting for my long-term crops to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha maná shika oya ni mikɛkwɛ mihe yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ awo yibii?

english: Short-duration crops like tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs can be harvested within 3 to 4 months, providing steady cash flow while long-term crops like plantains or cocoa are still developing.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa shika ni yaa hiɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain loo cocoa lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo

english: How do I choose crops that will ensure I have steady food and income all year round?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha maná niyenii kɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can combine fast-growing staple crops like maize with drought-resistant, long-duration crops like cassava, allowing you to harvest at different times during both rainy cycles and dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ afata ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he koni onyɛ okpa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How does the type of crop I plant affect how much work I have to do on the farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ saa nitsumɔ babaoo ni esa akɛ matsu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Vegetables require continuous daily care like watering, weeding, and pest control, whereas crops like cassava or plantain require heavy labor mostly during land clearing and planting, with less daily maintenance afterward.
ga: Aduawai biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi, tamɔ nu kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli. kɛ daa gbi saamɔ fioo yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: If I hire farm hands to do the planting for me, will my crops grow as well as if I planted them myself?
ga: Kɛ mihe okwaafonyo ko ni edu tsei eha mi Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ tamɔ bɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ midu lɛ?

english: Crops grow well based on correct planting depth, spacing, and soil care regardless of who plants them, but you must supervise hired workers to ensure they follow proper planting methods.
ga: Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. ekɔɔɔ mɔ ni duɔ lɛ he Shi esa akɛ okwɛ nitsulɔi ni aŋɔ amɛ nitsumɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛnyiɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Does planting long-term crops require more workers than planting short-season crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Long-term crops like cocoa or cassava require labor spread out over many months for clearing, pruning, and harvesting, while short-term crops demand intensive labor packed into a brief 3 to 4 month window.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei biɔ nitsumɔ ni gbɛ eshwa nyɔji babaoo mli ni akɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa. Yɛ be mli ni be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa ni akɛwoɔ be kukuoo mli ni ji nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a crop can survive on my land through a long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Crops with deep root systems, like cassava or pigeon peas, can pull water from deep underground during dry spells, while shallow-rooted crops like lettuce will dry up quickly without regular rain or watering.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Abaanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ lettuce lɛ, gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo afɔɔɔ amɛ nu daa.

english: If I have a stream on my land, how can I use it to grow crops continuously throughout the year?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ faa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛtsu nii ni mikɛdu tsei daa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: A reliable water source allows you to irrigate high-value crops like pepper or cabbage during the dry season, giving you fresh harvests when market supply is low and prices are high.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo kaabe nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ehaa onáa nibii ni afee ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ́ jara nɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops produce a big harvest during the main rainy season but fail during the shorter rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ nii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli shi amɛkpaaa nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a specific amount of continuous water to mature fully; the minor rainy season is shorter, so crops with long growth cycles run out of water before they can finish producing.
ga: Tsei biɔ nu babaoo ni yaa nɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ be lɛ yɛ kuku. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni amɛdaraa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nu baaho dani amɛgbe yibiiwoo naa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain suckers next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that create natural shade, acting like protective umbrellas to keep the young cocoa cool and moist while it grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela koni eha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes them to grow tall and weak with very small cobs, resulting in a smaller overall harvest than if they were spaced correctly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi fe kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the crop needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps refill the soil with nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer on damp soil right after rain or before a light drizzle. Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer away into streams before the plant roots have time to drink it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo fioo dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ fioo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ.
