english: Leaf curl is often spread by tiny insects like whiteflies that bite the leaves and carry viruses into the plant. Using insect nets, spraying neem leaf extract, or removing infected plants stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ baa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ ni amɛwoɔ hela lɛ amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I still need to clear weeds away from my cassava plants even when the cassava is already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ amli lolo eyɛ mli akɛ yucca tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ momo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients out of the earth that your cassava tubers need underneath the ground. Keeping the ground clear lets all the soil's strength go into making big, heavy roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, ebaawaje shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun so the moisture stays in the dirt longer, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from the nice market tomatoes I buy to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ tomato kpakpa mli lɛ toɔ? Nɔ ni miheɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market tomatoes are often hybrid varieties whose seeds will not produce plants as strong or high-yielding as the parent fruit. Buying certified seeds ensures your crops grow strong and produce plentiful fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii babaoo loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo tamɔ fɔlɔ aduawai lɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by small insects after I store them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kpata mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahiɛ beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive when grains are stored while still damp or kept in dusty, open containers. Drying maize thoroughly until it is bone-dry and storing it in airtight bags starves insects of the moisture and air they need to survive.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa to be mli ni edɔ lolo loo yɛ tsɛnsii ni agbele mli ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ anáaa amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil away from roots, so applying fertilizer or organic manure helps the plant stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops improve my field's soil quality?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for nearby crops without expensive chemical inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stems in the correct direction in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ miidu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Check the small buds along the cassava stem; they should point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to bend around to reach light, wasting energy and reducing root growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Yɛ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ ookwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni la lɛ abote mli. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many of their small flowers before pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed. When the tree experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or insufficient shade, it drops extra flowers to protect its overall survival.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni ekɛbu ewala fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my mature tomatoes split open while they are still ripening on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take in sudden heavy water after a dry spell. The fruit's inside swells faster than its skin can stretch, so maintaining regular, balanced watering prevents bursting.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni akagbala.

english: Why did the tips of my crop leaves dry up and burn after I applied solid fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ egbi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ebɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to plant stems or applying it when the ground is dry pulls moisture out of the root zone, causing leaf scorch. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from stems when the soil is damp.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the fresh young leaves on my pepper plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curled foliage on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf sap. Spraying neem seed oil or a mild soap solution deters these pests so healthy new leaves can open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo samla ni mli jɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa. Enɛ baaha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ agbele.

english: Why does my sorghum crop stop growing whenever those purple-flowered weeds appear in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni ji purple lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic plant that latches directly onto your crop's roots to steal its water and food. Rotating cereal crops with legumes helps reduce Striga seed levels in the soil over time.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha Striga dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainy season winds once the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni aduawai niji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can struggle to anchor the heavy weight of mature bunches. Piling soil higher around the base and using bamboo props to support the main stalk stops the tree from falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua panicles ni eda lɛ ni tsii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni nɔ kwɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ shishitoo kɛ ŋmei nibii ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ koni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin sprouting green shoots in the storage barn before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that break dormancy when exposed to warmth and moisture, signaling the plant to start growing again. Keeping your yam barn cool, shaded, and well-ventilated delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni fiteɔ wɔɔhe kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ. Ha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i, hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Sɛɛ ni tsɛɔ yɛ kwɛ̃mɔ mli

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and burn easily. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛshãa oya. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each crop proper spacing allows its roots to spread and leaves to catch enough light to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ebaa lɛ naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves toward sunlight, which feeds the growing tubers underground. Keeping vines off the hot ground prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Kɛ́ ajie wein tso lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops water from drying out quickly, and slowly turns into natural plant food as it decays.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaaa nu lɛ agbiɔ oya, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the land naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to turn green and process sunlight. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ni tsei ahe baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛtsu hulu la lɛ he nii. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Watering your crops consistently early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔji amli po?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your main crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out seeds before they establish roots. Waiting for the major rains to become steady ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baa be fɛɛ be lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep into the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as natural food for the next maize crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny pollinating insects in the farm to turn the flowers into young pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ, nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii afee ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the plant starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni obaanyɛ ole be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my yam plants turning brown and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Early leaf browning in yam is often caused by a fungal leaf spot disease that spreads quickly during warm, rainy weather, cutting short the time tubers have to grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ he ŋmɔtɔ ni baa mra lɛ jɛɔ fungal leaf spot ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha yitsei ni miida lɛ afee kukuji.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my tall crop plants even if the crops are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? mi tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa momo moŋ.

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water from crop roots, and they also provide shelter for harmful insects and diseases that can attack your maturing crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Ehaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua onibii ni eda lɛ hu nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ he.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop black patches on the bottom while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee okadii diji yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant does not get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo amɛnáaa nu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and shed leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni eshwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop leaves in high heat to reduce water loss, entering a resting state to keep their roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ la ni mli wa woɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli koni ekwɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ni mikɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain, so you must dry your maize completely under the sun until it is hard before storing it in clean, sealed, pest-resistant bags.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni mli tse, ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light green and yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen acts like food for the plant's leaf growth; without it, the maize takes nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa tso baa lɛ daa. Kɛji akɛ ebɛ lɛ, ŋmãa baaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farmland help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops must compete with each other for space, water, nutrients, and sunlight. Because they are fighting for sunlight, they stretch upwards quickly, making them thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko, nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la beni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ hulu la lɛ. Amɛjaje amɛhe oya. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees shield young cocoa leaves from scorching sun and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. During continuous heavy rain, if water sits on the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and causes rot-causing organisms to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ be mli Kɛji nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ, Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ayiɔ babaoo

english: Why does my lowland rice crop perform better when water stays on the field compared to dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ?

english: Lowland rice is naturally built to absorb nutrients while submerged in shallow water. Standing water also prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice plants for food.
ga: Afee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli koni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni awo lɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed, usually by extreme afternoon heat, insufficient soil water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, edɔɔ waa yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo, ni haa tsei lɛ náa baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves wide in full sunlight to make energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from weeds and shade, sending maximum food down to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo akashɛ he. Amɛtsuɔ niyenii babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni amɛkwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly spread by tiny insects like whiteflies that feed on the leaves and pass on a plant virus. High heat and dry winds can also cause leaves to curl up to save moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baa curl ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and the trunk snaps easily before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fãa oya dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: When plantain trees snap or fall easily, tiny worms called nematodes or beetles called stem borers are usually eating the roots or burrowing inside the stem, stopping water and food from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain lɛ fã loo egbee shi oya lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ loo amɛfoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I properly mix liquid fertilizer with water before spraying it on my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nu afutu ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛshwie ŋmãa tsei anɔ?

english: Always fill your knapsack sprayer halfway with clean water first, add the recommended measure of liquid fertilizer, stir thoroughly, and then top up with the remaining water. Mixing this way ensures the fertilizer distributes evenly so it does not burn your crop leaves.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse awo sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi fã klɛŋklɛŋ. Okɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo mli, ni okɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ, no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ afata he. Kɛ́ okɛfutu nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaja ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaaa tso baai lɛ ashã.

english: How often should I water my newly planted tomato seeds during their first week in the soil?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mitato dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: During their first week, tomato seeds require consistent moisture to break dormancy, so water them lightly once every morning or late afternoon. Avoid heavy flooding, as excess water can wash the small seeds away or rot them underground.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfo ŋmiŋmi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ nu fioo daa leebi loo shwane mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu afua ni naa wa he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. baanyɛ ayaje kpo loo egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why should I wait a few days after clearing and tilling my field before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni mijie ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Allowing your tilled soil to settle for a few days lets the soil temperature and moisture level balance out. It also allows buried weed seeds to sprout early so you can remove them easily before planting your main crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ekome. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ hu koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya bɔni afee ni onyɛ ojie amɛ oya dani odu otso titri lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my cassava in straight, measured rows instead of planting them randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi ni ja mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows creates clean pathways that make weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier without stepping on stems. Straight spacing also ensures every cassava plant gets equal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa gbɛ ni he tse baa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa ni anaaaa tsei lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ hu haa ŋmei tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent my pepper seedlings from dying right after moving them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings suffer from transplant shock if handled roughly. Always lift seedlings gently by their root ball rather than pulling the main stem, transplant in the late afternoon when the sun is low, and water them immediately.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui naa amanehulu kɛjɛ tsakemɔ mli kɛji akɛ atsu he nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ. Okɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ blɛoo moŋ fe ni ooogbala tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ. Akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli. beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni awo nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and shed leaves when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots that cannot take up water fast enough to match water lost through leaves in direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective shield against heat stress during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha gbɛtsii nii ko aba kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I apply fresh poultry manure directly around my plantain stems as soon as I clean out the coop?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ kooloi afɔfɔi heei abɔle he. Ani manyɛ matsumɔ plantain tsei lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji matsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fresh poultry manure is too strong and generates intense heat and ammonia gases as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots. You must let fresh manure rot and cool down in a shaded heap for several weeks before applying it to your crops.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã hee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ ammonia gas baa be mli ni ashishifã lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ agbo ni edɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ mli otsii komɛi dani okɛwo onibii amli.

english: How deep should I bury my yam setts when planting them on ridges?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu sweet potatoes lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miida yɛ ŋmeii anɔ?

english: Yam setts should be buried about 10 to 15 centimeters deep with the cut surface facing flat or downward. Placing them too shallow causes heat to dry them out, while planting too deep delays sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ afu sweet potato set lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 ni fã ni afo lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi loo shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛwo he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha egbi kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize crop is ready for harvesting as dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Dry maize is ready for harvest when the husks turn completely brown and dry, the cobs droop downward, and the kernels become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily leave a mark on them.
ga: Abele ni egbi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni eshishifãi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa, ni eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni eshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ oniji ashishifãi lɛ abɔ he mlɛo.

english: Why do my harvested cowpea seeds develop mold and rot when stored inside tied plastic bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ kɛ akɛwo plastic kotokui ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plastic bags trap air and moisture inside, creating a warm, humid environment where fungi and mold thrive. Storing well-dried cowpeas in breathable woven sacks or sealed airtight hermetic bags prevents moisture buildup and protects them from pests.
ga: Plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotokui ni akpɛ́ ni mumɔ tsɔɔ mli loo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the living shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia baby cocoa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal diseases and helps the plant produce bigger, healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant cowpeas on land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ kɛkɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil fertility without needing to buy extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to insert my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new shoots to struggle, resulting in weak growth and poor tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ abɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because a dry spell might follow, killing the newly sprouted seeds. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures the soil has deep moisture to sustain seed growth.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa koni dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya nɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and dirt inside the top whorl of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the growing center of the maize plant, feeding on soft leaves before they unfold and leaving behind frass that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ni tamɔ jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, during dry spells, or when there is an over-application of high-nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo beni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why is it important to weed my crop field while the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are easily choked out by weeds. Weeding early prevents weeds from stealing sunlight, soil nutrients, and water while your crops are trying to establish strong roots.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ jwɛi gbeɔ tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli be mli ni otsei lɛ miitao ni amɛwo shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: What benefit does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants bring?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, reduces water loss through evaporation, and stops weeds from easily germinating around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees lower ambient temperatures and trap moisture in the soil, protecting the delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward usually signals a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize plants naturally move available nitrogen from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli kɛ sũ ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This pattern indicates a Fall Armyworm infestation. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where it is moist and sheltered, feeding on the tender emerging leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni Fall Armyworm lɛ gbɛ eshwa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni jeɔ kpo lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I allow them to climb tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛkwɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves require direct sunlight to carry out photosynthesis efficiently. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground and spreads the leaves out, allowing the plant to generate more energy to feed tuber growth.
ga: Atomɔ baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni baaye abua bulb lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves soil waterlogged for extended periods, air is cut off, causing the roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Abaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small suckers grow around my main plantain stool at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii wulu lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Pruning back excess suckers ensures the main plant gets full nourishment to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ abɔi akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei niji ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress tomato plants and can dry out or damage flower pollen, preventing fertilization. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei haoɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha pollen lɛ agbi loo efite. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ Ashwieɔ tsei koni akɛto hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viral infections spread by whiteflies. These pests disrupt leaf growth, causing curling and stunting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas form relationships with beneficial soil bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into a soil fertilizer, leaving the soil enriched for subsequent crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ sũ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ wekukpaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay fresh during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ehi shi ehee yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, shielding the soil from direct sunlight. This reduces evaporation, preserves water in the root zone, and keeps soil temperatures cooler during dry weather.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Kwɛmɔ nu yɛ shishifã lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up into funny shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When the leaves curl and turn yellow, the plant cannot make enough food, which leads to small cassava roots and a poor harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi bibii baa, ni akpaaa ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall, but the corn cobs remain tiny and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: Maize needs enough nitrogen in the soil and sufficient water during the flowering stage to fill out cobs. If the soil lacks nutrients or if dry spells hit when the plant is tasseling, the cobs will not develop grains properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo egbi be mli ni tsei lɛ miibua amɛhe naa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ ewooo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my underground yams rotting in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is often caused by waterlogging when heavy rains stay on the field without good drainage, or by tiny soil worms called nematodes that bore into the tuber and allow fungal decay to set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potatoes ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni buɔ bulb lɛ mli ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over easily whenever a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often weakened by stem borers or root nematodes that eat away the underground base. Planting them too shallowly without proper mound support also leaves them vulnerable to strong winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers loo nematodes ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishi lɛ haa plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ ni yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa bɛ he lɛ, no hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa amɛ oya.

english: Why did my seeds fail to sprout after I planted them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a 'false rain' that wets the topsoil briefly before a hot dry spell returns. If the soil dries out quickly, the planted seeds dry up and die before they can fully germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ amale’ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ be kukuoo ko. Dani nugbɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and shallow roots that cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight and dry winds. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, planted around them to trap soil moisture and shield them from the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛhe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become tired and needs nutrient replenishment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Tired soil usually shows signs like stunted crop growth, light green or yellowish leaves on young crops, sudden appearance of stubborn weeds like spear grass, and lower yield totals compared to previous years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa lɛ kpo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ Jwɛi ni mli wa tamɔ spear grass ni jeɔ kpo trukaa kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating large holes through my pepper and garden egg leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye buji wuji kɛmiitsɔ ŋmeii kɛ eggplant baai amli yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny invisible eggs under crop leaves, which hatch into hungry caterpillars that chew the foliage to grow. If left unchecked, they destroy the leaves the plant relies on to capture sunlight and produce fruits.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. ni anyɛɛɛ ana yɛ tsei ahe baai ashishi Enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Efiteɔ baai ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni emɔ hulu la ni ewo yibii lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger on my land than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe wa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and weather conditions. They aggressively suck up soil water, space, and nutrients faster than farm crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ nu, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Why are white, powdery spots spreading across the leaves of my tomato plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and damp conditions. It spreads quickly when crops are planted too close together, preventing air from flowing between the branches.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei niji ateŋ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for longer during hot dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, dead leaves, or palm fronds—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating too quickly into the air.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi gbohii Loo ŋmei—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ha he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, or you can carefully dig up one stem to check if the tubers underneath are large enough to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso lɛ shishi koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okpa.

english: What can I do to stop my plantain trees from blowing down when the fruit bunches grow heavy?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni dumɔwui lɛ akatswa shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and soft trunks, making them easily top-heavy. You can support them by propping them up with strong bamboo poles or wooden stakes tied firmly below the fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooohe agbɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ aduawai akui lɛ ashishi lɛ aye abua amɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small worms eating holes through the leaves and shoots of my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Niyeli bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ yiteŋ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hatch from eggs laid by moths and feed on young leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars come out to feed will help protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboi dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded, and high-humidity environments. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and removing infected pods quickly helps control the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ latsaa babaoo kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room to grow large and produce high yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I clear weeds while the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops a strong head start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy improved seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their vigor and produce smaller yields in the second year. Certified improved seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases, survive local droughts, and produce bigger yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ye nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ nibii babaoo aha

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Ensuring consistent watering during hot spells and planting shade trees around your vegetable garden helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu awo mli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ni odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ Vegetable gardens lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi ahe.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, your maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant is moving its remaining food up to the young leaves to survive, showing that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tsei miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my yam plants growing big leafy vines, but the yams under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji nɔ ko bibioo kwraa?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground. To get big tubers, yams need fertilizers rich in potassium and phosphorus instead.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo sweet potatoes mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwoɔ efoji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ená yitso agbo Atomɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the daytime heat is too high or when water is unpredictable. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save water and stay alive instead of spending energy on fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nu lɛ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ yɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why are my green pepper fruits developing black soft spots at the bottom and falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili yibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ diji yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This issue is usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull calcium up into the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛgbala calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing bright yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, which leads to weak plants and small cassava roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why is my maize staying short and weak even though I cleared all the normal weeds from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ ekpɔtɔ lolo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Your field might have a subterranean parasitic weed called Striga (witchweed). Its roots attach to your maize roots underground and steal food and water before the maize can grow.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ shishi jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga (witchweed) lɛ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ o-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu dani abele lɛ baanyɛ ada.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need plantain trees or shade trees planted next to them to block the harsh sun and protect them during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu plantain loo shade tso yɛ emasɛi. koni ekɛha amɛhe ajɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop in the hot afternoon but wake up again the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can draw it from dry soil. The wilting is a defensive move to save water, and the plant recovers overnight when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Withering ji nɔ ni tsiɔ nu naa koni akɛto nu he. Ni tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push pegs into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After pollination, the plant naturally pushes stems called pegs into the soil so the nuts can safely develop away from the heat.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tsei tsiɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ jɛɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the heavy bunch of fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai babaoo bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny pests called nematodes. Weakened roots cannot support the heavy fruit bunch, causing the entire tree to tip over during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei muu fɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko ba.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener when I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your crops. It supplies vital nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus that are often missing in the soil, helping the plants build strong stems and green leaves quickly.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa onibii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni bei pii lɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli oya.

english: Why do I need to get my fertilizers ready before my seeds start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo ŋmɔshi nii dani dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young crops need immediate nourishment as soon as they sprout. Having fertilizer ready ensures you can feed the plants at their critical early growth stages without delay.
ga: Niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-fertilizer lɛ fee klalo lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohaa otsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ ni okɛ be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: What makes imported fertilizers different from the normal soil on my land?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Imported fertilizers are specially manufactured to contain high, balanced concentrations of plant nutrients that natural soil may have lost over years of farming.
ga: Afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni tsei amli niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛ nɔ ni sa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɛɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and full of holes during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes and yellow leaves are signs that pests, like insects, are eating your crop or that heavy rains are washing away plant nutrients. Using appropriate crop protection chemicals stops insects from destroying the foliage so the plant can grow healthy.
ga: Bu kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ kooloi bibii, miiye onibii. Aloo ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiho niyenii mli hewalɛ nii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ? Tsofai ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa kooloi bibii afite baai lɛ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do crop protection chemicals keep pests from destroying my tomatoes?
ga: Te tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite mi-tomato lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop sprays act as medicine or a defense barrier. They kill harmful insects or stop plant diseases from spreading, allowing the tomato plant to flower and produce healthy fruits.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa loo hebuu. Amɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo amɛhaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop if I spray weed control chemical on the field before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani midu?

english: Weed chemicals clear away competing weeds so your new crop seedlings get all the sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients without struggling against wild grass.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ koni ekɛha otso hee lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ hulu la he. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni kɛ koo mli jwɛi ebɔɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants give smaller roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete underground for limited water, nutrients, and space, which prevents the cassava tubers from swelling properly.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ nu, niyenii kɛ he ko ni faaa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves wilt temporarily to conserve water during extreme heat. Providing adequate water to the roots helps the plants recover faster and maintain continuous growth.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi oya ni eyaa nɔ edaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep producing new flowers every time I harvest the mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei be fɛɛ be ni makpa fɔfɔi ni eda lɛ?

english: Harvesting mature fruits signals to the crop that it needs to produce more seeds for reproduction, encouraging the plant to grow fresh flowers and fruits continuously.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ehe miihia ni ewo dumɔwui babaoo kɛha fɔmɔ. Wo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei.

english: How does harvesting and selling my farm produce in large quantities help my profit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii babaoo ni mikpaa ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Gathering a large yield attracts commercial buyers who offer better bulk prices, and it reduces the overall cost of transporting your produce to the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo ni abua naa lɛ gbalaa jarayelɔi ni kɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ haa. Ni ehaa shika fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛya jara nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crop roots rot in the field when the heavy seasonal rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause water to collect and overflow in the soil, which cuts off the oxygen supply to the roots. When roots cannot breathe, fungi thrive and cause root rot. Creating raised ridges or drainage channels helps excess water flow away from your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ Fungus baakwɛ̃ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my groundnuts if I harvest them while the ground is still very wet from heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Harvesting groundnuts in overly wet soil causes the stems to snap easily, leaving pods buried underground. The excessive moisture also promotes mold growth on the nuts, which leads to harmful toxins that ruin your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii to shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akumɔ oya. ni eshi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hu haa ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ ŋmeii anɔ. Enɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They require temporary shade plants, like plantains or shade trees, to shield them from excessive heat and retain soil moisture while they grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and dry up directly on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during wet and humid conditions. Pruning your cocoa trees to let in light and air, as well as removing infected pods immediately, helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ kookoo tsei lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely— green pods turn bright yellow, and reddish pods turn bright orange. A ripe pod also produces a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su etsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kpɛɔ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu jieɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do experienced farmers say groundnuts are good for improving the soil for next season's crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei hi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil. This enriches the land for future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele.

english: Why are my groundnut plants growing lots of green leaves but producing very few pods under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or a lack of calcium and phosphorus. High nitrogen encourages leaf growth instead of pod formation, while calcium is needed for strong pod development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo calcium kɛ phosphorus bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baa lɛ daa yɛ pod feemɔ najiaŋ. Yɛ be mli ni calcium he hiaa kɛha pod ni mli wa lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree drop most of its flowers before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers due to sudden water stress, cold winds, or attack by pests like thrips and diseases like powdery mildew. Regular watering during flower development and protecting the trees from pests saves the blossoms.
ga: Mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nu mli haomɔ ni baa trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips kɛ helai tamɔ powdery mildew ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ, kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my pineapple leaves turning reddish-yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-tsuru yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Reddish or yellowish pineapple leaves indicate that the plant is stressed, often due to a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or because tiny insects called mealybugs are damaging the roots.
ga: Pineapple baa tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo iron ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Aloo yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts in the open spaces between my young fruit trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ mi-berry tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping groundnuts between young fruit trees is very beneficial. Groundnuts stay low to the ground so they won't block sunlight from your trees, while they protect the soil from direct sun and add nitrogen to feed your young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Peanuts baa shi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ koni hulu la akashɛ otso lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa he koni ekɛha otsei bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How often do I need to walk through my cocoa farm to inspect the crop?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ?

english: Regular monitoring at least once a week allows you to spot diseases, pest infestations, or nutrient deficiencies early before they spread and destroy your financial investment.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ hela lɛ mli daa shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mra. Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa ni efite oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to rely entirely on hired labor to manage my cocoa farm without supervising them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ kpaŋmɔ nitsulɔi anɔ koni amɛkwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mikwɛɛɛ amɛnɔ?

english: Even with reliable workers, active supervision is essential because improperly performed pruning, weeding, or harvesting can lead to low yield and heavy financial loss.
ga: Kɛ nitsulɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ po lɛ Nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa hu he miihia. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ afolɔ jwɛi, jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi ni shika babaoo hu afite.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack essential nutrients, or face severe sun heat, causing the tree to save energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo esa akɛ ekɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akpee Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and burning around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing or burnt leaves usually mean your trees are getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade, or they are experiencing a lack of nitrogen and water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen kɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cocoa harvest keep reducing every year even though the trees look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ miiba shi afi fɛɛ afi eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Trees can look healthy while depleted of key nutrients in the soil; without regular fertilization and soil maintenance, the trees lack the energy needed to grow full pods.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afee tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ bɛ daa lɛ, Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛdumɔ nii ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ.

english: What happens if I don't treat diseased branches on my cocoa farm right away?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mitsaaa tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fungal diseases like black pod or viral infections like swollen shoot spread rapidly from tree to tree, which can cause you to lose your entire crop and farm revenue within a single season.
ga: Fungal helai, tamɔ black pods, loo virus helai, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni onáa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ afite yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do mirids and other insects affect my cocoa trees' ability to produce pods?
ga: Myrids kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Te enaa hewalɛ ni cacao tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mirids suck sap from young shoots and pods, creating wounds that dry out branches and destroy developing flowers, directly reducing your harvest yield.
ga: Mirids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ehaa pilamɔi ni haa tsei aniji egbiɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?
