english: Shade trees act as protective shields that reduce intense sun heat, keep the soil moist, and break strong winds so cocoa leaves and pods don't get damaged.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he koni ekafite kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it important to prune off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to flow through the tree canopy, which prevents damp conditions that breed diseases.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does delay in harvesting mature cocoa pods cause financial loss?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ akpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa shika fiteɔ?

english: Overripe pods attract pests, can cause seeds to germinate inside the pod, and become vulnerable to rotting, which ruins bean quality and reduces the price buyers will pay.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni eyɛ oshara akɛ ebaafite. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ahe afee fɛo. ni eba jara ni esa akɛ mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ awo lɛ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key soil nutrient that water alone cannot provide. Heavy rain can also wash away soil nutrients or cause waterlogging, which stops roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eha nu ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to live in the soil and attack your crops faster every season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa onibii oya daa be.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow thin and yield small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. overcrowding also prevents air flow, making it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tomato ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tomato kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: How does burning my farmland before planting affect my soil and crops?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ baaná mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys essential organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms. Over time, this makes your soil weaker and less able to hold moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes in the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwie bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the growing tip of maize plants. If left untreated, they can destroy the entire leaf area and lower your yield drastically.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite baai lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛha onibii lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops the flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When the ground stays soaked for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing water rot fungi to multiply and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ ayi fa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting tall crops like plantains near them provides shade and traps humidity, protecting the tender cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl in intense heat to reduce their surface area facing the sun. This is a natural protective behavior to keep water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots even when I store them indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ shia moŋ

english: Yams are living tubers that go through a natural sleep period after harvest. Once that period ends, warmth and light signal to the yam that it is time to wake up and sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ nakai be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ la lɛ tsɔɔ o-sweet potato lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ote shi ni okwɛ wain tsei heei.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow from the middle instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes the topsoil around my crops to dry out and crack so quickly under the heat?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwereɔ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaa oya waa yɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly when exposed to direct sunlight. Covering the ground around your crop roots with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture inside for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally and yields two different crops from the same farm.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ jɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry weather to conserve water. Planting shade trees overhead and putting dry mulch around the roots helps retain soil water so the trees stay healthy during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ yiteŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding in the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize shoots. Applying neem leaf extract, wood ash, or approved crop treatments into the center shoot early will control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Neem baa mli nu, tso sũ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ mra. lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ nibii nɛɛ

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap and spreading viruses. Spraying the plants with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps remove the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa baa. Ekɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains flooded because the roots cannot get air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to hold up heavy bunches in strong winds. Using sturdy forked wooden poles to prop up the main stem once bunches form prevents the trees from snapping.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ beni abua naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: High heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop flowers before fruiting. Watering regularly at the base of the plant and providing light shade during peak sun helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: Yam plants are vines that require maximum sunlight on their leaves to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing disease and helping the plant gather energy from the sun.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuaa hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize is missing nitrogen nutrients in the soil or standing in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating holes into the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the central funnel of maize plants. Spraying approved bio-pesticides or putting clean sand/neem powder into the funnel early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Bio-insecticide ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ loo ni akɛ ŋã/neem powder ni he tse fataa ŋmeii lɛ ahe leebi lɛ baafite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or insect attacks from mirids (capsids). Providing moderate shade and feeding the soil helps the tree keep its flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni faaa, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. loo kooloi ni jɛɔ glase lɛ mli (capsid) lɛ tutuaa. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a survival mechanism to conserve water. As long as the stems stay healthy, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves quickly once the rains begin.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ shishitso lɛ mli wa lolo lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: What damage does burning my farmland before planting do to the crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops and retain moisture. Over time, burning makes the soil hard, dry, and dependent on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ ni ebiɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight through, weeding your farm, and removing infected pods stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it good to save seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, or should I buy new ones?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaato dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli koni akɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid varieties lose their yield potential and disease resistance in the second generation. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures high yields, uniform growth, and protection against common diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ yibiiwoo kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli ni atsĩ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces your crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Giving crops the right spacing produces bigger fruits and healthier plants overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo yibii wuji kɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are naturally adapted to sprout rapidly when water arrives. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks of your crop's life is essential so they do not steal food away from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nu bote mli. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ ni tso wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or excessive chemical nitrogen. Mulching around the plant base to cool the soil and maintaining steady watering helps peppers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I plant plantain together with my young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains ni cacao tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain grows quickly and provides wide leaf shade to protect young, tender cocoa seedlings from scorching sun, while also helping the soil hold moisture during its early development.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Will planting plantain alongside my main crop take away all the nutrients and choke my land?
ga: Ani plantains ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: When spaced correctly, plantain acts as a protective nurse crop rather than a competitor, shielding main crops from harsh heat without damaging their growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni buɔ mɔ he fe amɛhe akaŋshilɔi lɛ. Ebuɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni efiteee edalɛ.

english: What happens to the plantain shade trees once my main crop grows big and strong?
ga: Mɛni baaba shade dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mitso titri lɛ da ni ehiɛ wa?

english: As your main tree crop matures and forms a full leaf cover, it naturally dominates the area, indicating the plantain has done its job and can be harvested or thinned out.
ga: Beni otso titri lɛ eda ni ebaaha ehe kwraa lɛ. Ebaaye jɛmɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni abaanyɛ akpa loo afee lɛ bibioo.

english: How am I supposed to earn money while waiting over a year for my tree crops to start producing?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ nɔ ni fe afi koni mitsei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Planting quick-yielding crops like plantain alongside slow-maturing tree crops gives you interim harvests to sell, providing quick income while your main crop matures.
ga: Nibii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains ni oookwɛ yɛ afi mli tsei ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ ahe lɛ haa onáa be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ. Na shika oya be mli ni onibii titrii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I have to spend so much money on my farm during the first few months before seeing any harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli dani mana ŋmaakpamɔ ko lɛ?

english: Initial expenses go toward land preparation, planting material, and early maintenance, which creates the strong foundation necessary for long-term crop survival and high future yields.
ga: Shishijee nyɔmɔwoo lɛ ekomɛi ji shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, dumɔ nibii, kɛ shishijee saamɔ. Enɛ haa shishitoo ni wa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa.

english: Can short-term food crops really help cover the maintenance costs of my farm?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ saamɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: Yes, selling quick harvests from companion crops like plantain helps cover labor and weeding costs during the critical early months before your main crop yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaa ni akpaa oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ amli lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ he nyɔmɔ yɛ shishijee nyɔji ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli dani onibii titrii lɛ baa.

english: How long does a plantain sucker usually take from planting until it gives me a harvestable bunch?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain suckers lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A plantain plant typically takes around a year to a year and a half (12 to 18 months) to fully mature, flower, and produce a ripe bunch ready for sale or consumption.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee afi kome kɛyashi afi kɛ fã (nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18) dani ekwɛɔ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ loo aye.

english: How do I know if my newly planted seedlings have successfully survived and established in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛye omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When your seedlings survive the initial dry months and start pushing out strong, healthy leaves and shoots, it shows they have overcome transplant stress and taken firm root.
ga: Beni odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ejeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eye nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ nɔ kunim, ni amɛshishifãi etswa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings look weak and stressed during their first two months in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhaoɔ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants experience shock after being moved to the field and need a few months to grow deep roots, requiring shade and regular care to adjust to the outdoors.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakpokpo beni ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Ni eheɔ nyɔji fioo dani ewoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe amɛwo kponɔgbɛ shihilɛ mli.

english: Why is constant weeding so critical in the first few months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ he hiaa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni aduɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, so clearing them early ensures your main crops survive their vulnerable early stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and struggle to stay moist. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo lolo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same plot of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the farm patch.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji amli.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts help make my land better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their root nodules, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited light, water, and soil nutrients, leaving each plant with less energy to make large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii agbo.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops before your crops can absorb them, acting like resource thieves on your farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ. ni feɔ enii tamɔ nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jumɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water covers the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop roll up tightly like narrow tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves into tight tubes during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it good practice to cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, prevents weed seeds from sprouting, and slowly feeds the soil as it decays.
ga: Mulching kɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii fiofio be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or lack of pollination, sacrificing reproduction to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Shaa fɔmɔ afɔle koni eha tomato tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so when the soil runs out, the plant pulls remaining nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put essential nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Large trees act as protective umbrellas that provide shade and keep the air moist around young cocoa; without them, the harsh sun scorches the leaves and dries out the young roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ parasol ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli fũuɔ. Kɛ́ amɛbɛ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any tomatoes during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants undergo heat stress, which prevents proper pollination inside the flowers. Because the flowers cannot be fertilized in extreme heat, the plant drops them to save its energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee fɔmɔ nii yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up in the hot afternoon even though it rained early this morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli beni Ni nugbɔ nɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Curling or drooping leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and save moisture.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get fewer or smaller tubers?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yitsei fioo loo bibii?

english: Crowding cassava stems makes plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each stem enough space allows roots to expand freely underground into large, healthy tubers instead of thin, weak ones.
ga: Cassava tsei ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfeɔ tso agbo ko ni mli wa. Mohu ɔ, yi ɔ he tsɔ nɛ e he gbɔjɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist after a light rain, or just before a moderate rain. Heavy downpours will wash top-dressed fertilizer right off your farm, while bone-dry soil will burn plant roots when fertilizer is applied without moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ baashã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide deep inside the soft central funnel of maize plants during the daytime to avoid heat and natural predators, coming out at night to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do white, powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves during wet and humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetable baa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: White spots during humid weather are usually fungal diseases like powdery mildew. Fungal spores thrive and spread rapidly when high moisture in the air combines with poor airflow between tightly packed leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela tamɔ powdery mildew. Fungal spores lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ ateŋ lɛ fata he.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil in large numbers, ready to sprout rapidly the moment sunlight and rain hit cleared land.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Edumɔwui lɛ kã shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo Efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants grown beside them to act as natural umbrellas until they are older and strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should leave only one or two strong shoots (suckers) and remove the rest. If too many shoots grow together, they steal water and food from the main plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (tso) ni ojie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ebɔ he lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with brown dust inside the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing leaves and eats the young stem. Catching them early with proper treatment prevents them from destroying the entire maize crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsamɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmãa fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wither and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a soil sickness called bacterial wilt. The disease blocks the tiny tubes inside the stem that carry water from the roots to the leaves, causing the plant to dry up despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacteria wilt kɛbaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tsɔnei bibii ni hoɔ lɛ anaa. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli Ha tsei lɛ agbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ po.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy soil, or due to fungal rots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. loo ŋmeii ni egbo kɛbaa Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer restores green leaves and helps the plant produce more peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmei babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young crops after clear-cutting the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ beni mifolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong root systems designed to grab light, water, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from choking out your young seedlings.
ga: Weed ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli wa waa yɔɔ mli. Afee amɛ koni amɛ gbala la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei daa. Okɛ ohe aaawo mli mra Enɛ baatsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo.

english: Why do I need to lift and support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wein tsei lɛ anɔ ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji mafi shi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make the food needed to grow large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is often better to wait until the soil is consistently moist after a few reliable rains. Sowing after just one rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out and die if a hot spell follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ko sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulutsoo be ko ba.

english: Why do I see a strange white powder forming on the leaves and stems of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa powda yɛŋ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miifee yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is often a early warning sign of a fungal disease. It means microscopic fungus spores are growing on your plant, which can weaken the crop and spread to other trees if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, powda yɛŋ ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii bibii waa miida yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi anɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How can I tell the difference between simple rain damage and a real disease on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni efiteɔ nii kɛ hela diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Rain damage usually dries up without spreading, but a disease will continuously spread, cause spots, create powdery patches, or cause parts of the plant to rot over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɛɛ eshwaa. Shi hela lɛ baaya nɔ agbɛ ashwã, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaba. aloo eha tsei lɛ ahe nibii srɔtoi lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why are the joints and branch connections on my cocoa tree turning dark and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fãji kɛ eniji ni yɔɔ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ewo duŋ ni egbo lɛ?

english: When infections attack the joints or branch junctions of a tree, they block the movement of water and nutrients, causing the branches above that point to wilt and die back.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ tutua tsei lɛ ahe fãi loo amɛniji ni kɛ amɛhe kpeɔ lɛ Etsĩɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa niji ni yɔɔ nakai ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I clear the weeds and vines away from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ wain tsei kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing vines and weeds from around the trunk allows air to flow and sun to reach the soil. This prevents excess moisture from trapped around the stem, which stops fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Wein tsei kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ashishifãi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabɔle tso lɛ he, ni no baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Do climbing vines actually harm my cocoa trees or do they just grow alongside them?
ga: Ani wain tso ni akwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ mi kokoo tso lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ loo ekɛ lɛ miida?

english: Vines harm your trees by competing for sunlight, trapping damp air that causes fungal rot, and creating easy pathways for pests and diseases to travel up into the tree canopy.
ga: Wein tsei yeɔ otsei lɛ awui kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ lɛ. ni efee gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai Ebaanyɛ efã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya tsei ashishi.

english: What causes the roots of my cocoa trees to turn soft and start decaying underground?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Root decay is typically caused by soil fungi that thrive in overly wet, poorly drained ground. These fungi attack the root system, causing it to rot so the tree can no longer take up water.
ga: Sũ mli ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi fitemɔ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: Can standing water around the bottom of my cocoa trees make them sick?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛye hela?

english: Yes, waterlogging starves the roots of air and creates ideal conditions for harmful soil fungi to multiply and attack the roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa koni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers ask me to inspect my cocoa farm regularly even when the trees look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ mi koni miyakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Checking your farm frequently helps you spot hidden signs like tiny powdery spots or early root rot before the disease spreads widely and causes heavy losses.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ powder bibii loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ mra. dani hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni ekɛ nibii babaoo ni elaaje lɛ aba.

english: What basic steps can I take today to protect my cocoa farm from getting sick?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee ŋmɛnɛ koni mabu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela he?

english: Keep the base of your trees clean, remove climbing vines, ensure proper drainage, and regularly walk your farm to catch signs of disease early.
ga: Ha tso lɛ shishi he atse. Jiemɔ wain tsei lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni onyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni ona hela he okadii mra.

english: How does working with Ministry of Agriculture extension officers help my farm stay safe?
ga: Te mikɛ Ministry of Agriculture extension nitsulɔi lɛ baatsu nii aha tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe?

english: Extension officers provide early warnings about disease outbreaks, teach modern farming practices, and guide you on the right treatments to protect your yield.
ga: Amralofoi woɔ helai ni baa lɛ he kɔkɔbɔɔ mra he hewalɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi tsɔɔmɔ kɛ tsamɔ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛbuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he ŋaawoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the ground, away from the roots, so adding compost or fertilizer helps restore the green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni haa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to save energy to keep itself alive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes and powder-like dirt inside the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji tamɔ powda yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which crawl into the soft center of the young maize plant to feed. Checking the crop early allows you to remove them or apply suitable treatments before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tso lɛ loo okɛ tsofa ni sa woɔ mli dani efiteɔ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni eekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and allowing the leaves to capture light to feed the growing tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi helai anaa, ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná la ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very leafy tall stems but small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso ni baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or remains too wet, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in its roots. A balanced soil helps direct growth underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots; their roots stay close to the topsoil. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the shallow roots struggle to hold the heavy plant in strong winds.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli ni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ tso ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that stored food stays in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are left growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni ashiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Because weeds are tough and fast-growing, they steal these resources away from your crops, slowing down crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ wa ni amɛdaraa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and look wrinkled during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to reduce the leaf surface exposed to hot sun, helping the plant conserve water. However, if the leaves also turn yellow, it can be a sign of a virus spread by tiny flying insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ hu. Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees actually need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: When cocoa trees lack proper nutrients, their leaves often turn yellowish, growth slows down, and they produce very few pods. Fertilizer adds essential plant food back into the soil to help the tree produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni ekɛ pods fioo ko pɛ baa Fertilizer kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it important to spray chemicals on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai afɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying helps protect cocoa trees from destructive insects like capsids and fungal diseases like black pod, which can destroy your pods and reduce your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ afite o-pods lɛ ni eha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the stem or base of my cocoa tree to look damaged and weak?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tso loo shishitoo lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Damage at the base of a cocoa tree usually happens due to poor soil conditions, water remaining stagnant around the stem, fungal infections, or accidental wounds caused by cutlasses during weeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ ni kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi fiteɔ lɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle tso lɛ he. Fungal hela. loo pilamɔi ni jɛɔ osharai ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni afoɔ beni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mli baa lɛ mli

english: How does the condition of the soil affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil holds the water and nutrients your trees need to survive. If the soil is too dry, lacks nutrients, or holds too much standing water, the roots cannot breathe or feed properly, causing the plant to suffer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ toɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa tsei yeɔ amanehulu

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees suddenly dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho trukaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often dry up and die due to disease attacks on their roots, severe heat and drought, bad soil conditions, or damage to the main stem that stops water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shishifãi ahe hela hewɔ. latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni efiteɔ ni haaa nu ashɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist during the rainy season, because water helps dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can easily absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya.

english: Can using too much chemical spray harm my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, applying too much chemical spray can burn plant leaves, damage young flowers, waste money, and harm the natural soil balance, so always use the correct recommended mixture.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai. Fɔfɔi bibii lɛ fiteɔ, amɛfiteɔ shika ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does standing water around my cocoa trees cause them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni ekã shi yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: When water stays around the tree base for too long, it cuts off air to the roots. This soggy soil environment creates ideal conditions for root rot fungi to attack the bottom of the tree.
ga: Kɛ nu hi tso lɛ shishi he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua tso lɛ shishi.

english: How can I protect the bottom of my tree stem from getting diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tso lɛ shishigbɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Clear weeds carefully around the tree base without cutting the trunk, create small drains to prevent standing water, and keep rotting pods away from the main stem.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afɔ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ akafolɔ mli. Feemɔ paipi bibioo ko ni haa nu hoɔ. Bɔni afee ni nu akabote mli Ni okɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akabɔ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he.

english: If a cocoa tree dies on my farm, can I plant a new seedling in the exact same spot right away?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ gbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to check why the tree died first. If it died from a soil disease or root rot, the fungal infection in that soil might attack and kill the new young seedling as well.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji hela ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ gbe lɛ Fungal helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ atutua ni egbe dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do crops grow differently in Northern Ghana compared to Southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ akɛto Ghana kooyigbɛ he lɛ?

english: Southern Ghana has two rainy seasons and humid forest conditions suitable for tree crops like cocoa and plantains, while Northern Ghana has a single rainy season with hotter, drier weather best suited for grains like sorghum and legumes like cowpeas.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ kɛ kooi ni mli efɔ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ plantains. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Ghana Kooyigbɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome ni mli edɔɔ ni edɔ waa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa.

english: Why do crops like sorghum and millet handle hot, dry conditions much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum and millet have deep root systems and special leaf structures that roll up to conserve moisture, allowing them to survive long dry spells that would cause maize to wilt and fail.
ga: Sorghum kɛ millets yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ agbi ni egbee shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient that helps plants stay green and grow leaves, often washed out of the soil by heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaai lɛ daa. ni bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leaves above ground but very small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants get too much shade, the cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of storing energy underground to form thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ebaa lɛ akwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ zugba sisi konɛ a kɛ pee yihi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits when the heat increases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: High temperatures dry out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination. The plant drops the unpollinated flowers to save energy and water.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting root crops like yam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii adumɔ?

english: Yams require deep, loose, and well-drained soil so the tubers can easily push down into the earth without rotting from water trapped around the roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni nu ni ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ egbooo.

english: Why should I rotate my field between groundnuts and cereal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mi-acreage lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ateŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturalizing fertilizer for the next maize crop while preventing soil diseases from building up.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with hardy seeds that lie waiting in the soil, ready to sprout rapidly and absorb the first flush of water and soil nutrients before cultivated seeds can establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni mɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds right after the major rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting early allows young seeds to take advantage of warm soil and steady moisture, helping them establish deep roots before sudden dry spells or heavy soil-washing downpours occur.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ daa lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani trukaa nugbɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do groundnut pods rot underground when there is heavy rainfall close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Excess water in wet soil suffocates the underground pods by cutting off air, creating ideal conditions for soil fungi to grow and rot the nuts before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adara ni amɛfite dani akpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight and hot winds. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to protect them, direct sun burns their young leaves and dries out the moisture in the plant.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ kɛha hebuu lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ agbi.

english: What is causing small, neat holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? fɛfɛo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: This is usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm or stem borers. They crawl into the central leaves of young maize plants to feed, which leaves small holes or ragged edges as the leaves expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms loo stem borers kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. ni haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni etsilɛ baa kɛji baai lɛ mli lɛɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but tiny stems and roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing lush leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots into big tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ faaa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ lɛɛɔ kɛ yaa siɔ nɛ a peeɔ zugba agbohi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow corn plants turning bright yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the stalk usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant takes nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy at mid-day even when there is moisture in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water, but usually recovers when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei baagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Will planting cowpea alongside my maize crop hurt my yield or help it?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed the maize while also cover-cropping the field to stop weeds.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hu koni jwɛi lɛ akpa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit. It often happens when water supply is irregular—like a dry spell followed by heavy rainfall.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ be ni sa mli, tamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops during their first four weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni mikɛwoɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ he miihia.

english: During the first month, young crops have weak roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Early weeding ensures your crops get all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, soil moisture, and fertilizer, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small or missing corn ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Dense tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo ni bɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear small trees and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii lɛ? Ni ato tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight. When leaves are lifted off the ground, they stay free of soil diseases, capture light easily, and feed energy down to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaafee nɔ ni hela bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooomɔ kane ni ehaa hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and strength, so when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have a special superpower: they take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil, reducing your need for expensive commercial fertilizers while giving you two crops from one piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi. Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How does adding dried leaves and animal droppings into my farm plot help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Te baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Decayed plant matter and animal dung act like a slow-release natural food and sponge for your soil. It improves the soil's structure, allows roots to breathe, holds onto rain water longer during dry spells, and feeds crops natural nutrients.
ga: Tsei kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo kɛ sponji kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ Ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa tsei

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition leaves all the plants thin, weak, and produce small ears of maize, whereas proper spacing yields fewer but much healthier and heavier crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi bibii. Yɛ be mli ni sɛɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo lɛ, eyɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni eyɛ tsiimɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds around my pepper plants while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than young crops, so they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your peppers. Clearing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the available resources to grow big and produce good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-peppers lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-pepper tso lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ená koni eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to build tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the open air and sunshine, which prevents leaves from rotting and helps the plant produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai ni hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my new farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii gboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under the strong tropical sun. Leaving or planting shade trees provides a cool environment, preserves soil moisture, and protects delicate cocoa seedlings until they are old and tough enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ oshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded or waterlogged for too long without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and drown, allowing soil fungi to rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite dani akpa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without turning into tomatoes during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to drop their flowers as a survival trick to save energy. When the air is too hot and dry, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can form a fruit.
