ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani aduawai baa.

english: Why are small worms chewing holes inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are pest caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, that target the softest part of the young maize plant. Catching them early with proper biological or recommended spray treatments protects the main growing tip so the crop can recover.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaabu ŋmeii titrii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I dissolve my crop fertilizer in water instead of just scattering dry granules on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli moŋ fe ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat solid food; their roots can only drink nutrients dissolved in liquid. When you mix fertilizer in water, the crops absorb the food immediately, which prevents waste and helps the plants grow faster.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni wa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu nu mli Tso lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa nibii afite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone does not contain all the food a crop needs to grow strong. Pale leaves usually mean the soil is missing essential nutrients, so you need to supply dissolved plant food alongside water to feed the roots.
ga: Nu pɛ bɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tso niyenii ni mli tse aha kɛfata nu he koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much or too little fertilizer in their water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiha nu lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: Every crop needs specific nutrient amounts depending on its age and type. Too little food causes slow growth, while too much can burn root tips; measuring your fertilizer carefully according to your water volume prevents these issues.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko. Edamɔ tso lɛ afii kɛ henɔ nɔ. Niyenii fioo tsɔ haa edaa blɛoo. yɛ be mli ni babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ asusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu lɛ falɛ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagbai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do plants grow better when water and plant nutrients are given together rather than separately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ha amɛ ekome moŋ fe ni akɛaaha amɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Mixing water and nutrients delivers plant food directly to the root zone at the exact time the roots are drinking. This guarantees every plant gets an equal share of nourishment with minimal effort.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ kɛ tso niyenii yaa shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be ni sa mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii lɛ mli gbɛfaŋnɔ ni sa nɔ. kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko pɛ fata he.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables at night or during the day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu gbɛkɛ loo shwane?

english: Watering in the cool evening or night is better because water does not evaporate quickly in the hot sun. This allows the soil to stay moist longer so plants can drink comfortably all night.
ga: Nu ni oooha gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu lɛ shwieee oya tamɔ bɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ anu nu yɛ hejɔlɛ mli gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Will giving my crops liquid fertilizer at night cause the sun to burn their leaves the next day?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha hulu la ashã baai lɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ?

english: No, applying liquid food at night actually protects the leaves. The plants soak up the food in the cool dark, ensuring no wet leaves are exposed to strong daytime heat that could scorch them.
ga: Dabi, niyenii ni ji nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei gbalaa niyenii yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ ewo. Enɛ ji koni baai ni efɔ lɛ akashɛ la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ aha amɛshã.

english: Will watering my crops late at night make the roots rot in the ground?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa tsei gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: As long as your land has good drainage and you do not flood the field, nighttime watering will not cause rot. It helps reduce heat stress and lets the plant save its energy for growing.
ga: Shii abɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu shwieee ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ haŋ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛdara.

english: How can using a water tank to feed my crops save me labor on the farm?
ga: Te nu ŋtayaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: By dissolving fertilizer directly into a central water tank, you feed and water your whole crop at the same time through your hose or drip lines, saving you from carrying heavy fertilizer buckets across the farm.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Obaatsɔ hose loo drip hose nɔ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ niyenii ni oha amɛ nu yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haaa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I dissolve any type of store-bought fertilizer into a water tank?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ awo nu baagi mli?

english: No, you must use water-soluble fertilizers that dissolve completely. Regular fertilizers may leave heavy dirt or rocks at the bottom of your water tank and block your watering pipes.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ nu mli ni shwieɔ shi kwraa lɛ atsu nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashi muji loo tɛi ni tsii yɛ nu ŋtayaa lɛ shishi ni etsĩ nu paipii lɛ anaa.

english: How does feeding my crops through a water tank save me money on fertilizer costs?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiye niyenii kɛtsɔ nu ŋtayaa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni mikɛ shika akafite yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Mixing plant food into a water tank delivers exact amounts directly to the crop roots. This stops rainwater from washing away dry powder scattered on top of the soil, ensuring you waste less fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso niyenii lɛ futu nu tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ falɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does the shape or slope of my farmland matter when choosing what crops to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɔɔ loo eshishijee lɛ he hiaa beni mihalaa tsei ni mikɛbaadu lɛ?

english: The shape of your land affects how rainwater moves across it. Flat or gently sloping land holds soil and nutrients in place, while steep hills cause heavy rains to wash away topsoil, so different crops need different types of ground to grow well.
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa nugbɔ nu lɛ nyiɛmɔ he. He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo he ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ kɛ niyenii mli nibii hiɔ shi. Beni gɔji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Bɔni afee ni eda jogbaŋŋ

english: Can I plant coconut trees on a steep hill on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better not to plant coconut trees on steep hills. Coconuts do best on flat land or gentle slopes because heavy rain on steep hills can wash away the topsoil around their roots and lead to severe soil erosion.
ga: Ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Kokooi hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. shishifãi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: What is a gentle slope, and why is it good for planting certain crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ blɛoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha tsei komɛi akwɛmɔ?

english: A gentle slope is land that leans slightly rather than rising sharply like a steep hill. It is good for planting because water flows over it slowly enough to feed crop roots without carrying away the rich topsoil.
ga: He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo ji he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo moŋ fe ni eeewo ŋwɛi oya tamɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ ejaakɛ nu hoɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ tsei shishifãi ni ejieee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the land on my farm is too steep for coconut trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kwɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmei tsei?

english: If rainwater rushes quickly down the hill and leaves deep tracks or washes away loose dirt easily, the slope is too steep for coconut trees. You should look for flatter ground or a very mild incline instead.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu ho oya kɛjɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ ni eshi gbɛ ni mli kwɔ loo efɔ muji ni jɛɔ mli oya lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmei tso lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e sa nɛ o hla hehi nɛ a ngɛ tsɔ aloo he nɛ a ngɛ tsɔ bɔɔ ko ɔ.

english: What is soil erosion, and how does it hurt my crops on sloped land?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi? Ni te eeye miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil erosion happens when heavy rainwater washes away the dark, rich topsoil that contains food for your crops. On sloped land, fast-moving water leaves behind poor soil, making your crops weak and reducing your harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛ Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ shĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii yɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How does heavy rain destroy crops planted on steep hills?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on a steep hill, water flows down fast like a river, sweeping away fertilizer, soft soil, and even young roots. This deprives crops of the water and nutrients they need to stay upright and produce good yields.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ oya tamɔ faa, ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, kɛ shishifãi bibii po shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Does planting on a gentle slope help prevent soil erosion?
ga: Ani dumɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa?

english: Yes, a gentle slope slows down rainwater as it moves across the land. Slower water gives the soil time to absorb moisture safely without stripping away the valuable topsoil and nutrients your crops rely on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ shweshweeshwe ni ejieee sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii ni otsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli.

english: What kind of terrain is best for planting coconut trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Coconut trees grow best on flat land or gently sloping ground with good drainage. This type of terrain protects the trees from soil erosion while making sure their roots get steady moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ he mfonirifeemɔ nɛɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Does the slope of my ground affect how much fruit or yield my crops will give me?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ehaa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii loo yibiiwoo babaoo he?

english: Yes, because crops on gentle slopes or flat land keep their soil nutrients and water better than crops on steep slopes. When crops keep their topsoil and nutrients, they grow stronger and give you higher yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ tsei hiɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Ebaada waa ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I decide which part of my farm is safe for crops sensitive to soil erosion?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe?

english: Observe how water moves on your farm after a heavy rain. Put soil-sensitive crops on the flat areas or gentle slopes where water moves slowly, and avoid steep areas where water strips away the dirt.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Okɛ tsei ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ he lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni nu shwieɔ muji kɛyaa lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my main crops produce better when I plant beans between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ titri lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside crops like maize, they enrich the soil naturally with food that helps the neighboring plants grow bigger.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa masɛi Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná niyenii ni baaye abua tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a protective canopy that cools the seedlings and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my heavy plantain stems fall over during strong wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. Building soil mounds around the base of the stem and supporting the fruit stalk with a sturdy wooden fork keeps the plant standing during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Muji ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ tso ni akɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ asɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots decay when water gets trapped around them in soggy soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei kɛ tsei ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on tall stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight to grow big tubers beneath the soil. It also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ anaa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small worms inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ bu ni etse amɛhe lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and powdery waste in young maize plants are clear signs of Fall Armyworm attack. Early detection allows you to apply proper biological or targeted chemical treatments before the caterpillars destroy the central shoot.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm tutua mɔ. Nibii ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these sap-sucking insects early keeps the leaves flat and growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or using too much chemical fertilizer can stress tomato plants and cause them to drop flowers. Consistent watering at the roots and balanced feeding ensures the flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tomato he.

english: Why is it harmful to spray crop chemicals in the middle of a hot, sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Spraying under a hot afternoon sun causes liquid chemicals to evaporate too quickly before taking effect, and hot sunshine combined with chemicals can burn plant leaves. Early morning or late afternoon is best for spraying.
ga: Tsofai ni mli tse lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii. Ni hulu la ni mli edɔ ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ashã. Leebi loo shwane mli Ehi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ

english: I see bees flying around my tomato flowers; are they destroying my farm or helping it?
ga: Mina ŋmeii ni miiho kɛmiibɔle amɛhe. mi tomato fɔfɔi Ani amɛmiifite miŋmɔ lɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua lɛ?

english: Bees are actually helping your farm through pollination. They carry pollen from flower to flower, which causes the plant to set fruit and produce big, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Wuobii miiye amɛmiibua oŋmɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni ewoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I let my chickens walk around inside my farm, or will they ruin my crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ maha kooloi lɛ abɔle amɛhe. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo amɛbaafite minibii lɛ?

english: Chickens can help your farm if managed well. They eat harmful insects and weeds, and their droppings fertilize the soil, though you should keep them away from young seedlings so they do not scratch them up.
ga: Kooloi baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ okwɛ amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi. ni amɛsũi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ okɛ amɛ akabɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkafo amɛhe moŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants producing flowers, but no corn cobs are growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi ŋmãa ŋmãa ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Maize needs enough water and good soil nutrients right when it starts flowering to form cobs. If the soil is too dry or lacks food during this time, the flowers will not turn into cobs.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ebɔi fɔmɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmãa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeŋ ŋmeii.

english: My cassava leaves are turning yellow instead of staying deep green; what is happening to my crops?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your cassava plants are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or they are getting too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-yucca tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans between their maize rows, and should I do it too?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafee nakai hu?

english: Planting beans with maize is called intercropping. Beans feed the soil with nitrogen from the air, which helps the maize grow bigger while keeping weeds down.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ akɛ intercropping. Beans kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ejieɔ jwɛi hu kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why should I spend money to buy new seeds when I can just use seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui heei lɛ? Akɛni manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii hewɔ lɛ.

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops often yield smaller and weaker plants the next season. Buying fresh certified seeds gives you stronger plants that fight off diseases and produce more food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ haa onáa tsei ni he wa ni baanyɛ awuu ashi helai ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look soft during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during intense heat to conserve water and protect themselves. If they open up again in the evening, they are healthy, but if they stay curled, they need water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ agbele ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehi kɛha ohewalɛ. Shi kɛji okɛ ohe wo mli lɛ, nu he miihia bo.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant yam on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yam in the same spot every year removes all the specific nutrients yam needs and lets soil pests build up, causing your yield to reduce each season.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni oha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa onibii ni ofeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my plants instead of packing them close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ abɔ he koni mawo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plants need space to get sunlight, air, water, and soil food. When crowded, plants fight each other, stay small, and fall sick easily.
ga: Tsei taoɔ he ko ni amɛna hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe baawuu, amɛbaafee bibii ni hela baamɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do people cover the ground around vegetable plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like an umbrella that keeps water in the soil from drying up in the sun and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like a tube during intense heat to conserve moisture and reduce water loss. Once the temperature cools down or rain falls, the leaves will unfold naturally.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa paipii amli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛbu hulutsoo be lɛ he ni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baajie amɛhe kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their lower leaves during dry periods to save water and energy for the tubers underground. As long as the top leaves remain green and healthy, the plant is safe.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Shii abɔ ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why are there white powdery spots spread across the leaves of my okra plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi okra baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those white spots are a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly when humidity is high and airflow between closely planted crops is poor.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ nɛɛ ji ŋmeii hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create the shade and moisture cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each plant enough space to grow, makes weeding and applying fertilizer easier, and helps you get a better yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda. Ehaa jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo. ni eye ebua bo ni oná nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent even when the leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand properly. If the soil is too hard or rocky, the tubers cannot push through easily, resulting in small or misshapen yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo tɛi Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ yitso lɛ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow big leaves instead of flowers and pods. Less nitrogen fertilizer allows the plant to focus on producing beans.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can check groundnut maturity by pulling up a test plant and opening a few pods. If the inner shell lining has dark spots and the seeds are firm and fill the shell, they are ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni o-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ha kɛtsɔ tso ko ni okɛkaa ohe lɛ ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmɔtɔi fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni dumɔwui lɛ ewo ŋmei lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow when I cannot afford to buy chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shika bɛ ni akɛbaahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. When chemical fertilizer is too expensive, you can pile decomposed organic leaves, poultry manure, or compost around the base of the trees to feed the soil naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ, kooloi afɔfɔi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ato he. Tso shishitoo ni akɛhaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Can I leave dried leaves and clearings under my cocoa trees instead of buying weedicides?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi baai ni egboi lɛ ni majie amɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi?

english: Yes, leaving dry leaves and clearings under your trees creates a natural carpet called mulch. It prevents weeds from growing, keeps the soil cool and moist, and slowly breaks down into free plant food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli kapɛti ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, egbɛɔ etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: When is the best time during the year for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time is early in the rainy season when the soil is wet. Moisture helps the plant roots absorb the nutrients quickly before the sun burns them off or heavy rains wash them away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani hulu lɛ shãa amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose water fast under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby keeps the soil moist and protects them from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava on the same piece of land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava too close to young cocoa. Cassava roots spread fast and steal water and nutrients from the soil, while its broad leaves block out too much light from the young cocoa plants.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ tsɔ. Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ la babaoo ni jɛɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before making any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack. Providing adequate shade, keeping the soil moist, and managing pests help the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ He hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛhaa Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cutting away weak, extra, or shaded branches helps the tree direct its energy and food into growing big, healthy pods instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ Shade loo shade ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why does my cocoa harvest keep reducing every year even though the trees are getting bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ daraa moŋ?

english: As trees grow older, they exhaust the nutrients in the soil if food is not added back. Also, trees that grow too bushy block air and sunlight, which reduces how many pods the tree can produce.
ga: Beni tso lɛ da lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ awooo niyenii lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How can I tell if the hybrid cocoa seedlings I am buying will actually give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Good quality hybrid seedlings usually come from certified government nurseries or trusted extension officers. They should have thick stems, dark green leaves, and healthy root systems free from insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ jɛɔ maŋ nɔyeli ŋmɔji loo mɛi ni heɔ amɛyeɔ ni haa amɛyaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ amɛná tsei ni mli tse. baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni kooloi bɛ mli

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees shade and keeping the soil moist while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or compost helps restore this nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass on the ground around my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni mabɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It acts as a blanket that protects the soil from the hot sun, keeps water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, cocoa trees drop their leaves on purpose to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out completely until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cassava tubers so small even though the leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much water or rich fertilizer early on, the plant puts all its energy into growing thick top leaves instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nu babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mra. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet, which shocks the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. ni haa tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning brown near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: When yam plants mature, the top vine naturally dies back because the plant has finished growing leaves and has transferred all its food energy down into the subterranean tuber.
ga: Beni sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Wein tso lɛ yiteŋ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni sweet potato tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ ebaai lɛ amli ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ eshɛ shi kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater gather and stay on top of my land instead of sinking into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy clay or hard-packed soil prevents water from soaking down into the earth quickly. Creating raised mounds or drainage channels helps direct water away so plant roots do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni wa baatsi nu naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛ ni aaafee lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteee.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are being eaten by insects or damaged by a sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi eye mitso lɛ baai loo hela efite?

english: Bites, ragged edges, or visible holes mean insects are physically chewing the leaves, while yellow circles, spots, or white powder usually mean a fungal or bacterial sickness.
ga: Bits, ŋmeii ni ekumɔ, loo bu ni anaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miiye baai lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo powda yɛŋ tsɔɔ ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ahela.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the dirt. Rotating with groundnuts or beans restores soil strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much moisture in the extreme heat. By curling, less leaf surface is exposed to direct sunlight, helping the crop save water until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from fertilizing and forming fruit. When pollination fails, the plant naturally sheds the useless flowers to save its energy for cooler days.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛwo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ amɛshwieɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide broad leaf shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Buu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, ensuring the leaves get maximum sunlight and preventing them from touching wet soil where diseases can spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha baa lɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni otsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water, soil nutrients, and light from the main plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main tree produces a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ Dumɔwu kome pɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ la ni jɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná plantains babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stunted even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots that drink water and steal soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. They also grow aggressively to block sunlight, effectively starving your crops of energy and light.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Amɛdaraa oya hu koni amɛná amɛhe shade kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ kɛ la ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and passing viruses to the plant. The plant responds to this feeding damage and infection by curling its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, ni miinu baa lɛ mli nu ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ miiha tso lɛ. Tsei tsuɔ nibii ni efite kɛ helai ahe nii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cassava roots become tough and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant's food supply. As the cassava plant gets older or prepares to grow new stems after rain, it converts its soft starch into tough fiber, making the root woody and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ akɛ tso niyenii. Beni ŋmei tso lɛ eda loo eesaa ehe koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei, ni ewa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. Planting maize afterwards allows the maize to feed on this natural fertilizer left behind in the dirt.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly in standing water while my maize crop rots and dies in flooded soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that pipe oxygen down from the air to their roots underwater. Maize roots lack these air tubes, so standing water drowns the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why does my soil break down into soft powder during the dry season but turn hard like a stone after it rains and dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ? yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Shi ebafeɔ nɔ ni wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil high in clay loses its structure when exposed to intense heat, turning powdery. When rain hits this exposed soil, the fine particles wash together, and intense sunlight bakes them into a hard crust that prevents seedling emergence and root growth.
ga: Shikpɔji ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, afɔɔ Fine particles lɛ ekome. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmei ni wa ni tsiɔ dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why has the NPK fertilizer I stored in my shed broken down into powder and clumped into hard stones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fãa ni etsɔɔ powda ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni efeɔ tɛi ni wa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer grains absorb moisture from humid air if bags are opened or stored on bare ground. As moisture enters and leaves, the fertilizer breaks down into powder on the surface and fuses into hard blocks below.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli kɛji agbele kotoku lɛ mli loo akɛto shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli ni ejeɔ kpo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fãa ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ekɛ ehe feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning dusty with a white powder that makes the plant stiff and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ sũ ni tamɔ powder yɛŋ ni haa amɛwaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. The fungus covers the leaf surface in a white powder, blocking sunlight and preventing the leaves from producing food for the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Fuŋ lɛ haa baa lɛ hiɛ tamɔ powda yɛŋ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa baai lɛ afee niyenii kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn stiff and hard as stone when I delay harvesting them past their maturity date?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ tɛ beni mikɛ kpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ sɛɛ kɛyashiɔ be ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ eho lɛ?

english: When cassava stays too long in the ground, the plant converts soft starches into tough, woody fibers. Over time, these fibers harden, making the tubers tough and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei hi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ tsɔji nɛɛ baafee mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: What happens when I spread fine white lime powder across my acidic field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ lemon powda yɛŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ shwie mihe ni acid yɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Agricultural lime powder reacts with soil moisture to lower soil acidity. As it breaks down in the soil, it releases essential minerals that allow crop roots to absorb nutrients more effectively.
ga: Okwaayeli mli lime kɛ sũ mli nu lɛ feɔ ekome koni ekɛba sũ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ minerals ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my harvested yams dry out, shrink, and become stiff like wood after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ gĩ, egbɔjɔ ni efee nɔ ni wa tamɔ tso yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvested yams are living tissues that continuously lose water through respiration. If stored in hot, unventilated conditions, they lose moisture rapidly, causing the inner flesh to shrivel and harden.
ga: Akpaa sweet potatoes akɛ fãji ni hiɛ ka ni nu fiteɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔɔ mumɔ ni amɛmuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Ebaafite ŋmɔtɔ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbi ni ebaawa.

english: How do I know when my heap of farm waste has fully broken down into proper compost?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ato lɛ efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni sa?

english: Compost is fully decomposed when the original crop waste and manure break down completely into a dark, powdery material that crumbles easily in your hands and smells like clean earth.
ga: Kompost lɛ fiteɔ kwraa kɛ́ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fite ni etsɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni tamɔ powda ni fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni he tse.

english: Why is the soil around termite mounds on my farm as hard as rock compared to the rest of the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle termite gɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ kɛ akɛto hei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Termites cement soil particles together using their saliva and droppings to build sturdy structures. When exposed to the sun, this organic glue bakes into a dense, stone-like material that resists water and hand tools.
ga: Termites kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fĩɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee nɔ ko ni wa. Kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ nɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ glu ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ mli waa ni etsɔɔ nɔ ko ni mli wa ni tamɔ tɛ. ni nu kɛ nitsumɔ dadei nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he

english: Why do my maize grains turn hard and stony as the crop dries on the stalk late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ tɛi beni ŋmãa lɛ gĩɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: As maize reaches maturity, the plant cuts off water supply to the ear. The starch inside the kernels loses all moisture, compacting tightly into a hard, protective grain suitable for long-term storage.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baafo nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ toi lɛ mli lɛ. Starch ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ emli nu fɛɛ. ni afee lɛ dumɔwui ni wa ni buɔ mɔ he Ehi kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ

english: Why does the surface of my farm soil get stiff and crack into pieces during prolonged dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely dry soils lack organic matter to hold soil particles loosely together. Without organic moisture, soil clay shrinks and tightens, causing deep surface cracks and a hard, stiff top layer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ ahi shi mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa, ni wa baa.

english: Why do my mango trees stop producing fruit after I finish harvesting, and how do I get them to yield again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei ekpaa yibiiwoo beni akpa amɛ lɛ? Ni afi ni baa lɛ, te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ewo yibii ekoŋŋ?

english: Mango trees need time to rebuild energy after a heavy harvest. Applying compost or fertilizer and pruning dead branches right after harvest helps the tree prepare for the next flowering season so it can continuously yield fruit every year.
ga: Be he miihia mango tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni wa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ni afo tsei niji ni egboi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni esaa ehe kɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni enyɛ eya nɔ ewo yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What care should I give to my tree crops right after harvest to keep them healthy through the dry season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: After harvesting, trees need nourishment and water conservation. Clearing weeds around the trunk, adding compost, and applying a thick layer of mulch helps retain soil moisture and restores nutrients the tree lost while producing fruit.
ga: ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii ni tso lɛ laajeɔ beni ewoɔ yibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Does adding animal manure to my farm work immediately, or does it take time to help my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo ebaahe be ni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Organic manure works like a long-lasting treatment for soil. Unlike chemical fertilizers that give a quick, short-term boost, manure breaks down slowly to feed the soil and crops over several seasons, preventing nutrient loss.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsamɔi ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa oya, ni ehiɔ shi be kukuoo lɛ he. Manure baafite fiofio. Koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ bei babaoo mli Koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akafite

english: Why does treating my farm soil with lime help my crops grow better over multiple years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛ lime tsuɔ nii lɛ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Lime reduces soil acidity, which unlocks trapped nutrients so plant roots can absorb them easily. One proper application improves the soil environment for years, making it a lasting fix rather than a quick, temporary solution.
ga: Lime haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acidity lɛ baa shi. Enɛ gbeleɔ niyenii mli nibii ni emɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ aya hiɛ afii babaoo. Ha efee tsakemɔ ni hiɔ shi daa moŋ fe nɔ ni baatsu he nii oya, ni baatsu he nii yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I use crop leftovers like spoiled fruits and peels so they do not go to waste on my farm?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ aduawai ni efite kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii. Te mafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: Crop waste can be collected in a pit to make rich organic compost or processed into animal feed. Turning farm waste back into soil nutrients ensures that nothing goes to waste and keeps your soil fertile for the next planting.
ga: Abaanyɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi anaa awo bu mli koni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji loo afee lɛ kooloi aniyenii. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ ekoŋŋ ofee shikpɔŋ mli niyenii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my fresh fruits from rotting when I cannot sell them all immediately at the market?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi yibii heei lɛ akafite? Akɛni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Fruits can be preserved through simple processing methods like drying or making jams and juices. Processing extends their shelf life, allowing you to store or sell them later instead of losing your produce to spoilage.
ga: Abaanyɛ akwɛ aduawai anɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ amɛgbimɔ loo jam kɛ nu feemɔ nɔ. Nitsumɔ haa shɛlɛf wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛtoɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ sɛɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baafite kɛya fitemɔ mli lɛ

english: Why does my fruit tree produce a heavy harvest one year and very little the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a massive crop uses up almost all the tree's stored food reserves, leaving it exhausted for the next cycle. Balanced feeding and fruit thinning help smooth out yield from year to year.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. Ha eya yɛ kpokpaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa kɛ aduawai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do I correctly save seeds from my current crop so I can plant them again next rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ato jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni anyɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Select seeds from healthy, high-yielding plants, dry them thoroughly in the shade, and store them in airtight containers with a little wood ash. Proper drying and storage keep the seed vigor intact until planting time.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Haŋ koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni tso sũ fioo ko awo mli lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi dumɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Should I keep using traditional farming methods learned from my family, or should I change completely to modern techniques?
ga: Esa akɛ maya nɔ mikɛ blema okwaayeli gbɛi ni mikase kɛjɛ miweku lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Aloo esa akɛ wɔtsake kɛya ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaa gbɛi anɔ kwraa?

english: The best approach is combining both. Traditional practices like mulching and crop rotation maintain long-term soil health, while modern techniques like proper planting distance and improved seed varieties boost your total yield.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ enyɔ lɛ afee ekome. Kusum nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spraying pesticide once not solve my farm's insect problem for the entire season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ekome pɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ahe naagba lɛ he nii yɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pesticide sprays usually only kill insects present at the moment of application and do not affect unhatched eggs or pests coming from neighboring fields. Long-term protection requires regular field monitoring and clean farm maintenance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. ni enaaa ŋmeii ni efɔko loo ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Be kakadaŋŋ mli hebuu biɔ ni akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions when farm foliage is too bushy. Clearing weeds and pruning excess leaves allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, stopping the spread of the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli beni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. These caterpillars hide inside the central part of the plant during the day and eat the leaves, which weakens the plant's ability to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds inside the very same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to fight each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting only one or two seeds per hole allows each plant to grow thick stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná tso lɛ shishifã ni mli tse kɛ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to turn watery and rot in the ground when the rainy season is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhiɛɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains drown the soil for too long without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and bacteria cause them to decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ boteɔ nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ ni nu tsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my land make the soil better for my next crop of cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it inside the soil. When the bean plants decay, they leave this free fertilizer behind for crops planted after them.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmei tso lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛdu tsei yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight balls during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's way of protecting itself from losing water in severe heat, or it can be a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids. Watering the plant and managing pests keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ he okadi. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get steady water. Stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning pale yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or heavy rains have washed the topsoil nutrients deeper down out of the reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ nɛ waa ni efo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds stop growing fast once my sweet potato vines cover the whole ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines form a thick blanket across the earth that blocks sunlight from reaching the ground. Without sunlight, weed seeds beneath the leaves cannot sprout or grow.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei feɔ tsɔne ni mli tse ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to make food and grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli.

english: Can applying animal manure to my soil improve my yield as much as store-bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure builds long-term soil health by feeding beneficial soil life and helping the ground hold water, which gives your crops steady support year after year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii maa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ekɛhaa kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off before they produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or gets too much or too little water, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo enine shɛ nu babaoo loo fioo nɔ. Okɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni okɛbu ohe he

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up, so the plant temporarily wilts to save water until the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa tree growing tall and leafy but not producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee baai lɛ? Shi pods ko kwraa bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: When cocoa gets too much shade or too much leaf-growing fertilizer, it puts all its energy into making leaves instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ná hulutsoo be babaoo loo akɛ tsofa wo baai lɛ amli babaoo lɛ, Cocoa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Will my cassava produce bigger roots if I plant them closer together?
ga: Ani mi-cassava lɛ baakwɛ shishifãi wuji kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting cassava too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating in the hot sun, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season; rotating with beans or groundnuts helps restore the land's power.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii shwie shi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough space on the land?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crop, acting like thieves that starve your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Feemɔ onii tamɔ julɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ koni okpa nikpamɔ nii lɛ.

english: Is it effective to use traditional plant mixtures like neem leaf water to protect my vegetables from pests?
ga: Ani etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ blema tsei amli nibii tamɔ neem baa mli nu baatsu nii koni mikɛbu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, traditional neem extracts contain natural bitter compounds that stop insects from feeding on your crops while remaining safe for the soil and your family.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni yɔɔ neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ blema lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni oyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ oweku lɛ.

english: Is it true that using organic manure will not damage my crops even if I apply a lot of it?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli po lɛ, efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, organic manures like compost or dried poultry manure break down slowly in the soil. Unlike synthetic chemical fertilizers, organic options release nutrients gradually, so they will not burn your crops' roots even if applied in slightly higher amounts.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ fiofio yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Esoro ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio. No hewɔ lɛ, eshãŋ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ nɔ ni fa fe nakai fioo po wo mli.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow slower with compost compared to when I use chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ? Kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Compost feeds the soil first, requiring soil organisms to break down the organic material before plants can absorb the nutrients. Chemical fertilizers provide immediate nutrients directly to the plant, which shows faster short-term growth but doesn't build long-term soil health.
ga: Kompost haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Ebiɔ ni nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbala nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ be kukuoo mli shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat and sunlight. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water and prevent drying out during intense heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ekɛtsiɔ egbimɔ naa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in a cleared open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from direct sun and keep the soil cool during their first two years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause waterlogging in soils with poor drainage. Excess water deprives the cassava roots of oxygen, causing them to suffocate and rot due to fungal infections.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egboɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruit during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with low water availability cause severe stress to pepper plants. To preserve their own survival, the plants abort their flowers instead of using energy to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi Tso lɛ baashi efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip of older leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, and when missing, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from older leaves to newer top leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Ni kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my green tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Bacteria or fungi invade the water-transporting tubes inside the stem, blocking water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Muawai loo ŋmeii boteɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Can chemical weedkillers hurt my crops if the wind blows the mist onto their leaves?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa afua kɛyaa ebaai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, non-selective chemical herbicides will damage or kill crop leaves if spray drift touches them. You should spray on calm mornings when there is no wind and use a protective spray hood.
