ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa mɔ lɛ baafite loo ebaafite tsei ahe baai kɛji akɛ aerosol lɛ kɛ amɛ kpe. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔse yɛ leebi ni efee dioo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. ni okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow much faster than my planted seeds after I fertilize the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that allow them to absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crop seeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the full benefit of the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yes, combining cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the field later, giving you two harvests from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei futu mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Ehaa okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why should I buy improved seeds instead of just using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases and produce higher yields compared to seeds saved from older harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ blema ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without bearing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛlɛɔ shi amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them weak. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni edaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting soaked in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree lacks water, receives too much direct sunlight, or is attacked by insects like mirids. Pruning heavy shade branches and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. nine shɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Shade ni afoɔ ni tsii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my crops after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady for about two to three weeks so the soil retains enough moisture to help your seeds sprout and grow without drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be otsii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Should I place fertilizer right next to the plant stem or further away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ he loo mikɛwo tso lɛ he shɔŋŋ?

english: Place fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in a small ring or hole. Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant, while placing it near the roots allows it to feed safely.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko loo bu ko mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Shi kɛ́ okɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha efee shweshweeshwe aha tso lɛ ni eye nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, holds water in the soil during hot days, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: What is causing small worms to eat holes inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by fall armyworms, which hide inside the leaves of young corn. Spraying recommended treatments or neem leaf extract early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji cutworms ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellow and light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties from agricultural officers protects your farm from this problem.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots, preventing the plant from staying green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɛɛɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots under the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I leave enough space between my yam mounds instead of placing them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ aaato he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Yam tubers need room under the soil to grow big, and spacing mounds properly ensures that plants do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛdara. Ni ŋtayaai ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them onto the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Transplanting in hot afternoon sun shocks delicate young roots; moving seedlings late in the afternoon or on overcast days gives roots time to settle in cool soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe feɔ shoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are fall armyworms and caterpillars worse on my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworm kɛ fall armyworm lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce faster in warm weather, and plants stressed by dry conditions are weaker, making it easier for pests to attack their leaves.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Ni tsei ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa amɛhaoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua amɛbaai lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into a cup shape during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward to protect themselves from intense sunlight and reduce the amount of water escaping from the plant during the hottest hours.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest tree canopy above them is too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa plants need shade to survive, full-grown cocoa trees need direct sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and develop healthy pods.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi. Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops right after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are built to survive dry periods in the soil and can absorb water instantly when rain comes, giving them a head start over cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Abɔɔ jwɛi dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ Enɛ haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava roots are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off and the remaining leaves turn pale, typically between 9 and 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or develop mold when I put it into bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain still holds a lot of internal moisture; if you do not dry the grains thoroughly in the sun first, trapped moisture encourages mold growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ ogbiii dumɔwui lɛ kwraa dani okɛ amɛ wo hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped moisture woɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in fertilizer. When the soil lacks nutrients, the plant pulls food from its older leaves to feed new growth, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii heei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if I run out of fertilizer halfway through the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ fã mli?

english: Crops that start with fertilizer and suddenly lose it will slow down in growth and yield less harvest, because their nutrient supply drops sharply right when they need energy to produce seeds or fruits.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishi ni no sɛɛ lɛ efiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni tso ko yɔɔ lɛ baa shi oya kɛ́ hewalɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: Will my crops suffer if I switch to a different brand of fertilizer because my usual one is out of stock?
ga: Ani ebaana miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ kɛji mitsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ efo?

english: Switching brands will not harm your crops as long as the new fertilizer contains the same key nutrients (like Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium) that your crops need at their current stage of growth.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ahe tsakemɔ lɛ yeŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Shii abɔ ni niyenii mli nibii titrii (tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium) ni he hiaa otsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rain or after the ground is damp?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a light rain. Applying it right before a heavy downpour can wash the nutrients away before your crop roots have time to drink them in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, poor soil nutrients, or improper watering, which stops the flowers from pollinating and forming fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he haomɔ he. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni esaaa Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Cassava planted too close together or given too much nitrogen puts all its energy into competing for sunlight and growing leaves above ground, leaving little energy to build big, heavy roots.
ga: Yucca ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo hulu la kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe akaŋshii mli. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than my crops after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive roots that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear weeds before fertilizing, the weeds will eat the food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. By curling, the leaf reduces its exposure to the sun and saves water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do crops like millet and sorghum grow better in northern Ghana compared to humid southern areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ? kɛ akɛto hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ anaigbɛ lɛ ahe

english: Millet and sorghum are naturally tough crops designed to survive hot temperatures and dry weather. Northern soils and weather suit their natural growing habits better than wet forest zones.
ga: Millet kɛ sorghum ji tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha adebɔɔ mli dalɛ fe hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure to my soil help my crops stay green during short droughts?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ mli?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It traps moisture from rainfall and slowly releases water and food to plant roots over time, helping crops survive when rain stops for a while.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ nu mli lɛ mli ni ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai fiofio koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ be ni sa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be ko.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight. Planting broad-leaf crops like plantains or leaving shade trees nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects the cocoa from harsh sun and keeps soil moisture from drying up.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui adumɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ shade ni ashiɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni ekagbi

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, prevents soil-borne diseases, and helps the plant produce large, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa eniyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Why do groundnut flowers push stems downwards into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique growth behavior where the flowers pollinate above ground, but the actual nuts (pods) must grow underground. The plant grows special stems called 'pegs' that push down into the soil so the nuts can safely mature away from heat and light.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ su krɛdɛɛ ko ni haa amɛdaraa. He ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii (pods) lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni ashɛɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ la bɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it up to support the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua ŋwɛi dalɛ hee.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can suck it up. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts around the roots, which can scorch or burn the crop instead of feeding it.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã loo eshã amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to put all its energy into growing thick green foliage. When leaf growth dominates, the plant forgets to store food underground, leaving you with small tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji baai lɛ dara lɛ Tsei lɛ ahiɛ kpaa nɔ akɛ amɛkɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ohiɛɔ oyitso bibioo.

english: Why are small coconuts dropping off my tree before they get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokooi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early coconut drop is commonly caused by severe water stress during dry periods, a lack of potassium in the soil, or tiny insect pests sucking sap from the stem where the young coconut attaches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa. potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot or when humidity is extremely high or low, which stops pollen from moving properly. Without proper pollination or consistent watering, the plant sheds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo eba shi. Enɛ haaa pollen lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi.

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding underneath, or a virus spread by these insects. They drain nutrients from young leaves, causing them to distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo amɛshishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main plant. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only the strongest stem, which will yield a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ, juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha plantains babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green, healthy leaves and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crop with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground moist during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and prevents the sun from baking the roots.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni etsĩ hulu la naa koni ekashã shishifãi lɛ

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not like direct intense heat; bright sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out their roots, causing them to drop their leaves to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra small shoots from around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fe nine kɛjɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain, they steal water and nutrients from the soil, leaving the main plant with a very small bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ yɛ aduawai bibii bibii.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their roots fight for space and soil nutrients, resulting in long thin stems and small, poor tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunshine; full light on the leaves feeds the underground tuber so it can grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. La ni jɛɔ baai ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young corn shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn shoots lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to feed on the tender, growing center of maize plants and can ruin the yield if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ atsui. ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani mifee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water, as the plant tries to save its energy to stay alive during harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ diji yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering while the peppers or tomatoes are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni ŋmeii loo tomatoi lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting so fast just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug out of the ground, it reacts quickly to oxygen in the air through a natural process called post-harvest deterioration. Because it no longer receives water and nutrients from the living plant, the root flesh turns brown or black and begins to spoil within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ post-harvest aging lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnáaa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɛɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli dɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shishifã lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: What happens to my tomato crop if I leave the ripe fruits on the vine for too long before picking them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving ripe tomatoes on the vine causes them to become overripe, soft, and split open. These cracks attract pests like fruit flies and birds, and allow fungal rot to set in, which can quickly spread and destroy the remaining crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fe nine, efee blɛoo, ni egbɛ eshwa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ okpoi. ni eha ŋmei lɛ afite ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop a green or black powder when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The colored powder is mold caused by excess moisture. If maize grains are not dried thoroughly until they are hard before storage, trapped dampness allows fungi to grow, which spoils the grain and creates toxic substances that make it unsafe to eat.
ga: Pigment ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa ni ewaaa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Trapped moisture baaha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni ehaa tsofai fɔji ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. When the plant does not find enough food in the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni tsei lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to survive heat or drought.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there is bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade plants like plantain to protect them, the hot sun evaporates water from their leaves much faster than their small root systems can absorb it from the ground.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni buɔ ehe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie emli babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily even when the wind is not strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes or insect larvae called stem borers destroy their shallow root systems. Without healthy roots anchoring the corm to the soil, the plant cannot support the heavy weight of its fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa ni hiɛɔ rhizome lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by fungal infections or tiny soil worms that enter through small wounds on the tuber skin. It also happens when soil becomes waterlogged, cutting off oxygen to the tubers and causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afo yɛ tuber lɛ hewolo lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ebaa hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ faaa. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii lɛ ni shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and developing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is transmitted by small insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from making food properly, which stunts the plant's growth and drastically reduces the size of the roots underground.
ga: Cassava Mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ayibɔ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my garden vegetables wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil feels moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Vegetables wilt temporarily to close their leaf pores and reduce water loss until the air cools down in the late afternoon.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aduawai shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛgbala baai lɛ amli buji ni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong, green leaf growth. It can also happen when too much standing water in the field prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow tall and thin with tiny roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight and space. The plant puts all its energy into growing upward to reach the light instead of storing food in underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ he ko he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara bɔni afee ni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why does my cocoa tree shed many of its small young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiho amɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Babaoo dani ebatsɔ agbo?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees drop young pods when they do not have enough water or soil nutrients to support all of them, sacrificing some pods so the remaining ones can mature.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shi kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii komɛi ashã afɔle koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or from a virus spread by whiteflies that damages new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ shweremɔ heei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieee shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away pollen before insects can pollinate the flower. Excess water also stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani kooloi bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ. Nu babaoo hu haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Gbalamɔ fɔfɔii koni okɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cabbage seedlings wither immediately after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock. Moving plants damages their fine roots, and sudden exposure to strong sunshine dries them out before the roots can recover and drink soil water.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso ko ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ, ni kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ trukaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛnu sũ lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop dies, that trapped food stays in the soil and acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know that my yam under the ground is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yam is mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished sending energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda kwraa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why are my young crops bending toward one side of the farm instead of growing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants bend toward the strongest source of sunlight so their leaves can capture energy to make food. If big trees block sun on one side, crops lean toward the open sky.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hei ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛji tso agbo ko tsi hulu la lɛ naa yɛ fa kome lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the soil, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the center of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build food. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure will help the maize turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants producing huge green vines but tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: When sweet potatoes get too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of food under the ground. Reducing nitrogen and using fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant focus on building bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I harvested my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava takes away a lot of nutrients from the earth. Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the ground, restoring soil strength for your next crop.
ga: Cassava heɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that thrives in dark, wet weather. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and clearing surrounding weeds helps keep the pods dry so the disease cannot take root.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ duŋ, ni efɔ shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ bɔni afee ni helai akatswa shishifãi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight little cups and stopping plant growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiikpa tsei lɛ adalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or spreading a leaf-curl virus. Protecting plants early with neem oil or targeted sprays prevents these insects from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes the white powdery dust on my watermelon leaves during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sũ yɛŋ baa mi-watermelon baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called Powdery Mildew. It spreads easily in warm, humid air. Spacing your plants further apart improves air flow and keeps the leaves dry enough to prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ to amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ha baai lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the plant cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does covering my vegetable soil with dry grass help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a shield against the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and slowly turns into compost to feed your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fiofio ni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why must I remove weeds while my young crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are not strong enough to fight for food. Weeds grow much faster and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your young plants need to grow, stunting their growth early on.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛha niyenii. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ebaaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. ni okɛ dalɛ aba shi mra

english: Why does my locally grown rice cook differently than the packaged rice bought at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties have varying levels of starch and moisture content, which affects how much water they absorb and whether they turn out soft, sticky, or firm when cooked.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi lɛ yɛ starch kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ saa nu ni ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ he. Ni ani ŋmãa lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ, ebaakpɛtɛ, loo ebaafee shiŋŋ kɛ́ ahoo?

english: How can I tell if a new rice seed variety will grow well on my farm before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu amɛ?

english: You can check whether the seed is certified for your specific land type—such as lowlands that flood or dry uplands—and verify its maturity period with your local extension agent.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ atsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛha shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ nɔ, tamɔ nu afua loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Ni obi omaŋ nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛha be ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I replant saved seeds from last year instead of buying fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni midu dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their genetic purity and vigor over time, making them weaker against pests and disease, while fresh certified seeds are bred for high yields and uniformity.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛ fɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do my rice plants need to sit in standing water while my other crops like maize would rot in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ata nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, fiteɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems and roots that allow them to breathe underwater, while water helps drown out competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he ko krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. yɛ be mli ni nu yeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow even though I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii.

english: Why do my rice stalks fall over flat on the ground right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, and it happens when plants grow too tall due to excess fertilizer, weak stem development, or heavy winds bearing down on heavy grain heads.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ mli waaa. Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa waa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops in the first few weeks after land preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to quickly steal available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not fall off on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Ani ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛŋ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn golden yellow, but the main stem still holds a bit of green moisture to prevent shattering.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Shi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko koni ekɛtsi gbeekpamɔ naa.

english: Why does my rice grain break into small pieces during milling instead of staying whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ani ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baahi shi moŋ?

english: Grains break during milling if the harvested crop was dried too quickly under harsh sun or if it was milled when it was either too dry or not dry enough.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Aloo kɛji akɛ afee lɛ mfoniri beni egbi tsɔ loo egbiko bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: How does storing my harvested grains in proper heavy-duty bags protect my crop after harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni sa ni tsii mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Good quality, airtight bags seal out moisture and oxygen, preventing mold from growing and keeping storage insects like weevils from eating your harvest.
ga: Vacuum kotokui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food for crops, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients beyond the roots' reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil, but alternating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my crops if I leave them in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal the sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer that your crops need, leaving your crops starved, stunted, and producing smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni otsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, dark conditions, especially when trees are overcrowded and air cannot flow freely around the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle amɛhe. Sheath heyeli

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the plant sap and spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in saturated soil because water fills all the air spaces around the roots, suffocating them and encouraging harmful ground fungi to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or sudden dry spells as a survival effort to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, and lifting the leaves off the damp ground protects the plant from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Ni baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crops from my land?
ga: Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ, Ani mahaŋ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for water, nutrients, and light, producing weak plants with very small fruits or grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, niyenii, kɛ la he, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have heavy stems and shallow roots; when heavy rains make the soil soft, the roots lose their grip and strong winds can push the top-heavy plants down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsei ni tsii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsi tsei ni tsii kɛba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—their leaves are very tender and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains provides a living umbrella that shields the cocoa seedlings and keeps the soil moist until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Ebaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants have to fight each other for the limited sunlight, water, and nutrients in that spot. Because they are all competing, every plant stays thin and weak instead of growing strong to bear full, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Esa akɛ Tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe shiɔ akaŋ. Tsei lɛ fɛɛ batsɔ shwilafoi ni amɛhe waaa. Mohu ɔ, e waa wawɛɛ nɛ e woɔ yiblii nɛ tsii nɛ e yi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up even when I water them at noon on hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ shwane mli yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Watering during the hottest part of the day causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it. In addition, hot sun can warm up standing water on the soil surface, which damages the tender roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ babaoo atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni ekã shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu adɔ. Enɛ baafite shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants rot at the stem near the ground after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the farm without draining, it starves the plant roots of air and allows soil fungi to breed. Raising your planting beds above ground level helps extra rainwater drain away so the stem and roots stay healthy.
ga: Be mli ni nu yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu homɔ bɛ mli. Nu haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Kɛ́ awó dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally feeds the soil with free fertilizer, which helps the neighboring maize grow taller and greener.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even though the leaves above ground look very big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ baai moŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much leafy fertilizer or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of pushing roots into the ground. Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil so the roots can swell into fat tubers.
ga: Beni akɛ baai babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsi shishifãi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ, Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Heat prevents the flower from forming seeds inside, so the plant drops the flower to save its strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo dumɔwui yɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing leaves, but refusing to produce flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Plants delay flowering when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much water without enough sunlight. The plant gets comfortable growing foliage instead of feeling the need to reproduce and make fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ baaha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛji amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nu babaoo ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tso lɛ baaná baai ni baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a nuɔ he kaa e he hia nɛ a fɔ nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cabbage plants curl up and feel sticky during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are signs of tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves to suck plant juices. They leave behind a sweet, sticky waste that attracts black soot and stops the leaves from catching sunlight.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛhe ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tsei lɛ amli nu. Amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. No gbalaa sũ diŋ ni haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less than the certified seeds I buy from the agricultural officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over multiple seasons lose their natural vigor and can carry hidden diseases from last year's farm. Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist diseases and produce high yields consistently.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ bei babaoo lɛ fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out so fast during the hot sun, and how can I keep it wet for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha efee ŋmɔtɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight causes water in bare soil to evaporate quickly. Spreading a cover layer like dry grass or leaves over the ground shades the soil, keeping it cool and trapping water inside so your crops stay hydrated.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu mli koni onibii lɛ aná nu.

english: Why do my young crops wilt so fast when the top layer of soil gets dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso bibioo lɛ gboɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa lɛ?

english: When the topsoil bakes under the sun, it loses all its water and hardens, making it difficult for roots to drink. Keeping the ground surface covered protects the topsoil from drying out and keeps it soft for root growth.
ga: Beni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shãa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ. Ebaafite nu lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaawa. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaanu shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: How does covering the soil surface help my farm survive through hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the ground acts like a protective blanket. It blocks the direct heat of the sun from reaching the earth, which slows down water loss and keeps moisture in the root zone much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: How can I prevent weeds from growing back quickly right after I clear my farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When land is cleared, buried weed seeds get sunlight and sprout fast. Spreading a layer of organic material like straw or dry leaves over the cleared earth blocks sunlight, which stops weeds from coming up quickly.
ga: Kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ naa hulu la ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why is it helpful to loosen the topsoil when preparing my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ aaaŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni asaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Loosening the topsoil allows water to soak deeper into the ground quickly and makes it easier for young plant roots to spread out and establish themselves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ, nu lɛ boteɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. ni ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni etswaa shi mlɛo

english: Does spreading dry grass or leaves on my field really reduce the time I spend weeding?
ga: Ani jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛshwãa mishia lɛ mli lɛ haa be ni heɔ kɛhaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, putting a layer of dead plant material over the bare earth smothers weed seeds before they can sprout, keeping your field cleaner and saving you time on weeding.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni egbe jwɛi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Ha oyale lɛ mli atse ni okɛ be akafite jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: What is the main purpose of spreading dry plant material all over my crop field?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri ni yɔɔ tsei ni egbi ni migbɛɔ mishwaa he fɛɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Spreading dry plant material over the soil protects the land from sun heat, stops moisture from escaping, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops for water and food.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he.

english: Should I cover the soil inside my nursery plant bags, or leave the soil bare?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ grow bag awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: You should place a light layer of cover over the soil in your plant bags because soil in containers dries out very quickly in the sun, and ground cover keeps the water locked inside the bag.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo. kɛya dumɔ kotoku lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsɛnsii amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa kɛ́ hulu la shɛ nɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi kotoku lɛ mli.

english: What local materials can I easily collect to cover my soil and protect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii manyɛ mabua naa mlɛo koni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mikɛbu he?

english: You can gather cheap, natural materials found right around your farm, such as dry grass, fallen leaves, or crop residues, and spread them over the soil around your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jara waaa ni anaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ anaa, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai ni egbee shi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ni okɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave the soil completely bare without any cover under the sun?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ mihe?

english: Bare soil loses its moisture very fast to the hot sun, hardens up, and allows weeds to take over, which stresses your crops and stops them from growing strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ewaa ni ehaa jwɛi yeɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛdara waa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow strong. Adding composted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping them from producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa lɛ gbɛ koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or soapy water helps clear the insects so the foliage can expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots for too long, it chokes them and encourages fungal disease, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves high to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to feed its underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsei yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Watering regularly around the roots during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Kɛ́ afɔ nu awo shishifãi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ tomato.

english: Why is my cocoa tree dropping its small green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? dani eda

english: Cocoa trees shed young pods (a process called cherelle wilt) when they don't have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them. Pruning overgrown shade trees slightly and feeding the soil helps the tree retain its pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ. (gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt) beni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye niyenii Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ fioo ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay so small when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and leaves to spread out and grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara ni amɛfee tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why does fall armyworm attack my maize mostly when the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ babaoo be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths prefer laying eggs on young, soft maize leaves because the tender central whorl is easy for the caterpillars to eat. Checking young leaves early allows you to catch and manage the caterpillars before they ruin the plant.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeli waaa. Baai bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold or turn away from direct sunlight during intense afternoon heat to prevent water from evaporating out of the plant. It is a natural defense mechanism to help the crop survive hot, dry conditions.
ga: Akɛ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them creates living umbrellas that shade the cocoa and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why didn't my planted maize seeds sprout after I pushed them deep down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy before the shoot can break through the soil to reach sunlight, causing the seedling to die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi dani ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food nutrient that plants use to build healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: Why does cassava planted on the same plot every year yield smaller tubers with each harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ woɔ ŋmei bibii yɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls specific nutrients out of the earth every season. Without resting the land or adding compost, the soil gets tired and cannot feed new tubers properly.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua bulbs heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the stems of my maize plants breaking easily and showing small holes with powdery dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa oya ni buji bibii ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny caterpillars called stem borers eat their way inside the maize stalk, weakening the plant from the inside until the stem breaks.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emligbɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifã lɛ fãa.
