english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Very small insects like whiteflies sit on the underside of leaves to suck the plant's juice, spreading leaf-curl viruses and leaving behind a sticky residue.
ga: Kplukai bibii waa, tamɔ whiteflies, taraa baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Egbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa. ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: When the sun is too hot or the soil is too dry, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm right after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy rain follows a long dry spell, the plant drinks up water very fast, causing the inside of the melon to grow quicker than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei nuɔ nu oya waa. Enɛ haa melon lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly in the heat before I even reach the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli dani mishɛɔ jara nɔ po lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and release heat after harvest. Packing them tightly in hot, closed boxes squeezes them and speeds up decay.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kpo beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ adeka ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha efite ni eha efite oya.

english: Why do my stored yams start rotting or sprouting leaves inside the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo baai miifee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living roots that naturally break dormancy and sprout when exposed to warm temperatures and light, while cuts from harvesting allow rot fungi to enter.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ la he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes line cleaning and weeding much easier, gives each plant equal space to get sunlight and nutrients, and helps you estimate how many crops you actually have on your land.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ linei ni ja mli lɛ haa linei lɛ amli saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enine ashɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ. Ni ehaa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ oyɔɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akɔntaabuu ni ja.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds between my crop rows every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe lɛ ateŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops, and they also hide pests and diseases. Regular line cleaning keeps your crops strong and makes walking through your farm safe and easy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai hu teeɔ. Line mli saamɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them acts like a sunshade, keeping the air cool and moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and balanced feeding help the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow leaves, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa baai lɛ daraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná su ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close to other leafy crops, it puts all its energy into growing tall branches instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni kɛlɛ fe nine ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the Harmattan dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai babaoo fite beni Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's way of surviving drought. By dropping leaves, the tree loses less water to the hot dry winds, helping it stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite nu fioo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Cutting unnecessary branches, or pruning, lets fresh air and light pass through the canopy, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and directs energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds under the trees and removing infected pods quickly keeps the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi oya kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade because direct sunlight overheats their tender leaves and dries out their surface roots before they can establish strong root systems.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛbaai bibii lɛ adɔ fe nine. ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high above the ground into direct sunlight, allowing the leaves to make maximum food energy which is stored underground to form large tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agboi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which forces the maize to pull nutrients out of its older leaves to support new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ koni ejie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni dalɛ yɔɔ ŋmãa heei anɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in root nodules, which enriches the soil with free nutrients for hungry crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he ehiaaa kɛhaa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to be wet before applying granular fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji granular fertilizer abɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water so roots can absorb it; placing dry fertilizer in dry soil can scorch the crop roots and waste the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap and spreading viruses that deform new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ hee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do small green worms start chewing big holes in my cabbage leaves as the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛyeɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: These green worms are diamondback moth caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves, feeding aggressively on soft tender greenery to fuel their growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ diamondback ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli niyenii kɛ miishɛɛ koni amɛha amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent soil moisture, saving their energy instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi moŋ fe yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rains when carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ́ miiwo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems close to the surface, making them easily top-heavy and vulnerable to uprooting under heavy wind and wet soil without physical stakes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaná ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsii, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa bo ni akɛ tsei tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot beneath the ground during long rainy spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up air spaces in heavy soils, starving cassava roots of oxygen and encouraging soil fungi that cause tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ekanyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the tall shade trees growing in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ tsei kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming shade trees lets in just enough sunlight for your cocoa trees to produce flowers and pods, while also preventing too much moisture from getting trapped and causing fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa haa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ shwereɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I let my cocoa trees grow too tall like natural forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ daa tsɔ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli koo mli tso lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees grow too high, it becomes very difficult for you to harvest the pods, prune bad branches, or spray for pests, which lowers your yield over time.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da tsɔ Obaakpa ŋmeii lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ Enɛ baaha nibii ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat. They need temporary shade trees or plantains nearby to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛsɔmɔ akɛ hulutsoo be ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade or too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miihe hulutsoo be babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo?

english: If your farm is too dark and damp, you will see a lot of moss and rotting pods; if it is too sunny, the cocoa leaves will turn yellow and dry up. A healthy farm gets broken, filtered sunlight on the soil.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Obaana ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ babaoo. Kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa lɛ, kookoo baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baafite. ni hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli

english: When I am cutting heavy tree branches above my farm, how do I prevent them from breaking my cocoa trees?
ga: Be ko lɛ, mifolɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ?

english: You should cut branches in small, manageable pieces and guide them carefully into open gaps so they do not crash directly onto delicate cocoa flowers and young pods.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli bibii bibii. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ ni akɛwo he ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli blɛoo Enɛ ji koni akagbee kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to cocoa pods if falling branches scratch or hit them?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tso nɔ kɛji akɛ atswa tso nine ni egbee shi lɛ loo atswa lɛ?

english: Wounds created on cocoa pods by falling branches create open doors for diseases like black pod rot to enter and destroy the beans inside.
ga: Pilamɔi ni tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ kɛbaa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does clearing away dead branches from my farm help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni egboi ni mikɛbaakpa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Removing dead wood clears out hiding places for harmful pests, allows better air flow through the farm, and helps the crop focus its strength on growing healthy pods.
ga: Tsoi ni egboi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I see so many ants crawling on my cocoa trees, and are they harming my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Ants are often attracted to sap-sucking insects like mealybugs on your tree. Some ants protect these harmful insects and spread diseases between trees, so managing them helps protect your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Tsɛi komɛi buɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ahe, ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa tsei ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhe ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it dangerous to let shade tree branches touch the tops of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aaata mi-cacao tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: When shade tree branches touch your cocoa trees, pests like ants and mirids can easily crawl straight down onto your crop and damage young pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shade niji kɛ kookoo tso lɛ kpe lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ atsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya. ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop easily when the tree is stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or damage from sap-sucking insects. Proper shade and pest management help flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ fitemɔ mli. Shade ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ pods ni eyi obɔ.

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow from the tip inward in a V-shape, it is usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen nutrient, or the plant roots are struggling to absorb nutrients due to compacted soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee mli kɛtee mli yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, tsei shishifãi miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛha hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I do not leave plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mishiko cacao tsei komɛi yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and broad leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the air temperature gets too hot or when there is extreme dry weather followed by sudden heavy watering, which stresses the plant's reproductive system.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi waa ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni saa tsei afɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he lɛ

english: Curled or twisted leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn black and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain saturated soil stays flooded for too long, water displaces the soil air, causing the roots to drown, rot, and turn soft.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nugbɔ eyi shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers underground when their leaves can climb high to capture maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and maximizing food production for the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa niyenii ni anáa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller cobs when I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete heavily for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving each individual plant with less energy to develop full cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers drop down and push themselves into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique plants that form their pods underground. After the flower on top is pollinated, the stem lengthens downward into a 'peg' that pushes into the soil, where the peanut pod safely develops.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei ni yɔɔ srɔto ni feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ‘peg’ ni ashɛɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers act like competing mouths, stealing water and soil nutrients from the main plant. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures the main plant produces a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu, ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛ tso ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Niji bibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has left to the newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, especially nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the dirt, refreshing your soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store food in their underground tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves into the air so they get maximum sunlight and airflow, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ niyenii toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he babaoo. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the main stem of my plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajieɔ plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and feed on nutrients that your main plantain stem needs to bear fruit. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa plantain tso titri lɛ koni ewo yibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ baaná plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I just scatter my seeds randomly on the farm instead of measuring space between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijaa dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo susu blɔ nɛ ngɛ jamɛ a duwu ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ he.

english: When seeds are scattered too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin and weak plants. Proper line spacing gives each plant its own space to grow strong and makes weeding much easier.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Line ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa jwɛi anɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso lɛ? Ani ooogbɔjɔ ni ooofee tamɔ mɔ ko ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying early with organic solutions like neem leaf extract helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Organic tsabaai tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in the center leaves of my young corn and brownish dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Muji ko ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa baa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing point of the maize plant to eat tender leaves. Catching them early and applying localized treatments prevents them from destroying the growing stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water in the soil starves the root tubers of air and creates perfect conditions for harmful fungi to grow. When roots sit in soggy soil past their harvest time, fungal rot easily sets in and destroys the crop.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ baa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he lɛ, Rot fungus baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off the plant without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, lack of consistent soil moisture, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot weeks helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi etswa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism for cocoa trees during dry weather to stop water from escaping through leaf pores. Plantain trees or shade trees planted around cocoa help block hot dry winds and keep humidity high so cocoa trees retain their leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni cacao tso lɛ anyɛ ahi ebaa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I pour granular fertilizer right against the main stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer woɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem concentrates harsh chemical salts right where the plant is tenderest, which burns and destroys the roots. Placing it a few centimeters away allows the plant's feeder roots to drink the nutrients safely as they dissolve in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsofa mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ hei ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛfite. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe beni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means they naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the groundnut roots decay, that stored nitrogen enriches the soil, giving nearby maize free food to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Nitrogen ni abua naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii. Enɛ haa niyenii ni ŋmãa bɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ baa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural defense mechanism to save water. Because leaves lose water through evapotranspiration, shedding them helps the cassava root stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ latsaa mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ejɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce big tubers underground only when their leaves get maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground on tall stakes keeps them healthy, catches sunlight, and prevents fungal diseases from spoiling the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji pɛ kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe, ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year even though the stems look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally produce many young suckers around the main stem. If you don't prune away extra suckers, all those stems end up fighting for the same food and water in the soil, leaving too little energy for the main stem to build a big bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tso titri lɛ he kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baawuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there tiny holes and dark powder inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni powda ni tsuɔ waa lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing central funnel of the maize plant. The dark powder you see is the insect's waste, indicating that the pest is actively eating the growing leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Pauda ni tsuɔ diŋ ni onaa lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ miiye baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my fresh cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji heei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, humid conditions. When rain falls continuously and farm shade is too thick, moisture stays on the pods and lets fungal spores grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli ewo wu tsɔ. Fɛ̃i hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and stopping flower growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiikpa fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves and transferring viruses. The sucking damages leaf tissue, causing the leaves to twist and preventing the plant from setting peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Suction fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa chili tsei lɛ ama shi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get scorched easily by direct tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce large broad leaves that provide temporary living shade, protecting fragile cocoa plants while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ebuɔ cacao tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly, making it impossible for the plant's roots to transport calcium into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ calcium aya tomato ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green foliage. Rain often washes nitrogen out of sandy soil, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will help the plants grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Nugbɔ lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ ŋã sũ mli lɛ he nitsumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do cowpeas and groundnuts help improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baafee tɛŋŋ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes have small swellings on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi ni efuu fioo ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen to stay healthy. In waterlogged soils, water fills all the tiny air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing rot to set in. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi he miihia oxygen koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the field right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons split open when heavy rainfall or heavy watering follows a dry spell. The fruit rapidly absorbs excess water, causing the inside to grow faster than the rind can stretch, which bursts the skin.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Yibii lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya. Enɛ haa loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. ni haa hewolo lɛ fãa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the delicate cocoa seedlings while keeping the soil cooler and moister during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines produce large tubers only when their leaves get full sunlight to manufacture food. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows all leaves to catch light while keeping them safe from ground heat and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs agboi kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa naa la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or drought. When temperatures rise too high, the plant saves energy by shedding flowers until moisture levels improve and weather cools down.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing around the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain shishitoo lɛ ekomɛi.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow together, they steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant, resulting in small bunches. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers for big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi kɛha ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into small knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of new leaves. Neem oil or insecticidal soap sprays clear these pests so healthy, flat leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ baagbe kooloi nɛɛ koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my young rice grow so poorly when weeds are left on the farm during the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa bibioo lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young rice plants grow slowly and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives the rice plants space to tiller and produce maximum grain stalks.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛtsu nii ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my maize plants suddenly turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or are getting too much water around their roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them protects the cocoa from heat while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he be mli ni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after growing for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni mikɛdu lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-tilled soil to expand. If the ground is too hard or lacks nutrients like potassium, the roots stay thin instead of growing thick and bulky.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or dry soil. Water them regularly during hot spells and add organic manure to help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ mli. Nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ chili peppers.

english: How do I know if the tiny worms on my maize leaves are going to destroy my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If small caterpillars are eating holes in the leaves and inside the central shoots of your maize, it is likely Fall Armyworm. You should apply neem seed extract or approved bio-pesticides early before they destroy the crop.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye bu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, Etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baagbee shi. Esa akɛ okɛ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. dani ekpãtãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why does my harvested dried maize turn into white powder while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow inside stored maize and eat it from the inside out. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is hard and using safe storage dust keeps these pests away.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ sũ ni ato he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii koni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Is it bad to burn the bush on my farmland before I plant my crops?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, burning destroys organic matter and beneficial insects that nourish the soil. Clearing land without burning allows dead leaves and grasses to rot into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni oshãaa lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ jwɛi ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between stands helps every plant grow strong and bear big cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 75, ni ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 40, ni no haa tsei fɛɛ daa waa ni amɛnáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I grow tomatoes on my farm during the peak rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Excessive rain often causes tomato leaves to develop fungal spots and the fruits to rot on the plant. Tomatoes grow better in the minor rainy season or on raised beds with proper drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii baa tomato baai anɔ, ni aduawai hu fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Tomato daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli loo yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that steal food, water, and sunlight from your crops very quickly. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks after planting gives your crops the best chance to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad if I water my tomato plants in the middle of the day when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering during the hottest part of the day causes the water to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and hot leaves mixed with water droplets can cause heat stress. It is best to water early in the morning or late evening so the soil retains moisture.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni akɛ nu mli nu shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo he haomɔ aba. Esa akɛ afee nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to my pepper crop if I skip watering for a few days during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo amɛ nu gbii fioo komɛi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Skipping water disrupts the plant's growth routine, causing it to drop its flowers and produce small, dry peppers. Crops need steady, regular watering to continuously develop healthy fruit.
ga: Nu ni afoɔ lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ dalɛ gbɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni chili bibii ni egbi lɛ feɔ. Tsei biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa kɛ daa koni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ daa.

english: Is it okay if I delay applying fertilizer to my maize by two weeks because I am busy?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo mli otsii enyɔ ejaakɛ mibɛ deka?

english: Maize needs nutrients at precise growth stages to build strong stems and big cobs. Missing or delaying your fertilizer application means the plant loses out during its most critical feeding window, which permanently reduces your harvest.
ga: Niyenii he miihia ŋmãa yɛ dalɛ be pɔtɛɛ mli koni efee tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ yɛ amɛ niyenii yeli be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi kwraa.

english: If I put double the recommended fertilizer on my vegetables, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo mli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ, ani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once can burn the plant's roots and yellow the leaves. Plants need exact amounts at set intervals, and overfeeding can ruin the entire crop.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Tsei biɔ yibɔ ko yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Ni niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ.

english: If I mix more chemical medicine into my spray tank than specified, will it kill bugs faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo futu spray tanki lɛ mli fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ, Ani ebaajie ŋmeii oya?

english: Adding extra chemical will not solve the problem faster and can actually burn your plant leaves and poison the soil. Chemical treatments require strict measurement to protect both the crop and your money.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛbaafata he lɛ tsuuu naagba lɛ he nii oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni ekɛ tsofa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa helai lɛ biɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni akɛbuɔ onibii kɛ oshika fɛɛ he.

english: Why should I spray my cocoa trees for black pod disease before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afɔse kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa koni ejie black pod hela lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Black pod fungus spreads rapidly in wet weather. Applying protective medicine on a strict schedule before the rain starts creates a shield, preventing the fungus from ruining the pods before it takes hold.
ga: Black pod fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa ni ayeɔ yɛ be ni ato jogbaŋŋ mli dani nugbɔ anɔ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafite ŋmeii lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Does it matter what time of day I spray liquid treatment on my cabbage leaves?
ga: Ani ehe hiaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ kaabe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, spraying in the cool early morning allows leaves to safely absorb the treatment. Spraying in direct afternoon sun can scorch the foliage, while spraying at night can encourage fungal rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ agbo.

english: Why do my crops look weak even though I gave them a huge amount of water and fertilizer all at once last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miha amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome too mli yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops thrive on consistent, scheduled routine rather than sudden, heavy feedings. Overwhelming plants with a massive dose of water or fertilizer causes root shock, whereas regular, measured care keeps them steady and healthy.
ga: Tsei shwereɔ yɛ nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ni tsii trukaa lɛ Nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akwɛɔ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does leaving tall weeds around my cassava ruin my final harvest?
ga: ŋmɛɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ he Te ŋmei baafite mi naagbee nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds consume the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your cassava. If you miss your scheduled weeding window, the weeds take over and stunt the growth of the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛhaa o-cassava lɛ. Kɛji oshɛɛɛ be ni ato akɛ okɛbaakpa jwɛi lɛ he lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye nɔ ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to plant my maize right after the first major rain instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni ooomɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the main rain ensures seeds get the exact moisture required to germinate at the right time. Delaying planting means the soil dries out, leading to poor germination and weak seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant my cocoa seedlings so they do not dry up and die?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui? Bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ akagbi?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the onset of the major rainy season, usually around April or May in Ghana. Planting during this period gives the young plants enough moisture to build strong roots before the harsh dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ April loo May mli yɛ Ghana. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba.

english: How many years will it take after I plant my cocoa seedlings before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 4 to 5 years before they begin bearing fruit.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and dropping off when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sun and heat. Without temporary shade trees or food crops like plantains to cover them, the heat scorches their leaves and causes them to dry out and fall off.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ, latsaa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day as a survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which minimizes water loss through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my newly planted cocoa seedlings on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ pɛŋ lɛ?

english: It is not advisable to intercrop cassava with young cocoa because cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively competes for soil nutrients and moisture, and its bushy leaves block too much light from reaching young cocoa.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei bibii afee ekome kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ ehe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ la babaoo naa koni ekashɛ kookoo bibioo lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, fertile, dark, and well-drained with plenty of decayed organic matter. You should avoid rocky ground, hard clay, or low-lying swampy areas where water stays flooded.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni nibii ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Esa akɛ okpa shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu lɛ ekã shi.

english: What causes the green cocoa pods on my trees to suddenly turn dark brown or black during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, excessively humid conditions when rainwater remains trapped on the pods for long periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do small insects like mirids attack only the tender young shoots and fresh pods of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi heei pɛ lɛ?

english: Mirids, also known as capsids, feed on young shoots and fresh pods because the plant tissues are soft enough for them to pierce and suck out sap, which damages the stem and causes dieback.
ga: Mirids, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids lɛ yeɔ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii heei ejaakɛ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efo mli ni ekɛ nu lɛ atsu nii. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ ni ekɛ gbele baa.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow into full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛgbi ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree deliberately sheds excess young pods that it cannot support due to nutrient shortages, dry weather, or overcrowded branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Ebaa kɛji tso ko jwɛŋ ejie ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo tsei niji ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and shade leaves from my mature cocoa trees if I want a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛ shade baai kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead wood and useless shoots, allowing sun and air to move freely through the farm. This lowers disease risk and directs the tree's energy into developing bigger pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding balanced fertilizer like NPK or compost will supply the needed nutrients to turn the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo?

english: Yes, planting direction is very important. You must plant the cassava stem with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow, resulting in poor crop yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ he miihia waa. Esa akɛ odu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil moist around the roots and giving the plant adequate nutrients will help flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Roots lɛ he lɛ mli fũu ni okɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young vegetable plants if they are not touching each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi tso bibioo lɛ Kɛji amɛtaaa amɛhe?

english: Even if weeds do not touch your crop, their roots under the ground steal water and nutrients meant for your plants. Weeds also shade your crop from sunshine and hide harmful pests.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaaa gbee po, Shi amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ onibii ahe ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to reduce water loss through their leaves during intense heat. Providing regular watering near the roots early in the morning helps the plants retain moisture and lowers leaf stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough direct sunlight to make food, which helps grow big tubers under the soil. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai srɔtoi anaa.

english: Why should I keep some shade trees on my farm when establishing a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mima kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under full sunshine. Shade trees protect fragile young cocoa plants from intense sun and harsh winds, helping them stay cool and retain soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant plantain suckers that already have wide leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers with wide leaves grow weak stems and produce smaller fruit bunches. It is better to choose suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves because they establish stronger roots and yield larger bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baaná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii bibii. Esa akɛ ahala tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ ejaakɛ no baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii akui wuji.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are generally ready when the leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. You can pull out a sample plant; if the inside of the pods has dark markings and the nuts are firm, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ. Obaanyɛ ojie tso ko he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ pod lɛ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ wa Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by small caterpillars that feed on the leaves during the night. Applying recommended botanical treatments like neem oil or appropriate protective sprays will stop the insects from destroying the heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite bulb lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Ebote mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshi powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central whorl of the maize plant during the day and feed on the tender growing leaves, leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛye baai bibii ni miida lɛ Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and stop producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites. Their feeding damages young leaves and can spread plant viruses that stunt flower growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baai bibii ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and soft before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells that prevent roots from absorbing nutrients from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct intense sunlight and severe heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted beside them to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist during dry spells.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does adding dried chicken manure help my vegetable crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure adds essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to the soil. It also helps sandy soil hold onto water better and makes heavy clay soil softer for roots to grow.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni ewo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require soft, loose soil to expand smoothly. If the soil is hard, shallow, or full of rocks, the growing tuber encounters resistance, causing it to become stunted or distorted.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, Tubers ni miida lɛ baafee nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main tree receives full energy to produce a larger bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to survive long dry seasons in the soil and react instantly to moisture, taking up quick-release nutrients before newly planted seeds fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsuɔ ​​nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Enaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo oya dani dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark and spoil within two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ ediŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are detached from the stem and exposed to oxygen, a rapid natural chemical breakdown begins. Because fresh roots carry high moisture and no thick protective skin, they must be cooked, processed, or sold within 24 to 48 hours.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛboteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai baabɔi fitemɔ oya. Akɛni shishifãi heei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni amɛhewolo lɛ mli tse hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ahoo amɛ, atsu he nii, loo ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want my plantain farm to yield big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji?

english: Plantains grow best in deep, loose, black soil rich in decayed leaves and organic matter that drains water well. Avoid planting on hard clay or rocky ground where water collects and stays stagnant, as this rots the roots.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ he ni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shi lɛ nɔ dumɔ he. Ejaakɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains should be planted about 3 meters apart from each other. Spacing them properly gives the roots enough room to find water and nutrients, and allows enough sunlight to reach all the leaves so the trees produce big, heavy fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantains kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. ni ehaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or cassava together with my plantains on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa kɛ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow crops like maize, vegetables, or beans between plantain trees during the first year. This helps you get early food and money while the plantains are still growing, before their leaves grow big enough to shade the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai, loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná niyenii kɛ shika oya be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ miida lolo lɛ. Dani baai lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do so many small shoots grow around my main plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Midumɔwu titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers. If you leave too many of them, they steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, leading to small fruit. You should cut off the weaker ones and leave only 2 or 3 strong suckers for the next harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji ashi lɛ babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii ni mli wa 2 loo 3 pɛ kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?
