english: Plantains have broad leaves and need a lot of water. In the dry season, the soil loses moisture quickly, so the plant drops its outer leaves to conserve whatever water is left in its main stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu babaoo he miihia amɛ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: When is the best time for me to spend money on clearing weeds and fertilizing my plantain farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafite shika kɛjie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The best time to weed and add fertilizer or manure is at the beginning of the rainy season. Moisture in the soil allows the roots to absorb the fertilizer quickly so the plant grows strong before flowering.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Koni tsei lɛ adara waa dani amɛwo fɔfɔi

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches high off the ground. When the soil becomes soft from rain, strong wind can easily pull them up. Supporting the stem with a sturdy wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: How do I protect my plantain stems from small pests that weaken the trunk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-plantains lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ni haa eshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Stem borers and root pests hide in dry leaves and weeds around the base of the tree. Keeping the base of your plantain stems clear of old vegetation and using healthy, clean plantain suckers when planting keeps pests away.
ga: Stem borers kɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Ni aaaha plantain lɛ shishi lɛ afee nɔ ni tsei momo bɛ mli Ni akɛ plantain ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii beni aduɔ koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How can I tell when a plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to cut when the individual green fruits lose their sharp edges and become plump and rounded, and the dried flowers at the tips drop off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ beni aduawai eŋɔli fɛɛ eŋɔli sɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baagbee shi mlɛo.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains generate heat and release gases that speed up ripening once cut, especially under direct sunlight. Harvest them early in the morning, keep them in the shade, and cut them while they are fully green so they stay firm during transport.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji afo amɛ. titri lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi Kpamɔ leebi Ha ehi he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa. ni afolɔ mli be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli kwraa lolo koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up and turning yellow when the dry season starts early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot, dry periods to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve moisture inside its leaves and stem until rain returns.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ bei amli koni eha baa lɛ nɔ hulu la aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing completely during extremely hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kwraa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures become very high, crops temporarily pause their growth process and close tiny pores on their leaves to prevent water loss, resting until the air cools down.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakpa edalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ be kukuoo ko. ni oŋa bu bibioo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ koni nu akaje mli Kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni ooofee kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli baajɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or soil moisture drops suddenly, causing the plant to drop flowers to protect its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are turning yellow because they are ripe or because they are getting sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: A healthy ripe cocoa pod turns a clean yellow or orange with smooth skin, whereas a diseased pod usually develops dark brown or black patches that feel soft or look powdery.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni he tse ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni haa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of dark green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi peppers fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, the plant spends all its energy developing heavy foliage instead of growing flowers and fruits.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my cassava plants produce giant leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava roots require soft, loose soil to expand; if the ground is too hard or compacted, the plant cannot push its tubers outward and puts energy into leaves instead.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛmli alɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre e-bulbs lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo baai lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hiaa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into full sunlight to make plant food efficiently, while keeping the foliage away from damp soil where fungal rot spreads easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa baai lɛ jeɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster and greener in spots where cleared bushes were burned before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hei ni ajie jwɛi lɛ dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning plant vegetation leaves behind wood ash, which temporarily adds vital nutrients like potassium and reduces soil acidity, giving crops a quick burst of nutrition.
ga: Tsoi ni ashã lɛ shĩɔ tso sũ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than the crop seeds I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to survive on very little water and food, allowing them to germinate faster and consume soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu fioo kɛ niyenii fioo nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ada.

english: Why is it better for me to plant seeds in neat rows rather than broadcasting them loosely across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, spaced rows prevents plants from overcrowding each other for sunlight and water, while making weeding, spraying, and harvesting far easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli ni gbɛ kã amɛteŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛha hulu la kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your trees are suffering from nutrient deficiency, drought stress, or root disease like swollen shoot virus. When trees get sick or lack food, they drop leaves to save energy and protect their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo shishifã helai tamɔ shoot swollen virus kɛji tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ loo niyenii bɛ ehe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does a disease spread from one sick plant to all the healthy crops on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic germs that spread through wind, splashing rain, contaminated farm cutlasses, or small insects carrying the sickness from leaf to leaf.
ga: Muawai bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ ŋmɔ mli kaklai ni mli ewo muji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛ tsei helai baa. loo kooloi bibii ni hiɛɔ hela kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a soil fungus that thrives in wet conditions. Rain splashes the fungal spores onto low pods, and heavy shade keeps moisture trapped, causing the pods to rot quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa pods lɛ fiteɔ oya

english: What causes small caterpillars to suddenly appear and eat all my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ba trukaa ni amɛye mi-baby corn baai lɛ fɛɛ?

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by nocturnal moths. When the eggs hatch, hundreds of hungry caterpillars emerge at once and feed heavily on young, tender maize leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be kome mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ji ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leafy tops but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Giving crops too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting in rich soil causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in roots to make large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ni akɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: How do weeds in my field actually stop my pepper plants from growing well?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your soil; their strong roots steal water and food meant for your pepper plants, while their leafy tops block sunlight needed for crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛhaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ ada lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach light, leaving no extra energy to grow thick stems or big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ kɛha tsei ni mli tse loo tsei wuji lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off side shoots from tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ wɔ tomato tsei lɛ asɛɛ tsei lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots forces the plant to send all its water and food into growing larger, healthier fruit rather than wasting energy on useless extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ aha koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any fruit during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up the pollen inside the flower. When flowers cannot get fertilized properly, the plant drops them to conserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu.

english: Why do seeds I save from my last maize harvest yield less than new certified seeds from the agronomist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni agronomist kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields and vigor in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these strong traits in the next generation and are more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger growth at the top, signaling that it needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea he miihia.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of large leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi eshishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air, so adding too much manure or high-nitrogen fertilizer stops them from fruiting properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkawo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. High heat dries out the flower pollen before fertilization can occur, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ dani fɔmɔ baanyɛ aba. Koni akɛtsi yibiiwoo naa

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody so quickly before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni amɛfeɔ tso oya dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods develop rapidly after flowering and mature into tough, fibrous pods within three to five days. Harvesting them while they are small and snap easily keeps the plant producing soft, edible pods.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ be mli ni eji bibioo ni efiteɔ oya lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. As they feed on the underside of young leaves, they damage the tissue and can transmit plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ Efiteɔ fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ lɛ eshwa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Heavy rain splashes fungus spores from the soil onto the pods, while lack of sunlight prevents the farm from drying out.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni bɛ lɛ baatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have holes in them with powdery dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorl to feed on tender growth. The powdery material is the pest's waste matter left behind as it eats the stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛfee powda lɛ ji jwɛi ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stem turns dark brown, and small cracks appear in the soil near the stem base due to the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi ni shwereɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my seed yams take so long to sprout after I plant them in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. During this time, the tuber will not sprout regardless of soil water until internal chemical changes end dormancy naturally.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kwɛŋ ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko kɛyashi tsofa tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over easily during strong rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots concentrated near the surface and heavy foliage at the top. When rain softens the soil and wind pushes the leaves, the shallow root system loses grip, making prop stakes necessary.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ebɔle nu lɛ hiɛ, ni baai ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa baai lɛ. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ. Ehaa ehe hiaa ni aná tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under direct sun. They require shade crops like plantain or forest trees to shield them from heat and retain soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn ears form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize often signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires heavy nutrients to grow strong stems and leaves, so low soil nitrogen forces the plant to pull nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed newer top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nitrogen ni faaa lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings so that the roots grow very large?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa?

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about one meter apart. If planted too close together, their underground roots compete for water, nutrients, and space, resulting in thin, small tubers instead of thick ones.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii kɛ he ko he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tseee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Staking exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie ehe kpo lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop due to extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. When temperatures are too high or water is scarce, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to survive rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii hewɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Removing extra shoots, called suckers, leaves only one main stem and one strong follower. This ensures all water and nutrients from the soil go into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains rather than feeding multiple weak stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii titri kome pɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni he wa. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ni ekɛ plantains ŋmɔji agboi ni tsii baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei bibii babaoo niyenii lɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my young crops during their first few weeks make such a big difference?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛwo midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ha tsakemɔ kpele ba.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping fields weed-free during early growth gives your crops an unchallenged start to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔji lɛ amli jwɛi bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa amamɔ shishi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko akaŋ amɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that it does not damage them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, usually early in the morning or late afternoon a few weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer directly onto dry soil or burning plants during peak midday heat can scorch roots and leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli leebi loo shwane mli. Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsei ni eshã lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do I suddenly see so many armyworm caterpillars eating my crops after the first major rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii babaoo ni miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain triggers armyworm moths to emerge from the soil and lay hundreds of eggs on fresh green foliage. Warm, moist conditions allow the eggs to hatch quickly into hungry caterpillars that feed on young crop leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa cutworm ŋmeii jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa wɔji ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is very delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the leaves from burning and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa kwraa. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer maize cobs every year when I plant it on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes all the specific nutrients that maize needs to grow strong. Rotating your field with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores essential nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni he hiaa koni abele lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide in the central funnel of the plant and chew on the leaves as they unroll.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava roots are generally mature when the lower leaves of the plant turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to bulge and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛji tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before planting my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, deep soil to expand downward without restriction, and the raised mounds prevent excess rain from sitting around the roots and causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi ni naatsii ko bɛ he. Ni gɔŋ ni awó nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer right against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the plant stem can scorch the plant's skin and roots due to concentrated mineral salts; placing it a few inches away allows roots to absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without setting fruit due to high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients, which stress the plant and make it shed blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why is it recommended to cut down the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ajie tsei ni eda fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow around one mother plant forces them to share limited nutrients, which leads to smaller plantain bunches and longer fruiting times.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo shwereɔ yɛ fɔlɔ tso kome he. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛja niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ baaha plantains lɛ afee bibii ni amɛyibii lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ.

english: Pepper leaves roll up during the peak heat of the day as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss from their leaf surface, usually relaxing again when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide quick shade and moisture to help cocoa seedlings survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo oya kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava allows you to harvest maize early while cassava grows slowly underneath, giving you two separate harvests and helping to suppress weed growth.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi. Enɛ haa onáa kpamɔ sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen nutrient or that waterlogging around the roots is preventing the plant from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when weather becomes extremely hot, when soil moisture is irregular, or when there is insufficient airflow and insects to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to leave space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop receives adequate sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants for resources.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ abɔ he akaŋ yɛ nibii ahe

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need light moisture, air, and warmth near the soil surface to break open; planting them too deep starves them of air and exhausts their energy before they reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ dani hulu lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around pepper roots suffocates them and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungal diseases to grow and attack the root system.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛmli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do holes appear in my cabbage leaves during warm dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by moth larvae and caterpillars that multiply rapidly in warm weather and feed on the soft leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight for better growth while keeping them off wet soil, which prevents foliage diseases and results in larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ hulu la mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa etsɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa ni ebaaha bulbs lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why does my orange tree produce plenty of fruit one year and very few the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Citrus trees can experience alternate bearing, where producing a massive yield uses up most of the plant's stored nutrients, forcing it to rest and produce less the next season.
ga: Orange tsei baanyɛ akpee tsakemɔ. Kɛtsɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni ato lɛ mli babaoo tsuɔ nii. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ejɔɔ ehe ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it so hard to clear and break up the soil before I plant my crops, and does it really help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ abaatsumɔ sũ mli ni akumɔ mli dani adu nii lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Hard, tightly packed soil prevents plant roots from spreading out and reaching underground water. Clearing and loosening the soil lets young roots breathe, drink water easily, and anchor firmly so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ muɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooonu nu ni omɔ mli shiŋŋ kɛha tsei adalɛ ni mli wa

english: Why does my soil get dry and crusty so quickly after I clear the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie he ni mikɛbaadu nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed directly to the hot sun loses water fast through evaporation. Adding organic material like decaying leaves or manure helps the soil hold onto water like a sponge, keeping it soft and moist for your plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings drown or rot when heavy rains flood my farmlands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli loo amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: When water collects on hard or poorly drained land, it fills up all the tiny air pockets in the soil. Plant roots need air to survive, so standing water smothers the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni wa loo hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to add fertilizer to my land if crops already grow naturally in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miida momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Soil is like a food bowl that gets empty as crops eat from it harvest after harvest. Fertilizer refuels the soil with essential nutrients that crops must have to grow tall, stay healthy, and produce large yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ niyenii tsɛnsi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ́ tsei ye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Ha oná hewalɛ ni owo yibii babaoo

english: Why do extension officers tell me to apply fertilizer a second time while my crops are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Crops need different amounts of food at different stages of life. The first fertilizer helps them build strong roots and stems, while the second application gives them extra energy to produce big fruits, grains, or tubers.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji, dumɔwui loo bulbs.

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on dry soil or after the ground is wet from rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to melt into the dirt so root systems can drink it in. Applying fertilizer to moist soil after rain stops it from burning the plants or blowing away in the wind.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã loo amɛkatswa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I put in the soil if a huge rainstorm hits my farm right after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ wulu ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash loose fertilizer off the top of the land before the roots can eat it. Placing fertilizer slightly underground next to the plant helps trap the nutrients in the soil where roots can reach them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aye. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni emɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crops are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the soil has run out of nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay bright green and make strong leaves, so yellowing means the plant is starving.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they end up fighting each other for the limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight available on that spot of land, leaving all of them weak and underfed.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe baawu koni amɛná nu. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni faaa yɛ nakai he lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing them early gives your crops full access to the good soil so they can grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ kpakpa kwraa. Koni amɛha amɛdara ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready for harvest so I do not pick it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ kaabua naa mra tsɔ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the husks turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard. If you press a grain with your fingernail and no milky liquid comes out, the crop has reached full maturity and is safe to harvest.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛji okɛ onineshi tsɔne nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ejeee kpo lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ edara kwraa ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic manure helps the plant retain its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow and drop when the soil lacks nitrogen or during dry spells. The plant naturally sheds lower leaves to conserve water and direct energy toward its growing stems and roots.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aya amɛshishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up in intense heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant save water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why is my yam plant growing plenty of leafy vines above ground but producing very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing green leaves and stems instead of storing energy underground. Balanced feeding ensures the plant builds larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I prevent my harvested tomatoes from getting squashed and spoiling when I pack them into wooden crates?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite kɛ́ akɛwo tso adekai amli?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when packed too deep because the weight of the top layers crushes the bottom ones. Using shallow crates lined with dry grass or soft leaves cushions the fruit and keeps them whole.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo mli tsɔ ejaakɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ tsiimɔ shwieɔ shishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ adeka ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai bibii ewo mli lɛ nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tso yibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes soften and rot quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes rot easily if their skin gets bruised during digging or if they are stored in hot, unventilated rooms. Drying them in a shaded, airy place for a few days thickens the skin and helps them store much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ shwie shi beni akuɔ shi loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ agbi yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni ehiɛ emli nibii lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my stored maize grains to turn into white powder after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils bore into dry grains to feed and lay eggs, leaving behind powdery waste. Drying your grain thoroughly and storing it in airtight bags keeps these pests out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ boteɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni afee lɛ powder ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: What happens if I plant my garden egg seedlings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu eggplant dumɔwui yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them grow weak and tall, producing fewer and smaller garden eggs.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛdaraa. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits crack open while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst when they receive a heavy burst of water or rain after a long dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nu loo nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yibii lɛ amli fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when I cut down all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting tall shade trees protects the young cocoa from heat stress and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ loo aduɔ Shade ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy, which is stored in the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents wet soil from causing leafy diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni abaato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli Wein tso lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ tsei ahe helai aba.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips in a V-shape is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil consumes all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaawo niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ fɛɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and promotes fungal diseases that rot the tubers, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why will my corn ears stay very small if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded corn plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense corn plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize look like they were chewed with sawdust left inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii ewo mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of the maize plant. Identifying it early allows you to treat the plant before it destroys the entire stem.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ lɛ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tso lɛ dani efiteɔ eshishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that swallow up water and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the full benefit of the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni miɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently watered and fertilized encourages the flowers to set into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu kɛ muji daa lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow at once, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ dara babaoo shikome Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ awo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain plants start producing smaller bunches after 3 or 4 years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii bibii feemɔ lɛ? Afii 3 loo 4 sɛɛ?

english: As plantain plants age, their underground root system becomes congested and less capable of taking up nutrients efficiently, naturally reducing their energy and bunch size.
ga: Beni plantains lɛ dara lɛ Amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ kɛ bouquet lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when a plantain plant has reached the end of its lifespan and needs to be cleared?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eda ni ehe miihia ni ajie lɛ?

english: When the main stem produces thin stalks, pale leaves, and tiny fruit bunches even with good care, the plant's natural vigor has run out and it is time to replant.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ wo tsei bibii, baai ni tsuɔ kɛ aduawai bibii akui. Eyɛ mli akɛ akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ. Adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ etã. Ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What actually causes a crop like plantain to lose its growth vigor over time?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ nyɛɛɛ adara yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Loss of vigor is caused by a natural aging process combined with soil nutrient depletion, root overcrowding, and pest accumulation around the base over several harvest cycles.
ga: Hewalɛ ni baa shi lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ nifeemɔ mli. kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni laajeɔ yɛ sũ shishifãi ni ebɔle ehe kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni abua naa yɛ shishigbɛ he yɛ kpamɔɔ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ fata he

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra sprouts coming up around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and food, which weakens the whole cluster and leads to poor yield.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tso lɛ nine muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaaa yibii kpakpai aba.

english: If I keep cutting back the extra shoots at the bottom, will my plantain plant keep producing fruits forever?
ga: Kɛji mifo nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ani midumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii kɛya naanɔ?

english: No, cutting extra shoots helps the current stems grow strong, but the underground parent root naturally weakens after a few years and still requires complete replanting.
ga: Dabi, tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ daa waa. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ, ni ehe baahia ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ kwraa lolo.

english: Why do new shoots sprouting from an old plantain root often grow up weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, tsei heei ni jɛɔ plantain shishifãi momo amli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: New shoots depend on the old root system for food; if the parent root is old or exhausted, the new suckers will lack the nourishment needed to grow strong.
ga: Tsofɔi heei damɔ shishifãi momo lɛ anɔ kɛha niyenii. Kɛji fɔlɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ lɛ Sucker hee lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there a medicine or fertilizer I can put at the base of an old plantain stem to make it young again?
ga: Ani tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛfata plantains momoi lɛ ashishi koni eha amɛfee tamɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ekoŋŋ?

english: Fertilizers add nutrients to the soil, but they cannot reverse the natural biological aging of an old plant root; new suckers or fresh planting are needed for renewed growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi enyɛŋ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tso shishifãi momo lɛ daa lɛ asɛɛ afo. Akɛ tsei heei loo tsei heei ni adu lɛ he miihia kɛha dalɛ hee.

english: Does applying fertilizer to the soil fix a weak plantain plant, or is that just how the plant behaves?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ he naagba lɛ he nii loo eji tsei lɛ ajeŋba kɛkɛ?

english: Fertilizer helps healthy young plants reach full yield, but natural decline after several years is just how plantains grow, so soil inputs alone cannot stop old plants from dying out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Shi adebɔɔ mli shigbeemɔ ni baa yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ ji dumɔwui adalɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsĩ tsei momoi anaa koni amɛkagboi.

english: Is it better to keep treating old plantain stems or cut them down completely and start over?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooya nɔ okɛ plantain tsei momo lɛ ato loo ooofolɔ amɛ kwraa ni obɔi ekoŋŋ?

english: After 3 to 4 years, it is more profitable to cut down old stems and plant fresh, healthy suckers because old plants yield far less despite the heavy labor put into them.
ga: Yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he akɛ aaafo tso lɛ tso momo lɛ mli ni adu tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baawo yibii fioo kwraa yɛ nitsumɔ ni tsii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my soil seem to lose its power to grow plantains well after a few harvest seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy feeding crops like plantains draw substantial amounts of nutrients out of the earth over 3 to 4 years, requiring organic manure, fertilizer, or crop rotation to rebuild soil health.
ga: Tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ, jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni no biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ atsu nii koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the fuel it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná fuɛl ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and drop their leaves. Fast-growing plantains act like giant umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the air cool and humid while the cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much fresh manure or excessive nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrition encourages tuber expansion.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress during dry spells. Without steady moisture and moderate heat, the flowers dry up before pollen can turn them into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani pollen lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my pepper seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too close forces peppers to compete for sunlight, ground nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and tiny peppers. Proper spacing gives each plant room to branch out and bear larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ akashɛ amɛnɔ. Niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa chili lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni ekɛ niji baaje kpo ni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same bed where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of soil nutrients, but cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the dirt through their roots, naturally fertilizing the field for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts show readiness when the outer leaves start to turn yellow and dry. You can dig up a test plant; if the inside of the pods is dark brown with clear dark veins rather than pale and spongy, they are ready.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ hesaamɔ kpo beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa tsei atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni anaa jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami nɛ e ngɛ sponji. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Can I cut any part of a cassava stem to use as planting stick, or only certain sections?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afo ŋmei tso lɛ fã ko ni akɛtsu nii akɛ tso loo fãi komɛi kɛkɛ?

english: Only the mature, hard middle section of a healthy stem makes good planting material. The soft, tender top dries out quickly and dies, while the very bottom wood grows slowly and yields fewer tubers.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni eda lɛ pɛ ji dumɔ nii ni hi. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ. yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ bulb fioo.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet peppers turning black and rotten before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiitsɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot and happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular—cycling between very dry and soaked soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa lɛ teŋ ni etsiɔ ehe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily when a strong rain wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its prop roots—the anchor roots near the base—are shallow or weak. Planting seeds too shallowly or having pests chew through underground roots prevents the plant from locking firmly into the soil.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ fi sɛɛ. (anchor roots near the base) shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo egbɔjɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli tsɔ loo nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my seeds failing to grow when rain water sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When rainwater stays trapped on your field without draining away, it cuts off air to the soil. Without air, seeds drown and rot underground instead of sprouting into healthy crops.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oyale mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crop roots when excess water gets trapped inside the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Trapped water becomes stagnant and displaces the air in the soil, causing crop roots to suffocate, rot, and eventually die because they cannot breathe.
ga: Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ.

english: How does creating drainage channels on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mafee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Drainage channels direct standing water off your field, preventing water from becoming stagnant so that the soil stays well-aerated and suitable for seed germination.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Koni nu lɛ akatsi shi Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ehi kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, water settles around the stems and stagnates. Damp, airless soil promotes fungi and bacteria that decay the stem before it can form roots.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Nu baakã shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. trunk and keep still Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it important for my crop soil to be loose and airy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni midumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ahi mli lɛ?

english: Loose and airy soil allows air and water to move freely to the roots, giving sprouting seeds the oxygen they need to push through the ground easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu yaa shishifãi lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why won't my seeds sprout even when I water them every day on hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ daa gbi moŋ?

english: Hard, compacted ground traps water on the surface and blocks air from entering. Without clean, airy space in the soil, even good seeds cannot germinate.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabote mli. Kɛji he ko ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui kpakpai po nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: How does clearing and tilling my land help protect my seeds before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe dani aduɔ?

english: Tilling breaks up hard ground to make it clean and airy, while removing hidden pest habitats so your seeds have safe, breathing space to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni ehe atse ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ahi mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛmuɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How can I keep tiny bugs and pests from entering my stored harvested grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ amli?

english: Using well-sealed, clean, and airy storage spaces or airtight bags prevents pests from crawling inside, keeping your harvest dry and safe from destruction.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ he ko ni akɛ nibii toɔ loo vacuum bag ni atsĩ naa, ni ehe tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli. Ha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ agbi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my seeds more when the soil is wet and soggy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa midumɔwui lɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Wet, stagnant soil weakens seeds and creates damp conditions that attract soil insects and worms looking for easy decaying food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni ekã shi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni taoɔ niyenii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep harmful creatures out of my vegetable seedbed?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui akahi mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Keeping your seedbed elevated, clean, and well-drained creates a dry, airy barrier that pests cannot easily enter or live in to destroy your young plants.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui ashishi lɛ aya ŋwɛi, ehe atse ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli. Ehaa gbɛtsii nii ko ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli baa. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ abote mli loo amɛhi mli mlɛo koni amɛfite odumɔwui lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow. When the soil lacks nitrogen or gets waterlogged, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves, turning them yellow. Adding manure or the right fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ adu Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant there.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before growing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani midu pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or insect damage. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and watering regularly during hot weeks helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu ni afɔ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines make energy for the tuber underground by catching sunlight with their leaves. When you stake them high, the leaves spread out toward the sun instead of crowding on the damp ground, allowing the plant to build a much larger tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ okɛto nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why does cutting off some healthy branches from my fruit trees make them yield bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa amɛwoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or extra branches so the tree does not waste water and food on leaves it does not need. Instead, the tree directs all its energy straight into developing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa babaoo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa tso lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ tsɔɔ e he wami ɔ tsuo kɛ yaa yiblii nguahi nɛ a ngɛ he wami ɔ a nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by soil-borne sicknesses like bacterial wilt. The germs enter the roots and block the tiny tubes inside the stem that carry water up, making the plant dry out from the inside despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Muawai lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ paipii bibii lɛ anaa. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu baa ŋwɛi lɛ Gbi tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ po.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots reach full maturity, heavy rain or underground insects like termites break through their thick skin. Excess groundwater enters these cuts, causing fungal rot to spread quickly through the starch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii baabote ehewolo ni mli tse lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ boteɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.
