english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I sow them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain warms up dry soil but often evaporates quickly before the next rain comes. Seeds need continuous moisture for several days to sprout; if the soil dries out midway, the young seedling dies under the dirt.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ oya dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa. Dumɔwui hia nu ni yaa nɔ gbii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋ Tso bibioo lɛ gbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I plant my cassava and maize very close together, why are both harvests small?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ yibiiwoo enyɔ lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight above ground and water and food below ground. Giving each crop its proper spacing prevents them from starving one another.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tsei ateŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even if I water my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have stronger, faster-growing roots than most farm crops. They drink up the water and suck out the soil nutrients long before your main crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why is it important for me to check my soil before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Checking your soil tells you what plant food is already available and what is missing. This helps you pick the right crops for your field and avoids wasting money on unnecessary fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo tsofai ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei amli kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oŋmɔji lɛ, ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ shika ni okɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my land has enough nutrients for my crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Land with good nutrients usually has rich, dark soil and supports healthy green weeds. If your crops grow slowly, have yellowish leaves, or stay weak, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔji ni niyenii kpakpai yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo, eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ, loo ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one part of my land but struggle on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ fã kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality and nutrient levels are not the same across an entire field. Some areas may have deeper, richer soil that holds water better, while other spots might be rocky, sandy, or washed out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ekolɛ hei komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi baanyɛ afee tɛi, ŋã, loo nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do crops need nutrients from the soil just like humans need food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei he hiaa niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii he hiaa adesai lɛ?

english: Nutrients are the basic building blocks crops use to grow strong roots, green leaves, and big fruits. Without enough nutrients, plants become weak, fall ill easily, and give very small yields.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ji shishijee nibii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai wuji. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, hela mɔɔ amɛ oya, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: What happens to my farm when heavy rain washes away the top layer of my soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away topsoil, which contains most of the natural nutrients crops need. Once that top layer is lost, the remaining hard ground makes it difficult for roots to grow and absorb food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛya. Beni ŋwɛi fã lɛ laajeɔ Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops behave differently when the weather changes from year to year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Crops react directly to changes in temperature, sunshine, and water supply. When the weather changes, it affects how fast plants absorb food, flower, and produce seeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, hulu la kɛ nu nibii amli lɛ he nii tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ. Esaa bɔ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii oya, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to plant after the rains have established steadily rather than after the very first light rainfall. Planting too early during unpredictable rains can cause seeds to dry up and die in the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can too much rain actually hurt my crops, and how does that happen?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni baaba?

english: Yes, excessive rain can flood the soil and starve plant roots of oxygen, causing them to rot. It can also wash nutrients deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afua ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if the rain suddenly stops for a few weeks during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of water while forming stems, leaves, and fruits. A sudden dry break stresses the plant, causing leaves to wilt, flowers to drop early, and yields to drop significantly.
ga: Tsei hia nu daa be mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi, baai, kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ egbi trukaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni shwieɔ shi Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ eba shi waa.

english: How does very hot weather affect the growth and yield of my crops?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat forces plants to lose water faster through their leaves to stay cool. If they cannot pull enough moisture from the soil, they stop growing well, drop their blossoms, and yield smaller harvests.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ. Kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow when the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves early in the season usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build green leaves, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava with maize covers the ground to reduce weeds, and because maize matures in a few months while cassava takes longer, you can harvest food twice from the same plot of land.
ga: Cassava ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi. Ni ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa niyenii shii enyɔ kɛjɛ he kome.

english: Why do the cocoa pods on my tree turn black and rot before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaajie amɛ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet conditions and heavy shade. Clearing weeds and pruning tree branches lets sunlight and air in to keep pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with big leaves but gives me tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant uses all its strength to grow leaves above ground instead of sending food down to make big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni efee bulbs agboi.

english: What is making small holes in my tomato leaves and causing the young green fruits to drop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ tomato baai amli lɛ baa? Ni ehaa aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Insects or caterpillars feed on the leaves and bore into green fruits, which weakens the plant and forces it to drop fruits early to survive.
ga: Kplukai loo ŋmeii yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai eŋɔli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbee shi oya bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save water and prevent drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my yam plants produce weak vines and small tubers even though I built big mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mifeɔ gɔŋ agbo moŋ?

english: Yams need strong wooden stakes to climb; without tall stakes, the leaves cannot capture enough sunlight to generate the energy needed to expand the tuber inside the mound.
ga: Atomɔ biɔ tso ni wa ni akɛkwɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ hu nyɛŋ amɔmɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulbs yɛ gɔji amli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients, as they cannot afford the water and energy needed to turn flowers into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛha nu kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfee chili.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to come up out of the soil after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep, if soil insects ate them underground, or if the soil lacked moisture to wake the seed up.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kplukai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ atswa

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my groundnuts cause the pods to be empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi ŋmei pods lɛ mli efolo?

english: Weeds compete directly with groundnuts for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, stealing the food the plant needs to fill its pods with healthy nuts.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ awo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I start my fruit tree seeds in a nursery bag instead of planting them straight into my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maje aduawai tsei ashishi kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery protects young, delicate shoots from heavy rains, hot sun, pests, and weeds. It allows you to nurture strong roots so only healthy plants are moved to the field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa he. Hulu ni mli edɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi yeɔ ebua bo ni ohaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii koni amɛjie tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What makes nursery-grown tree seedlings produce better fruit than wild trees growing on my land?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe koo mli tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are grown from carefully chosen parent seeds under controlled watering and soil conditions, giving them a stronger start and a higher chance of bearing quality fruit early.
ga: Akɛ fɔlɔi dumɔwui ni ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ duɔ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii mra.

english: Why do young seedlings need special soil mixed with manure while growing in nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ krɛdɛɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii efutu mli he hiaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Young plant roots are soft and sensitive; loose, rich soil allows them to spread easily and absorb essential food to grow strong stems before being planted outdoors.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa dani amɛdu yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Can I grow extra tree seedlings in my nursery to sell to other farmers in my village?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, preparing healthy seedlings in polybags for other farmers to buy and plant is a great way to earn extra farm income before your main crops even mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooosaa yɛ poly kotokui amli koni okwaafoi krokomɛi ahe ni amɛdu lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ona shika kroko yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adara.

english: How do I know when my fruit seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to be planted out on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have developed multiple sets of dark green leaves and a firm stem, showing their roots are strong enough to handle field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui kɛji amɛyɛ baai eŋɔlii srɔtoi kɛ tso ni ma shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu shihilɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my fresh seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens due to transplant shock, caused by damaging root hairs or exposing tender plants to hot afternoon sun. Watering immediately after planting and shading them helps them survive.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ hewɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni fiteɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How should I transport young nursery plants to my farm without hurting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: You should lift the plants by holding their containers or root soil balls—never by their thin stems—and protect them from direct wind and heat during the journey.
ga: Esa akɛ owó tso lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsɛnsi loo sũ ŋmɔtɔ ko ni ooomɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ—jeee tso lɛ shishifã bibioo lɛ—ni obu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli.

english: How long does a transplanted fruit seedling typically take before it starts bearing fruit on my farm?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduawai dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Depending on the crop type and care, most fruit trees take between two to five years after field transplanting to mature and begin producing saleable fruit.
ga: Yibii tsei babaoo heɔ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛjeɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ shishi. Enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is selling my harvested fruit to outside buyers often better than selling only to people in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaahɔɔ mɛi ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ hi be fɛɛ be fe ni mikɛbaahɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli bii pɛ lɛ?

english: Outside traders and city markets buy larger quantities and usually pay higher prices because city consumers face shortages and high demand for fresh rural produce.
ga: Jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ baahe babaoo ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ maŋtiasei amli lɛ kɛ nibii heei ni anáa lɛ he naagbai kpeɔ, ni amɛtaoɔ nibii heei babaoo yɛ akrowai amli.

english: How can I prepare my harvested fruits after picking so that commercial buyers will prefer mine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa aduawai ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ? Koni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ asumɔ mi yibii lɛ

english: Sorting fruits by size, washing off dirt, and removing bruised ones before transport keeps your harvest fresh longer, attracting wholesale buyers willing to pay top value.
ga: Yibii lɛ amli gbalamɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ naa muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ hei ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ dani akɛyaa he kroko. Ebaaye ebua ni onibii lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ. Gbalamɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii babaoo ni sumɔɔ ni amɛwo jara ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize if I leave some of it unharvested in the field because my workers get too tired?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi eko yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni mikpako ejaakɛ etɔ mi nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔ?

english: Leaving mature maize in the field exposes it to rain, mold, and pests like grain weevils. Over time, the unharvested crop rots or gets eaten by animals, causing you to lose profit and attracting diseases that can damage your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi ni eda lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baa enɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akpaaa lɛ baafite loo kooloi baaye. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni egbalaa helai ni baanyɛ afite nii yɛ okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I leave remaining produce in my field after harvesting, will it turn into good fertilizer for my next crop?
ga: Kɛji mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ Ani ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While rotting plants do break down into organic matter, leaving leftover fruits or roots in the field is dangerous. They attract pests and hide fungal diseases that will stay in the soil and attack your fresh crops when you plant again.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli moŋ, Shi aduawai loo shishifãi ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Amɛgbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaatutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ kɛ́ odu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can small farm tools or machines help me harvest my cassava faster without breaking my back?
ga: Te okwaayeli he dɛŋdade loo tsɔne bibioo ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa ŋmei oya ni misɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Simple tools like manual cassava lifters or small mechanical diggers use leverage to lift roots cleanly out of the soil. This drastically cuts down on human effort, stops tubers from breaking underground, and lets you finish harvesting before you get exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaa ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii loo tsɔne bibioo ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ. Akɛ lever tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo shishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa adesai amɔdɛŋbɔɔ shi kwraa. Kpa tubers lɛ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehaa ogbeɔ okpamɔ lɛ naa dani ogbɔjɔɔ.

english: Are there affordable small machines that smallholder farmers like me can use to help with harvesting?
ga: Ani tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ ni jara waaa ni okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ ekɛye ebua yɛ nikpamɔ mli?

english: Yes, small motor-powered reapers, threshers, and mechanical diggers are designed for small farms. You can often hire them for a day or share the cost through local farmer cooperatives so you do not have to buy them outright.
ga: hɛɛ ŋmãa tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa kɛ tsɔnei bibii ni akɛ tsɔne kudɔɔ ni akɛfoɔ ŋmãa. Afee aha ŋmɔji bibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii gbi kome loo okɛ shika lɛ aha kɛtsɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ohé amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can joining a local farmer group help me get machinery to assist with my farm harvesting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná tsɔnei ni baaye abua mi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Farmer groups can pool their resources or register with government programs to access shared machinery like threshers and harvesters. Sharing equipment makes it affordable for small farms, saving time and keeping crops from being left behind.
ga: Okwaafoi akui baanyɛ afee amɛnibii loo amɛŋmala amɛgbɛi amɛwo nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi amli koni amɛná tsɔnei ni amɛjaraa tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ haa ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ahe jara waaa. Enɛ haaa be afite, ni ehaaa ashi ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I end up losing so much of my crop right at harvest time, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fite yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Harvest losses usually happen when physical fatigue causes workers to leave crops behind, or when rough harvesting damages the produce. You can stop this by using proper harvesting tools, working in structured shifts, and using labor-saving techniques.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ ha nitsulɔi lɛ shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdu lɛ. aloo kɛ́ kpamɔ ni mli wa fite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsu nii yɛ shift ni ato he gbɛjianɔ mli ni okɛ nitsumɔ he ŋaai atsu nii

english: Is there a better technique for harvesting rice so my family doesn't waste energy and drop grain on the ground?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni hi fe enɛ yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa ŋmãa koni wekui akafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Using sharp, serrated sickles and harvesting at the right crop maturity allows you to cut stalks easily without shaking the plant. Harvesting systematically in rows reduces tiredness and stops grains from shattering onto the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ni naa wa tsu nii ni okɛkpa nii beni tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ofoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mlɛo ni okɛ tso lɛ ekpokpooo. Nikpamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaaa ŋmaa mli agbala.

english: How does worker fatigue during the harvest season directly affect the quality and total yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nitsulɔi agbɔjɔmɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ?

english: When workers become overly tired, they slow down, handle crops roughly, and often leave produce behind in the soil. Rough handling bruises crops so they spoil faster, while left-behind crops directly cut into your total harvest yield.
ga: Kɛ́ nitsulɔi lɛ etɔ amɛ tsɔ Amɛbaafee mlɛo. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni bei pii lɛ, oshiɔ nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni adu lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔni afee ni efite oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ mli.

english: Does the time of day I choose to harvest my crops affect how heavy or difficult the physical work is?
ga: Ani be ni mihalaa akɛ mikɛkpaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ saa bɔ ni ewa loo ewa ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, harvesting early in the morning when temperatures are cool and the ground holds light moisture makes digging and cutting much easier. In the hot afternoon sun, workers tire out twice as fast and crops wither quickly after being picked.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ Nitsulɔi nijiaŋ jeɔ wui oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot so quickly in storage after I dig them up from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly when they are cut or wounded by sharp farm tools during digging. When harvesters are exhausted or use improper digging methods, they accidentally cut the skin, creating entry points for rots and bacteria.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ okwaayeli nibii ni yɔɔ oya fo loo pila amɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Beni nikpalɔ lɛ he ejɔ lɛ loo ekɛ gbɛi ni esaaa ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ. Amɛfo hewolo lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Ekɛ fitemɔ kɛ helai baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates living shade that protects the young leaves from burning and helps keep the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa shade ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ tsei awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. Providing stakes helps the leaves produce more food through sunlight, which is directly transferred downward to make the yam tuber grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. ni abaajie kɛya shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong stems. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot if heavy rains stay on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater stays on the land without draining, it suffocates the roots and creates the perfect environment for soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops right at the start of the rainy season instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: Planting early ensures that seeds get steady moisture right away to germinate, giving the young roots enough time to go deep into the ground before any sudden dry spells begin.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ daa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers give very small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close to each other, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, while their wide leaves block light from each other, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii bibii.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that attack maize to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and puts good nutrients back in.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaf, or by a plant virus spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by very high temperatures, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but produce very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: If cowpea plants get too much nitrogen from rich soil, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. Tiny insects called thrips can also eat the young blossom buds before they turn into pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ hu baanyɛ aye fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom up even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is their main food. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant steals food from its older bottom leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji amɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baai heei.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi attack them, causing them to rot before you can harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ. Ha egbo dani obaanyɛ okpa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without producing any young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ amɛshwie shi ni amɛwooo ŋmeii bibii komɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, drought, or lack of shade. Flowers also fall off if there are no tiny insects, called midges, around to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms just when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli pɛ beni jwɛi lɛ ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support a heavy bunch during strong winds. Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes can also destroy those roots, leaving the plant with no anchor.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ hu baanyɛ afite nakai shishifãi lɛ. Feemɔ tso lɛ ni ŋwɛi ŋta bɛ he

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot and happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil. It usually occurs when watering is irregular, causing the soil to swing between too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap, or passing a virus to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu lɛ. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: Why do officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally traps nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, restoring the nutrients that maize took away.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. ni kɛ ehe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Koni ekɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa ejie lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and shrinking inside my barn while waiting to go to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni miigbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni maya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. Heat and humidity in the barn tell the yam it is time to grow a new plant, so it uses up its own stored food and water to sprout shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ edu tso hee. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii kɛ nu ni eto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with small fruit when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight and nutrients. The plants waste all their energy stretching tall to beat their neighbors for light instead of making thick stems and big fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛkumɔ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo yibii wuji lɛ

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaf funnel instead of just eating the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi-corn lɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant because the tender new leaves are soft to eat, and it keeps them safe from sunlight, rain, and predators.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ayeɔ. ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ hulu, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the center, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to make dark green leaves, so without it, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni tsuɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have huge leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and cool soil moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ni akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ Ehe miihia ni Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to protect itself when water is scarce. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and goes into a resting state while keeping its underground tubers safe until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe kɛji nu bɛ. Kɛtsɔ ebaai ni eshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I have to clear branches and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei aniji ni madu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbers that need to lift their leaves up to catch full sunlight. Staking keeps the foliage off the wet soil, which prevents leaf diseases caused by soil fungi and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When daytime heat gets too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up and fails to fertilize the bloom. The plant then drops the unpollinated flowers to save energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they work with tiny beneficial bacteria in their roots to capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt, naturally enriching the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves on peppers are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap, or by a plant virus carried by these insects that disturbs how the leaves expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni gbalaa baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my seed maize deep under the ground when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds buried too deep run out of their stored food energy trying to push up through the heavy layer of soil before reaching the surface light, causing seedlings to emerge weak or die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. dani la baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cold, damp air. When tree branches are too overcrowded and block air movement, moisture stays on the pods and lets the rot spread.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ mli kɛbaa. Kɛ tso niji lɛ shwere tsɔ ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Fɛ̃i hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my sweet potato crop produce huge leafy vines but tiny potatoes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli shi ŋmɔtɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving sweet potatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing big green leaves on top, leaving little energy for developing the storage roots below the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ashi kɛha shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them creates living umbrellas that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko. Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ hulutsoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the plant's growth helps turn the leaves green and boosts yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I harvest much less food if I leave weeds to grow around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into growing your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ koni kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when there are many shoots growing around one trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ daa bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they all fight for the same food in the ground. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two healthy ones allows the main tree to make big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Amɛbaawuu yɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ená niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plant helps hold flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ ekome kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps moisture trapped in the ground during dry days, stops weeds from sprouting, and keeps the root area cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why does cutting off excess branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and forces the tree to spend its energy producing pods instead of leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ diŋ lɛ baa shi, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the heart of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh middle leaves of maize. Applying control measures like neem leaf extract or recommended sprays directly into the funnel kills the pests before they ruin the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tso lɛ tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani ekpata tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my farm only when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop's roots, while wet soil safely carries the nutrients straight into the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them, excessive heat dries out the leaves, causing them to burn and wither.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ, la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the essential food the plant uses to build strong green leaves and develop full corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from producing big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus disrupts how the plant moves food, stopping it from flowering and bearing good fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus gbalaa bɔ ni tsei tsɔɔ niyenii amɛyaa lɛ mli. Ekpaa fɔfɔi ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if I plant the stick cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close, their underground roots compete with each other for water, space, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of big, thick ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa yɛ yitsei wuji ni mli tseee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to start properly before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni sa lɛ aje shishi dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need continuous soil moisture to sprout and establish roots. Planting in dry or hot soil before regular rains arrive causes the seeds to dry up or fail to grow properly.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right young plantain shoots from an old plant to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei momo amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for young shoots with narrow, sword-like leaves rather than broad leaves. These shoots grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ofee plantain ŋmeii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally enrich the soil and help feed the maize plants.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does leaving tall grass and weeds growing around my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ miiba shi.

english: Weeds act as competitors; they aggressively drink up the water, steal fertilizer, and block the sunlight that your young crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ miishɛɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to capture sunlight. Raising the leaves on stakes helps the plant make enough energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I see small holes and chewed edges on the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing part of the maize plant (the whorl) and eats the fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the scorching sun, helping it retain moisture until it gets water.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enine shɛɔ nu nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: Giving plants too much water drowns their roots and suffocates them. When roots cannot breathe air in the soil, they fail to absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and eventually drop off.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ agbo ni ebaaha egbɔjɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crops in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can drink it, and hot water droplets on leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: How does placing green protective nets over my nursery beds help my young vegetable seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni buɔ mɔ he ni mikɛwo mi-nursery saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ ye ebua mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Protective nets block harsh, direct sunlight that can burn young shoots, soften the impact of heavy rain, and stop insects or birds from eating the tender leaves before the plants are strong enough to survive outside.
ga: Nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baatsi hulu la ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ anaa. Ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hewalɛ aba shi ni etsĩ kooloi bibii loo okpoi anaa koni amɛkaye baai bibii dani tso lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits when the heat gets too high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot or water is scarce, tomato plants undergo heat stress. To save their own lives, they shed their flowers so they do not waste energy trying to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Bɔni afee ni mɔ diɛŋtsɛ wala ahere Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do crops seem to grow much faster with natural rain than when I water them from a well or tank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ nɛ fe kɛ́ nu jɛ nu bu loo baagi mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries small amounts of dissolved nitrogen from the air, acting as a light, natural fertilizer every time it falls, whereas well or tap water usually lacks this extra plant food.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni mli ewo la fioo ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo be fɛɛ be ni ebaagbee shi. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, nu bu mli nu loo pɔmpi mli nu lɛ bɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso nɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer and smaller pods now compared to thirty years ago when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ akɛto afii nyɔŋmai etɛ ni eho nɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 30 years, their internal branches weaken, and the soil beneath them loses vital nutrients. Without heavy pruning, soil nutrient replenishment, or eventual replanting, older trees naturally yield less fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 30 lɛ, emli niji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii bɛ lɛ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo yɛ naagbee lɛ, aduɔ ekoŋŋ Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops near the end of my long farm plot look dry even when water is flowing into the field irrigation canal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji kakadaji lɛ anaagbee lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu hoɔ kɛyaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water loses speed and volume as it travels over long distances, especially if irrigation channels are old or cracked. Plants at the far end end up receiving less water than plants near the water source.
ga: Nu lɛ oyaiyeli kɛ egbɛɛmɔ baa shi beni efãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ egbɔ loo egbɛ eshwa. Tsei ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ naa nu fioo fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: How does laying rubber sheets or plastic mulch on the ground help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ rɔbɔt loo plastic ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around crops prevents sunshine from reaching weed seeds so they cannot grow. It also traps moisture in the soil, keeping the root area cool and damp for a longer time.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni adu lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe, no hewɔ lɛ amɛkwɛɛɛ. Amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted cassava after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe mi-cassava lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots naturally suited to local conditions. They absorb water and soil nutrients instantly, whereas cultivated crops like cassava need time to establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi egbɛ eshwã, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ heɔ be dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize crop and leaving brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (whorl) of maize plants during the day and eat the tender leaves, leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Sprays targeting these insects help prevent the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains, allowing soil fungi to infect the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen. ni ji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree naturally thins out pods it cannot feed, but it can also be caused by insect attacks or black pod disease during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘Cherelle wilt’, ni baa beni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Shi ŋmeii ni tutuaa mɔ loo black pod hela ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why does planting my seeds in straight lines give a better harvest than broadcasting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients while making it easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and spot pests early.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai mra.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha he ni mi-vegetables lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from growing and competing with your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring the natural fertility that maize used up in the previous season.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied into moist soil shortly after rain, usually a few weeks after germination when roots are ready to feed, and again when the crop starts growing rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii. Ni ekoŋŋ beni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa oya lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to keep big shade trees on our cocoa farms instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔha tsei wuji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi moŋ ni wɔbaafolɔ amɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young and adult cocoa trees from burning under harsh sunlight, help the soil retain moisture during dry periods, and shield the cocoa crop from strong winds.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Why should I trim or cut off some of the extra branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can move freely through the farm. This reduces humidity that breeds damp diseases and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ hulutsoo hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers insist that we cut down cocoa trees when they get infected with Swollen Shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei beni bud swollen hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen Shoot is caused by a virus that spreads from tree to tree through tiny insects called mealybugs. Since there is no chemical cure for the virus, cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the disease from destroying your entire farm.
ga: Virus ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni efuu baa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ bɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa hela lɛ koni ekafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree produce good yields before I need to cut it down and replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kookoo tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani esa akɛ afo lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: A cocoa tree usually gives high yields for about 20 to 30 years. After this age, the tree naturally produces fewer pods and becomes more vulnerable to diseases, so replanting with new seedlings is necessary to keep your income steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ yibii babaoo afii 20 kɛyashi 30 yɛ afii nɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni helai baanyɛ aba enɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia koni shika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: My cocoa farm used to give me many bags of beans, but now the yield is dropping every year. What could be causing this?
ga: Kulɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ haa mi kɔfe ŋmeii kotokui babaoo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Yields drop when soil nutrients get washed away over time, when trees get too old, or when pests and diseases attack unseen. Adding fertilizer, pruning branches, and controlling pests can help restore your harvest.
ga: Yibiiwoo baa shi be mli ni sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tutuaa mɔ ni anaaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, tsei ni afolɔ mli Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need extra food or fertilizer from the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia nibii ni akɛfataa he loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, growth slows down, or the trees produce small and very few pods despite good rainfall, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, edaa blɛoo Aloo tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize inside my mature cocoa farm to get extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda mli koni maná niyenii kroko?

english: Growing food crops like cassava under mature cocoa is not recommended because they steal water and nutrients from the cocoa roots. Cassava also blocks sunlight from reaching young cocoa leaves.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Kasava lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cold, and dark conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning excess branches helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ oya kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What are those tiny bugs that bite my young cocoa pods and turn the stems dry and dark?
ga: Mɛni ji kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ni amɛhaa kookoo lɛ tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: Those insects are called capsids (or Akate). They suck the sap from young shoots and pods, causing them to dry up and die, which severely reduces your final harvest if not controlled with approved spraying.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai kooloi lɛ akɛ capsids. (loo Akate) Amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. ni haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ akudɔɔɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to leave old, ruined pods hanging on my cocoa trees after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni ekumɔ lɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Old and rotten pods left on trees act as homes for fungi and pests. During the next season, rain washes those disease spores onto your new, healthy pods, infecting the fresh crop.
ga: Pods ni egbɔ ni efite ni ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ. yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ baawo nakai helai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛya ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee ehee lɛ aná hela.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the leaves stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔleɔ Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves when the sun is strong to hide from the heat and save water. It is a natural defense mechanism to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly, and the leaves will open back up when the air cools down.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni ekɛ nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Ni baai lɛ gbeleɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my cassava stems and roots rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain leaves standing water around the roots, it drowns them and allows fungal diseases to develop, so planting on raised soil ridges or mounds helps the water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing through the soil underground. If the soil is hard or compact, the tuber cannot expand easily and becomes twisted, which is why building soft, tall, loose soil mounds gives the yams space to grow smooth and large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã oya ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni kɛlɛ, ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ, ebaaha ŋshɔŋloo lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni elɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, hot sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turning shriveled and dark before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbo ni efee duŋ dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This is called cherelle wilt, and it happens when the tree gets stressed by hot dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests. Pruning excess branches and feeding the soil helps the tree keep enough strength to carry pods to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherelle wilt ni ebaa kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyaa dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny soil pests like nematodes or weevils can eat away at these roots underground without you seeing it. Without strong roots anchoring the plant, heavy bunches or strong winds easily push the tree over.
