ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo weevils baanyɛ aye nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni onaaa amɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ bɛ lɛ, Jwɛi ni mli wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei lɛ kɛba shi mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are suffering from heat or if pests are attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ miitutua amɛ?

english: Plants suffering from heat will wilt in the hot afternoon sun but stand upright again by morning. If pests are the problem, you will see physical damage like holes in the leaves, dark spots, sticky fluids, or leaves that stay curled even in the cool morning.
ga: Tsei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baagboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaate shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ji naagba Obaana gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔi tamɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli, he ni edɔ, nu ni shwieɔ shi. Aloo baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso po lɛ.

english: When the weather gets extremely hot, pepper plants drop their flowers to conserve water and survive the heat stress. Giving your plants light shade or watering them early in the morning helps them hold onto flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu wo tso lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my orange trees produce sour fruit even though the tree itself looks big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ lɛ? Ani nakai akutu tso lɛ da ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Sweetness in oranges comes from good sunlight and specific soil nutrients like potassium while the fruit is filling up. If the soil lacks key nutrients, or if the fruit is harvested too early before it fully ripens on the branch, it will taste sour.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ jɛɔ hulu la kpakpa kɛ sũ mli nibii komɛi ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ potassium, yɛ be mli ni citrus lɛ eyi obɔ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akpa aduawai lɛ mra tsɔ, dani niji lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa. Yibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with very little harvest when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni ŋmaa fioo ko pɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition forces them to grow tall and thin searching for light, leaving them too weak to produce good yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ hu Akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛfee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ koni amɛtao la. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why did my cassava plants grow huge leafy tops but produced very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ baai shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava plants to put all their energy into leafy top growth above the ground instead of storing nutrients in the roots to build big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ nɔ baai. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and snap when strong dry winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves have broad surface areas that lose moisture rapidly during dry winds, making the leaves brittle and heavy so they break under pressure unless protected by windbreaks.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ he ko ni da ni ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe wa waa aahu akɛ amɛkuɔ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. ja kɔɔyɔɔ ebu he

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants curl their leaves during the hottest hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying even though the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive root systems and tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers and rot at the bottom during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain keeps the soil waterlogged, which prevents root breathing and causes fungal diseases to splash up from the wet soil onto the blossoms and fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amumɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils lay microscopic eggs inside the seeds before or right after harvest. As the eggs hatch, the young insects eat the inside of the seed, leaving behind empty hulls and dust.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ dumɔwui amli dani akpaa loo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Ashi ŋshɔŋloo ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize field turning yellow with light green stripes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing with light green stripes is a clear sign that the plant is either lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or has been infected by a plant virus carried by tiny insects.
ga: Yellow ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ emɔ lɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds from around my yam mounds make the yams grow so much larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ babaoo?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil minerals that the yam vine needs. Removing weeds ensures that all available nourishment goes directly into feeding the expanding yam tuber.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take almost two weeks to sprout while my maize seeds sprout in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ otsii enyɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Pepper seeds have a thick, tough outer shell that takes a longer time to absorb water and break open, whereas maize seeds have softer coats that absorb moisture and sprout rapidly.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni mli wa ni heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but only a few turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers cannot turn into pods on their own or through wind. They need tiny, beneficial insects to carry pollen from flower to flower. If there are not enough insects around, many flowers dry up and drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Amɛmiitao kooloi bibii. No he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii babaoo bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Are all the insects I see on my cocoa farm bad for my crop?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, not all insects are pests. While some attack leaves and pods, tiny friendly insects like midges are essential because they pollinate the cocoa flowers so pods can grow.
ga: Dabi, jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi tutuaa baai kɛ ŋmeii moŋ, shi kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ midges lɛ he hiaa waa ejaakɛ amɛhaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Does the wind carry pollen between cocoa flowers like it does for my maize?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ tamɔ bɔ ni etswaa mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: No, cocoa pollen is sticky and heavy, so wind cannot carry it. Cocoa trees rely almost entirely on small insects crawling into the flowers to transfer pollen.
ga: Dabi, kookoo pollen lɛ wa ni etsii. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atswa lɛ kɛya. Cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ fɔfɔi amli koni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya lɛ anɔ aaafee kwraa.

english: How can I tell if pollinating insects are doing their job on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji pollinators miitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When insect pollination is successful, you will notice tiny green pods, known as cherelles, starting to swell at the base of the flowers shortly after the blooming period.
ga: Kɛji kooloi amli ŋmeii lɛ ye omanye lɛ Obaana ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel. ni jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ

english: How does the timing of rain affect my cocoa tree's flowers and pods?
ga: Te be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ saa cacao tsei lɛ ahe fɔfɔii kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain provides the water cocoa trees need to blossom and creates the damp environment that beneficial insects need to stay active and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ haa kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehe miihia ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers dry up and fall off during long dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, cocoa trees drop flowers to save energy and water. Additionally, the tiny insects that pollinate cocoa need moist conditions to survive and work.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kplukai bibii ni feɔ cacao lɛ hu he miihia shihilɛ ni mli edɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsu nii.

english: Does shade on my farm help with cocoa pollination?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yes, shade trees keep the soil cool and moist, which creates a healthy living space for tiny pollinating insects to multiply and visit your cocoa flowers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ náa shihilɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ. koni okɛgbɛ o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ashwã ni osara amɛ

english: Will spraying insecticides on my cocoa farm reduce my pod yield?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi-pod lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: If you misuse or over-spray chemicals, you can accidentally kill the friendly insects that pollinate your cocoa flowers, leading to fewer pods forming on your trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ loo okɛwo mɔ mli babaoo. Obaanyɛ ogbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ feɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect beneficial insects while still controlling pests on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni mikwɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: You can spray chemicals carefully by targeting only damaged areas, avoiding heavy spraying directly on open flowers, and keeping the ground moist so good insects have a safe habitat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ, ni okɛ ohiɛ ama he ni efite lɛ pɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shwiemɔ ni tsii he. tɛ̃ɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni kooloi kpakpai aná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhi.

english: What can I keep on the farm ground to encourage helpful insects to stay?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makɛto ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛwo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: Leaving damp leaf litter and decaying plant material like banana stumps on the soil keeps ground moisture high, providing ideal breeding spots for tiny cocoa pollinators.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni mli efɔ kɛ tsei ni egboi, tamɔ banana ŋmɔji, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ. Eji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to start planting cocoa during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli?

english: In Ghana, planting in March and April is ideal because the major rainy season begins around this time. The early rains provide young cocoa seedlings with the deep moisture they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, dumɔwui yɛ March kɛ April mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa nu ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do some farmers plant crops in months like July or October instead of early in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji tamɔ July loo October mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ

english: Ghana experiences a minor rainy season later in the year. Planting in July, October, or November takes advantage of these secondary rains, giving seedlings a second natural window to grow safely.
ga: Ghana naa nugbɔ be fioo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Dumɔ yɛ July, October loo November mli lɛ heɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli samflɛ ni ji enyɔ ni amɛkɛdaraa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it possible for me to plant crops during dry months like November and December?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ November kɛ December lɛ amli?

english: Yes, you can plant in November and December, but because rainfall decreases during these months, you must provide manual watering or irrigation so the young plants do not dry out.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ November kɛ December mli. Shi akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nyɔŋ nɛɛ mli hewɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ onine awo mli nu loo okɛ nu awo mli koni tsei bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why should I start my cocoa seeds in a nursery instead of planting them straight into my big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: A nursery acts as a safe baby shelter. It protects fragile young cocoa sprouts from harsh heat, heavy rains, and pests, allowing them to build strong root systems before moving to the main field.
ga: Daycare lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha abifabii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni atoɔ shishifã ni mli wa shishi dani aduɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need special attention compared to fully grown trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and vulnerable to drought, pest attacks, and direct sunlight. Intensive early care ensures high survival rates so your farm reaches full productivity.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hɔmɔ, kooloi, kɛ hulu la baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Helatsamɔ ni mli wa kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ

english: What does proper cultivation mean when I am preparing my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsɔɔ kɛ́ misaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Proper cultivation means clearing harmful weeds, loosening tight soil so roots can spread easily, and digging planting holes of the correct depth and spacing to give each crop enough room to grow.
ga: Odumɔ ni sa tsɔɔ jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa. shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo kɛ dumɔ bui ni mli kwɔ ni sa kɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa koni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: What kind of extra inputs do I need to add to my field to help my crops do well?
ga: Mɛɛ saji krokomɛi ehe hiaa ni mikɛfata ŋmɔ lɛ he koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops need balanced nutrients to thrive. Adding fertilizers, compost, or organic manure enriches the soil, giving plants the essential food required to grow strong and yield heavily.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa he miihia tsei koni amɛshwere. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛnamɔ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to spray my crops with chemical treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying protects crops from devastating pests like capsids and fungal diseases like black pod, which can eat away leaves, damage stems, and destroy your yield if left untreated.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ capsids kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods, ni baanyɛ aye baai, afite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How early in the crop's lifecycle should I start spraying my farm for pests?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɔi tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: You should start monitoring and spraying early in the growth process, as pests like to attack soft, fresh leaves and shoots. Catching insects early stops infestations before they spread.
ga: Esa akɛ oje kwɛmɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shishi mra. yɛ dalɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii. Kooloi ni amɔmɔɔ amɛ mra Ekpaa gbɛfaŋnɔ dani egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What major steps must I follow from the beginning until my cocoa farm is ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa ehe baahia ni mafee kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A successful cocoa farm requires raising healthy nursery seedlings, preparing and clearing the field, planting at the right time, applying fertilizer, regular weeding, and spraying for pests until the trees mature.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni yeɔ omanye lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei lɛ anɔ. He lɛ he saamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does water collect in one spot on my farm and refuse to flow away after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaajɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water collects in low-lying spots or hard clay soil that water cannot easily pass through. Digging simple drainage channels or a collection hole directs excess water away from crop roots so they do not rot.
ga: Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ loo bu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsa lɛ buaa nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: What is a dugout pit, and how does digging one help my crop farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai dugout lɛ? Ni te bu ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei ŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A dugout is a deep hole dug in low areas of your farm to trap excess runoff water. It prevents standing water from drenching your crops and keeps moisture nearby in the soil that plants can draw on during dry days.
ga: Dugout ji bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni atsa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ koni akɛmɔ nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when rainwater sits on my field for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When standing water stays around plants too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Without air, crop roots choke and cannot take up nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and soft.
ga: Kɛ nu hi tsei ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo.

english: How can digging trenches across my farm protect my crops during heavy rainfall?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Digging trenches gives heavy rainwater a clear pathway to flow safely off your field. This stops topsoil from washing away and prevents standing pools of water from drowning crop roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejoɔ foi kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho, ni ebaaha tsei shishifãi lɛ akabote nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Can trapping rainwater in small holes on my land help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni amɔmɔɔ yɛ bu bibii amli Yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani ebaanyɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Yes, digging water-trapping pits catches surface runoff during rains and allows moisture to soak slowly into the surrounding earth, keeping crop roots hydrated longer into dry weather.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋshɔŋ nu ni atsa lɛ baamɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni oha ŋmɔtɔ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why does the soil in some wet parts of my farm smell bad like rotten eggs when I dig it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni efɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbo kɛ́ mifo mli lɛ?

english: A bad or sour smell in wet soil means water is trapped underground without air, causing organic matter to rot improperly. Digging drainage holes lets fresh air in to heal the soil so roots can thrive.
ga: Fuu loo ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ efo shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbɛ ni esaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ atsa nu lɛ buji lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why should I dig wide planting holes instead of putting seeds directly into hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo bu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mafu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Hard ground makes it very difficult for young crop roots to push through and find water. Digging loose planting holes allows tender roots to grow deep and wide, supporting strong stems and fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii ashishifãi akɛ amɛaabote mli ni amɛna nu. Dumɔ bui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsa lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛlɛɔ. Efiɔ tsei kɛ aduawai ni wa lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow well on one side of my land but stay stunted on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fa kome nɔ shi amɛmiiya hiɛ yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different parts of your farm have different soil types and water drainage. Wet patches that hold water without good drainage starve roots of air, producing weak crops compared to well-drained spots.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Hei ni nu yɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛ akɛto he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How can I test if a spot on my farm has poor drainage before planting my crops there?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji he ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Dig a small hole, fill it with water, and watch how fast it sinks. If the water sits in the hole for a long time or the dirt smells bad, the spot drains poorly and needs drainage trenches before planting.
ga: Tsamɔ bu bibioo ko, ni okɛ nu awo mli, ni okwɛ bɔ ni emɔɔ oya. Kɛji nu hi bu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ loo muji lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo. He lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aná nu homɔ tsɔne dani adu nii.

english: Why does digging up and turning the soil help my crops grow bigger and healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mifoɔ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Turning the soil breaks up hard dirt crusts, allows rainwater and air to penetrate deep down, and buries surface weeds so they rot into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ gbálaa muji ni mli wa lɛ mli. Ehaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ofu jwɛi lɛ yɛ nɔ koni amɛgboi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the soil becomes too dry or when daytime temperatures get too hot. Regular watering at the base of the plant helps keep the plant cool and allows the flowers to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ shishi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni etse ehe kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats the growing leaves of maize plants. Identifying them early allows you to spray the central shoots before the pest destroys the entire plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kpataɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little fruit when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crops fight each other underground for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other's sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow big and strong.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtao niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a major food component in the soil. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure replenishes nitrogen and turns the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen afata he ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it naturally into the soil. This provides free plant food for your maize and keeps the soil healthy without spending extra on chemicals.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ náa tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry leaves and grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Spreading dry plant material, known as mulching, shades the soil from the sun. This prevents water from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa ni ekaho oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many bags of maize can I expect to harvest from one acre of farmland?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ji acre kome mli?

english: With good rain, quality seed, and proper weed and fertilizer management, one acre of farmland in Ghana typically produces between 10 to 15 standard 50kg bags of maize.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu jwɛi akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ji acre kome ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni tsiimɔ ji 50kg ni ji ŋmãa ni ji kotokui 10 kɛyashi 15.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the bottom leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the main stem will start to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune the small extra stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni miida yɛ Midumɔwu titri lɛ he

english: Extra stems, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main tree. Removing most of them and leaving just one or two allows the main plantain tree to produce larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui titrii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist during the cocoa tree's first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep shedding their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the soil gets too dry, when temperatures are extremely high, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering and placing dry grass around the base as mulch helps keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni ashwieɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shishitoo ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding poultry manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea will solve this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and water stress. Using neem oil spray or insect-proof netting helps protect the plants from these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo kooloi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from the growing roots below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest for dry grain versus fresh eating?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha ŋmãa ni egbi ni aye ehee?

english: For fresh eating (boiling or roasting), harvest when the silks on the cob turn brown and squeezing a kernel produces a milky liquid. For dry grain, wait until the whole plant and husk turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard.
ga: Kɛha niyenii hee (Ahoo loo ashã) Kpamɔ be mli ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa nu ni tamɔ mliki baa. kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi Mɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ agbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and expose them to direct sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which travels down to create much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrink before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungus called black pod disease, which spreads rapidly in overly damp, shady conditions, or by cherelle wilt where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support. Pruning extra tree branches helps air dry the farm and reduces fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ cherel wilting nɔ yɛ he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsoi krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the heavy winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy tops, especially when carrying a large bunch of fruit. Supporting the main trunk with strong bamboo props and planting suckers deep in the soil prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akui wuji yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ, ni adu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant cassava around the borders of my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Planting cassava along the boundary acts as a natural windbreak to protect delicate crops, deters free-roaming livestock, and serves as a clear, living marker for your land boundaries.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ husu lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa lɛ ahe. ni tsiɔ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛheee nɔ ko lɛ anaa ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, ni hiɛ kã kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get hot and rot inside the sacks when I keep them stored for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli beni mikɛtoɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn breathes and releases moisture. If you put grain into tight sacks before drying it thoroughly, trapped water creates internal heat, causing mold to grow and ruining your crop.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ muɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku ni mli wa mli, dani ebaagbi Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa emli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shwereɔ ni efiteɔ onibii.

english: How can I stop small insects like weevils from eating my corn inside storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mi-nitoo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weevils thrive in dark, humid sacks with air. To protect your grain, dry the corn completely until kernels are hard and store them in sealed, airtight bags (hermetic bags), which deprive pests of oxygen so they cannot survive.
ga: Beetles lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ kotokui ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni obu odumɔwui lɛ ahe Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Akɛ nɔ ko tsiɔ amɛhe (vacuum bags), ni no haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time when my corn on the farm is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is fully ripe when the outer husks turn brown and dry, the kernels feel hard when pressed with a fingernail, and a small black spot forms at the base of each kernel when pulled from the cob.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ edɔ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi. Dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne miimɔ nɔ. kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii Efeɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi kɛji ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my corn turn dark or moldy while drying it on the ground after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ediŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Drying corn directly on damp soil exposes kernels to dirt and moisture trapped beneath them. Drying your harvest off the ground on clean tarpaulins, raised wooden racks, or concrete platforms allows air to flow and keeps grains clean.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa abɛi ŋmɔji lɛ naa muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ abele ŋmɔji lɛ ashishi lɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni ooogbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ. Tso shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ loo kɔnkrit kpoku Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsɔɔ mli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow small, thin cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Bei komɛi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one spot, the roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole at recommended distances gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ yɛ he kome. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why does my corn grow tall and produce big cobs on one part of my farm, but stays short on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ miida ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji miiwo miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi ebɛ lolo yɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Soil quality varies across the same land due to differences in depth, drainage, and organic matter. Short plants usually indicate nutrient-poor or waterlogged soil, which can be fixed by applying compost or manure to those specific patches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su srɔtoi yɛ he kome mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, emlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, tsei kukuji tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nakai hei pɔtɛɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing large ragged holes in my young corn leaves before the cobs even start growing?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ baa dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ shishi edaa?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the central whorl of young corn plants. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended pest control treatments prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii lɛ baatsi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafite onibii.

english: Why do mature corn cobs start rotting on the standing stalks when heavy rain falls late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater gets trapped inside open, upright corn husks, creating a moist environment for fungus. Doubling or bending mature corn stalks downward allows rainwater to drain off naturally while the cobs dry safely in the field.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ efo ŋmãa ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ abɔle ŋmãa tsei ni edara lɛ ahe enyɔ loo akumɔ shi lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from the corn I harvested this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Replanting seeds saved from commercial hybrid corn usually results in lower yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh, certified seeds each planting season ensures high germination, strong growth, and maximum harvest yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa dalɛ be yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ nibii ni anáa babaoo

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow from the tip along the middle, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen nutrient or the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out juice, or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli

english: Why do my tomato plants show so many flowers, but the flowers just dry up and drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there is insufficient wind or insect activity to help pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? babaoo dani etsɔ agbo

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally discard young pods they cannot support, especially when the tree suffers from water stress, lack of soil nutrients, or heavy shade.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects and stays around the roots for too long without draining away, choking the roots of air and allowing soil fungi to infect them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. shishifãi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out crooked, branched, and short instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle, eyɛ niji, ni eyɛ kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow bent or deformed when the soil mound is too hard, stony, or shallow, forcing the expanding tuber to fight against compacted ground as it tries to grow down.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, tɛi yɛ nɔ, loo ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛ he ni etse lɛ kpeɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin, but falling over when slight wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi egbee shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the young plants stretch upwards quickly to fight each other for sunlight, resulting in weak, thin stems that cannot support the plant.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ aahu akɛ enyɛŋ efi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take almost two years to produce fruit when I plant them under large timber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afii enyɔ dani amɛwo yibii beni midu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require full sunlight to manufacture energy for fast growth. Deep shade from big trees slows down their feeding process and delays flowering and fruit formation.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛdara oya. Tsei wuji amli hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific plant food that crop needs from the soil, while allowing soil pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small weeds lower my crop harvest so much even when my crops are bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ da fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that secretly steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and room from young crops long before you notice the damage on top of the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ teemɔŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ he ko ni jɛ tsei bibii amli dani ona nɔ ko ni efite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. It can also happen when the field stays flooded with water for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds rot when planted in soil that is too wet or buried too deep. Seeds need warm, moist soil with air spaces to sprout; excess water cuts off oxygen, allowing fungi to attack the seed.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo afu mli tsɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over, or lodge, when they grow too tall and top-heavy, often from using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Strong winds, heavy rains, or planting seeds too close together can also weaken the base of the stems.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ kɛji tsei lɛ kwɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ, ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water fills the air gaps around the roots, suffocating them and encouraging harmful fungal rots. Harvesting mature cassava before prolonged heavy rains helps prevent root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni egbɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward the sun so they can manufacture more food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground also protects them from soil-borne diseases and dampness, resulting in bigger tuber sizes.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli helai anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by prolonged dry weather, nutrient-poor soil, or attacks from insects like capsids. Providing adequate shade trees, mulching, and protecting flowers from pests helps them set into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo kooloi tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ, ni akɛ hulutsoo ni sa haa, ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe, ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, ensuring the main plant gets enough strength to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni tsii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant move calcium smoothly from the soil to the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled, tiny pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or passing along a plant virus. Controlling insect pests early prevents leaf damage.
ga: pepper baai bibii Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bend lɛ baa. loo tso mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Mra Be mli nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas between my maize crop help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots break down in the ground, they feed the soil with fresh nutrients that nearby maize plants absorb to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni saa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ gbá kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii heei ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why didn't many of the seeds I planted come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry, or if red ants and pests eat them before they germinate. Planting seeds at a shallow depth—about twice the size of the seed—and keeping the soil moist helps them sprout safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo ŋmeii tsuji kɛ kooloi krokomɛi yeɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ—aaafee dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ toi enyɔ—ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem when sticking it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei tso lɛ, ani gbɛ ni etsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the crop will struggle to grow leaves and will produce very few roots underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ baai ni baa lɛ mli ni ebaana shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a living shelter that protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ he ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. Providing light shade during very hot weather and keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao tso lɛ. Kɛ́ aha hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and bushy instead of growing tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil makes it difficult for roots to spread out and gather water and plant food. Digging up the soil well before planting and mixing in animal manure softens the ground so roots can grow deep and nourish the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbua nu kɛ tsei ahe nibii anaa. Kɛ́ atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow while the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed food out of the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer around the base of the plant restores its green color and helps form large cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests each year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific foods from the soil every season. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the dirt and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishigbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eefite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often caused by inconsistent watering. Covering the soil around your tomatoes with dry leaves or straw keeps moisture in the ground and prevents the fruit from turning black.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Mulching around Kɛ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ha tomato nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars chewing holes through all my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay invisible eggs on the underside of leaves, which hatch into hungry caterpillars that eat the leaves to grow. Checking under the leaves regularly and spraying the crop early with neem leaf water keeps these pests away.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni okɛ neem baa nu afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots and becoming soft while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams start to sprout when exposed to heat and light because the tuber thinks it is time to grow in the soil again. Storing yams in a cool, shady, and well-ventilated barn slows down sprouting and keeps them firm for a long time.
ga: Sweet potatoes jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ la wo mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ susuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛdu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooto atomo yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, shade, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ afo ni eha ehi shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food young maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or animal manure helps the leaves turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa abifao koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: What does adding animal manure to my farm soil actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients, helps the ground hold water better during dry periods, and softens hard soil so crop roots can spread and breathe easily.
ga: Manure kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛmu mlɛo

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like cowpea or groundnut lets the soil rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into your farm helps stop the fungus from growing.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni ooofee koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akadara.

english: Why do small holes appear in my cabbage leaves even when no goats or farm animals are around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi kaabaji baai lɛ anɔ Kɛji tooi loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: Tiny insects and caterpillars hide under the leaves or in the soil during the daytime and feed on your crops at night. Checking under leaves regularly and spraying natural remedies like neem water can keep them away.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is a natural survival trick to keep moisture inside until the sun goes down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: When tomatoes lack water, their leaves wilt and feel dry; when they get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and the roots rot. Soil should feel damp like a squeezed sponge, not waterlogged.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tomato mli lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛgbi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni ashɛre mli, shi jeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams bend when the soil underneath is hard, stony, or clay-heavy, making it difficult for the tuber to push downward. Clearing stones and building high, loose soil mounds gives yams space to grow straight.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo shikpɔŋ sũ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa yitso lɛ akɛ ebaatsi kɛya shi. Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afeɔ lɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of leaves and flowers but very few nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnut flowers must bend down and push pegs into soft soil to form nuts underground. If the soil surface is too hard or lacks calcium, the pegs cannot enter the ground to make nuts.
ga: Esa akɛ abɔle ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ajie amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa tsɔ loo calcium bɛ mli lɛ Pegs lɛ nyɛŋ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why does my cassava taste bitter after staying in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli ŋɔɔ beni mikɛ be babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally produces bitter chemical compounds as a defence mechanism against dry weather or pests over time. Harvesting at the right maturity stage prevents bitter chemical buildup.
ga: Cassava jieɔ tsofai ni mli wa waa kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ he. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ tsiɔ tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees turn yellow and shed leaves when they receive too much direct sunlight without enough shade or soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young leaves from scorching sun until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni hulutsoo be ni sa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves with small caterpillars hidden in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛbaai amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on the growing heart of the maize plant. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves and applying recommended treatments prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei atsui ni miida lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is developing. It usually happens when watering is irregular or during sudden dry spells that stop the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edara lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer bags of maize every year even though I clear the weed and plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji mijie jwɛi ni midu yɛ be ni sa mli po.

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot season after season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds come just as the fruits are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and as the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top becomes unbalanced. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy branched wooden pole (propping) prevents the wind from snapping or uprooting the tree.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ, Yiteŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛ niji ni wa (fiɔ sɛɛ) fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafo loo ekajie tso lɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted yam pieces rot inside the mound before they even sprout above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛdara po yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when cut pieces are not allowed to dry and heal in the shade before planting, which allows soil fungi and bacteria to enter the open wounds.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ aŋmɛɛɛ hei ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi ni amɛtsa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ ni agbele lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my hot pepper plants dropping to the ground instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress or dry soil during flowering. Mulching around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and retains moisture so flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look healthy above ground, but when I pull them up the pods inside the soil are empty without seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ migbala lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efee efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Empty groundnut pods occur when there is insufficient calcium in the top layer of the soil where the pods form. Applying lime or wood ash to the soil during planting helps the seeds fill out properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get covered in tiny black insects that cause the pods to dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii diji ni haa ŋmeii lɛ miigbi oya lɛ ehà mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are aphids, sucking insects that drain the sap from tender cowpea pods and leaves, causing them to wither. Spraying early with natural neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments keeps their population under control.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii. Emuɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsina ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ. ha amɛgboi Adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo ani tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni gbɔmɛi ayibɔ lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: Why are my crops producing very small harvests even though I work hard on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Over time, planting crops repeatedly on the same land drains essential nutrients from the ground. Without replacing these nutrients through compost, manure, or fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee niyenii nɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: What causes the leaves of my young crop plants to turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong stems. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mɔ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around the roots without draining properly. This excessive wetness allows soil fungi to attack and break down the roots before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and preventing fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from the leaves and transmitting viruses, which stops the plant from flowering and fruiting properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out and wither so quickly during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to heat and wind. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and traps moisture near the root zone.
