ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewɔ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baadu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does planting shade trees alongside cocoa help my cocoa seedlings grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shade tsei ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Taller shade trees protect seedlings from harsh heat, conserve soil moisture, and create a cooler climate for young cocoa to establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ aba koni kookoo bibii lɛ afee shishifãi.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in my farm fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deeply, if the soil lacks sufficient moisture, or if the seeds were improperly stored and damaged by heat or moisture before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ etooo jogbaŋŋ ni latsaa loo ŋmɔtɔ fite amɛ dani adu.

english: Why do my maize stalks blow over and fall easily when heavy winds arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when planted too close together or in shallow soil, which causes them to grow thin stems with weak root anchors that cannot withstand strong winds.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Can I grow vegetables between my main crops while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping fast-growing short-season vegetables between slower main crops optimizes land use, suppresses weed growth, and provides early income and food security.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo, aduawai ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Tsĩ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni okɛ shika kɛ niyenii ni anáa mra aba

english: Why do groundnuts and cowpeas make the soil better for other crops planted after them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, this trapped nitrogen enriches the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease is coming back to my field after I already cleared infected plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ahe hela eku esɛɛ eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Diseases can hide in nearby weeds, surrounding trees, or the soil. Checking your crop leaves regularly—especially on the edges of your field—helps you spot yellowing, spots, or stunted growth early before the sickness spreads to all your healthy plants.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ helai ato jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ, tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ mra. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa otsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots are usually signs of cassava mosaic disease. It is spread by tiny whiteflies that thrive when young plants grow. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your harvest safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni daa be mli ni tso bibioo lɛ daa lɛ Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha onibii ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I clear the wild bushes around the borders of my farm if they are not touching my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie koo mli jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? edge of my farm Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ekpeko

english: Bushes and weeds along your farm boundaries act as breeding grounds and hiding spots for insect pests and plant diseases. Keeping the borders clean creates a barrier that makes it harder for pests to invade your crop rows.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ. Kɛ́ oha ohusui lɛ ahe tse lɛ, ebaa gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa ewaa ahaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall with tiny cobs when they are planted too close together or when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus. When crowded, the plants fight for sunlight instead of putting energy into filling the cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi phosphorus bɛ mli. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree branches before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks essential soil nutrients, or is attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids. Ensuring adequate shade and moisture helps trees hold onto their flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ aná hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excess leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when insect pests destroy the flowers before they turn into pods. Avoid heavy nitrogen fertilizers on legumes.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shã ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from fierce sunlight until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo bibioo lɛ he lɛ, ebaabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm become hard like rock after heavy sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ eshɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost or dead leaf cover. Adding animal manure or leaving dry crop remains on top of the ground keeps the soil soft, cool, and able to hold water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi bɛ mli. Koolooi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, edɔɔɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yam tubers so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and the vines dry up completely. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil after the vines die makes them spoil quickly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ beni wain tso lɛ egbo sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant does not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular while the fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ejaaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo yibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs to grow, while allowing pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I stop burning cleared bush and weeds on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa brɔshi ni ajie kɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shãa dani madu nii?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial insects and micro-organisms that keep the soil fertile. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose naturally or turning them into the soil adds free fertilizer and helps the soil retain moisture.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ ahiɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko fataa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for leafy green growth. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tiny balls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray or insecticidal soaps prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water when the sun is too hot. It hides the leaf surface from direct sunlight to prevent water loss, and the leaves usually open back up when temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he kɛji hulu la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ekɛ baa lɛ hiɛ teeɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni nu akafite. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ gbelemɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui kɛfata kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients during flowering. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and maintaining consistent watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Mulching koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on top of raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripened pods ensures the best bean quality and flavor during fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛhooɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native, wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, making them expert at quickly absorbing available water and nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life prevents them from choking out your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛhe esa waa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛheɔ oya lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to level my field flat before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Flat, leveled land ensures that water spreads evenly across the entire field so that all rice plants get the same amount of moisture and nutrients without some parts being submerged and others left dry.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akabote fãi komɛi amli ni ahaaa ekrokomɛi hu agbi.

english: Why does rice need flooded or very wet soil compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu afua loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmãa he kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in saturated soil because their roots are adapted to grow in low-oxygen water, which also naturally smothers weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice for nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛdaraa yɛ nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii faaa lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ he akaŋ kɛha niyenii kpakpai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better for me to plant rice seeds directly into the field or transplant seedlings from a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo makwɛ dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Transplanting seedlings gives young rice plants a head start against weeds and saves seeds, whereas direct seeding requires less manual labor upfront but needs very strict weed control to succeed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ fe jwɛi lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ baa shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ niji atsu nii babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Shi jwɛi akudɔmɔ ni mli wa waa he miihia koni eye omanye.

english: What causes one single rice plant to sprout multiple extra stems?
ga: Mɛni haa omɔ tso kome kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Rice plants naturally produce extra shoots called 'tillers' from the base of the main stem, which is healthy behavior that allows one plant to produce multiple heads of grain and increase your yield.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘tillers’ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ ji su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa ŋmãa tso kome woɔ dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the rice plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth, or that the soil is either severely lacking water or completely stagnant without fresh oxygen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu efo waa loo ebɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hee kwraa.

english: Why are weeds growing so much faster in my rice field during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings grow slowly early on and do not cast enough shade, leaving open sunlight and space for aggressive local weeds to sprout quickly if not cleared.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. mra ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa Shi hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ gbɛ aha maŋbii jwɛi ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛji ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my rice field at different times instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni mawo amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Rice needs nutrients at distinct growth stages—applying nitrogen early builds strong roots and tillers, while applying it later when the heads form helps fill out heavy grains.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ dalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen ni akɛbaafata he mra Ebaaha shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa aba. yɛ be mli ni akɛfataa he sɛɛ mli beni yitso lɛ feɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ eyiɔ mli.

english: Why do some heads on my rice plants turn completely white and hollow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi feɔ futafuta ni amɛhe ewo muji dani akpaa lɛ?

english: White, empty grain heads are typically caused by stem borer insects eating the inside of the plant's stalk, which cuts off the flow of nutrients up to the developing grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borer kooloi ni yeɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui yɛŋ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Will my rice crop fail if the field dries out completely for a few days?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ baafite kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbi kwraa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Most lowland rice can tolerate short dry spells during early growth, but severe dry soil while the plant is flowering will cause the grains to form empty hulls and reduce your final harvest.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baanyɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ afee ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ebaaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when the grains turn from green to a golden-yellow color and roughly 80% of the grain heads across the field have turned hard and dry.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. Ni aaafee 80% ni ji ŋmãa yitsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mli wa ni egbi.

english: Why do my crops need potassium fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii he hiaa mi tso lɛ?

english: Potassium acts like a shield and fuel for plants; it strengthens their stems, helps them survive dry weather, and makes fruits and tubers bigger and heavier.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi kɛ tsofa kɛhaa tsei. Ehaa tso lɛ mli waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. ni ehaa aduawai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking potassium?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ potassium?

english: When soil is low on potassium, the edges of older leaves turn yellow or brown as if they were burnt by fire, and the stems become weak and easily broken.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ potassium faaa lɛ Baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ tamɔ nɔ ni la eshã amɛ. ni tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekumɔ oya

english: Can I use leaves from local plants to make medicine that protects my crops from pests?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe baai afee tsofa ni buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Yes, plants like neem, chili pepper, and garlic contain natural plant chemicals that repel insects and fight plant diseases without harming your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tamɔ neem, chilli, kɛ galiki yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni shwieɔ kooloi ni kɛ tsei ahe helai wuɔ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Are natural plant-based sprays safer for my food crops than strong chemical sprays?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi niyenii tsei lɛ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plant-derived sprays break down quickly under sunshine and rain, leaving no harmful chemical residues on your food by the time you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishi. Eshiii tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oniyenii lɛ nɔ kɛ́ okpa.

english: Will spraying plant medicine on my crops leave any bad side effects on the harvested food?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai gbohii baaba niyenii ni akpa lɛ nɔ?

english: No, because natural plant medicines break down rapidly in nature, leaving no dangerous chemicals or toxic side effects on the food you take to the market.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, eshiii tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara loo nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baa niyenii ni okɛbaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation, keeping moisture inside until the weather cools down.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ emli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli. Enɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow while the new top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When plants lack enough soil nutrients, they pull nutrients out of their older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to fade.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Egbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Are all the insects I see crawling on my crops harmful?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa ni amɛmiikpã miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yɛ oshara?

english: No, many insects act as natural helpers on your farm by eating harmful pests like caterpillars and aphids before they can damage your crops.
ga: Dabi, kooloi babaoo tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Dani amɛbaafite onibii

english: Why does growing certain crops together in the same field help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Some plants act as good companions by offering shade, suppressing weeds, or repelling pests that would normally attack the crops planted next to them.
ga: Tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ nanemɛi kpakpai kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhaa, jwɛi ni amɛtsiɔ naa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to throw chemical fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer during heavy rain causes the running water to wash away all the nutrients before the plant roots can soak them up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and harsh winds. Keeping or planting shade trees like plantains protects young cocoa from burning and keeps moisture in the soil until the plants are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing sticky white spots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling with sticky white substance is caused by small pests called whiteflies or mealybugs that suck food out of the plant. Spraying the leaves with soap water or organic neem seed oil helps clear them off without harming the crop.
ga: Akɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo mealybugs ni nuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo organic neem seed oil shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afɔ baai lɛ ahe ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits turn black and rot at the bottom before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of peppers is caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mixing compost into the bed helps the plant build healthy fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pepper fitemɔ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfutuɔ saatso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I let my yam vines crawl on the ground instead of tying them to wooden sticks?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miha sweet potato wain tso lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛbaakpɛtɛ tso he hu?

english: When yam vines trail on the hot ground, the leaves burn easily and catch diseases from the wet soil. Tying vines to sticks lifts the leaves up to catch sunlight, which helps the plant grow much bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei nyiɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shãa baa lɛ oya ni ekɛ hela baa. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ fĩ tso nine he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo baai lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi plantain tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving too many small shoots forces the main mother plant to share its food and water with all of them, resulting in thin plants and small fruit bunches. Removing extra shoots so only one or two remain gives you larger, healthier plantains.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ efee babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ agba niyenii kɛ nu he sane. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ tsɔi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii akui. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does water stay on top of my field for days after rain and cause my crop roots to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? kɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miifite

english: Water sits on top of fields when the soil is packed too tight or lacks proper drainage. Excess water starves plant roots of air, so digging small channels or planting on raised soil mounds helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Nu taraa ŋmɔ ko nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, nubu bibioo ko ni aaaku Loo dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but the flowers drop off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when insects aren't around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist with grass mulch protects the plant from heat stress so flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ tomato.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots like a thief. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all the food in the ground goes directly into growing your crops.
ga: Tamɔ julɔi lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ, ehaa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛduɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves roll up and drop off during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss. By dropping old leaves, the plant conserves moisture in its roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ́ ashi baai momoi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing after heavy flooding in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa shweremɔ beni nu afua ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain covers the soil with water, oxygen cannot reach the roots. This suffocates the root system, preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my seeds wither and die if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil without providing deep moisture. If a dry spell follows, the soil heats up and dries out quickly, killing the newly germinated seeds before their roots can reach deep water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũɔ ni ehaaa sũ ni mli kwɔ aba. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baadɔ ni ebaagbi oya. Kpatamɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ahiɛ dani shishifãi lɛ ayashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in full sun without taller plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni cacao tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out faster under direct sunlight than their weak roots can absorb groundwater. Shade trees or plantains act as natural umbrellas to protect them from excessive heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Efa tsɔ akɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Shade tsei loo tsei bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he.

english: Why do my plantain crops grow tall and weak with small fruit bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ aduawai bibii akui lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients. This forces the plant to spend all its energy growing tall to reach light instead of producing big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii koni amɛdara koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce big, healthy leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni mli wa lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to build heavy stem and leaf leaves above ground, while neglecting root development below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Covering the soil—also called mulching—shields the ground from direct sun heat, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and prevents heavy rains from washing away rich topsoil.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant maize on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi nakai nɔŋŋ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause pepper plants to drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to preserve energy and water for the main plant's survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do insects damage my tomato crop more heavily during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures speed up the life cycle of insect pests, causing them to reproduce faster, while dry conditions force pests to gather on irrigated crop fields to search for moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɔ kooloi anɔ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji ni afɔɔ nu yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive until their own canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know which way is right side up when pushing cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole fã ni kwɛɔ ŋwɛi beni otsiɔ ŋmei nine kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Look at the small buds or nodes along the stem; they should always point upwards toward the sky. Planting a cassava stick upside down forces the shoots to grow backwards, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be kɛya ŋwɛi. Kasava ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to convert solar energy into food for underground growth. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛtsake hulu hewalɛ lɛ ewo niyenii mli kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the mother plant gets enough strength to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure supplies the nutrients needed to make leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as free fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers cover the dry soil around their crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, keeps weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down into rich plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni okɛ nu akawo mli babaoo Etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbɛɔ etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii

english: What is causing the small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typical signs of Fall Armyworm damage. These caterpillars hide in the central funnel of the plant, and treating them early with organic remedies like neem extract or approved pesticides stops them before they destroy the stem.
ga: Buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm ni efite lɛ he. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. ni otsa amɛ mra. Kɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ. baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull up calcium naturally to form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because cool temperatures let the water soak deep into the soil without evaporating quickly in the sun, giving plants a good drink to handle the day's heat.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ shwieee oya. Ha tsei lɛ aná nu kpakpai. Koni ekɛkpee dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ gbi lɛ mli lɛ naa

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to grow healthy green leaves, and adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry leaves or dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbo loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in a much smaller yield.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the bottom leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem will start to crack as the roots expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to push wooden poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso ko awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground with poles also keeps them dry and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi, ni ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot on the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates too much. Regular, even watering helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly to build strong fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. If the soil gets too dry or waterlogged during hot days, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm dirt better for the next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume plants like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When these plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt, serving as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tsei nɛɛ gboi lɛ, Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad canopy shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is causing small chewed holes in my young maize leaves and green dust inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ani okɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ye ni sũ eŋɔli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant, eating the tender young leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. Eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil has too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot on the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early with recommended sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop during very dry weather, when there are not enough pollinating insects, or when the soil lacks nutrients. Keeping shade trees on the farm and maintaining healthy soil helps more flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers on my land?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted about 3 meters apart from each other. Good spacing gives each plant enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mitai 3. He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell, which can dry out and kill new seedlings before their roots grow deep.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpea together with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmã fata ŋmãa he?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good. Cowpea plants take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps your soil rich.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Cowpea tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why does burning my farm to clear weeds harm my crops in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ni mishãa koni mikɛgbe jwɛi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Fire burns away the organic matter and friendly insects in the soil that help retain moisture and feed your plants. Over time, burning makes your soil dry, hard, and poor.
ga: La shãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ewa, ni efee ohiafo.

english: What happens if I leave my cassava tubers in the ground for too long past the harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil too long causes the tubers to become tough, woody, and lose their starch content, which reduces their quality for eating or processing.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfee tsei, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu baaje mli. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni ayeɔ loo bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout naturally when their resting period ends or when the barn gets warm and humid. Breaking off the shoots early and keeping the barn cool and airy helps the yams stay good for longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be naagbee loo be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Ni aaagbala ŋmeii lɛ amli mra Ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaves and strong growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce water loss from direct sunlight. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism against drought and high temperatures.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛjɛ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperature stress or irregular watering occurs. When the soil becomes too dry or hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for survival instead of making seeds.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo edɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo dumɔwui lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing taller once they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Once pepper plants begin flowering, they redirect most of their energy and nutrients away from branch growth and into developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ Amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when they encounter hard, compacted soil or stones underground. Making deep, soft, raised mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kpe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha yitso he lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crops struggle to grow when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young crops have small root systems that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do ragged holes appear in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are commonly caused by pests such as the fall armyworm, which feed inside the leaf funnel where it is soft and moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Eyeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lasu tsuji lɛ amli, ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaf tips turn brown and look burnt along the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Brown, burnt edges on plantain leaves usually show that the plant lacks potassium or is suffering from a lack of water during dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain baai lɛ asɛɛ ni shãa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting quickly when I stack them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto amɛhe lɛ?

english: Onions rot if they are harvested while still wet or if they were not dried properly in the shade before storage. Proper drying hardens their outer neck skin to seal out moisture and fungi.
ga: Sabolai fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo loo kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsitsi lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my stored cowpea seeds after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Tiny holes in stored cowpea seeds are caused by weevils that hatch from eggs laid while the crop was still in the field. Drying seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight containers prevents these pests from damaging the grain.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni awoɔ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa seedling take before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually take about three years to mature and produce their first pods, provided they receive continuous care, regular weeding, and adequate shade during their early growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ daa Ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli daa. ni amɛná hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in strong heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or food crops to act as protective covers until their roots establish and they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo niyenii tsei. Koni etsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa shi ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with shade-providing food crops is very effective. It gives your cocoa plants protection from the sun, keeps the soil moist, and gives your family food and early income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo bibii ni akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika ni anáa mra be mli ni emɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I schedule farm work so my family doesn't get overwhelmed during the clearing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔ koni miweku lɛ akawo jatsu fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ be mli?

english: Breaking major tasks into small weekly plans allows family members to share responsibilities evenly, ensuring crucial work like planting, weeding, and shading is completed on time without straining anyone.
ga: Nitsumɔi ni he hiaa lɛ amlijaa Jaa mli owo otsi gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko mli. Enɛ haa weku lɛ mli bii lɛ jaa gbɛnaa nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni agbe nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui, jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ hulutsoo be naa yɛ be naa ni mɔ ko mɔ ko mli efuuu.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ jwɛi krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, extra, or diseased branches so the tree does not waste energy on unnecessary leaf growth, allowing nutrients to flow directly into developing heavy, healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Efee fe nine loo hela emɔ lɛ Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛi hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni wa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Do I still need to give my cocoa farm regular care once the trees start bearing fruit after three years?
ga: Ani ehe miihia lolo ni makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ́ tsei lɛ je shishi amɛwo yibii yɛ afii etɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa is a long-term commitment that requires continuous weeding, pruning, and monitoring every year to maintain good yield and prevent diseases from taking over established trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ji shiwoo ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni biɔ ni ajie jwɛi. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa afi Koni yibii kpakpai ahi shi ni helai akaha tsei ni adu lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my young cocoa trees help them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Weeds compete with young trees for moisture, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing them removes competition so your cocoa roots can absorb all available nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba shi bɔni afee ni o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease triggered by excessive moisture and humidity. Keeping the farm weeded and pruning trees to let air and sunlight through reduces wet conditions that spread the fungus.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa. Akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ agbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ashwã lɛ aba shi.

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival mechanism for cocoa trees to conserve internal water during hot, dry periods so the trunk and roots stay alive until rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs added nutrients or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii kpakpai loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If your trees show slow growth, pale or yellow leaves, or fail to produce good pod sizes despite proper watering and shade, the soil is likely low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo Pale loo yellow leaves loo ekɛ pods ni dalɛ fa bɔ ni sa baaa yɛ nu kɛ shade ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many seed cups of rice do I need to plant on one acre of land?
ga: Omɔ kɔɔpoi enyiɛ ehe baahia ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: To plant one acre of rice evenly, you typically need about 20 to 25 kilograms of seed, which equals roughly 80 to 100 standard milk seed cups depending on whether you are broadcasting or planting in straight rows.
ga: Bɔni afee ni odu ŋmãa acre kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui aaafee kilogram 20 kɛyashi 25 he baahia bo, ni no tamɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui aaafee kɔɔpoi 80 kɛyashi 100 ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ. Edamɔ kɛji oodu dumɔwui loo oodu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ.

english: Why do my rice seeds need so much moisture in the soil before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds have a hard outer husk that needs to absorb a lot of water to soften and trigger the seed inside to wake up and start growing roots and leaves.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni esa akɛ eŋɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ afee blɛoo ni ewo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi shishifãi kɛ baai akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ wuobii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do some crops like maize grow taller and faster when planted after beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, daa ni amɛdaraa oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and leguminous plants pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving rich natural fertilizer behind that helps crops like maize grow much faster.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdaraa oya waa lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grains turn from green to a golden-yellow color and the stalks start bending gently under the weight of the grains.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni o-rice lɛ mli aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ blɛoo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ tsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my root crops like cassava rot if I leave them in wet ground too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: When mature tubers stay in overly wet soil, oxygen cannot reach them, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to attack and cause the soft rot.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa egboɔ.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested rice in the sun immediately after cutting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Drying fresh rice lowers its internal moisture so that mold, fungi, and storage insects cannot grow and destroy the grain while it is stored.
ga: Omɔ hee ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, no hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ nyɛŋ adara ni amɛfite ŋmaa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains spoil faster when I keep them in warm, unventilated rooms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm and airtight spaces trap moisture coming off the grains, creating a humid environment where heat-loving insects and mold multiply rapidly.
ga: He ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ latsaa lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: How does transporting harvested crops during the hottest part of the day harm them?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harvested crops continue to 'breathe' and generate heat; exposing them to direct mid-day sun speeds up moisture loss, wilting, and spoilage before you reach your storage site.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ ‘amɛmuɔ’ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya. ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ dani oyashɛ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their soft leaves from heat stress and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni abu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in too much water, preventing the plant from making food and growing healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ewo niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ baai ni wa.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do I see small holes and ragged edges on my maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworms feeding on the soft, growing parts of the maize plant inside the central leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Excess water in the soil fills the air spaces around roots, causing root rot disease because the cassava roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does leaving heavy weeds around my young cassava plants slow down tuber growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi cassava tsei bibii lɛ miiha tuber lɛ dalɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds steal essential water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight from the cassava plant, leaving it with less energy to expand its roots into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná ni akɛgbala shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛfee ŋmei wuji.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to survive the stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ha tomato tsei lɛ agbo koni amɛye nɔnyɛɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous crop yield less harvest than certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength and vigor over generations, whereas certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and produce high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ helai anaa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of crawling on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves on stakes allows them to capture full sunlight to make more food, which is then sent underground to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛhoo nii babaoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I not pour fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can chemical-burn the stem and tender roots because fertilizer salts pull moisture directly out of the plant tissues.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ adara. Tsofai baanyɛ ashã Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What are the main categories of land we have for planting in Ghana, and how do I know which crops suit my land?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔji titrii ni wɔyɔɔ ni wɔbaanyɛ wɔtsu nii yɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Farmland is generally categorized by soil type, drainage, and topography—such as dry uplands or moist lowlands (valleys). Uplands are good for crops like maize and cassava that need well-drained soil, while low-lying, swampy land is ideal for crops like rice that thrive in heavy moisture.
