ga: Ajara okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni egbi loo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ (jɔɔ lɛ). Shikpɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ edɔ waa lɛ ji hei ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly whenever I plant them in the swampy part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different types of land behave differently. Waterlogged or swampy land restricts air flow to the roots of crops like maize or pepper, causing them to rot. That category of land is better saved for water-loving crops like rice or sugarcane.
ga: Shikpɔji srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ. Esa akɛ ato shikpɔŋ nɛɛ he gbɛjianɔ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops each year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant continuously on the same land without replacing those nutrients using manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and production drops over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ odu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I make my crop yields go up season after season on the same piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aya hiɛ afi fɛɛ afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You can increase your production by feeding the soil. Adding compost or animal manure, rotating different crops, and leaving crop residues on the land to decay will replenish soil fertility and lead to better harvests.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha lɛ nɔ. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ Tsakemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is still healthy enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil usually has a dark color from rich organic matter, feels moist without being overly muddy, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains natural organisms like earthworms.
ga: Okwaafoi ashikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ fɔɔ su ni tsuɔ waa kɛjɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ amli. Enuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni ebɛ muji tsɔ. Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya ni adebɔɔ mli bɔɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ

english: Is it possible for me to keep farming my plot of land continuously every year without letting it rest?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ maya nɔ madu mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi ni mahaaa ehi shi?

english: Yes, continuous farming is possible, but only if you actively maintain the land. You must replenish nutrients by rotating crops, applying organic matter, and protecting the topsoil from wash-away rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba mli. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he

english: Why do my crops perform better when I plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural fertilizer left behind, growing stronger and yielding more.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ehaa ewaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Does burning dry bushes to clear my farm damage the land for future crop growth?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egbi ni ashãa koni akɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha tsei adalɛ wɔsɛɛ?

english: Yes, burning destroys organic matter, kills beneficial earthworms and soil organisms, and strips the land of its natural protective cover, which reduces crop yields over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. kɛ hei ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akpãtãmɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Where can I get reliable, modern information about the best seeds and farming techniques for my region?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana saji ni yɔɔ be mli ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni kɔɔ dumɔwui kɛ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ?

english: You can talk to local Agricultural Extension Officers from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture. They are trained to share proven scientific findings, seasonal weather updates, and improved farming methods directly with farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni jɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ awie. Atsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛja jeŋ nilee mli nibii ni ana ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ. Be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe saji kɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ okwaafoi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to consult an extension officer before trying new farming methods on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ extension officer ko agba sane dani maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Extension officers have access to government research on soil behavior, crop varieties, and pest control tailored to your specific area, helping you avoid costly mistakes and improve your yield.
ga: Extension officers lɛ yɛ hegbɛ ni amɛnáa nɔyeli lɛ niiamlitaomɔ ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ subaŋ, tsei srɔtoi, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Eye ebua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he ni oha onitsumɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and withering even though I planted them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves wither and turn yellow when the roots cannot get enough moisture or nitrogen from the soil. During dry spells, applying mulch around the base of the plant helps trap moisture and stops the hot sun from drying out the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Mulch ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings burn and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very quickly in intense heat. Providing light temporary shade or watering early in the morning and late in the evening protects them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and wither after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash soil containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves, causing fungal diseases like blight. Pruning the lower leaves and leaving enough space between plants allows air to dry the leaves and prevents disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ agbi baai lɛ ni ebaatsi helai anaa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast and choke my crops after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil and quickly germinate when sunlight hits the cleared ground. Clearing weeds before they flower and using cover crops or mulch blocks sunlight and keeps new weeds from taking over.
ga: Afuɔ jwɛi dumɔwui awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi Ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ atsu nii ni akɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni atsĩ jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and weed the farm the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil, keeping it fertile.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or sudden changes in soil water levels. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli tsakemɔi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What causes my yam seeds to rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Yam seeds rot underground when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil or if the seed yam was damaged before planting. Planting on raised mounds improves drainage and prevents water from surrounding the seed.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efite dani adu Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo ni ehaaa nu abɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotting inside when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ mli kɛ́ mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground mainly due to poor soil drainage or root-rot diseases caused by excessive standing water. Planting on sloped land or ridges helps water drain away from the root system.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ kɛbaa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the bunches of plantain get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji amɛje shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, making them top-heavy when carrying full bunches. Propping the stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo supports prevents strong winds from knocking them over before harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ babaoo baa kɛ́ tsɔne lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔne. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani akpa.

english: How can I improve my farm yields step-by-step so I don't have to leave for the city to find work?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni mashi maŋ lɛ mli kɛyatao nitsumɔ?

english: Improving farm income starts with small steps: using quality certified seeds, applying organic compost, mulching for water retention, and spacing crops correctly. Better yields per acre make local farming sustainable and profitable.
ga: Okwaafoi ashika ni anáa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ gbɛ bibioo ko: dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Organic compost Mulching ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni ka ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ Yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ acre kome mli lɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli yaa nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ baa.

english: Why do my crops need more fertilizer as they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo beni edaa lɛ?

english: Just like growing children need more food as they get bigger, crops require larger amounts of nutrients to support their growing stems, bigger leaves, and developing fruits.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛ ni miida lɛ he hiaa niyenii babaoo beni edaa lɛ. Niyenii babaoo hu he miihia tsei koni eye ebua amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ. baai wuji kɛ aduawai ni daa

english: Why are the lower leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen or lacking water, causing it to drop its older bottom leaves to save energy for new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo nu efo mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ashɛrɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashwieɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yields get smaller when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves out of the soil and allows plant-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate from tomato leaves faster than the roots can drink it, so the plant temporarily curls its leaves to conserve moisture until the heat passes.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ be kukuoo ko koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baaho.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings shade each other and stretch rapidly upward to fight for sunlight, resulting in weak, thin stems.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as temporary sunshades while the cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli ni cacao tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my crops if there is enough dirt for all of them to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ nɔ?

english: Weeds steal the moisture, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots, leaving your crops starved and stunt-grown.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots ensures that the mother plant does not have to share its food and water with too many stems, leading to bigger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sun, allowing them to gather maximum sunlight energy to produce larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛbua hulu la hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ naa koni amɛkɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if my maize plants are getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If maize gets too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow and the roots rot. If it lacks water, the leaves roll inward tightly like tubes during the day to save moisture.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Kɛji nu bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe kɛya mli shiŋŋ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Should I water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the late afternoon?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, and the leaves can dry quickly to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Ni baai lɛ baagbi oya koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot mid-day sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo moŋ?

english: Hot midday heat causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can drink it up. If the plants bounce back by evening, it is normal heat stress, but if they stay limp, they need consistent irrigation.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ efo gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi kɛji tso lɛ nyiɛɔ lolo ni egbɔjɔ Ehe miihia ni afɔ lɛ nu daa.

english: How does heavy standing water in my field affect my cassava crop?
ga: Te nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to grow; standing water smothers the roots and causes the tubers to rot underground before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly when the dry sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the leaf area exposed to the hot sun and keep water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahe hei ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ afee bibioo. ni etsĩ nu ni hoɔ oya tsɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa

english: Why is it important to complete my field land preparation before the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbe ŋmɔ mli saamɔ naa dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing land early allows the soil to loosen and absorb the initial rains immediately, giving planted seeds a fast, strong start before dry spells return.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eŋɔ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jeɔ shishi oya, ni mli wa dani majik ni egbi lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How does spacing my crop plants properly help them handle dry weather better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are spaced properly, their roots do not compete with each other for underground water, allowing each plant to reach deep moisture.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my yellow crop leaves turn back green after I fix the soil drainage in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni ji yellow plant lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli beni misaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he naagba ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Draining excess water lets air return to the soil roots, allowing the crop to absorb nitrogen again, which turns the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ nitrogen ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I plant them in full open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong direct heat; they need temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them while their early leaves develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I know the best morning hours to apply liquid chemicals or water to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male leebi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu loo nu baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time is between sunrise and early morning when crop leaf pores are open to absorb liquids and before heat evaporates the water.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji hulushitee kɛ leebi maŋkpa teŋ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ koni amɛhe nu. ni dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why should I dig drainage ditches on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Digging drainage ditches allows excess rainwater to flow off your land instead of settling around your crops. When water collects and stays around plant roots, it causes diseases and destroys crops like cassava and rubber trees.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ebɔle tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ, ekɛ helai baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ rɔba tsei.

english: What causes the soil in the low areas of my farm to turn into heavy red clay?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni tsii?

english: When land frequently collects water that has nowhere to go, the prolonged flooding and wet conditions change the soil texture over time, turning it into thick red clay.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa nu naa shii abɔ ni he ko bɛ ni ejɛɔ mli kɛbaa. Nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baatsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ be ni sa mli. Etsɔ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni mli tse.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava rots easily when it is planted in places where water gathers and stands. Cassava roots need soil that drains well; sitting in water deprives them of air and rots the tubers.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni nu buaa ehe naa ni edamɔ shi yɛ lɛ. Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ota nu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ogbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant cassava in a low valley area where rainwater usually settles?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: It is not advisable to plant cassava in places where water settles, because prolonged standing water will cause the cassava roots to decay and rot in the soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Akɛni nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will standing water on my land harm my rubber trees?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye mi rɔba tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, rubber trees suffer greatly in standing water. Much like cassava, when rubber tree roots sit in collected water, it causes severe disease and rot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, rɔbɔt tsei naa amanehulu waa yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Tamɔ ŋmei pɛpɛɛpɛ Kɛji rɔbɔt tso lɛ shishifãi yɛ nu ni abua naa lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ helai ni naa wa kɛ fitemɔ baaba.

english: Is soggy, flooded land suitable for starting a rubber plantation?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ani ehi kɛha rɔba ŋmɔji?

english: No, land where water collects is bad for rubber trees because excess water brings root diseases. If you must use such land, you must first dig ditches to drain the water away.
ga: Dabi, hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha rɔbɔt tsei ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ shishifãi helai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baatsu nii lɛ, esa akɛ atsa bu ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do tree diseases spread much faster on my farm during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause excess water to settle on the ground. Wet, waterlogged conditions create the perfect environment for root diseases to breed and spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi helai ni baa lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: How can I keep my crops healthy when the rainy season is unusually heavy?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your crops by digging clear drainage paths so that heavy rainwater drains off your field quickly, preventing the standing water that triggers fungal and root diseases.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ ni mli tse ni oootsɔ mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ oya kɛjɛ oŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni ekã shi ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi helai baa lɛ naa.

english: How does standing water affect crop roots underground?
ga: Te nu ni damɔ shi lɛ saa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Standing water suffocates crop roots and creates unhealthy soil conditions, causing the roots to rot and making the entire plant vulnerable to deadly diseases.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni ehiii baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ woɔ helai ni naa wa he oshara mli.

english: How do I tell if my farmland has a water drainage problem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nu homɔ he naagbai?

english: If rainwater stays pooled in areas long after the rain stops, or if the ground turns into sticky red clay, your land has poor drainage that will rot sensitive crops unless you dig channels.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ tsuru Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo. Ja otsa gbɛ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when the hot sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not have strong roots yet and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains next to cocoa trees provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get regular water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching the base helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can develop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense to prevent losing water into the hot air. Watering early in the morning and putting dried leaves or straw around the base helps keep the roots cool and reduces leaf stress.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu akafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Okɛ nu awo mli leebi ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi abɔle he. Kɔnii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi.

english: Yellowing on the bottom leaves usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow well. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the crop needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo okɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually right after a light rain or early in the morning. Avoid applying it right before a heavy downpour, as heavy running water will wash the fertilizer off your field before the roots can take it up.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo loo leebi maŋkpa Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni owoɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli wa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my maize plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh middle leaves of growing maize. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem leaf extracts directly into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai heei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy or flat soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rain to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: What is this pink-flowered weed that attaches to my maize roots and makes the plants stay small?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi ahe ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛɛ?

english: This weed is called Striga or witchweed, and its roots attach to maize roots to steal nutrients and water. Planting leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut on that land for a season helps break the weed's life cycle and clean the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Striga loo Witchweed ni eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe koni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ be kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efo jwɛi lɛ ashihilɛ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse.

english: Why do my crops produce very small cobs and tubers when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to grow large ears, pods, or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ toi wuji, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni makwɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out on stakes to catch direct sunlight, which allows the leaves to make food. The food produced in the sunlit leaves travels down the vine to feed and expand the yam tuber under the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã tso nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. Niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ mli baa lɛ fãa kɛyaa wain tso lɛ shishi koni eyaye sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni ekwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green, bushy, and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛfee ŋmɔji, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my soil produce lower yields every year even though I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ?

english: Soil loses its fertility over time when the same crop drains the same nutrients every season; resting the land or rotating crops like groundnuts brings nitrogen back to the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ, ejaakɛ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and crooked instead of thick and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deeply mounds of earth to expand easily; if the ground is hard or compact, the tubers struggle to push through the dirt and turn out misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tubers lɛ naa naagba ni amɛkɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight; high canopy shade trees protect them from sunburn and keep the air cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant plantains alongside my fresh cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential temporary shade and humidity for delicate cocoa saplings while giving you food early on.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ehaa bo niyenii mra.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their flowers before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or irregular water supply, as the plant saves water and energy by sacrificing flowers instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛkɛshãa afɔle yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies and starves the roots of full size.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. ni eha eshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ fo kwraa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark soft bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant lacks calcium or receives uneven watering while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Tomato ni shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsuɔ waa Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo afɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and break down during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaa yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly strip moisture from broad plantain leaves, causing the plant to drop outer leaves so it can preserve remaining stem water to stay alive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya. Ha tso lɛ ajie esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛ nu ni jɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I wait until cocoa pods turn bright yellow or orange before harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse dani akpa?

english: Green or green-yellow cocoa beans do not have enough developed sugars inside, which prevents proper fermentation and results in bitter, low-value beans.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei lɛ bɛ sugars ni etsɔ hiɛ bɔ ni sa. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjara waaa.

english: When is the right time to start applying fertilizer to my young crop seedlings after they come up?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi midumɔwui bibii lɛ awomɔ beni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young seedlings feed on the stored energy inside the seed for their first few days. Around 10 to 14 days after sprouting, when their first true leaves open up, their roots are ready to take in external plant food, making it the ideal time to start giving them light doses of liquid fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaye hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli. Eheɔ aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ, beni klɛŋklɛŋ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ fãa lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaye niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ okɛ nu fioo loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ aje shishi.

english: How do I correctly apply plant food to very small seedlings without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei aniyenii awo dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Small seedlings have delicate roots that burn easily. You should dilute liquid fertilizer with water or place dry fertilizer a few inches away from the stem rather than directly on it, then water the soil lightly so the tiny roots can easily drink in the nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya. Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni okɛaawo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fioo. koni shishifãi bibii lɛ Anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo

english: Why do my seeds take so long to break out of the soil holes after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ amɛbu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need adequate moisture, warmth, and the right depth to sprout. If they are planted too deep, the soil is dry, or the earth is packed hard over the planting hole, the tender young shoot struggles to push through to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni sa, dɔlɛ, kɛ mlibotemɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe yɛ dumɔ bu lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some seeds in the same planting hole sprout fast while others fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ bu kome mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Not all seeds in a batch have the same strength or maturity. Some may be damaged by insects underground, or buried deeper than others in the hole, which delays or prevents their emergence.
ga: Jeee dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kuu mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ loo shweremɔ kome. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi baanyɛ afite kooloi srɔtoi komɛi loo afu amɛ yɛ bu mli shɔŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi, ni no baaha amɛ sɛɛ atsɛ loo amɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: How do I protect my tender young crop shoots from dying in the harsh afternoon heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Just like young infants, newly emerged sprouts cannot withstand full, hot sun. Building a temporary palm-frond nursery shade keeps the temperature moderate and prevents the young leaves from drying out and wilting.
ga: Tamɔ abifao pɛpɛɛpɛ Tsobii heei ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa kwraa. Be kukuoo mli shade ni afee aha greenhouse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ hiɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. ni etsĩ baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkagbo

english: Why do my young nursery seedlings bend sideways instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee afã moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings naturally stretch towards light to feed themselves. If your nursery shade is too dense or uneven, the young plants will bend and lean heavily toward wherever the sunlight is breaking through.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baajie amɛhe kɛya la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛye amɛhe niyenii. Kɛji akɛ o-nursery lɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baakoto ni ekɛ ehe afɔ shi waa kɛya he ni hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves spread out wide in the morning but droop or close up late in the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo leebi shi amɛgboɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi blɛoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural defense behavior. Plants open their leaves in the cooler morning to catch sunlight and make food, but they droop or curl up during peak heat to save water and rest until temperatures drop.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Tsei gbeleɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ si aloo a ngɔɔ a he ngɛ be nɛ la mi ngɛ wawɛɛ ɔ mi konɛ a kɛ bu nyu nɛ a jɔɔ a he kɛ ya si be nɛ la mi ɔ maa ba si.

english: Why do my young crop shoots look soft and pale yellow when they first come out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Sprouts coming out of dark soil holes lack sunlight initially, which keeps them pale. Once they spend a day or two in ambient light, they produce chlorophyll, turning a healthy deep green as they begin manufacturing food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ bu ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hulu la yɛ shishijee mli. ni haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ amɛye gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ yɛ la ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ klorofil. ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ beni amɛjeɔ niyenii feemɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know my seedlings are mature enough to move out of the nursery into the main farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready to leave the nursery once they have developed 3 to 4 strong, healthy true leaves and a sturdy stem—usually around 3 to 4 weeks after sprouting—showing their root systems are strong enough to handle field soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni amɛná baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji anɔkwale kɛ tso ni mli wa—bei pii lɛ, otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ—ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops get weak and shocked immediately after I move them out of their nursery holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe efee shoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Transplant shock happens when fine feeder roots are broken or exposed to sudden heat during moving. Transplanting late in the evening and watering immediately helps the young roots settle into their new homes without drying out.
ga: Transplant shock baa kɛji akɛ niyenii kpakpa ko shishifãi lɛ fã loo hulutsoo trukaa ba be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ gbɛkɛ ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ amɛshia hee lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ gĩii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmei ekoŋŋ.
